entries.text: It was the same mountain, the same narrow path, and maybe the same plain and grassy field which were covered by snow.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It seemed pointless to think much of it; we hadn't been there for more than a decade, but back in the day, it was the perfect hidden place for us to go spend our time.{w} Not once had we seen anyone else there, but eventually, going to the mountains just to play was seen as rude by the people who tried to make a daily living on them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Admittedly, we also didn't want to have anything to do with the strangers on the mountain, which decreased the frequency of our visits until we finally stopped going altogether. The final visit was something we hadn't even realized was final.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Do you remember?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah, of course. I'm not sure the place is the same, but thinking back on those times makes me happy.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're right. We used to have a lot of fun there.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Reminiscing evoked a very particular feeling within me. When the weather was ideal, we would spend entire afternoons in our unreachable hidden place, playing all sorts of different games. We brought things from home every day we went to make it ours.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though if you were to look at Shiroya, you might not have believed it, her usual self was a very cheerful one, so remembering some of those early memories was bittersweet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the other hand, after I looked at her... She was smiling, and wore an expression that had lately disappeared from her face. The memories we shared from that time were very special.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No matter what I'd tried to say, I hadn't been able to cheer her up. That might've been the first time in two weeks she'd clearly reacted positively to anything, and I probably knew why.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Those memories were so old that Miiya had not yet appeared in our lives. That was why Shiroya was able to think about them without sparking the negative reactions that obfuscated everything else.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe we should go back one day and see what it looks like now.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah... That is a good idea.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Even though her smile had slightly faded, she seemed to genuinely mean that. It was reassuring to hear, and it made me trust that everything would eventually get better.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei had continued talking while I'd been digging up old memories, but he'd only gone back over his previous points.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is all I know. It's not much, but hopefully you can at least believe me.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You sure are good at coming up with stories to cover your ass. It's honestly impressive.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai said that, but it didn't look like he disbelieved Katei's explanation. He was most likely referring to everything else Katei said previously with the sole intention to provoke him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If that didn't please you, there's not much else I can say. This was probably more than I am allowed to, actually.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Ah. I see.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Even though I could've seen Sai's playful behavior as intriguing earlier, it had become off-putting. After shifting my thoughts to some of my childhood memories, the thought of getting out of the tower was much more appealing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Finding out who was responsible for the attack was a goal, but as long as the police had some way to recover the camera footage, they could handle that. They could have already captured the person responsible for all we knew. Ashiya's compensation was certainly a nice thought to keep in mind, too.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was more important to keep an eye out for anyone doing anything suspicious and nail them once we got out than constantly and baselessly accuse anyone in the vicinity like Sai seemed to want to.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Anyway... weren't you all supposed to be investigating the building? I think it's time for that. We keep repeating this, but Naomi's disappearance gets weirder by the second.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yeah, we should go.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I agree. Let's look through this floor first; it's where she was when the smoke appeared, and it has plenty of disabled cameras.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We made our way to hallway A. Finally starting to inspect the huge building was an imposing task.{w} A lot of time had already passed, so I had no idea what to think of Naomi's disappearance. She was either incapable of reaching us... or didn't want to.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How do we do it? Do we split up?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No. Let's make the situation clear first. Funny things can happen later.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Let's enter every room in this hallway and then move on to the other one. After we're done with this floor, we'll move up one at a time.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yeah. Let's begin there.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Erina looked at the crystal room in front of the security room. It was the one labeled "A1" on the map.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Given the floor's layout, if there was someone who wanted to avoid being seen, as long as we didn't split up, they could easily achieve that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There were three different ways to make it from one hallway to the other, so we would never be able to rule out a sneaky moving culprit.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Taking that same possibility in mind, though, the thought of splitting up was distressing. It was better to investigate together and hope that wouldn't happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were in front of the room we'd start with. Katei opened it, and yet again, I felt the same recurring sensation of stepping into a different world.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A clean floor, walls, and ceiling awaited us. Just like in the room I'd looked at, there were many cabinets, presumably displaying different kinds of valuable gemstones.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why are they covered?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: As Isla said, the interior of the cabinets wasn't visible. Velvet curtains, as pretty as the Sekimeiya's had once been, were neatly placed over all of them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, yes, this is something that we do every morning. Except on Sundays, when the tower is closed.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: While at {time=9:00}, the floor opens to the public, it isn't until {time=9:10} that the showcase cabinets are uncovered. This is purely done for dramatic effect and, honestly, to give the visitors the impression that they're about to witness something very valuable.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Oh... Can I?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Yeah, of course. Let me raise them for you.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: In the same manner that Katei might've seen it done daily through the cameras, he carefully rolled up every curtain, letting us see what they were hiding.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As amazed as a little girl trapped in a building could be, Isla lit up while Katei uncovered the next mysterious interior.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai gave it a similar look, one I couldn't help but question.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The cabinets in those rooms were different from the Sekimeiya's. They were lower to the ground, and on top of them was a screen of glass that sheltered the gemstones.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wow, look at this black one, Mom! Isn't it pretty? I love it.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: It's quite pretty. I wish I could wear it as a necklace.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: If nothing else, it was good that Erina treated Isla as if they were in a normal visit, letting her feel comfortable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shortly, Katei finished with every cabinet.{w} They had all contained gemstones of different shapes and tones. Some also had a brief explanation below them, detailing where they'd been found along with the name of who'd found them. Most were discovered in the mountains I was used to seeing in the background of Yushibana.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Despite the events and my lack of interest, I spent some time looking at each one, immersing myself in them without noticing it. Everyone else did the same, drawn into Isla's rhythm briefly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you like this one?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shiroya was pointing at a tiny, light blue jewel with round white marks on its smooth surface. She'd said it because I'd been looking at it for a while, and she knew that shade of blue was my favorite color.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I really do. I wouldn't mind going to the mountains someday if I can manage to find one like this.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm sure it wouldn't be easy, but it'd be worth the effort.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: After talking about going back to our personal playground, I started to really look forward to the time where we'd visit it again, spending a day trying to find a gem as pretty as that one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Can I see it again, Tanya?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...Huh? Are you talking to me?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes! Can I see your pendant?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: A bit confused, Shiroya took it out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew it! It's even prettier than everything here!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...What's with that name, though?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Hm? Tanya? That's you! It's for tanzanite.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Oh, I see.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'll admit I'm a bit fascinated by these myself.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai's voice sounded from behind us as he peeked over my shoulder.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I came here of my own volition, after all. We shouldn't spend so much time doing this in the next rooms, though. We have other priorities.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes. Sorry, Isla, but once we're done, we'll have more than enough time to revisit every room.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hm. You'll still let me see them though, right?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Yeah. We'll briefly look over them.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We moved on to the next room, which looked almost identical.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The same procedure was repeated: Katei uncovered every cabinet, and Isla had a few seconds to appreciate all of their contents.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Undercurrent
After we finished with it, Akaro spoke.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do we really have to look at the inside of every cabinet? It's only slowing us down.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Yes. It doesn't take up a lot of time, and remember what Suripo said. He mentioned some gems on this floor had been stolen. We need to find that room and see if there's something to find there.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh, yes, that's true. He said it happened in one of the farther back rooms.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You're right... I'd forgotten about that, but it still sounds very weird to me. What do these gems have to do with anything? It sounded like Ashiya have already assumed those gems were the target, which feels off considering nobody even knows how they were brought outside.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You mean to say they were probably a measure to distract, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I agree. If this supposed theft is over or already failed, it could be that some kind of trick was used to get the gems outside and make Ashiya think they were the goal. Once their guard is lowered, steal the actual target: the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Yeah, something like that, even though I can't really visualize how the plan would work.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Before you assume that, there's something else to consider in opposition.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What would that be?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Well... the two side hallways and the event room were put out of commission with the smoke. If the gems were the goal, it could be assumed that the event room was, for some reason, only attacked because it's the only way to go from the middle of one hallway to the other.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: However, that has a flaw. Even though the smoke certainly disabled the security cameras, the room those gems were stolen from wasn't ever subjected to the smoke, according to what Katei told us.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's weird, don't you think? It outright implies that the room's security camera was never a factor they took into consideration. So, if that were the case, why did they disable all the others?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What I mean to say is that the robbery of those gems could've been executed without needing to release smoke in the event room, and the substance to cover the lenses of the security cameras wouldn't have been needed.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If being spotted by the security cameras in the room of the robbery wasn't an issue, it means the only other goal of the smoke was to provide a clear route to the outside. The event room and the opposite hallway wouldn't have been needed, and there would be no point in disabling the cameras. This immediately indicates that the gems were never the goal, which shatters any illusion with them.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Maybe you're right... If they were the goal, only one hallway and that very room would've been attacked.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And you also can't assume the smoke was released to make everyone nearby fall unconscious because not all the rooms where people could've been were attacked.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And yet those gems were brought outside in a suitcase before the exit closed...
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yeah, only for that person to then be arrested immediately. I can't quite figure out what the whole deal is here, especially given the Sekimeiya is still with us.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The people outside think the gems were the goal and that the robbery was a failure. However, part of that relies on them not knowing the exact rooms that were covered in the smoke.{w} I'm sure more people will conclude what I'm saying once they enter the tower. If the culprit intended to use those gems as a feint, this plan is lacking.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: There's no way it ends with someone sneaking the Sekimeiya out as soon as the exit opens, right? That would be beyond stupid. Not to mention that stealing the gems would be rendered useless since Ashiya would quickly notice that the Sekimeiya has been stolen too. Then, the gems would ultimately return to Ashiya, and the person who had them would be arrested.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I hadn't taken those gemstones into consideration for any of my thoughts, but he was right.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey, Katei. I know you brought this up earlier, but are you sure that the exit was sealed immediately after the alarm went off?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm... While it is the first time the alarm has been activated, it's how it was programmed to work. Anything else would be pointless, really.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Could it have been another malfunction? I was just thinking that Naomi might have brought the gems out.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Naomi? But that should be impossible, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Not if that malfunction actually occurred. When Suripo mentioned the person who brought them outside, he only said it had been an "individual". It could've been a woman, but I think he would've said it when we mentioned Naomi was still with us.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If the alarm's effects were delayed, Suripo would've brought it up, or someone from the outside would've entered. But it is true that Naomi, who's disappeared and knows the entire layout of the tower, is a pretty good candidate to take out a bunch of gems and play this silly role of purposely getting arrested with a conspicuous suitcase.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If that is what happened, targeting the event room too would make sense even if the goal was elsewhere. It was Naomi's location, and she would've needed a way to escape.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're... right. I hadn't thought of this, but I'm not convinced.{w} Targeting both hallways still wouldn't make much sense, and most importantly, it implies her plan only worked because the alarm's effects got delayed; it would've been no so-called malfunction.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yeah... Also, we still don't know what actually triggered the alarm, and while I could be wrong, it really seemed to me like Naomi did fall unconscious in our room.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm...{w} Remember what Suripo said? If anyone was in front of the shutter as it closed, it would've stopped. It's possible it was delayed, which gave Naomi enough time to leave even though she was in the event room when the alarm played.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's true, but Suripo would've told us as well.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Wait, no. I don't think that could've happened.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why not?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: When I heard the alarm, there was another sound too, much fainter. I just realized that must've been the shutter closing, because it was pretty rough and came from the lobby.{w} That means there was no delay, and there was a louder sound at the end when it hit the floor. I'm almost certain it went the whole time without stopping.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If that's true, it confirms Naomi's still here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yeah.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Is this a key?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I saw Shiroya staring at the floor, confused as to where to direct her gaze.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Oh, you're right. What's this doing here?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: When we went quiet, the two people who hadn't participated in the conversation spoke.{w} They were a bit ahead of us, so we walked up to them. After focusing on the point where they were staring, we saw what Isla had found. Next to the right wall was a small, rusty key.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla kneeled to pick it up. Once in her hands, she showed it to us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was this on the floor?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes... I just saw it.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: There's no way we've missed it until now, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The color is close to the floor's, and the lighting is bad. I'd say we did since it took me a few seconds to see it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Really? It was right next to the event room.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: More importantly, what's it for? Do you recognize it, Katei?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...No. I don't think I've ever seen this key before.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei grabbed it to give it a closer look. It appeared very old and rusty; it wasn't the kind of key that would be used in a modern building.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's impossible this belongs here. I know it's an old building and there are keys I don't possess, but it must be for something else.{w} Keys are not prohibited items in this tower. It's possible someone dropped it and didn't realize it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: How would you not notice it? If you drop it here, it would make a noise when it hit the floor.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: For sure. Which means that whoever dropped it knew they did and then didn't pick it back up.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It would have been a bit ridiculous to think that it had been left purposely to indirectly pass it on to someone or something of the sort. Given what we knew had happened so far, what Sai said made a lot of sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You get what I mean, right? This key probably belonged to the culprit.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: As they were running against a timer that would trap them, they dropped this key. Naturally, they didn't waste time stopping to retrieve it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It could be a pretty important key if it's one the culprit was holding as they were committing a crime.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'll keep it safe and give it to the police as soon as I can.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's a good idea.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You might be jumping to conclusions again, though. It could belong to an innocent person who rushed to escape from the tower.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You think so? I'm not sure that's possible. I've gone over this.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why would an innocent person ever rush to escape? One reason would be if they saw smoke appearing out of nowhere. However, they would've fallen unconscious if they ran through this hallway.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The other reason would be if they heard an unknown alarm, but this can also be ruled out because the alarm blocked off the exit. Naturally, this key doesn't belong to any of us, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Nobody answered.{w} He was saying that no innocent person aware of danger could've escaped through the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If the key didn't belong to the culprit, it had to belong to someone who'd also gotten trapped and we hadn't seen. Even Naomi didn't make sense as a candidate—I'd been with her up until the alarm had sounded.{w} If someone had fallen unconscious there, they could have dropped the key and failed to realize it upon waking up. Perhaps even the sound of it falling was obscured by the alarm, but I considered it unlikely.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I doubt this was here before the attack. There was a janitor cleaning the floor in the lobby, so I'm sure these hallways were cleaned today too.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...On the surface, that appeared to be a very solid argument, but there was a way around it, and it involved something I'd thought before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We didn't know for a fact the smoke in hallway A had been released at the same time as in the other two places. There was no reason to believe it hadn't been, but it also would've allowed one of Katei's claims be the truth.{w} One part of me wanted to directly ask Katei, but I held off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If someone had heard yells coming from the lobby or seen smoke coming through the door of the event room, they might've rushed out without stopping to retrieve their key...{w} I recalled that I'd heard only silence when we were about to fall unconscious.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I saw Isla in front of the next door. Even though she'd found a key, she didn't seem very interested. Inspecting the contents of every cabinet was probably far more exciting for her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's continue for now. If this was important for the culprit, it's likely they'll try to get it back, so I'll make sure to keep it safe until we get out.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We accepted that and moved on.{w} The next room was no different from the previous. Katei went ahead and began to make sure nothing had been stolen from its cabinets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai approached me while I was separated from the others. Anticipating his reason, I was first to speak.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you still doubt Katei? I think he did a good job of proving his sincerity.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, of course I do. I'll agree that he's pretty good at lying.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You already realized he was never in the security room, right? Why are you defending him?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I looked at Katei. He was putting up with Isla and acting interested in the gems he'd presumably seen hundreds of times.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you certain he wasn't?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: He couldn't have been there after the alarm went off. I checked the time needed for the computer to go to sleep, and that confirmed it. The only other possibility is that he was there and lied about using the computer, but that doesn't make it any better.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Have you considered that the computer time might not have been accurate?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The computer time?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes. If it was wrong, Katei could've had the time to be there without lying.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, and then lied about how much time he spent outside it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I know. Maybe you're right and there's no other explanation.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I have considered the computer time being wrong, and not only that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai raised his sleeve. Under it, there was a digital wristwatch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I always wear this. It doesn't seem like there are wall clocks anywhere, so the time displayed on the computer is the only source we have available.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Besides my wristwatch, that is. My time and the computer's are the same.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I see... So that can't be it either.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, as I said, I didn't consider that the computer time was wrong, but rather that someone went way further than that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh... I-I see what you mean. Yeah, that should be the only way out Katei has.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah. If someone messed with my wristwatch while I was unconscious, they could've made me falsely confirm the computer's time.{w} Someone could have done that to frame Katei.{w} It's too ridiculous to consider it seriously. They'd need to know that Katei would say everything he said only to turn around and disprove it with the computer's sleep mode, risking the possibility of nobody noticing it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And not only that, but it's also something that only works with the people who got trapped. This wouldn't mean anything if we brought it up outside.{w} And Katei, who didn't fall unconscious, would've said the time was wrong. It would be insane for him to create a problem for himself by changing my watch time.{w} He also let us talk to Suripo, who could've mentioned the time at any moment.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...But why would Katei lie about being in the security room? Do you actually think he's responsible?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Or heavily involved in some way. There's no way he's not hiding anything or looking to gain something.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So, you don't believe his story about how the Sekimeiya was found? You were accusing him of lying about that too.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, no. I do believe everything that he said there. It just gave him even more of a motive.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I still think the Sekimeiya has to be the core of all this. That has to be right.{w} Now, don't you find it strange that a simple security member would know all that?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He said it in a desperate time because he wanted to earn our trust, which is why he relied on factual truth to lessen our suspicion.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But what I think he did was change his own perspective. I'm telling you this in case you think I'm missing something, but I think all he did was merge his version with what Suripo told us to form an accurate story and pass it off as something Ashiya told him.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't follow.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm saying he could be the the guy who originally found the Sekimeiya. He didn't know about what Suripo told us beforehand. Otherwise, he would've said it all to earn our trust.{w} Once he knew about Suripo's factual story, he combined his own knowledge with it to make us believe he truly works in the tower.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The way he detailed some things was very questionable. He knew the exact location where the Sekimeiya was found, and everything he told us was information the person who found it would've known after hearing Suripo's story.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...That might be true, but it sounds like a pretty big assumption, and didn't he say the seller was already paid?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'll tell you one of the theories I formed. It's all speculation, yes, but I think it could make sense given whoever's behind this already went pretty far with all the smoke.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I haven't told you this since it might not mean anything. You and I both showed up early and were at the front of the line for a while, in front of the hallway B door.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Right. We didn't have a way to check the time, but we were definitely there for a few hours.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: All right. So at approximately {time=8}, I saw Katei in the lobby. The reason why I started questioning him so quickly was because when I first saw him, he was wearing normal clothes.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Of course, back then, I didn't think anything of it. I don't know what he did either. I just saw him for a few seconds, and I'm certain he was never actually in line.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Considering everything, I think this is one of the ways everything could've played out. Take whatever you want from it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The person claiming to be called Katei found the Sekimeiya a couple weeks ago. He contacted the Ashiya family, and given their interest, they bought it from him.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: At no point did he expect they'd set up so much advertisement for his own find. It's possible Ashiya said things that were wrong only to draw people in, and perhaps not being credited with the discovery bothered him.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's a pretty plain motive, but think about it. If you sold it to them and they started playing up its value like crazy, would you be happy about how little you were paid? The scale of this attack is a bit much for one normal person to come up with, but things line up here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Xyn isn't behind this, which is why it's happening during the day. He enters the tower at {time=8:00} this morning. He could have somehow met with the real Katei Kuiji and learned about the alarm and emergency contact line from him.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The way he learned that information isn't important. At the very least, I know the man with us right now wasn't in the lobby shortly after I saw him. What matters is that they met and he put on Katei's clothes. Then, he proceeded to hide Katei somewhere without cameras.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He could have done this any number of ways, but Katei was charged with keeping track of the security cameras, so obviously nobody would notice his body being hidden if he was the one who was supposed to watch everything.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Along with the clothes, he also took the security room key. Then, he released the smoke in the two hallways and event room through some method I'm unaware of. It's likely he knew he'd get trapped by doing so.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He acted as if he'd found us and played the role of a security member to justify his presence in the tower.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Naomi... It's possible he hid her body while she was unconscious. He'd have a good reason for it, because Naomi would've revealed that he doesn't work in the tower.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: By saying everything is confidential, he's managed to avoid explaining anything he doesn't know. He lied about spending any time in the security room since he'd been carrying out this plan of his. That's why he knew things only a person inside the room with all the monitors would've known without actually being there.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Suripo clearly told us that security staff would stay in the room and relay information through the installed microphone. But Katei told us that he left it because he didn't know about that before talking to Suripo. He said he used the microphone while we were unconscious, but I'm sure he was lying.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't know why he let us talk to the outside, but it's possible he had something to gain from that. Maybe he wanted everyone outside to think that Katei Kuiji really is in the tower and that everything here is going well.{w} Maybe he wanted to make sure the bait gemstones worked and tricked Ashiya. This is so messy that it almost feels unrelated to what he did, but that can't be it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Anyway, it all comes down to this: he had no way to get the Sekimeiya out without spending twelve hours here, so he's intentionally spending twelve hours here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't know how this plan ends. I have no idea how he intends to get the Sekimeiya out once the exit opens, but consider the following. If he manages to do it, nobody will miss him—none of us will know who he actually was. I'm only speculating that he originally found the Sekimeiya to give an easy explanation for all the knowledge he's had since the start.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Once he makes it out, only the Sekimeiya will be missing. Katei Kuiji will still be here, since he's where that guy talking to Isla right now hid him. This ghost of a person will have escaped with the real target.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...After saying it all out loud, I know it sounds pretty absurd, but whatever this plan is, it has to be far from over. There are a lot of things that don't make sense, and somehow, the Sekimeiya is still in its cabinet as if nothing happened.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Also, one last thing.{w} We only think that what we saw is the Sekimeiya because Katei told us so. The plan could already be further along. The real Sekimeiya could've been replaced while we were asleep.{w} That could be another reason why Naomi's presence had to be taken care of, as she would expose that illusion.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I'm done. What do you think? Do you agree with anything?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I was looking at the floor, and I'd been listening to everything expressionlessly. Katei remained engaged with Isla while her mother looked on from behind. Akaro and Shiroya were leaning against the wall, waiting to move on. Before I responded, we all walked to the next room, A4.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I waited for Katei and Isla to begin uncovering the cabinets before resuming the conversation with Sai.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: *sigh* I don't think I can directly object to anything you said...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Admittedly, I did think Sai's theory was a leap. It didn't have to be wrong, and I had come to a similar idea myself, but some of his assumptions were a bit of a reach. Despite Sai's fervor, I cared about what was going on as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no way it had been an accident. Many things indicated that nothing had happened coincidentally: the particular day, the smoke locations, the alarm, the recurring Xyn events, Naomi...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before anything else, there are two options to choose from. The plan failed, probably because of the new alarm, or the plan hasn't ended yet.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If whatever this plan is hasn't ended, it's almost certain that a culprit must be here with us.{w} Who would that be, and what do they intend to do next?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There weren't that many possibilities.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everything has pointed to Katei, and there are multiple ways to construct it. If he's really a security member, he probably would've had an easy time setting this up. If he's not, Sai's theory is valid too. He's definitely the most suspicious person here.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Unless I choose to doubt Sai, it's almost a guarantee that Katei lied about being in the security room during the attack. There could be many reasons behind the lie, though. If Katei is actually innocent, a similar plan could be adapted around anyone who got trapped.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Of course, I can rule myself and Shiroya out. We've come here innocently and never expected anything like this to happen. Shiroya and I have spent our entire lives together, and I know she'd never think of doing such a thing, not even with her being less than fond of Ashiya.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I myself don't suffer from memory loss or split personalities, nor do I have a particular interest in ruining my life after failing a robbery attempt.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Akaro was the last person in our group. Out of us seven, I feel he's the easiest person to suspect after Katei. He claimed not to care much about today's event but was here from the very beginning. Earlier, his behavior was clearly off, but it's gotten better since we woke up.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It could be that he's letting the time pass so that his plan can conclude. But since he stands out from the rest of us, he's an easy target to blame for a plan Sai and I have concocted.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The same could be said for Erina and Isla, even though it sounds less likely. It's too naïve to rule them out because of Isla's age. A well-constructed plan could take advantage of that to lower our guard.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Out of the six of us that were waiting for the event, only they have their early arrival justified... Isla's the only one who seemed to care about the event, but I can only truly rule out Shiroya and myself.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And Sai... I don't believe he's the culprit, but if he's even crazier than he seems, he could've designed the whole thing and then messed with me for entertainment, maybe even to prevent my suspicion and interference. He could be trying to manipulate me into thinking whatever is convenient for him.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I don't think that's likely, though. Similarly, he might've determined I'm not a likely suspect.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There are two more options: Naomi, and an unknown person.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If Naomi wants to wait until the exit opens to execute the last part of her plan, then hiding from us is probably a good idea. She's been hidden from the very beginning and will spend all the remaining time without being spotted, able to move by herself whenever she needs to. There's gotta be a good hiding spot somewhere in this huge building.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Using Naomi as the culprit helps explain the alarm triggering. Suripo said that the only way to activate it was by breaking open the Sekimeiya cabinet, and when I heard the alarm, Naomi was the one next to it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If she silently "broke" it in a way she knew would work and then faked being unconscious, she could've covertly trapped us. Then, when we looked at the cabinet, we failed to recognize what had triggered the mechanism.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Why would she do that? Could she have wanted to make it look like it was a malfunction, so anything else could be a malfunction too? The fact that the alarm went off right after Naomi unlocked the cabinet with her key also leads me to think that the source of the alarm had to be something else.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: However, this also could have been done purposely to make the three of us confirm that by the time the alarm was set off, there was no reason to force the cabinet open. After all, there's no way Naomi could've known I'd stay conscious for enough time to hear the alarm.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But if Naomi is innocent, is there more than one option behind her disappearance? Unless she woke up ahead of time and saw the culprit, the only person with a clear motive would've been Katei. She could still be trapped and walking around, but I'm not sure why she wouldn't have shown herself already if she has nothing to do with the attack...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Is it actually possible Naomi is currently outside the tower? This would mean that the alarm had a delayed effect and Naomi's not innocent at all. I'm pretty sure what I heard in the event room was the shutter, but I can't be totally certain.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The only way she could be outside is if Naomi is a culprit. Otherwise, Suripo surely would've said that she was outside when we brought up her name. The only way this wouldn't have happened is if Naomi was the "individual" with the suitcase whose identity was kept a secret.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The "unknown person" option is basically the same, but better. After all, with Naomi, we'd know the identity of the culprit by the end. If an unknown person has stayed with us and somehow plans to sneak out with the Sekimeiya when the time comes, we'll have no way to know who they were.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The lobby doesn't have security cameras. When everyone evacuated, someone hid behind the reception desk or entered the staircase to the mechanical room. Once the smoke faded, they hid in a better place, maybe after moving Naomi's body. Maybe they were in one of the rooms in a hallway, and that's why they made sure we couldn't look at the recorded footage.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Once this is all listed out, there are a few extra options, like two people working together. If Naomi and Katei were in cahoots, one would cover what doesn't make sense if the other person is working alone.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The two staff members could have easily designed an internal attack thanks to the knowledge they possess. Katei made us think the Sekimeiya we saw was the real deal. Now, Naomi can do as she pleases since she'll be constantly covered by Katei, who will guide all of us as the most knowledgeable person here.{w} ...Perhaps that's unlikely since he had no problem staying behind in the security room while we went to investigate.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Surprisingly, the conclusion I drew was that if the plan was still being carried out, Sai's theory was close to what I believed to be likely.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We had to know what triggered the alarm. It would clear up multiple doubts and remove possibilities such as the person responsible already escaping.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe what you said is the most likely possibility. A lot of things point to Katei being suspicious, and he knew about the alarm from the start. That could mean that he's the most likely person to be carrying out a plan that involves waiting for the alarm's timer.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Yes, I agree.{w} Either him or Naomi, but with the scenario I constructed, Naomi's already taken care of. Most things are, actually. I don't know how the smoke was released, what triggered the alarm, and how Katei plans to disappear with the Sekimeiya. It's also good to note that regardless of the method, a member of security staff like him could easily design a way to release the smoke.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It'd be wise to keep track of him at all times. He stayed alone earlier, and in the security room of all places. I'm very curious to know how he intends to make this plan work. He'll probably make sure that we don't come across Naomi or the body of the real Katei, if I'm also right about that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You seem pretty excited.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: A bit. Aren't you?{w} Aren't you looking forward to knowing which theory ends up being the correct one? Or maybe to find out that we were both incorrect. What if this is all bigger than we think, or just a coincidental accident?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I want to make a lot of theories and then have the best one turn out to be right. That would be great.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: For example, think about this. Everything we've thought about has been in part based on the call with Suripo. However, our main assumption right now is that Katei is responsible for all this.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You brought up a good point earlier when you asked why Katei said we could communicate with the outside. You're right. If he's a security member while also being the culprit, he'd look incredibly bad to the police if he never told us about it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But if I'm right and he doesn't work here, it wasn't very smart of him to bring it up voluntarily.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're saying that Suripo was an accomplice, and they planned what to tell us?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Exactly. ...He spoke very highly of Xyn.{w} What if he was speaking very highly of himself? The group he works for, alongside Katei?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He had a police uniform and was in a car next to the tower, ignored by everyone around it. If it was a real video feed, he's an actual policeman. Wouldn't things make sense if Xyn was involved with the police?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That program hidden deep within the computer's folders could've been another factor of this plan designed by Xyn. They knew Ashiya were working on a mechanism to defeat them, so they created this plan to keep their superiority. Assuming part of what he told us was the truth.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: As soon as he began to explain things, my suspicions about Katei immediately lessened. After all, what that policeman was saying matched up well with the information Katei gave us. Now, if they were working together, made-up details would appear like the absolute truth, and they'd make all of Katei's subsequent claims sound authentic.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Suripo mainly spoke to Katei. If they were following a script, they could pretty easily deceive us. Suripo is the only reliable source we think we have.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And after he was done, the power conveniently went out. Not only that, but Katei was unable to contact him again. How believable is that, really? Did the Ashiya family really revoke his authority, knowing they'd leave us incommunicado for twelve hours?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wouldn't it be exciting if we were in the middle of such a plan? Would you stop Xyn if you saw through everything?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I'm not excited about being caught up in this, I can say that much. But if I get the chance to take these guys down, I absolutely would. I won't let them get away with this... this shit.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see.{w} Me, I'm just curious. I can't wait to know how this plan ends. Sadly, there's still a while until that. Maybe they need these twelve hours for something... Suripo corroborated the amount of time Katei said, so it would be strange if it turned out to be wrong.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We'll have to see what happens.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I suppose so, but if this is an ongoing plan, they won't make it obvious. If they're trying to trick the Ashiya family, we might get tricked too. I'm just not going to get fooled so easily.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Hm.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I didn't feel like saying anything else. A part of me thought that everything Sai was saying entailed pointless danger. I related to the interest, but not so much to his approach.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In our situation, there was no reason for us to be in danger. It was something between Ashiya and Xyn, and we'd just been caught up in the middle of it. Letting everything happen without giving our own input to strangers seemed like the smarter course of action.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, trying to piece things together on the side probably wouldn't do any harm.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Although I hadn't reacted, what Sai said was intriguing. I'd let Suripo influence my thoughts with no opposition, but it was true that Katei had been the one who'd let us hear him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The first thing he'd said was that Ashiya instructed the police to talk to us, but he'd never proven that at all. It hadn't sounded all that strange, but instead of telling the police what to let us know, Ashiya could've said everything directly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Suripo also said that Ashiya told them about the communication method. Initially, the other side should've been picked up by Ashiya, who'd supposedly passed it off to the police...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While there was room for suspicion, thinking that he was an actual corrupt policeman was probably incorrect. If he had fed us false information, he would be exposed after we got out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could feel my head getting cloudy. The tiredness was coming back, so I tried to cool off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The room's inspection finished without anything missing. Once again, we silently moved on to the next one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After not talking for two weeks, my voice had easily come out in front of Sai. As I'd thought, it was only Shiroya who I had difficulty talking to.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At the same time, the incident had given me something else to think about after so long. It was likely I was trying to fill up my mind with it, as I knew what would fill it otherwise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Isla didn't look tired of repeating the same procedure. She ran to the door, eagerly awaiting Katei.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd noticed that every room had a specific theme. Before leaving, I'd glanced at the cabinets and seen a bunch of unimpressive white gemstones, much smaller in size than the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Labeled A5, the last crystal room in the hallway was left before the storeroom. When Isla turned the knob, we expected to be met with the same scene as the other rooms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The entire room was tinted black, and it was shaped differently. The ceiling and four walls had been deprived of their color, as a dry, dark coating had taken hold of them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every cabinet was covered by a curtain, but instead of bright red, they were gray, black, and purple, colors that removed all of their elegance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was the same appearance the hallways bore. We immediately understood the smoke had also gotten into the last room.{w} We only found it a shocking sight because of what Katei previously told us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see. This makes a lot of sense.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What does? Didn't Katei say that the smoke hadn't been released in any other room?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Instead of clarifying, Sai moved forward. He stained his hand black by grabbing the bottom of a curtain, and without any care, he raised it to show us the interior of the cabinet it was covering.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...? There isn't anything...
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: He did the same with every cabinet, and the result never differed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see, this is the room that was robbed. The gems found in the suitcase came from these cabinets.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes, that has to be it. But the smoke...
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You all remember what I said earlier, right?{w} That this part of the plan didn't make a ton of sense. The gems were stolen without releasing smoke in their room, which implied that the smoke had another purpose.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But it seems the smoke was released in this room too. Of course, that's required if they wanted to make it seem like those various gems were the target.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The lens of the single camera was stained black, showing that we weren't being recorded. The green light had been buried under the same blackness, but it was still discernible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei told us the places where the smoke was released. Obviously, he wouldn't have said that if he hadn't been sure of it, so I believed him.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm sorry. I must've made a mistake.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No. I have no idea why you did that, but this settles it: this proves you were not in the security room when the alarm went off.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai glanced at me to let me know that he'd been correct. I was probably the only person aside from Katei who knew what he was talking about.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What do you mean...?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Exactly! What are you talking about?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You didn't even suspect it? This is about the fifth thing that confirms it, but this one lets me bring it up openly. After all, it also rules out a few things I talked about with Atsuki.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I more or less understood why Sai said that. Without inspecting every room, Katei felt confident in saying that only three different places had been hit with the smoke, but he'd been incorrect.{w} That indicated he hadn't been behind the attack itself, since he wouldn't have made that mistake. It let Sai confront him since he no longer believed he was confronting Xyn, but a mere suspicious individual.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know what you mean... How does this indicate in any way that I wasn't in the security room?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It's very simple, but let me ask first: why did you say that only the hallways and the event room had smoke released in them?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I had a bit of time to inspect these rooms before I found Erina's group. Every room I entered was clean, so I simply assumed it was the case with all of them. I shouldn't have made such an assumption.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: All right. This proves it further. You were not in the security room.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You all get it too, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei has said multiple times that during the time the smoke was released, he was locked inside the security room. He also claimed that he tried to monitor what the situation was on this floor by looking through the available cameras.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Not only that, but he also said that he saw the smoke rising out of nowhere. I'm saying that if he really was looking through the cameras when the smoke appeared, he would've seen it being released here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What? No. I was in a rush, so I never realized it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I don't understand it at all. You were never in the security room and you never inspected the first floor. So then, why did you say that only three places had been hit by the smoke? Why were you certain you could say that, despite being wrong?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That was the same question I'd been wondering. If Sai was right, Katei wouldn't have stated incorrect information he hadn't been able to verify, which meant that he felt certain about the room's appearance without personally seeing it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Your assumption is mistaken. I can explain what led to that assertion.{w} When I was in the security room, most of the cameras from this floor were being displayed. It is true that I saw the smoke appearing out of nowhere, but at that time, this room's camera was not being shown. Usually, monitoring the interior of a room isn't needed if another camera shows its door.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then, I proceeded to look through all the other cameras while trying to determine what was happening. As you saw with your own eyes, some of them had been disabled; because of the smoke, a black screen was all that I could see through them.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So, all that this room's camera showed was a black screen. This means that I was unable to recognize that one of the disabled screens belonged to this room.{w} Since both hallways possess numerous cameras, I did not notice there were one too many black screens. Later, since I looked into most of the clean rooms, I wrongly assumed that they all were the same.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hm.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We all thought about it. Did what Katei said make sense? If I'd been in their places, it's likely I would've believed it, but Sai and I had more reasons to think Katei had never been in the security room and that he was fabricating another lie out of nowhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you really sure about this, Sai?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Absolutely.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Now answer me this. At first, you saw the smoke being released through some cameras. To assess the situation, you looked at all the remaining places on this floor, and this room wasn't initially being displayed.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Correct. That is why I never saw the smoke appearing here.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: All right. So then you switched the displayed cameras. This means that at some point, you switched one of the cameras for this room's. You're seriously saying that when you did that, you didn't realize the smoke had also been released here?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh, I see what you mean. That eventually, I must've chosen to observe the live footage of this room by manually selecting its camera and I would've noticed the black screen.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Yes.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's understandable you'd think that, but no. That would've been slow and suboptimal given the situation. Do you remember earlier, when I looked through the cameras while talking to Suripo?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The program that manages them lets me replace the nine cameras being displayed at once for the ones that come next on the list. That's what I did.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I was nervous and switched the cameras nine at a time. I never consciously acknowledged that one of the new cameras belonged to this room. As I already said, I simply failed to recognize that there was an extra black screen. The crystal rooms all look very similar, so I didn't really miss this one.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The shape of this one is completely different, though.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: To tell you the truth, it all threw me off. The mere sight of the screens displaying nothing but black was disconcerting because they're equipped with night vision and I'd never seen them like that. I wasn't really thinking about the number of crystal rooms.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei's explanation was unconvincing, but there was nothing Sai could use to object to it. At least, not without the computer's sleep mode timer, which Sai didn't appear to be using for his argument.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei hadn't addressed the event room either. If he'd seen the smoke appearing in the event room, it should've been a given that our group had been trapped in the tower, but that wasn't what he said when we met.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was unbelievable that the event room wouldn't have been displayed on such a special day. If it really hadn't been, it meant that Katei hadn't failed to notice one extra black camera, but two. And it was still very questionable that he had stopped at Erina's group before ours.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everyone else looked dubious as well, but less so, as they hadn't yet entertained that possibility.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Not for a second do I believe anything that you're saying.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I apologize for not being more convincing. I understand why you might find what I'm telling you strange, but I promise all of you that I'm telling the truth.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So, you switched all the cameras at once and, for some reason, assumed only three places had been exposed to the smoke.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes. I saw the smoke appearing in the hallways, which disabled multiple cameras. I mistakenly assumed all of them belonged to the hallways.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: And after that, despite not having looked through every room, you claimed that the smoke hadn't been released anywhere else but in the three places we'd all personally observed.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Correct. I apologize for my mistake. It seems it led you to suspect something about me, but I repeat that it was all a mistake I made in a rush.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Let me be clear: I don't believe you nor intend to do so. You are full of shit. However, I don't know why you told us that only those three places had been hit, and it's pissing me off.{w} Do you remember when you said you'd left the lobby door open? Like Atsuki pointed out, it was opened after the smoke was released since almost none went through it. Still saying that's true?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes, of course.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, when you said that, I looked at the hallway A door. That one was properly closed.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...And?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: According to you, after you left the security room, you ended up where we were without going through the event room. If you'd done that, you would've gone through the lobby, so you should've opened both doors.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Which is what I did.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: And why did you leave the hallway A door closed but not the other one?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Because the three of you were unconscious in hallway B, and I hurried to kneel beside you.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sure, I imagined you'd say that. However, if you really opened that door, what I find most likely is that you didn't come from the security room and that you never went through the other one. Maybe it was Naomi who opened it and you had to say you did it because of the movements you'd already claimed you made.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're ridiculous.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Okay, but if you'd never looked at the cameras or entered the rooms, why the hell did you say something that could easily be wrong...? Were you misinformed about the plan you took part in? That's what would be ridiculous.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: *sigh* I already told you what happened. If you find it hard to believe, there's nothing else I can do.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: There were a few seconds of silence during which nobody knew what to say. In the background, Isla ignored us and kept looking through the cabinets, hoping something had been left behind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina followed everything she did with her eyes, obviously unwilling to needlessly engage in the barrage Sai was firing off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You know... It's possible you're right. It's possible that not noticing the extra black screen and the missing crystal room is too unlikely. Even under the stress of not knowing what was happening.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What if this room was clean at that time? It has already been a long time since I looked through the cameras. The smoke could've been released here afterward.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: This wouldn't contradict anything, and it might make even more sense than what I first believed.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Quick lie revision? Are we supposed to listen to that?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well, I don't know why that would've been done, but you can't deny it just because you find it unlikely.{w} It could very well be that it happened after I left the security room. The rooms all look very similar, so maybe I did see this one when I looked through the cameras. Now I'm not sure. I don't know which of the two possibilities I'm presenting is the correct one.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You know very well they're both incorrect. But yes, I can deny the second one.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: How would you do that?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It has to do with something very important. Normally, I would've brought it up straight away.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It makes this whole situation much easier to understand. Remember the two questions from earlier? Why were the gemstones stolen, and how were they brought outside before the alarm went off?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm fairly sure the answers are, respectively, to make it seem like they were the goal of the attack, and because they were stolen before the time we thought.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I mean, the curtains here were lowered when we entered. Most importantly, they were stained with the smoke.{w} This means that during the time the smoke was released, the cabinets were covered.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If someone stole the contents of these cabinets when the smoke was being released, as the Ashiya family thinks right now, why would they have lowered the curtains again? No way they would've all fallen down by themselves.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You all see what I'm saying, right? It would have been a pointless waste of time to lower them. After the smoke was released in this room, the curtains weren't moved.{w} To put it simply, the gemstones that were once here were stolen before the smoke was released. This is why someone was able to bring them outside before the exit closed.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I suppose that makes sense, but how did they do that?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You tell me. What's important is that they could've been stolen during the night. Then, before the exit closed, they were brought out.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: By releasing the smoke here too, they tried to make it look like the gems were stolen at a later time and that they were the actual target of the theft.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What you're saying makes sense, but I still have a hard time visualizing how this plan works.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Me too. A very important thing we don't know yet is whether the alarm was taken into consideration. You said it was a top-secret alarm, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes. I believe it's nearly impossible that Xyn designed a plan with it in mind.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: If so, that means the smoke here couldn't have been released after you left the security room. That would only have been done if they already knew the exit was getting locked down.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I believe you're right. If they didn't know about the alarm, they would not have staggered the smoke in this room. It would've been released everywhere at once.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Exactly.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Can I say something? We're only assuming the gems here were stolen before the time of the attack because the curtains were down. That makes sense, but wouldn't they have thought of it?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's true. If Xyn didn't know about the alarm, they must've expected Ashiya to rush in right away. They would only have seen these curtains, not that the gems were missing.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah. After all, they only believe these random gems were the target because they don't have access to the tower. Isn't it as if the alarm is working positively for the culprit?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yeah... There's no way Xyn would've ignored the curtains giving away the timing of the theft, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Not if they didn't know about the alarm. If they did, and the intent was to simply let Ashiya think what they think until the tower unlocks, it doesn't matter that we've figured it out. After all, it's not like we can contact the outside to tell them, is it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're wrong. Then they would've had no reason to release the smoke here.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Hm, I'm not sure. We did have the chance to talk to the police, but it happened before we came here.{w} I'm saying this was done to trick Ashiya into thinking the gems were the goal. However, I also think that the plan must somehow end by stealing the Sekimeiya, which will directly reveal that the gems were never the goal. It could definitely be that the smoke was released to trick us—the people who got trapped. It all depends on whether someone is trying to trick us.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: There were a few seconds of silence. Would Xyn have put so much effort into deceiving us? It didn't sound likely, but it was true that we had a method to contact the outside and could've informed Ashiya of every suspicious detail we'd noticed. It was strange, because if the culprit had always been able to disable the communication method, there would have been no point in doing any of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Do you actually believe the alarm was considered?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Who knows? If the gems were stolen during the night through some method Xyn are capable of, they'd leave the curtains lowered to prevent it from being noticed through the cameras and so that the visitors couldn't see them before {time=9:10.}
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I wasn't the guard on duty last night, so I can't help you with that.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...{w}Well, they were forced to leave the cabinets covered, but doing so also indicates that the gems were stolen before the doors were open to the public...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: *sigh*
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't know why. I've approached it from different angles, but I can't come up with something that makes sense.{w} In some way, these gems must've only been a side part of the plan. Them getting stolen before the smoke was released is close to confirmation, but how everything pieces together is not as simple to figure out.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I apologize that I can't be of more help. I assume this is Xyn's doing, but I don't know what they intend to do. I am equally clueless when it comes to how these gems could've been stolen before this morning.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai, I know you don't believe much of what I say, but I have been honest from the beginning. I have just been trying to help and provide you with as much information as I can.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Is that so?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: While everyone stood still, Sai began to examine the room. Even though it looked drastically different from the others, only the illumination and shape varied. It was still a simple room that only contained cabinets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't think there's much to do here. Every cabinet is empty, and the same kind of smoke was released, most likely at the same time as in the other places. We should move on.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Yeah. Let's get going.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Isla seemed happy with that proposition as well. We all agreed and left quietly to avoid any more conflict.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Only the storeroom remained in hallway A. We tried to enter it together, but it was too narrow for all of us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was a stretched-out, dim room. While the name implied that its purpose was to store things, the amount of space didn't allow for much of that, and it only contained a few empty shelves and a dusty couch that looked dangerous to sit in. Even the door was lower quality than the rest.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I exited the room as Akaro and Erina entered it. Sai seemed to be enjoying himself, considering different options in an attempt to "win".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If we parted from the assumption that there was a plan more complex than met the eye, I had something to consider.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We had all assumed that the gems were stolen before the smoke was released since the curtains had been lowered. If anyone stole the gems after the attack, there was no reason to waste their time lowering the curtains again.{w} However, that was a very simple indicator of the time the gems had been stolen, and one that would not have been overlooked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, what if the curtains had been lowered again precisely for that reason? To make us, or anyone who looked at it, think that they had been stolen before the time of the attack. After all, anything else would've been a huge mistake.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't think of an immediate benefit, but deliberately misleading us about the time or reason behind an action was a potent move. That effect wouldn't have been achieved if the tower had really been robbed at night and the curtains were left down. {w} ...And realistically, even though Xyn could've been involved, how could they have emptied so many cabinets during the night? Hadn't the police been nearby? Hadn't the cameras been monitoring everything?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before I could determine if there was a better conclusion to reach, everyone left the storeroom, Katei returning last.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We didn't all have to enter. There isn't anywhere to hide in here.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What's this room even for? It's called the storeroom, but there isn't much inside, and I doubt it'd be much use with how small it is.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Things have been stored here before, but it's true that now it looks like a useless room. I heard that this room already existed before this building started to be used for business, and it was too small to give it any other purpose.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The door didn't look that different from the others. However, once you opened it, the room would detract from the aesthetic the place usually had. I figured that when the building was repurposed, they replaced the door but left the inside unchanged.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...So we're halfway done with this floor. Maybe we'll find something in hallway B.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: To get there, we stepped into hallway C for the first time, which contained the stairs and elevator to move through the different floors.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's this...?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Something immediately caught our attention.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's a suitcase, Katei.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Yes. What is it doing here?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We all approached it. Just like he said, a small and conspicuous black suitcase was lying in the middle of the hallway, next to the wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's see... There might be something inside.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai went ahead and unclasped it. He opened it up on the floor and exposed its interior.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nothing...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's disappointing, but I suppose otherwise they wouldn't have left it here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Did you see this when you looked through the security cameras?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Erina looked at Katei. The cameras in hallway C hadn't been touched, so Katei should've been able to look through them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He didn't.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Right. I would've told you if I had.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see. Does that mean that it was left after we woke up?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No, of course not. Did you not hear anything I said? He never looked through the cameras.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're still going with that? I guess you'll never change your mind.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I understand you can't say that you saw this suitcase since it'd be suspicious you hadn't told us, but you should give up on the lie. It's kind of pathetic.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If you really didn't see this, it would mean that someone was here after or right before we woke up. It's not impossible, but I don't find it more likely than you lying.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei looked at us. He was asking if we all thought the same, and no replies were heard.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Look at where the cameras are positioned. A bit of smoke covered them, but not enough to block the image completely.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: One encompasses the bathrooms, and the other records the staircase and elevator. This middle section isn't shown at all. Even if the suitcase was here, I wouldn't have seen it. That's why none of us saw it earlier when we briefly looked through the monitors.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I figured you'd say that, but it's only an excuse. If you actually inspected this floor, there's no way you never came across it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I inspected part of this floor and didn't see it. Not because I didn't come here, but because it wasn't here yet.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see. It's a shame the recorded footage just so happened to stop being accessible.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're right, that's unfortunate. It'd be an easy way to prove myself.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai and Isla continued examining the suitcase, but they didn't find anything. No smaller compartments appeared to exist, so it was actually empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Look. I can see traces of the smoke.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh, right. There's no way it was hit directly, though.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah. Perhaps it made contact with it before it had fully faded. I'm not sure.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why was it left here, then? If it happened after you looked around, it's a big red flag telling us that someone else is still here.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: But we already know that. It must've been Naomi.{w} After she did something, she must've wanted to get rid of this and didn't care about leaving it here. It makes sense that she would have disabled the security system before dropping it.
entries.speaker: k
