entries.text: That's stupid. Footage is still being recorded, so I doubt she'd care whether we saw her or not. Especially given that leaving the suitcase after we woke up tells us she's here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...The culprit must've wanted to get rid of the suitcase as soon as possible since it's linked to the robbery attempt. Suripo did tell us an "individual" was found outside with a black suitcase, so being seen with one wouldn't be desirable.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If Katei is telling the truth, it means that whoever left it here could've only been Naomi or an unknown culprit. ...There's technically another possibility, but it's too ridiculous to consider it seriously.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When we went to the mechanical room, you all stayed together, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: For better or worse, Sai had been thinking the same.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes. Nobody left the security room.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You want to suspect us this openly? Did you two get separated at all when you left?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: N-Now that you mention it, yes.{w} I went to the mechanical room while Atsuki said he would inspect the rest of this floor.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wh-What?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It was a strange sensation, seeing everyone turn to me while I silently waited for Sai to retract what he said.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...He's messing with you.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Probably. We didn't get separated.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You aren't being funny.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, I'm just surprised you don't find us suspicious.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why would we? Even though you left, that's not enough of a reason.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Ah, no. That's not what I meant. I think you have a good reason to suspect us.{w} Don't you remember when we got back? We said we'd gone to the bathroom, didn't we?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Did you? I didn't hear you from under the desk.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I bet you regret not accusing us first, then.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Did we go to the bathroom and miss this suitcase? It could be Katei was right and it wasn't here yet.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Don't take him seriously. We didn't go.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Of course. Katei wouldn't really tell the truth, would he? Admittedly, we were a bit late, so we agreed we'd say that so we weren't suspected of anything.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We never came here, but I knew we should've. Didn't I tell you?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So you accuse me of lying and immediately admit to lying yourself. Your arguments keep falling apart.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...We don't really have a way to know when this was left here, but I'd say it's likely it wasn't one of us. It must've been left by the people behind the attack.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Right, and most likely before we woke up. There could be a reason why they had to leave it here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Like what?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No clue. I'm only saying that because the smoke wasn't released here. Even though this exact spot isn't recorded, whoever left the suitcase must've been seen by one of these two cameras.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If you wanted to dispose of something incriminating, I'd say you'd do it in a place without cameras, and there are many.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's true. If it was put here after Katei inspected this floor, whoever did it is back to hiding.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Which is why we should keep investigating. Let's finish checking the crystal floor and move up.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The bathrooms were empty, so we were ready to move on. Regarding the suitcase, we weren't sure what to think, but we didn't take it with us.{w} The location where it had been discarded was the only information we had to work with. I didn't want to think too deeply into every detail, but something came to mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It could be that Katei was right this time. The location someone chose to leave the suitcase was one we hadn't yet been in.{w} If the culprit left it there before we woke up, I can't think of a reason why they wouldn't have left it in one of the two main hallways. After all, the plan only involved them and the event room at a glance. At no point was it necessary to enter hallway C, which has security cameras.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I felt someone might've been nearby and had known we hadn't yet been in hallway C. They'd chosen it so that we couldn't be sure it hadn't been there the whole time. If they'd known we couldn't access the saved footage anymore, they could've tricked us. If they'd left it in one of the two parallel hallways instead, we would've immediately known it wasn't there before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In addition, that spot wasn't in range of any of the cameras, so we couldn't have seen it while we'd been in the security room.{w} ...But the trick wouldn't work on Katei, who'd already inspected the area.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, there was a plethora of reasons to believe he was lying. The culprit could've known that Katei had never been in hallway C, and unaware he had lied about it, placed the suitcase to trick him as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There weren't many better places to do that. It was true that upper floors existed, but according to Katei, they weren't open to the public. No matter the way I thought about it, it was baffling that it hadn't been left in a room without cameras like the storeroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I thought about it as we entered hallway B, and an ominous feeling hit me. If I was right, someone else trapped there was still very close to us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We walked to the first room, which had a sign stuck on its door. When we removed the smoke dust on it, we saw an image of a mop and a bucket.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As you see, the cleaning cart is left here when it's not in use, alongside cleaning products and items.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yeah, there's probably nothing of importance here. It's not a big room.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Akaro was the first to step inside and glance around. As he'd said, the room was small and only served the obvious purpose of storing cleaning materials. After stepping in and out, we all agreed and silently moved on to the crystal rooms in hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We had the first one in front—B6. Once Katei and Isla made sure nothing was off, we moved to the next door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is the staff room, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes. Visitors are not supposed to go in, but it's not locked.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So we can't go in?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Don't worry. It's fine under the circumstances.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei opened the door. Behind it, we saw another small room, different than all the others we'd been in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every staff member has their own space here. We use it to leave and pick up personal objects, and it's where we store our uniforms before heading off.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see. So the belongings of some employees are still in these lockers.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Isla soon stopped looking interested, but for the rest of us, it was the most notable room yet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes, but everyone tends to lock them.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Let's see if any are open.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not sure we should. We might get in trouble.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: You kidding me? There could be a phone or something in here. I'd call that incredibly useful.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: As I said, they're not usually left open. You can check if you want.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai went ahead and tried to open every locker.{w} Shortly, we confirmed that Katei was right: they were all locked tight.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You have your own locker, right? Do you keep anything that could be useful in it?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No. They do allow us to bring phones in as long as we keep them here, but I never bring mine. Right now, the only thing in my locker should be my coat.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Can we see it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You want to see my coat?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Partly yes, but I also want to see the lack of other things.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Do you still think I'm lying? Very well, it's good that this is something I can easily prove.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei took a few keys out of his pocket. One of them was the one he'd used to unlock the security room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He inserted a small one into a locker and turned it. Without a problem, he opened the door and showed us what was inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We could only see a coat, but Katei went ahead and brought it out to show that nothing else was hidden behind it. He went as far as to show us every empty pocket.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You see? I understand it's easy to suspect me, but I've only been telling the truth.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: One truth doesn't make up for all the previous lies. Certainly, if the contents of your locker were harmful to you, you would've claimed not to have any.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I really can't make you happy. Do you have more requests that would prove my sincerity?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No, not really.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei put the coat back inside and locked it up again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All the lockers were very tall and had an extra smaller compartment in their upper part. Three horizontal bars could be seen in the metallic doors, slits that allowed us to somewhat see the interior of those smaller compartments. However, I couldn't spot anything of importance, as the darkness concealed what was in them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everyone was listening closely to the conversations between Katei and Sai. Sai had continually reiterated that Katei was openly lying to us, so it was no surprise that they wanted to form their own thoughts.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai knew nothing would be found inside the locker, so I suspect he wanted to see that coat. If it was the same one he'd seen Katei wearing in the lobby, it could back up his identity.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Since he didn't react to it, it's fair to assume it was the same one, but it doesn't settle anything. One extra step of his impersonation plan could've involved changing the locker's contents while we were unconscious.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Could there be a way to force open the lockers? One of them must be Naomi's, so it'd be interesting to look inside it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What? No, please don't think about that. There are no tools to do it with, the lockers are quite sturdy, and I'm sure Ashiya would not be happy about it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Similarly, I'm not happy with spending twelve boring hours here without getting to conclusions. Right now, Naomi is very suspicious.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And what if she is? What do you think you'll find inside her locker? I'm letting you overstep a little. You shouldn't be allowed in this room, but I will not be giving you free reign. Please, get this idea out of your head.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'll keep thinking whatever I want, but I agree. It'd probably be a worthless hassle. If Naomi is the culprit, she must know how suspicious she is, so she wouldn't have left anything relevant in her locker.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...That's what I'm saying.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Isla tugged at Erina's clothes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's go. There's nothing in here...
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: We kept moving at a good pace until we had searched through the remaining five crystal rooms in hallway B. They all looked the same, and nothing felt out of place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is it. We knew that if someone was hiding, it wouldn't be easy to find them.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah. It's already past {time=10.} One more person is confirmed to be with us, so if she hasn't appeared yet, she must not intend to show herself.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Sai and I considered that Naomi's body might've been hidden. If that's what happened, it's likely no one else is hiding. The main point that indicates otherwise is the suitcase, but if Katei lied about it, he could be the one who hid Naomi.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: We'll have to move up, then. We might find something on the higher floors.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Our priority should be to understand the structure of this place and find Naomi. We'll have many hours to go after that, which won't make it easy for anyone to stay hidden.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We approached the hallway C staircase.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Only employees ever go to the other floors. The structure of this building is like this...
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Right now, we are on the crystal floor. The five floors above us are offices, and they were empty during the attack.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Why are there so many offices?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: When the structure of the building was first expanded, it served the purpose of containing many offices that worked for Ashiya. This was before they thought of using the lowest floor as a sort of museum.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That was the case for a while, until the perception people had of this place shifted to what it is now: the single remaining entity of Ashiya in Yushibana and a tourist attraction point.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Nowadays, not many people who work in the offices remain, and they closed entirely just this December. Ashiya doesn't make much use of them anymore, so they might disappear and be reworked eventually.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The seventh floor is the Ashiya floor, also called the attic. I explained that one earlier.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Can we go in there?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: There's no way. As I said, I've never entered it, and only a handful of people who remain here have. Ashiya are very fond of it since it's where they once lived, or at least that's what they claim. Regardless of the reason, they want to preserve it well.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: How would we go about getting in?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Like most places, you enter with a key. One that I don't have.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei pointed his finger up the stairs, where a door prevented us from making it all the way up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I have the key for this one since it only keeps us from accessing the offices.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He walked up and inserted another key of his in the keyhole. As he'd already done twice, he turned it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Unlike previously, however, the door didn't appear to smoothly unlock.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What? It's not letting me.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hold on.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai stepped up to him, twisted the knob, and pushed the door forward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was open.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: O-Oh... That's strange. Sometimes this door is left open, but it's weird that it was now. Nobody has worked upstairs for two weeks.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It's not really strange. Naomi also had the key, right? It just means that she probably opened it or someone did with her key. If it was you, you're not very good at remembering whether you locked a door.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'll ask one more time so you guys understand it better. Katei, you did not see anyone when you looked through the security cameras, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Correct.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then, once again, that's strange. It's very likely someone unlocked this door and went through it. If they wanted to hide from us, they wouldn't have done so on this floor, meaning that it's likely they went up some floors before we woke up and while you were allegedly in the security room.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You won't stop trying to find ways to frame me, will you?{w} You're wrong. They would've known I was inside the security room and must've only gone up when they saw I'd left it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei was right. Sai's thoughts operated under the assumption that Katei hadn't been in the room, so he hadn't considered that simple angle.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, let's go up. I bet the person we're searching for is currently above us.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We began to climb up the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Can't we take the elevator? There's a lot of stairs to get to the top, right?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: The elevator...? I'm not sure that'd be appropriate.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: We all slowly stepped down. We had entirely ignored the elevator.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There shouldn't be an issue.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The elevator door was fully metallic, so we weren't able to see the inside without opening it. Next to it was the button to call it with, and nowhere did it indicate whether it was being used or on which floor it was situated.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei called it quietly. Many seconds later, the button lit up for a second, indicating that the elevator had arrived. Then, Katei opened the door, exposing an empty and narrow interior.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't on this floor... It took a while, so it must've been pretty high up.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That doesn't mean anything, does it? It could've been up before today's event even started.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You're right. Katei, do you happen to know where the elevator should've been?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Not at all. I didn't have the night shift, and I didn't see it being used.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It'd be good to know when it last moved.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Doesn't this elevator bypass the door in the middle of the staircase?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, it does.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then what's the point of locking it...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I just said that it's not unusual for it to be left unlocked. In the past, when the offices were actively used, measures were stricter. Since nothing ever happened, everyone started to be more lenient, often leaving the door unlocked.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: A similar change occurred to the elevator. Look inside.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We all peeked in. What Katei was referring to was above the floor buttons.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Keyholes? Do you need a key to make the elevator move?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: In the past, you needed the same key that opens the door to reach floors 2 to 6 from here. That regulation was removed since the door was continuously left open and there were some complaints about it being pointless.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: However, this other keyhole is still mandatory. To reach floor 7—the attic—a special key is needed. The same key opens the door that leads up to it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So that's the only floor we can't get to at all.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Right.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Isla hopped into the elevator by herself, causing Erina to gasp slightly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is interesting, actually.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What is?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, whoever went up to hide from us used the door instead of the elevator.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're right. They wouldn't have needed to.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I don't think so, at least. If it's true that it should've been locked, by leaving it unlocked, they're telling us they possess the key.{w} Naomi wouldn't do that purposely because it makes her suspicious. It's possible someone who's not a staff member unlocked the door.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I see what you mean. There could've been a reason why they didn't use the elevator instead.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: For example?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well, if the elevator wasn't on this floor, and the culprit knew it while they were in a hurry, they would've gone through the door instead of waiting for the elevator to arrive.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I suppose so.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's a bit strange they didn't lock the door behind them, but there's any number of reasons for that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm. This should help us visualize this person's movements a bit more.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are we going to go up?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Don't be impatient. We can't all go up at once.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: With Katei keeping the door open, I was able to see why he'd said that. Inside the elevator was a sign indicating the number of people that could board it before the weight could prove a problem.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Only four of us can be inside at once. It's a fairly old elevator.{w} The stairs really aren't so bad, so let's walk up.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No! I wanna use the elevator.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...We hadn't yet had an issue with Isla's behavior, so we didn't want something so trivial to put an end to that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sweetie, come on. We can't demand things like this.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I wanna use the elevator... If not, I can just stay on this floor and go back to the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: It's fine. We've already spent a while investigating, and it's getting old. Let's move it along.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If someone's hiding from us and we want to find them, we won't accomplish it if we stay together. The culprit has an elevator, stairs, and knowledge of the layout. Much like on this floor, they could easily avoid us.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: To speed it up and increase our chances of finding them, let's split into two groups.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Weren't you against that earlier?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm fine with it depending on the groups. Isla and Erina will take the elevator up to the sixth floor. As long as Atsuki and Shiroya go up with them, it should be all right.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why us?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: To isolate the least suspicious people, of course. A problem with splitting up would be if someone could take advantage of it before we're able to thoroughly inspect this building. Katei, Akaro, and I will start with floor 2 and progress upward until we meet you guys again.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Okay!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Is that a good idea...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Any reason why it's a bad one?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's fine by me, but we don't have to do it like this. We could use the elevator twice or simply take it to the second floor.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I looked at everyone else, and their reactions indicated indifference toward Sai's arrangement. It was true that it'd increase our speed and chances of finding the culprit, and as long as Isla's whim was satisfied, she wouldn't complain.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All right, let's go.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai went up the stairs and quickly disappeared from my field of vision. Akaro and Katei followed him, and I held the door Katei had kept open until then.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Let's go too.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Isla went in first, followed by her mother. After Shiroya had entered, I boarded it last and closed the door behind us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This isn't exactly spacious. I'm surprised it's supposed to support four people.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: In the cramped space, Shiroya moved her finger up to the floor 6 button. Admittedly, she was right, since Isla didn't occupy the space of an adult and ended up buried in the back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As soon as the button was pressed, the translucent secondary doors closed, and we slowly began to rise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {w=0.6}The elevator didn't shake at all, so we only knew we were moving because of the screechy noise the ropes above us were making.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {w=0.6}They were a quiet few seconds, and since the doors to the other floors were fully opaque, they were also dim. I felt a vague sense of claustrophobia for the first time since we had awakened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {w=0.6}Once the elevator slowed down and we were allowed to leave, I opened the door that would lead us to an unknown place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Line Art
{w=0.6}We stepped out and looked around us. A long hallway composed of calm colors extended far ahead.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Is this really the same building?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Compared to what we'd seen downstairs, it was far more pleasant. We even felt a slight cold breeze that alleviated some of the tension we'd been accumulating.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: More bathrooms?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Since people used to work here, there might be two on every floor.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Outside the elevator, we found ourselves in a wide corridor that only contained a few potted plants. At our right were the bathrooms and the staircase that led to floor 5.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I suppose we should look around.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The other three entered their bathroom while I stepped into the men's by myself. Like the one on the crystal floor, it was spacious, but only contained a sink with a mirror, a garbage bin, and a toilet. It was immediately evident that I was the only person inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Although a potentially dangerous culprit might've been hiding from us, I loosened up a little. The thought of looking through those huge floors without restriction released some strain from my body, which allowed me to think about needs that had disappeared from my mind, like using the bathroom for its intended purpose.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Outside, I found the others waiting for me behind the door, and we went ahead to see if anything of importance awaited us nearby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We turned left past the large hallway and were met with a narrower path whose left wall was made of glass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's this?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: These must be the offices. I can only see desks and computers.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shiroya felt the handle and realized that the door wasn't locked. She easily pushed it open without making a sound and let us pass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's another door in the back. This floor is as big as the first one, so it must have a bunch of these to fill the space.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Isla walked up to the far door and opened it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It looks the same.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: We glanced through it and saw a replica of the room. It looked identical down to the last object, with the same arrangement of desks and computers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's another door there.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We approached it. Although the first wall was made of glass, the next two partitions were separated by plastic that heavily obscured the other side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {w=0.6}Through the door, we were able to see that, once again, the third section looked exactly like the first two. The exception was the lack of a door leading to a fourth.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though the initial concept of inspecting a huge building had sounded somewhat involved, the layout made it a trivial task.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's nothing here either.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Let's look around a bit. I doubt it, but we might find something.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah. Let's see.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We dispersed ourselves throughout the three large partitions, and I was left with the third one. The desks all had drawers, but upon further inspection, they didn't contain anything relevant to us. The only thing of note was that each desk contained a computer tower inside its lower, larger compartment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I returned to the second partition.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There are even cameras here?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, I saw them. They do look a bit out of place.{w} No idea what they're so paranoid about.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm not sure these would help them much.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Maybe it was to make sure the workers here didn't slack off.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Even though it had sounded like a joke, I understood she hadn't intended it as one. After all, in the second and third partitions, you couldn't be seen from outside. The wall covered the partitions' sides, and a cloudy white one kept them from seeing each other. It was a pretty cramped place, and I couldn't imagine myself working calmly with that camera pointed at me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wasn't sure what the jobs there entailed, but judging from the number of computers, a large amount of people must've worked at once. Adding the fact that five similar floors were supposed to exist, it felt a bit excessive.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped into the first partition to see Erina and Isla looking at a lit screen. Upon noticing me, they were first to speak.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I powered on this computer, but it's taking a while to boot up.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: On the screen, I could see a progress bar that was nearly finished. I briefly worried that Ashiya would review the footage of us using the computers, but it wasn't like we were doing anything illicit.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Soon, Shiroya came from the middle partition and the four of us stared at the same screen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Found anything?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No, and I don't imagine we will.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see. I haven't either.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Isla was mimicking what she'd seen Shiroya do, opening and closing the drawers. She appeared visibly sad when the last one still contained only pens and papers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, look. I doubt we'll be able to access anything.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: On the screen were two text boxes demanding a username and a password. Without them, we wouldn't be able to look at anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's unfortunate.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Just in case, I tried inputting common default information, but nothing yielded a positive result.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, these won't be any use.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I gave up and straightened myself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's keep going. The lower floors will probably be the same, so we'll go through them faster.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The stairs leading to floor 5 were next to the elevator, but let's see what's on the other side first.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We walked out, Isla holding the door for us. Shiroya gave her a charming smile and helped her before Erina exited.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As soon as we turned left, we were met with something I'd seen from behind the glass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's that for?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Oh, right, I forgot about these.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Two big windows were in the wall, but as we'd been told, a shutter prevented us from seeing through them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, they're the windows. These are the same kind of shutter as the one in the lobby.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Isla made a thinking sound. I also hadn't thought of the windows, and since they were barely visible from the first partition, their purpose must not have been to relax the workers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I remember seeing them from outside.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Yes, they should be facing the front of the tower. We'd normally be able to see most of Yushibana from here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I knew it.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Isla approached the shutters with her hand and felt them a bit. They seemed properly sturdy.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm not sure this would be the most viable escape route for a criminal. We're on the sixth floor, so to escape through here, you'd definitely need special help.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yeah. They took no risks this time.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Hm. It would be tough, but even this window could serve as an exit with a proper plan.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Isla, who had been acting as if she were at home, left us behind and went to explore what looked to be another corridor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After understanding that nothing was to be done with the windows, we moved along too.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A narrower path was on the other side of the floor. However, it didn't appear to lead anywhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is it a dead end?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Oh.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Isla turned around when she realized it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As nothing else was left to be inspected, we walked back and returned to the initial hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I guess this was floor 6. Let's see if anything's different on the others.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We came to the conclusion that it's very likely the culprit is here, so this layout makes things easy for us.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We arrived on floor 5 in silence. It looked very similar to the sixth, and it had the same bathrooms at our right.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We looked at them while making sure nobody could sneak past us and go a floor up. At first glance, the floor appeared to have the same structure as the previous.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I inspected one of the plants just to be safe.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The soil in these is actually really shallow. I don't think anyone could hide something in here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The pots themselves weren't hollow, either. Nobody could hide anything underneath them. I didn't think anyone had, but in case there was still something else going on, I wanted to have my bases covered.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't actually tell if the plants were fake or not.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I visualized the layout of the floors in my head as I considered how unlikely it actually was for someone to be hiding in them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After walking farther into it, it was clear that it was almost identical.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is every floor exactly like this?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: They probably are, but we'll have to look at them to be sure.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Why is this place so big?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Come on, Isla. You're bothering Shiroya and Atsuki. We need to keep moving.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: As long as someone stays in the first partition and can look through the glass, we can make sure nobody moves between the floors unseen.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Right. One person always needs to stay out of the last two.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: All right.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Since we'd seen no stairs going down, I walked to the other side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, that's what I figured. The stairs to the fourth floor are here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I walked back as the others entered the first partition. Once again, the four of us found ourselves in a room full of desks and computers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I've been trying not to think about it, but what if there's someone in one of the next two rooms? What do we plan to do?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We went quiet for a bit.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She's right. We've been going about this with a light-hearted attitude, but things can change drastically in an instant.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: We don't know what we're up against, but the truth of the matter is that we're in a dangerous situation. Maybe we should just stay put.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Without Sai around, that sounded a lot smarter. Erina'd been playing along with us, but she was almost definitely afraid something could happen to Isla.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I doubt they'd want to hurt us, but without Akaro, our only physical advantage is that there are four of us. ...Although I guess if someone's hiding, nothing guarantees it's only one person.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: As our perspective on the situation shifted over a single comment, I slowly moved toward the door in front of me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though those walls weren't transparent, they let light through. If someone were right next to them, we'd see a fuzzy outline of them. Slightly tense, I placed my hand on the handle and slowly opened the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I don't see anybody. I'll check the last one.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya kept the door open so that my voice could still reach the first partition. I grabbed the next handle and pushed the door forward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's empty too.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I loosened my grip and walked back to the others. It seemed nobody had been on floor 5 either.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Should we also look around here?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: We probably won't find anything, but I think we should.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I agree. We're not only looking for people. In the instance that the culprit wanted to get rid of something like they probably did with the suitcase, they wouldn't have had many places to do so.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's true. The crystal floor has a simple layout, but these are even worse. If you wanted to hide something here, you'd only have these drawers.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: That's what I mean. Someone was likely here since that door at the stairs was unlocked, so let's see if we can find something.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Isla took that as her cue to start opening all the drawers. Again, I went to the third partition while Shiroya stayed in the middle one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Opening every drawer was all I could do. There wasn't anything under the desks that could hide something, and the floor had nothing on it but cables.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In less than two minutes, I could be sure that nothing of importance existed in that section of floor 5. I left it to find Shiroya nearly done with hers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nothing, I imagine?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah. I looked at some of these papers, but I don't think they have anything to tell us. Some were financial reports, but others I didn't understand at all.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's about what I saw on the other floor. I tried not to look at them too much since a camera was right behind me.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, yeah. They'll probably look through the footage to make sure nothing strange happened.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She apologized, facing the camera, before opening the door to the first partition. ...She might have been doing better than I thought, gradually moving back to her usual persona. I smiled at her and went through the door she'd opened, calmed by the thought that my worries about her had been overblown.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you done? We didn't find anything.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Neither did we.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We can move on, then. If the other group went at the same pace, we should find them on the next floor.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: We were about to leave when a sound alerted me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A vanishingly faint but deep noise that lasted almost two seconds was very slightly audible from where we were. Two of us visibly reacted at the reminder that our situation was uncertain, and hearing it after moving through two harmless floors amplified its effect.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla, however, appeared unfazed. Perhaps ignorance was bliss, but it seemed like she had no concerns whatsoever.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You guys heard that, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Hm? I didn't hear anything.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I-I'm not sure I did. What was it?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I don't know, but I heard it too. It was quiet, but I think it came from this floor.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya and Erina looked a bit unnerved and focused their hearing in case something else made a noise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It must've been the others.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I opened the door. I wanted the initial inspection to finally end, to permanently release the stress I'd been building up at the concept of someone hiding.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I realized Erina and Shiroya were coming along. We only had two directions to choose, and I hadn't made out the origin of the sound. However, since the right path led to floor 6, it was fair to assume it had come from the left.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina quickly checked the right hallway and indicated that she hadn't seen anything. As I reached the end of the glass through which Isla was watching me, I peeked into the next corridor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I don't see anything.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya looked too and saw the completely empty path.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It might've come from floor 4.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Possibly. I couldn't tell.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We entered the first partition again, where Isla was calmly sitting on a rotating chair and staring at our distressed faces.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do we keep going...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yes. We need to ask the others what that sound was.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: All of us felt it appropriate to exhale. However, Isla disagreed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You don't need to look so worried. Nothing bad will happen.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...I would always have imagined I'd be the one saying that in a time like this...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Believe me. There's no reason to be scared.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Any particular reason you're saying that?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm... I know nothing will happen. We just need to wait until we can leave.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Shiroya stared at her skeptically. She knew optimism was great when it hadn't failed you yet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're probably right. We only got caught up in an inconvenient situation.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yeah. We'll be back home in just a few hours, so let's go back down already.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: If nothing else, her playful smile made it clear that she was aware she was being unreasonable with that last part. Her high spirits were genuinely impressive.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I'm being serious. We don't need to search for any hidden person. There's no one here.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: We're searching precisely to know that for sure.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm already telling you. These floors are a lot more boring than the crystal floor, so we don't need to waste our time like this.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: "Waste our time"... If I had intended to take her seriously, I couldn't have helped but laugh.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So you know the result of a search that hasn't finished?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: *sigh*
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya's and Erina's expressions told me that arguing would lead us nowhere.{w} But I was stubborn and slightly curious about her attitude.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How can you possibly know that?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Because I was told!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...{w}My brain processed that line as another thoughtless remark she had made up to justify what she was saying. Only after a few seconds of silence did I fully comprehend it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What do you mean? ...Who told you?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: My friend.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Not again... Don't take her seriously. She's been acting like this lately.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What do you mean? Maybe she's a bit careless, but she's a kid. I don't think it's anything strange.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I don't just mean the lies. Her behavior has been changing recently...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: In what way?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Isla, who was right there, responded with a disgruntled look.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well... I've talked to her a bit about this. I don't know why, but a few weeks ago she started talking about this friend of hers.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Again, Isla exhaled in a sad manner, as if she were being ridiculed unfairly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She just doesn't wanna believe me, but I know I'm right. I only tried to make you feel better...
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: What kind of friend do you mean? Who are they?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I can't tell you that. It's our secret.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: See, this is what she says. Recently, she started constantly referencing this intangible friend of hers. At first, I was happy to hear her talking about a friend since the teachers at her school usually tell me that she's more on the lonely side. She never really talked about her friends until now.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: But she made it sound as if she was always with them and kept telling me things that she'd been told. I knew she made it all up because I never saw her with anyone, and the things she'd presumably been told were all things that she'd said before or things I already felt she would say.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: "We watched my favorite movie together, and it was her favorite too!" and "She went to the aquarium last month, just like us!" You see what I mean?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: So she's a girl too?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes. That's the only thing we agreed we could say.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I'd probably be taking it better if it was the only thing that changed, but she also started to behave differently in other ways. She stopped listening to what I told her to do, spent less time with me, and one day I found out that she hadn't gone to school because she "didn't feel like it". I really don't know what's gotten into her.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: An imaginary friend at her age isn't too strange, but it makes me feel a bit uncomfortable, especially if it comes with so many more changes.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...Why won't you believe me? She is real, I keep telling you...
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I don't think you need to do anything about it, do you? Let her have fun with her friend.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So she told you that everything would be fine and that we'd make it out safely, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I believe you. There's nothing wrong with what you're saying.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Thank you, Tanya.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: So, how is she handling this? Did she like the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Isla looked confused, as if she'd been betrayed by the first person who'd accepted her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No, of course not... She's not here, right?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: O-Oh, no, I suppose not.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She told me that we would make it out safely before we came to the tower.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: What are you trying to say...? What exactly did she tell you?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You shouldn't listen to her. Don't you see this isn't something to take seriously? I've tried it, but it's pointless.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Hm... She told me that something would happen in the tower, but not to worry. She said that if we stayed calm in one place, nobody would be hurt. And she promised I'd be able to see and touch the Sekimeiya, so she was right, wasn't she?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...{w}Before answering, I kept trying to make sense of such a confusing bunch of words. I was starting to think that her story could be seen in a completely different way—a much more ominous one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You never lied like this until a month ago. What happened?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Do you mind telling us details about this person? How old is she, for example?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I won't tell you anything. That's what we promised...
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Erina, you said she's an honest kid. Do you think there's a chance she's telling the truth?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I understand you'd think that, but no. I'm sure that she's lying. She always makes it sound as if her friend lives with us, but of course, I know that's not possible. We live alone.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Isla, we're talking about a human person, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. Animals can't talk.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: R-Right. You got me there.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She was clearly unhappy with our reactions, but we had no other way to respond to what she was saying. Obviously, no friend would appear out of nowhere and start living with you. If that was what Isla claimed, then I agreed with Erina's conclusion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, what did she tell you about today's incident? Any more details?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why would I tell you if you won't believe me? She couldn't come, so she said that even though she didn't know how it would end or how long we'd stay here for, she'd wait for me at home.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: She didn't know how it would end? What does that mean? And why couldn't she come?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She can't see the future. She was right about a lot of stuff, so I trusted her. And today, she couldn't come here because I was supposed to.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: You were supposed to? What does that even mean?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I was supposed to come here, right? We planned this since the Sekimeiya was announced, and I was really excited, so you even let me skip today's classes. If she had come, you would've seen her, so that's why she couldn't.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: All right, then. I apologize for putting a damper on your fun.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Don't worry about that. What matters is that nobody else is here. We don't really need to keep searching.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Is that something your friend mentioned? Did she tell you the people who would get trapped?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Maybe. I'm not really sure if I should tell you, but she didn't say a lot about it.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: It might be helpful, so we'd appreciate it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well... She didn't tell me the names of everyone, but she did say that only seven people would get trapped, and that if we kept calm, nothing bad would happen.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Seven people? But Naomi must also be here.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Hm... She wanted to be helpful, so she told me as much as she could. She said it'd be me, Mom, three boys, and two girls. ...And that they wouldn't be bad people.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Come on, Isla. How can you possibly explain her knowing that?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: She's very smart. A lot smarter than me. But she was wrong here, so I think I might not be remembering right...
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Yeah. According to her, three men and four women would end up trapped. As things are right now, it's four men and three women, not counting Naomi.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's true, see? If she was wrong about this, she might've been wrong when she said that nobody else would get trapped.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: But, no... That's not right. I might be wrong about the number of boys and girls, but I'm sure she said that only seven people would stay.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Listen, we can't stop searching because of what someone told you before we came here. She couldn't have known anything. Don't you get it?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...But she was right. We ended up trapped, and it's seven of us. She even said that all the windows would lock down.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I'm very confused about this. Are you just making this up for fun? Because only a very select number of people would've known about the alarm's existence. If she really said that, could it be that your friend works here?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, that's impossible. I won't say anything else or I might put her in danger... You can believe what I said if you want.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Standing up from the chair, Isla reached for the door and left. Despite all she'd said, we still saw leaving her alone as dangerous, so we followed her toward the fourth floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell was all of that?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There really are only two options. Either Isla is lying, or someone who knew the attack would happen has been in contact with her.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I'm not sure I want to believe her, but I think it's much more likely that the first option is correct. Creating an imaginary friend and making up all sorts of lies and excuses to justify their existence isn't the most uncommon behavior.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But some things she said are really strange...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If she was trying to justify her friend's existence, why would she purposely list out the number of men and women incorrectly? And given how likely it is for Naomi to still be here, why would she claim otherwise? Wouldn't finding Naomi disprove her friend?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If someone told Isla about the alarm, they had to work here. We've been told multiple times that very few people knew about it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I guess another possibility is that Xyn found out about the alarm and its features. Isla did say that her friend doesn't work here.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Now the big question: why would Xyn make contact with Isla and tell her all that? What's there to gain, and why Isla?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There's no way her friend lives with them like she said. That would mean that Xyn instructed her to lie about her friend's identity so that the actual person couldn't be found.{w} But why the hell would they let her speak about it at all instead of telling her to keep fully quiet?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Isla told us that she promised her friend not to reveal information about her, but it doesn't seem like they agreed not to reveal information about today's incident.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I have no idea what anyone would have to gain by telling Isla about any of this, but if their intention was to manipulate her actions in some way, there has to be a very important reason...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: One last thing is that Isla's friend didn't know how things would end. This appears to back up Sai's theory: the plan isn't over yet.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: However, she also said that she didn't know how long we'd stay here for.{w} Twelve hours is the maximum time... Is it possible that depending on how some events play out, we could leave earlier?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Incidentally, her friend told her that everything would be fine if we stayed put somewhere. Could it be that Xyn doesn't want us to search around the building?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I'm not sure how I should be handling this. It doesn't seem as if she was instructed to tell us any of this. She just mentioned it out of honest concern after seeing how worried we were. If none of her actions were coerced and she was only given details, I can't think of a single reason why Xyn would do something so pointlessly risky.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If her friend is an actual person who knew this incident would occur, it follows that they knew she would end up involved in it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Since I can't think of why Xyn would do it, the smallest thing I can construct has, once again, Katei as the focus.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The only things Isla revealed about her friend's identity were her gender and the fact that she doesn't work in this building. I've been thinking of Katei as the core suspect, so it's easy to pin him as the identity behind Isla's friend.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If he instructed Isla to make sure not to reveal his identity, she would've called her friend a girl, and the one thing she would've denied would've been them working in the tower.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I'm not sure how much credit I should give Isla or if I'm going off too many branches, but even though she's a kid, she should surely be able to bring things up without making it evident she'd been waiting for a good moment.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I have no idea what any of this accomplishes, but since only some Ashiya workers should've known about the alarm's existence, only they or an attacker with inside information could've been in contact with Isla.{w} Reasons aside, an Ashiya employee could have been relaying information to her. Two happen to come to mind, one being a man, and the other a woman.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: In the end, though, I went back to thinking that the most likely possibility was that Isla had made everything up. Maybe she had randomly thought of mentioning the number of men and women but purposely said them incorrectly as an unusual thing there would've been no reason to make up. Maybe she'd intended to say it the right way but quickly realized that she miscounted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The whole thing really messed with me, and I kept trying to make sense of it as we reached the fourth floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It appeared desolate as soon as we arrived. The chances of finding people increased with each floor, so with a bit of precaution, we moved toward the offices.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is the other group not here yet?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: The first partition looked empty. Once again, we saw the same layout as the other floors.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe they found something. I'd think they would've already arrived here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I repeated the earlier process and quickly deemed the three partitions empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next were the two bathrooms. However, before we headed to them, I thought I noticed another sound, just as faint as the last.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was easy to pinpoint its origin. I peeked into the right corridor and saw two human figures standing next to the staircase.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They're here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Our attention was quickly diverted. The other three with me quickly spotted them as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where's Katei?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: As Isla pointed out, only Sai and Akaro were there. As soon as they noticed us, they stopped talking and gestured at us to come over.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How did things go? Anything notable?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Nothing. Are the other two floors like this one?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Exactly the same. They only contain three big rooms full of offices.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Where did Katei go? Why is he not with you?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, it's not the easiest thing to explain.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Sure it is. Naomi showed up and requested to talk to him privately.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Huh? Where was she?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What...? Naomi shouldn't be here.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: It's time to stop, Isla. Don't keep going when it's clear you were wrong.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Why shouldn't she be here? We were about to move up to this floor when Naomi came from the second. I'm positive she came from the stairs.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: From the stairs? Shouldn't you guys have inspected floor 2?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We did. It's very possible she was on the crystal floor since there was no place to hide on the second one.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: And she voluntarily appeared to talk to Katei?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Pretty much. It looked like she wanted to talk to Akaro first, but as soon as she saw Katei, she forgot about him.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Well, she approached me first because I was closer to the stairs. Then they went down to talk.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Yeah. We finished up floor 3 and have been waiting here since we looked at the two bathrooms. They left about fifteen minutes ago.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Did you not try to follow them? What did they want to talk about?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Naomi went ahead and asked us not to follow them, so unfortunately, I had to abandon my plan of tagging along. Realistically, if they made sure they were alone, we couldn't have done anything to eavesdrop without being noticed. The quarters here are pretty tight.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It sounded like they wanted to talk about "confidential" matters. When I first saw Naomi, I got really surprised, but she must've been even more than me. She looked preoccupied and determined at the same time—that's how she was when insisted that Katei talk with her privately.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I see...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We were debating the contents of their discussion just now. I gave Akaro the rundown regarding Katei, and he really hadn't considered anything.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I still think you're overthinking a few things, but I can't deny they're the two most suspicious people. Sai really thinks they're up to no good.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Am I being unreasonable? If I was wrong, they would've told us the main gist of it. Naomi might not have been with us the whole time, but she must've been conscious of the situation and our perception of her. Despite that, she barely acknowledged us.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm still trying to process everything. So Naomi really was here. Doesn't that mean the most likely scenario is that she was the one to leave the suitcase downstairs?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. She might not have been aware of how wary we were of her and openly showed up to talk with the other main suspect. Katei didn't look like he was expecting it, so perhaps he thought she should've remained hidden. Regardless, it's safe to assume they're now talking about their plan.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You should trust them a bit more... Since the two of them work here, I think it's very possible they're talking about Ashiya matters.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Okay, then why did Naomi hide from us? Why did she appear out of nowhere and not even try to explain anything? Her actions are strange even if she's on the culprit's side, but her face wasn't the one of someone who suddenly got trapped and looked for people for an entire hour.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Her perspective might be different from ours, being an Ashiya employee that's aware of Xyn's attacks.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: And I acknowledge that possibility. Her actions simply make it unlikely.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We'll have to wait for them to come back. I'm sure they'll clarify all of this.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yeah. We decided to stay here to make sure they couldn't escape, but we were also waiting for you four.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If there are more than two of us, we can split ourselves through the first three floors while someone stays here to make sure they're confined below.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Wouldn't they be able to use the elevator?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, but we would know. I meant to ask you guys about that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: A few minutes ago, after Katei and Naomi left, we heard the elevator moving through our floor. Even though we were next to it, we weren't able to determine the direction it was going.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But since you took it to the sixth floor, it could only have been going down. We only heard it once.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Oh, so that was the elevator.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That made sense. It had been a deep noise that had lingered for a bit. Since it was moving, the exact position and floor it had come from hadn't been easily distinguishable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I thought, none of you used it. That's strange, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We're sure it was the elevator because it made the same noise we heard when you used it on the lowest floor. Even if you'd decided to go back down for some reason, we found it appropriate to stay here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you sure it only moved one more time?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, we were right next to it and only heard it once. So if Katei and Naomi use it, we'll know.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We could even call it and keep the door open. That way, they wouldn't be able to use it at all.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Right, that's what I thought you'd suggest.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I stayed here for another reason too, which is why we didn't call it here and do that immediately. The sound might make it possible to anticipate the elevator. We might be quick enough to press the button before it goes past us. That would trap them inside it, and we could open the door before they could start moving again.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I see.{w} The sound from earlier doesn't make much sense, though. We left the elevator on floor 6 and heard it moving on floor 5. Like you said, it could only have been going down.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, I don't get it. By floor 5, we knew nobody could've been above us.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Is it possible someone sneaked past you while you investigated? If all of you were inside the offices without looking through the glass, it could've happened.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I really don't think so. I stayed in front for the most part, and I really doubt I missed anyone.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Well, if you didn't, then someone below us could've called it, and what we heard was the empty elevator.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Huh? It must've been either Katei or Naomi, so if you didn't hear it again, they must've called it and then not used it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Right. Maybe they wanted it easily available on floor 1 if they needed to use it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We began to hear footsteps in the distance. We all quieted down at the same time, straining to check if we'd imagined it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They didn't stop. The sound became more and more perceptible until it was clear that only one pair of legs was approaching.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's see what's up.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We stared at the staircase, where the sound was coming from, until Katei's white hair peeked from below.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When he saw all of us, he looked up with a plain expression and stopped moving partway up the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where's Naomi?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...{w}We went to the crystal floor, but she didn't want to come back.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Why not?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai's immediate reaction threw Katei off, and he took a few seconds to answer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: During that time, he looked at the rest of us. It might've been just my impression, but it felt like he particularly fixed his eyes on me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She didn't explain it. I asked her to come since I knew I'd be suspicious otherwise, but she refused. She left the room where we were, and I stayed there a few more minutes, sorting my thoughts out before returning here.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What did you talk about?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: About the incident, of course. It surprised me a bit, but her intention was to clear her name. She told me she hadn't done anything.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That was what she wanted to talk to you about privately?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes. I didn't believe her, though.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...You didn't?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No. Her words sounded forced, as if she was trying to cover herself up with lies. I know you've been suspecting me, but since I know I'm innocent, my main suspicions were directed to Naomi from the beginning.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: She saw her explanations weren't working and refused to appear before you all. She must've tried her luck with me because we've worked together for a long time.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So you're the only one she wanted to convince?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes. I don't know why, though. Even if she'd achieved that, it's not like she could've convinced the police. Hearing her justifications made me even more convinced that she's involved in some way.{w} Even though she ran away, I didn't try to find her immediately since I figured there was no way she could keep hiding. She still has to be somewhere on the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Out of curiosity, did you ever call the elevator?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The elevator? No. Why?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We heard it moving down, so if it wasn't you, Naomi might've called it. It didn't go up again, though.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I see... So she's definitely still under us.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Regardless, what did Naomi tell you? What was it that made you suspect her even harder?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}She spat out nothing but inconsistencies.{w} She said that she'd been trying to find help since waking up. She couldn't answer why she'd gone up to the office floors instead of aiding Erina's group or staying with everyone in the event room.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: She tried to make me believe that she'd been searching for people until now and that, coincidentally, she hadn't found us yet. There was no way I could have believed that.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: According to her, she had nothing to do with the power outage or the suitcase. She said she didn't see the suitcase the first time she went up, but it was there when she came back down.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...I assume you didn't find anyone, naturally.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Right.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Then that has to settle it. If nobody else is here, only she could've left the suitcase in hallway C. She almost broke down as she thought of more ways to explain herself. You'll see when we find her.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: By the way, when the elevator moved, couldn't it have been the higher group?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Us? No. We didn't use it again.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Is that so? And you didn't get separated?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Again, he said that while looking directly at me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...No. We stayed together until now.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Are you sure?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Why are you being so insistent? Do you have a reason to think we split up?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, no, I don't think so. Forgive me, Atsuki.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What the hell was up with him? That had sounded like a taunt without feeling like one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: His behavior toward me had changed in some way. I didn't know the reason, but it felt like he was trying to incite me to say something.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm sure they didn't split up. The four of them came from floor 5, and nobody could've gone past us while we were investigating floors 2 and 3.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...All right, then.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: As if we were all conspiring against him, he turned around and stopped moving. I was a bit puzzled, trying to understand how to interpret his new attitude.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, we will always be able to check the security footage once that's fixed. For now, we should make sure to find Naomi, I'd say.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Implying one more time that there was more to our actions than we'd let on, he breathed slowly and started to go back down without turning around.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Someone should stay here in case Naomi tries to go up. The rest of us will split downstairs to make sure she's found.{w} Another person will also be needed to stay on floor 2 to make sure she doesn't intend to pointlessly go hide there. Three will be enough to inspect the whole first floor. One person will stay in the lobby, the other in hallway C, and the last person will check every room in both hallways. She will not escape.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The person at the lobby will look through hallway B, and the one at hallway C will look through hallway A. This time, Naomi won't be able to cross between hallways. Let's go. I'll stay in the lobby and check the mechanical room.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...All right. That doesn't sound bad to me.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'll look through the rooms. I think I should be the one to do that.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Isla and I will stay here since only four people are needed. We'll keep watch at the elevator.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No! I'll look through the rooms too!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Be a bit cooperative, Isla. I think staying here would be better for everyone.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: As if she hadn't heard her mother, Isla ran down the stairs. Instead of trying to convince her, the others thought it better to follow behind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya, Sai, and I were the ones without an assigned position, which left us unaware of what to do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's not ideal, but I'll quickly check through floors 3 and 2 with Akaro's help and then stay in hallway C. You two make sure the elevator doesn't let Naomi escape.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Without waiting for a reply, Sai left both of us on the fourth floor, all by ourselves.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Ring Chain
All right then. Here we are.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Hopefully they can find her and clear everything up.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I can't imagine Naomi hiding from them unless she knows about some secret spot.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah. It won't take very long either.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm curious to see what'll happen. It's unfortunate she showed up while we weren't there.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But it's very likely she actually did appear since the three of them would have no reason to lie together.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Were you thinking that maybe Naomi was never there at all?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No, not really. I just couldn't take it completely seriously since we hadn't seen her.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You thought Katei was lying to us earlier, right? Have you changed your mind?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Thinking back on what Katei had just said... I wasn't sure how to approach it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know. Honestly, everything Katei said regarding Naomi just now was pretty questionable, but it seemed like he really wanted us to find her. You heard how determined he sounded. I'm not sure he'd lie about what Naomi told him only to turn around and make us find her.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So it's likely it was all the truth.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm really not sure.{w} Anyway, how are you holding up? Sorry, I've just been trying to think about—
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We were both startled. Though louder and clearer, the same sound we'd heard earlier repeated.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She took the elevator...!
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why would she run away?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I recalled what Sai had said too late. We weren't close enough to stop it on the fourth floor. Trying to avoid wasting time, we ran toward the other side to arrive at her destination before we missed her.{w} In our defense, we'd heard the sound when the elevator had been about to pass us by, so stopping it in time wouldn't have been possible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We should've just kept it open...! I didn't think she would actually go up!
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: And I didn't think fast enough, damn it! Sai just wanted us to keep them in place.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya ran behind me. I wanted to tell her to slow down and let me go by myself, but it would've been inconsiderate.
