If I thought going up was dangerous, I would've tried to make her stay behind, but Naomi was presumably running around defenseless, so the odds were probably in our favor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though the floors were very wide, the path to the next one was straightforward enough to make it a quick trip.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We arrived on floor 5. We thought the elevator hadn't stopped there because it seemed to linger for a bit too long, but I still quickly went through the three partitions while Shiroya stayed next to the first door.{w} As I'd thought, they were empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I met Shiroya by the door with a dubious look. We would hear it if Naomi used the elevator to go back down, so there was no way she'd make it past us unnoticed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nothing. She must be upstairs.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We directed ourselves toward the sixth floor, but Shiroya stopped me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: H-Hold on, let's check this.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She tried to open the elevator, but the door didn't budge. Since that meant it was above us, she pressed the button to call it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shortly, the button lit up orange in silence. Then, Shiroya opened the door and we saw the empty elevator.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With how fast it got here, it must've been on the sixth floor.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Technically, there was just one more possibility: the attic.{w} But you'd need a unique key for that, and Shiroya was right. The elevator only took a few seconds to arrive, indicating that there had only been a single floor of separation.{w} By moving it, we'd also prevented Naomi from using it upstairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We quickly went up to the sixth floor, where the elevator had been taken. It was only used once, so someone was definitely there. Naomi was very close.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The bathrooms were empty, so she had to be farther ahead.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll go check. Make sure nobody can leave.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What? It might not be safe. Don't just go alone.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: With a meaningless head gesture, she ran off and left me by myself. She was clearly not content with the thought of waiting behind again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew I had to go with her. Letting someone escape was far less important than letting Shiroya confront potential danger, but I couldn't bring myself to move.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She had disappeared from my field of vision. Given the layout of the floor, she wouldn't be able to make sure nobody could sneak past her, so I had to wait behind in anticipation.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If she first checked the opposite corridor and someone was hiding in the offices, they could then escape. If someone was in the corridor and she chose to first inspect the offices, they could also escape.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, that didn't actually hold up perfectly. To inspect the corridor, she would only have to see if it was empty from a position that would still let her see the inside of the first partition. That could let the culprit escape, but at least they'd be seen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I felt like she'd known I'd been about to ask her to stay behind and had chosen to reverse our roles before I had a chance to act. Trying not to let undesired thoughts get the best of me, I attempted to stay calm as Shiroya had asked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Almost half a minute passed, and I began to get impatient and a bit anxious. While the floor was big, it was also silent except for air movement. If she felt she was in danger, I would be able to hear her shout easily.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Only a few seconds after that, I snapped. What was I doing, standing there and leaving her up against an unknown person who'd been involved in the attack? I prepared to take off running as soon as the realization finally came to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But before I could, I saw Shiroya's figure coming out of the narrow passageway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She approached me slowly and noticed my anxiety.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: D-Did something happen?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...No, nothing. You took a bit, so I started to worry.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, really...? I'm sorry. I didn't find anyone, though.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...How is that possible? There should've been someone.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I know. But look, this is what I wanted to show you.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Once again, she walked back to where she'd come from, instructing me to follow her. Had she found something important?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Instead of stopping in front of the offices, she continued toward the other corridor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Earlier, we thought this place was empty and completely missed a door.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: See, look. But it's closed.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She was right. At the far back of what had appeared to be a dead end, there was a small door that we'd entirely failed to notice.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, of course. We were told this door existed.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It looked just like a plain door. Instinctively, I reached for the doorknob and tried to get it open to no avail—it was tightly locked. Under it was a big keyhole that would require an equally big key to unlock the special section of the tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, past this door must be the attic, where Ashiya lived for years.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, it has to be that. There must be different stairs leading up to it since it's a floor higher.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Right, so it's very likely whoever came up here had a way to open this door. There's no other explanation, really.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I thought about it a little, and that doesn't make sense to me.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I looked through this corridor first, and since you were covering the only exit, I knew I had plenty of time, so I walked farther and realized we'd missed this door.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I tried to open it, but it was already locked. Then I went to the offices, which were empty. Since nobody could've left this floor, the only explanation is that they went through here.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What doesn't make sense to me is that they got off on this floor with the elevator.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...You're right. We determined it was here, so if whoever used it was able to open this door, they would've just taken the elevator all the way up.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah. Katei specifically said that the key works for both the door and the elevator.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I tried to look through the keyhole and under the door, but nothing could be seen. Was there someone behind it, possibly listening to us?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We went up fast, so I doubt they could've taken the elevator up to the attic and then sent it to the sixth floor to conceal where they'd gone.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, we experienced how slow it was. There wouldn't have been time for that.{w} I thought that maybe this door was already unlocked or that they had the key hidden somewhere on this floor.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I doubt the door was unlocked. We could've easily found it earlier, so they wouldn't have let us enter it like that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Also, it's locked now. If it was actually open, unless it can be manually locked from the inside, they must've had the key.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I stayed quiet for a bit. Were we on the right line of thinking? If the culprit had access to the attic, a few things we'd considered would be invalidated.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What if the elevator was empty?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And someone sent it here from the crystal floor?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm not sure what the intention would be, but it's possible whoever sent it was hoping to lure us out of where we were.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, yeah. If they wanted to get to the fourth floor, they could've sent the elevator to make us follow it, but that seems pointless. It'd give them time, but they'd still be cornered. It's not that difficult to inspect every floor.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...And Sai did say that he would check the second and third floors before staying in hallway C. Unless he was the one who moved it, the culprit would've also had to make it past him.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Such a theory sounded very unlikely, but if it was right, we'd soon find out. We couldn't know if the elevator had moved before the others reached the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was also thinking that if the person we're searching for has access to the attic, they might've been responsible for the first time we heard the elevator.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We made sure floors 5 and 6 were empty, but if that person was one floor higher, they could've called the elevator resting on floor 6 and then gone down with it. That would explain why it didn't immediately go back up.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm... Then the same person must've been who used it just now. It's possible they got off on floor 6 instead of the attic because they knew it would be empty and could easily reach this door.{w} If we noticed the elevator and followed it, it would look like it was empty, but if they went directly to the attic instead, we might've noticed it went there if we called it fast enough.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I see. Something along these lines might make the most sense. We should go see if the others found Naomi.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We slowly walked back. I'd always seen Shiroya as intelligent, and she had just shown that sharing my thoughts with her was a good idea despite her recent state of mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Perhaps she had been silently thinking by herself until then. Regardless, that was the longest conversation we'd had in many days, but it already felt like we were many steps closer to normalcy.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew things wouldn't quite feel right for a much longer time, but if we went back to being our normal selves around each other, we could get there much quicker.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been thinking about it nonstop. I didn't know if wishing to go back to how things used to be meant that I was a bad person, but I couldn't change the way I felt.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before we reached the staircase, we noticed that fast but quiet footsteps were approaching. We stopped awkwardly and waited to see who they belonged to.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It was Akaro. He came running from floor 5.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What are you doing here? We need you two to come to the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Did you find Naomi?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, quite the opposite. Sai said that all of us should be there to discuss what happened.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: A-All right... Let's go, then.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Akaro, out of breath, turned around without wasting time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't think you'd be on the highest floor. Weren't you supposed to wait on the fourth?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We began to go down the stairs. Meanwhile, we told Akaro that we'd determined the elevator stopped on the sixth floor and there was no one there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Our conversation continued as we quickly circled through floors 5 and 4. Akaro was hurrying up a fair bit, and he hadn't given us much context.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, right. We heard the elevator going up too, but Sai told us not to chase it since you two would take care of it and could've been sent as bait.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I suppose he gave us too much credit. We didn't react immediately, but I doubt we could've intercepted it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Those were the last words we heard during the way down, as neither of them chose to reply with anything else.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once we'd made it to the last set of stairs, we slowed down our pace as I began to think about what could've happened to warrant the demand of our immediate presence.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The others were all next to the stairs, waiting for us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That took a bit. Where were you?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: On the sixth floor.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Oh, so you had to check every floor.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I just ran up hoping to eventually find them, and they said they hadn't seen anyone.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It's where the elevator stopped, but we're not sure anyone came out of it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So I was right. For some reason, they just wanted it to be followed.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I doubt it, honestly. They could only gain time doing that, and given there are eleven hours left, it seems silly. It's possible they don't know that they've been trapped here for twelve hours, but they can't be simply trying to buy themselves time. I think they actually might've escaped by using the elevator.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: How?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Before that, why don't you tell us what happened? Was Naomi here?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I couldn't see her, so it was safe to assume that wasn't the case. I wanted to get straight to the point before suggesting that the person hiding from us might've had access to the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We haven't looked through the whole floor yet, actually.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I quickly made sure nobody was on the third and second floors while the others prevented anyone from sneaking past. That was when the elevator was used, and I assume you couldn't stop it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No, we weren't expecting it so soon.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Whatever. We went to the first floor, and we did what you heard Katei propose. He went ahead and looked through the lobby and the mechanical room. When he was done, he stayed next to the door leading to hallway B.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Akaro began to look through the hallway B rooms since he'd looked at the bathrooms previously. Isla wanted to join him, so Erina had to follow behind. The three of them started to enter the rooms while I stayed here, looking at hallway A so that nobody could escape.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Since the elevator had already gone up, it was pointless to call it and leave its door open. I couldn't see the three of them looking inside the rooms since I was staring at the other hallway and blocking the staircase, though.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Anyway, apparently when they entered the event room, Isla went ahead and raised the curtain on the cabinet. The "It's gone!" shout I heard even from here conveyed her surprise pretty well.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What...? The Sekimeiya's gone?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes... It should've still been there, but I didn't see it anywhere.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Katei abandoned his post after hearing Isla shout, but I didn't want to rush inside and leave an easy escape route open. When they came and told me what had happened, I thought you two had to get down here. Since we're dealing with this situation, I found it appropriate to join up and make sure nothing slipped away.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I told Akaro to go find you, and I took that time to check if it really had disappeared while the others waited here.{w} It's gone. I stayed there a while, thinking about what could've happened, and expecting to find you two when I came back. Anyway, many of these rooms haven't been investigated yet. We stayed here until you came back to secure the only exits.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I understand... It's good that the stairs and the elevator are next to each other.{w} Can I go see it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If you're looking forward to seeing an empty cabinet, go ahead. As long as someone stays here, we can move through this floor.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Everyone else had been looking at us without uttering a word. Shiroya and I slowly walked toward hallway A, and as we saw that nobody was stopping us, we sped up to the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's really not here.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I suppose he was right. There wasn't much of a point in checking.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Not really.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We left through the same door and approached the others as I thought about it: what had happened? Were there really that many possibilities?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was it gone, or did we all lie?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Apparently not.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The Sekimeiya has been stolen this early, which is surprising. Anyone have a suggestion regarding what could've happened before we resume our search?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It could only have been Naomi, right?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: No. It could only have been Naomi, Katei, or an unknown person.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you going to suspect me forever?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It seems so. When we split up in two groups, it's possible either Naomi or an unknown person had already stolen the Sekimeiya. That's very easy to conclude. When we were in hallway B, Naomi could've entered the event room from hallway A, for example.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The group that took the elevator—Atsuki, Shiroya, Erina, and Isla—couldn't have gotten to this floor.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you sure? It's possible they went past us and we didn't notice.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You already tried to say this earlier, didn't you? They couldn't have done that.{w} The way we looked through the floors would've made that impossible, and they couldn't have used the elevator since we only heard it once.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And, naturally, when you came here with Naomi, you would've had an easy time picking up the Sekimeiya and then hiding it somewhere. Later, we'll check that mechanical room you were so happy to inspect.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: This is ridiculous. Didn't I say how important it was for the Sekimeiya to stay in its cabinet? Why would I hide it? There aren't even places to hide it in this building, and it would be pointless!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I will admit that I have no idea what your reason could be, but similarly, I can't think of one regardless of who the culprit is. It is true that there aren't many hiding spots, and it's very early for this.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If one thing's for sure, it's that right now, the Sekimeiya must be on this floor with the culprit. There's no other possibility unless you question me and think that Akaro and I could've gone down instead of waiting on floor 4.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't believe that's true. You looked through floors 3 and 2 for Naomi, but if the Sekimeiya was left there, you might've missed it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, correct. That's a possibility too, but since the elevator that went up was probably empty, nobody can still be upstairs and hide it further, so we can go look for it above if nothing's found on this floor.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Even though floors 2 and 3 were a possibility, I knew it was also very possible that the culprit had gone to the attic holding the Sekimeiya. If our search amounted to nothing, I would bring up the conclusion Shiroya and I had reached.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's proceed, then. We'll need to start from the beginning. Someone else go look through the lobby and the mechanical room, though.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Maybe we should start with that one.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I directed my look at the room where the gemstones had been stolen—A5.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Because of the camera?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes. Like Sai said, hiding anything on this floor right now seems weird since we should be able to find it easily. We have plenty of time, and it's not a hard task. ...Not to mention that even if we can't find it, Ashiya surely will. It feels pretty redundant.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But there must be an actual reason behind it, and if they really intended to hide it from us, a room that's not being recorded seems to be the most likely place. Even if it's found, Ashiya will never be able to look at the footage to see who hid it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: This is a bit confusing, though. It's true that our three suspects are Katei, Naomi, and an unknown person. All of them would've had access to the Sekimeiya while we were knocked out, so I wonder why they didn't hide it then.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's true...{w} Well, we can check there first if someone stays here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai walked to the room and gestured at me to follow him. Everyone else stayed next to the stairs, as it wasn't yet a thorough search that would require further positioning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's see. We should keep the door open. Otherwise, we won't see anything.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: At first glance, there wasn't anything odd in the room. It all looked as it had when we'd last been there. Even though cabinets were the only thing inside, Sai started slowly examining them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I began looking through the opposite side of the room. There were plenty of places to hide a small object.{w} Behind the cabinets, under the pillows that normally held gemstones... A cabinet even had empty drawers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I looked at Sai, I realized that even though their appearances were nearly identical, not every cabinet was the same. He was inspecting the expansive interior of a cabinet after he'd opened up the heavy-looking lid. It seemed that the upper sections, where the gemstones usually were, could be lifted up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is there anything there?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Yes. Some of these have hollow interiors, most likely to store things. Look, though.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I had to get close to him, as the lack of illumination made it impossible to see what he was holding.{w} It was nothing noteworthy; he was cupping a small, yellow gemstone on his palm.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They must keep some of these inside the cabinets to swap out the displayed ones. Apparently, not all of this room's valuables were stolen.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I see. I guess this could make for a decent hiding spot.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sort of. The others were taking a while earlier, so they probably opened up some cabinets too. It's still an obvious spot if you're trying to find something.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I went ahead and opened up a cabinet that looked like the one Sai was next to. It was a lot easier than it looked, and a wide but completely empty compartment appeared before me. As all the displays were usually attached to the surface below the glass, when the lid was opened up like a chest, they wouldn't roll.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's nothing in this one.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, the first one I looked at was empty as well.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Not many more cabinets were left. Shortly after that, we had looked through all of them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It seems you were wrong. It's not here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I started to go over the cabinets Sai had looked through to be confident.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you doubt my searching abilities, or do you think I hid it here and ignored it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Neither, I just want to make sure we don't miss anything.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I answered without looking at him. It didn't take me long to come to the same conclusion: the Sekimeiya was not in the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you done? We'll take forever if every room takes us this long.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We should probably look for anyone on this floor and then do a slower search for the Sekimeiya. The chances of someone and the Sekimeiya being here are pretty much the same.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That could be a good idea. Let's go back.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: When he turned around, I fixed my eyes on Sai's back. Specifically, at the hip pack going around his waist. He stopped when he noticed I was still staring at him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you looking at this?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He turned it around him and showed me its contents. I could only see a wallet and lip balm appropriate for the cold.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't be stupid. It might fit in here, but it'd be more than noticeable. Did you think I'd found it and masterfully put it in without your notice?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh, no. I was just looking at it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I quite like it too. One of those birthday presents I first shrugged off and then ended up using frequently.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Once again, he turned around and quickly left the room.{w} I sighed and followed his steps. Outside, he was already next to the others.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Anything...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Nothing.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I tried to think of places where the Sekimeiya could've been hidden, but I couldn't come up with any good ones. If it was still on the crystal floor, we should've been able to find it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In a locker, maybe? That's the only safe place I can think of.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Oh, how about there?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The suitcase was still on the floor of hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did they bank on us not checking it again?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: As I got closer to it, my confidence in that theory decreased. Surely they hadn't relied on such a simple trick.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was still empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's start, then. I suppose checking the bathrooms again is pointless since nobody could've entered them.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Without waiting, Akaro stood up and headed toward hallway B. Isla followed behind, which obligated Erina to go with them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's continue with hallway A, actually. It's about time we find out if someone else is here, so let's first check for that. Akaro, before you move on to hallway B, look through the mechanical room too. Mind being the one in the lobby this time, Atsuki? Katei and I will stay here to watch hallway B.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Sure.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The others accepted it easily and began with hallway A, ignoring the room we'd just gotten out of.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Presumptuous as it was, Sai could've kept ordering us around as long as it was efficient. Since Shiroya didn't have a fixed position, she moved to the lobby door with me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: From there, we looked at the three people checking every room. Akaro led the pack.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My first idea was that someone left the Sekimeiya in a room without active security cameras. While the first location had been incorrect, that was still the most likely possibility.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Five other rooms that met that criterion were still available: the staff room, the cleaning room, the mechanical room, the security room, and the storeroom.{w} I looked inside the cleaning bucket, the only place in the lobby where the Sekimeiya could've been hidden from view, but it only contained soapy water.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The storeroom was examined, but they were just quickly looking for people—not the Sekimeiya. It was very possible it was in one of those rooms, and if Naomi had put it inside her locker in the staff room, for example, there wasn't much we could do about it. That was one of the only good hiding spots I could think of.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They entered the event room once again. After that, the security room, another place with a route to it that had no concern for cameras, was acknowledged as clean.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once I'd seen them come out of every room and claim that nobody had been in them, Akaro went to look at the mechanical room. Even though Isla remained outside, uninterested, Erina joined him as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They took a considerably longer time with it since the messy interior made a proper search difficult. Once they returned, their expressions indicated that again, nothing of relevance had been found inside, refuting Sai's suspicion. Afterward, they moved on to hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya and I headed to the hallway B door too, as it wasn't necessary to keep watching A any longer. As soon as it was confirmed empty, the only remaining concern was whether someone could move from hallway B to A through the event room, and since Sai and Katei had watched hallway B, it wasn't a real possibility.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Technically, only two people were needed to optimally search through the whole floor as long as someone stayed next to the stairs while looking into hallway A. Then, the other person could safely look through every room. We'd only been doing it differently because it was what Katei had suggested.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They started from the rooms on the lobby side onward. Shiroya and I could clearly see Sai and Katei standing on the other exit of the hallway, enacting tight control over the few rooms that remained for Naomi or an extra person to be inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If nobody was found in them, the possibility Shiroya and I had come up with would be almost confirmed: that the actual culprit had been in the attic until we'd heard the elevator going down, and that they'd brought the Sekimeiya up with them to hide on a floor we couldn't access.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As that theory grew more likely, I thought further on it and quickly picked up on an important inconsistency.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro and Sai said that when they'd heard the elevator sound, Naomi had already shown up and left with Katei.{w} If that was the case, Naomi could not have been in the attic the way I'd thought about things. To make it work, I had to slightly change it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nothing was out of place if we'd missed Naomi when we'd inspected the crystal floor together, she went up to the third floor to talk with Katei, and she then called the elevator to keep it on the first floor. Later, she'd used it to move to the attic as soon as she'd obtained the Sekimeiya, probably because she'd realized she couldn't convince Katei.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The first three rooms were handled with ease. The others kept going and looked through the event room once again despite the fact that it was impossible anything in it had changed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nonchalantly—almost forgetting what could've been resting in any of the rooms—Akaro opened the door in front of it. He looked inside, and his body froze.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: From afar, I was able to see his expression shifting to a blank and pale one. With his hand on the doorknob, he turned around, frantically trying to meet someone else's gaze.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's wrong...? Anything inside?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The silent corridors allowed us to make out their words. On the other side, Sai and Katei had also realized that something unusual was inside that room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Wh-What!? Isla, stop!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Erina, after peeking over Akaro's shoulder, immediately pushed aside Isla, who'd been about to glance into the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm...? Let me see...
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Guys, come here. It seems we weren't wrong.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: With an altered voice, Akaro instructed we could abandon our positions, as the search had finished.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Unnerved, we went to see what had caused those reactions. Sai brushed past Akaro to see what he'd found. Despite his constant effort at appearing unfazed and composed, the moment he set his eyes inside, he was visibly startled.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: S-Seriously...?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The room, B4, was in the middle of the hallway. Katei, Shiroya, and I arrived at the same time, silently glancing at each other. Erina was still tightly holding Isla, and both of them moved back to let us see through the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh God, no...
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Darkroom

It took us not even a second to understand it. On the floor lay the body of Naomi over a pool of blood. On the wall, close to the door, were traces of more blood. Not only that, but a strange odor became noticeable as soon as I stepped inside. I couldn't associate it to anything, but it wasn't prominent enough to be aggravating.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei, if you're gonna kill somebody, don't make it so obvious.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It was far from the first time Sai had said something careless, but it was far over the line for all of us that time. Especially Erina, who had been trying to keep Isla unaware of what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You must be joking... Don't even think about accusing me.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai moved over to the body. With two fingers, he confirmed its status.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She's definitely dead. She probably already was when we got back to this floor. This room wasn't searched earlier, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No. We stopped at the event room. This one was next, so you could be right.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: No, th-that's...
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Wait!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Isla, who hadn't yet put up any resistance, was able to escape from Erina's grip. Her shock escalated when she understood that we were telling the truth.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But... that's impossible! Why did—
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: It's clearly possible, just look at her. And I'll sure think about it, Katei. You are the only person who could've done this.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: While they were audibly reacting, I found myself silently aghast, which I hadn't been prepared for. I'd been carelessly going over the entire incident, but as soon as the image of the dead Naomi met my eyes, any focus on reality departed from my body.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya, at my side, looked identical to me. The concept of death and loss had recently been changed for us.{w} She and I hadn't experienced it until two weeks ago, when the world we'd created together crumbled down without warning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi's lifeless body was an immediate reminder. One that came as soon as I started having hope for the future again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I fixed my eyes on Shiroya's face as the others kept up their arguing. They wouldn't have noticed the sheer panic she was experiencing, but I knew her better. Her effort at moving on had been denied by reality; we'd been put back in our place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I never knew how to respond. Thoughtless reassurance wouldn't achieve anything. However, even though it might not have been any help, I tried to put everything I wanted to say into a hand that I placed on her shoulder—as a way to distance myself from the insentient and inanimate support I'd been until then.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya and I knew each other since our first year of elementary school, where we became classmates for the first time. Our parents were friends, which quickly tied us together.{w} We would see one another during school and our parents' meetings, so we rapidly grew close. Before becoming classmates, we'd already met a few times, but we'd never really spoken.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Our parents worked for Yushibana's hospital, but their work involved securing deals with entities outside the town, which made them travel very often. We'd been told that the four of them were a group of friends since long before we were born, and that they all met when they were lower down their workplace's ladder.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A bit more than a year prior, they accepted a job offer overseas. Despite their insistent attempts at making us accompany them, we were strongly against it, as we'd lived in Yushibana our whole lives. The idea of traveling to another continent wasn't a pleasant one. Unlike them, we didn't even know the language there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They eventually had to give up and accepted paying for our necessary expenses like food and rent. We'd lived by ourselves since then.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: One year ago, Shiroya and I finished high school together. In Yushibana, people tended to move out if they planned to attend university, seeing as the closest one was hours away. That was why we hadn't yet decided on what to do and thought of the year 2011 as a pivotal point where we'd decide. Money wasn't an immediate problem for either of us, and we weren't sure what we wanted to study if we decided to move.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The last important factor that influenced our decision first made an appearance in our lives when we started middle school. Most of us were the same people who had attended elementary school together, but a new classmate named Miiya moved to Yushibana that year.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At first, Shiroya and I didn't talk to her much, and neither did our usual group of friends. Miiya quickly became comfortable with other people in our class, which kept some distance between us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That changed three years later, the day she approached me when I was alone. She was curious about us and wanted to hang out. I never really understood what drove her to do that, but we spent an entire afternoon together, and following that day, she would spend some time with me every so often.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A few months later, she appeared when Shiroya and I were together, and they introduced themselves in more depth. Since then, the three of us started to become comfortable around each other after school. It was out of the ordinary for us since we were used to being alone, but we quickly took a liking to Miiya.{w} She was a blunt and sincere girl—one who didn't seem to have many worries in life or think too hard about things. Even though she'd made her way into our lives out of the blue, we became accustomed to her presence.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Initially, she passed the time with us sporadically and acted as another link between Shiroya and me, but the frequency increased to the point where the three of us would spend almost every afternoon together.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Last year, the end of high school became somewhat of an obstacle for what had grown to be our daily lives. Miiya was different from us in the sense that she knew she didn't want to continue studying, and she instead started searching for a job in Yushibana while living with her parents.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The previous summer was not an easy one for us. Shiroya and I weren't sure what to do with our futures, and we knew that if our decisions differed, we might stop seeing each other. Behind everything else, that was always my biggest worry, and at the same time, Miiya was only focused on searching for a job that wanted her.{w} I felt like I was stuck in the past, wishing that our school days could continue as always. Meanwhile, the uncertainty of the future prevented Shiroya from resting easy. That made it hard for us to keep up with each other, and even though the circumstances were perfect for a summer together, the three of us spent it alone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It all started to shift back to normal once Shiroya and I decided that neither of us wanted to move out for the time being. We would spend one extra year thinking about it, so at first, that was a perfect excuse to go back to how everything had been before the holidays.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Unfortunately, all of our conversations had grown stiff. Shiroya and I talked frequently about our decisions through messages, but the three of us hadn't personally seen each other in a while. None of us were at our best, and none of us felt anything resembling enthusiasm. Our relationships loosened even further, and the distance between us widened into a chasm.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I recognized what it had all turned into, I grew despondent. I couldn't do anything to return to our routine, and I wasn't sure if they wanted to. Other friends I had from school completely disappeared from my life in the blink of an eye.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: For two or three months, my old life continued fading away.{w} ...That was until I received a call from Miiya. She confessed to feeling a lot like I had and wanting to restore everything. I immediately called Shiroya, who sounded like she was in the same position.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was just over two weeks before the Sekimeiya showing when we met at my house. We'd gone our longest ever without meeting, but we still recognized each other as the people we'd spent the entirety of our teenage years with. It was difficult at first, but since we knew the three of us wanted to finally get over our new barriers, the constricting ice that had formed around us broke much more easily than I'd anticipated.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We said that we'd go back to how everything had been during the start of the year. The three of us needed it and all feared that it had ended long ago.{w} Even though we'd settled that, there weren't many things to do during the winter in Yushibana. Hanging out and talking for hours used to work in the past, but if we were starting fresh, that might not have sufficed. That was how we came across Ashiya's advertisement; on December 15th, their biggest event to date would be held.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya and I disliked Ashiya to an extent, but Miiya, having moved to Yushibana as a kid, didn't share the same feeling that had been prominently pushed onto us by the older residents. She had only been vaguely told about the main outline of it all, so when she proposed that we attend the event, we didn't refuse.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It honestly sounded like a fine idea to us. Anything the three of us could go to was good.{w} According to the announcement, an event was held in Ashiya Tower every Thursday, each one requiring special entrance tickets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We accepted it and bought them before they ran out. December had always been a special month for me and Shiroya: my birthday was on the 21st, while hers was on the 19th. We were happy we had reunited just in time for them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As no other special matters were scheduled to happen in Yushibana, we decided to keep looking through Ashiya's events. One that might've been interesting was scheduled for January 26th, when every gemstone in the building would be replaced. We thought that if we enjoyed it the first Thursday, maybe that'd be a good day to return. Meanwhile, we agreed to meet up frequently until the 15th.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, just the next day, Miiya died. We found ourselves in an incident that took her life, and Shiroya had to be hospitalized.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was comically tragic. Everything we thought we had regained was immediately ripped away from us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya was in a coma for a few days, but she ultimately didn't suffer from anything major. The days during which I waited still, thinking that I might've lost the last two people remaining from my normal life, were harder than anything I ever thought I'd have to suffer. To add unnecessary cruelty, neither my parents nor Shiroya's were able to show up, and they only talked to police officers and doctors over the phone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My parents even used the opportunity to tell me once again that I should go live with them. They'd been very insistent about that in the past, and the incident gave them the chance to force it even further.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had almost never talked to Miiya's parents, but when I saw them talking to the agent in charge of things, it was clear that they were devastated; everything in their lives had collapsed in the span of a single day.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When Shiroya woke up, I was in her hospital room and told her about what happened. She couldn't even cry—she must've despised everything that led to that outcome. After the doctors told her that she wouldn't have to spend more time in the hospital, I offered to let her stay at my house. Having each other as company should've been beneficial for both of us, and my parents' house was big enough.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She almost accepted immediately, but she ended up saying she'd think about it. I insisted, saying that she wouldn't be a bother, and accompanied her to her apartment.{w} The next day, she accepted and came over for a temporary stay.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Despite all my efforts at being helpful, I spent the days closed up physically and mentally, hating myself for that too. I remained shut in my room, sleeping during the day and glancing through the window at night.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The life we'd lived for years had met an abrupt end immediately after resuming itself. It wasn't something anyone should have experienced, and it was nothing short of impossible for us to stop wallowing in our own pathetic misery.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't want to distance myself from Shiroya; facing the thought of being left alone was unbearable. That was why I'd immediately asked her to remain together for a few days. At home, we briefly saw each other every day, but no conversations aside from simple words to coordinate ourselves came from either of us.{w} At least, she spent the days with Maxi and Umi, a dog and a cat that had lived with me for years, which I hoped made her feel less lonely. I also got to hear her voice a handful of times when she talked to her parents over the phone, but they were too busy to leave.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the 14th, the day before the event, we met in the living room and saw the three tickets we'd bought for it inside the brown purse Miiya would sometimes carry. Knowing that our plans would never happen completely tore me up. I didn't know whether to throw the tickets away, but before I could decide, Shiroya spoke.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Should we still go?"
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't something I'd expected to hear at all, but it conveyed everything Shiroya had been feeling. ...I'd been trying to muster the strength to say it myself too. Despite our sudden loss, she didn't want us to grow cold again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We decided we'd go anyway, trying not to let the death of our closest friend directly kill our relationship too. We saw it as confirmation that even though everything looked more than grim, we'd do all we could to make it eventually get better.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We finally talked a bit before the night came. Our schedules were all over the place, and we had to wake up very early to make it to Ashiya Tower before {time=9.}{w} As the night went on, it was clear that neither of us would be able to sleep.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Painfully conscious of our surroundings, we both stayed awake, unable to rest in any way. Once it was clear that it would persist, Shiroya suggested leaving early. It was a relieving thought, one I'd also considered.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I agreed immediately. I needed to move and feel the cold night air. Shiroya took two of the three tickets from Miiya's purse and put them in hers, along with our identification to validate them and the keys to my house. As we stepped outside, a calm and pleasant night welcomed us back to our town. We walked through desolate streets without an objective in mind, letting time move at its own pace.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Eventually, we reached the outskirts. We were close to Ashiya; we wouldn't usually walk through that part of Yushibana, but we waited right outside the tower in a little plaza Ashiya kept clean, waiting for the sun to rise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At {time=6}, everything around us was covered in snow, and even though we'd grown used to the sheer cold of the mountains, staying outside for that long exceeded our limit. We walked to the entrance of the tower and were told by a guard that we could wait inside until the doors opened to the public.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were met by a lady sorting a bunch of papers behind the reception desk. Shiroya and I hadn't talked much, but staying with each other was more than enough. The only other person there was a man in the middle of the room, wearing a lost look. He glanced at us for an instant before going back to how he had been.{w} We'd later learn his name was Akaro, and I would speak to him for the first time in the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Things had continued and led to... death. Once again, the cruel sensation of death had appeared before us after avoiding it for almost twenty years.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It took a single dead body to make me reminisce over my whole life. I'd started to think that I'd been climbing the first steps to get over what happened by immersing myself in our present incident, but that was far from accurate. Even though I'd gotten Shiroya to start returning to her usual self, at that moment, her face gave away how meaningless that was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Words started making sense again. Sai, who had been thoughtlessly messing with me without a clue what my last few days had been like, was accusing Katei of murder.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're out of your mind! I would never kill anyone!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then why did you? Don't you recall what we've been doing? Nobody else could've been here to do this.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What if you were the one who did it, Sai?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It was pissing me off. It was reasonable to think that Katei was the culprit, but accusing anyone of stealing someone's life so lightly was something I really didn't like. Even Shiroya didn't expect me to suddenly spit that out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Excuse me? I was with Akaro on the fourth floor, and the last time we entered this room, we all saw it was empty.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He's right, we didn't move from there. Are you saying that maybe we both did it to frame Katei?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: No. Sure, that might also be a possibility that lets Katei not be a murderer, but Sai had an easier way all by himself.{w} He said it earlier, right? That he went to check if the Sekimeiya had truly disappeared while you all waited next to the stairs.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: He even admitted to spending a while thinking about what happened. The event room connects both hallways, and from the stairs, you wouldn't have seen what was happening in hallway B. You saw Naomi and chased her over to this room. You definitely could've done this.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I couldn't let out the word "kill" easily since I didn't believe that Sai being responsible was the most likely thing, but I didn't want to let him forcibly label Katei as a murderer if other possibilities existed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're not being serious, are you? Don't you think Naomi would've yelled? There's blood on the wall, so since blood is coming from the back of her head, she was probably pushed into it. It follows that she was seeing her killer as it happened, so she would've yelled.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We would only have missed a yell like that if Katei and Naomi were the only ones present on this floor at the time.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But what if she didn't yell? You can't possibly be saying that blood on the wall means she had to. Maybe it happened too fast for her to react, or maybe her mouth was covered.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Atsuki, don't be stupid. You must also be aware that Katei has to be the one who did this.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The blood on the wall is next to the door, and Naomi's body is perpendicular to the wall. If you're gonna push someone against a wall, you'll need to be farther from it than your victim, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Meaning that the culprit was farther from the door than Naomi. You could infer from there that they either entered the room before Naomi or that they entered at the same time.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That makes sense if Katei was the culprit, but if I chased Naomi here, I wouldn't have had an easy time pushing her into this wall. She would've been farther into the room than me, so I would've had to push her against one of the other three walls.{w} Ignoring, obviously, that she would not have run into a room and cornered herself; she would've escaped from the hallway.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Or maybe you entered the room first and the noise lured her in. Maybe you chased her down when she was in the middle of the room, and since she headed to the exit, you pushed her against this wall.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm not trying to accuse you, but stop acting as if Katei must be responsible.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Also, what the hell is this smell? Does anyone recognize it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Everyone denied it with nearly imperceptible movements. They'd all noticed it, but seeing so much blood under a body must've forced them to ignore it. We had to continue for eleven hours bearing the thought of being trapped with someone who had killed a person.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I have no idea what it is.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Me neither, but fine. Atsuki, do you honestly believe I killed Naomi? There's a working security camera here, for fuck's sake. Do you think I'd ruin my life to kill someone I didn't even know a couple hours ago?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't really think you're responsible.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Then you're accusing Katei too! Sure, I could've had the chance to do it, but there's no other possibility. If you're saying you think I didn't do it, you're also saying you think Katei did.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I would never kill a person. This has gone too far, Sai.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Oh, shut the fuck up.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're wrong. There's at least one more possibility.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What, did Naomi jump into the wall and break her head open?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Remember when the elevator went up before you all reached this floor? It stopped on the sixth. Shiroya and I made sure nobody could've gone unnoticed, but there's a way around that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Right, through the door we can't open.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The one leading to the attic.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...He's right. Someone could've gone in before we got there.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shiroya was trying not to let the shock and despair consume her, and I was glad to be backed up. Even though Erina and Isla should've reacted to the mention of a door they hadn't seen, they didn't so much as twitch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it was locked, right? Didn't Katei say that a unique key was required to enter the attic?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes, but imagining a culprit with that key isn't all that crazy, is it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: *sigh*
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Please... This is just pathetic to watch.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hm? What is?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It also took me by surprise. Katei was looking directly at me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki, stop trying to find nonexistent ways out.{w} You are the one who killed Naomi.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You're kidding, right...? You're accusing him?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: He absolutely could not have done it. You had the opportunity to at least accuse me.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I was still recovering from the most unexpected words I could've heard. He had, without warning, accused me of killing Naomi...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I'm sorry, but how do you think I did that? I was always with Shiroya, and security cameras recorded every one of my actions on the upper floors.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And not only that, he didn't have a chance to make it down without being spotted.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's why I have to come to the conclusion that you're all lying to me. All of you.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'm sure of it. Atsuki was here when Naomi and I were on this floor. You guys are giving him a very solid alibi, one that's not possible to circumvent. That's why you must all be lying.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: However, it is as you say. Security cameras had to record what happened in this room and on the office floors. Your lie won't last long once the system is recovered.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What's gotten into you...? At least your lies earlier had some effort.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: He's right. This is almost disappointing. Try to convince anyone of that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: For the first time, one of Sai's retorts was well-received by everyone else. Katei had alleged they were all liars, but they knew the truth: I hadn't killed Naomi.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're only digging your own grave by acting as if we're all conspiring against you. You had an actual method of escape that Atsuki provided you with. Taking it would've been a much smarter decision than accusing him.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It's especially idiotic even for this guy. Why are you saying that Atsuki was on this floor?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Because I saw him!{w} After Naomi left, when she understood that I wasn't buying it, I heard a noise. In this hallway, B, I saw Atsuki.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It surprised me, so I kept silent and waited for him to move. However, trying not to be seen also made me lose track of him completely. I looked around a bit, but I couldn't find him or Naomi again.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: When I went back up, I saw him with the others, and you all said that he could not have been downstairs. That's what leads me to the conclusion that you've all been lying to me.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...That ridiculous claim, if anything, explained why Katei had insisted multiple times that the elevator group might've been able to sneak down. Naturally, though, it was met with silence and shared disapproval.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At least this proves you're nothing but a lying machine. Your fuel must've run out and now you can only fabricate these limp little things.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You think you sound smart, but I believe all of us here know that you are the one lying.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Let me just tell it to you straight. In the one in a million chance that you're either telling the truth or hallucinating, what you saw could not have been Atsuki. If you actually saw someone, it wasn't him.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Incorrect. I am certain it was him. His clothes could've been borrowed, but borrowing a face and the size of someone's body is much different. I don't know why you're all lying and aiding a criminal, but I'm certain of what I saw.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then we're left with a hallucination. You get your brain checked recently?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I will refrain from saying anything else. When this is all thoroughly investigated by the police, the truth will be proven.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: As I knew I hadn't killed anyone, I hadn't been seriously considering any of it. I'd ruled it as just Katei's desperate, pathetic, and ineffective way of not being suspected.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My attention had been drawn to one of the cabinets present with us in the room. At first glance, it looked like every other cabinet we'd seen, but there was something unusual about it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On its right side was what looked to be a small wheel. To get a closer look, I approached it, making sure not to step on any of the blood. As I moved to it, I was once again reminded of the inexplicable odor I had never smelled before, which was starting to blend in seamlessly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did you see something?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, this.{w} Oh, it's a temperature regulator.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: How interesting. What's it set at?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Nothing. It says "room temperature".
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I turned around to meet Katei's eyes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Some cabinets have temperature functions, like the Sekimeiya's. This room has them.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The white wheel looked a bit damaged, which was what caught my attention. Anything could've caused that, but it stood out from everything else in the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kept inspecting it. Behind it, I quickly noticed another similar wheel, a bit smaller in size.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And what's this one for?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That one? It regulates the temperature.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I can see the degrees symbol, but this one isn't set to anything, not even to "room temperature". I mean, why are there two of them?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, I think that one regulates the temperature of the gems behind the glass while the big one regulates the temperature inside the cabinet.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see, to store gems that also require a determined temperature.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I tried to lift up the cover, but it was too heavy.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How do I open it, though? I don't seem to be able to.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't know, I've never opened one.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: And you've never seen anyone opening one through the cameras.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Perhaps I have. I think they first look behind the cabinet, but I'm not sure what the process is. These cabinets have an actual method of locking them so that the temperature inside is well-preserved.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I tried following his instructions. Behind the cabinet and next to the wheel, there was a tiny plastic latch that I was able to open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I think it should be unlocked now...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I put my hands under the lid and brought it up while everyone else stared at me dubiously. Then, Sai began to approach me with curiosity.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Like before, I was able to open it with ease. When I had fully opened it and kept the lid supported against the wall, I looked inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no appreciable change in temperature, as the wheel hadn't been set to anything. However, there certainly was something inside. I saw the Sekimeiya resting at the bottom, covered by walls with a velvet texture and emitting a faint glow.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I-It's here.{w} I have no idea why, but it's here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Before the others could react, I stretched out my arm to grab it. With one hand, I leaned on the cabinet to support my weight while I put the other inside. As I slowly approached it, I thought to myself: what possible purpose could anyone have for leaving the Sekimeiya there?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Without giving it much thought, I touched the surface of the egg-shaped object.{w} A burst of heat flowed through my fingers, and the world broke.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: B-Side

The burning sensation vanished, and I was no longer stretching out my arm. Before me was a long corridor that I'd seen before.{w} My body froze, and I broke out in a cold sweat. A heavy cloak of confusion was cast on me as my heart took off like a rocket.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Something had happened to me—something that I hadn't ever experienced before. When I slowly began to discern my surroundings, I saw that I was in hallway A, next to the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to calm down and think. I timidly moved my head and saw the huge shutter blocking my way to the outside world. Around the hallway A door, dark marks left by the smoke were easily noticeable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next, I moved my legs forward. I was still able to control my whole body; nothing seemed to have changed in that regard. I moved up to hallway B, which surrounded me with its dark, unsettling scenery and pure silence.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the right wall, I could see the door of the room I'd been in a few seconds ago. It was closed, like all the others.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I gently approached it, I tried to think about what could've happened. However, it was as bizarre as it sounded: I had touched the Sekimeiya and appeared in the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Not only that, but it had been instantaneous. Not a moment of time had seemed to pass before my surroundings changed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I gripped the knob. As soon as I started to open the door, I saw blood. On the floor, Naomi's dead body rested, her face clearly distressed. My senses alerted me of another change: the strange smell didn't appear to exist anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kept looking inside the room. Everyone else had already left it, and the cabinet I'd opened was closed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The haunting atmosphere radiating throughout the room was overwhelming, and it chased me out. I closed the door behind me and made an effort at breathing properly to calm myself down. What the hell was happening?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was there a blank spot in my memory? Had I forgotten about something past the last memory I had?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nothing made sense. It couldn't make sense. The others had disappeared, and I had, in the blink of an eye, moved from one place to another.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Was I knocked out?{w} I had my back against the others when I reached for the Sekimeiya, but wouldn't I remember it? Wouldn't I feel pain in my head if I was hit?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And... when I realized I was somewhere different than before, I was standing up. If I'd been knocked out, I would've woken up on the floor...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: No matter how I thought of it, it felt as if no time had passed between the Sekimeiya's touch and the change in what I was looking at. To put it bluntly, it felt as if I had teleported between places.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, that was impossible. There must've been a reason why it had felt like that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened the door to the event room. Nothing but a single, ugly cabinet was inside. I couldn't see its contents, but I didn't care. I kept looking through every room in the hallway to find the people that should've been there—to confirm that I hadn't been left alone and to understand what had happened to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened and closed every door in quick succession until I knew that I was on a desolate floor. ...Where was Shiroya?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In front of me was the elevator door. I wanted to see the others, so I called it. If they were somewhere above me, they would hear the sound and come down to find me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After I pressed the button, though, nothing happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Is it here?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I grabbed the handle of the large, metallic door. As I'd suspected, I was able to open it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Since I wouldn't be able to draw people down to me, I had to modify my idea. I boarded the tiny elevator and pressed the button for the sixth floor. If anyone could hear it, I hoped they'd be lured.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was my second time taking a full six-floor trip in that gloomy space, and being alone only made it worse. Just what had happened? I'd been accumulating questions since we'd gotten trapped, but the situation I was in surpassed all of them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Being alone let me look inside the elevator freely. ...I stared at the red button with the word "stop" on it. They would usually stop it abruptly, mostly in case someone got stuck on a door. Other times, they'd only play a loud alarm throughout the building.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the wall next to it, there was a little paper with instructions detailing how it worked. I took the time to read it, trying to calm myself down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Pressing the stop button will instantly deactivate the elevator and contact an emergency line. It is strictly prohibited to press it without a good reason, and to prevent ulterior uses, the elevator won't be enabled again until a staff member consents. Keep in mind that you are being recorded."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked behind me, and sure enough, I saw a small camera in an upper corner with a green light on it. It seemed Ashiya had made sure the button would only be used during a real emergency. Regarding the contact line, it was likely it had been nullified by the alarm.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The remaining seconds once again left me in awe at how unsettling that small and quiet elevator could get. Even though I could hear the friction of the ropes, that imposing and deep sound that was more than apparent outside couldn't be appreciated well from the interior.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went to the highest accessible floor and hastily pushed the door open. The sight was just as I remembered. I remained solitary and was met with another silently overwhelming floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While I hoped people had heard me and were coming, I had to know whether there was someone around. We'd seen how easy it was to inspect those floors, so I started the same procedure from before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked at the empty left corridor. A door was hiding from my field of vision, but there was nobody to be seen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, I made my way to the offices to see if they weren't vacant for some reason.{w} There was something I recognized in the first one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The computer we'd powered on earlier still showed a lit screen and an empty prompt to input access information.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Without paying any mind to it, I entered the second partition. Being alone meant that I couldn't keep watch over the connecting corridor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the second and third partitions, my only company was a functioning camera recording my every movement.{w} I sat on a chair and sighed deeply, unraveling at the sudden turn things had taken. Did we not have enough already? What the fuck had just happened!? My whole body hadn't stopped shaking for a second. I rejected the thought that any of it was real.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I left the offices once I felt ready to continue, but I was still hopeless.{w} I was about to repeat my movements on the floors below when I heard a very distinguishable sound coming from my left.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Footsteps. And ones I knew I'd heard many times in the past. I turned around and saw Shiroya coming out of the left corridor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't have time to act surprised or throw a bunch of questions at her before she spoke.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, you're here. I found something.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Completely unfazed, she opened the transparent door and entered the first partition. I was left outside, utterly bewildered.{w} Without looking back, she stepped to the next door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How was that her reaction after seeing me? I was too shocked to follow her. Even though my confusion had only intensified, I was at least glad to see I wasn't alone, and she had appeared from the left corridor...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked over to it. I knew an extra door was located at the end, so I approached it, wondering if she'd come out of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it was still locked, and there was nothing out of the ordinary about it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Trying to decipher what she said, I ran back to the door of the offices and entered them in a desperate attempt at understanding.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The first partition was empty. So was the second one. A chill ran down my spine when the third one didn't appear any different.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I froze for a few seconds, questioning what had happened to me and Shiroya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I recalled teleporting from one place to another. She couldn't have disappeared from the offices, could she? I exited them to look at the other corridor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was nobody there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Dumbfounded, I went down the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was nobody on the outer part of the fifth floor, so I looked through the partitions.{w} The three of them were empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I was about to make it out, I stopped myself in the middle partition, far beyond confusion. What the hell was my objective?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hadn't I just found Shiroya and been completely ignored? She'd acted as if I was a ghost and moved on only to immediately disappear again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been in continuous motion since we'd gotten trapped, but that was the first time I couldn't settle on an objective to pursue. I took advantage of it to sit on a chair for a little while, attempting to calm my alarmed heart down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it was useless. I thought about what had happened and felt as if I was driving myself crazy. What could I make of Shiroya's behavior after feeling like I'd literally teleported? It was insane, and I feared there was something wrong with me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After a while, I knew I had to continue looking around, but no determination came to me. Since I'd already seen Shiroya, everyone else should've been nearby, so I kept moving down the floors.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went to the fourth floor and looked through it. I slowly moved down to the third and repeated the same process.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't see any signs of life.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I repeated the same inefficient movements on floor 2, and yet again, the result was the same. The crystal floor, where my lonely adventure had begun, was the one that remained.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Surely anyone would've been able to make it past me while I'd been looking through the offices, so I couldn't even be certain nobody was above me, even less so having spent minutes inside one of them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know where to begin, but I quickly spotted an obvious point. After peeking at both hallways, I saw an open door in hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It belonged to the room where we'd found Naomi's corpse—where I'd last seen the others.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I approached it, but I couldn't see what was behind it through the small gap.{w} As I approached, I started to hear something. There were voices, ones that sounded shocked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The doorknob was finally in reach. I ignored it, simply pushing the door open, and a very familiar sight appeared before me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What...!? How did you...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Where the fuck did you go?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Shiroya rushed to me and asked the same thing. Meanwhile, I looked at the six pairs of eyes focusing their most intense gazes on mine. ...On the floor, Naomi still lay in her own blood.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I-I don't know? What exactly are you asking me?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Just a minute ago, you were looking inside that cabinet. How did you make it out of the room?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: "Just a minute ago"? Were they messing with me? There was no way Shiroya would...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...You mean to say that I disappeared from in front of the cabinet?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Atsuki, don't fuck around. We don't mean to say that you disappeared, we're asking you how you did it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I didn't do anything. I touched the Sekimeiya and instantly appeared in hallway A.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Excuse me?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We were talking about how you were the true culprit of this murder. You clearly did something to shift our focus.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Wait a second, though. What's in this cabinet is not the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Huh? I'm certain it was. I touched it and felt a burn on my fingers.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Not the one we saw earlier, at least. Look.
entries.speaker: sai
