entries.text: He put his right arm inside the cabinet and removed it, holding an object that looked very similar to the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah. That's the only thing that was inside.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I have no idea how you made it to the hallway. There's nothing else in the cabinet.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: My eyes were still directed at the Sekimeiya in Sai's hand. It no longer glowed at all, and it was gray.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm telling the truth. Wh-What I found in the cabinet looked like the Sekimeiya we'd seen. I saw it glowing in the dark.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I had to explain myself however I could, but I had no concept of what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But this thing doesn't glow. Katei says he doesn't know what it is, even though that means nothing.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I'm telling you what I know. This Sekimeiya was never here.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Atsuki, let me try to understand what you're saying. You mean that when you touched that thing, you teleported outside?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...{w}Th-That's what it felt like.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Everyone looked skeptical, but they remained quiet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...You weren't here by that point yet, though. When I found myself in the lobby, I entered this room and only saw Naomi's body on the floor.{w} I went up to the sixth floor to find you and eventually went back down. That's when I just found you here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I felt strangely uncomfortable while I attempted to explain myself. I sounded crazy, and if I wasn't, they were the ones tricking me. The only explanation was that I'd been knocked out in some way and they were acting as if it had just happened seconds ago.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Isla, still between Erina's arms, looked the least dubious of me, but she still seemed to be trying to process that her friend's prediction hadn't come true.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, you want to make us believe that you traveled to the past. That's impressive.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: "To the past", right. That was the conclusion to draw from what I'd said.{w} Not only teleportation, but time travel too. It was a ridiculous claim even if they'd really seen me disappear.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you hearing him? I bet you all thought he was innocent before seeing his true colors. You can't honestly tell me you believe a word of what he's saying.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then how do you think he escaped from this room? I... I saw him vanish with my own eyes, and I believe we all did. You told us there's no hidden paths in these rooms.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Tell us, Atsuki. How did you do it? There is a security camera here, so your trick has been recorded. Are you going to claim ignorance and state that you traveled to the past?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Did I travel to the past? I couldn't have. That's impossible.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Even if such a thing were possible, would everything hold up?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I have no idea what caused it, but if the others didn't knock me out, I must've teleported in some way. I guess traveling to the past only adds a bit more impossibility to that.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: At least, one thing would begin to make sense if that's what happened. Earlier, when I looked in this room, Naomi was already dead. Didn't Katei say this? That I was on this floor during the time Naomi died?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Through normal means, I wouldn't have been able to be on the crystal floor. I was upstairs, and I would've been noticed if I'd headed down. This would make it possible.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It would be absurd to immediately justify Katei's accusation like this, but it would explain why he decided to make such a nonsensical claim in the first place, and it would make a lot of what he said believable.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I'd seen it countless times: time travel appearing out of nowhere to construct crazy events. I'd experienced many stories that were ruined by such an exploitable mechanic. Thinking about it, I felt as if the same thing was happening to my reasoning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I couldn't explain my own experience, did I have to assume that time traveling was possible? Had it been a factor the whole time?{w} I thought about the full sequence of events up until that point. If they were somehow related to time travel, how were we supposed to think about that?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What would be more reasonable? To deny its existence and ignore my unexplained experience, or to think that it could be possible?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I felt no enthusiasm thinking about either option, so I thought back on the previous few minutes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How would this even work? Whenever time travel comes up, the word "paradox" is usually thrown all around. Depending on its rules, the way time travel works can greatly differ.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: One simple type of paradox is the famous "going back to the past and preventing your birth". Would you instantly disappear, or would you live a life in a world where you never existed? Either way, the past was changed.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: On the other side is the bootstrap paradox: you find a key, open a door with it, find a time travel machine inside, use it to go back to the past, and finally place the key on the floor so that your past self can find it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: In that case, did time travel matter at all? The past was not changed, so by traveling back, you only understood how it all came to happen. Essentially, it's a loop without a starting point, and it only occurred because it occurred.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That's a concept far from sensible. It could come in handy to justify grand motives in a story, but it's nothing short of completely impractical.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: However, no matter how I feel, I think that everything points to this direction: that if I have just traveled to the past, I haven't actually changed anything. It seems like I just reexperienced the events I previously lived.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The starting point seems to have been making physical contact with the Sekimeiya. As nothing that I did once I arrived in the past directly led to my travel, I'm not sure I'd quite perceive it as that kind of paradox.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Looking ahead, though, it seems that I unconsciously repeated the past I had lived with Shiroya.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "Just a minute ago, you were looking inside that cabinet." According to this, I can draw that I supposedly went back about twenty minutes to the past. That's the time I estimate I spent confusedly looking around for people.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: By that point, Naomi had already been killed. Shortly after, I took the elevator that was on this floor up to the sixth.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: This cleanly holds up with what we experienced... At that point, the elevator was on the crystal floor, as it had probably arrived there when we'd heard it on the fifth.{w} Then, when I went up to the sixth would be when Shiroya and I rushed to follow it up.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: What the hell is this? Did I, without being aware of it, replicate the past I'd experienced?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I think that something curious happened when we chased the elevator up. If the elevator hadn't been empty, we had to assume that whoever went up entered the attic. The only other explanation was that the person inside vanished.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But... it seems that what I just went through explains what actually occurred.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I got out of the elevator and looked through the sixth floor. The corridor appeared empty, and I spent a bit of time inside the offices.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: As I was there, Shiroya and another version of myself were chasing me. They called the elevator to the fifth floor, but as I saw earlier, that wouldn't have made a noticeable sound from where I was.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Then, as I remember, the previous me stayed next to the elevator while Shiroya looked through the two main parts of the floor. She also mentioned how she'd first looked through the opposite corridor.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: She and I saw each other when I was about to continue looking for people. She was about to look through each partition.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That's why she reacted the way she did. From her perspective, I should've been next to the elevator, but where she found me, my job still would have worked. From there, you could still prevent anyone from escaping, so she thought I had moved from next to the elevator to outside the offices.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So, to her, it appeared as if the floor had been empty. She didn't realize that she'd actually seen the person who'd brought the elevator up.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Oh, you're here. I found something.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That was her reaction when she thought I'd slightly moved.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Similarly, when she was done investigating, something she said did throw me off a little.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But look, this is what I wanted to show you.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She was referencing what she'd told me just before that point, unaware that she wasn't talking to the same person.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When she reacted coldly to my presence and said she'd found something in the corridor, I thought I had to look at it, so I went to check. During that time, she confirmed that the offices were empty.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I didn't see anything of importance in the corridor because what she had found was the attic door itself. I entered the partitions to demand a further explanation, but she was already talking to the previous me, next to the elevator.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When I left, the two of them had gone around to inspect the door they'd just discovered.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And later, I spent a few minutes inside the offices of the fifth floor, so I didn't notice Akaro going up or the three of us going down.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: After a while, I continued looking through every floor until I reached the point I'd traveled from.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...Even though I couldn't easily accept such a concept, it neatly explained many things.{w} Was it all a ridiculous coincidence...? A trick, maybe?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Insulation
...Do you intend to answer?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'd briefly fallen silent. Once I'd thought of the possibility, answers had quickly fallen into place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Something so outlandish certainly sounded impossible under any normal circumstances, but the simple fact was that it had happened to me. Unless there was another explanation I was missing, there was no choice but to accept it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I... don't have a reason to deny that traveling to the past seems to be the most likely answer. Rather, it's the only one.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Pathetic. You were accusing me of being a bad liar, Sai?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: If that was truly what had happened, it also meant that Katei had to be the killer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The elevator going up was my doing, so there'd been nobody else on the first floor. Nobody had gone to the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But a line of reasoning that time traveling demolished was another one that it created. That was the can of worms that thinking about possibilities involving time travel opened.{w} After all, I had randomly teleported to hallway A. Someone could've been on the same floor, killed Naomi before we'd thoroughly investigated it, and then traveled through time to an entirely different place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was still one thing to keep in mind: the first time the elevator had gone down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was possible someone had been in the attic before we'd heard it. They could've gone down with the elevator, killed Naomi, and then traveled to the past, back inside the attic. Thinking about tight possibilities with such uncertain and volatile mechanics was impossible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So according to you, his claim is as bad as or worse than yours, but yours were all easily disproven. Can you give an alternative to what Atsuki's saying?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you going to tell me that because I don't know how he made it out of this room, he must've time traveled? For the love of God, Sai, and you were trying to act smart?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, let me tell you something. If Atsuki didn't time travel, he can't be Naomi's killer. If he did, though, it's still an option.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai and Shiroya had realized the same thing. I was really there by the time she died.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Okay, it might happen to explain that Katei saw Atsuki here, but it doesn't make it any less insane.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Hm, why not? I think it makes sense.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...What? Don't be crazy. We can't use time travel to explain anything...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Why not?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I'd say that's a fair question. By the way, it seems Katei was right about something. The Sekimeiya appears to have broken, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We were all taken aback by that question, but we quickly understood what he meant. It had changed colors to a much less pleasant gray.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: See! This is all because it was removed from the cabinet!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Are you sure? It was still white when I saw it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Go ahead and prove that. Did you put it there and just want to avoid facing the consequences?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Shut up. God.{w} This is what Atsuki asked about earlier. It's a function to regulate the cabinet's temperature, is it not?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes, but it's set to room temperature.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It's slightly damaged, though. And let's think: out of all of us, who would hide the Sekimeiya in a place that has a cold temperature function?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Even when I'm proven innocent, you still insist on suspecting me.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: This guy was scared out of his mind at his bosses, remember? He would be dumb enough to hide the Sekimeiya here after he told us that story.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Do I have to repeat it? The cold function wasn't activated.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Who cares about that? It was still hidden here of all places. You'd also be the only one to know about the function of the cabinets, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What? Didn't Atsuki notice it too? That's why he appeared intrigued by this cabinet while he was being accused, acting as if he'd found the Sekimeiya he hid. I bet he put it here to frame me after I explained the cold rule.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...That's not at all what happened, and the cameras will eventually prove it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm sure they will. For now, let's hurry up and put this thing where it belongs. Just in case it's not too late.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yeah, sure. We can try that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Holding the Sekimeiya in his hands, Sai closed the cabinet, which made a metallic sound as if it had locked automatically. Then, he left the room followed by Katei.{w} Shiroya was still unsure of what to say, and Akaro and Erina both looked at me with uncertainty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were in front of the event room. I squeezed my eyes shut and rubbed at the bridge of my nose, remembering that someone in the building had actually died. Things were moving too fast. A death, moving through time after touching a gem...{w} But it would have been even more dangerous to stop thinking. Before I entered the room, I realized that something else went against the theory that Katei hadn't killed Naomi.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai was holding the Sekimeiya with his hands. However, I recalled feeling a painful burn on my fingers during the split second before I'd disappeared from the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At that moment, the Sekimeiya was glowing white, so if that was still the same object, it meant it had changed colors as soon as I'd traveled. In other words, it had powered off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, if anyone had consciously vanished from the first floor after killing Naomi, it should've powered off just like it did when I'd been the one to travel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't know how it worked, but the fact that I'd seen it glowing might've indicated that nobody had traveled before me—that Katei was the only suspect.{w} In addition, the Sekimeiya had been inside a locked cabinet. To travel and leave it inside, the culprit must've had to shut themselves inside it and then touch the Sekimeiya...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was another problem, though. I didn't think about it until we'd all entered the room.{w} "Touching the Sekimeiya made me travel to the past". Ignoring how an item with such an obvious power could've made it to a place where they'd let us touch it, something directly contradicted its powers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Earlier, Isla had touched it inside its cabinet, and so had Shiroya. Following that, Sai even took it out of the cabinet while holding it with his hands, and none of them teleported at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was I the difference? Since I hadn't touched it back then, I couldn't discern whether the differing factor was the person to touch it or something about the Sekimeiya itself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe it wasn't actually powered off. It could be that Sai couldn't travel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Can I touch it again?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Of course. Have at it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He handed me the gray gemstone.{w} I felt no burn, and I remained where I was. However, I was able to appreciate the smooth surface of the Sekimeiya, which definitely hadn't disappeared with its beautiful white.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're putting on such a pathetic show. You should know that.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You're beginning to get on my nerves. I know how crazy I sound, but if anyone's been putting on a pathetic show from the start, it's been you.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, he caught you.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: This is unbelievable. Put it in the cabinet already.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I didn't want to argue further, so I opened the glass covering and placed it inside. The colder temperature became easily noticeable as I left it on top of the cushion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then I closed it again, and everyone remained staring at the mysterious source of the day's incident.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What? Did it change back?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It did...?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Yes! It's white!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: We all saw it firsthand. A couple seconds after I put the Sekimeiya in the cabinet, it regained its old white glow.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's interesting. The temperature brought it back.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's it, then. We must not take it out of here until the front door opens. It's clear that will bring us a bunch of issues with Ashiya.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei, this thing made Atsuki travel through time. Can you shut up for a second about goddamn Ashiya?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You were right. The cold fixed it, so isn't it strange? According to your story from earlier, the original discoverer of the Sekimeiya realized the cold was needed.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If this can send you to the past, they must've certainly touched and tried all sorts of things to keep it stable. Could they have not noticed its power?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What power!? Kid, this thing will not send you to the past! Something like that is impossible!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Didn't we touch it earlier? Isla definitely held it, and nothing happened to her.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's true... Why didn't it make me go anywhere?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Because it's just a gemstone!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, it appears to have fixed itself. Shall we test it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm beginning to wonder if you process any of what I say. We're not taking this out of here again.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Okay. Sure thing.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai's insincere reply left us with a few seconds of silence. Erina was the one to break it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Isn't that a lock?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I tilted my head to look at where Erina was pointing. Under the keyhole, on the left side of the cabinet, there was a small arrow directed to the word "unlocked", with "locked" being right under it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's just indicating the status of the cabinet, right?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Let me see.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: With a finger, I rotated the dial. It didn't appear to move at first, but as soon as I applied a bit of pressure, it gave out and locked itself into place with a click.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did that do it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sai, next to the glass, tried to scroll it down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I think so. I did hear a sound coming from here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I attempted to set it back to "unlocked", but it was impossible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You must actually need the key for that.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So we can lock it manually but not unlock it again. That's almost fair.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei, you work here, right? Did you not know about this mechanism with how much you've insisted to keep the Sekimeiya inside?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I didn't. It seems changes were made to this cabinet, as the others don't possess this function.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, congratulations. You did it. Now we'll have to keep it here for the remainder of the day. Ashiya will be pleased.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Since we'd evidently not looked through the cabinet well enough, I inspected it further. Shortly, I noticed something else.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's an outlet behind it, and the cabinet's connected to it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Of course. It's needed for the temperature regulation. Every cabinet with that function has to be connected to a power supply.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It had already happened a few times, but once again, the immediate shock of hearing something we couldn't have heard infested the room. From outside, we all distinctly heard the sound of a door closing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...That was a door, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shit, there's actually someone else here!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We all hurried to open the right door, but we were stopped by Sai.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What are you doing? Someone look at hallway A too!{w} The staircase is there, so we can't all leave from here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai, Shiroya, and Akaro exited through the right door since they'd been next to it. I'd been to the left of the cabinet, so I went with the others through the left door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As usual, hallway A appeared empty. We'd continuously done the same thing, but it seemed we had to search it one more time. ...Was it really possible a hidden culprit had remained unspotted for that long? The question had already come back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Looking through the whole tower left me exhausted, so I moved to the lobby door to make sure nobody was there and to keep watching the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The atmosphere continuously shifted in the span of a few seconds. After looking at the empty hallway C, Erina and Isla entered every room together while Katei checked through some others to speed up the process. My position guaranteed that nobody could come out of a room while the others were busy inspecting them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I sighed deeply. If nothing was found in either of the two hallways, would we have to move upward once again and look through every floor? The door we'd heard couldn't have closed on its own.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Surprisingly, the others were taking a while with every room, as they knew that they all contained cabinets with empty interiors big enough to fit a person. While I stared ahead, I realized that making such an obvious sound seemed to defy the persistent stealth of the culprit.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: About ten minutes later, the search in our hallway concluded. I could hear that Isla, who was still holding up surprisingly well, had slowed them down, constantly asking to stay with the gems for longer. My group came to me and reported the result I'd already seen. The mechanical room still remained unchecked, so since I'd stayed put, I told them to make sure nobody appeared in the hallway while I went to inspect it myself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the way, I looked at the few drawers the reception desk had, which were only filled with papers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Downstairs, I was reminded of the fact that such an off-putting place existed on that same floor. Being alone there was much different from the time I'd looked through it with Sai, and when I considered that I was searching for a hidden culprit that could easily catch me off guard, tension constricted my body once more.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Fortunately, it wasn't a big space, so confirming it was empty was easy. I went back up to see my group where I'd left them, and I saw that the others were by the end of hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I approached my group first. Erina told me that nothing had happened in hallway A, so we regrouped in C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nothing, huh?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yeah, the rooms were all empty.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...So, if a person made the noise, they must be above us right now.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Someone watched your hallway to make sure it was always being observed, right?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes, Sai did. We also checked the bathrooms once we were done.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Who remained outside in yours?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It was Atsuki.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Oh, my friend Atsuki? That's good.{w} Say, did Katei look at any room all by himself?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I did. Are you implying that perhaps I ignored something on purpose?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yup. Stay here. Sorry for slowing the process down, but I can't just take his word for it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai stepped into hallway A. He didn't ask for the rooms Katei had entered and simply went ahead with looking through all of them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't blame him for suspecting Katei, and the rest of us felt the same: there was no complaint besides Katei's outraged look.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After the smoky crystal room, Sai entered the storeroom. We expected him to silently move on to the next one again, but once he exited it, he directed his look at us and showed what he had between his hands.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Upon processing the sight, we ran to him in a daze.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...? Was it in the storeroom?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Held in Sai's hands was the Sekimeiya. It was white, as being touched hadn't changed its color at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes. I found it hidden behind the sofa.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Without warning, he moved the object to make contact with my skin. It scared me a bit, but nothing happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So it's not working now.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Anyway, Katei, did you look through this room?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Yes.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Not only that, but it was the first one he entered.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: That's true, I remember.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But that's because it's the farthest room from this side. I was looking for a person, so I didn't look behind the sofa.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What a convenient excuse.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Do you actually think I hid it? I couldn't have done that. We locked the cabinet.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Atsuki, was Katei the last person to exit the event room? He might've had a key.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't know, but we all left very fast. I don't think he could've had the time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Someone stay here. This floor is definitely empty, but we need to check the event room while making sure that nobody can move between the floors.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: All right. We'll stay behind.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Can't we go too...?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Isla, enough. You all can go.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Let's see what happened.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Erina and Isla stayed where they were. That was the safest option up until that point, but as things were, staying in an uncertain spot such as the stairs was more dangerous than moving through an empty floor. It was something Erina must not have realized, but her demeanor was clear: she wasn't leaving Isla alone.{w} Nonetheless, the rest of us agreed and entered the event room once again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I-It's really not here. How's that possible?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Raising the curtain revealed that the Sekimeiya we'd left there a few minutes ago was gone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It shouldn't be, right? We made sure nobody was in the two hallways.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's why I said that the last person to exit must've already had it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Look. It's unlocked.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Of course it is. Katei must have a key.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I already said that I don't have it. There's no way I could've unlocked this cabinet.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Could he even have unlocked it if he had it? Did he enter this room again?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Not that I saw. When they were done, I went to the mechanical room, so he might've had his chance then. Erina would've brought it up, though.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see, so he had an opportunity.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But there's no way he did that, right? Our group was done quickly, so we could've appeared at any moment. And Erina would've had to keep this from us.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It's amusing to see that now you have to resort to this to keep suspecting me. Erina wouldn't lie to you.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Weren't we all liars a second ago? And what else makes sense? Did it disappear magically?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well... It made me teleport. Would it be that crazy to think that maybe it did?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And it unlocked the cabinet too, right? Did the fucking Sekimeiya send the cabinet to the past to when it wasn't locked and just stroll on out of it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I didn't discard the possibility of you traveling to the past purely because nothing else explained what happened. This has a simple explanation: Katei did it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I know that you think he didn't have the time, but I don't care about that. I left this room when he was inside, so for all I know, he could've easily done it, even if all of you are lying.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well, you're free to think that. I highly doubt it, though.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It seems that your reasoning has stopped being so influenced by Sai. That's good, Atsuki.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Now put the Sekimeiya in the cabinet at once. It hasn't changed colors yet.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Fine. There you go.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai put it in the cabinet and closed the glass. It was a slightly funny sight after hearing him say that we wouldn't take it out again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do we lock it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why would we? Katei will be able to keep getting it out.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You can watch everything I do if you so desire. I will never get the Sekimeiya out of here.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You said that Naomi had the only key to open this cabinet, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The only one I'm aware of, yes.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: But she's... The culprit must have her key.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We saw her unlocking the cabinet before the smoke appeared. If the culprit didn't take it, could anyone have picked it up from her dead body?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Sai checked her pulse, isn't that right?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I did. Why, are you concerned that she had a key up by her neck?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No, but only you approached her.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That was after you killed her, though. It sounds to me like you had a much better opportunity.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Sai couldn't have picked it up. I was paying attention.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Thank God someone's competent enough. Nobody else checked her corpse after that, so the key must've already been gone.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why don't we go see if we can find it?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...Sure.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai opened the hallway A door to indicate to Erina and Isla that we'd go check the other hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They're still there, so let's go see if we find the key.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Opposite to the event room in hallway B was the room where we'd found Naomi—B4. The last time, we hadn't searched her body.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who wants to look for it? I'd do it, but I don't wanna be suspected even more.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Nobody volunteered. Being close to a corpse was already enough for us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Fine. I'll do it, but if I find it, don't suggest that I could've skillfully placed it in one of her pockets.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Go ahead already.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai started feeling every pocket of Naomi's clothes. It didn't take long for him to find something.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Here, these are keys.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yeah, this is the pocket where she had the cabinet key.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Sai was holding a keyring containing three keys: two big ones and a small one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's none of those. They wouldn't fit.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yeah, that's what I thought. Do you know what these three open?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That one opens the door in the floor 2 staircase. I don't know about the other two, though.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So she doesn't have the key for the cabinet?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Let me keep looking.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai searched through the remaining pockets, but they were all empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It seems not. Her killer took the cabinet key after killing her, and we know who that was.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei looked at me while everyone else looked at him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't try it again, Katei. You must have killed Naomi and then unlocked the cabinet with her key. You've proven yourself to be quite stupid a few times, so you must've hidden the Sekimeiya in a room you looked through hoping we'd ignore it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's ridiculous. I'd have no reason to do that, let alone the time. It's baffling how you don't realize only Atsuki could've done this.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...What now?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You killed Naomi, so naturally, you got your hands on her key. Then, while you were looking at hallway A from the lobby, you went to the event room. You unlocked the cabinet and left the Sekimeiya in a room I had searched in order to frame me. There's no other way.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Don't you know how risky that'd be? He could've been seen at any time.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Likewise, if you intend to blame me, you're implying I took the same risk.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The difference is that Atsuki had a reason to move it: to frame me. If his plan succeeded, I would've been the main culprit. However, by hiding it, I wouldn't gain anything.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Neither of your motives are enough, and Atsuki would've been more likely to be seen with the Sekimeiya. You're not going to convince anyone.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why don't we do a thorough search, then? Let's search each other to see who has the key.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Of course not. Nobody would be dumb enough to keep it on themselves. I bet you already disposed of it in another one of the rooms you inspected.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Even though he said that, I still showed my empty pockets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki doesn't have a motive. Please, stop accusing him... There's so much blood, so this is where everything happened, and to do this to someone in front of a camera... You'd need to have a real reason for it.{w} We need to find the person who did this to Naomi. They made that noise earlier...{w} L-Look at Naomi's face. She must've been terrified, and being afraid of this happening might even be why she hid from us.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You said that, right, Akaro? That she looked preoccupied when she appeared. She didn't do anything, and the real person responsible took her life.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: And why would they do that? It's true that she looked like the culprit, and that's why I still think she was. By killing her, they'd only be confirming that she was innocent.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Or involved in a way that's harmful for them. We need to know what happened to her and find who's actually behind it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...We shouldn't leave her like this, though. She doesn't deserve to spend eleven more hours lying face-up with that expression.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What, do you wanna cover it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Isn't that... what you do for corpses?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We should prioritize maintaining the crime scene.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't think so... She died in this room, and cameras recorded it. There's nothing to preserve, and we can give her some dignity.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Her stance was understandable, and nobody wanted to argue against it. It was possible I'd get in trouble for it, but I went ahead and detached a curtain from a cabinet and laid it over Naomi's body, covering the face that communicated how she'd spent her last moments.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Thank you... I'm sure she would appreciate it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm not sure that was a great idea, but now let's make sure to find the person who did it. Doesn't it feel like they're taunting us, making noise to let us know they're there and refusing to appear?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: But even so, they wouldn't have had a chance to move the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Can we really be sure? Our priority should be to find them. I don't think any of us did this. There's a real culprit who murdered Naomi and is responsible for the Sekimeiya vanishing. ...Who knows what else will happen if we don't stop them immediately?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I don't know how they did everything or how they weren't found, but we have to hurry. They're somewhere on a higher floor right now, so let's find them.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We left the room behind, and with it Naomi's corpse, which lay under a beautiful red cloth. She had lost her life in the tower with us, and yet we knew nothing about her or the identity and intentions of her murderer. I was trying not to let it get the best of me, but my mind was all over the place. I couldn't allow anything to happen to me and Shiroya, and the moment I'd instantaneously moved between places kept replaying in my head.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We met up with Erina and Isla and summarized the few conclusions we'd been able to draw. Once again, we had five floors to go through.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Were we going to find anyone a second time? It must've been almost {time=11}, implying that someone might've been able to remain unseen for two full hours.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is starting to get old, so let's be fast. This person only wants to hide from us, and they're also being recorded by cameras, so our only goal is to find them and question them.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Since it couldn't have been any of us, splitting up won't matter. Everyone make sure a floor is empty and then stay somewhere outside the offices. This way, someone who's hiding can only escape by moving between floors, and they'll be easily spotted.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: After a few minutes, it'll be impossible not to have found them, so we'll all move back to this floor with that person in tow.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I don't think this is needed at all.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We went up the stairs, following Akaro. If none of us were the culprit or had ulterior motives, then the plan would work. It was only slightly faster than moving up progressively, but it'd be equally successful.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'll stay here, then.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Hm.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...Actually, never mind. This arrangement of yours is a great idea.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: After we checked that nobody was in the bathrooms, Erina and Isla were left behind on floor 2, free to enter the partitions. Sai said he'd inspect and wait on floor 3.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll look through this one. The rest of you keep going up.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: With Akaro staying on the fourth floor, Shiroya and I remained on the fifth. Katei was left with the last one, and he said that he'd make sure nobody could stay hidden there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We easily looked through our three sections. There was nobody there, so we stayed next to the elevator.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'll have to wait, then.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We can head downstairs whenever Katei comes back.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We have to find someone this time, right? Someone must've been on the crystal floor when we heard that noise.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'd say so. Unless they can make it to the attic, the only way we could miss them is if someone purposely covers for them.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you tired? When did you wake up yesterday?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sometime in the afternoon. I'm okay, though, just a bit hungry.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah, I'm the same. I'm glad I ate a bit before leaving. Do you not carry cereal bars with you anymore? You always used to have one or two in your purse.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That was at school. I brought the ones I had when I came over, but I finished them off a few days ago. I wouldn't be surprised if they stopped people from bringing food in here anyway.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Right. I didn't think about that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I was thinking that if we want to go find that old cabin, we could do it tomorrow. It hasn't snowed in a bit, so that should help us get there. It was pretty far.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Are you sure it'll still be there? I don't think I remember how to get to it, and I'm sure it's changed a lot since then.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It wasn't that fragile of a cabin. I'm sure it held out against the weather, but maybe the door is buried in snow. We'll have to see.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You know, I thought of something earlier. Do you remember Danny?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Danny?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Danny the tiger.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Oh! That stuffed thing? Yeah, of course. It's been forever since I thought about that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I haven't been able to find him in years. I just thought that maybe I left him in that cabin.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You think so...? You definitely brought him there a few times. Maybe I left something there too. Now I want to go even more.{w} Katei didn't mention a cabin in his story, but I'd be shocked if it was the same place. There are probably a few similar fields on that mountain.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Mmm. I'd be happy if we could find him. I used to have him with me all the time.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah. We'll get through this. We'll find the person who made that noise and put an end to everything. There was a pretty big couch in the lobby, so you can probably rest there if you need to.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya didn't reply. I was forcing myself to be optimistic and distract her from what was going on, but it wasn't enough. Naomi's empty eyes weren't something she was going to easily forget. She lowered her shoulders, trying to loosen up, but her posture was still completely rigid.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Our arrangement was efficient, but if someone had gone to the sixth floor, Katei could pretend it was empty. Due to the attic door, we wouldn't be able to prove he lied unless we had the security footage.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, it seemed like Katei was serious about finding the culprit. If he hadn't been making that up, he would report his part of the search truthfully.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I thought of him, I heard muffled noises coming from above us. They were incredibly faint footsteps we could hear solely because of the pure silence surrounding us, which indicated that Katei was walking across the sixth floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Do you think I could've time traveled?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Huh? I don't know. It's kind of unbelievable...{w} Do you think you did?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I think so. Experiencing it myself makes me doubt that anything else could've happened.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see... How was it? Did it hurt at all?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Oh, no. It was immediate. Did I really disappear from your perspective?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Yes. I thought I must've imagined it somehow, but my first impression was that you instantly vanished. I actually ran up to the cabinet to check if you fell inside, but I could only see the gray Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: If anyone else said that, I would've left it open for doubt. Someone else could deliberately lie to make me think I'd teleported when they knew what actually happened.{w} But I had to take Shiroya's experience at face value. If I intended to think of an alternative to time travel, I had to factor in her viewpoint as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm also pretty sure I time traveled because of what happened on the sixth floor earlier. You saw me next to the offices and thought I'd moved over there, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, that's right. When I got back, you were next to the elevator again. I was gonna bring it up, but you looked a bit nervous, and I thought something might've happened.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So you were the one who brought the elevator up?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It seems so...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Traveling to the past had caused her search to come up empty, but the circumstances of that were highly specific. For our second search, everyone was watching over a separate floor, so it was unlikely something like that would repeat.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I'm sorry. If I hadn't brought up coming here, this wouldn't have happened.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...You don't have to apologize for that. I wanted to go too.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you sure? Nothing has happened to us yet, but depending on what's really going on, we might be in danger. Someone is... dead.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I feel... horrible about what happened to Naomi, but it's likely she was involved with this plan in some way. There's no reason for anyone to target us.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But we're searching for the person who did it, right? That might be a motive in itself. They killed Naomi in front of the security cameras, so they're not afraid of being recorded. ...And there's also this teleportation.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Not only that, but a lot of things don't seem right, do they? How did the Sekimeiya disappear just now?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Well, someone must have used the key to open the cabinet...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But nobody could have. And if someone did, it was one of us seven. Or, I guess, either Sai or Akaro. You were looking at hallway A, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That sounded reasonable from her point of view. She wouldn't have kept track of Sai and Akaro while she'd looked through the hallway B rooms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes, but that's not really the case. Sai, Akaro, Katei, Erina, Isla, and an unknown person could've still done it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: When I went to look inside the mechanical room, Katei, Erina, and Isla were looking at hallway A. During that time, they had the chance to enter the event room.{w} Although it would imply that they were either working together or threatened into silence.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Similarly, if they didn't keep watching the hallway or were working with an unknown person, that person could've also had the opportunity to enter. That doesn't make much sense to me, and it means that they had Naomi's key even before we found her body.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But what you said about Sai and Akaro doesn't make much sense either because the Sekimeiya was found in the storeroom—in hallway A. Sai and Akaro were looking through hallway B, so they could've opened the cabinet by picking up the key from Naomi's body and then going to the event room.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But then they couldn't have left it inside one of the hallway A rooms.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah. The only way to do that would've been by cooperating with Katei and Erina. When I was in the mechanical room, either of them could've entered the event room knowing that their hallway B companion had unlocked the cabinet, or maybe they let them hide it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So, in the end, the only possibilities are that either Katei and Erina are the culprits, worked with them, or were forced to keep quiet.{w} ...Nobody could've hidden it in the storeroom without being seen by both of them... and Isla too, I suppose.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's right. And if it's true that no more keys exist and they weren't threatened, they must've been behind what happened to Naomi... They wouldn't have been able to unlock the cabinet otherwise, unless they cooperated with someone from hallway B.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: "At least three people are lying to us or nothing makes sense". That was the conclusion we'd come to, and Shiroya looked pretty defeated about it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What you said earlier... that nobody from hallway B could've hidden the Sekimeiya in the storeroom... Could there be a way around that?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I considered that it was Sai. He entered the storeroom and acted like he'd found the Sekimeiya inside, when in reality, he'd had it on him the whole time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's the only way I can think of, but it's not really possible. Technically, Sai could have hidden the Sekimeiya in his hip pack.{w} However, we talked for a bit before he went to examine hallway A, and his back was facing us when he entered the two rooms there.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm sure that if the Sekimeiya had been there, one of us would've noticed. His pack would've looked bulkier than normal.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're probably right. He wouldn't have any other way to keep it hidden.{w} ...So the only possibility is that Katei and Erina did it while you weren't there.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I think so... They must've had the key before we found Naomi, and only Katei could've killed her.{w} However, Katei can't be responsible just by himself since he wouldn't have been able to get the Sekimeiya before I went to the mechanical room. By that point, he was already with Erina and Isla.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: When I left the mechanical room, Erina told me that nothing had happened. So she was either working with Katei, or she was threatened to keep quiet. Nothing works involving someone from hallway B acting on their own, and the only other possibility could be an extra person threatening Erina and Katei to keep quiet.{w} You were with your group in hallway C when you finished, so it's unlikely that person came down from a higher floor. They might've been in one of the hallway A rooms we checked.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm...{w} Someone else was definitely on that floor, right? So that shouldn't be impossible.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's true, and if someone was threatened like that, they wouldn't reveal the culprit's position now even if they found them... In fact, they might still be on the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So... maybe the way everyone spread out on these floors wasn't the best idea.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I can hardly take myself seriously, but I have to think about time travel and teleportation too. I just don't want to miss possibilities, and... ones involving what should be impossible have now become potential realities. I can't deny what I experienced.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I have no idea what the rules would be, but if the Sekimeiya grants time travel abilities, it makes a lot of sense that someone's chasing after it or trying to accomplish something with it. They could know more about its powers than we do—they might've been making use of them from the beginning.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But why would anyone bother hiding the Sekimeiya? No matter what I think, there doesn't appear to be a clear purpose since it would always be trivial to locate it if it's not brought to a locker or the attic.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But let's assume the culprit wanted to hide it in the storeroom, whatever their reason. If they truly did it with the time travel that occurs upon touching the Sekimeiya, it follows that in the future, they'll have access to it.{w} So someone could be ready to go to the past and hide it in the storeroom right this moment. They might intend to make it out of here with the Sekimeiya in some way.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It teleports you to the past, doesn't it? One goal could be to make it to the past holding the Sekimeiya itself or other gemstones. It would appear as if they'd disappeared from inside the tower, and only one of us could be responsible. But I wasn't holding the Sekimeiya when I traveled to hallway A, so how would you go to the past with it?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Avoiding the two hallway groups is more than possible if someone used time travel: first, they lured us out of the event room by making the sound we heard.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Then, they appeared inside the event room from the future.{w} I don't know what could determine the position you teleport to, because I appeared in hallway A when I hadn't been there twenty minutes before, but if the culprit touches the Sekimeiya while holding the cabinet key, they could appear inside the event room with it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Once we were all in hallway C, they got out of the event room and left it in the storeroom while they hid elsewhere.{w} If they had already lived through that portion of time, they could've known the entire sequence of events—that they would be safe in the event room until we found the Sekimeiya. But then they'd also know that it would be found right away, so why bother doing all this?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Regardless, that leaves open the possibility of the culprit still being on the crystal floor. They could've even disappeared by touching the Sekimeiya if it was necessary, and even though it was white when we found it, maybe it didn't make us travel because someone else had just used it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: My initial thought is some sort of cooldown: after I traveled, nobody else could travel. Once the cold restored it, it allowed for one more travel. That still doesn't explain the strange color change it underwent right as I touched it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If we're chasing a culprit who has knowledge of how to disappear and go to the past easily, it makes a lot of sense that we haven't found them yet. It also explains why they're trying to hide from us when we would normally find someone right away in this building.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But the person who lured us out of the event room would've had to go up the floors before traveling to the past, and they can't disappear from there since the Sekimeiya's still on the crystal floor.{w} ...Once again, though, the attic makes it possible.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Nonetheless, if no time travel or teleportation was involved at all in what happened, Katei, Erina, and Isla know the truth of it. If it really was a factor, I wonder how far we are from understanding anything at all that's happened.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Katei's coming.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I anticipated his arrival thanks to the echoing footsteps. He came from the floor above.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did anything happen?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...No. There was no one there, so as we agreed, I stayed on that floor for a while to make sure no one escaped there with the elevator. More than enough time has passed, so we should go back down.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He shot me another incensed look, but I tried to ignore it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If anyone was here, they must've been found.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Okay. Let's go to the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We took the stairs down. Akaro was waiting for us, uncertain of what to do. He also hadn't found anyone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: One floor below was Sai. According to him, the third floor was empty and nothing had happened after we'd left.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The situation was the same on the second, where Erina and Isla had remained. There was no point to it, but as we'd said earlier, we all moved down to the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well. Did anyone find the culprit and let them escape?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Everyone stated that they had found no one. We'd just searched through the entire tower without a result, so the only remaining possibilities were that the culprit had access to the attic, that one of us was lying, or that they'd managed to escape by teleporting through time, which should've only been possible on the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...So that's a no?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We all kept quiet, as we'd already announced our results.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They have to be in the attic, then. We just searched every other floor, after all.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: O-Oh, wait, I can actually think of another place where they could be.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Are you sure...? We looked through the whole tower. The way we did it didn't allow for anyone to hide from us. Where else could they have been?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: There.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shiroya turned around and pointed at the elevator.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, inside the elevator? Nobody went into it, correct?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: No one spoke up. Could someone have been inside the elevator the whole time, banking on us ignoring it?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Which floor should it be on?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We were the last ones to use it. We called it from floor 5 to test which floor it stopped on when we followed it up.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's good. If we left it here, they could've come out as soon as we went up. At least we don't have to search this floor again.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: *sigh*
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Anything wrong?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Plenty. Wait a second.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Following the out of place sigh, he walked up to the elevator and pressed the button to call it.{w} After a few seconds, the orange light surrounding the button told us that it had arrived, and Sai immediately grabbed the handle.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's see, I suppose. There's no way anyone's inside. They would've gotten out as soon as they heard people leaving the floor it was on, and if they'd still been inside, they could've pressed any floor button before this one to stop it earlier.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He opened the door. It was empty, as we'd all expected.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, I meant to ask you something, Katei. The instructions inside state that pressing the stop button will enable contact with an emergency line. Is that possible right now?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No. Naturally, the alarm shuts that down. The line can enable communication both with the outside and the security room, but right now it's disabled completely.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...I'd strongly recommend that none of you touch it. It was originally installed knowing Xyn could try to secure the elevator, but there's no point in that now, and we left up clear instructions.{w} If you press it as the elevator is moving, it won't move again until permission is granted from outside, and given communication has been temporarily disabled, I fear nothing could be done until the exit unlocks.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's scary. We'll keep it in mind.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Anyway, given how long it took to get here, it was on the fifth floor.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You can tell?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Yes. I've never used it, but it's fairly slow. The seconds I counted match up with it being on the fifth floor, assuming it doesn't take very long for the doors to close and to start moving.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That would add five seconds at most.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Which is what I added. I tried to open the door as soon as the button lit up, but since it didn't budge, it must light up before the inner doors open.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But as you said, if someone stopped it before it got here, it would have taken longer. What if it was on the third floor and had someone stopped it on the second?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: No. That whole process would've taken even longer.{w} If it wasn't on the fifth floor, the only way I could get the time I counted is if the door was open before I called it.{w} This is kind of batshit, but if someone kept the door open upstairs and closed it a few seconds after I called it, it would've started to go down later than I expected. That would have made it seem like it was higher.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And why would anyone do that, let alone know when you called it?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No idea, I'm just saying it's possible. Is there a light that indicates someone is trying to call it while the door's being kept open?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No such thing exists.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then it's incredibly unlikely that's what happened.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So it was on the fifth floor, right? There's no point in thinking too hard about this.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Incorrect. There's a very big inconsistency with the elevator being on the fifth floor, but it has to do with something I haven't mentioned yet. I imagined someone else would've figured it out, though.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What is it...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I found it quite intriguing, and I wasn't gonna comment on it immediately if you hadn't brought the elevator up. Let me explain what I heard.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I was on the third floor, waiting right outside the offices. Imagine my surprise when I heard the elevator moving.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wait, the elevator moved?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. Did nobody else hear it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: For the third time, one of Sai's answers was received with silence. Personally, I hadn't heard anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: See, what makes this weird is that I know I heard the elevator three times. Did not even one of you hear it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No one had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You heard it three times and didn't follow it?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Of course not. I didn't know if it was going up or down, and we all agreed to stay put. I also didn't want to unwittingly bite some bait.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Unfortunately, since there's no light that indicates the door's open on another floor, I couldn't know which floors it stopped on by counting the seconds as soon as I heard it moving.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But three times? Surely something must've been happening.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Who remained on each floor above me?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Erina and Isla remained on the second floor, apparently you heard the elevator from the third, Akaro stayed on the fourth, Atsuki and Shiroya on the fifth, and I went up by myself to the sixth.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: And when you went down, everyone was still on their appropriate floors, correct?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: A lot of things could've happened, but some people here have to be lying. After three trips, no matter where the elevator started from, anyone could've gone to a different floor and then back to their own.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes, two trips would be required, and the third one could've been them calling the elevator for the first time.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's wrong. That order of events is impossible.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The elevator was on the fifth floor, right? I could've only heard someone who called it from below me. If Akaro called it from floor 4, I wouldn't have heard it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So, if Erina and Isla called it and then I heard it two more times, the elevator would've stopped under me. And I just determined it was on the fifth. That couldn't have happened.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If anyone above me used it, I wouldn't have heard them calling it. The strange thing is that I heard it three times, and I'm sure of that.{w} This is the inconsistency here: even if someone above me used it, it would not have ended up on the fifth floor because I heard it three times.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It was there initially, right? The first trip was the elevator going down, then it went up, and then down again. There is no other combination that works, of course. Despite that, the elevator ended up above me.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We were a bit speechless, unaware of how to take all that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina, Isla, and Akaro. Are you sure you didn't hear the elevator even once?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I didn't.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...Me neither, but the first time was almost unnoticeable, so it's possible we missed it. We were far away from it.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I'm sure I didn't hear it either.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What the hell? I heard the elevator three times, so it had to be on floors 4 and 2 also three times.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Be honest. Are you just making this up? I'm sure I would've heard it at least once if it passed my floor multiple times.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: There's a way you would've missed it only once, but it's almost as unlikely.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What are you talking about?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We understand, it couldn't have started on floor 5 if you heard it three times. So if you actually did, it must have been on floors 1 or 2 at the start.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: As an example, what if it was on the second floor and then went to the fourth? After that, from the fourth to the second, then from the second to the fifth.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Just now, we didn't hear any sound. We only knew the elevator was here because the button lit up. If it stops on your floor, you won't necessarily notice it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm... So Erina and Isla couldn't have noticed it at all, and Akaro would only have had the chance to notice it when it went to the fifth.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And we wouldn't have heard it either when it stopped on ours.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Well, hang on. This doesn't explain anything. Nobody got off on my floor.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...I'm certain nobody got off on ours either. We were next to the offices, keeping an eye on the elevator from a bit away. We might've missed the button lighting up, but not someone getting out.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yeah, I get that. So whoever was inside the elevator didn't open the door when they came to a stop.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...And what would the purpose of doing that be? They're only alerting us that they're moving.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't know, but you should understand that hearing the elevator three times already confirms that someone moved the elevator before we started searching. It's confirming the presence of a ninth person.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It couldn't have been on the fifth floor, right? It was on one of the first two.{w} Why would someone move it like that when all it does is reveal them?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Maybe it really was on the fifth floor... It's not completely impossible.{w} You heard it three times, Sai, and that put it below you. When we all came back here, someone got out and sent it up to the fifth before we called it. We wouldn't have heard it no matter where it was.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It could also be that it moved four times and you missed one. That'd solve everything easily, excluding who moved it, of course.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You know what I find to be the most likely scenario? That you're all deaf.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: These situations you're all presenting are ridiculous, so let me detail what probably happened.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: When I entered the storeroom and found the Sekimeiya, the rest of you remained in this hallway, next to the elevator. Someone, probably Katei, called it here knowing it'd be unnoticeable.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Excuse me...! Are you blaming me again for something that doesn't make sense?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes. It could've been Akaro, Atsuki, or Shiroya—anyone who later searched above me.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Maybe someone wanted to create the illusion that it was impossible for anyone above me to use the elevator. I don't know.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But this relies on knowing that we'd separate across the floors, all our positions, and that you'd both hear the elevator and not follow it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Not too plausible, is it? It's also possible some hidden culprit moved it down before our search started, but the truth of the matter remains that we looked through this entire building and found nobody else. The sound we heard is no confirmation of anything.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Once we were all in place, Katei used the elevator. He first called it up to the sixth floor, which I heard. Then, he took it down.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Nobody saw the elevator stopping on their floor, but that's fine if he stopped here. I heard it three times no matter what happened, so that means it went down at least once. Since Erina and Isla didn't see anyone coming out, the times it went down must've been to the crystal floor.{w} Afterward, Katei took it back up, to the sixth. He knew it should've initially been on the fifth, so he sent it back there.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's not at all what happened, and I would've noticed that the elevator was far below me with how long it would take to arrive. I just can't wait to show you the security footage once this is all over and see the look on your face.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I also really don't believe we would've missed the elevator three times.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shiroya's right. Even if it was a faint sound, we were paying attention right next to it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I agree. No way we would have missed it.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...All I can say is that we didn't hear anything and nobody stopped on the second floor.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It's clear as day, isn't it? He's just making this up.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Most likely. The elevator was where it should've been, after all. There's probably no inconsistency.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Just in case, all of you take a hearing test after we're out. At least one of you has to be lying—that's for sure.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: According to what you heard, someone got off here, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, and we know what the reason would be. We didn't lock the cabinet the last time, so someone must've realized they had a free path to the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Let's see if it's there, then. If it's not, that'll give you some credibility.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Of course. We're in front of the stairs, so there was no reason to hurry. Let's see what we find.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That time, all of us went to the event room. We'd just looked through every single floor, and even though some things still didn't make sense, it felt pointless to guard the exit.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We entered through hallway A. As soon as we set foot inside, the status of the Sekimeiya became apparent.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: See? It's still here! Nobody came down at all.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's what I thought. You're just trying to have a bit too much fun.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's true, but I did definitely hear the elevator, so I'm not sure what happened. They might've had another reason to come here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm confused. Do you think it was one of us or someone we still haven't found?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Who fucking knows? If it was one of us, it could have only been someone who was above me and is still lying.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If it was someone else, there's one extremely tight explanation: unless someone is still working with the culprit, they would need to have been inside the elevator from the beginning.{w} The elevator would've been below me and not where it was left, but then all its movements become useless.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You might just be mistaken about the goal. Yes, if they wanted to come down here, there was no reason to ever send the elevator up. There's not much reason for someone to stay down here, though.{w} What you heard could've been someone going up to the attic. They get to hole up there and nobody sees anyone coming out.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So this person was in the attic, which is why we didn't find them. From there, they called the empty elevator up, went down once, and finally back to the attic again. Is that it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Maybe, but I have no idea what the purpose would be. They also would have sent it to the fifth again. It'd explain why we didn't find anyone, and nobody would have to be lying.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You'd all still be deaf, and why would the culprit come here from the attic if they'd been here just minutes prior? Surely this same person made the noise we heard?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: This is risky anyway. If anyone from below entered the elevator before they called it back up, you could make it to the attic without the need for the key.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I guess so...{w} Meaning that it's really difficult to explain this unless one of us is lying.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And conveniently, we know of someone who's been lying from the beginning.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Talking about yourself, or Atsuki?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'm not sure what to think anymore. If the Sekimeiya's still here, there's no reason to come down in such a risky manner.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Unfortunately, even though I was allowed to reason things out with time travel in mind, it didn't make them any easier. The issue of the motive was just as hard to settle despite the fact that I could create even more theories.
entries.speaker: i
