entries.text: Since keeping the Sekimeiya in the pack doesn't make me travel, it could be that it requires physical contact with your skin. I'll try to only touch it with my shirt.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He held it in his hand, which was covered by cloth. He didn't disappear, so what he said made sense. Then, I scrolled open the glass for him, and he placed the Sekimeiya on top of the cushion. Finally, I closed the glass again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I suppose I was correct.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Maybe, but touching it has done nothing a few times. It's possible it wouldn't have worked even if you'd touched it directly.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Uh... I doubt it, actually. Feel this.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He touched my arm with his sleeve.{w} It was hot.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't hot at all when it was gray, but now it is—even the pack is. I bet something would happen if I touched it. That's probably why the refrigeration is needed.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But that's strange. We took it out of the cabinet earlier and touched it while it was white, but it was still cold.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Maybe something else is needed to activate it. Who knows?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Whatever. What are you doing here? You should still be in the attic.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And I am. Consider the me you're talking to right now as a ghost.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Are you just fucking with me? You traveled to the past, just like I did.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No way. Traveling to the past is impossible.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're getting irritating. I admitted I traveled to the past, so just do the same.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Don't get me wrong, I would if I had. It's just that I haven't. I haven't traveled in time, teleported, or activated the Sekimeiya successfully even once.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's bullshit. How can you be here, then? It's not possible.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You said I should be in the attic, right? Consider this: what if I touch the Sekimeiya in a bit to go back to the past, then go to the attic? I don't have to be the version that's already traveled. I can be the original.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...So, at some point, the Sai that was around us changed places with you?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Of course not. I was only letting you know that it's not impossible. I'm telling you, just treat me as a ghost you hallucinated. I can't be here, you know? I'm in the attic.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why are you being so stubborn? After Shiroya and I headed downstairs, you did too. Then you traveled to the past, and that's why you're here now.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Except that won't happen. You might not believe me, but it's the truth.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Then how can you be here?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you sure I truly am? Am I not a figment of your imagination?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...You're not.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I suddenly thought of something I could corner him with.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I grabbed Sai's hand. It was definitely corporeal: he was no ghost. Without explaining, I dragged him to the security room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Immediately, I noticed something odd.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai, did you enter this room?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Didn't we all enter it at some point?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Did you enter it during the past forty minutes?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, I didn't.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's strange, because the door wasn't completely shut. And look, the computer isn't suspended.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And so what, I must've entered it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I walked forward to see the time displayed on the computer. It said it was {time=11:57.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I used this computer 47 minutes ago, at {time=11:10.} You determined that Katei wasn't in this room during the attack thanks to the sleep timer, so it must be more than 45 minutes.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes, fifty minutes of inactivity are needed for the computer to power off the screens.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So if we wait these remaining three minutes, we'll be able to see if I was the last person to use the computer. If the screens stay on, someone else used it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Brilliant.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Also, the last time this door should've been opened was earlier, when we searched through the entire floor. We made it a point to close every door when we were done for efficiency, so it would be harder for anyone hiding to move between rooms.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, I saw the computer was powered on, which told me that someone had used it in the past hour. The others didn't pay much mind to it, and neither did you. After that, we closed the door.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So you remember. Good.{w} Despite that, it was open a little bit just now. Someone must have come in here. This door isn't loose, and it won't open all by itself.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes, and? Do you think it was me?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well, I found you in hallway A, and you said you were searching for the Sekimeiya. Did you really not enter this room?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I didn't. And even if I had, would you have anything to say?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not sure yet. Let me tell you the reason I brought you here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Show me your wristwatch.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...My what?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's hidden beneath your sleeve, but I saw you still have it. This is the only room that provides us with the current time, so show me what your own watch displays.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Because it might reveal your lie.{w} Let's say you traveled from {time=12:10.} It's possible the time displayed would now be something like {time=12:20.}
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see. That would reveal that I've come from the future. It's a smart idea.{w} I even said earlier that my time matches the computer's, didn't I?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...You did.{w} If your time's ahead, you time traveled. If it's the same, it's possible that the body you appear with is identical to how it was at that point in time. That would help us confirm what happened with the second Naomi.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What if someone edited the computer's time? It'd be trivial.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well, if someone did that, it would've been you. The door was opened, and the screens are still lit. Although I did check the time fifty minutes ago, so I guess it couldn't have been modified recently. Technically, I guess you could have changed your wristwatch's time instead.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I actually don't even know how to do that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Just as he said that, the computer entered sleep mode.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, unfortunately, there goes your little theory.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So did someone enter this room and not use the computer? There's no way the door just opened.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Who knows?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Just show me your watch.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: My what?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Your watch.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But I'm watching you right now.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He clearly had a problem with showing me the time, so I knew I was correct. I quickly positioned myself in front of the door so that he couldn't escape again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If you don't want to, you can just admit that you traveled. It's not very hard to figure out.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: After he spent a few more seconds in silence, I decided to act first. I grabbed his arm and looked at the miniature screen on his wrist.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What?{w} Did you just do this?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh? What's the time?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Don't be stupid. {tip=9999}It's broken{/tip}.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: E-Excuse me?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The screen was blank. Nothing was being displayed on it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Really...? When did it stop working?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you just fucking with me again? Did you do this right now, somehow?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I didn't do anything. You were looking at me. I didn't even touch the watch.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I couldn't object to that. Even though he'd been buying time, he hadn't touched it at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You might have anticipated I was gonna ask this and disabled it as soon as we entered this room.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It's flattering if you think I did that, but honestly, I have no idea what happened. I've had it for a long time, so perhaps the battery ran out. I don't even know how I'd "disable" it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Let me look at it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I was already grabbing his arm, so I inspected the wristwatch a bit more. It had two buttons on its sides, probably to edit the time and other parameters.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Can you remove it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. I take it off every night.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...You've become pretty uncooperative. Just take it off.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you confiscating it? You've taken a liking to this watch.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: While he continued speaking in his frivolous tone, he handed it to me. I'd gotten curious about what happened since Sai clearly didn't want to show me his watch at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How did you do it? I don't see a power button.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I didn't do anything. It just so happened to run out of battery now.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That'd be a little too convenient.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You can call it fate. Don't worry, though, I didn't have anything to hide in the first place.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: On the backside of the watch, there was a slot for the battery. It took some effort, but I opened it to see a single lithium battery.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How long have you had it for?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: A few years.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: How many, approximately?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Seven or eight.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Maybe it would have run out now, but I'm not sure. Lithium batteries are more expensive, but they last a very long time. They outlast plenty of devices.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hey, you're pretty good. In that case, maybe the watch itself broke.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It looks perfectly fine to me.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Unfortunate, then. I'm curious about what happened too, but it might be a bigger mystery than we thought.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're ridiculous. You know exactly what you did to avoid being exposed.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I think you're the one being silly here. First, I didn't have anything to hide, and second, I did nothing to this watch. I take good care of it, so I wouldn't break it on a whim.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}You know, remember upstairs, in the attic?{w} I looked through a few drawers and found a bunch of useless junk. I believe I might've seen a compatible battery somewhere.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...And you were talking about conveniences. You're pretty insistent.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I want to know what happened. It's not uncommon to have a couple batteries like this lying around. It's also true that I didn't see you mess with the watch, and since it's not damaged, the most likely explanation is a faulty battery or that it actually was time for it to run out. Let's see if we can power this back on.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: This watch doesn't receive the time from a satellite. You sounded pretty convincing earlier when you said that you didn't know how to edit the time. Maybe you just didn't foresee this at all and the battery actually stopped working.{w} If the battery ran out when the displayed time was, say, {time=12:10}, it could pick up from there when we put in a new one—watches like that exist. Also, this watch was working just earlier, when you said it was {time=11:36.} Let's see what happens when we insert a new battery.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you being serious...? We can't go to the attic.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I bet I know why. You're up there and we'd see your past self. Additionally, you don't remember anyone going up.{w} Where did you stay? We could just avoid anyone else.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're getting annoying. I don't know what the people above us are doing.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Let's go, then.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Where did you see the battery?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: In the living room, under the television.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Hm, okay. Let's be quick.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That works.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I made sure to keep my grip on Sai's sleeve so that he couldn't escape. I hadn't disregarded Shiroya, so before moving up, I looked through hallway B and still found no trace of her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I started to get a bit worried. She wouldn't have gone off anywhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd entered the room soon after we'd left, and she no longer seemed to be on the crystal floor... She couldn't have been attacked, could she? We would've heard a yell, and there hadn't been that much time for anything to happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: By going to the attic, I could also check whether she was on the higher floors. For that reason and because the elevator was still supposed to be disabled, we took the stairs up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We circled through every floor without finding her.{w} The attic was unlocked, so we went up the last, narrow staircase and entered the living room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The floor showed we'd surpassed the time we'd gone down—I could see Shiroya's and my own footprints heading out. I looked at them for a few seconds, but it was difficult to determine if anyone had left after us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It should be here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I kneeled down and opened a drawer. I had to let go of Sai's hand, but he didn't run away. He at least seemed to be genuinely confused about what happened to his wristwatch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, here it is.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: All right. Let's leave.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If he wanted to leave, the most likely reason was that he'd lived through that time already and knew the people who were still in the bedrooms wouldn't notice us. If that was the case, there was no point in defying what he'd experienced.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Both of us stepped out of the living room. Before moving down, I looked at the floor one last time, making a mental note of the arrangement of footprints for later.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Will it work?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes, I think so. It should be compatible with your watch.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It was still inside its original package, so it hadn't been used at all. It took me a couple of minutes to get it out with no tools, and as soon as I succeeded, it became clear that it would easily fit. It looked the same as the one that was already inside the wristwatch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I uncovered the battery slot again and removed the original battery. I headed to the first partition and left it in a drawer since I didn't have a proper place to dispose of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After that, I put the new one in place. It was small, so it took me a bit, but it fit perfectly. Finished, I put the cover back on and left the packaging in the same drawer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Anything?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I turned the watch around and immediately saw that something had changed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It did, but I was wrong.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...I told you. I wasn't hiding anything.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's not quite what I meant. Look.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I showed him what the screen displayed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The four digits displaying the time showed a "--:--", which most likely indicated that no time had been set.{w} I would have assumed that the battery removal reset the internal system if not for what was above the time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's strange... It might've been like this when I first got the watch.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: This should be displaying the current date, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...It wasn't.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The date, above the time, showed "9999-12-31".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I suppose there was no point to my plan, then. I don't know if you purposely arranged this, but something definitely happened to this watch.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It still works, though. The battery had to be the problem. Give it to me.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I handed it over, and he began to fiddle with the buttons.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see, I can easily set the time with these.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The time began displaying numbers, and Sai set it to {time=4:00.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I really don't get what happened, but I'm glad I won't have to get rid of it. I'll make sure to thank Ashiya for the new battery too.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I wanted to object again, but I couldn't find the words. I didn't know anymore if Sai was aware of what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You traveled to the past, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Me?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Let's say you appeared in hallway A. I'll even believe what you said: you realized the Sekimeiya was gone and failed to notice it was in your hip pack.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You have a watch, so you would've looked at it to find out how far back you went.{w} Did you do that?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}I didn't.{w} However, I didn't travel to the past either, so your question is pretty pointless.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The date was the odd point. Swapping the batteries shouldn't have changed it to "9999-12-31", and it was unlikely Sai edited it. Needless to say, it was the highest date the format of the watch would allow.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Anyway, let's go back down.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: To the crystal floor?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. I have something to do.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...All right.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We started moving down. I didn't know what Sai planned to do, but I still had to find Shiroya, who most likely was somewhere below us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya's not currently in the attic, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Who's that?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I let it go before he got on my nerves.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We silently walked all the way down. At first glance, the floor still appeared desolate.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What did you want to do?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, let's go to the security room.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Through hallway A, we began walking toward it. His pace was slow, and I'd been in front of him the whole time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once I was about to reach the doorknob, I heard a sound behind me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I saw an empty hallway as I heard the event room closing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Upon realizing I'd lowered my guard, I sprinted as fast as I could.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I entered the event room, but it was empty. By the time I opened the door to hallway B, I'd lost him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every door around me was closed except the lobby's. I didn't know where he'd gone, but as soon as I picked the wrong path, Sai would escape.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Running toward hallway C meant facing the task of searching through every floor, and going to the lobby meant that he could already have been in hallway A. Instead, I opened a bunch of doors in hallway B hoping he'd taken shelter in one of them, as I couldn't hear the distant sound of running footsteps.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They were all empty, and I didn't bother searching too deeply into them.{w} I understood what Sai's business on that floor was. He needed us to go there to have a chance at escaping—he had no way of dodging me on the upper floors.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I sighed. Perhaps I should've expected it, but I didn't blame myself too much. I'd lost Sai, and he'd accomplished his goal of ditching me. Just in case, I went to the security room, where he said he wanted to go.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was empty, and the computer remained suspended. In a corner, I saw the suitcase that Katei had brought there from hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What was Sai's deal, exactly? Maybe I'd have a better idea once I returned to the attic, but I still needed to find Shiroya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went to look at the computer's time, which read {time=12:18.}{w} I sat on the chair and sighed in exasperation for a few seconds. There were plenty of things to think about, but instead my mind went to something that continued to gnaw at me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai's watch. More specifically, the date "9999-12-31".
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When I found Sai, he should've been in the attic. This means that it's very possible he traveled through time in some capacity, even though he kept denying it. If he did, his watch would've done the same.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "9999-12-31" hints at that even further.{w} It's the highest date the watch could display, so it could be linked to another common concept related to time travel: loops.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Looping through time—reliving the same portion of time over and over. I'm jumping to this thought not only because of the date, but also because the battery ran out before the time it was supposed to.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: For example, if the watch is in the process of traveling from {time=12:20} to the past, until it reaches the travel point, the time displayed would increase per travel. If that's repeated infinite times, the date would eventually hit its maximum value and stay there.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If the watch had repeated that process infinitely when I saw it, the date could make a bit of sense. Similarly, every few years, the battery would run out, so replacing it would allow the time to continue advancing.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So, assuming something of the sort is what happened, is it a coincidence that I just so happened to experience the loop in which the battery had to be replaced?{w} There would be times in which the watch would appear functional and ones in which the date wouldn't have reached the year 9,999 yet. All of those would have to reach the same loop point, which contradicts the way I thought this worked, because traveling to the past would end up modifying it in different manners.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But I suppose it's pointless to think about this because a bunch of other contradictions prevent anything like that from ever happening.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: To begin with, if the wristwatch had traveled back insane amounts of times, it would have physically degraded. If it had survived at least the 8,000 years needed to reach 9,999, the metal would've appeared rusty, and it's hard to believe it wouldn't have just disintegrated instantly.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Also, Sai had to be the one to bring it back through time, so he'd be older, and he couldn't have existed for the same number of years without dying. This would be circumvented if going to the past replicated your past body, but then the watch's date and time would reset after every travel too.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: This is not how the Sekimeiya works. If you travel thirty minutes to the past, during those thirty minutes, two versions of you exist at the same time. If Sai went back with his watch that many times, he would have created a new copy of himself each travel.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That isn't all. Naturally, I'm thinking about this to justify the watch's date, but there's no apparent reason why Sai would travel back to the same spot more than once.{w} And if he somehow could circumvent aging, it'd mean that after the point he traveled from, he couldn't exist anymore; if there is a point in time in which he always travels back, he could never make it past that point. Despite that, I'm sure that if I go to the attic right now, I'll see him.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The origin of the Sai I was talking to a few minutes ago should give me some insight, but I'm not sure how much, because he himself seemed unaware of what happened to his watch.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Did the date go up to the year 9,999 for no reason? Was it a malfunction, maybe? Tied with the battery's loss of power, it seems like a bit of a stretch to treat it as one.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The facts are as follows: Sai probably only traveled once because countless versions of himself didn't exist at the same time. The watch can't be in a regular time loop because the Sekimeiya doesn't work like that and because the watch would physically degrade before reaching the year 9,999.{w} And yet the date reached its highest possible value. I really feel that something of significance might be the cause behind it...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: One last important thing I can take from this is that if the watch's status was caused by Sai traveling to the past, adding that he was surprised to see it disabled and that it was working at {time=11:36}, it's possible that he hadn't yet traveled by that time.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I also had to keep in mind that Sai had some good reason to escape from me and that he was in the middle of doing something when I found him. The battery's power running out also felt like it was pretty important, but I couldn't reach any conclusion regarding that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I shifted my focus. I had to find Shiroya, but I'd already looked through the crystal floor twice.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Being in front of the computer made me think of the cameras. It was possible the system had restored, so I tried to see if I could do something with it and find out where Shiroya and Sai were.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I clicked on the program with a security camera icon. The text "logged in as Katei Kuiji" was still on the bottom. When I noticed it, I wondered if Katei intentionally left his account logged in to use the excuse that anyone could've used it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next, I pressed "Initialize Camera Monitoring", but as before, I was met with a message box containing the "Couldn't detect video footage" text. Trying to look at the archived footage yielded no result either.{w} In the lower right corner was a button that read "Power system off", but it was grayed out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was a messy and hard to follow interface, so the only thing I recognized was a symbol of a wrench that was probably the settings menu.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I clicked on it, a panel with several options appeared. One in particular caught my eye: "Footage".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A new screen appeared after selecting it, showing the path where the recordings could be found. The set path was "B:\Archived", which sounded simple enough.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In case the program was the cause of the issue, I went ahead and looked for that specific folder. "B:\" indicated that it wasn't saved on the main drive.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I searched for it, but I couldn't find it. No extra drive appeared to exist whatsoever, so it made sense that the footage wasn't being detected.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kept looking, but to no avail. I performed a thorough search for the word "Archived", but none of the results interested me. The time had been passing fast, and I didn't want to waste any more of it. The computer displayed {time=12:31.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood up from the chair. I had to search through the entire floor, but going to the attic for aid was potentially a better choice. Although I didn't think Shiroya would go hide, searching alone was never ideal.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once I left the room, I was once again met with the cold silence of a barren floor. The door closing behind me didn't echo as well as it should've because the smoke cover on the ceiling didn't allow the sound to bounce back properly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Despite that, I still noticed the sound of someone approaching from hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was Shiroya. As soon as she saw me, she sped up with a concerned look. As if I were her reflection, I reacted the same way.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where were you...!? Are you okay?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Y-Yeah, I'm fine... I've been on this floor, for the most part. I was searching for you.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I went to the room where you said you'd return to, but you weren't there...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You went there? You just had to wait.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No... Right as you touched the Sekimeiya, I disappeared too.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...{w}Those words came as a surprise, so I forced my breathing to remain normal.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You traveled too? At the same time...?{w} Why did I never see you, then?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well... Just as you touched it, I appeared on the second floor, inside the offices. It was disorienting, like I changed places instantly. That's what happened to you too, right? I thought your travel might've somehow taken me along with you.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I couldn't believe it was real... Talking about it and having it happen are two totally different things. Where did it send you?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I appeared in the security room. Do you know how far back you went?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I think so. I spent a few minutes sitting down since I could barely understand what happened... Then I went to the attic to confirm I'd really traveled back in time. When I saw that the door was still locked, I figured it had really happened.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Eventually, I started to go back down until I heard sounds approaching me from below that made me hide on the fourth floor. It was a group of people, so I thought it was us when we first entered the attic.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I figured I could go to the crystal floor to look at the time. I looked at the computer and estimated I'd gone back about forty minutes.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So you opened the door to the security room... We both traveled the same amount of time, then.{w} I-I see... I was in the cleaning room when you came down, so we didn't see each other.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm...{w} The others returned and then went up again. I knew they were going to the attic, so I followed them to see if everything was actually repeating.{w} I didn't go up immediately, so when I got there, Sai and Katei were already in the bedroom. I entered and listened from the hallway, and they were saying the same things as before.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I was so scared of being seen, Atsuki. If the past changes, do things just... unravel?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I have no idea. Nobody noticed me this entire time, so it was all consistent with the past that we know. I think nothing changed. Everything I experienced with people from the past was just me observing them without them knowing I was there, so nothing deviated. I even tried to change the past by saving the second Naomi, but it was useless.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Anyway, Sai and Katei really didn't leave the attic, did they...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't think so, no. I knew we'd be going down in a bit, so I hid in the floor 6 offices. I stayed there for a while so Akaro didn't see me as he went up. Then I came here to meet with you, but you weren't in the room.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I wasn't...? I suppose I might've spent a few minutes with Sai in the lobby, but I thought you'd stay there.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: With Sai? But he was in the attic. What do you mean? I waited a bit in the room until I got worried something had gone wrong. I saw the Sekimeiya too. It was still where we left it, but it changed colors to the gray from before.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So activating it is what powers it off like that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Probably, but I didn't try to touch it again. I closed the cabinet before I looked around this floor briefly, and I thought that you might be back in the attic. I went there, but not much had seemed to change.{w} I stayed in the hallway to listen to the conversation going on in the bedroom. Even if they'd seen me, it wouldn't have mattered much since we had just left from their perspective.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: At that point, Sai was still there, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. He was leading the conversation, telling everyone not to follow us down. Akaro was there too, and he confirmed that he saw us. Sai told them all to wait for us because we'd be responsible for anything that happened after leaving of our own volition...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...I see. So he wanted the others not to come down.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: He kept saying it. He never left, and the elevator was still there with the door open. The conversation started winding down, and when they talked about going to the bathroom, I left right away so nobody would see me.{w} I stayed in the living room for a couple minutes with the doors closed, but I think that they all took that time to go to the bathroom, so I started going down again to find you. I looked through every floor until I saw you right as I was about to start with this one.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Hm...{w} I suppose it makes sense we never saw each other. Five minutes before the point we traveled from, I saw Sai on this floor. I thought he traveled from the future because he was supposed to still be upstairs.{w} If he actually was there during that time, I had to be right in some way. He escaped from me more than ten minutes ago, so I'm not sure where he is right now.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, I haven't seen him anywhere.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I guess he didn't go up.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, I looked inside every partition, so he might've been able to.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I don't know what his goal was, but he's probably accomplished it by now. Regardless, the most important thing is that you were able to travel without touching the Sekimeiya. Not only that, but you went back just as far as me.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I considered that I went back twice as far as my initial travel, but that shouldn't matter anymore since this was your first.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And our locations were also different. I'm not sure why I appeared on the second floor.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah... It could be that it chooses random nearby locations, but that might be a bit of a stretch. It would mean that we could keep trying it until we appear outside the tower, but that recording didn't seem to indicate that will be possible.{w} There's no way it was real, though...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Forty minutes before we traveled, both of us were together, moving down from the fifth floor. It can't be that where we appear is decided based on that position, or we would've appeared together.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, I don't know. The amount of time traveled and the location might just be random.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Both were different than the first time I traveled, but when I disappeared in front of all of you, nobody else went with me. Why did it affect you as well this time?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I thought about this... I was a few steps behind, and I'm sure at least Sai was closer to you the first time. He was walking to you before you disappeared.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: But Sai didn't vanish. From that, we can probably assume that the Sekimeiya has an effective range around itself.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You think so...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Well, even though you were picked up too, it's not like the people in the attic traveled. There's a specific distance from the Sekimeiya in which people can travel if it's activated.{w} The first time, it was smaller, which is why Sai didn't travel.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...If that's the case, are the distance it picks people up and the distance you move through time related?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That was my first thought too. The first time, I went twenty minutes into the past, and Sai, who was a few steps behind me, wasn't within range. This time, I went forty minutes into the past, and you went too despite being a bit farther away.{w} Both times before traveling, I felt a painful burn on my fingers for a split second. The Sekimeiya was searing. I believe the second time it was even hotter, so that could be tied to this as well.{w} Inside its cabinet, the Sekimeiya is kept cold. Once it's removed, it begins to get progressively hotter at an unnatural rate. Sai brought up something like this earlier.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: After traveling, I paid attention to the room where we found the Sekimeiya, but I didn't see anyone hiding it there. We don't know how long it was there, but it should've been outside the cabinet for longer than the first time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It could be something like that, yeah. The distance traveled, the range around it, and how hot it gets could all increment slowly as soon as the Sekimeiya's away from a regulated temperature.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: The place we teleport to still seems to be completely unrelated, though. Despite everything we've learned, I'm not sure if there's some other factor given that it hasn't responded on touch sometimes.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It seems that when it's activated, the energy stored is released completely, and the Sekimeiya turns gray and cools off immediately. I think it starts glowing again after some time, but exposing it to the cold might accelerate that, like we saw. I'm saying this because the Sai I met had the Sekimeiya on him, and it went from gray to white before we put it in the cabinet.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I still don't follow what you're saying about this Sai. We should go upstairs already to see what he's been getting up to. He was priming everyone to suspect us.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, but hang on a second...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I hadn't fully explained to her what I'd gone through upon traveling to the past. The big mystery I'd experienced was still the killer vanishing from the bathroom without being able to touch the Sekimeiya. I'd gotten to the conclusion that, most likely, the bathroom was completely empty when we saw Naomi's second body.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And we'd just learned of a supposed "range". It would let someone travel without needing to touch the Sekimeiya, but they'd need to be close to it. Since the Sekimeiya was in its cabinet at that time, it wouldn't have been possible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was in front of the bathroom when it was locked, so if that was when the culprit disappeared, it would've teleported me as well alongside the others in the event room, assuming that was the source.{w} After we heard the sound, we first searched through hallway A. During that time, is it possible that someone used the Sekimeiya and the range encompassed the culprit in the bathroom? Given that we still found it inside the cabinet after finding the second Naomi, that doesn't seem feasible.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But... there might be one way. According to Shiroya, she returned to room B3 and found the Sekimeiya in the cabinet where I'd activated it, and at that point, Sai had a disabled Sekimeiya in his hip pack. Was there a second Sekimeiya at the same time as another?{w} While the culprit was locked in the bathroom, could it be that someone made them escape with another Sekimeiya? ...Someone who remained in hallway B, maybe? Could it have happened from the second floor?{w} And then, did both that person and the culprit escape to the past? If so, where the hell have they been all this time? This concept of "range" must start to explain what happened...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...Before we go up, let's check the Sekimeiya. Katei might get unreasonably angry if we don't leave it in the cabinet, and something's still really strange.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What is?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Well, Sai was holding a powered-off Sekimeiya in his hip pack right when we both traveled.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm, so there were two of them at that point.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: If the past wasn't changed at all, yes. Sai seemed legitimately surprised to see himself holding it, but it's insane to think that it was put there without him noticing. Even if he somehow traveled from the future holding it, he should've been conscious that he had it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: How would you appear while taking it with you, though?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I can't think of anything. But right now, more than one Sekimeiya might exist.{w} If you had two, you could bring one to the past. You just need to be holding one while you touch the other.{w} I really don't think that can be the answer. The second one would've spawned out of nowhere.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We entered the event room, where that Sai and I had left his Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, the cabinet was empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh... What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What's wrong?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Right, the Sekimeiya Sai had... We put it here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh? Then, did he...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Instead of answering, I opened the opposite door and entered the room we'd traveled from.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You closed the glass again. Did you also put the cushion back in place?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. It was left out, and I put it back with the Sekimeiya under it so that it wouldn't stand out. I didn't want to touch it, and I thought you had to be nearby.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I went ahead and grabbed it.{w} It didn't take me long to confirm that nothing was below it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It's not here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah, Sai must've taken it. Both of them.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: He had the perfect chance and alibi. After he slipped away, he came here. Maybe he hid it somewhere else.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Really? What's he trying to do...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I don't know, but he might have an extra Sekimeiya at his disposal. If he travels to the past holding one, he could appear where I saw him and explain the existence of it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But... like you said, this is a paradox, right? The other Sekimeiya has no origin, and him traveling with it is what allowed him to travel with it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Which is why I think there has to be more to it. We need to go talk to him.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya agreed, and I repositioned the cushion before leaving. Since the elevator should've still been out of commission, we took the stairs up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In a short time, we were in front of the top staircase. Before stepping inside the attic, I asked Shiroya to hold up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I looked at these footprints before leaving. They've all degraded, but I believe these are new.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I pointed at the pair of footprints that looked more prominent.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You can tell? These should be mine since I was the last person to leave the attic. They fit.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I thought so. Meaning that nobody else entered or left through this door apart from you...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We walked in. Nobody was in the living room, but faint voices could be heard coming from the bedroom where we'd been. Upon opening the door, five pairs of eyes fixed themselves on us, and Sai took the initiative to begin speaking without letting anyone else react.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey, you two. Did you enjoy your fifty minute trip downstairs? What the hell were you doing?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We were getting worried...! Why did you leave without saying anything?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Well, we went to check if the Sekimeiya was where we thought it'd be.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What? We left it in the cabinet! Where else would it be? And that doesn't take fifty minutes!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Before we explain ourselves, let me request something. Sai, can you show me your wristwatch?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What? Do you wanna know the time? It's {time=12:37.}
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No, just show it to me.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Do you not believe me? Look.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He turned his wrist around. That was the time displayed on the watch's screen, along with the correct date: "2011-12-15".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you just set the date back to normal?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What do you mean? Why would I need to change it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Forget it. When we went down, we found the Sekimeiya in room B3 after seeing that the cabinet in the event room was empty.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What...? That's impossible.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We all instinctively looked at Akaro, who seemed like the only person who could've done it, but he denied any involvement.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After that, we told them about our respective travels, about seeing Sai on the crystal floor with a disabled Sekimeiya, about being unable to find Shiroya for a while, about coming to the attic, and about Sai's escape. It all amounted to the fifty minutes we'd been gone, but from our perspective, we'd been gone for about an hour and thirty minutes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is a laughable story you're making up. You hid the Sekimeiya and are now trying to blame me.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It can't be... Sai was here the whole time.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Are you sure? Did he ever have the time to go down?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No, he didn't leave.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Sai, do you really not know what I'm talking about?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I have no clue.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: If that's the case, you'll eventually travel back to the past and experience what I said.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm sorry, but that won't happen. You've said that you spotted me in hallway A, so if I ever go back to the past, I'll avoid being seen.{w} It's that simple. You've told me what happened, so you've made sure I won't ever let it occur. If I travel to the past, I'll quickly check my hip pack, so there's no way I won't know I had the Sekimeiya there. This proves you're just making it all up.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I didn't know how to refute that. If he was truly unaware of the events downstairs, he couldn't live out what I'd experienced unless he lost his memory of me describing it. After all, when I saw him, he'd looked legitimately surprised to see me because I shouldn't have been there. If the Sai in front of me traveled, he would know about it, causing that reaction to be either impossible or fake.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You know, Atsuki... Are you sure you're not just creating an alibi for Shiroya? She seems like the most suspicious person to me, given what you told us.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm sorry...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya frowned too. How was she any more suspicious than I was?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This version of myself you describe... It just seems like your imagination. I was here the whole time, so what's with this Sai appearing down there for no reason and clearly holding the Sekimeiya, which told you he was up to something...?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: According to you, Shiroya went back to the past. She knew where to hide the Sekimeiya and was the only one who could've done it. She also wasn't where you agreed to meet, right? This version of myself you saw, who couldn't have existed, is nothing but an excuse to remove suspicion from her. Am I wrong?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're being ridiculous. If anything, I now know you're very aware of what I saw, or else you would've suspected both of us. You know my story is true.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Don't act like a smartass. I just chose to suspect her before you. Are you sure you can really trust her that much? Didn't she have the cabinet key in her purse?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I also remember that she couldn't have hidden the Sekimeiya in the storeroom.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's true! Unfortunately, nobody else could have, which means that someone who appears not to have been able to do it did it anyway. What if it was her?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Don't look at me like that. You're the two people who left us without saying a word, and now you claim the Sekimeiya disappeared from the cabinet. Either you two are responsible, or only one is. I was only trying to trust you, Atsuki.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm going to make this very clear for you, Sai. Don't try to push her around. You can say what you want about Katei, even about me, but you'd seriously better think twice before you go accusing her. She's done nothing wrong. In fact, she's the last person who would ever try to take advantage of this incident, right after me.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't follow.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You don't need to. Sometimes, you just need to be quiet and listen.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I-I still can't believe this is all for real. Are you two being serious? Did you travel through time? Atsuki said it before, but...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yes. I'm completely sure now. There's no other explanation for what we experienced.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm certain too. Somehow, the Sekimeiya has that power.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Listen, if I'd hidden a device that lets me travel to the past, I'd currently be buying yesterday's lottery ticket, not hanging around here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The rules seem a bit volatile, so maybe you're not aware of them. Something led me to believe that the Sai I met never traveled before. Your purpose might be to experiment with it or to try to leave this building with it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Did you lose your mind? How would I get out and still keep it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: At one point earlier, two copies of the Sekimeiya might've existed at once. I'm not sure how that came to happen, but by hiding only one, you could lead Ashiya to believe the Sekimeiya hadn't been stolen while keeping the other one hidden to retrieve it later.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, unfortunately, this second Sekimeiya is just part of your imagination. It can't exist, and it seems both of them vanished. We're not going to take any of this seriously when it comes from the most likely suspect behind this new disappearance.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Do you no longer think an "unknown culprit" is behind this?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's still the second most likely possibility along with Akaro.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It wasn't me. I promise.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We have to go downstairs. If someone hid it again, we should be able to find it just like before.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's true. We keep repeating this, but the cameras are still working. They will eventually expose everything to the police.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Akaro seemed to have gone back to his normal self. He was probably right, but a culprit with time traveling knowledge might not have cared too much about that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do we need to? We can just stay here, where we're more comfortable.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not fond of staying with people I know are plotting something, especially when it's more than one of you. Let's go see what these two are talking about.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We agreed to go down. Meanwhile, I continued to debate whether the Sai next to us the one I'd seen on the crystal floor. If so, how had he managed to trick all of us?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Because if he wasn't the same one, the origin of the extra Sai remained as the hardest mystery to solve, alongside his motive and actions.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Had two Sekimeiya ever existed at the same time? Was that still the case? And if so, how had it happened?{w} I hoped we'd quickly have a better idea of all that, but in the meantime, I continued running through my previous thoughts. We were only four hours into our imprisonment, and we were already dealing with a seemingly incomprehensible pile of questions.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before leaving the attic, we made sure nobody else was there. The elevator was still open, and we left it that way.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As we moved down the floors, we entered all the offices; once we were done with the ones on floor 2, nobody could've been above us. At the end, only the crystal floor remained.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All of us went to the event room, leaving Erina and Isla by hallway A to watch the stairs like before. Shiroya and I had left the cabinet uncovered, so everyone else immediately had a view of the empty interior.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Atsuki, be aware that if this is your doing, Ashiya will figure it out.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's fine. We had nothing to do with it. It must've been Sai.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We waited a couple seconds for his denial, but it never came.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait... Is he not here?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We turned around to discover that Sai wasn't with us. Shiroya, next to the other door we'd left open, peeked at hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where are you going...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Sai didn't reply. When I looked at the hallway, I saw him in front of a door. Even though he'd heard us, he ignored our call and disappeared off to hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck is he doing now...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Katei gestured at Erina to stay in the opposite hallway. Shiroya and I were interested in the room Sai'd been next to, so we approached it with Katei behind us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai! Come here! Where did you go...!?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Shiroya reached the door first and opened it. Inside was the cleaning room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wasn't sure what Sai planned to do, but we'd seen him standing in front of the door. Shiroya and I entered while Katei continued toward hallway C in pursuit of him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He stopped himself, but I saw his arm about to open this door. He was definitely going to go in here.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: There was only one reason why. He wanted to activate the Sekimeiya there after previously hiding it. If he did that, he could disappear without us noticing it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya was looking around while I questioned Sai's ambiguous action. If he'd concealed the Sekimeiya in that room, I wasn't sure why he left upon realizing that we'd seen him. He had the opportunity to give up, but instead, he left for hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Airtight Room

Before I had time to think about it, the dim environment around me changed; a large light was illuminating the much more comforting room. I felt no confusion that time, as I realized immediately that I had teleported to the living room in the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is getting too crazy... What the fuck happened now...?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I knew I had traveled, but I wasn't the one to activate the Sekimeiya. It didn't catch me completely off guard—I already knew that was possible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That meant I had just been in the range of the Sekimeiya. It was most likely in the cleaning room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And Shiroya was probably been the one to activate it, meaning that she should've also appeared somewhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How far did I go this time...?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Once I thought that, I considered some implications of what had occurred. The past hour was extremely dense; Sai managed to appear and disappear, and Shiroya had investigated every floor. Assuming that Shiroya traveled with me, we had both remained unseen for that entire duration. I looked behind me and saw that the door to the staircase was open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Drawn to my noise, a figure appeared from the hallway. It was Shiroya, with a disoriented expression.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh...! You're here. Wh-What time is it...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No idea. You just traveled from the cleaning room, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. You did too?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I did. I appeared here, so I don't know the time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see... I thought I saw something inside the cleaning cart. I reached out for it, and I suddenly felt pain and appeared in this hallway. I think there was {tip=grenades}something else{/tip} pretty small and dark next to the Sekimeiya, but I didn't get to see what it was.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So I did get caught in your travel.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Regarding your question, I think I might know the time, approximately.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The staircase door is open, so this is past the time we unlocked the attic. There are a bunch of footprints next to the door, but I don't see ours. This must mean that you and I haven't gone down yet.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: These are probably the ones that we left after going back up, when we found Akaro in the bathroom. We're not before that point since there are too many.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Then we're all in the bedroom right now?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Most likely... I think we should hurry.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What do you mean?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I started moving toward the hallway as I explained it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I whispered to her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Earlier, you said that you followed the group up, and when you got to the attic, Katei and Sai were already in the bedroom telling us about Naomi's letter. This is happening now, so we're about to head downstairs, and your past self hiding inside the floor 6 offices is going to come up here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's... Right, yeah, and we weren't seen.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We hadn't left any footprints right in front of the door. The ones around the room would blend in with the others, making it unnoticeable that we'd appeared there. In a few minutes, Sai and I would also arrive, and that past me wouldn't pay any mind to those footprints.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Should we take the elevator?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Its door was open. If Shiroya was on floor 6, she'd probably hear it, and she said that it hadn't been used once.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't want to use it, but not only because of that. By going down, my past self who was looking around for Akaro on the crystal floor could see us. During the following minutes, Shiroya and I had inspected every floor and managed to miss each other.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm not sure what we should do. Hiding from ourselves purely because we didn't see anyone in the past seems pointless and kind of crazy, but the only place we can actually stay hidden is this floor.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah... We should probably stay here. Maybe we'll be able to understand what Sai did, too.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She was right, and we had three places to choose from: the elevator, the storeroom, and the other bedroom. We knew every other place would be entered eventually, so of course, we chose the more spacious bedroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As we headed there, our bodies froze for a second.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Coming from the bedroom where our past selves surely were, we heard footsteps approaching us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We knew we had to speed up, so we opened the opposite door and closed it slowly to avoid making noise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What do we do...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: In a quiet voice, Shiroya asked the same question I had. It was my third trip through time, but that instance didn't seem like we'd get much out of it, given how Shiroya had already witnessed the attic the previous travel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was this door closed while you watched from the hallway?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We should just stay here, then. It's hard to believe anything important will happen, but we didn't come back until fifty minutes after we left, so we might have to be here a while.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It was a bit frustrating because the only reason we couldn't head down and suss out the situation was that we'd already done that; we couldn't easily exist on a lower floor. Traveling under those circumstances had turned out to be a literal waste of time, but something was piquing my curiosity.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though there shouldn't have been any danger, we didn't feel safe staying there because someone could discover us simply by opening the door. For that reason, we went up the ladder and sat on a bed above, where we could speak without being easily heard.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took a pillow and shook it, removing a bit of dust from the cover. It wasn't hygienic in the slightest, but I rested my head on it since my body noticeably demanded it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While Shiroya did the same, we were startled by a sound. As was becoming common, it was the sound of a door closing, and it came from the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It must be us...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Right. We'll be back in fifty minutes, then.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Before that thought could become too overwhelming, I began speaking about a detail that I'd noticed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, Sai most likely stored the Sekimeiya in the cleaning cart. He wanted to either activate it or move it. I'm not sure why, but he knew a search was coming.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: He might've hidden two of them, right? I never really got to see it, so it's possible there were two inside the cart. The plastic bag and the light being dim meant I couldn't exactly see inside it, and I only noticed something strange when I saw a glow coming from the inside.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I see. You did feel a burn, didn't you?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes, when I touched the Sekimeiya. It disappeared as soon as I changed places.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Precisely. I think this means that our bodies now aren't the same ones we traveled with. If they were, the burn would still persist, and you'd still feel it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I suppose so...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I think we went about an hour to the past. I'm not sure if this is a coincidence, but that's twenty minutes more than my second travel. First, I went twenty minutes back. Then forty, now maybe an hour. Every subsequent travel has had an incremental increase of twenty minutes.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But I activated the Sekimeiya this time, and this is only my second time.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I know, which is why I still think it could be a coincidence.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Remember what we thought earlier? That the time traveled is dependent on the amount of time the Sekimeiya's not in the cold? That might remain consistent.{w} I'd say we traveled at approximately {time=12:40.} The one before this was at {time=11:50}, and after that, you saw the Sekimeiya had powered off. That Sekimeiya shouldn't have been put in the cabinet again, so if it's the one you activated, it was out of the cabinet for a long time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Right, so we would've gone this far back.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: But the origin of the Sai I saw downstairs still doesn't make sense. He traveled to the past at some point to appear there, but if he did it between this time span, he would have reset the Sekimeiya. You didn't see him going down from the attic, and neither did the others... I can't figure out what happened with him.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Can't he just go back to the past after {time=12:40}?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, but if that's what happened, it means that his surprise at seeing me was fake. It means he knew everything that would occur. I really don't think that's what happened.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm...{w} Well, there's still the Sekimeiya he had in his hip pack, right? Maybe he traveled using that one.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I can't say since the origin of that Sekimeiya is a mystery in itself. If he did use that one, it was somewhere else when we traveled from the cleaning room. It could be that Sai ignored us to go use that one instead...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Both of us sighed. The possibility of spending a very long time there had forced its way in front of us, and if we knew what was going on, the thought might've been a bit more bearable. On the other hand, it was also useful to have information that could protect us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya had apparently recovered somewhat from her grief at Naomi's death, but I was sure it was due to absurdity. Someone dying twice made the whole thing surreal and removed from reality.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I spoke again after a few seconds, as I hadn't yet explained what had piqued my curiosity about our travel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The place we teleport to has seemed random every travel. But if we believe the amount of time traveled isn't at all random, it's hard to believe the place would be.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You thought of something?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Not exactly, but I appeared in the living room while you appeared in the hallway. There was a time when those were our locations, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh? Definitely not an hour before we traveled, right? At that point, we were all in the other bedroom.{w} Oh, you mean later?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes... When I explained to the others what Sai and I did downstairs, I mentioned that we briefly came up to the attic. I didn't elaborate on that, but we went to grab a battery. At that point, you were in the hallway, listening to the conversation going on. That coincides with the locations we appeared at, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I... think so. I didn't notice you two back then since I was paying close attention to the bedroom.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That had to indicate something. On the surface, the location you appeared could seem like something trivial, but with how many things didn't make sense, understanding smaller mysteries could work well to decipher others.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: For example, if we figured out what determined our arriving location, we could predict where we'd appear if we were to touch the Sekimeiya. That could help us decide if traveling purposely would be a good idea.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh... So where we appeared might be related. We went an hour to the past, and at around {time=12:10} both of us were in the attic, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That would hold up, I think. That's around when Sai and I went to the living room.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, you said we traveled at around {time=12:40}, so to {time=11:40.} That means {time=12:10} was the middle point.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Oh, hm... You're right.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I thought about it and quickly found direct contradictions.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's not consistent, though.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: "The location we appear at is determined by the midpoint of the distance traveled". It sounds promising, but it only happened during this travel.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The first time, I appeared in hallway A. I went twenty minutes to the past, so at the midpoint before traveling, ten minutes later, I would've been next to the stairs. That was when I was being told that the Sekimeiya disappeared from the cabinet for the first time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: However, now that I think about it, around five minutes later, at fifteen out of those twenty, I was in the hallway, keeping watch from the lobby while the others looked through every room. That's pretty much where I appeared, so it could actually have been that same position.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I-I see. So you appeared where you were at three-fourths of the distance traveled...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I have no idea. I said I was there fifteen minutes after the point I appeared, but I can't be sure about the exact number of minutes.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: This falls apart in the second travel, though. We went forty minutes to the past, and I appeared in the security room while you appeared in the floor 2 offices. Not only that, but I was sitting down in midair.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We traveled from {time=11:50} to {time=11:10}, and during those forty minutes, I was never in the security room. We just found the second Naomi and moved back and forth between the attic and the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah... During that time, I never entered the second floor's offices either. Well, before we found Akaro in the bathroom, we came down from the attic and searched every floor, but I didn't step very far into the partitions since everyone else was looking too. I appeared deep into the second one, so it can't be from that time.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So we can't get anywhere with this. Appearing where both of us were at {time=12:10} could be a coincidence, but if it isn't, I have no idea what determined it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: As I said that, I thought of another valuable thing we could get out of figuring out what determined the appearing location.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were dealing with Sai and a culprit who had traveled with the Sekimeiya. If the place you appeared somehow depended on a previous location, we could know exactly where someone had been in the past if we knew the location they'd appeared in, effectively drawing information out of them.{w} I couldn't apply it to Sai, since I hadn't seen him appearing anywhere, but it was something to keep in mind in the future.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...After that, the silence persisted. Both of us lay down completely and gave our bodies their needed rest. We had fifty blank minutes in which our existences were isolated from the rest of the world, so we weren't in any type of hurry.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My eyes closed, and I realized that I was a lot more tired than I'd thought. I'd been awake for over twenty hours.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As soon as I thought that, it all came back to me. How we'd spent our past week and everything about Miiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't see Shiroya's face, but her immobile body gave away that she was exhausted too. Our deep breathing became background noise as I subconsciously reminisced about how our life had been until recently.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew none of that would go back to the way it was, but even though I had already accepted it, I still felt the same sharp pain every time I acknowledged the truth.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And instead of moving through things normally, the Sekimeiya had appeared before us. It was still unbelievable, but I'd traveled back through time more than once. It was real, and highly ironic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: During the past two weeks, I'd pointlessly thought about it a number of times. "If only I could go back in time."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every time something negative of significance occurred in my life, I'd resorted to those useless thoughts. They were necessary, though, as immersing myself in a better world often seemed to temporarily alleviate the pain.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While I thought of a world in which Miiya hadn't met such an abrupt end, I could successfully depart from the real one briefly. The only way to truly achieve that, I'd thought, was by traveling through time and avoiding the path that led to her death.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And then, as if the universe was laughing in our faces, time travel had become possible right in front of us. However, instead of reopening the door to the normal world, it created a tangled mess, threatening to trap us in the tower for weeks.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Not only that, but it seemed that even if we managed to solve every riddle surrounding the Sekimeiya, it would be useless for us. Changing the past was not possible—traveling back would just form a loop.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If we were right about the power storage, left the Sekimeiya out of the cold for a very long time, and traveled more than two weeks to the past, we wouldn't be able to change anything. Perhaps that wasn't the real way to put it: something would prevent us from traveling like that in the first place, as it was an impossibility. ...Or maybe we'd travel and suffer an accident before we could try to defy reality.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no way Shiroya hadn't thought of it already. If we went back prior to Miiya's death, we'd just have to suffer it again from another angle.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In my head, as my consciousness slowly dissipated more and more, it all sounded like an outlandish story I was making up. Although, in reality, plenty of time travel stories revolved around going back to the past to prevent an incident from taking place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Be it to save a person or save humanity—I wasn't the originator of that idea. It might have been present within every person; haphazardly thinking of going back in time after a bad experience was fairly common.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I laughed inwardly because something else usually present in those stories had occurred in the incident two weeks ago... Miiya's body hadn't been found.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I would've already jumped into all sorts of possibilities if it had only been that. In fact, Miiya's body couldn't have been found. It disappeared in the blink of an eye due to the explosion that took her life.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Despite that, parts of her had been quickly found. Her jaw confirmed her identity with zero chance of doubt. Her clothes were identified all over the place as well, and it hadn't been anything short of a miracle that Shiroya and I made it out safely without critical injuries.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was why thinking about giving another meaning to the past was also futile. It was the only way to get around causal loops: going back to the past to explain what had happened in a different way. Lamentably, her jaw had been found, preventing that completely.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was aware that I was about to fall asleep. I didn't want to, but I also couldn't resist it. I didn't know if Shiroya had already given up, but she hadn't moved in a while.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Can I not go back to the past, save Miiya, and threaten the forensic technicians to say that they've found her jaw?"{w} Something like that was a complete delusion. Had I already saved Miiya? Of course not. I often used to be optimistic as I fell asleep, and I'd realize how foolish I'd been immediately after waking up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In reality, I'd personally seen pieces of her clothes with burnt skin stuck on them. I could have very slightly embellished it by thinking that they could've belonged to someone else and that Miiya had already been saved by one of my future travels, but I knew that the flesh I'd seen really belonged to her no matter how many imaginary scenarios I intended to make up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The next thought I had was very different.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {w=0.5}...I fell asleep.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: During all my fantastic thoughts, my consciousness had receded. It felt like no time had passed, but I knew better, as sometimes that meant I'd been asleep for a full day.
entries.speaker: i
