entries.text: ...We could all easily have been in the middle of their process.{w} All of us had learned about the Sekimeiya's powers. Then, someone decided to trap us for an entire month and would actually accomplish it somehow.{w} In the future, once the required time passed, they would travel back and exist at the start of the day's events with a full understanding of the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They would cause what they'd once seen, which meant that at that moment, a future version of one of us existed somewhere. It was a bit paradoxical too, but depending on how they would replicate the events they'd experienced, it might've made sense.{w} It was like the first time I'd traveled to the past, when Shiroya hadn't realized that I was from the future.{w} What if we had already found the culprit in one of our searches but didn't realize it? Could they have impersonated their past self at some point?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I might've been completely off, and without the recording's existence, my thoughts would've been vastly different. If it had been faked in order to mislead us, it had proven to be very effective.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If we had to trust it, the fact that the person who traveled brought the voice recorder with them was still crucial. They surely had a solid reason to do that, one I wanted to believe they'd come up with independently. Not just "because they previously experienced the reality in which the voice recorder was brought back to the past".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We wouldn't have food to survive, and there was no way Ashiya and the police would abandon us. However, if the recording we'd heard would truly occur in the future, there was one last thing I had to consider.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I believed that, somehow, it would be one of us who would trap everyone inside the tower for longer than we expected. While it sounded impossible, we possessed the Sekimeiya, which had powers we didn't know the extent of. It was likely that keeping the tower shut would be even harder from the outside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Inside, we had access to the computer that managed the security system—altering the alarm's functions was well in reach.{w} It wasn't that simple, though. Even if one of us permanently locked the exit, the outside would have to get us out in less than a month, as it would become a life or death situation.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They had said that blowing off the shutters wasn't viable, but there had to be something they could do if it came down to it. An underground passage, for example; there was no way shutters alone would keep us trapped for a month.{w} And regarding the motive, I didn't think I was being unrealistic. It might've been to use the Sekimeiya in a specific way, and I couldn't think of anything else. That would confirm that the time traveled wasn't determined with a 1:1 ratio.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If ten stored minutes resulted in a travel of ten minutes, storing more time, or up to a month, would be useless. No matter how much time the Sekimeiya spent outside of its cabinet, activating it would always send you to the point where time had begun to be stored.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I thought of that, I came to a pretty unsettling realization.{w} If that was the motive of someone's grand plan, the Sekimeiya would have stored a great deal of time after a month—at least one month back, probably more. We'd reached the conclusions that the range was likely proportional to the time traveled and that it most likely went through solid objects.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If the range of a forty-minute travel had equaled a sizable room, a thirty-day range would surely reach far outside the tower. That would encompass many people outside, and they'd be sent back alongside the culprit who activated the Sekimeiya. Of course, there hadn't been any reports of a bunch of people suddenly arriving from the future.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The minutes continued to pass, and the mutual silence remained broken.{w} I went back over everything I'd considered, but ultimately, we would have to wait to decide further on any theory. At the very least, considering all those options would prepare me for whatever would end up happening.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't reach any conclusion. Everything that came to mind, I had already thought of.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Waiting like that only slowed our perception of time, but there was nothing else we could do. Shiroya kept looking at her lap, breathing deeply every so often. Erina hadn't moved in a long time, and her knees hid her face from us. Sai's, Akaro's, and Katei's expressions alternated between concern and thought, and they rarely lifted their heads.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: 30 Minutes Later

We remained frozen like that for a long time, during which we all must've been thinking about Isla, Naomi, the Sekimeiya, and the culprit behind it all.{w} The sound that resumed time's march came from one of us. We turned our blank faces and saw Katei standing up, stretching his arms a little.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm going to the bathroom.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: With a faint but hoarse voice, showing that he hadn't cleared his throat in a while, he let us know his destination. Nobody responded to him, so he left through hallway A.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We turned our eyes back down as if nothing had happened. What he'd just done was easy to label as suspicious behavior, but nobody said anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya was in its unlocked cabinet. However, it was kept cold, and Shiroya and I were in possession of the other one. Katei wouldn't be able to activate it and go substantially back into the past. All he could do was move it, leaving himself as the only suspect.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At least, that was what I thought until another sound reached our ears.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll go too. It's been a while...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Without paying attention to our reactions, Sai stood up and left through hallway B, which he'd been closer to. All of a sudden, the two most questionable people had gone off on their own, and they'd closed both doors behind them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It didn't change what I thought: they couldn't go back to the past.{w} Shiroya and I looked at each other, but we decided to ignore them and wait.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was a little strange that Sai had left right after Katei. Perhaps he was still wary of him and wanted to see what he'd gone to do.{w} I thought further on it: was the possibility of one of them going considerably back to the past truly something I could rule out?{w} If everything was as we thought, yes. I'd personally put the Sekimeiya in its cabinet, and at that moment, I felt the cold temperature. After that, nobody had entered the room. It wouldn't have been possible for anyone to unplug the cabinet or take the Sekimeiya out later...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We remained on the floor, waiting for Katei and Sai to come back as we kept every thought to ourselves. The atmosphere had suddenly become a lot more uneasy as soon as one of us departed.{w} Akaro kept looking at the door Katei had disappeared through, visibly doubting him. Erina, on the other hand, hadn't reacted to Sai's movements in the slightest.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Two minutes passed without either of them returning. It was nothing alarming, but every second dragged on. I expected Katei to come back first, so as I watched the hallway A door, I considered how odd it was that he'd left through it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After more than five minutes, I began to worry. I'd chosen not to pointlessly voice my suspicions because of Isla's death, but Sai and Katei might've purposely abused that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll see if I can find them.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I stood up and directed myself toward hallway B. I didn't want to be the third person to leave suspiciously, so I only intended to check if I could see anyone next to the bathrooms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before I could reach the doorknob, the opposite door opened. From behind it came Katei, who quickly saw me and gave me a conspicuous frown.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where are you going?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...To see if I could find you and Sai. Why did you take so long?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I went to the bathroom, so that's not a very appropriate question. ...Did Sai go to find me too?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No, he said he'd also go to the bathroom.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Did you not see him? Also, forgive me for all these questions, but why did you leave and come back from hallway A if you went to the bathroom?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Atsuki, do you not remember what's in the bathroom on this floor? I could have chosen to go to the women's, but I went to the one on floor 2 instead. That's likely why I didn't see Sai.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hm... All right.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Perhaps I'd jumped the gun too quickly, even though Sai's long absence was still on my mind. He'd gone to a different bathroom, so he hadn't had to wait for it to become available.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I resumed what I was doing and opened the hallway B door. I saw it devoid of anyone and with every door closed, including the bathrooms in the distance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't see anyone. It's been almost ten minutes, so I'll try to find him.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Before I could leave, Shiroya stood up and came with me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll help you. I... can't just keep sitting there.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: All right. We shouldn't take too long.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: As Sai had done, we closed the door behind us. I knew Shiroya had spent plenty of time silently mourning our loss, so I understood her—repeating it was unbearable, and I needed to occupy myself with something after sitting for so long. I was sure she felt the same about Sai's behavior being off; he'd openly accused her earlier, so her impression of him had to be poor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's check the event room first.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We headed there and verified that the Sekimeiya was still present. I looked behind the cabinet and saw the cord plugged into the outlet too.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next, we moved to the bathrooms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Although the doors were closed, neither one was locked, and Sai wasn't inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It looks like he really took this chance to do something. If he went to a bathroom above, Katei would've seen him.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I feel like he might've gone to search for the Sekimeiya that we have. It was the one he hid in the cleaning room.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah, it's possible. He's probably somewhere on this floor.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Beginning with the hallway B rooms, we opened every door and briefly searched for him. We'd learned already which cabinets had interiors large enough to contain a person, and after what had happened to Isla, checking them was less due to routine and moreso necessity.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We decided that there was no purpose in checking the Sekimeiya in Naomi's locker since we could've been seen, we didn't want to move it or activate it, and it was possible it wasn't working anyway. Shiroya sounded hesitant about that decision, but I also hadn't abandoned the thought of trying to use it later and find out what had happened to Isla, at the very least.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We entered a room, made sure it was empty, and moved on to the next one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I was checking the cabinets in the room where we'd found the first Naomi, the interior of one of them immediately let me know something about it was different. Upon unlocking it and opening its cover, a frigid burst of air hit my face.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei had stated that room contained the cabinets with temperature regulation functions. However, the previous times we'd opened them, no special temperature had been set. Shiroya noticed my reaction and came to see if anything was wrong. After feeling the cold air that had begun to diffuse through the room, she checked the wheel on the right side of the cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's set to 0 °C.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Hm... It had to have been changed recently. There's nothing inside, so that's pretty strange.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It was a different cabinet than the one I'd first traveled from, and I wasn't sure why it would be done since the Sekimeiya hadn't been put inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When we got the locker key from Naomi, it might've already been like this, so we can't just suspect Sai and Katei.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah, and we can't blindly believe Sai's story either. Regardless, whoever did this didn't let the others know, so we should probably revert the temperature.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Someone might be counting on this cabinet for later if they changed the temperature in preparation. If I switch the wheel to "room temperature", we should be able to close the lid.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I nodded, and she did so before we left the room. It wasn't clear if setting it to room temperature would make the inside of the cabinet match the outside or if it would only stop the regulation, but leaving the lid open would communicate to whoever changed the temperature that their measures had been reversed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We proceeded to the other rooms and resumed the search. We didn't want to waste much time, or we'd become the suspicious ones. As soon as hallway B was done, we began with the parallel hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The first room we entered was the storeroom, continuing with our backward order. It was one of the smallest rooms on the entire floor, and its purpose was still a bit unclear, as it wasn't storing anything that was particularly useful.{w} Given how small it was, we should've left it immediately, but Shiroya noticed something that prolonged our stay.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, come here. Look at this part of the wall.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shiroya, who'd gone to the end of the dimly lit room, was pointing her finger at the place she wanted me to see. I stepped in, making my way through the cluttered, narrow space. Then, I looked beyond her finger, faintly illuminated by the single light.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It took me a while to understand what she meant. She was pointing at the left corner, and after glancing up and down in search of anything out of place, I finally noticed the oddity she'd found.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh... How did you even notice this?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The wall was dirty and uneven from years of aging. You could still see the outline of a grid that separated the wall into tiny squares. They were all defined by white lines which had started to fade with time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On one of the squares touching the left wall, Shiroya had seen a slight lack of dust, which was otherwise present over every surface of the room.{w} Even though the poor illumination made it hard to see, what seemed to be fingerprints existed on it. Not only that, but its close surroundings were a bit cleaner than the rest of the walls.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: From the door, I saw this area reflecting the hallway C light a lot more. I don't know when, but it looks like someone touched this corner.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I suppose so...{w} But I doubt it means anything, and we can't even be sure it happened today.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hold on. These fingerprints... It's hard to see, but they're not vertical, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, they look horizontal.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You wouldn't touch any wall with three fingers in this horizontal position... accidentally.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I wouldn't think so. Just touching it would leave them vertical, and more separated.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I shaped my hand to match the three fingerprints and placed it over them. My arm formed a right angle with the left wall, but it didn't make me understand the meaning of what we'd found.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I have no idea why you'd ever touch a corner of a room like this.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: There's nothing important in this room either.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...{w}Huh?{w} Wh-What...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: As I removed my hand from the wall, I felt something.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did something happen?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: When I took away my hand, it seemed as if this square moved a bit.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Hm? I didn't see anything.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I pressed my fingers on the square again. Instead of pulling away, I moved my hand around, and as I'd thought, it was a bit loose.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're right. It's moving a little.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It didn't go anywhere, though. I could only move it sideways, and it wouldn't detach from the wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This must be why someone touched this spot, but it's not doing anything.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Will it move any more than that?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It was sliding side to side, almost imperceptibly. Realizing that I hadn't been applying enough force, I attempted to move it past its apparent limit.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All of a sudden, as if it were a door, the wall opened, revealing a hidden space behind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I-It's a hidden door!?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'd slid the moving piece to the right, and before I could think, my hand had pushed open the entire wall. It was revealed to be very thin, and past it, the corridor extended.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They've even got secret passages here? What is this place...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No light existed on the other side, but it seemed to lead to a narrow area.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's another door...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Y-Yes, but it doesn't have a handle. At first I thought it was just another wall.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I tried to push it open, but it didn't move. Where a handle or a doorknob should have been, there were two round holes: a big one with metallic pieces inside, and a smaller, empty one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Someone here knows about this, right? Those marks have to mean someone opened this recently.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...And no matter if they went through this door, the culprit could've easily escaped from us if they just hid here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why was something like this even built in the first place?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It might've been part of Ashiya's countermeasures to Xyn, but that means that Katei would have to know about it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I mean, no matter what it's for, there's no way he doesn't know about this, right...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That part of the storeroom felt colder than the rest of the building, likely because the temperature regulation didn't reach it. Still awestruck, I kept examining the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I think there should be a handle here. When you remove a handle with a keyhole from a door, you're left with these holes. I think the small one is where the keyhole would be, and the bigger one is what connects the handle with the turning mechanism. This means that this door can usually be unlocked with a key, but without the handle, we won't be able to open it even if we find the right one.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, I guess someone could've unscrewed it on purpose to make sure it's never unlocked again.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah. I have no idea what's through here, but we can't find out. It looks like a sturdy enough door, so it won't open without both the handle and the key.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I tried it a few more times, but it didn't budge at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey!
entries.speaker: q

entries.text: What the hell is going on!?
entries.speaker: q

entries.text: The sudden voice startled us, and we turned around instantly. Katei's silhouette was behind us, the single light only hitting his back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...We found this hidden section behind the wall. Where does this door lead to?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You must be screwing with me! A hidden section? There's no way.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You're seeing it right now. Did you not know about it...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, I did not know about it! What is this!?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Whoa, look at this. Good find, Atsuki.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: From behind Katei, another silhouette appeared. Without a doubt, the voice belonged to Sai.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya found it, actually.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, you finally did something. Good job.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai's condescending attitude had already resurfaced. He skittered over to us and began to examine the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Two more figures peeked in from the entrance. As they stepped in, the light revealed they were the last two remaining people: Akaro and Erina.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were gonna search for you. Did you take this chance to sneak into your hideout?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We actually found it while we were searching for you, so you tell us. Where did you go? The bathrooms here were empty.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're all always in a rush as soon as I go somewhere. I just went to the floor 2 bathrooms since Naomi's still in the one down here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wait, what? No, you didn't. I was there, and you definitely didn't come.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...{w}All right, let's settle this quickly. Katei is lying. I was up there, and he never showed up.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I bet he already told you he'd gone upstairs, right? Now, since I revealed I was there, he couldn't back out of his lie, so he chose to accuse me. That's Katei for you.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: This is getting old. You guys can choose to believe him if you want, but he's only manipulating you.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei, we found a hidden passage, so stop trying to always be the center of attention. Let's cut to the chase: did you leave the bathroom's door open or closed?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Closed. I always close doors behind me when I leave an empty room.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Unfortunately, he's right. I closed the door, so take him up on his offer and believe me.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Now look at this. Someone removed the keyhole from this door to prevent us from opening it.{w} Hm... Not only that, but the inner mechanism was broken too. This won't allow for a new handle to be inserted.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Whoever the culprit is, they're likely to still be somewhere, so they might be behind this door right now, which is how they keep avoiding us.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei, be smart for once and tell us where this goes.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You heard me earlier. I was unaware of this hidden area entirely.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You're awful at your job, then. Ashiya must've constructed this for a reason, and it's impossible you weren't aware of it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Do you guys not think it might lead to the left side of the tower?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...You mean, outside?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes.{w} This entire corridor now stretches farther than the crystal rooms. I think it might extend far enough to reach outside.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's some hope you're giving us. Katei didn't know about this door, so if it leads outside, the alarm shouldn't have blocked it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Th-That's right. I can assure you that the alarm did not do anything to this door.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Someone did, though. The keyhole was removed, probably to prevent us from unlocking it with the key. Isn't that implying that one of us has it? Otherwise, the lock would be enough of a barrier.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well, nothing around here looks modern. If this door is old, the chances of picking the lock are high. Maybe it was done to prevent that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: True, yeah. How did you spot the hidden opening, Shiroya?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I saw some light reflecting off one of the tiles. Someone's fingerprints had removed some dust in the corner of the wall. That ended up being the way to open it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Listen, then. This was recent. If the door leads outside, the culprit might actually have escaped with the handle. This building is situated at the outskirts of town, so the sides and back are never seen by anyone and are empty, grassy fields.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm sure the police are keeping watch outside, but probably only at the front, where the entrance and windows are. They shouldn't be aware of this door either, so escaping unseen is certainly doable.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: There's no way this leads out of the building. I've never seen the outline of a door from the outside, and there's no light coming from behind the door. It's absolutely impossible this kind of way out exists.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The gaps aren't big enough to let light pass, or the door is wider than it seems. Just think about it, though. Why would this secret passage exist?{w} If they had something to hide in it, they wouldn't have another locked door past it. They would just hide it in the secret passage itself. Otherwise, this door wouldn't be here or be locked.{w} This passage is the secret itself. It's hidden because this door leads outside. If the middle wall didn't exist, the length of the room would reveal it.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I think you're right. That's what this wall is hiding.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So, we're a single door away from making it out...? Can we break it down?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: There's no way, just look at it. Whoever removed the handle knew very well that we couldn't do that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I know this is bound to happen eventually, but do you realize what will occur if we manage to force it open? We'll reveal that the Sekimeiya has time traveling powers. What kind of consequences will that have?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...That was completely inconsiderate. Erina was still next to us, and she hadn't said anything in a very long time. Our priority had to be making it out as soon as possible so that the police could understand what happened to Isla even if it invalidated the recording.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't get me wrong. I'm not worried. I'm just intrigued.{w} How is it even remotely possible the Sekimeiya exists? How did it make it here without anyone finding out about its powers? These big picture questions are what I'm most lost about.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I hit the door, and the sound echoed heavily throughout the corridor. I repeated that a few times, trying to be as loud as I could and intending to be heard from the outside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nobody will come. I refuse to believe this leads outside. I'm more inclined to think the culprit is currently behind this door, listening.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Is there nothing else we can do? Sliding anything through the gaps, for example?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What, a letter? We're too far from the entrance to be heard, and I doubt anyone is currently looking at this side. Regardless, these gaps are way too thin—probably to hide the door's existence from the outside.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It was incredibly frustrating. We'd finally discovered an exit that the alarm shouldn't have affected, but the culprit had made sure to finish the job. ...Was it just in case we found the moving wall, or was there a deeper reason?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And how did the culprit know about it, but not Katei? Why was it there in the first place? Not only did the door lock us inside, but it also produced even more questions. Feeling defeated, we left what had become a narrow, dim corridor to return to the wider but still dark hallway A.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I thought something was noteworthy. Even though a perfect hiding spot existed, the Sekimeiya had never been hidden in it.{w} ...Why? Earlier, it had been hidden in the storeroom. Therefore, the person who hid it there was probably not aware of the movable wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...We'd ignored the little fight between Sai and Katei, but there weren't many layers to it. One of them was lying, and it was nothing new, as they'd surely lied more than once already. The fact that one of them took advantage of the situation with Isla to act on their own, though, proved that they weren't to be taken lightly. In addition, one of them could've easily been responsible for the cold cabinet Shiroya and I had returned to normal.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Mechanically, we went to the event room. It didn't have anything new to tell us, as the Sekimeiya was still present behind the glass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So it hasn't moved. It's clear that either Sai or Katei didn't go to the bathroom earlier, so they were up to some other business.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Good thought. Tell us, Katei, what exactly were you doing that justified lying to us?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: *sigh* It's time to put an end to this. Sai won't stop lying as much as he pleases, so we'll have to wait until the security footage reveals all of his actions.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You keep saying that, but do you really believe the footage will be salvaged? Even though the cameras are recording, is it really being saved somewhere?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Of course. The computer isn't detecting the system, but as soon as that's solved, it'll have access to all the stored footage. Did you perhaps think you'd be able to roam freely without consequences?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No, but I have trouble swallowing that. The culprit made sure to cut our access to the system, but why would they do that if Ashiya will come in and be able to look at what happened?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's not all they did, though. At the same time, our only method of communication was removed. I believe the reason behind that entire thing was to prevent us from conveying what's happening while we're still here. It's possible that whoever did it doesn't care about Ashiya finding out.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You try to make that sound interesting, but it's idiotic. They were able to power off the computer, but it turned back on minutes later, so why didn't they choose to keep it off forever?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Most likely, the reason they let us use it again was because they'd made sure that the recordings wouldn't be accessible. Additionally, it clearly told us that they could somehow disable our communication method.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So, to be honest, even though the cameras are still functional, I find it hard to believe what's being recorded will ever be seen. There's no way the person responsible would be fine with being seen once we get out, so if we can't access the system, it's doubtful Ashiya or the police will be able to.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I feel like you're right about that. It would also explain why they keep putting themselves in front of the cameras.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Now, I understand I'm repeating myself, but wouldn't you think that the security staff member among us who conveniently avoided giving us information, has lied multiple times, and could've had knowledge of the secret passage is the most likely candidate to have orchestrated this?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's enough, Sai.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Is that all you have to say? Of course, once your "the security cameras will prove that I'm right" excuse runs out, you have no arguments to defend yourself with.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It seemed the discussions between those two wouldn't cease until one was proven wrong definitively. I knew that Sai wasn't any less of a liar than Katei, but if that hadn't been the case, I would've quickly sided with him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Why don't we stop with this and wait until we can leave?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Surprisingly, it was Erina who tried to calm them down. Her voice came out like the wind rustling on dried leaves.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's easy to say, but Katei will just take advantage of that again.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...No matter who's in the right, someone is guilty. Although we don't know who it is, can't we lock ourselves up in one place so they can't move around freely?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Is anyone opposed to that? Technically, only the culprit should have a problem with it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If that was what Erina wanted, I'd attempt to make it happen. She wanted to avoid any more tragedy and only intended to wait for external help.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Locking ourselves up...? Isn't that going a bit too far?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Why would it be? You'd agree if you were innocent, and if something happens while we're staying somewhere, it means the culprit was never one of us.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Could we even do that if we wanted to?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I doubt it. We can lock the bathrooms, but they're not big enough for all of us.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Are there no other places?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What about the security room? Didn't Katei have the key for it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We won't be able to lock ourselves in there. From the inside, the lock can be undone with just the doorknob.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What about the lobby? The hallway doors are locked until {time=9}, isn't that right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: They aren't. Permission to move ahead is simply not granted until that time. They can be locked, but I don't have the keys.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: If we do this... we'll have to commit to it. Locking ourselves in a place with the key to unlock it doesn't prove anyone's sincerity since they could leave any time they wanted.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: But that's all we could do if we managed to find the right keys. We won't be able to lock ourselves inside and leave the key out because the doors won't close if the deadbolt is set.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Are you all forgetting about the attic bedrooms? We saw they had a keyhole, one had a working chain, and they're spacious enough for all of us. Could they work?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Wouldn't we run into the same problem?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I turned around, and after staring at the door for a short time, I spoke.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm... I don't think so, actually. I can think of a difference that would let us lock ourselves up without being able to leave.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The silence let me know that nobody would directly oppose me. I began to walk until I thought of a question to ask.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, does anyone have the cabinet key? If we're gonna stay put, let's make sure to lock the cabinet too and keep the key with us. It's possible the person behind all this has a duplicate, but nothing actually proves that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Once again, nobody said anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...If not, it has to still be where I left it, on top of that bed in the attic.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Let's see if it's there, then.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We took the stairs up. The elevator had already been out of commission for a very long time, and it was better to keep it like that, as it had caused us a few headaches during the short time it worked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wind Shelter
It's actually still here. Good.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Surprisingly enough, the key hadn't been taken while everyone had a chance. I picked it up and glanced at the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I messed with it a little. It appeared to be a double cylinder lock, meaning that to unlock it, the key would be needed from each side, as opposed to the security room's lock.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's going to work. We won't have to lock it either.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: How?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I went ahead and looked through the drawers I'd inspected earlier. First, I took out the key to the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'll have to leave this outside. Now, I'll explain how we can technically do this, but it's not exactly a smooth way.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The second thing I took out of the drawer was a screwdriver. Admittedly, what I'd thought of had been inspired by the secret door we'd just found.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Removing a handle is incredibly easy. We can take it out, leave it outside, and close the door. Since we'll be unable to turn it, even though the door will be unlocked, we won't be able to open it. That's the big difference with this door—the handles on the crystal floor don't have visible screws to detach.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Since the keyhole isn't on the handle itself, we would need to leave the key outside. Otherwise, we could still get the door to open by inserting the key and turning it. Even though the lock wouldn't be set, it would act as a turn of a handle, and the door could be dragged open. On top of that, we can remove the outer handle as well so that no one can easily get in.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Finally, even though we'd hide the key outside, if someone found it and wanted to enter, they couldn't do it. They could find the key and open the door like I just described, but we can set the chain from the inside. If we do this, the door shouldn't be opened until the police enter the building. There's no way it'll be broken down.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Nobody was sure what to say. Personally, I knew that it meant giving up on understanding the Sekimeiya's mechanics, but after what happened to Isla, it was clear that something terrible could come out of that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You must be joking... This is Ashiya's special place, and we're currently being recorded. Do you not understand what will happen if they see us ripping the handles apart?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Honestly, who cares? It'll be easy to reattach them. We could do that right as the tower opens, but we'll unfortunately have to leave the handles out of the room or else we could leave at any point.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That reminds me... What time is it? It's been a while since the last time I checked it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: With a brief sigh indicating that he wasn't fond of my proposition, Sai turned his wrist. I looked at his watch and saw that the displayed time was {time=14:56.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Almost {time=15}, I see. We're past the halfway point, so with all that's happened, let's spend the last six hours calmly until the police enter and we can have a better understanding of what's been going on.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It was an easy way to finally test the recording. If nothing happened after we waited those last six hours, we would have to have a long discussion about it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is what I wanted. Thank you.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Erina's gratitude was the ultimate deciding factor. We'd lock ourselves away from the Sekimeiya, ensuring that its powers wouldn't influence our peaceful wait. Hopefully, we'd also be preventing the culprit's plan from moving along.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd go lock the Sekimeiya cabinet myself, but we're trying to act together by doing this. Let's avoid separating now and creating chances to prepare anything.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Any objection?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sai and Katei rolled their eyes, but they kept quiet. If we were alone with both Sekimeiya locked in place as well, nobody could use them.{w} Everyone looked uncertain, and Sai seemed depressed. He'd made it obvious he was enjoying his time in the tower, and instead of having another six hours to play with a time travel device, it was already over.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We entered the event room and saw that the Sekimeiya hadn't moved. I made sure the glass was properly adjusted, and I manually locked it. From that point on, only the key that I had could open it, so I possessed the keys to both Sekimeiya. Regarding the locker key, I'd have to surreptitiously leave it somewhere in the bedroom after waiting a while. That way, anyone could've had it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Finally, we went up again. We'd just gone through staircases eighteen times, so we were pretty exhausted. The idea of waiting calmly in a bedroom with three big beds started to sound slightly more pleasant.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'll be here for six hours, so it's the right time to use the bathroom.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Once inside, we'd have no way to exit, so everyone made sure to prevent a future problem. All of us went to the bathroom one at a time, and when we were all set, Sai spoke.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sure, if we're gonna do this, let's do it well. We're dealing with someone who's teleported and gone back in time before, so regardless of whether they're one of us or not, we need to keep that in mind.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We need to make sure the door won't be opened no matter what, but a single key can ruin that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He went to grab the bedroom key that I'd left on top of the drawers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei, are you sure the key in the other bedroom won't work?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I said it earlier: they're not interchangeable.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai moved from one room to the other and came back with the key for the neighboring bedroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're right. They're different.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He attempted to insert the wrong key into the door's keyhole, but it only went halfway in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He went to return it and closed the door behind him once he came back to the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Now, there've been instances where we thought the Sekimeiya teleported. The first time was when it appeared in the storeroom, but recently, it appeared inside the cabinet, next to Isla...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Atsuki and Shiroya could've put it there, but if they didn't, it might've moved by itself. That's not a random location either, so if it was part of the culprit's plan, there's a chance they understand how to exploit this self-teleportation.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's more likely they moved it themselves, but keep in mind that if that's what happened, they had to travel from the future because we inspected the whole building before that point. If we're gonna stay here until the end, that means that none of us will have the chance to go back in time and move the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The four main possibilities are: the culprit isn't one of us and we kept missing them.{w} The Sekimeiya teleported there randomly.{w} The culprit made the Sekimeiya teleport there without touching it.{w} One of us will go back to the past after spending six hours here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No matter which one is right, before we lock ourselves away, we need to thoroughly inspect this bedroom. Both levels.{w} If a Sekimeiya's already here, the imprisonment wouldn't mean anything, as anyone could leave at any time after making sure nobody else is in range. A key would do the trick too, and we've seen that some kind of replication has occurred. We found two identical suitcases and two Naomis.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He didn't mention it, but even though I hadn't seen both at the same time, two Sekimeiya had to have existed too, at least at one point.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Searching for an extra key to this bedroom might sound paranoid since nothing indicates it exists, but it's necessary. If we ignore these precautions, we're leaving a potential escape route for the culprit that can be used at any time.{w} They have higher knowledge of the Sekimeiya than we do, so we have no guarantee that they couldn't obtain a key they would hide later, use it to escape, go back to the past, and preemptively hide a replicated key inside knowing we'd lock ourselves in here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}Yeah. Our intention is to be safe in here, so let's search around beforehand.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're saying "be safe", but at the same time, you and Sai keep implying that one of us is behind all this. This person has already killed up to three times, so if what we're doing opposes their plan, wouldn't they just kill us instead of escaping in this convoluted way?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I wouldn't say they'd have an easy time of it, but let's see...{w} Hey, jackass, if you're actually here, we're gonna lock ourselves in this room for six hours.{w} If you intend to kill us to continue with your plan at some point, hurry up and do it now before you need to deal with breaking the door down.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Nobody moved, but it was clear that we all had our guard up. If someone was around and didn't care about killing us if they had to, the right call would likely be to start after we were locked inside so that nobody could run away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's not like anyone has really spoken up against this plan, right? It might even be that by staying here, we're not inconveniencing some mastermind. In any case, it's undeniably safer than continuing to roam around.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That seemed to assuage Akaro's worries.{w} The six of us went to the upper section of the bedroom to inspect it. I used that time to try to prevent something really bad from happening, as Sai's insistence made me realize something else was to come.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The space was small, so we shortly determined that there were no keys anywhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We repeated the process below, and once again, it seemed nothing had been preemptively hidden, revealing that nobody had already attempted to outsmart us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We're ready, then.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Don't be silly. We're missing the most important part.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What do you mean?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We need to search everyone. Someone could currently have the key.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Of course, as I'd thought, Sai wouldn't miss such an obvious procedure. It was very important to do it, but in our situation, it meant something else: the key to Naomi's locker that I'd kept on myself was likely about to be found.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya must've been aware of it too. As soon as I found myself in that unavoidable situation, there was nothing I could do without being seen. ...All I managed to do was prepare a risky trick before we went up the ladder, and I'd already begun to run through possible excuses while foolishly regretting that I hadn't hidden it in the bathroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When we were up top, I made sure nobody had the funny idea of leaving anything hidden for later. I am very sure that, right now, both sections of this bedroom don't contain anything the culprit has deliberately left here.{w} I'll begin.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai showed us the contents of every one of his pockets, his hip pack, and shoes. He held the original key to the bedroom, but he'd been gripping it even before we'd started to look around. However, he took something else from one of his back pockets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is the key to my house and my identification, and this is the ticket for today's event. I have nothing else on me.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Let's all do the same.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Hold on. You don't mean to say that proves you're clean, do you?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: My objection had a reason behind it.{w} That method of showing we didn't possess anything was highly disadvantageous for me. Even though letting them find my key wouldn't have been the worst, Shiroya and I would've become very suspicious, and if anyone realized what the key was for, they would all see the Sekimeiya in the locker. Furthermore, it'd bring back the commotion Erina had been trying to eliminate. That was why I took the single chance I believed I had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No, of course... Do you want me to get naked?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Just a while ago, you said we should do this well. You could have a key under your clothes, yes, but you don't have to undress.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I walked up to him, and like a security agent, I began patting his body from top to bottom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All right, now you can say you're clean.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, thank God. I was going to do this too, don't worry. ...Let's continue with you, then.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I just wanted to make sure, and that's fine, since you won't find anything.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I immediately knew that I had sounded a little off. It was intentional, to set the expectation that nothing would be found on me.{w} As such, when he got to the right pocket of my pants, he looked at me with a frown, noticing that I'd been incorrect.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took that brief moment of surprise to take out what he'd felt from my pocket.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Ah, right. I'd forgotten I put this key there.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: With two fingers, I was gripping the Sekimeiya cabinet key. I moved aside and placed it on top of the drawers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll leave it here; we need to lock ourselves inside with it, as I said before.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Trying to appear nonchalant, I walked back and told Sai to continue. Like I'd done to him, he finished checking the lower part of my body.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Okay, you're clean too.{w} Katei, mind being next?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I took a deep, discreet breath. Shiroya had been fixing her eyes on me, but I'd attempted not to meet them. I stepped back, and Katei took my place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I moved to Shiroya's side; she was probably wondering if I'd already gotten rid of the key. Later, without being heard, I'd have to tell her what I'd done. Despite how things seemed, it was still located in my right pocket.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before going up the ladder, I'd thought that I had only one way to avoid being found out; I would've been easily noticed if I attempted to leave the key somewhere.{w} Taking advantage of the fact that I also had the cabinet key and that it was slightly bigger, I'd removed the locker key from my back pocket and slid it into the same pocket as the cabinet's. Until that point, I'd avoided keeping both together so that I didn't produce metallic noises as I walked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The locker key was small. I'd purposely put it horizontally behind the cabinet's so that Sai would press his hand on it and only notice the bigger shape at the front.{w} Fortunately, I'd been able to abuse his minor surprise by taking out the cabinet key and leaving the smaller one inside. When the body inspection proceeded, he assumed the right pocket was clean and didn't check it again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Hm, what's this?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I looked up. Sai was feeling one of Katei's pockets, and it appeared he'd found something inside. That time, it was Sai who first put his hand in and retrieved, yet again, a key.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, right. I'd also forgotten I had this.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We all recognized it. It was the old-looking key we'd found on the floor of hallway A.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Didn't you say you'd keep it somewhere safe?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I forgot, but don't worry. My pocket is plenty safe.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: After staring at it, Sai put the key back in.{w} In the next pocket, he found something else. For the third time in a row, they were keys.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You know these four as well. One is for the bathrooms, another is for the security room, this one opens my locker in the staff room, and this one is for the door leading to floor 2.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Silently, Sai finished the inspection without finding anything else. Still unsatisfied, he took out all the keys once again and attempted to insert them into the door's keyhole.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They don't work.{w} You're done, then.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He gave the keys back to Katei, and before the next person could be examined, I voiced a thought.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That first key... Could it be for the hidden door we found?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I just thought the same thing. Both have this feeling of being fairly old, and there's no other door in this building that does.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Huh. You might be right, actually.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We thought the culprit dropped it in a hurry. If that's what happened, it could be why they had to remove the handle.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But the key spent a long time on the floor, so why didn't they retrieve it before we found it? They already left the suitcase in hallway C at some point.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We went quiet at the mention of the suitcase. We'd more or less assumed that Naomi had left it there, but we weren't sure anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're right... Maybe they wanted to avoid every possibility of being spotted and didn't want to step into hallway A.{w} The fingerprints that you saw... Are they clear enough to be useful? If the police can figure out who they belong to, that could be a path to the culprit.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not sure. The clear ones were all replaced by mine, but there might've been some more around because you need to push the wall in order to open it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see. If whoever it is doesn't go erase them upon realizing that we found them, some should still remain. But if they're one of us, the fingerprints won't mean anything since it won't be provable that they were left before we found the door.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yeah. There's one more thing, too.{w} When we discovered the secret door, my first thought was that someone bypassed our searches by hiding there.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: However, even though the light wasn't very bright, what Shiroya and I initially saw were three distinguishable fingerprints. I don't think any were overlapping.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You mean that the door was only recently opened once?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: From hallway A, maybe. If it was only opened once, it can't be that someone went to hide there all the times we searched unless they spent hours inside. Maybe that proves it wasn't one of us.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh...{w} I suppose they could've used the Sekimeiya to teleport inside without opening the wall, but that doesn't sound likely.{w} Anyway, who's next?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Shiroya volunteered.{w} In her case, nothing was found in her clothes. Her purse was almost empty and only contained a wallet, two of the three tickets we'd bought for the event, our personal identification to match the tickets, and the key to my house.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro was next. In the same way, his inspection was handled quickly, and once again, personal keys, his identification, and his own entrance ticket were all we found on him. It wasn't surprising, as the same kind of body search would also be performed before entering the tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All right, done. Finally, I don't mean to suspect you, Erina, but ignoring you would defeat the purpose of what you're trying to accomplish.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I know. That's fine.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: She moved ahead. Usually, it would've been worth considering that the person who proposed the arrangement had a secret reason, but I knew Erina was genuine. Sai gently made sure she hadn't been concealing anything, and by letting us know that her purse was clean as well, he put an end to our last measure.{w} Personal keys and identification had also been found in her purse. We were specifically searching for hidden keys, so even though it was normal we all possessed ours, Sai made sure to confirm that their shape didn't match the bedroom door's.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Good, this went well. Now, doing what I explained should be easy.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Since nobody had any complaints, I took one screwdriver out of a drawer and compared it with the screws that kept the door's handle attached.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It'll work. It's not a perfect match, but it'll definitely suffice.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We wanted to hide the key and outer handle outside, right? There's not much of a point to it since the chain will prevent anyone from entering, but can you think of a good place to hide it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I feel like under the bathroom carpet is good enough. Like you said, it's not too important.{w} Regarding the handle, no great spot comes to mind, but it doesn't matter anyway. The attic's full of removable handles, so someone outside could probably unscrew one to use it on the door if they really wanted to open it. In case that happens, we have the chain to rely on.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, that sounds fine.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: From the hallway, we clearly saw Sai leaving the key under the carpet without any kind of trick involved.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There it is. Only one thing to do, then.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We all moved back inside. With the big screwdriver, I removed the four screws of the inner handle, which fell on my hands.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It'd be great if we could use this on the storeroom door.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We should all get ready to face the consequences of this. Don't be surprised if Ashiya blows this tiny action out of proportion.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We get it. That's fine, they can do what they want.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I unscrewed the outer handle too and left both of them under the bed in the opposite bedroom.{w} In the door, only one hole became visible, as the keyhole wasn't found on the handles themselves. I made sure that the door couldn't be opened through the hole. A very short metal cylinder was poking out, but it was incredibly tight; we weren't going to turn it from the inside. When I was certain, I asked one last time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Okay, this is it. If I close this door, we won't be able to open it again. Any final objection?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I looked at the five of them, who knew what their next six hours would be like. Nobody opened their mouth, so I proceeded with the most important action.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Slowly, I pushed the door forward. There was no friction against the floor, so I applied force until it satisfyingly set into place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...We'd sealed ourselves in. Surprisingly, it had taken a fair amount of concord. It was clear that nobody wanted to oppose the request because Erina made it. Any regrets were no longer meaningful.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As the icing on the cake, we set the chain. I attempted to pull the door inward and push it outward, and as expected, it didn't budge. It had become a barrier from both sides, and the only way to unlock it would be telling the police where we'd left the key and detaching the chain for them. Cooperation from both sides was needed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Now we wait. We could do with a deck of cards.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We don't have any, so just try to stay still and quiet for once. You have been enough of a handful for one day.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei, there's a lot of resentment within you. How does it feel to know that after we wait six hours, you're gonna go straight to prison?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I haven't done anything, so that won't happen.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, Ashiya doesn't seem to think the same, remember? Wasn't your authority revoked?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What's the time?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Did nothing else happen to your watch? Seems like it's still working fine.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Excuse me?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Oh, you know about that? Yeah, we fixed it earlier.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes, when we were waiting in the lobby, before you two appeared.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Wh-What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...You didn't know? Sai asked me if I had lithium batteries because his watch wasn't working. He didn't mention that part when he told you what happened, but it was insignificant.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's right. How did you know that, Atsuki?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I wasn't talking about that. It didn't work once before that point. You're still claiming that wasn't you, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Probably, since I don't know what you're talking about. It was convenient that Katei had the right type of battery in the security room.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What time and date was displayed when you changed the battery?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Some minutes earlier than the time shown on the computer, which is when it must've stopped working. Then, I synced it properly again.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Is that so...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't know what you two are talking about, but I bet Sai failed at looking innocent again, right?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Your irony knows no limits. Are you already thinking about how you'll lie to the police?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Stop. We decided to stay here to end these discussions.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I know. We're already locked in, though, so I have to rub it in Katei's face. I bet he's crying internally since his plan can't be finished now.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...But Katei was right. Sai had noticed his watch stopped working again, so like I did, he asked for lithium batteries. That was further indication that he remembered the time he and I fixed the watch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I'll go up and wait there.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Before the conversation snowballed again, Erina was the one who stopped Sai. To get as far from the door as possible, she chose to go rest in the upper bedroom. I knew that the illusion of tranquility was well achieved there, so taking advantage of her opening, I decided to follow her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We will too. Separating ourselves into two groups of three will be the best way to utilize the space.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Taking my cue, Shiroya went up with me. It seemed that Erina wanted to distance herself from the commotion that Sai and Katei continued to spawn, so by claiming the upstairs area for ourselves, we at least had a chance to remain unbothered for a long time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina was sitting on a bed. She didn't pay much attention to our presence, so we silently sat on the opposite one.{w} Although six hours still had to pass, I promptly realized that I was still exhausted. It was possible I could sleep and fast-forward to {time=21.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'd closed the hatch, so we couldn't hear the people under us. If they decided to keep arguing with moderate voices, we wouldn't hear it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was time to disconnect. I'd been actively trying to piece everything together, but after choosing to abandon that, only time would force me to go back, in the case that something horrible awaited us at the end of the road.{w} At least, that was what I'd been ready to accept.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You two didn't do anything to Isla, right...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Taking both of us by surprise, Erina broke the silence she had set up. We raised our heads to see her deep eyes peering at us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Absolutely not...! We were sleeping in the other bedroom when everything happened.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Is it possible one of you left while the other was sleeping?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...There's no way that happened.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Do you two... trust each other that much even though there's a... a killer around? Are you two related? I saw that only one of you had house keys.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...We're just friends. Unfortunately, we have no way to prove it, but I promise that we left after... Isla was found.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Earlier, I thought that Sai had a point. Why did you go straight to the lobby from hallway B without looking at the cleaning room?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...That was my mistake. I should've acted as if we had already seen the cart and the missing Sekimeiya, but without a second thought, I had tried to appear surprised to make it seem like we'd never entered the room and couldn't have hidden it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It might sound iffy, but what we said earlier was the truth. We went to the bathroom and then checked the event room and the lobby, where we thought people could be.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Then, is Katei the only person who could've done it?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Him...? Right, a lot of things regarding his whereabouts still don't make sense, but it shouldn't be that straightforward. It could've been an accident caused by the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It was no accident. Isla saw something inside that cabinet, so she must've been lured there. Katei could've made her disappear; he's known about the Sekimeiya for longer than anyone else.{w} Then, he showed up after he left Isla's body in the cabinet... You two have experienced what the Sekimeiya does, but I don't know how to think about it.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It's possible that she... was sent to the cabinet from the future, right? Isn't that similar to something you said a while ago? If that happened, it could've been anyone, but she would have to still... be alive.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It was clear that Erina was attaching herself to the slightest gleam of hope that still persisted. The recording "proved" that Isla would be alive in the future, so Erina needed the time to pass to know if there was any trust left to be placed in it. She must've suggested waiting in the room in the hope of nothing occurring at {time=21.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I've been thinking about it, but I don't know what could've happened. I-I'm sorry...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I wanted to give her even more hope, but I stopped myself, knowing that it would only make things worse if I was wrong. Even if Isla would somehow be alive in a month, her fate had already been shown to us: she would end up dead in the crystal floor's cabinet even if she had to travel there from a month in the future.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At least, that was what I thought until I remembered that the two Naomi bodies defied that belief.{w} I believed that no matter what had happened to Isla, being dead inside the cabinet had to be the end of her path. However, two identical corpses hinted that the Sekimeiya could have some sway even after death. That was the actual hope Erina had to rely on—the recording didn't guarantee a bright future even if it turned out to be legitimate.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In that instant, I felt a bubble of hope growing in my head.{w} The Sekimeiya hadn't caused any apparent effect when it touched Isla's dead body, even though we might not have seen it immediately. If that had created a living version of her at an earlier point in time like I speculated with Naomi... My thoughts were directed to Miiya once again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...But that bubble popped as soon as images of her burnt pieces of flesh appeared in my mind. The Sekimeiya had to exist somewhere two weeks in the past, but how could I touch a body that had been blown to pieces?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I forced myself to stop thinking. The three of us present in the room had all lost someone very dear to us, and we all silently prayed that somehow they could be brought back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was cruel to consider that there was a culprit somewhere who had killed at least once, possessing a higher knowledge of how the Sekimeiya worked—exactly what all of us needed the most.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It's my fault, isn't it? It doesn't matter who did it... I brought her here.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I bought the tickets for today... to make Isla happy. And instead, she...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It should have been me. Why would anyone want to hurt Isla?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I had no idea how to respond to something as dark as that, and Shiroya clearly didn't either. We lapsed into silence for a few minutes. Part of Erina, I was sure, believed that Isla was still alive somewhere, while another part accepted that she was dead and already mourned her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Do you know about Akashic Park?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The amusement park?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I'd heard about it. It was a few hours away from Yushibana. Apparently, it was surrounded by mountains, and it competed worldwide for the largest park in size. Its selling point was that it contained "all possible configurations of every ride in the world", so despite my low interest, it had piqued my curiosity more than once.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You might've thought Isla was obsessed with the gems downstairs, but that didn't even come close to how much she wanted to go there. ...She brought it up countless times, but it's really expensive, and I've always been a bit afraid of ride malfunctions.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I was going to have more money than usual this month since it's the end of the year. I decided to finally give in and surprise her with a trip after Christmas...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I told her about it less than a week ago, in case she preferred to hold off with the money and plan a trip during the summer instead. Even though she was really excited at first, she actually told me that she didn't want to go.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I couldn't believe it, but she said that she didn't want to leave her friend alone while she went to have fun. At one point, she also said that she would only come to see the Sekimeiya because I already bought the tickets and she didn't want to make me waste money... even though she started to talk about her friend before we got the tickets.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I told you the other ways her behavior changed, right? I forgot one. Sometimes, she hid something from me. A small object, I believe.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's what it felt like. I noticed... a few times, she'd keep her hand in a fist for a long time. If I asked her to show me what she was hiding, she would run off, so I had to ignore it. It must've been something very small.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I can't get it all out of my head... Whatever happened to Isla started weeks ago, and I never realized it.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: All of that was difficult to respond to, so I stayed quiet. However, Shiroya said something far from the shallow answers I'd kept to myself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hold on... Erina, I might know who Isla's friend was.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Wh-What...? Who?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I frowned. How could she have known that? The only ideas I'd kept in mind were an imaginary friend, a Xyn member, and a staff member from the tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm not sure if it makes sense... When we learned about her friend's story, we hadn't experienced the Sekimeiya's powers yet. But just now... I thought of something that could make a lot of sense.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Apparently, she and her friend were living together, but you said that was impossible since you hadn't seen her.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Could it be that her friend was herself? After traveling to the past?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...{w}With that sentence, the huge but simple possibility opened up in my mind. I hadn't considered it at all since I'd been blinded by conspiracies, but I immediately understood why Shiroya reached that idea.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: H-Herself...? What are you talking about!? I would've seen her!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I... think Shiroya might be right.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: You would've seen her, yes. You said that she started to disobey you sometimes, and you even found her at home once instead of being at school.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Right. They were actively keeping her identity from you because they felt like they couldn't reveal that another Isla had appeared, but when one of them went to school or to do what you instructed her to do, the other couldn't follow. During those instances, you could have been seeing the Isla who came from the future.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Wh-What...? Did I just imagine that her behavior changed? She distanced herself and spent much less time with me...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Then this is one of the few things that explains it. Why else would she hide a friend from you? She didn't have bad intentions, and neither did her friend.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: "We watched my favorite movie together, and it was her favorite too!" "She went to the aquarium last month, just like us!" I recalled a few things Erina had said.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The way Isla described her friend made it sound as if she'd made up a persona that had her own traits and experienced the same events. However, it was herself from the future, wasn't it...? She wasn't lying.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why else would she refuse to go to the amusement park? Both of them couldn't go at once, so she must not have wanted to leave her behind, knowing firsthand how much she wanted to go too.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Then, right now, she's outside...!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Isla... specifically said her friend was waiting for her outside.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That has to be it! She will exist in a month!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...I didn't want to deny it, but it wasn't that simple.{w} In fact, nothing about her fate had changed.{w} I could assemble things the following way: "when Isla disappeared from the cabinet, she went far into the past. The range should've been a lot bigger, but we might be wrong about that part. In a month, that Isla will somehow enter the tower".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Tragically, no matter what I thought up, the following step had to be: "Isla travels to the past and ends up dead in the cabinet". There was no way to end it differently.{w} However, even though the voice recorder had appeared in Isla's purse, the origin of it was still unexplained with that theory.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina's head lowered, and her expression went back to how it had been minutes before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I don't know. I appreciate that you want to believe Isla, but there's no way what she said was true. You remember what her friend supposedly told her about today's incident, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...I'd tried to leave the major inconsistency for the end, but Erina was right.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Hm... She told me that something would happen in the tower, but not to worry. She said that if we stayed calm in one place, nobody would be hurt. And she promised I'd be able to see and touch the Sekimeiya, so she was right, wasn't she?"
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah... According to her, there was going to be no danger. ...And she said that only seven people would get trapped.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Exactly. There's no way she'd say those things after seeing Naomi's body and after everything else that happened.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Actually, this isn't what I'm the most worried about. Thinking about it conceptually, this is something that cannot work.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Conceptually...? You have time traveled, right? Things that would normally be impossible are happening. You've said so yourself.
entries.speaker: aki
