entries.text: That's not what I mean. We've come to the conclusion that the past can't be changed, so what we're suggesting is that Isla met her own self who had traveled from the future. They kept her existence hidden from you, and the friend let the original Isla know about today's events.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Ignoring that what she was told was incorrect, the next step is flawed. She can't go back to the past and "relive what she experienced". She would have to replicate exactly what her friend had done and said, as the past would occur exactly as it already had. There's naturally no way she would willingly do that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Isla said they'd been hanging out a lot, so as I said, conceptually, it's incredibly unreasonable to think that she spent the time as her friend knowing how everything would play out.{w} You saw her once when she hadn't gone to school, which should be an impossibility since she would've known you would see her, and she would've avoided that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see... Y-You're right. It's not possible. I hadn't seen it like that...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Everything we think about goes back to the same core: we don't really understand how the Sekimeiya works. We can't say it's not possible, but the way we're currently thinking about it can't function.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I've made up arbitrary rules to explain a few things that have occurred, but as long as they work, we can't discard them. If traveling so long to the past made Isla's memory fuzzy, for example, she might not have remembered the time she spent with herself.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: From her perspective, that would've been happening for the first time, so she would've acted on her own without being aware that she was repeating everything. She would've also misremembered what occurred today and given Isla false information that she trusted completely.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: All right... Thank you.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Instead of continuing, Erina turned around and lay on the bed while Shiroya and I looked lost. Her idea had a lot of promise, but it appeared ultimately impossible until we had more information.{w} I'd usually been able to create a patchwork design out of the loose ends of a theory, but in that case, I couldn't think of anything else. Needless to say, I didn't think any part of my memory had been erased upon traveling—although, to be fair, perhaps I wouldn't have realized it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Were we completely off-base? Was it all just a scheme planned by someone? Before I gave up on the idea, an extra piece of the puzzle that we'd ignored came back to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Where am I...?
entries.speaker: il2

entries.text: Wh-What do you mean? We're still in Ashiya Tower. Do you not remember?
entries.speaker: sai2

entries.text: No, I know. What I mean is... What happened to me? Where am I?
entries.speaker: il2

entries.text: "Following that, there were a couple of unsteady, heavy footfalls, most likely someone staggering. During the next few seconds, Isla cried, and nobody spoke, inside or outside the recording."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Those were words said by Isla, and they were scheduled to happen in about a month. Was the dark meaning behind Isla's future actions... that she'd discovered the fate that awaited her?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Had she found out that she had died and that her fate had been sealed?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "...What happened to me? Where am I?" I remembered the agonizing way that sounded.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I breathed deeply, but anxiety began to crawl up my back, exacerbated by my own lack of knowledge.{w} I hated exploring all sorts of options without knowing if I'd ever find the truth. Isla's bleak ending had already been revealed to us, making the process of putting together its outline all the more draining.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya was resting her head on top of a large pillow. We'd been there for a little while, and the people below us hadn't interrupted us yet. It seemed like relaxing would be an actual option.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I climbed over Shiroya and lay down, making contact with the cold wall. She was occupying both pillows, so I knew I'd have a hard time staying in a comfortable position. Trying to not mind it, I closed my eyes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As usual, attempting to keep my mind blank was futile, but the contents of what tormented me were very different. Time travel, a smoke attack, body doubles, murders, suspicion... What kind of mess were we in?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was aware that there was no guarantee I'd ever feel my own bed again, depending on what the truth around us really was. Ironically, the stiff bed began to help me get rid of those thoughts, and my senses slowly faded away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nobody moved for many minutes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki! Who do you think you are!?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I was about to lose touch with reality when a sound brought me back to my surroundings. The three of us were startled simultaneously and looked at the hatch that had just opened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei appeared through the hatch with a dour expression. Since he'd addressed me, I tried to stand up, but I could only support my torso with an arm.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki!{w} Did you really think you could get out of this with simple threats? Those will not work on me, so once we make it out, you can say goodbye to your normal life.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I couldn't comprehend a word of what he was saying. He'd sat on the bed and put his face up close to mine. His eyes told me that he was being serious, but I couldn't help but respond with an exaggerated frown.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you listening to me!?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What the hell are you on about...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Stop with your façade. It all makes sense, and I know Shiroya must be working with you.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Huh?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: For a second, I thought he might've figured out we'd hidden the Sekimeiya and decided to blow it out of proportion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't worry, Erina, I know he's been threatening you from the start. We're all locked up here, so now he can't pull one of his tricks.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: When I left the lobby earlier, you were who followed me, not Sai. However, you made the others cover for you. That wasn't a smart move, idiot.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I didn't realize that everything was a fabrication. You killed the first Naomi and had everyone else lie about it. That's why you made up the elevator noise: to frame me or someone else.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Are you fucking out of your mind...? Why would I want to frame you if everyone else was covering for me?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Do not try to change the facts. When the second Naomi died, conveniently, I ended up on floor 6 while you and everyone you'd threatened were under me. That's why you could all act as if you had an alibi for her death.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You knew about the attic key and had been here already. You could've had every key from the beginning.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Right! How did I ignore such suspicious behavior? You and Shiroya left the attic and didn't come back for fifty minutes! And then the Sekimeiya mysteriously disappeared!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: But you instructed Sai to immediately act suspiciously as soon as we went down to confuse me.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Despite everything that had occurred, my bewilderment thus far couldn't compare to what I felt from the words I was hearing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And then... Isla died. You were behind that, right? You tried to make us believe that you were sleeping as it happened! How did I swallow that lie...?{w} Shiroya found the hidden passage in the storeroom? How was I so stupid...? You were about to use it...!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Before showing up in the lobby, you came from hallway B! You were too stupid to appear from hallway A after removing the Sekimeiya from the cleaning room!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No wonder you sided with Erina and wanted everyone to stay locked in here. After all, you'd hidden the Sekimeiya and could safely sleep like you were doing just now. Did you actually think any of this would work?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...{w}Are you just fucking around, or are you really this dumb?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I suppose you're not going to give up. You two are the culprits behind this incident.{w} Why were you in the first group of the guided visit when you've shown no interest in the gems? Now that I've learned about it, you must confess. I know you didn't attempt to threaten me individually since I work here and there's no way I'd give in to you.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'm having a hard time following. Do you actually believe what you're saying?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Katei's face shifted. I couldn't understand what was happening.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I never thought you were brilliant, but come on. There are some huge inconsistencies with everything that you said. What's gotten into you?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Instead of replying, he looked at Erina. Upon seeing that she didn't immediately corroborate his story, he breathed faintly to keep calm.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm serious, tell me. Did you just rub some brain cells together for this and come here thinking that you'd cracked the mystery? I discarded a few theories earlier because they relied on you being completely brainless, but now I should reconsider them.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Once again, he decided to remain quiet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Subsequently, he retraced his steps and looked through the hatch. My perception of him had been changing as time advanced, but it had suddenly taken a significant turn. I still hadn't processed a few of the things he said.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell...? That son of a bitch...!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...It was time to stand up. I moved first since Katei had forcefully changed my mood. I walked up to him, and ignoring his awkwardly placed body, I kneeled down, trying to understand what he was looking at.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What? There's no way...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sai and Akaro weren't there.{w} From the hatch, I could see the entire lower bedroom devoid of any human presence.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where are they? They couldn't have left...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I went down the ladder.{w} They weren't in the wardrobe or under the bed.{w} Countless questions hammered from inside my head, but I immediately went to check the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The chain isn't set.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I said that out loud to inform the others who still remained upstairs. I attempted to get the door to open, but it still was locked in place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't get it... How did they do it?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It had to be around {time=15:30.} I doubted we'd been in the bedroom for more than 25 minutes. No matter what had happened, it was clear that calmness wasn't what awaited us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...At first, Sai began telling me that you'd threatened him and went into detail explaining how you'd managed to accomplish everything.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I didn't believe him at all, but he started to make some compelling arguments. It was Sai, though, so I didn't take him seriously.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: However, even though Akaro had been looking at him with skepticism from the start, after a while, he confirmed Sai's story and gave us his version. He said you'd threatened him too, that Erina had fallen victim as well.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'm sorry... But at that time, everything was pieced together, and I truly believed them.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: This is too much... So they escaped after you went through the hatch?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't know how, but yes.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I had no idea what was happening. Leaving should've been impossible, let alone in such a short time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Both of them probably wanted you to go up so they could leave without being seen.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: And your stupidity was the perfect base for that to work. Like flour in a cake.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Maybe the lock could be forced with something like a card, but it'd take a long time. There's no way they could've escaped in less than a minute.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: The chain isn't set, so they definitely left through the door.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Would we not have heard it if they'd forced it open? Maybe it was removed as a trick, to make us think they used the door.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I hated that feeling. We'd been shoved into another mystery without solving anything, and Sai's plan had worked. Additionally, it appeared that Akaro had no problem working with him to create a story where I was the main culprit.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We would've left eventually, but the notion that nobody would be able to go back to the past if we stayed there was already obsolete. It had become possible for Sai and Akaro to appear in the past, if that was part of their intent.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though Erina hadn't reacted strongly, there was an important implication: Sai and Akaro worked together, so they could've orchestrated the recording if they'd either worked with Isla or threatened her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Does it even matter? This is the logic Sai used when Shiroya and I left the attic: if something happens, it'll be their fault. Can we not apply it now?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Admittedly, I was tired, and my body demanded me to sleep again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're crazy. They played us like this!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: They played you. Do you want to break the door open? We agreed to stay here until the police come, and now we've learned who the culprits were. They must've had a goal in mind, and it's very likely they accomplished it already. You can go search for them if you think that'll do anything.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I was exhausted. I let my body fall onto the bed at my side and disconnected from the conversation.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei began knocking on the door and yelling. I didn't know what to think, as I couldn't bring myself to completely trust his story. If everything actually happened like he said, Sai and Akaro would have clearly communicated that they had ulterior motives—which they'd managed to keep mostly hidden until that point—even though they escaped.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Leaving anyway meant that they'd needed to get out so badly, they didn't care.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: *sigh* Should we try to leave? They were probably hoping we'd still stay here after they escaped, which is why they blatantly did so.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I don't want to. I'm not sure what Akaro's deal is, but if Sai was the only one to escape, I would've thought that his motive was to make us chase after him to undo the bedroom lock.{w} If they're still in the tower, there's not much they can do. They can go to the past or hide the Sekimeiya, but they'd still be trapped in here. Even if they went far back enough to exit the tower, there's no reason for us to chase them.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But what if one of them had the handle for the hidden exit? They could leave with the Sekimeiya!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then they're already gone. However, if they could open it, they would've done that earlier.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Th-They could've figured out a way to open the door after they found it!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei sighed in exasperation and set the chain again. The key was outside, so the chain would prevent Akaro and Sai from returning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Why is the culprit hiding the Sekimeiya if we'll be able to find it?" That recurring question felt similar to our present situation.{w} What could they have wanted to achieve by making it out? Unless they wanted to experiment with the Sekimeiya or hide it, the only reason I could produce was that they'd needed to go back in time to finish something off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The other question was a lot more intriguing to me: how had they escaped? There was time to break the door open, and there was no way we'd missed a hidden person who'd opened it from the outside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: To open the door, the key would have been needed. There was no other way to accomplish it. However, we knew it couldn't have been inside the bedroom.{w} As I'd thought earlier, the only way to undo the lock was by using the key from the outside and then unsetting the chain from the inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With my eyes closed and without giving it much thought, I could reach a very easy explanation, similar to what Sai proposed before we'd locked ourselves in the bedroom:{w} "they left through the door and went to the past with the Sekimeiya. Then, they opened the bedroom's door with the key that we hid under the bathroom carpet. To escape, they simply pulled the door open from the inside, which would've been slightly open".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was reminiscent of the first bootstrap paradox concept I'd thought of a few hours earlier. The clean, brief way they'd managed to escape could have been an indication that it was accepted in our universe.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was an inherent property of those types of paradoxes: they had no origin. They were closed loops that occurred with no root or motive whatsoever.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Their escape method, though, had a real origin.{w} Sai's and Akaro's thoughts.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If one of them had thought of the way to escape, the final thing they needed to perform it was the universe's approval. They would've set an intangible origin of the loop, making it fundamentally different from a causal loop.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The key to the Sekimeiya cabinet isn't there...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Wh-What?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'd realized that to accomplish that sort of plan, they had to escape with the cabinet key to be able to go to the past. Upon turning my head, I'd seen that it wasn't on top of the drawers where I'd left it anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell did they want to do?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: In short, Sai and Akaro could've attempted one type of escape route: they knew where the Sekimeiya was, so they were in reach of one of the points necessary to accomplish the creation of the loop. After thinking of the way things would play out, they baited Katei out of the room. Subsequently, they left through an unlocked door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The last thing they had to do was travel back in time and unlock the door. If a result of their travel hadn't incited the idea to travel in the first place, their loop had a clear starting point. It also implied they were both culprits in the incident—we knew that any culprit possessed higher knowledge of the Sekimeiya's mechanics and limits.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was a slight problem: unlocking the door from the outside would make a bit of noise. If it happened before they thought of the concept, the loop would have no origin, as the noise itself would tell them what to do.{w} I couldn't think of a way to circumvent it easily. If the key could fit under the door, their future selves could've slid it inside. However, the gap wasn't big enough, or else we would've simply locked ourselves in and slid it out of the bedroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Beyond that concept, I felt that Katei's story was iffy. As likely as it was that Sai and Akaro could've conspired together, nothing told us Katei hadn't been in on it too.{w} They could've spent half an hour unlocking the door and then made it seem as if they'd magically escaped. Katei immediately suggested unlocking the bedroom to us, making for a simple motive if all three of them were secretly against Erina's request.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai! Akaro! What the hell are you trying to do!?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei continued knocking on the door, acting accordingly for someone who'd been played as badly as him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey! Sai! Akaro!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes, Katei. I'm sure they'll come back if you ask nicely.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you not worried at all about what they could be trying to do?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Not very much. If they're the culprits, we're safer now that they left. All they can do is go back in time, which sounds fairly harmless at this point—and unavoidable.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're right there. It's now clear that they were the culprits, so if they come back, we won't let them in.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sure, so you can stop with the knocking. They have the Sekimeiya, though, so I'm betting they could teleport back inside if they really wanted to.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...That's not a great thought to keep in mind.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei stepped aside. It appeared we'd decided to stay.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though Shiroya and Erina hadn't given their input, I figured they wanted that too and were likely dumbfounded by the fact that our self-imposed imprisonment hadn't even lasted for thirty minutes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Cable-Stayed
Synchronized, we all looked at the door. As we thought, Katei was no longer in front of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the...? Did they come back?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Hey! Who is it!?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It's me. What are you doing here?
entries.speaker: q

entries.text: Without a doubt, Akaro was behind the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't play dumb. We won't let you in!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Wait, wh-who...?{w} What the fuck happened to this handle...?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Ignoring Katei's assertion, Akaro began to forcefully attempt to open the door. We understood he had the key, as we heard it being turned over and over.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell are you doing!? You're not getting back in!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: But he was mistaken. After a few seconds of Akaro's struggle, the chain burst out and the door opened. Akaro's figure was behind it, and we saw the key placed in the outer keyhole.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...That's not a very good chain.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What do you think you're doing!? Where's Sai!?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Everyone was speechless. The chain hadn't broken, but it had been forced open. It was old, so it wasn't too surprising. Apparently, my plan had an obvious hole from the start.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Strangely, Akaro wore a very confused expression. He looked at us one by one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck...? Who are you?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Seconds of silence followed. Nobody knew how to answer, as we weren't sure who that had been directed at.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who, me...?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes!
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...What's your game? Are you going to pretend you don't recognize me?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Akaro responded by looking at the rest of us, expecting to be backed up. However, his confusion only grew when he realized we found his words to be the strange ones.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Excuse me? Why are you all looking at me like that? Where the fuck did this man appear from?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You will not trick me twice.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Where's Sai?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sai? I have no idea. He left the room earlier and didn't come back. What are you all even doing here?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: As I saw how lost he looked, I began to take him seriously. He sounded genuine, but not a thing he was saying made sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What do you mean? Do you really not remember Katei?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Katei? Is that his name?{w} Where should I remember him from?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: He's been with us the whole time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: He took a few seconds to answer, during which he eyed me like I'd gone insane.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why... are you all lying? What's happening?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...H-Huh? What do you mean?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Out of nowhere, he looked at Shiroya. Like the rest of us, she was taken aback, as the two of them had barely exchanged words since we'd gotten trapped.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I mean... what I said. Why are you all here?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We tried to stay put in one place together. Do you not remember that?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, I do. That doesn't answer my question, though.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: How does it not answer your question? You and Sai escaped, and now you came back.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What!? That's not true! I didn't escape.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I couldn't quite grasp it, but something felt off about Akaro's behavior. Past his bizarre claims, he seemed more aggressive, and his voice sounded more composed. Not only that, but he'd been fixing his gaze on Shiroya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro, why did you come back? Do you intend to stay here again?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The door was locked, so were you all waiting here? I'm very confused.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What you are is a lying piece of shit. Do you think you can simply come back acting as if nothing happened?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I don't know who you are, but don't yell at me. I'm not opposed to staying here, but you'll all need to explain yourselves.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Erina moved forward and took the key out of the door. She brought Akaro inside, closed the door, and locked it. Then, she set the chain again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even if the chain can be ignored from the outside, we'll easily hear it if someone tries to force it open again.{w} I was probably wrong before. We should've kept the key inside to avoid all this. I'll keep it with me. This way, if Sai comes, he won't be able to enter or let anyone leave easily.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What about Isla? Aren't you going to go get her?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: None of us could believe what we were hearing. Had he forgotten what had happened, or was he talking about her dead body?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know what you're trying, but it's futile. You're revealing your true colors by trying to play dumb.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...I don't understand anything. I saw that the elevator was fixed, but how did you all get here?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Again, such an ambiguous question couldn't be answered by any of us since we didn't comprehend its meaning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The elevator? That was fixed a long time ago. And where do you mean...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Here, the Ashiya floor.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Uh... With the key Naomi had. Do you actually not remember that?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Are you fucking with me...?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: She's not. What's wrong with that?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well... I don't get it. Where was the key, exactly?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: In one of her pockets.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But... there's no way.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Do you not remember that Naomi died?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What? No... I mean, when was her body found?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Many hours ago.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Akaro closed his eyes and took a deep breath. He was as confused as us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you all lying to me?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's funny of you to say. Wasn't it you who told me that Atsuki had been threatening everyone?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Excuse me...? I never said that.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: My head was going numb. I had no way to interpret what I was hearing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is ridiculous. Did you all go insane?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: If you're being sincere, it's clear that your memories contradict ours. What time do you think it is?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I have no idea, but I don't think it's {time=16} yet.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Right, that matches the current time. What do you remember, beginning at the start of our imprisonment?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Atsuki, please don't tell me you're playing along. He's trying to manipulate us, and this time it's a lot more obvious.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Shut up. As I said, we stayed put, but eventually, you all left. Then, I went to find you and I heard knocks coming from here.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's not how it happened. You and Sai were the only ones who left. Do you not remember anything from the time before we started to wait?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I understood why Katei didn't want me to humor Akaro, but not too long ago, I'd considered the possibility that the Sekimeiya could cause memory loss. I wanted to know if that was possible, as it could've let Isla's story occur as we'd imagined it.{w} If Akaro had traveled through time after escaping, it could have been the direct cause of the state he was in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I-I'm having trouble understanding what you're referring to. Before we started to wait? We investigated the building, and Naomi appeared briefly just to disappear again.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's not true. You were surprised that Naomi's body was found, but not that she died. Subconsciously, you must've known that, but you didn't remember finding her. Is that right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you sure that nothing happened right before we began to wait?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't know what you're talking about.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We found a hidden passage in the storeroom, and a door that could lead outside.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You can't be serious. A hidden exit? Why are we still here, then?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We had no way to open it. Do you really not recall any of that?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't, because it didn't happen. There are no gaps in my memory, so don't treat me as if I'm delusional. Shiroya, tell me, is this some sort of trap?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I understand. That's fair, I suppose.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I'm sorry to sound so blunt, but is there a reason why you keep talking to her specifically?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh...{w} I don't know how to answer this. I sympathize with you two, as I've already said. That's why it's surprising to see you lying like this.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You're really saying that this guy has been with us the whole time... I suppose I deserve this treatment, don't I? Why don't you be straight with me, then?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Akaro... What the fuck are you talking about?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You sympathize with us...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Just drop it.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What the hell does that mean!? Everything about you has been suspicious from the start!
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I get it.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What do you get? Is your plan to drive us insane? Because you're doing a great job!
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why won't you answer? ...Why did you say that you sympathize with us?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Maybe you're the ones who lost your memories and forgot about the time when you told me.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...Are you out of your mind? Why the hell would we tell you anything about us?{w} No, I get it, the Sekimeiya must've inserted false memories into your head, right? Is that what you're going to say next?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Oh, you forgot about it too? That's funny.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I didn't forget about it, of course not. Why would it give me false memories, though?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I... wasn't being serious.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I was beginning to lose it. Until then, I'd been trying to tackle every mystery calmly no matter how crazy it had been. That time, though, knowing that Akaro could've been lying to us, I couldn't do the same. Was he messing with us and hinting at knowing more about us deliberately? I couldn't tell if he'd been referring to that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I could tell you weren't serious, but why did you mention the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Do I have to give you the rundown? We found out the Sekimeiya could make us travel to the past, so we locked ourselves up to escape from the culprit who's been using it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Akaro didn't answer, but he remained pensive. Since he hadn't objected to the existence of a time travel stone, he must've known about it in some capacity, even if some of his memories had really disappeared.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is there anything wrong with what I said?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Of course.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You don't seem too fazed after hearing that the Sekimeiya made us travel through time. But earlier, you didn't mention it when you explained your version of events, so how did you know about it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}I'm not sure.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You're pathetic, Akaro. What's your goal with these theatrics?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Shut the fuck up...
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...In the case he was telling the truth, some of his memories must've remained hidden within his mind, as Naomi's death and the Sekimeiya's powers hadn't been received as a surprise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you really not remember Katei at all? He works in this building, managing the security system. He told us about all of that a while ago.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: None of that happened.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I laughed in frustration. Since we'd gotten trapped, not a single thing had made sense, and when we'd thought we'd begun to have the slightest grasp on some events, Akaro appeared and threw it all into question. If touching the Sekimeiya had caused it, we had probably ignored an extra effect of the travels from the beginning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wha... Isla?{w} Isla!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: All of a sudden, Erina snapped. Her whole face shifted into the most desperate expression a human could make, and she dashed toward the door, slamming into it.{w} Ignoring that she had the right key and that the chain was set, she tried to pull it open frantically until her motions abruptly stopped.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What are you doing!?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I stood up from the bed, reacting to her sudden change. With Shiroya's help, I grabbed her shoulders before she stopped moving, thinking that she might've suffered from a panic or anxiety attack. Before we could say anything else, she crumpled down and started crying.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla... She's there. I heard her.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: In a voice distorted by sobs, she let out those words. The four of us exchanged looks, unsettled by that claim.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though Akaro seemed to have forgotten about Isla's death, he looked confused as well since none of us had heard anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She was suffering... I could hear her yell. She's here, outside this door.{w} There. You all hear her too... right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Whenever Erina stopped speaking, pure silence filled the room. After she asked us that, we paid attention, but no sound entered our ears.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes... it's her!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Erina, there's nobody outside...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't hear anything. You should lie down.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What? No, there's no way...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Even though she said that, her body gave out even further, as she understood that what she was saying couldn't be true.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She tried to steady herself by supporting her body on the door. I helped her stand back up and brought her closer to the bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She was forcefully shutting her eyes as a measure to resist the pain. What had happened to Isla might have suddenly rushed back to her—it was trauma she could never truly forget. She had surely hallucinated the sound, given how no one else had heard it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey... you don't mean to say that Isla...?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I nodded, making eye contact with him. Even though we knew nothing about Akaro, if he was acting disconcerted, it meant he'd maintained a façade from the start and had begun taking advantage of the low amount of suspicion we'd openly thrown at him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's... It can't be. She was with us the entire time.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Akaro sat on the other bed and placed his hands on his forehead, staring at his lap. He had stopped questioning us since we had mentioned the Sekimeiya, realizing that we hadn't been lying. Instead, he seemed to be trying to comprehend what had happened to him and why his memories didn't match ours.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you remember touching the Sekimeiya after leaving with Sai, even vaguely...? Touching the Sekimeiya with your skin makes you travel to the past. You know that, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, stop. I haven't seen Sai in a while, since he left the room, and I haven't touched the Sekimeiya like that either.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's not true. You admitted to touching it a while after we found the second Naomi.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The second...? I have no idea what you're saying. Please, shut up.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I was seriously straining him, so I refrained from continuing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He knew what time it was and didn't remember touching the Sekimeiya even once...{w} If he was being honest, it indicated that he hadn't traveled far through time. His internal clock would've differed from ours if he had, and if he'd looked at the time, he would've known it was earlier than it should've been, as he didn't remember the exact moment of the travel.{w} ...So if his memory issues were caused by the Sekimeiya, it was unlikely it was due to traveling farther than I had yet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm sorry, but can you leave me alone? I don't feel well, and it's hard to breathe with so many people around.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: He might not have been aware of how unreasonable his demand was since he hadn't yet accepted what Erina was going through. His face was identical to the one he'd been making when we found him in the bathroom—maybe he had a tendency to seek solitude when overwhelmed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina gave an immediate, wordless response in the form of standing up and moving to the ladder, obviously intent on going up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All right. Let us know if anything comes to you.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Mind Over Matter

Shiroya and I followed Akaro's request too, and Katei, while he maintained an offended expression full of doubt, joined us last. He closed the hatch so that anything he said couldn't reach Akaro's ears.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki, I thought you were a bit smarter than this. Are you going to let him trick you so blatantly?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The irony of his question was almost nauseating, but I fought back the urge to object to it. I was in no mood for pointless discussion. He sighed and sat on the same bed as Erina, in front of Shiroya and myself. He tried a few positions until he decided to lean back against the wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And we need to leave him the entire lower bedroom so that he doesn't cry. Meanwhile, only God knows what Sai is doing.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Once again, nobody acknowledged Katei's presumptuous and poorly timed jabs. He rolled his eyes, accepting that nobody would humor him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: His behavior had clearly changed gradually as time had gone on. While he'd attempted to look composed and firm at the start, he was no longer actively suppressing his anger and frustration.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to clear my head a bit. Nothing about Akaro's or Erina's recent actions made sense, but I knew I'd be lost if I tried to tackle those questions. Instead, I went one step back as I realized that I'd missed an important detail during all the fuss.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro was able to enter the room on his own, and when he did, we saw that the key was placed in the outer keyhole of the door. Since Akaro later told us that he'd only been drawn to the bedroom after hearing Katei's knocks, it's very unlikely that he had the key on him.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Instead, it must've already been placed in the keyhole, and he used it to open the door. This is a solid indicator of how Akaro and Sai managed to escape: the door was opened from the outside, using the key we'd hidden.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Of course, it's always possible they left it there to make us think that, but that seems a bit pointless because they didn't hesitate to leave us behind, openly telling us that we should suspect them anyway. Once they made it out, they probably left the key in the keyhole since they didn't need it for anything else.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Outside help was used to escape, and they accepted it by unsetting the chain. This supports what I thought of earlier, regarding the looped set of actions they could've fabricated on the spot.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: They thought of the loop, lured Katei up here, saw that the door had been opened, exited through it, traveled back in time, unlocked the door from the outside, and left the key in the outer keyhole. If the universe accepted this, it was a completely viable way out.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: In fact, since the door had to be opened from the outside, not much else works. It's very unlikely anyone else could've fulfilled that role. If one of us exits the room with the key that Erina has in a while and goes to the past to unlock the door, we'd still be creating a causal loop, as the only reason Erina has the key is because someone unlocked the way out for Akaro and Sai.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So if someone does go back to the past to unlock the door, for it to be a cohesive travel, that person will have to be unrelated to our imprisonment, and going back to the past can't be a result of our actions after we locked ourselves in here. Each of those actions branches out from the fact that Akaro and Sai have left.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: With how likely it is that Akaro and Sai dealt with the Sekimeiya after escaping, the person who will or already has traveled through time must use the Sekimeiya we hid in Naomi's locker, as its location hasn't been influenced by the escape.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Lastly, there's a much easier solution: that there was always someone else inside the building who we missed.{w} Just now, Erina acted like she heard Isla outside the bedroom. Even though nobody else heard anything, if it truly happened, she could've opened the door for Akaro and Sai if her existence there wasn't in any capacity derived from their escape.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I tried to calm Erina down by saying that nobody was outside, and I thought that it was impossible. However, it shouldn't be. It follows Shiroya's theory from earlier, in fact.{w} If Isla went weeks back in time, dying in the cabinet must be the final step of her travels. However, she said that her friend would wait for her outside the tower, meaning that there can be a living Isla somewhere right now.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And we found a door that might lead outside. We can't open it from here since we have no handle to turn, but the story might be different from the outside. Thinking about it, it's technically possible for anyone to have entered the tower after the last time we did a thorough search, so they could've opened the bedroom's door. Of course, they would've required knowledge of what was going on inside...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I was still fixated on the thought that Akaro and Sai had the chance to retroactively open the door through the mere idea of having thought of a causal loop well-aligned with the circumstances...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If it was possible, it was a very powerful concept to put into practice, and the only requirement was to properly think of what you had to do. I knew I could be seen as suspicious, but I decided to attempt it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina, can you lend me the key for a second?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm...? Why?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What are you doing?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: A slight frown also appeared on Shiroya's face in response to my request.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I honestly just want to understand how Akaro and Sai left. I won't use it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Then why do you want it?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Because I need it to see if what I'm thinking of could work.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Technically, I'd lied. If it worked, I would end up using the key.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is it important...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I think so.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}Okay. As long as you don't run off with it or anything.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I'll be back in a second.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She gave me the key with her trust. My idea might have been rushed, but I didn't think that posed an issue. Essentially, I wanted to replicate what I thought Akaro and Sai did to escape.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They didn't need to have the key inside since it was outside the room from the beginning and they could've used it after traveling. However, if I just managed to leave the room, I couldn't open the door after traveling. The key would be inside with Erina. That wouldn't allow the loop to work, so I wouldn't be able to exit in the first place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hence, my idea had to be shifted a little bit.{w} I would go down and attempt to open the door. If it was open, it'd mean that the loop could be completed. I'd leave, and on the crystal floor, I would unlock Naomi's locker and activate the Sekimeiya.{w} It was likely I would go back far enough, given how long the Sekimeiya had already been there. Then, when the time came, I would unlock the door from the outside with the key Erina had handed me, allowing the loop to be created.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Finally, once my original self left the room, I'd enter it immediately after experiencing the whole loop. For them, it would seem as if I hadn't gone anywhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened the hatch and went down, a little nervous to see if it would work. Akaro raised his head, but he didn't say anything until I began to walk toward the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Are you leaving?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: No idea.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If it worked, the door would be very slightly open, enough to allow me to drag it inward. Since Akaro had been sitting on the bed the whole time, in the future, I would have to open the door very slowly so that I didn't make noise he could notice.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I unset the chain, put two fingers in the hole, and dragged the door toward me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You need to use the key.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It didn't budge.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Could such a thing really not occur...? I sighed, slightly disappointed, and set the chain again.{w} Figuring the trick out would've felt like good progress toward understanding the Sekimeiya, so it was unfortunate that I couldn't know the reason why it hadn't functioned.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Ignore me. Do you remember anything else?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No, and I won't ever, since I have nothing to remember.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...If you say so.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I accepted his claim and went back up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you find anything out...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I doubt it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I gave the key back to Erina and sat where I'd been before. I heaved a sigh, ignoring the odd looks I received, and wondered if I could work with the result of my little test.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is really frustrating... There's no way to know why it didn't work.{w} While it's easy to assume that the existence of this kind of loop is impossible, or perhaps willingly creating one is... I can't draw a single conclusion. There are too many factors that could've stopped the loop from reaching its end, effectively denying its existence.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: For example, what if Akaro is lying to us?{w} He became cautious of my presence as soon as I approached the door, so if I'd gotten it to open, he might've restrained me if what he's after is preventing us from leaving and allowing Sai to roam freely. That could be why he prompted the four of us to go up top.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If he did that, I couldn't proceed, so the door would never have been open.{w} Similarly, what if Sai took the Sekimeiya out of Naomi's locker? Downstairs, I couldn't have used it to go back to the past, yet again cutting off the loop.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Depending on what determines the amount of time traveled, it's possible that activating the Sekimeiya wouldn't have sent me back far enough to open the door and that this problem would've repeated in the future if I'd tried it again. There are plenty of unknown factors that would make this loop an impossibility.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I recognized another potential point that could've interfered with my plan, and it was a pretty big oversight, as it had to do with the biggest difference between what I'd attempted and what I thought Akaro and Sai might've done.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Right... When Shiroya and I traveled from the cleaning room, even though the cart disappeared, it didn't appear in the attic with us, as the bodies we appeared in were most likely identical to how they had been at {time=12:10}, when both of us were in the attic in those same locations...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: This means that if I had traveled holding the bedroom key, chances are I wouldn't have appeared with it in the past. Akaro and Sai wouldn't have encountered that problem since, for them, the key would've always been under the bathroom's carpet.{w} But... no, that shouldn't have been a problem. I could've used one of the handles we left under the beds. There might've been another screwdriver in the opposite bedroom, and even if there wasn't, putting in screws without a screwdriver isn't too hard. Could it be that wasn't possible because it wasn't part of the loop I'd thought of...? Or maybe I just wouldn't have been able to do it without alerting Akaro.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Or, what if I wouldn't have been able to travel? When we left the Sekimeiya in Naomi's locker, it wasn't working. Perhaps it never started to function again for some reason.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Finally, I thought about the most interesting reason why the loop might not have worked for me, and I was reminded of how messy time travel could become in the blink of an eye.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We've already been here for more than forty minutes, and we think that the location we travel to is somehow determined by where we were in the recent past.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So, for example, it's possible that I would've gone thirty minutes to the past and appeared where I'd been fifteen minutes prior. Since I've been here in both of those time coordinates, I would've appeared in this bedroom.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Even if I appeared with the key, that would cause a situation that I never experienced. Going to the past would've immediately changed things, overwriting the way in which I'd gone to the past in the first place. The loop would've become impossible if this happened, resulting in my failed attempt.{w} ...And Akaro and Sai, who spent less time in the bedroom and most likely used a different Sekimeiya, might not have faced this issue either.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: For a few minutes, my mind lapsed into silence. I'd managed to ignore how tired I was, but the feeling was starting to kick back in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The four of us kept shifting around, mindlessly looking at the ceiling or at the walls. We were all powerless, and our lack of mutual trust wore us down from constantly being on guard.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't discard my recent thoughts. Akaro and Sai had found a way to escape that involved outside help. Furthermore, if the Akaro below us wasn't acting, he had undergone something that caused his memories to differ from ours.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The more I thought about it, the more I realized how powerful it would be if you could create loops that ensured your success from the beginning. The culprit we'd chased behind could've taken advantage of it, making sure that their movements would always work.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's bizarre, but if you understood how the Sekimeiya works thoroughly, you could abuse this concept to a sky-high extent.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: You want to cross a hallway full of doors and deadly traps, but you can think of many ways to do it and you're not sure which one will work.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: With the Sekimeiya, if you could be the creator of causal loops, assuring success in these situations would be a way to use them.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: You could think: "I will try doors 1, 3, and 5, and I'll walk touching the right wall. After I make it across, I will go around from the outside and leave a mark behind the door to this place."
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If you look where you'll leave a mark and find it, you'll know that arrangement of doors and movements will work. If the mark isn't there, you'll know you would die midway, rendering you unable to leave the mark.{w} You can keep thinking of different arrangements until the mark appears. Since you'll only move forth once you see the mark, it's an effective bootstrap—the end result is what allows it to happen. But despite being a "paradox", there's actually an origin to it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Even though this is an extreme situation, it can apply in any circumstance because it removes the generalized risk associated with going back to the past.{w} Regardless of the circumstances, you can think something up in your head. If it'll work, you'll see the successful result, and if it won't, nothing will happen. You would be guaranteed to never fail, no matter what you attempt.{w} The killer could've used this method before killing Naomi; "if I move this specific way after killing her and I'm not seen, I'll let my current self know by leaving a drawer in the next room open", for example.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Another big advantage is that you'd be able to make any move that's currently hard to accomplish by deciding it to occur retroactively.{w} At some point, the killer might have wanted to prevent us from entering a room. However, they couldn't go and lock it, or they would've been seen.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Their solution would've been to decide: "in the future, I'll go to the past and lock it, so it's already locked now". This doesn't have to be a bootstrap paradox, but it's fundamentally very similar to what I'm thinking.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Depending on how it works, the possibilities could be limitless. There's even a higher step to reach.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It's considerably different, but it follows along with a few things I thought about earlier, regarding the date displayed on Sai's watch.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Out of the countless examples, could you go back in time, trade information with someone, write it all down, and leave it all on a note that you'd see before traveling through time?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: You'd read the note and go back to the past. However, since you would already know the contents of it, you'd have no reason to exchange the information—all you'd have to do is leave behind the note you'd read so that you could read it before traveling.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The note itself would be a paradox that you caused, but was the past truly changed? Was a past in which you exchanged information truly overwritten? ...Or did it never exist in the first place?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...If Sai's watch got to "9999-12-31" by spending infinite time in a loop, did the pasts in which the time counted up to that date really exist in any capacity?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The final step is one I'm not willing to accept:{w} could you witness a very smoothly committed crime, decide that you were the perpetrator, and go back to the past to replicate it?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The loops until now always had some kind of origin to them, but this one doesn't. It firmly defies causality.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: However, what would be possible is going back in time, preventing the real perpetrator from committing their crime, and then replicating it being certain of your success. That's just a way to use a time travel device.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The Sekimeiya must operate on one of these levels, the lowest one being "thought-up loops aren't possible". If this is the case, Akaro and Sai must've received outside help from a third party.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Level 1, using a loop they created mentally, would've allowed them to escape on their own in the way I've been thinking about.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Level 2 would complicate things, and it's more of an interesting concept than anything. The recorder in Isla's purse made me think that there are some possible benefits of staying here for a much longer time even though it seemed incredibly negative at first.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If I found a very important reason to stay, and a method to accomplish it, probably through the security room's computer... Could I grab the recorder, go back to the past with it, and place it in Isla's purse for the sole purpose of reproducing everything exactly and to get to the point in which I decided to turn it into reality? ...That would be level 2.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: For now, I'll ignore it.{w} Would I send the recorder back in time to reproduce everything instead of writing a note that details it all thoroughly purely because "I didn't live that"? That's ridiculous.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Even though level 1 appears to have endless applications, there should be a daunting barrier to cross: the memories of the person who thinks of the loop. Someone who did this would always have to work around the past that they remember.{w} Let's say the culprit wanted to kill someone in the event room and then had to choose between hallways A and B to escape.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: These loops always entail going back to the past. If the culprit had seen hallway A empty after the point Naomi would be killed, later, when they thought that they had to create the loop, they'd know they couldn't use hallway A.{w} If they'd seen both hallways A and B empty instead, they would've put themselves into a corner and would be unable to create a loop in which they escaped successfully.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It sounds a bit crazy; "it doesn't matter if they saw these hallways empty—if they hadn't looked at them, they still would've been empty".{w} That's not the case, though. That logic clashes with the most important part of this concept: that the origin of the loop is the mind of the person who will execute it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Both hallways were empty. Why hadn't the culprit seen their future self escaping through one of them? The reason is that seeing their escape route would've told them about the plan they'd later think of, and the origin would've disappeared.{w} So one would never see a result of a future loop before having thought of it, as that could induce or highly influence its creation, resulting in the classic bootstrap "they thought of the loop because they had experienced it".
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If the culprit is operating under this knowledge, that'd be a very good reason to stay hidden. If they spent all their time in front of the security screens observing what occurred in real time across the building, whenever they needed to make a retroactive move, their own memories of all the empty places would be the one thing preventing them from accomplishing it.{w} Of course, this is also because the past can't be changed, so if they observed too much, they would make any future loop impossible, as they would never see a loop in action before thinking of it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: What it basically boils down to is that, in some instances, having a lack of knowledge could actually be far more beneficial than knowing everything.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It was a very intriguing concept, but nothing assured me it was applicable.{w} I was still a bit upset that I had no indication of why my plan hadn't worked... Would it work if I could slide the key under the door and wait a few minutes before trying to leave?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That would've matched Akaro's and Sai's circumstances more closely, but it could've led into even more reasons behind the failure. For example, Sai could've taken the key from under the door if he'd been nearby.{w} ...I wasn't sure what to do or think.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There might've been indications of how loops are handled already.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Technically, the first time I traveled to the past, I could have created a bootstrap unconsciously.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: From room B4, I traveled twenty minutes to the past. I didn't know what had happened, so I ended up taking the elevator to the sixth floor.{w} That action made our original selves follow the elevator up, and eventually, it all led into me traveling through time.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If I hadn't gone up with the elevator, things would have played out considerably differently. We would've remained on floor 4, and everyone else's thoughts would've varied.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: In short, if I hadn't gone up, it's possible I wouldn't have ended up traveling to the past. Therefore, traveling to the past is, in a way, what led me to traveling to the past.{w} I'm not sure it was a bootstrap, but what's certain is that I didn't intend for it to occur; by traveling, I merely finished up the past that had already taken place.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I ceased my thoughts—I was getting dizzy. The minutes had continued passing, and as expected, nothing had occurred.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were facing a dilemma regarding Sai. We knew he was probably still down there, but we didn't know whether following him was what he wanted. His intent was unclear whether it was disrupting the peace, experimenting with the Sekimeiya, or following along with his bigger plan.{w} Ultimately, we had once again decided to continue staying locked up because of Erina's input.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My thoughts had trailed off and were revived by Shiroya's yawn. The silence had become unsettling, as it had gone on for more than thirty minutes since we'd left Akaro below.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Are you guys really fine with this?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei took my renewed awareness as a chance to question our actions again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We're letting Sai run free and ignoring Akaro's obvious lies. Don't you understand they set this up? Akaro's just making sure we don't head down. Why else would he have come back?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Don't you think that if that was what he wanted, he wouldn't have chosen to tell us such a wild story?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Of course I don't. Before they left, they made up this whole scenario where you were the mastermind. I'm betting they thought of this "Akaro has lost his memories" story precisely to make us think it's too ridiculous to be a lie.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, if you wanna leave, you're alone on that. We've already decided what we'll do.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: He glared at me with an incensed look and attempted to calm himself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He didn't insist further before closing his eyes again.{w} I thought he had given up, but not long after, he opened his mouth again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Fine. Stay here if you want, but unlike you, I won't let anyone laugh in my face like Akaro is doing right now.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: With three silent pairs of eyes looking at him, he approached the hatch and opened it. He roughly climbed down the ladder, not letting go of his indignation for one second.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We returned our gazes to where they had been, intending to continue letting time pass quietly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the...? What a joke.{w} Atsuki! Come here!
entries.speaker: k4

entries.text: Katei's voice boomed through the open hatch. Shiroya and Erina looked at me, in search of my reaction. I simply sighed and stood up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I mimicked Katei's actions and climbed down. Upon stepping off the ladder, it didn't take me even half a second to comprehend Katei's shout.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, this is just great.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Stop messing around. Perhaps the two of them weren't so far off the mark earlier.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: With intrigued looks, Shiroya and Erina peeked through the hatch. From it, they could see the empty room around Katei and me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is he gone again...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Well, he's not here! So yes!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I rubbed my eyes at Katei's obnoxious voice. Meanwhile, I got closer to the door as he confirmed that Akaro wasn't anywhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The chain is still set. That's strange.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Strange? No, Atsuki, you really screwed up this time.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: From Shiroya's face, I could tell she and I knew word by word the accusation Katei was about to make.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's strange is what you did earlier. You took the key from Erina, came here, and unlocked the door for Akaro. Then you set the chain.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Why the hell would I do that?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: To let him escape, idiot!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Wasn't he the one who decided to come in the first place?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. It appears both of you aren't quite on the bright side. If I'm wrong, go ahead and illuminate us: why did you want the key?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: To see if I could retroactively open the door.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...You think you're smart, don't you? You have gone too far. It seems that Atsuki, Akaro, and Sai were working together the whole time. Shiroya, are you part of the group too?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Instead of answering, she came down, followed by Erina. She looked around, but Akaro wasn't anywhere. He'd disappeared without leaving a trace, as if he'd been an illusion from the start.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At the same time, I couldn't blame Katei that much for suspecting me since I understood how questionable my actions looked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Anyway, this is more than enough. We're leaving.{w} Atsuki, this time, that camera clearly recorded your actions when you let Akaro escape. Don't think this will go unpunished.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Oh shit. How could I forget about it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I had to stop taking him seriously, as that would eventually drive me insane.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He pushed me aside, unset the chain, and tried to open the door, but only met with failure.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All right, Erina, we've tried your suggestion, but it's not going to work if half of us have different intentions. We need to go find Akaro and Sai. We can't even trust these two kids.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I didn't feel like giving my input, so I remained quiet. So did Erina, who looked down uncertainly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Enough already!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Remembering the pocket in which she'd hidden the key, Katei suddenly reached inside and retrieved it at the cost of startling her. Without reacting further, she stayed immobile, watching him insert the key into the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With abrupt and stiff motions, he turned it and dragged the door open. Without looking back, he walked away. He opted not to lock us inside and kept the door as it was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: None of us said anything or looked at each other. Instead, against my own expectations, Erina walked forward and exited the room too.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, Shiroya and I exchanged looks. She gave me a bitter smile that I replied to with a long sigh.{w} I estimated it was around {time=16:20}, meaning that less than five hours remained until our scheduled freedom. We stayed still for a few seconds, contemplating the open door in front of us that symbolized our utter failure to keep everyone in one place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Satellite
I'm guessing you wanted to try to see if Akaro and Sai could've escaped alone?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes. It didn't work, though.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I figured... Maybe we really missed a hidden person, then.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Maybe.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I shrugged lightly. I didn't know how else to approach their disappearance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, do you wanna stay here?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm not sure... First, we should fix that.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She pointed at the handleless door. The handles should've still been under the bed in the other bedroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Right, we shouldn't keep them detached.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: After more than an hour, I stepped out of the room and viewed the scenery of the attic again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, I entered the other bedroom and kneeled to see that both handles were still there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With the same screwdriver as before, I put them in place. I turned both to test that they worked properly, and I removed the key that Katei had left in the inner keyhole. Finally, I put it back in the drawers where we'd found it, along with the screwdriver.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Remember this?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: From my pocket, I took out the key to Naomi's locker.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh... You still had it?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah, I used the cabinet key to hide it. Akaro and Sai likely left with that later.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I think so, if they needed to use the Sekimeiya. I guess that's why Akaro was in such an odd state.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Most likely, if he wasn't lying. We could've been lucky the times we traveled since nothing happened to us. Maybe Akaro and Isla suffered from a side effect...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Like before, Shiroya went quiet at the mention of Isla. It had already been quite a while since we'd learned about her fate.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...By the way, is it me, or is the smell from earlier back?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, yes, now that you mention it... It's really similar to the one all around the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Hm... I can't tell where it's coming from, and it's not easy to perceive.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I moved around to see if getting closer to the source would be noticeable, but I felt no change.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I spent a while going over the way Akaro and Sai could've escaped, but I focused on the fact that the key was left in the outer keyhole. But even though Akaro escaped again, the chain is intact.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I know. I think we should go down to see what happened with the Sekimeiya. We could come across the person who opened the door for Akaro and Sai too.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: All right.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We hadn't inspected Akaro after he'd come back, so it was possible he had a key on him. Despite that, he couldn't have left the chain set when he exited.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We took timid steps out of the bedroom, as if an invisible net was still pulling us in. Once we were in the hallway, the first thing I did was enter the kitchen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's been so long since I drank anything. I bet you're thirsty too. We should've anticipated it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah. I tried to drink water when I went to the bathroom, but it wasn't very good.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I opened a cabinet to grab a glass. Tap water wasn't my preference at all, but it would suffice. I turned the valve, filled up the glass, and quickly took a sip.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, what the...?{w} You're right, no way this is drinkable.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I grimaced at the taste. Not much water had flowed out of the tap, but although it was pretty transparent, it wasn't something I could drink.{w} It had slightly alleviated the dryness, at least.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I left the glass on the countertop and went to inspect one of the many things we had to check: the living room's floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Look at this. I can see different pairs of footprints going between the entrance and the hallway, and there are many more under them that have degraded a lot.{w} It's too hard to conclude anything from them, though.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Erina and Katei had just left, so two of the pairs probably belonged to them. As I looked at the footprints more, I realized that at least three different pairs were distinguishable. One set was fairly small, another was medium-sized, and the last was the biggest. In addition, the smaller ones were older.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: H-Huh...{w} A-Are these Isla's? They can't be, right? And I think they're a bit too big.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Wait, look. The elevator's door is shut.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I walked back to the hallway and saw that the elevator was back in operation. After the many hours it had spent stuck in the attic, someone had chosen to reenable it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wondered if Erina or Katei had done it. What it meant was that the footprints wouldn't reveal the exact number of people who'd entered or exited the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We wanted to understand what had gone on while we'd stayed in the bedroom, so we chose to walk down a floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The attic key was still in the door. The vast and desolate sight of the sixth floor, which contrasted the comfort of the attic, was a stark reminder of how things had progressed since that morning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We should find Sai. He has to be somewhere, and he could know what happened to Akaro.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm not sure he'll willingly talk to us after what he did. If he's still around, though, we'll find him.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The same applied to Akaro, and there was a possibility one last person was to be found. Had Erina imagined her dead daughter's yells, or was there some truth behind them? After everything we'd thought, we couldn't fully rule out a living Isla being present around us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We monotonously circled down the floors like we'd done many times. We didn't waste time looking through the offices, as making it to the crystal floor was our priority. Although using the elevator would've been expedient, we wanted to stretch our legs and at least give a cursory glance through the drab center of the tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After moving down three floors, an unexpected sound interrupted the overwhelming silence. It was the elevator, moving through floor 4.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...There it is again.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We were in front of the elevator, but the opaque door didn't reveal any information.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wish the button would light up when the elevator's moving.{w} I doubt Erina and Katei would've used it already, no matter the reason. I'd say it was probably someone else.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We hadn't tried to open its door in the attic, so we couldn't know the direction it was moving toward. However, it was likely it had been used to move from one extreme of the building to the other.
entries.speaker: i
