entries.text: We would've gone back up if we'd known for sure that the elevator wasn't in the attic and was logically going up. Instead, it took us a few seconds to circle the outer corridors until we were by the staircase leading to floor 2.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There, the sound repeated, but it was much harder to notice.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Again?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm... It's only been a few seconds, so the first time, someone must've called it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You're right, yeah. So, either someone called it from under us and they just went up, or the opposite. I wouldn't think we missed someone above us, so I'd say the elevator was going up this last time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If we were about to find an empty crystal floor, we'd go up again. Since the attic key was still in the door, unless the elevator had been called from the attic, it could've only reached floor 6. Of course, assuming another key hadn't been used, but it wasn't likely one existed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Knowing that it still could've been going down, we continued heading toward the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shortly, we were in front of the stairs that led to that dark place where everything had started.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no revealing sight that immediately met our eyes. The floor spread out in front of us exactly as we remembered it.{w} In hallway A, the light had begun to find a path through the dark coating and bounced off the walls more than it had the last time I'd been there. The strange smell hadn't faded since we'd been in the attic, and it had started to seem like the natural scent of the tower. It wasn't unpleasant, only intriguing, as I couldn't associate it to anything I'd ever smelled, and we couldn't identify its source.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's see.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: At our left was the elevator. I approached it and grabbed its handle.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With little force, I attempted to open it, and there was unexpectedly no resistance. The door moved, uncovering an empty elevator and my mistaken assumption.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was going down...? Was there someone above us who we didn't see?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If so, they must be here now.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That left me more confused than I expected. While it was possible that someone went up and down from the crystal floor or sent an empty elevator down upon arriving in the attic, Shiroya's claim was the most probable one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, if we'd already missed someone on the upper floors, they'd probably stayed away from us intentionally, so using the elevator to reveal their existence was a little strange. I moved aside, trying not to obsess over it yet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before any of that, we should check if the Sekimeiya we left in the cabinet is still there.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, but I wouldn't bet on it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We stepped into hallway A. The cabinet key had been taken by Akaro and Sai, so no part of me expected to find a shiny egg behind the curtain.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We entered the event room, and I approached the cabinet to see if my expectations would be betrayed twice in a row.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's not there, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...No.{w} I can't wait to find Sai and hear the excuses he'll come up with.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Before I let the curtain fall, I tried to scroll the glass open, and it moved along with my fingers easily.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The cabinet was definitely unlocked with the key, so there's no way the Sekimeiya "teleported itself out".
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Isn't that still a little strange?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What is?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That they didn't lock it again. Maybe it's not, since it's obvious that Akaro and Sai did it, but I thought they would've done that to hide that they used the key.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm not sure. They could've been in a hurry, but they knew they'd be suspected regardless.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: However, the glass had been shut, not showing any signs of a hurry. The cabinet wasn't even locked, which was trivial to do manually. It was possible that there was more to Shiroya's input, but we had no way to be sure.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Earlier, I thought that they were maybe taking the Sekimeiya out so the cold wouldn't affect it. If that was the case, I'm pretty sure they would've locked the cabinet to prevent us from putting it back if we found it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: There are other cabinets with temperature functions, but I think you're right. I'm sure they could've taken care of the others in different ways too.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I suppose it's time to check our Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It's impossible anyone took it, but it might be working now. Do you want to activate it...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I don't know. It could be dangerous, but nothing happened to us the other times. It sounds reckless, but it can take us to the past... If it started working at some point, we might be able to go quite a few hours back.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If that happens, we won't appear in the tower, because there's no way we missed ourselves from the beginning. It could put us outside instantly.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Technically, we could've been in the secret part of the storeroom... You're right, though. It could take us out.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Seeing it like that, it was a lucky chance. Did the Sekimeiya have the power to kill us, erase our memories... and free us from the tower? Could it even let us see Miiya again?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't made up my mind. If we had the chance, activating it would always be tempting, as it could let us understand its mechanics and what had been going on. Undecided, we exited through hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Directly at our left was the staff room, housing our own Sekimeiya. We couldn't feel the presence of anyone else, so we entered it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Remembering which locker belonged to Naomi, I stepped toward it while Shiroya stayed by the door to alert me of any sound.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took the key out of my pocket and inserted it into the keyhole. With two fingers, I turned it to undo the lock. The sharp sound told me that I'd been successful.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Lastly, I removed the key, which opened the metallic door at the same time. I saw the narrow interior, with the coat hanging as we'd left it. Then, I raised my line of sight to reach the higher compartment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't storing anything.{w} Its interior contained nothing but an empty space waiting to be filled. ...My dumbfounded look persisted until the realization fully sank in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey, this is the right locker, isn't it? We left it up here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes... Is it not there?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Look, there's nothing.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She approached me with a neutral face. Not a slight hint of surprise emanated from her. By that point, something truly impressive would need to occur to evoke genuine shock from us. We felt like we'd seen it all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We definitely left it here. Was it still locked?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We let out exasperated sighs. We had kept the Sekimeiya hidden so that nobody else would find it, but it seemed it decided to spite us and disappear. Even though it hadn't made us travel before we'd left it, it evidently did have powers, as nobody should have been able to take it out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did it teleport like Sai's been saying?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Well, he and Akaro couldn't have taken it...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If it did, we might know when.{w} We've never seen two Sekimeiya exist at the same time, but it should've happened when one supposedly appeared in Sai's hip pack, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I nodded, unsure.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe there were two right then, but they had to be the same one and one had traveled from the future. Sai told you he didn't know he had it and he never put it there. He could've been telling the truth.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: At that point, there was another Sekimeiya in that cabinet in room B3, and we used it to travel to the past. If it can randomly teleport itself, it could be traveling to the past as well. After all, when we came back to that room, the Sekimeiya in the cabinet had disappeared after the time I saw it was gray.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Right, but we thought Sai took it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It could've traveled to the past, to Sai's hip pack. I get Sai's own existence is another mystery, though.{w} ...After that, he hid it in the cleaning room.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Next, we hid it in this locker, but at some point, the same thing happened. It teleported to the hallway A cabinet, with Isla...{w} This time, it didn't even have to go to the past. It could've simply teleported.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Then, since we brought it to the event room, Akaro and Sai could take it with the key. This could also explain how it appeared in the storeroom at the start...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I spent a few seconds in thought.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, is it disappearing randomly?{w} There are a couple things I'm not sure about. Even though it could have teleported to the storeroom, the cabinet in the event room was unlocked, so I think one of us moved it...{w} I suppose it's possible someone hid it in hallway B and it teleported to the storeroom, but that's hard to believe.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And there's one unexplained thing I can think of: the first time Isla disappeared from the cabinet, before appearing again.{w} Nothing was found inside it, so the Sekimeiya couldn't have teleported from this locker yet.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, something else is needed to explain that, yeah. I guess maybe it moved from the locker to another place, Katei activated it, and then it traveled again to the cabinet with Isla.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's one way to put it together. I think everything holds up.{w} Anyway, if the Sekimeiya was actually taken from here by someone, it's very possible they put it inside Isla's cabinet. Honestly, it feels out of place to think that it's been teleporting itself through time at random intervals.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, how else could it have disappeared from here? There's no way this lock was picked, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: After thinking about it, I spotted a couple of alternative paths to take.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The door was still locked, so I highly doubt the lock was picked and then set again. Only one thing would've been needed to get the Sekimeiya out of here if it never disappeared all by itself: the key.{w} Duplication can be easily achieved by traveling to the past since two versions of yourself exist at the same time. I'm still not sure about everything you can do with it, but it can work with objects, like how we're replicating our clothes after traveling.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't believe that ever happened to this key, but it's not out of the question. Since the time we found the first Naomi up to this point, it never traveled through time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Before that point, though, we don't know. While the mystery of the second Naomi is as unsolved as ever, she didn't have any keys on her, which makes me think that her keyring wasn't replicated alongside her body and clothes.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But that's not necessarily the truth. The main reason why I think that is because of the initial footprints in the attic and because her keys weren't removed from her first body. Maybe the reason for that is the killer had a replica of Naomi's keyring from the start.{w} It's even possible an entirely different person killed the second Naomi and grabbed her keys...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: They would've hidden them somewhere, so after how much we've searched, it's impressive if we still haven't found them. Since we searched everyone before locking ourselves up in the attic, it can't be that someone still had the four keys from the second Naomi at that point.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...While it's possible, I don't think another key like this one exists. I'm inclined to believe that the second Naomi never had any keys on her.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, so nobody could've opened the locker.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No, we could have.{w} We have the key, so we could go back to the past and unlock it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh... Well, I guess so.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: But this can't be it. I've spent a while thinking about these kinds of loops, and even though they seem possible, I find it hard to accept them.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If we go back to the past and get the Sekimeiya out of this locker, would the origin be that we realized it had happened? Would we be choosing to explain this mystery in our way?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Even if we go back to the past and get it out because we realize that Sai or Akaro will do it otherwise, the fundamental reason would still be that we've witnessed the end result already. On the surface, it sounds possible, but I don't believe it is.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya appraised me with an odd look. Perhaps listening to me toss out those words sounded bizarre, as we'd never had conversations remotely similar to that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're still saying that there's no other possibility, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No, I'm saying that, right now, there's likely only one:{w} someone else will grab this key, go back to the past, and use it to unlock the locker.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Such an abrupt response made me laugh. I might've been deluding myself a little, but I thought I'd reached that conclusion through semi-logical reasoning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I shook some thoughts away and closed the locker without locking it. Then, I left the room and told Shiroya to follow me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I entered the women's bathroom and waited for her to come in. While she looked at me quizzically, I opened the toilet's lid, dropped the key inside, and flushed it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There it goes. What are you doing?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah, it seems I was wrong. Perhaps I'm taking myself too seriously.{w} The universe didn't break, and I doubt the past changed.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: My theory involved someone else using the key to go back to the past and taking our Sekimeiya, so this was an easy way to deny that reality. It appears the answer was another one, though, meaning that the Sekimeiya vanished differently.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It could be teleporting itself.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Maybe it's just becoming invisible.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...We went back to the staff room. If, against all odds, my action had changed the past without breaking the universe or altering our memories, the locker would be locked and we'd have no way of getting the Sekimeiya out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped inside and tried to open it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd left it unlocked, so it opened. Once again, the winter coat was the only thing inside.{w} I brushed my hand through the higher compartment just to make sure that it wasn't actually going invisible or anything. I shrugged and closed the locker, unable to lock it anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Still nothing.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, Sai seems like a bottom feeder, so maybe you flushed the key into his home.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I exited the room without revealing that I'd been about to consider something similar. I smiled slightly to myself and looked around the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I guess we should try to find the others. We have to be close to someone.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, let's see who we come across.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: After the longest time, we put into action the usual procedure.{w} We began with the cleaning room at our side. Next was the crystal room B6, found on the opposite side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki, the Sekimeiya's on the floor.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'd been about to move to the next room when Shiroya's casual voice stopped me in place. I turned around slowly to see her nodding at my disbelief.{w} I approached the door and looked through it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In front of a cabinet was the Sekimeiya, lying on the floor and glowing white. Once again, Shiroya had found it as soon as we started to search.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's sudden. Who would've left it there?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Nobody. I bet someone activated it, disappeared, and didn't come back.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I thought of Akaro's case. If he'd forgotten about traveling from that room, he wouldn't have come back. Similarly, if someone had time traveled and appeared outside the tower, the Sekimeiya would've stayed there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We walked up to it with guarded stances. The sight was reminiscent of an anglerfish's lure, so we'd instinctively scanned the empty room before stepping in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kneeled, hid my right hand under my sleeve, and stood back up holding the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's definitely working. It burns.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What do we do with it?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I couldn't hold it for very long due to the heat increasing rapidly through my shirt. I started to walk toward the door as I thought about it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Either we use it or we leave it in its cabinet. There's no point in hiding it again if we're not gonna ever activate it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The potential for danger was real, but greed and curiosity were powerful. In my hands, I had the key to every mystery. I thought we had given up on understanding it, but if we figured out how to use a time travel device before it was exposed to the world, it was undeniable that the options were endless.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Given what happened while we were in the attic, it seems likely that whoever took the Sekimeiya was the main culprit behind everything. Despite that, they simply left it here, probably after using it. They haven't come back for it, so maybe that's a hint to their goal—or their failure.{w} Regardless, it was probably activated recently, so we shouldn't go too far back, just enough to understand what went down while we were in the attic.{w} Also, I don't think it's as hot as it was in the past, so depending on how far back we go, we could confirm that correlation.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...All right. Let's see what happens.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She moved closer to me, stating that she wanted to be in the range too. It was potentially a horrible idea, but the Sekimeiya's existence felt like nothing short of a miracle which we'd otherwise regret not taking advantage of. It could've been about to doom the entire world, but during those twelve hours, we had it all to ourselves... and a race to understand it could easily have been happening behind the scenes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We hadn't inspected the whole building yet, so the possibility of traveling to the recent past was open. I took my left hand out of my sleeve and brought it toward the Sekimeiya with intentions of further figuring out its mechanics, limits, and what had occurred outside the bedroom walls.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A Step Forward
As soon as I felt the direct heat on my fingers, I saw a door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm... back here.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Wait, the handle is attached.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I heard a sound coming from behind me. As I turned around, I saw Shiroya climbing down the ladder.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did you just appear there?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah. We traveled from room B6, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, and look, there's the handle. Either we went more than an hour and a half into the past, or just a few minutes.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya and I slowly scanned the place we'd traveled to, but we didn't spot anything else noteworthy. We'd appeared in the bedroom where we'd just been.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You said it didn't feel as hot as the previous times, so probably the latter.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She was right, meaning that we weren't going to see what had happened while we'd been locked up. However, every single travel revealed plentiful factors to analyze. Comparing them with earlier travels felt like the best way to get to conclusions.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is my fourth travel, and again, nothing bad has directly come out of it. I don't know what happened to Isla and Akaro, but I doubt the mere act of traveling is bringing any danger.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Regarding my memories, I summarized the basic events in case there was a glaring contradiction she could find.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, that's all that happened. Unless traveling affected our memories in the same way, there's nothing wrong with what you said.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm starting to think more and more that Akaro lied to us. He reacted to the mention of the Sekimeiya, but that could've been intentional, to relate his memory loss to it and make it more believable. I feel that Katei was right and he was trying to prevent us from leaving. After his job was done, he escaped somehow.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...How, though?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I don't know, but I can come up with a bit of an idea.{w} We had the key, and the chain was left set. That makes it likely that he teleported out. ...I thought that perhaps Sai did that.{w} Maybe he traveled next to the door to encompass Akaro and make him escape since neither of them could open the door. It could be that he made us go to the upper bedroom so that we wouldn't travel with him. I don't know why they'd do any of that, but there's not much else I can think of.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Actually, no, Akaro could've escaped all by himself and left the chain set.{w} Maybe he suddenly disappeared from the room, traveling to the past. Then, in the past, he activated the Sekimeiya to encompass the bed on which he was sitting; it wasn't necessary for Sai to do that as long as Akaro had thought of it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That must've happened before someone traveled from room B6, then.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We walked out. When I looked at the living room, I instantly recognized our own footprints.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: These are definitely ours, and they're very recent. We went a few minutes to the past.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Someone used the Sekimeiya very shortly before us. We can't see what happened, but we can be pretty sure of that.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: And if Akaro never actually escaped the way I said, it's possible they went very far into the past. We spent a long time in the bedroom, so there was a lot of time for the Sekimeiya to store energy.{w} You know, this could've been what Akaro and Sai worked together to accomplish. The stored time was originally Sai's idea.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Akaro's job could have been to keep us from exiting the bedroom, letting the Sekimeiya store time for a while. Once they'd waited the required amount, they activated it and went far enough into the past to exit the tower. Since the Sekimeiya was left on the floor, it's possible they aren't here anymore.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm... And they couldn't simply have waited more before escaping the bedroom because the Sekimeiya was chilled.{w} There's still the disappearing Sekimeiya in the locker to explain, but that'd be the only thing.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah.{w} Sai seemed to be having fun, so exiting the tower doesn't seem like something he'd want to do. However, they did this right after discovering the storeroom's secret exit.{w} As soon as they saw that, they probably realized they could go back many hours in time, find that door from the outside, and try to enter and exit with the Sekimeiya. They might be about to try coming back in since doing it earlier would've made their own travel impossible.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Let's go down and keep an eye on the Sekimeiya. It's a bit hard to believe that everyone doesn't want to escape with it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I nodded. Shiroya rushed to the elevator and called it after seeing that the door wouldn't open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh... This happened again.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: The elevator, remember? We were the ones to call it, it seems. This also happened at the beginning, during my first travel.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh... I didn't even think about it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It's coming up, meaning that it was below us when we heard it on the office floors. We're going to the crystal floor, where we saw it already arrived.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: According to her, she called it without realizing that she was about to cause the noise we'd already heard. The belief that every event had an origin point was reinforced once more, as she'd unconsciously reenacted the past. Us hearing the elevator had derived into traveling to the past, but the action of calling the elevator had an organic origin.{w} Not only that, we'd explained the single sign of life we'd experienced, so we had to seriously wonder what happened to Sai, Akaro, Erina, and Katei.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When the button lit up, she opened the door, and we boarded the elevator. Without a second thought, she pressed the floor 1 button.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While it started to move down, we once again experienced the claustrophobic atmosphere that the dim light and opaque doors effortlessly created. We soon passed floor 3, where our past selves surely found themselves wondering who was inside the elevator and where it was headed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We weren't in a big hurry, but we knew that we would soon appear on the crystal floor from the stairs. I thought of what to do to escape our past field of vision.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We entered the event room from hallway A, and after seeing the empty cabinet, we looked inside Naomi's locker. We should go to the lobby, where we won't be seen.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It sounded like the best idea, so we moved there and closed the hallway A door behind us. Even though there wasn't much to be tense about, we felt safe staying there, and we began to automatically move toward the metal shutter.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Remember what I thought the time you appeared in the living room? It seemed like we appeared where we'd been in the midpoint of the time traveled.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, and this time, something similar happened. I noticed it too.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I think it was the opposite. You appeared in the lower level of the bedroom, and I was upstairs, next to the hatch. Those exact positions occurred before we unlocked the bedroom.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Right. I followed Katei down, and you peeked from the hatch when I was already below. That might've been the location.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And that probably happened a bit more than ten minutes before we touched the Sekimeiya. After that, we discussed whether to leave, placed the handles back on the door, walked down to the crystal floor, and talked about the Sekimeiya vanishing.{w} We appeared in the bedroom before the time we'd heard the elevator... We might've appeared where we'd been ten minutes prior to traveling while only going back five. It's the opposite of what I thought before. It swapped the two points, although I'm not sure if the times fit that well.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That could be it, but it's still not consistent with any of the past travels. If there aren't set rules, there's no point in trying to understand how the Sekimeiya works. But what's most important is that a past position was once again used to determine where we appeared, even if it was done differently.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We heard an indistinct sound coming from hallway A, made by a door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's us. We just entered the event room.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We waited, and seconds later, the same sound came from hallway B. Unmistakably, a closing door had created it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Now we're in the staff room. We'll travel very soon.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We thought we only had to wait until Shiroya became aware of one thing we'd missed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: H-Hey, look at the floor, there. Isn't that blood?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She was pointing at a spot next to the hallway A door. From afar, I could see a tiny red spot, close to the cleaning bucket. Both of us walked to it, and as the sight became clearer, Shiroya's interpretation proved to be right. A single drop of blood existed on the spacious floor of the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's definitely blood...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The contrast with the shiny, white floor was immense. I looked around the entire room, but the drop Shiroya had found was the only one I could see. Fortunately, it was enough to tell us something very important.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's almost dry. It's been here for a little while.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: From when we were locked up in the attic. Blood dripped off someone...{w} Akaro didn't look injured when he came back, but that doesn't mean much.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Isn't it strange that it was left here? If someone was in a hurry or being chased by an attacker, they wouldn't have cleaned it, but I feel like the culprit would have, right? Maybe it's not evidence worth cleaning up, but it tells us that something happened.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Blood can never be a good sign... I feel like this is a place where evidence would be removed because it doesn't have security cameras.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I stared at the single drop of blood.{w} Something about it was intriguing—while it wasn't a puddle, it was fairly wide. It wasn't a single drop that would come out of an innocuous scratch. Despite that, there was only one mark.{w} Since any wound that produced a drop of that size would keep bleeding, it was likely it had been covered to prevent further blood loss.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina and Katei must be somewhere, but they can't have anything to do with this.{w} Even though Akaro didn't appear injured, it's possible he dripped blood before traveling to the past, and time traveling could have undone a recent injury.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: After saying that, a thought came to me. "Is the Sekimeiya reconstructing our past bodies?" We'd asked ourselves that question many times before, and I had found a way to answer it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Abruptly, I put my hand in my right pocket and felt something. I took it out and showed it to Shiroya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Ah, that's for Naomi's locker! Did you appear with it after traveling?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I must have. I flushed it away before touching the Sekimeiya, but since I had it when we were in the bedroom, I appeared with it in my pocket.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Like we suspected, the Sekimeiya has been replicating our past bodies exactly as they were in the past. In the bedroom, I appeared facing the door. Even the position of my body matched, and yours must have too.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Since the key was "under my possession" at that point, it was also on the body I appeared in. Again, that's why the cleaning cart didn't appear anywhere in the past. What's more likely is that it ceased existing as soon as you traveled touching it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see, yeah... That must be how it works.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I closed my eyes. It was very likely we'd concluded something regarding the Sekimeiya's travels, but at first glance, it didn't seem too important. I had even thought of it before without giving it much consideration.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, we could be almost certain that the Sekimeiya replicated our past bodies exactly as they'd once been. As soon as I tried to explore that concept, something major came to me. It was proof that small details could open seemingly sealed doors and that we had to explore every little path.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Escaping alive was our main goal at the start. Then, escaping with a time travel device had begun to sound like an achievable goal that some of us probably shared.{w} However, Shiroya and I had internally sought an unreachable peak while we'd been taunted by such inconsequential time travel. That was saving our friend who'd died two weeks earlier.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though it had appeared impossible regardless of the approach, concluding that last detail might've opened the first real path to it, no matter how vague or improbable.{w} If we could understand what determined the exact amount of time to be traveled, and most importantly, the appearing location...{w} If there had been a time in which I'd been touching Miiya, and I could replicate that body...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The possibility that Miiya would appear with me was potentially real. While it didn't sound all that special, the locker key had just been brought back into existence. I'd flushed it away through the toilet, and I'd managed to get it back with the Sekimeiya. Miiya's circumstances were the same, with the sole difference that she was a human being.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My past body and my possessions of the past could be replicated, but Miiya might not have counted if I'd simply been "touching her".{w} But what if I could think of a time where I'd been holding her hand or her shirt? None immediately came to mind, but they could apply.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked at Shiroya, whose pensive look surely resembled mine. We'd remained silent for many seconds, and while I hadn't thought of voicing my recent thoughts to her, it was a path she could also find herself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took a couple steps back to lean on the column, trying to break through the single wall that blocked my reasoning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I might have jumped the gun by minimizing the fact that Miiya is a human.{w} While I thought that we couldn't rule this out without attempting it, I see a big problem that might just reveal its impossibility.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The biggest difference between a key and a human being, is, without a doubt, the possession of consciousness.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: In the bedroom, our past bodies were recreated, and we appeared within them. The locker key is proof enough of that.{w} However, what happened to the brain? If our past bodies were recreated, the brain belonged to a past version of us. Despite that, we possessed memories and knowledge obtained after the recreated point.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So even though we appeared in bodies identical to our past's, the past minds were left out...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Why did our consciousnesses appear in our past bodies without conflicting with our past consciousnesses? That has to be because we touched the Sekimeiya while in possession of a future consciousness. Then, it was put within a past version of us—one that had a vacant mind.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So, what would happen if I could replicate my body from a time I was holding Miiya? My consciousness would make it to the replicated body, but since Miiya's wouldn't travel with the Sekimeiya, there'd be none to insert into hers. Therefore, it's possible I'd appear next to a lifeless body, as past consciousnesses aren't being replicated.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But I can't know whether I'm overwriting my past consciousness every time I replicate my body or if it's merely not being replicated and I'm occupying an empty spot.{w} After all, the Sekimeiya touched Isla's dead body and she didn't travel. That's probably because there was no longer a consciousness present within her.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: To try to make this happen and test which hypothesis is correct, attaching ourselves to the smallest possibility, we'd have to understand the Sekimeiya completely. We would need to make one final, thorough attempt to save Miiya. Shiroya and I can't arrange the necessary circumstances by ourselves to see if it could ever work because a successful result would create an extra, permanent version of one of us...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So, the first step: what determines the point in time our replicated bodies are based on? It's definitely different from the amount of time traveled, and it doesn't seem to be consistent.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But the second step—the amount of distance traveled—appears to operate under a consistent rule: the longer the Sekimeiya spends storing energy, the farther we travel.{w} ...Meanwhile, the replicated location has differed with each travel, and there's no clear rule to draw. Nonetheless, it's hard to think only one thing would be consistent.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The core of replicating a past location is purely teleportation. We're teleporting to a coordinate of space we were once at.{w} However, how is the Sekimeiya working with that coordinate? While the answer could be that its powers are simply magical, there's more depth to it than I first thought.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The easiest concept of teleportation to grasp consists of two containers and matter teleporting from one to the other. The teleportation point is "the other container" because it exists and can be accessed.{w} We aren't appearing inside designated and fixed containers, though, so let's assume that the coordinate of the bedroom, where I appeared, can be measured with a number.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When I touched the Sekimeiya, it sent me to that space coordinate after recognizing that I'd found myself there in the past. The problem is that we live on Earth, a planet that is constantly moving.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: As time went forward, Earth would've moved away from that coordinate, and it wouldn't have corresponded to the attic's bedroom anymore. If the Sekimeiya had simply sent me to one of my past coordinates, chances are I would've appeared in the middle of space.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Going off Shiroya's estimate, we appeared where we were ten minutes prior to traveling while only going back five. At that point, the coordinate that had once belonged to the attic's bedroom had already been vacated by Earth...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I'd been walking in circles around the column, absorbed in my unusual thoughts. Shiroya saw that I'd stopped and stretched her body a bit.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Should we go? It's well past the time we traveled.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, but I want to do one thing first.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I showed her the locker key. Then, we left through hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It became evident we'd left the doors of two rooms open: the event room and room B6. I ignored them and walked to the bathrooms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Like before, I raised the toilet's lid and tossed the key inside, then flushed it away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Had to do it. I want to deny the reality where someone uses it in the past to take our Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, the universe handled it fine again. The way the Sekimeiya disappeared from the locker is still basically a locked-room mystery.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She shrugged, and while she was right, I still went to the staff room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was able to open the locker just fine, and there was no Sekimeiya inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm...{w} Nobody else ever held that key, right? Could someone go back in time and replicate a position where they were holding it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Only when Sai found the whole set on the first Naomi, I'm pretty sure.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: My mind had gone pretty deep into it: what if someone replicated a position in which they'd been "holding" me? Had that ever happened?{w} ...If that would create a lifeless body of mine, it could appear holding the key.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Let's get the Sekimeiya. It still has to be in the other room.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Across the hallway was the crystal room we'd traveled from. We pushed the door farther and peered into the empty space.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We lowered our view and scanned the shining floor. With puzzled faces, we stepped in to access better angles after failing to spot the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It's not here.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That didn't make any sense. Had someone taken it while we were in the lobby?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When we traveled, it would've fallen to the floor. Did it roll somewhere?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I looked all around me and shook my head.{w} Then, I continued circling the room with my eyes until I noticed an oddity.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A few cabinets were composed of drawers instead of having a hollow interior compartment. One of the drawers was sticking out more than the others.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked up to it, unsure if it was anything important. When Shiroya saw what I was staring at, she also realized what was off.{w} Upon closer examination, even though the difference was minimal, my observation was proven correct: the lowest drawer of a cabinet wasn't fully closed. Before I could reach it, Shiroya spoke about a detail I'd missed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is the cabinet the Sekimeiya was next to, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Oh, earlier? You're right, it was on the floor, in front of it...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Which meant that, most likely, the person who left the Sekimeiya behind also opened the drawer.{w} I extended my arm and pulled the drawer toward me. Immediately, an object within rolled around the narrow interior, making dry noises as it hit the wood.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After it stopped rolling, the immobile Sekimeiya met our eyes, letting out a surrounding faint glow. Aside from it, there was nothing else inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya and I looked at each other, well aware that what we were seeing didn't make sense. The Sekimeiya had disappeared only to reappear inside a nearby drawer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is it even the same one? The drawer wasn't shut all the way, so we can probably ignore the self-teleportation we've been thinking of. Someone most likely put it here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But... who would've failed to properly close a drawer? Once again, it seemed as if we'd been lured to the Sekimeiya's whereabouts.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before questioning anything else, I put my shirt between my hand and the Sekimeiya's surface, as I'd been trained to do. However, I couldn't last more than a couple seconds before I had to take my hand off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck...!? It's burning.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If we're right, that must mean that it's been here for a while...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: "The longer the Sekimeiya spends away from a cold temperature, the hotter it gets, the farther back in time you go, and the bigger the range is". If that was correct, she must've been right.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm pretty sure it wasn't this hot during previous travels.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It was an imposing claim. Every time we'd found the Sekimeiya, the decision of whether to touch it had been quick to arrive. If the proposition was to go substantially back through time, I wasn't so sure about it, as it would make our presence in the tower hard to accomplish and we would still be unable to change the past.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's put it in the cabinet.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I looked at Shiroya and was met with a bitter expression. She'd already made up her mind.{w} Touching it could have brought us out of the tower, but it also had the chance to considerably drag out our stay while we'd be unable to have any impact on a history which had already occurred. I nodded and began thinking about how to move it without burning myself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I think we should just stop altogether... Let's just wait until we can leave.{w} We can travel through time, which is still insane to think about, but there's no point to it, right? At most, it can help us understand what's going on, but there are cameras all over the place, and the police are probably a few hours away from entering.{w} We don't even know how the Sekimeiya got inside the drawer, and it's clear that we don't understand anything about what we got caught up in. Touching it again could just be dangerous, so there's no point in risking it...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I tacitly listened to her giving multiple reasons not to touch it. It left me a bit confused, as she hadn't been opposed to it mere minutes ago.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I'm sure you can imagine that I've been thinking about how we could undo what happened... but it's not possible. The more time I spend thinking about it, the further I am from being able to let the wound heal. I don't think having hope itself is bad, but it is if we know that it doesn't really exist. The Sekimeiya is useless.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I was left dumbfounded by those harsh words, and I found myself trying to think about a reply before realizing that I agreed with her. I'd been going on about Isla's decided fate while obsessing over a way to reverse Miiya's. In reality, both were just as impossible to change. ...I recalled the pensive face Shiroya had been making in the lobby, where she must've reached that ultimate conclusion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We said we'd go to Airun after we get out to see what's become of the cabin. Let's make sure that happens.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: As I felt a breaking wave of emotions, I managed to give her a nod. I'd let the desire to escape become a background goal, while it should've been the only thing to strive for. It had been sudden, but after all those dreamlike hours, Shiroya brought me back to reality—Miiya's death was irreversible.{w} I breathed deeply, trying to keep myself balanced.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A-All right... I agree.{w} Let's wait patiently and ignore whatever the hell the others are doing. At {time=21}, the front door has to open.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Right... What's going on here has nothing to do with us, and it's gotten too big to try to understand. You said Akaro and Sai could enter from the outside to grab the Sekimeiya, so let's leave it in the cabinet and wait next to it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I grabbed the bottom of my shirt with my left hand to create a small hammock where I placed the Sekimeiya. As the cloth wasn't touching my skin, I was able to transport the Sekimeiya safely. I quickly headed toward the door, and we left the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were in hallway B. My perspective on the recording had been fluctuating drastically, and once again, it had become one of the worst possibilities. If it did occur, despite meaning that Isla would be alive in the future, that was only the illusion of an upside: she'd end up going to the past to die inside the room A5 cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took short steps so that the Sekimeiya would stay still. Eventually, I reached the open door that led to the event room, where we would again attempt a wait, detaching ourselves from our surroundings.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Touch the Sekimeiya.
Enter the room.
The world froze.{w} However, strangely, movement was still within.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki and Shiroya lived in a delicate universe. A single modification could collapse the complex structure they were climbing.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...However, the structure could be partially frozen and then changed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This universe will be frozen, and that will permit its observation. It will become a universe that would collapse if set in motion.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Rules have to be bent abstractly—the flow must stop. Only that will allow an impossibility.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Theater Under The Sun

Atsuki and Shiroya were in front of the event room. Unbeknownst to them, instead of deftly weaving their way through myriad, tangled threads, those very same strings took hold of their own bodies.{w} Atsuki's hand reached for the Sekimeiya, and as his brain was informed of the most painful burn he'd ever felt, his eyes took in the sudden darkness that appeared around him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He attempted to understand where he'd appeared, but the lack of light made it futile. He'd touched the Sekimeiya, going against what he'd agreed with Shiroya. However, while there hadn't been a reason behind it, he didn't question his action.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After a few seconds lost within the darkness, his eyes began to adjust, and he spotted a faint light coming from his left. Immediately, he recognized where he was.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It belonged to the reception desk found in the lobby of Ashiya Tower. That was where he had appeared.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He had to determine the time. While the lack of light wasn't a complete giveaway, he knew he hadn't traveled just a short time back.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He approached the hallway B door and surreptitiously turned the doorknob, spending a while locating it. Without offering any resistance, it opened the path to the wide corridor, which resembled nothing more than a haunting void. It was just as dark as the lobby, with no light to verify his surroundings.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, he knew the layout and began to move forward. Even though he was lost in time, his movements hinted at a goal.{w} After a few steps, his motion was halted by a sound that echoed off the walls.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Stop moving at once! Stay still and do not run away.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: The sudden, robotic noise pierced through Atsuki's chest, accomplishing its demand before the words could be processed. Atsuki understood the meaning behind the voice, as it had been explained to him. It must've belonged to the microphone installed in the security room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He hadn't seen it, but a speaker was surely placed somewhere in the walls. Conclusions could be drawn from the overly loud voice: someone was in the security room, and most importantly, the hallway cameras were functioning. As Katei had told them, they possessed night vision. Atsuki had traveled to a point that met those conditions.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Awaiting his next instructions, he stayed immobile, showing no intention of defying what he'd been told. However, when the voice played again, a frown drew itself over his face.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What are you doing!? You cannot escape!
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: Atsuki was beginning to lose his sense of direction, as he still couldn't discern the walls around him. Those words let him know that he was not aware of the situation either.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was unlikely the last message had been addressed to him because he hadn't moved at all. To test it, he walked forward, waiting to see if his existence would be recognized.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After a few steps, no new message reverberated.{w} He looked up and saw a distant and faint green light. It belonged to a security camera, but he couldn't know if it was working.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, he had a way to assure he remained unseen. Attempting to achieve a safer position, he took a few more steps and began to feel the cold left wall.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He shortly spotted a door and took hold of its knob. Then, he felt an alien pain in his hand that startled him. Confused, he tried with his other hand and pushed open the door with ease.{w} To comprehend where he was, he reached for the closest wall. After recognizing the shape of a locker, he knew he'd picked the correct door and had arrived in the staff room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He'd chosen it for its lack of cameras. He thought something was happening around him, so he didn't want to be mistaken for an escaping culprit, and he could feel slightly more comfortable in a closed-off space.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There, he waited. He didn't know why it had all come to that, but the imposing darkness only allowed him to wait until he could understand what was happening.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Just a few minutes earlier, he'd been talking to Shiroya about making it out of the tower and resuming their old life. He couldn't yet be sure if touching the Sekimeiya had made that easier.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He stood next to the door, certain that he'd notice it if someone were to try to open it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But what he'd expected to be a short wait eventually morphed into more than half an hour of pure silence. As the empty minutes kept going by, ominous emotions began to fill his mind. Would he be mistaken for a criminal at the end of his wait? Was he alone, even though someone else must've been addressed earlier? If someone else was present, should he try to evade them or go look for them?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Countless thoughts passed through his brain, yet he couldn't decide. Wherever that point in time was, Atsuki spent a full hour of it as the sole guard of the staff room while uncertainty permeated his being.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Suddenly, he checked his pocket. There, he found a small key, which he recognized had the shape of Naomi's locker's.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Without warning, the lights turned on, emitting no noise. Instead of being startled, Atsuki shut his eyes forcibly, attacked by the intense illumination.{w} After a few attempts at reopening them, his vision finally adapted, and he looked around the room where he'd spent so much time. He confirmed that it was the staff room, looking exactly as he'd thought.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The lights indicated that he wasn't alone in the building, but they were no cue to start moving. His dilemma hadn't yet been solved, so he remained indecisive.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Before he could give his updated situation much thought, he heard a sound coming from the hallway, resembling the one of footsteps he'd heard a few times during the past hours.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Further amplifying their presence, the person in the hallway continued to make noise. Atsuki heard a door being opened and closed as well as sounds coming from behind the wall to his left.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki's heart began to beat faster. As much as he wanted to understand what was happening, he had no desire to be found. He was paying close attention to every sound, but he failed to recognize that someone was right behind the door.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He heard the knob being gripped and looked at it turning. He stepped back, and as soon as the door opened, Atsuki fixed his gaze on the eyes of the person who'd finally found him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The figure was immediately taken aback while its expression shaped into one of defiance. Atsuki, on the other hand, wore an unsure look after immediately recognizing the man.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Wh-What the fuck are you doing?" Those were the first words Atsuki heard in more than an hour.{w} He didn't know how to reply, so he moved forward, drawn in by the scenery behind the man.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, he stopped himself when he spotted something of massive importance. The man was transporting a black suitcase.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Aren't you going to fucking answer me!? Who are you!?"
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Since Atsuki knew that explaining wouldn't serve a purpose, he produced an inquiry of his own.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "What's that suitcase for?"{w} The man's expression instantly morphed again. Those cold words were interpreted as a clear and sudden attack, but he tried to hide his reaction.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What do you mean? It's just a suitcase. How were you even here?
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: First, tell me what you need the suitcase for.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Are you trying to imply something? I'm not following.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: Huh... I understand what's going on now. Are the gems already inside it, or were you about to go get them?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Being able to reason something out had calmed Atsuki. Every trace of fear had left his body, replaced by confidence. "...Can the past be changed after all?" That question floated into Atsuki's mind.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The man's face didn't change. He was lost in thought after Atsuki's abrupt accusation.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Nonchalantly, he entered the room and locked his piercing eyes on Atsuki, who didn't waver.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Suddenly, he grabbed Atsuki's neck and threw him into the wall.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What the fuck do you know? Were you waiting for me?
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: Atsuki's reasoning had given him reassurance, but it hadn't prepared him. He had future information, so he should've had the upper hand. However, his discussions with Sai had given him false expectations, and he hadn't reacted properly to an abrupt physical attack.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Kid, no matter what you think you know, you are done for. You are sticking your nose into something very delicate, and this will not stand.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: Those words didn't reach Atsuki, as his head had slammed too hard into the wall. While the man threw more and more threats at him, he was unaware that Atsuki's sight was only registering a blurry image of his face.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Once he had told him everything he'd deemed necessary, he let go of him, thinking that he'd managed to convey the seriousness of the situation. However, Atsuki's body plummeted down, the same lost gaze looking upward at the ceiling.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As soon as he understood what he'd done, the man rushed to grab him, hoping that he was only being tricked. However, that was far from the truth. Atsuki's remaining time alive was in a countdown, and as it ticked down, he couldn't even process that his fresh start with Shiroya would never begin.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When the man realized he'd become a murderer, he froze, inheriting Atsuki's dilemma. He couldn't move, and he knew that the hallway's cameras would record him. For that reason, he stood next to the door, spending the minutes growing accustomed to the thought that his life had been ruined.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He ran through many courses of action. Suddenly, he concluded that there was some hope left for him. Even though exiting the room would cement the reality of his actions, he might've had a way around it. After what had happened, though, he was unsure he could count on it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Eventually, the previous events repeated themselves. The door was opened from the outside, and the man met face to face with the first person who'd see him as a killer.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On the floor, Atsuki spent the last seconds of his life facing up, unable to move any part of his body. Resembling a hallucination, he saw his killer being startled by the knob's movement. When the door completed its arc and bounced on the wall, three more figures entered Atsuki's sight, but he couldn't distinguish their expressions.{w} In front of him, he saw four people.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Two men, a woman, and a girl. It seemed all of them were looking at him, and he felt something: he knew all of them. He recognized their clothes, bodies, and faces. He saw the last three of them rushing to him, but his mind cut off.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That was the last image Atsuki saw. Then, his consciousness didn't fade away, as he had none.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Similarly, none of this happened, as it couldn't. If the frozen sections could've been reached, everything would've crumbled down.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But... that wasn't all. Something else denied the whole structure's connection.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Another rule had been defied.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Ending: Ethereal Arc
A Step Forward
Only White

Still cupping the Sekimeiya with my shirt, I stepped into its room, where I saw the cabinet and another open door. Shiroya came after me, glancing at the cabinet, which was partially covered by the dark curtain.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She scrolled open the glass and helped me place the Sekimeiya inside. After we closed it again, we had a question to ask ourselves.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Should we lock it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I think we should. We said we wouldn't use it anymore, so there's no reason not to.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I nodded after thinking about it. Akaro and Sai took the key when they left the bedroom, so it stood to reason that they still had it. If they'd traveled through time far enough to appear outside the tower, they wouldn't have appeared with it—if they planned to enter once more, they would have hidden it somewhere to retrieve it easily.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nonetheless, locking it would prevent everyone else from opening it. I moved to the left side of the cabinet and crouched to manually turn the wheel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There. Only someone with the key will be able to open it. We'll stay here, though, so that won't happen.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She tried to move the glass and confirmed that I had locked it properly. To achieve a better effect, she pulled down the curtain and proceeded to glance around the room noncommittally, unsure of what else to do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We haven't seen Erina and Katei since we left the bedroom. Do you wanna search for them before we decide to stay put?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She didn't answer. I thought she was considering the whereabouts of Akaro and Sai, who we had to find as well, but a single word defied my assumption.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Look.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Her gaze was fixed on the floor. I traced the line, spotting a drop of blood in the middle of a room for the second time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were right next to it and hadn't seen it easily. It was smaller than the one in the lobby, but there was a much more important distinction.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This one isn't that old. It's not completely dry.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Is someone walking around and bleeding?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Despite what it seemed, there had to be something more to it. If what we'd seen in the lobby was only a single drop, it came from a fairly serious injury. The one in front of us didn't give the same impression. I looked all over the floor again and didn't see even another speck.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I think we should try to find the others, in case something bad has happened.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I took a good look at the blood. It wasn't fully dry like the spot in the lobby, indicating that the bleeding could've gone on for a while. If a wound had started to clot, it explained the smaller drop.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Small amounts of blood dry up fast. While many factors are involved, I could estimate it would take, say, half an hour for a bit of it to fully dry in our conditions. This spot is close to meeting that mark, while the one in the lobby dried up before we saw it...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: How do we do it, then? Does one of us stay here to make sure nobody takes the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: After all we'd considered, exploring the possibility of a deliberate trap to send us out wasn't that ridiculous. In truth, the two drops of blood didn't feel very natural.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I think we should do what we've been doing up until now. One of us stays in hallway C while the other looks through the rooms. It's unlikely anyone had an accident and bled on and off for so long... We should be careful.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I wasn't opposed, so we entered hallway A. Our tension had gradually escalated since we'd seen blood on the floor of the lobby. Using that arrangement felt safe enough, as we wouldn't be forced to separate ourselves while searching. Moving to the mechanical room would be the only unavoidable instance of that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll see if I find anyone, then.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She nodded sharply, standing next to hallway C. Volunteering to look through some rooms was no heroic task, but I felt a bit better doing it myself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naturally, my attention was first directed at the storeroom. I opened the door with Shiroya looking on from behind. The long corridor still extended up to the door without a handle, and I stepped in to see if I could spot any change.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, everything was identical, just as I remembered it. I had no way to know if the door had been opened from either side, but I was certain that I still couldn't do it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In front was room A5, where the gems were stolen. Although "the room where Isla was found" was a more suitable name... I looked down as I entered it, knowing that I'd have to see her face again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There she was, immobile, her skin already showing a slight ashen tint. There was nothing next to her, so I quickly closed the lid and looked through the other cabinets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After I'd seen all of their harmless interiors, I moved to the next room. Deeming it vacant was an easy task, which was repeated for the next four identical ones.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Only the security room remained. After it, I'd go to the mechanical room, make sure nobody had entered the event room, and Shiroya would move toward hallway B. That would prevent anyone from using the event room as a bridge to remain hidden.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But when I opened the door, I was met with a sudden and unexpected sight.{w} My mind reeled as I stared at it, too stunned to react differently. I abruptly turned to face Shiroya, who responded to me with a plain expression.{w} I yelled at her to come over, and she sprinted toward me. Not only had I seen something that put an end to the search, but I also knew that Shiroya and I absolutely couldn't be separated.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As soon as she peeked inside, she visibly recoiled. Then, she had to force herself to breathe deeply and try to look again. Once she did, she saw she hadn't been mistaken.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei's body was on the floor, partially under his desk. It appeared the two drops of blood had been a mere introduction to the sea we saw in the security room. His clothes, the desk, the floor... they'd all been splashed by the same red substance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even after trying to process the image for a full minute, I couldn't bring myself to move. The thick smell of blood began to disperse through the open door, repelling us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What is this...? There's no way...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: At some point, she said that, radiating pure disbelief. I couldn't bring myself to reply, but I took a step forward, scanning the dimly lit room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Three bright lights were situated in front of me. They were the three main computer monitors, which indicated that less than fifty minutes ago, it had been used.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya entered behind me, taking careful steps to avoid the blood that covered the majority of the floor. We looked at Katei's face, under the shadow of the desk. His darkened expression looked distressed and agitated, reminiscent of the one he'd made in the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I swallowed my accumulated saliva and carefully crouched to check his pulse, but I didn't feel anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried not to look in Shiroya's direction and continued inspecting Katei until I saw that a bit of blood was still pouring out of his skull. I didn't have to turn his head too much to see a huge crack. I immediately averted my eyes, with no doubts about what I would've seen if his white hair hadn't prevented it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood up, shaken by the eerie background noise that the arrhythmic sound of dripping blood and the whirring computer had joined forces to create.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...There's a horizontal crack in the back of his head. Given how much blood is on the desk, I think he fell on its edge.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Once again, Shiroya looked down at the pool of blood. It was natural for a head injury to bleed so much, and what I'd observed didn't reveal much. For all we knew, it was an accident.{w} The way I imagined it, if he'd fallen back, he would've hit his head against the desk, ended up under it, and pushed the chair away. Despite how much blood covered the floor, there were no bloody footprints leaving the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, the gruesome scenery obligated us to think that someone could've done it. Pushing Katei would've achieved the same result.{w} Vast pools of blood would take a long time to dry, so I easily spotted smaller drops on the sides of the desk. Those were much closer to drying up, reminding me of the one in the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No matter what happened, though... he was dead. Katei, who was an enigma of his own and never stopped claiming his innocence, met his sudden end right after freeing himself from confinement in the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Look at the screen. There's a message.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I quickly glanced at it. As she'd said, in the center of the middle screen, I saw a tiny message box, containing one single line of text.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "{time=10:04}: Camera(s) disabled and associated footage erased".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, what...? At {time=10:04}?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That must've been when Katei was here alone. We checked the time at {time=9:41.}.. Twenty minutes later was when we left, and he stayed behind, trying to fix the system.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You're right. And instead, he erased the existing footage and shut down the cameras. That's what this is saying.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The most conspicuous hint, a message left on the computer, was potential proof that Katei had been the culprit we were trying to ferret out. I reached for the mouse and dragged the message aside.{w} Behind it, the program Katei had attempted to display the footage with was the only thing seen on the screen. It had a list of all the cameras, but they were useless if they'd actually been disabled.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I lowered my eyes. The taskbar contained the single clock we had at our disposal. As soon as I glanced at it, the numbers switched from {time=16:59} to {time=17:00.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's {time=17.} Only four hours are left.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Let's get out of here. From this room too. The smell is getting unbearable.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I had no complaints. Even though the hallway's illumination was worse, we left the much darker room and breathed steadily after the minutes we'd spent inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The message on the screen... Without a doubt, it belonged to the security system program, but was that full proof of its trustworthiness? With such an obvious message being found next to him, I had to ask myself if it was legitimate or a diversion left by his killer. Not only did the room leave the possibility of an accident open, it also displayed an incriminating message next to Katei.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was the message a fabrication by the real culprit to pin the blame on Katei and play it off as an accident while they were the ones to deal with the cameras and the security system? It wasn't easy to tell, and I wasn't sure which idea I was more inclined to lean toward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, no. It doesn't make any sense. Look.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I followed Shiroya's line of sight again, that time up to the ceiling.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That green light is supposed to indicate that the camera's recording, right? There's no way they were disabled so long ago.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'd forgotten about that... You're right.{w} However... it was Katei who told us what the green light meant. We can't be certain about it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: They haven't stopped flickering, and I'm sure they also were before {time=10}, so if the cameras really aren't recording, the lights must simply indicate that they're powered on.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It's strange that Katei would tell a lie like that. If he disabled the cameras, part of the reason would be that he didn't want the police to see him when they entered. Despite that, he incriminated himself by lying to us about what the lights mean.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah, that's... not consistent. Could someone else have left that message to blame him?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm not sure, but thinking about it more, there's no way this was an accident...{w} If Katei fell backward and hit his head against the desk, it means he was exiting the room. Why would he try to leave with that message being shown on the screen? Another person had to be involved somehow.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Shiroya agreed with me. After a few pensive seconds, being presented once again with the fact that a murderer was nearby, we had to decide on what to do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you want to search for the others?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: W-We should. We don't know what happened to Akaro and Sai, but I'm worried about Erina. Just... We can't split up, Atsuki. We have to stay together no matter what.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I couldn't say it was unlikely for Erina to become a target for the culprit. Katei was employed by Ashiya, a member of the security staff, but Isla had died despite being a complete outsider and a child. Any one of us could've been next.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, okay. Let's stick together and find Erina. Let's just be extremely careful. We have nothing to defend ourselves with if we're suddenly attacked.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She gave me a strained, saddened look. Even though only four hours remained, seeing the outside world felt infinitely far away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's see if the Sekimeiya's still here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We entered the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya hadn't been taken while our attention was grabbed by the security room, so it was unlikely that was the intent of the culprit's plan. As a routine effort, I lowered the curtain again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We have to find Erina. It's... not good that we haven't seen her yet.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: All right. There's no need to separate at all. We're only trying to find her, and she wouldn't hide from us. It could be dangerous to try to corner the culprit.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Right. Let's finish up this floor...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We went to the lobby to access the mechanical room. Down the staircase was the strangely imposing room which could have served purposes beyond our understanding.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There were some spots out of reach from the stairs—under a table or behind some chairs in the back. Stepping farther in revealed the lack of any hidden person.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I doubt Erina would be in a hallway B room, but let's look before going up.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The first room we looked into was empty. Failing to stumble upon anyone made things grow gradually more unsettling... We knew someone had to have traveled with the Sekimeiya shortly before we did...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd explored the thought that, perhaps, if the range was huge, Erina had the chance to be caught up in it and escape the tower. However, Katei had gone downstairs before her and should've traveled as well. Since the dryness of his blood indicated that he'd died almost half an hour before we'd found him, I was willing to disregard that theory.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya and I proceeded to the next room. Of course, if they'd traveled out of the tower after leaving the attic, it was possible Katei had reentered the tower through the storeroom entrance and then died.
