entries.text: I started to go back down, paying as much attention to my surroundings as possible. Soon, my quiet steps reached the last staircase, leading to the floor where my past self still was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew I hadn't looked through every room below yet, but I still felt that task to be too perilous, knowing any sound could alert the Atsuki in the staff room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Therefore, I decided to first look through hallway A, which Shiroya and I didn't have time to start before Sai reappeared. After that, I'd wait for my past self to disappear.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I carefully walked down the stairs and directed myself toward the storeroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't been in there since Sai and Shiroya traveled together, but there was no change that caught my eye. Knowing whether the door had recently opened was impossible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As soon as I opened the next door, something stood out. One of the cabinets had its lid open and leaning on the wall. I frowned while trying to understand if that made sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Inside it was Isla. It was the cabinet where she'd been found. But I knew it had been closed the last time I was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And that was just before I saw Katei's death. I looked at every room, and there's no way I left this cabinet open.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Was it a confirmation that someone else was still with me? Sai and the other Shiroya were the two likely candidates to have done it...{w} I was more confused than surprised. Why would someone have opened that cabinet... and left it open?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no need to leave Isla's body on display, so I gingerly lowered the lid. I scanned the rest of the room, but I found nothing else of importance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Afterward, I proceeded with the search, my expectations of finding something suddenly higher.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But every room was empty. I still didn't want to make any accidental noise, so I only took a peek at them. I finished at the security room, where the scene of Katei's death appeared essentially unchanged.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I moved the chair and looked at the computer, which displayed {time=18:24.} I felt that going back to the staff room at {time=18:30} was appropriate, but I didn't want to risk being too early.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't exactly the most comforting room with the state Katei was in, but I decided to stay there for the remainder of the time since it gave me access to the computer's clock.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: His face was under his desk, so I didn't have to look at it, and the unsettling smell of blood quickly became an afterthought. Standing straight and with a blank mind, I stiffly waited for the time to pass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Until I remembered the chase from earlier.{w} I kneeled beside Katei and put my hand in the pocket where he'd kept most of his keys.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's not here... the key to the bathrooms. All the others are, though. His killer must've picked it up, or maybe it was Sai, if they're not the same person. Regardless, it definitely would've been a bad idea to hide inside one.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Upon further inspection, I realized that the rusty key, which he'd kept in another pocket, was gone too.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They also took that old-looking key... Was the person who originally dropped it in hallway A responsible for this?{w} Maybe that's not it. I've been thinking that someone could enter the tower through the storeroom, but if that key belonged to that door, maybe they'd need it from the outside. I'm not sure they would try picking it up to appear in the past with it because their replicated locations holding the key would all be inside the tower...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Unless I go back to thinking about thought-up loops, I guess. There could be something that would work.{w} The person who killed Katei took that rusty key and walked out of the tower through the storeroom door, which was open. That created a location outside the tower where they were holding the key that could be replicated. Then, they reentered and used the Sekimeiya to go back in time. In the past, they appeared outside the tower holding the key, so they were able to unlock the door and reenter with something they'd obtained outside—like a knife. They left the door open so that their past self could exit with the key and create the replicated location.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Would that work? The key isn't here, so I can't even attempt it. But if the culprit's plan was to leave with the Sekimeiya, they would've been able to achieve it very easily by doing this.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I stood back up, trying not to meet Katei's eyes. When I glanced around the room again, I became aware of an obvious detail.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hang on, this is strange.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The computer's screen is lit, meaning that someone used it in the past fifty minutes. It was exactly {time=17} when we found Katei's body, so it's been far more than that.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I suppose Sai did say he saw Katei here. Unless someone else was here semi-recently, he saw it after us.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: What I found most strange was that the three screens looked identical to how they had at {time=17.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "{time=10:04}: Camera(s) disabled and associated footage erased". That same message was on the side I'd dragged it to, and behind it was the security camera program.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I grabbed the mouse and clicked on its "accept" button. The program used a pretty complicated interface, and I didn't know what many things meant. As I'd seen before, there was a list of all the cameras on the left.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I looked at it again, I saw that one in particular was selected, named "RECAM_12_01". I brought the cursor over and tried to view it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But an error sound played, accompanied by the same message. "{time=10:04}: {tip=camera}Camera(s) disabled and associated footage erased{/tip}".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It appeared we really couldn't look at the footage, but the message still felt like it too obviously incriminated Katei. I let go of the mouse and stepped aside from the computer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to think if the selected camera meant anything, but I had nothing to work with. Instead, I did what I'd planned to do and managed to let go of my thoughts until the time came.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At {time=18:30}, I left the room. It was time to reunite with the Sekimeiya, so I went to hallway B through the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The staff room was closed, like I'd left it. Warily, I stepped up to it and turned the knob.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I pushed the door open and saw the gray Sekimeiya on the floor.{w} Since everything had gone as expected, I entered, reclaiming my place as the sole Atsuki.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was relieved that nothing unexpected had occurred. I knew that I couldn't stop looking for Shiroya yet, so I picked up the Sekimeiya and put it in the newly accessible locker.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's good that I still have the key. If the replicated location was from earlier, I would've lost it. I shouldn't have traveled holding it, just in case.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I left the Sekimeiya above and closed the door. Then, I proceeded to lock it so that I would be able to wander around without leaving it easily accessible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I quickly became indecisive. Perhaps it was smarter to bring it with me while I searched so that I had an emergency escape method.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Having to constantly fear my death was disheartening, to say the least. While I decided, I sat next to the middle lockers. Maybe staying there was a better idea. I couldn't enter the attic, but it was clear that anyone remaining in the tower didn't want to show themselves.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I felt I had to look through the hallway B rooms before deciding to stop. I prayed that Shiroya was safe, but I could only assume that she wasn't nearby anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I might've already been in the tower for longer than the initially proposed twelve hours. Adding all the time I'd relived by traveling through time, I figured I was minutes away from meeting the mark.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once again thoroughly regretting my choice to ever set foot inside that building, I stood up to make sure a nightmare didn't await in hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had repeatedly considered that my hours in the tower were a dream. Had I already accepted the reality in which a time travel device existed? No matter what everything was leading to, would the world undergo a drastic change upon being exposed to the Sekimeiya? I'd wanted that day to be the first day of my new life with Shiroya... but was it set to be a turning point for every human being?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The item I'd just locked away... What was it going to be responsible for? I felt like it had nearly broken when it fell in the event room, something that might honestly have been for the better.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was walking to the door when I turned to glance at the locker. The thought of breaking the Sekimeiya crossed my mind, but my eyes locked on one spot for another reason.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...There was something on the floor—to the left of where I'd been sitting. I approached it and saw a small piece of paper, hastily folded.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naturally, I frowned. I didn't recognize it from anywhere in the tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I grabbed it and scanned its contents. A few lines of text had been written in black.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But before I read it, I had already stopped breathing. A single peek made my hand begin to tremble and my thoughts collapse entirely.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Fractal Freefall
One day, before the afternoon ended, you could see the figures of two young students on a bench, letting a cold breeze hit their faces while they looked at the park they'd grown to love.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They had been talking for a while, so they proceeded to quietly look at the younger kids run around, making good use of the last few minutes of sunlight.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They were a boy and a girl who had known each other for many years. For that reason, the level of trust they'd built allowed them to feel a peaceful warmth just by being next to each other.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Soon, after the other kids left, they would do so as well. After walking down a few streets, one of the two would take a different turn to complete the day on their own.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was a routine they were happy with and felt lucky to share. The boy let his mind relax, looking at the sky as it began to darken. It would soon be the winter, and the temperature would attempt to hinder those moments.{w} That was why he did as much as he could to enjoy the scenery he'd been granted, hoping the girl at his side was doing the same.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Eventually, the silence was their cue to leave. Their gazes met again, confirming that it was time. They stood up from the bench and realized that they were much colder than they'd thought.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They were about to stretch their limbs when an overwhelming light took over their sight. They lost control of their bodies and felt as if they were about to faint.{w} When they next opened their eyes, they were unable to recognize their surroundings.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They were together, and they started to throw out questions to each other. Despite what they had experienced, they felt well physically.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The room where they found themselves had a haunting feeling to it; it was dark but spacious. Neither of them knew where they were, and they quickly saw that there wasn't a door in any of the walls.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Their experience had felt so surreal that just by seeing that the other was still there, their hearts refrained from building up terror and panic. Trying to stay calm, they looked around the room to find any clue as to their whereabouts.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Very soon, the girl spotted a few words on the floor. When the boy read them, they could only share stares to see how the other had interpreted them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Both of you will spend one hundred years in this space. Once you exceed that time, you'll be brought back to your lives, but only one of you will keep your memories of your stay here."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They kept reading those ridiculous words, left in pink on the floor. Despite how nonsensical they sounded, they didn't question them. The room had two beds, no bathroom, and no kitchen. Not the conditions any human could live in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Close to the letters, they found another strange sentence. It said: "Once a day, you can ask for an object to materialize, and the previous one will disappear. This is only as entertainment—so that your minds don't break."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Instead of laughing at it, the boy tried it out. The way he attempted it was by thinking about the object he wanted to create.{w} Instantly, in midair, a red ball appeared. After gravity made it bounce on the floor a few times, he was left speechless by the result of his thought.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When he explained what had happened to the girl, they understood their fate would play out as predicted. They had to spend a hundred years in a bizarre world where their thoughts could materialize items but they themselves were restricted by the four walls of the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, the first thing they did was speak to each other. In their immediate future, it looked like a nightmare might've awaited them. Being trapped in a single room where they couldn't die sounded terrifying, but since they were together, they attempted to reassure each other by starting a pointless conversation about what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When they realized it was working, the conversation stopped being forced. Neither of them looked particularly afraid, let alone terrified. They kept talking like they would every day after school, knowing what their future potentially held in store.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The dreamlike setting they had been forced into didn't seem like much of a dream to them. Why had they been trapped? How were they going to survive for a hundred years? Why could their thoughts materialize objects? They knew all those questions were valid, but they simply accepted things for what they were.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the floor was the red ball, which had been the boy's first thought in response to the words he'd read. They weren't going to start playing with it, but something new every day sounded like a curious proposition that could keep them sane in the far future.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They soon understood that there was no way to measure the time, so they'd have to count the days themselves, using the daily objects. It had been late in the day in their old world, and their physical tiredness had carried over. At one point, they decided to lie on the beds and quickly fell asleep.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before doing so, the boy thought about what had happened. He was surprised not to feel many negative emotions nor the desire to go back to the real world. He couldn't call it being carefree, but he woke up well-rested nonetheless.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The ball was still on the floor, and they could only create a new object when it disappeared. Soon, when the girl woke up, they exchanged sleepy looks they'd rarely ever seen on each other before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was still the first day, but they already felt comfortable. Accepting that nothing had been a dream, they started to talk and began a long bed-to-bed conversation.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even when it ended, they didn't feel alone. That prevented them from seeing their future as grim.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Three days later, nothing had changed. They were perhaps as far from home as any person could be, but they still found themselves able to produce any topic and talk naturally, appreciating that they had each other more than ever.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They'd agreed they would trade off on deciding an object per day, but they quickly found that they didn't have many good ideas. The girl had always wanted a spinning egg chair, so she thought of one big enough to put her whole body in.{w} It turned out to be exactly as she'd wanted it, so she spent the full 24 hours inside with a joyful expression.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The next day, the boy couldn't think of anything. He thought of trying to spawn food, curious to see what would happen, but after running down some failed ideas, he decided to call for the same chair.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It would soon be the girl's turn again. She was looking up at the red top of her chair while the boy stared at the room's ceiling in the same way. Suddenly, words vibrated through the air.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "I love you."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The girl peeked out from the chair in disbelief at what she'd heard. She saw the boy who had been her closest friend for so many years nonchalantly lying on his back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But that was far from how he felt inside. He couldn't believe he'd said it. Just after those three days, her overwhelming presence had prevented him from holding back what he'd been wanting to say for years.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He'd always wanted to tell her how much he enjoyed being with her and how thankful he was for it, but he never knew how to truly express his affection... That was why he'd grown sad, knowing that their relationship had been built with only implied trust and fondness.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: For that reason, the first time he let his emotions burst out, they had automatically taken the form of those simple words. While he'd been wanting to say them for a long time, he wasn't scared the reception might've been negative. He'd simply never been able to bring himself to do it, justifying it as being disconnected.{w} As soon as their new reality had been presented to them, he'd understood that he couldn't spend all that time suppressing his honest and natural feelings.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And after saying it, his heart was pounding, like it was trying to break out of his body. He'd imagined the situation and many different outcomes, so he continued to look at the ceiling, awaiting whichever one would actually happen. He kept his mind as serene as possible in the eternity between confession and response—he was prevented from leaving the room even if he wanted to.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "...Really? I definitely didn't think so. That's surprising."{w} She had a smile on her face and looked genuinely happy. Looking down and seeing it, the boy sighed in relief, knowing that no matter what would happen, he wouldn't regret having said it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But as it turned out, that wasn't the end of it.{w} "I've liked you for a long time too. I was pretty scared to say it."{w} Keeping the same smile, she let him know his feelings were shared.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The boy wasn't sure how to feel or respond. He wasn't good with his own emotions, but if he'd looked at their situation from the outside, he would've thought that both of them liked each other. Despite that, he had never truly believed it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They managed to start up a conversation so that the mood didn't fade. There were many things they wanted to say and many questions to ask.{w} Since when, how much...? The girl knew her chair would soon disappear, so she left it for her bed, where they kept talking until they fell asleep.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was the beginning of the time they spent together. They had so many moments to reminisce about, and many things they wanted to do. The days began to pass, and the same uplifting atmosphere stayed with them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once he'd made the necessary step, the boy started to open his heart, no longer restricting himself. Elated to see it, the girl responded the same way, strengthening the unbreakable bond they'd built over the years.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: One day, they kissed. It brought them peace in the already peaceful room, and it reminded them of the park they were so far from.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The chair kept getting brought back every so often. One day, the boy tried it and understood why the girl liked it so much.{w} Glad to see his liking of it, she joined him inside. They hadn't ever felt as close as that, but the relaxing sensation let them spend an entire silent day together, content to be living in the moment.{w} At one point, the girl got confused, thinking the 24 hours must've passed, but she realized that the boy had already silently prolonged the duration, so she continued resting her face next to his.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Similar days continued until they had spent months together. Despite that, no second had felt stagnant. They continued to enjoy their stay, seeing in each other the same friend they'd always gone to school with.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Their relationship had surely surpassed the norm. They only truly had each other, but that had always been the case. Even after being secluded in that strange room for all that time, they could still talk casually about things in the normal world, making each other laugh and showing interest in what the other had to say.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Since he'd broken out of his old mold, the boy had grown used to only voicing his true thoughts, like he'd always wanted to do.{w} Some days, they would try to materialize new objects. When it was his turn, he created a huge trampoline. He'd always found them fun, and he'd thought of generating one for a while. They let themselves loose and used it for hours, as if their bodies couldn't wear out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At one point, they stopped creating new objects, knowing they could just be in the egg chair.{w} They were happy to live like that, but they knew there was a detail they'd barely talked about.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Permanently marked on the floor, next to where they were resting, were always the same words. "Both of you will spend one hundred years in this space. Once you exceed that time, you'll be brought back to your lives, but only one of you will keep your memories of your stay here."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They'd long since stopped keeping track of the days, aware that the final one would eventually come. They felt their sense of time had been altered since near the start, so they couldn't be sure they hadn't already spent years in that room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Aren't you scared to lose your memories when we come back?"
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The girl responded quickly.{w} "...Yes, but it'll be okay. We know how long we've liked each other for in the real world, so whoever remembers will just tell the other about it. There are so many things I want to do with you once we're back. Since one of us will remember, we can do all of them and more."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "All right. Whoever keeps these memories will confess to the other as soon as we come back."{w} Then, they would live the life they'd been talking about for so long.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was their promise. They had grown to love that room and the relationship they'd forged thanks to it. It was just a prologue for the inevitable return, but both of them saw it as much more than that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And, once again, time went on.{w} They didn't get tired of talking, of thinking, of caressing, and of living. They spent every second as if no time was passing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But, eventually, almost one hundred years had. They hadn't aged, and their physical condition hadn't deteriorated. Like they'd already done numerous times, they'd decided to bring a pool filled with water to the room, knowing how refreshing it was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Underwater, the round interior of the pool was the last thing they saw in that isolated reality. They had agreed never to say goodbye, and they couldn't have even if they wanted to. In the blink of an eye, the room didn't exist.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to a bench, a boy and a girl looked at each other. One was staring into the other's eyes, whereas the other had simply returned the gesture.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Hm? What's up?"
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The boy froze. Was it really over? Did the girl in front of him really not remember anything of what they'd experienced together?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "...Is anything wrong?"
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He had no idea what to say, but his own words echoed in his mind: "All right. Whoever keeps these memories will confess to the other as soon as we come back."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Hey...? Did something happen?"
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "N-Nothing, don't worry."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With a slight frown, the girl shrugged and picked up her purse. "We should go, then."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He couldn't bring himself to say anything and simply stood still, petrified. He'd feared many times that he'd be the one to keep his memories, but the girl's words had kept giving him peace, letting him believe that it'd turn out fine either way.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Are you coming?"
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Still trying to find a place to fix his gaze on, the boy began to step forward. Something was preventing him from looking at her face.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Whoever keeps these memories will confess to the other as soon as we come back."{w} What? No... he couldn't do that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He had spent one hundred years loving someone, but that wasn't the girl in front of him. He had come back—and the girl he'd loved had died. She only remained in his memories.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He had spent one hundred years finally letting himself be who he was, without judgment, without even thinking about it. However, in an instant, that had been reversed. He had never opened himself emotionally; to the eyes of the girl in front of him, he was the same reserved person he'd always been.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She approached him with a worried face. "Are you okay?"{w} He wasn't confused about what had happened. He understood it perfectly well, and the only thing he felt was emptiness. After nodding, he continued walking.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He hadn't seen those streets for so long, but he still remembered every detail about them. They began to walk through the quietness of the night, hearing their footsteps on the asphalt.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to the boy was his first friend, who he'd loved more than he'd ever thought he could. He knew his feelings were mutual, but how did that help? He'd always imagined that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The inevitable sadness started to build up within him. He remembered how much of himself the girl had grown to know during those years, all the conversations they'd had, and every time they'd materialized something. He'd been told that their time together would end since the first day, but he couldn't believe all of that had simply happened and been lost.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And there was nothing he could do. He couldn't confess his love again, and for the first time, he doubted it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The two same barriers had come back: himself, and uncertainty. Not a second of those hundred years had mattered.{w} No, of course that was wrong. He'd have to cherish and remember the times they'd spent in that intimate room... because, in the real world, they would never happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The turn where they always saw each other off came.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Are you sure you're okay?"
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Don't worry, I am."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Looking a little sad, the girl smiled and waved.{w} Then, as they always did, both of them took different paths. ...And yet again, only one of them found it significant.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was a story I'd once written.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd always been prone to letting my imagination run wild, and sometimes I'd make up full little stories.{w} Unable to sleep one night, I'd thought of that one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was a very shallow story, but that night, I'd felt the need to write it down, which I never tended to do. Of course, I'd never shown it to anyone, but every time I thought of it, a strong and bittersweet emotion would fill my brain.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I opened the piece of paper and read the four thin lines on it, every word of that story came back to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Hello. I'm sorry that I have to write this."
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "I still can't believe what happened. I haven't been able to stop crying, but I've always tried to tell myself that these things just occur."
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "I know how selfish it is that I'm writing this, but I won't be able to live with myself if I don't."
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "I need to say it.{w} I've always wanted to, and I can't believe I never will.{w} I love you."
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: My hand hadn't stopped trembling, and my heart began to catch up to it. What in the world was I reading?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd jumped back to the story I'd written a couple of years prior for a very simple reason.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The handwriting on the note was my own.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it couldn't be. I'd never written that, and I never would. However, I knew very well the single thing that could've ever made that note a reality.{w} A voice played in my mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Shiroya's fate is death."{w=2.8}{nw}
entries.speaker: saicenter

entries.text: Those had been Sai's words, but they couldn't be true. I'd feared before that the day would come where I could no longer tell her how glad and thankful I was to have her, but there was no way I'd let it happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No—it wouldn't happen. That note had my handwriting, but it didn't mean anything. I would never write it. Even if the worst happened at a later point, I wouldn't.{w} But... it existed. I had it in my hands.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where had it even come from!? I hadn't seen it on the floor, so had it been in my pocket and fallen while I'd been sitting? Or had someone left it there, knowing I'd come back?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My heart rate alerted me of how anxious I was. My existence felt insignificant, but I still told myself I wouldn't let that reality happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I burst through the door and was greeted once again by the desolate hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been tightly gripping the note, the thing I despised, with my right hand. I detested it and wanted to distance myself from it as much as I could, so I left it between the handrail and the wall to avoid touching it for even another second.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya! Hey! Where are you!?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I needed to see her and know that my fears wouldn't turn out true. We'd just lost Miiya, but I knew that I wouldn't ever be myself again if something happened to Shiroya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya! Can you hear me!?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I opened the room in front of me and left it as soon as I saw it was empty. I kept crying out, impulsively exhausting myself as much as I could.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're okay, right!? If you can hear me, please come out! Say something!
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Soon, my voice started to crack as I realized how close I was to the reality in which my oldest friend had died. Sai had spoken it like it was an absolute, and I'd found a note I wished I'd never read.{w} I kept telling myself that there had to be another meaning, but my shouts devolved into hopeless crying until I fell to my knees in the middle of the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was so lost that I didn't consider the importance of the sound I'd heard. Footsteps... I suddenly processed it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Abruptly, I raised my head and turned to face the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Lap Crossing

There, I saw a slender figure looking at me.{w} It was Shiroya, her face near the breaking point. However, she wasn't the one I'd been thinking of. Her clothes were from the attic, and despite her expression, she felt wrong in a way I couldn't define.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It seemed like she could disappear at any moment. Without taking my eyes off her, I stood up. She hadn't moved since we'd seen each other, so I began to warily approach her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Are you actually Shiroya?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: When I'd been crying her name, I'd only been wanting to find her to be able to hug her tightly. After she'd suddenly appeared like that, though, I couldn't bring myself to go forth, unaware of whether I'd stopped myself or her overwhelming look had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As if she hadn't heard me, she continued to stare at my chest with a melancholic look.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-Where were you? What's with those clothes?{w} Are you the same person who disappeared with Sai?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: After some seconds, she finally answered.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I-I'm sorry... I'm very confused too. ...I-I guess so, though.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You guess so?{w} What do you mean? You remember everything, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Right now...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She stopped.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She looked lost and glanced over my shoulder. When I realized she hadn't paused voluntarily, I turned around, thinking she might've seen something.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had failed to recognize the sound I'd been constantly anticipating. Footsteps were approaching.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, a person came with them. I could hardly believe my eyes until I understood that what I was seeing had already occurred before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm glad to see you two are safe. I was a bit worried...{w} Wh-What's with those clothes? You weren't wearing them earlier, were you...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I couldn't act shocked or even surprised. Erina, who had died, was behind us, quietly approaching. It looked like she'd come from hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who the hell are you? Or even you... How can you two exist!?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It was the same thing. The "body double" I'd gone on about earlier. Erina's had appeared, and next to me must've been Shiroya's.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where were you? How did you just appear out of nowhere!?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The confused expression she responded with was more than frustrating. I tried to focus on breathing to keep myself together. Just by looking at her, I'd noticed two glaring details.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She looked almost as if she was sedated and only partially conscious. Her voice and body movements gave off the same feeling, so it was clear that she wasn't in the best state, either physically or mentally.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But the major point was her clothes. Her chest was covered by the same bloodstain I'd seen before, and so were her legs and the upper part of her face. I spotted the same scratches that indicated a fight, meaning that her body was identical to the one I'd seen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What do you not understand? Did you just pop into existence at some point?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No... Why do you think that?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Have you looked at that room? Your body is there.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What...? That one? It... can't be.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: She staggered and took a while to complete her sentence. Trying to overcome whatever her condition was, she walked to it. The door was already partially open, so she just had to push it the rest of the way.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew you were lying. I-I can't be here, of course not...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I didn't have to move. Through the door, I could see that Erina's body had disappeared. Next to Naomi was Erina's curtain, but it had been left on the floor with no trace of the corpse I'd attempted to dignify.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Shiroya, what the hell is happening? Answer my other questions. How can you exist when it shouldn't be possible? Did the same thing happen to Erina?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: To Erina? She should be dead, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shiroya left my side to look through the door and saw that Naomi's corpse was the single remaining one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, the cross!
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: She was ahead of me, so I had the chance to look at the collar of her shirt, where I'd drawn a black cross.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's not there... I'm sure that's the spot where I marked it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: About Erina, I think what happened isn't what you think.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's probably right. I can't think of anything anymore.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Under those stained clothes, there's no wound, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Erina looked at her own chest and was taken aback by all the blood she saw on herself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There never was one. The body you think disappeared is her.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Do you mean that she never died?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She nodded.{w} If that was the case, it was painfully simple, and I'd failed to think about it because of all the overlapping thoughts I'd had on the matter. I'd been thinking about a replicated body who'd shared the stained blood but not any wound, while, sure enough, we'd never actually confirmed there'd been one.{w} And, of course, the blood. If it wasn't hers, there was another very clear candidate to consider.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A-Are you serious...?{w} Were you playing dead, then? Or just unconscious? It doesn't look like you feel very well.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm not sure... I remember I was drawn to this room, and then I think I blacked out.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Drawn? By a noise?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: N-No... Something stronger, but I'm not sure what, exactly. I don't know whose blood this is, but since I woke up, I've felt... groggy and numb.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I... see.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Would we have known she was alive if we'd felt her pulse, then? Her experience was enigmatic, but I understood that what had come afterward could've been a result of our mistaken assumption.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya, do you remember finding her body as well? And you realized what really happened? ...You still haven't explained what you're doing here. Are you the same Shiroya who disappeared from the event room with Sai?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...I wish I could explain everything to you, but I still don't really know what happened.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: But, yes. I'm really glad to see you again.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She smiled. It was her—the person I'd cried the name of. No matter how many questions surrounded her, she was okay...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What's with those clothes, then? Why is the cross not on them? Why did you ignore me when we saw each other in the event room and when I kept shouting your name?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Well, I—
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Hey... I'm still confused, but I have a question.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...Huh?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The Sekimeiya... does it really make you travel through time?{w} How does it work?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: If I understand it... touching it with your skin activates it, right? And you can go far into the past if it's out of the cabinet for a while.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: That's... what I've been working under, yes.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I looked at Shiroya in case she found something wrong with that, but she nodded, albeit uncertainly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was thinking. Why don't I just go back in time to save Isla?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...{w}Neither of us knew how to answer. We'd concluded the past couldn't be altered, so that shouldn't have been possible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the bedroom, despite managing to act semi-composed, Erina had always looked sorrowful as she tried to hope that her daughter had somehow survived. However, the woman in front of us was different.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know why I didn't think of it earlier. Someone killed her a few hours ago, so I just have to go to that time and prevent it.{w} But I couldn't find the Sekimeiya. I kept looking at Isla's face for a very long time, and she told me that she could be saved. Then, I saw a girl, and after that I heard you shouting.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...A girl? You saw Shiroya?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Um...{w} I guess it couldn't have been anyone else.{w} ...It must have been Shiroya.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I also saw what happened to Katei... It looked horrible. Did someone do that?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...It couldn't have been an accident.{w} But anyway, the Sekimeiya's not in the event room.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you sure...?{w} Do you know where it could be? I really need to find it.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No. I suspect Sai or Akaro must've taken it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I hated it, but I couldn't tell her where I'd hidden it. She couldn't accomplish anything by going to the past; she would just have to experience Isla's death a second time. However, we'd never seen that Erina in the past, so I could know for certain that she wouldn't travel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Are you lying?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What? No, I'm not.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She's been alive all this time. Could she have seen me bringing the Sekimeiya to the staff room...?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The way you two reacted. You don't want me to save Isla, do you?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: That's not it at all... Remember that Sai and Akaro took the cabinet key. They probably have the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shiroya was backing me up. I didn't know why something about her still felt off, but I was starting to accept that it was actually her. We'd just have to clear things up to understand exactly what had happened, but she remembered disappearing with Sai. That meant she already knew I'd taken the Sekimeiya myself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But Erina didn't give in. It was clear that she didn't trust us after all, despite what we'd talked about in the attic. She went to the event room, so we quietly walked behind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I-I knew it! You were lying...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You didn't want me to look at the cabinet!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Behind the curtain was the glass, and behind that, the Sekimeiya I'd just left in a locker rested on top of the cushion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya looked at me, confused. My words had led her to think that the cabinet would be empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's... teleporting.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I'm sure it just teleported from the locker to the cabinet.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And of course, this is no coincidental place. It must've returned to its "starting point", or something similar; a place where it's cold.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Erina opened the glass and rolled the Sekimeiya into her purse, avoiding direct contact with it. Then, she immediately let the curtain fall again to make it clear that she wouldn't put it back in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was a long silence until the hallway A door opened. Wondering what else could happen, we turned to face it and saw someone stepping into the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Uh...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I wanted to yell at him as soon as I saw his face, but I was too fed up to do so. I looked around me and laughed internally, having gone so quickly from thinking that I was alone to sharing a room with three people. Received with silence, Sai approached the cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's up?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What the fuck are you even doing here? Did you succeed with that plan of yours?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, not quite, unfortunately. I thought Erina was dead. What's she doing with the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You thought that too? No. I'm going to go to the past to save Isla.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Huh. I doubt that. The past can't be changed.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's nonsense! I'm going to the past, so I'll prevent Isla from dying. You've used the Sekimeiya before, right? How long do I need to wait to go enough hours back?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Um... It should be about fifteen minutes, but I still find it unlikely you'll change anything.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai... where the fuck did you go? Were you in the attic?{w} Do you know where Shiroya went? I saw her disappear with you.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Isn't she next to you? What's with those clothes, anyway? Aren't they from there?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...They are.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I see, they're definitely an improvement for you.{w} And just ignore me, Atsuki. I was busy sorting something out.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Ever since Sai had entered, Shiroya hadn't taken her eyes off him. Immediately after that last sentence, her lips curled up into a smile for a second, and her eyebrows raised.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: More moments of silence followed. Erina still showed no signs of reconsideration, and we couldn't forcefully take the Sekimeiya from her.{w} Sai had nonchalantly said that fifteen minutes would be enough to go many hours back when I'd just traveled approximately twenty minutes after storing that amount of time. I looked at Erina's purse, where the Sekimeiya was getting hotter and hotter.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait... that's...!
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Oh, right, I'd forgotten about this too.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Still sounding groggy, she traced my gaze up to her purse and took out a small piece of paper.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I found this just now. I tried to read it, but my head hurt a lot. Do you know what it is?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: She handed it to me, and I snatched it away, gripping it tightly. My hands started trembling as soon as I glanced at the words again and saw those familiar letters.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd left it behind without thinking about it, but I couldn't let Shiroya read it. Despite how suspicious it looked, I immediately stored it in my pocket.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: H-Hey... What was that?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Shiroya and Erina both found it strange, but I couldn't let them read the note under any circumstances. Shiroya would easily recognize my handwriting, so I'd run away if necessary.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't mind me, like you said.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You look pretty nervous. I saw something written there.{w} You were pretty in control of things when you pulled off that trick with the key earlier, so why is this getting you all worked up? Do you wanna hide it that badly?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}It's just a personal paper. It has nothing to do with you or the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Very intriguing, then.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He didn't push it further, but at my side, I saw a mix of confusion and sadness emanating from Shiroya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was understandable. I still didn't know what she'd gone through, but before entering the tower, we'd spent many days mourning our loss, our shared company being a silent healer. By saying it was a personal matter, I'd outright said I only wanted to hide it from her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd never made it apparent I could've been hiding anything, no matter how small. I still had many more questions to ask her, but what would my response be if she ever inquired about it...?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When she saw that I had nothing else to say, she smiled bitterly and looked down at her feet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, did any of you see Miiya...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Wh...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Who?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You don't know her, right? I... I knew I wasn't going insane.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: H-How do you know that name?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She's the person I was with earlier, before I saw you two... It just came back to me. I don't know where she went, though.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What...{w} the fuck is going on?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: What's with that reaction? Don't you see she's just delirious?{w} She didn't die, but I have a pretty good idea of what happened to her. Say, did you hallucinate someone?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's not it. That's not just some name she made up.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Do you know this person, then?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...We do, but Erina couldn't have seen her. She couldn't be here.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Are you sure? She could've entered through the storeroom. She could've even traveled from the future since the Sekimeiya's bound to be exposed to the outside world.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's not what she means... She's not anywhere right now.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh? Is she dead?{w} ...Wait, Miiya, you said...?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...No. She's with us. She has red hair, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Miiya's hair... was red.{w} I recalled Akaro's voice from the time he'd lost some of his memories. What he'd said almost implied that he knew what happened to Miiya and what we'd gone through.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did you actually see her? What did she say?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She told me her name, but she didn't look lost or anything. She knew me, too...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: She just suddenly ran away, and I haven't seen her again. I definitely thought I hadn't seen her before, but I honestly wasn't sure.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Is Miiya... here?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Is she alive? Are we going to succeed and save her somehow?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: As soon as I felt hope building up, I tried to contain it. That didn't make sense. Why would she have been in the tower? Why would she not have shown herself? There was no way Miiya was nearby, or anywhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know how to interpret this. Did you all agree to make up this story for when I appeared?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Shut up.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, I'm trying to figure things out myself and I thought I was close to understanding quite a bit, but now there's a bunch of shit I don't get, and it doesn't feel great.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I didn't ask, but it sounded like he wasn't only talking about the sudden appearance of an unknown person.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You did mean she died, right? Is saving her with the Sekimeiya not an option?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai, shut the fuck up. If it was, I promise you that we would've done it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Once again, there was silence. Shiroya looked pensive, but I had no clue what was going on inside her head. I basically understood nothing about her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't assume that Erina had just hallucinated because she knew Miiya's name and appearance, but I also couldn't accept that she was inside the tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did Erina just lie...?{w} How would she know about her? And why would she do that?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It's probably been close to fifteen minutes already, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I'd say so.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai looked at his watch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes, it's been almost fifteen minutes since I arrived.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you sure I'll go far enough back?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: She died at around {time=14}, right? It should be enough, yes.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I understood the lies, but not the heartless way in which he was deceiving a mother into thinking she was close to saving her daughter. Regardless, it had probably been fifteen minutes already, so Erina would travel to the past if we didn't stop her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's strange. Once again, if she's about to travel to the past, how come her past self hasn't already appeared?{w} Of course, seeing her future self should be an impossibility, but why would she have decided not to show herself?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...Okay. I'm going, then. Are all of you coming with me?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Don't worry, we're far enough from you.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai stepped back a bit anyway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I understand. Well... goodbye for now.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Earlier, Sai had traveled after storing energy for fifteen minutes—the same amount.{w} At that time, I hadn't traveled despite being next to Shiroya, so I knew how big the range would be. I stepped back too to be sure I wasn't included and wouldn't travel away from Shiroya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In a solemn manner and keeping her eyes on us, Erina reached for the Sekimeiya with her left hand.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When she touched it, there was a change.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Trampoline
...Huh?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Wait... what?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: None of us could understand what had occurred.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina didn't travel... Sai did.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why didn't it work!? Did Sai disappear?{w} Was everything that he said a lie...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I couldn't fathom it. What had happened defied everything we'd learned.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya and I had been pretty close to Erina, but going off Sai's previous travel, the range shouldn't have been large enough to pick us up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'd been farther back than Sai, but why had he been the only one to travel? And what I'd thought earlier still applied: where had his past self been all that time?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Admit it... Did you ever want me to save Isla? Were you... Were you involved in the first place!?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: You're wrong. We don't know how the Sekimeiya works, but this shouldn't have happened...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I don't get it! Is it all nonsense? Can we not figure out how it works because it just does whatever it wants?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It's been pretty consistent up until now, so what's this shit...? Why did Erina not travel but Sai did when he was out of the range?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There's even another instance... The first time I traveled, I went twenty minutes back, meaning that the Sekimeiya had to have been storing energy for fifteen minutes. At the time, Sai was the closest person to me, and he was pretty much at the same distance he was from Erina just now, but he didn't travel then!
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: No... I'm misinterpreting it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That has to be it... I assumed I knew what the range was since the conditions were identical to Sai's last travel.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I didn't travel that time, but Shiroya did, even though she was next to me. That led me to think I was just barely out of range and that only she was included.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But that wasn't the case. I was also in range, and I didn't travel for another reason, just like how Erina didn't just now. It's what I thought: something prevented me from traveling, and it just happened again.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Just earlier, I told Sai that I saw Shiroya disappear with him. He must've realized that I hadn't traveled, so he set up the same conditions for Erina's travel and felt safe at a slightly farther distance than I was from him before. However, he just fell victim to my own misinterpretation. The previous time, the range was actually big enough to encompass me, but I didn't go anywhere...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And in the latest travel, the four of us might've been included while only Sai disappeared. What was the reason...? It couldn't be that only two people could travel anymore. Was there anything that would make sense?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Wait! Where did it go!?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I quickly looked up and saw Erina's desperate eyes. She was staring at her purse.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's not here!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I was wrong. Sai wasn't the only thing to disappear—the Sekimeiya also had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It... teleported.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'd experienced it for the first time. The infamous teleportation we'd constantly thought about had revealed itself to us. Erina's travel activated it, taking Sai away in the process.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I remembered what had happened just minutes prior, so I took a few steps forward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I was in front of the cabinet, I crouched and grabbed the bottom of the curtain. I raised it violently and kept it from falling again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Behind the glass was the Sekimeiya. It had traveled from Erina's purse to its initial cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki, tell me... What do I need to do to travel through time?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Exactly what Sai and I told you. I don't know why it didn't work just now.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And since this confirms that it can actually teleport, there's no way I still have the Sekimeiya in the locker.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: In fact, the teleportation probably caused the illusion from the start... The "other" Sekimeiya.{w} I'm not sure how it happened, but I bet it was the same one every time.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Why is Sai not here already? ...Did he think of using the time he gained to do something?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: He had likely gone about twenty minutes into the past, so he had time to think of a better course of action than rushing in as soon as possible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Realizing our confusion was sincere, Erina's face went pale, and she would've fallen backward if not for the wall behind her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Three towering questions just presented themselves to us, challenging everything up until this point.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: One: was the range really the same as the last time the Sekimeiya stored time for fifteen minutes?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Two: why was Sai the only one to travel?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Three: why did the Sekimeiya instantly teleport away?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Regarding the range, we can't know how it actually functions. I've assumed it only starts to expand when time begins to be stored, but what if that's not the case? Could it also increase while the Sekimeiya's in the cabinet? Or what if the range from previous travels persists, for example?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The second is the most confusing one. Erina, Shiroya, and I haven't traveled. There's no way we weren't included in the range, is there? At least not Erina, who touched the Sekimeiya...{w} But it only worked for Sai... There has to be a reason why we were excluded, but is it reasonable to think I can figure it out?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: What does this do to the concept of range? Now how can we be sure that it exists? Perhaps there's no range at all, and something else entirely determines who's included in the travel.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And, finally, why did the Sekimeiya disappear from Erina's purse?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It's impossible that happens every time it's activated: it didn't disappear when Sai and Shiroya traveled.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Without a doubt, this is the strangest travel so far. Those three questions might all be connected to one single misconception.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: What are we supposed to do...? How am I supposed to understand this thing if it keeps breaking its own rules? How can I ever even hope to use it for anything?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Can I... not save Isla? Why did it not work...?{w} Oh, of course.{w} What was I even thinking? Traveling to the past isn't possible.{w} You lied about it since the beginning, right? That's why it didn't work: it can't happen. I actually fell for it.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I was too lost to answer. Something had happened to Erina—that was for sure. She'd just witnessed Sai's disappearance but was accusing us of lying. It seemed that trying to explain ourselves wouldn't be much help.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Just wait here. I'll be back in a second.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Before she could react, I moved to hallway B. I needed to check the staff room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The locker where I'd hidden the Sekimeiya was directly to my right. I unlocked it with the key and opened the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya wasn't there. Only the pants and the coat remained inside.{w} I closed the door and locked it again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see... Shiroya was right, then. The other time, it did teleport away from Naomi's locker.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: In hallway B, I saw Shiroya waiting for me next to the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did it disappear?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What else could've happened? I couldn't rule out another person having the key, but while I had room to construct a theory that didn't involve self-teleportation, it seemed pointless to do so.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Had someone put another Sekimeiya in the cabinet after entering from hallway A and taken mine out of the staff room while we were in the event room? There was no way. Nobody else had been involved.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What did you want to do?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Oh, I'm just wondering about Sai's whereabouts because an extra version of him has existed somewhere in the past.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Did we never see him in so many hours?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: "So many hours". Right, she thinks Sai went back to before Isla died. In reality, he went back about twenty minutes, if that's consistent.{w} ...Although she just went from saying time travel isn't possible to thinking it is again. She's more unstable than I thought.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...I'm not sure, but he has to be somewhere.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I was a little frustrated by Shiroya's continued silence. She was definitely thinking about what had happened, but she might've had information I wasn't aware of, and nothing she had revealed yet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The three of us were going over our thoughts when, suddenly, the door to the lobby opened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There you are. What were you doing?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Something was strange, and it immediately became apparent. Sai had shown up from the lobby, so I was relieved to know that he wouldn't be unaccounted for. He, on the other hand, looked completely different.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh...? What the fuck?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'd never seen him so confused. He'd tried to have the upper hand in every situation, but his face told the truth: he couldn't comprehend what he was seeing. From his point of view, something was very wrong.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Huh?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...!{w} Wh-Who the fuck are you? How are you here?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: From the event room, a door opened. After everything that had just happened, when I saw who came out, I barely reacted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Whoa! What's this girl doing here!?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Those were the first words I'd heard from Akaro in hours. Recognizing the person who shared his bewilderment, he stood next to Sai while the three of us looked at each other in case someone understood what was occurring.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki! Now you have to answer! Who is she?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Are you actually acting as if you don't recognize me?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Of course we don't!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well... No.{w} Of course we do.{w} Aren't you... dead?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Again...!
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "Shiroya's fate is death."
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "I need to say it. I've always wanted to, and I can't believe I never will. I love you."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nightmarish memories split my brain in half. It seemed like the world was abandoning all sense, warping into something completely repulsive.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: M-Me...? Why would I be dead?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: And you too, Erina! I thought you'd died!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wh...? Isn't that what you said earlier?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Earlier? What the hell are you talking about?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Before the conversation could escalate further, I had to ask a very important question which had been repeating throughout our imprisonment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai, what time is it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Uh...{w} it's {time=18:43.}
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: {time=18:43.}..{w} That was about twenty minutes behind the real time I estimated. That meant Sai's replicated location after traveling had been twenty minutes prior, and his watch hadn't stopped working.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why? Did you time travel?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: N-No. I didn't.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: He's right, though. Are you a future version of Erina or something?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Well, you're not dead after all, but we felt your pulse... In any case, I figured you would've come from the future. What even happened to you?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Um... I can't remember much. I think someone hit my head, and I fell unconscious. I don't know what happened before that.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yeah, that's about what we knew too. Sorry that we can't be of more use.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I was losing it. I was about to explode. What the fuck was happening? Was it all a joke, deliberately constructed to destroy me?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't get it either, but I'm glad you're safe. This means you're not guaranteed to end up dead, but you... What even is your name? How did you get here?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I've been here since the start.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's not true.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It was the same thing. In the attic, an Akaro who claimed to only possess partial memories of events had appeared. Was Sai a victim of that as well?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hold on, though... Your name... I think I might actually remember that.{w} Shi... roya, was it? My memories are a little foggy.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: She nodded, speechless.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I thought so. Like I said... I thought you'd died.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: As you can see, I'm alive.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Do you have a twin, by any chance?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What? No.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: But, then... It doesn't make any sense. I'm still really confused...
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What the fuck do you mean you're "confused"!? She just showed up like that! Did you enter through the storeroom?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I've been with you since {time=9}, Sai.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's a load of crap. Regardless, you'll definitely die. I'm sorry to tell you like that, but you're not making it easy for us. Atsuki, I know you know her.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}I do, and she's telling the truth.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you just fucking with me? What's the point of lying so blatantly?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He's... He's telling the truth. Shiroya's been with us the entire time.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The entire time? Not even you have been here since {time=9}!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: E-Excuse me?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Well, you get what I mean. You don't remember when you got attacked or where you came from very well, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Of course, Erina and Isla have been here the whole time, {tip=clash}but not you{/tip}.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It was settled. They had either gone completely insane or their plan was to make us go insane. After being told once again that Shiroya's fate was sealed, I continued to search for a method to refute it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I turned to look at her, but I couldn't make heads or tails of her expression. Her eyes fixed on a point in the distance, and that was all I knew. It had become a challenge just to know what anyone trapped in the tower was thinking.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did you notice something?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}I... need to go somewhere.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Wh-What...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm sorry, I need to go to the attic.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She ran toward hallway C. There I stood, petrified, until she turned around to say one last thing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Please, don't follow me.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I could only stare at her eyes, in search of any compassion. Why was she being so cryptic?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With an apologetic look, she spun and sprinted off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Please, don't follow me." Why...? Why did she want to go alone...?{w} I was sure I looked devastated, but I was only trying to decipher the sudden change of behavior my oldest friend had undergone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wow. Are we going to just let her go? Didn't you see how suspicious that was?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well, that's fine. She's just gonna get herself killed somehow. It's already unavoidable.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why!? Why is she gonna die!?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Did you hit your head and lose your memories? We know it will happen.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: How!? You seem pretty certain, so prove it!
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You know we can't anymore.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What the fuck does that mean!?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Akaro looked at me as if he was witnessing a man who'd gone mad.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's with that look!? Where did you even go!? You just appeared again, out of nowhere!
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh...? It's you who appeared again.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I hit the wall, furious. Their responses were making my blood boil, like they were sneering at me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You too, Sai! Did your memories also happen to get fucked? You traveled from the event room. Remember that?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...From the event room? No, I don't.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Have you two just lost it completely? Or this is a side effect of the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You can stop trying already. Since you sided with that girl, you made it clear you'll only spit out bullshit. I don't know what you're trying to pull, but you look pathetic.{w} She'll come back whenever she feels like, if she doesn't die in the process. Meanwhile, let's keep waiting for the shutter to open. I'd appreciate it if you told the truth, though. How did she get in?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: She was with us from the beginning...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That's false. Since she seems to be with you, I really doubt you were stupid enough to make her enter through the storeroom. That's what's strange, but perhaps you did.{w} Let me see.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Indifferent to my confusion and rage, Sai walked to hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What are you doing!?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Instead of answering, he entered the storeroom.{w} Seconds later, he returned.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I just wanted to verify that she hasn't entered through the storeroom yet.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Have you thought of a plan to keep the Sekimeiya for yourself? Then, once you succeed, you'll eventually make her go back in time to appear inside the tower and take care of whatever your plan requires.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What are you even talking about...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Maybe two of you weren't enough, I don't know. Although if that's what you did, you had to know you were sending her to die, even if she was already supposed to be dead. I don't get exactly what your idea is or how this all came to happen. It's a damn mess.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Again, what the fuck are you talking about? What does "maybe two of you weren't enough" even mean?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Of course, I'm assuming Miiya's in on it as well.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I gave up. I approached the nearest wall and kneeled next to it, only capable of breathing. It was incomprehensible. Nonsense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Not gonna keep trying to clear your name? I suppose it'd be futile with how obvious it is that this is your doing.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Okay, I'll ask. How do you know about Miiya?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What? She's been here—
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's it, ignore him from now on. He can't get out of the corner he's backed himself into.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I covered my eyes with my arm, applying as much pressure against my face as I could. Who had decided to make me go through hell, and why had Shiroya left me behind!?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Letting out a casual laugh, Sai sat next to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Aren't you going to follow her? It seemed really obvious that you gave her some kind of cue to leave, you know?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: She just got this blank look and suddenly had to go... Was that all you could come up with? I gave you a little bit of credit earlier, but honestly, what happened to Erina could definitely have been all you.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I pushed Sai aside with as much force as I could gather. If my mind had already broken, he was doing all he could to scatter all the pieces around.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's harsh. I suppose that's the only way you can defend yourself. We'll see what your plan amounts to soon.{w} Maybe not, actually. Maybe we'll just never see that girl again. At least not alive, of course.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai, I swear if you open your mouth again, I'm going to fucking break it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I get it, I get it. Let's wait as much as you want.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: My vision was dark, partly covered by my arm. Standing up were Akaro and Erina, whose expressions I couldn't see.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Beyond the meaning behind Sai's words and Akaro's appearance, I couldn't get my thoughts off Shiroya. Why had she left like that?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She hadn't even promised me she'd return. I tried not to let Sai's voice loop in my head, but there was no stopping it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was she going to die...? Would I write that note? ...No. Neither of those would happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She wouldn't just leave like that if she thought there was a chance she would die. There had to be a good reason behind her actions.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Don't kill me, but hasn't it been a long time since she left? What do you think she's doing?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Be quiet.
entries.speaker: a
