entries.text: What happened then?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't remember. All I know is that I didn't find anyone, and I rested in this room.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: And you're all right now? You're standing up just fine.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I just felt dizzy. I'm better now.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I looked over her body, and a subtle discomfort wormed its way into me. Perhaps I was making it up, but her face looked almost... worn out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, I guess this means you accomplished whatever you wanted to do, right? I'm very happy to hear it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The three of us stepped into hallway A. When Erina saw Shiroya, she approached us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya... I'm glad you're all right. What happened to you?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: She chose the "oh I'm so disoriented I can barely remember anything" excuse, just like you did earlier. Don't even bother.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: H-Huh...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Do you only not remember what happened after you touched the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I think so... Before that, we were waiting in the lobby, until I had to go to the bathroom.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I see. Do you not know where the dizziness came from?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}I don't know...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I had no clue what to think. She looked sad; that was all I could perceive. Maybe she'd been attacked or had an accident. ...Perhaps it was an effect of the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, the sadness faded away, and in its place came a gentle smile.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't worry, I'm okay. There's not a lot of time left, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It's {time=20:37.}
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: See... It's almost time.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Can you come here for a second?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Y-Yes.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What, going to go rub your hands together now that your plan has succeeded?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What plan, Sai? Do you think we did this to find the Sekimeiya you didn't want us to find?{w} You understand that doesn't make any sense, right? She found it in the bathroom. What's the point of forcing a search to find it if she already identified where it was?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}Why is she faking, then?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not. My head really doesn't feel good.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Right.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I was ecstatic that we'd be able to stop dealing with Sai relatively soon. I sighed and walked back, bringing Shiroya to hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you remember what we talked about before waiting in the lobby?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Uh...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I said the past could be changed, remember?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: O-Oh, yes. But we didn't find the Sekimeiya in that locker, where it should've been.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah.{w} You traveled through time. Do you think you might've changed anything?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I really don't think so.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Well, right now, the Sekimeiya's in the cabinet, but I didn't lock it. There's only about thirty minutes left, but we can still use it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We might be able to change the past. If we travel together, we'll keep our memories of this reality. I'm not sure how it works yet, but I thought of something.{w} Sai's definitely suspicious of us, so I doubt he'll let us just waltz on in and take the Sekimeiya. Obviously, given the time left, it's very unlikely we'll go back far enough even if the Sekimeiya stores energy the whole time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It could be a start, though. We'd go decently far into the past. Fifteen minutes sent me twenty minutes back, so every minute stored adds more than a minute.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: By which I mean, we could go more than thirty minutes into the past and change it in a way so that we can begin storing time at the point we arrive. If we repeat this, we'll go even farther, and we'll be able to store a lot more time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm not sure it'd work, but even though we can currently only store thirty minutes, we can keep doing this to maybe keep going back more and more.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: How do we store thirty minutes without Sai noticing? I feel like this is feasible.{w} Remember how the cabinet works? We could unplug the cord, which would stop the temperature regulation.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Then, even though it'd look normal, it'd actually be storing power. We can hide it in plain sight like that and activate it at the last second...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...N-No, let's not.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...{w}You don't want to try it...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't. Everything is fine as it is right now.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: But...{w} we'll regret it. If we don't even try it, the time will come when we'll hate not having tried it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No... That won't happen.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Why? That's not how you reacted the first time I proposed changing the past.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I know... I just thought about it more.{w} Let's wait until the time is up. We can end everything now.{w} We've been here for too long... I just want to get out.{w} Believe me, there's no need to do anything else.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I really didn't get it. I couldn't blame her for saying that, but every word felt distant.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...We just have to accept that Miiya died. Let's do what we said and try to be strong despite it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I know that Miiya died, but we can prevent it...!
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: No. Let's stop, please...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Tell me, at least. Why did you change your mind?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}To tell you the truth, I'm not even sure I'd want to do it even if we could.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What does that mean...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Most importantly, I just want to leave this place. We have to keep going with what we've got, and I'm sure it'll be fine.{w} This isn't a world where Miiya survives, so let's keep living the best we can.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What the hell was up with that change of philosophy? I was too lost to know if I agreed at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, I knew one thing. I also wanted to get out, and Shiroya was safe. ...Saving Miiya had been something of a dream rather than an actual goal. The main thing, the definitely achievable thing, was leaving with Shiroya, and it finally seemed within reach.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you sure? I know it sounds like a stretch, but I still think my idea is worth considering.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...I am, yes.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: What about the Sekimeiya? Do you not want to try using it again?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I definitely don't. I have no idea what will happen with it, but let's forget it exists if we can.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Okay.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That was the end, then. I tried to think of something else to say to her, but I found nothing. If that was the life she wanted to keep living, opposing it would have been a breach of our friendship.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What confused me was her change of heart. She'd been wanting to use the Sekimeiya to save Miiya up until it had actually become remotely possible...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What reason could there have been to not want to attempt it? Was she not fond of the idea of changing the cards we'd been dealt?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It had been a focus of my thoughts the entire day. Was I really going to give up so easily?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I glanced at Shiroya's expression, which told me how serious she was. I could only be saddened and maybe a little disappointed, but logically speaking, I hadn't lost anything. Miiya was already dead before we went to the tower, and the reason we'd entered was to begin moving past it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Let's go back to the lobby.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: The large room was empty. Shiroya walked up to the spot where we'd been sitting and returned to her previous position. I sat at her side, recalling the events we'd gone through. All my own recent experiences felt surreal, but I knew they had truly happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wonder where Erina and Sai went...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Even if they're up to something, we just have to wait here.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Right...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: However, Erina soon arrived from hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Here you are. I lost track of Sai at some point. Have you seen him?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't know where he is, then...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I saw her staring at the mechanical room. When I did, I also felt like something about it had changed. It hadn't been fully closed before, had it?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She looked away and came to sit by our side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's not much time left, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Less than half an hour.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Those twelve hours had felt so much longer. It was hard to believe they were coming to an end and that we could resume our normal lives after everything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was nothing more to be said—not from someone as tired as me. I tried not to think about Sai and focused instead on keeping my mind blank.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...We won't actually get out, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: We'll stay here for more than a month, won't we?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: There's no way. The exit will definitely open soon.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: How can that be, though? In a month, Isla will be alive here, and I haven't saved her yet. If the shutter opens, that'll become impossible.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...Every time similar things came out of her mouth, I went quiet. How was I supposed to answer that? I still didn't know what had happened to Erina, but her personality had noticeably shifted at one point. She hadn't yet recovered from her sedated appearance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I know it might sound shallow, but it'll be fine.{w} If Isla is fated to be alive in the future, she will be no matter what you do. You'll see her again, right? That's what the recording predicted. Now, you just have to wait until that happens.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Do I have to wait a month to see her, then?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...{w}I don't know.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I couldn't get a read on Shiroya. Was she just trying to be optimistic to calm her down...?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Or was she actually considering that what we'd heard in the recording would occur in the future? I didn't think that was it—she also seemed to believe we were just about to leave the tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina tried to accept what she'd heard, but after a couple minutes, it became clear that she couldn't be content with that alone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I'll go find Sai. I don't like thinking about what he might be doing.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: At this point, why aren't we doing more than doubting him? There's been a culprit among us the whole time. Now, only four of us are left, and we didn't find Akaro. It can only be him, right?{w} Of us, he's the only one missing. I think he disappeared on purpose. I need to find him.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: She walked back to hallway B without giving us time to answer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya and I looked at each other, hesitant to react. We'd agreed to wait until {time=21:05}, so Erina's abrupt departure wasn't enough to disrupt that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't like the thought of letting her and Sai both run free, but I let it go.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were alone, and time kept passing. Three or four minutes later, Shiroya spoke.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}How much time is left? Less than twenty minutes, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Sorry, it's all fine. Ignore me.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...{w}Wh-What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm not going to ignore you. What is it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I was just a bit confused. It's nothing important.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I was almost speechless. I didn't like agreeing with Sai, but I had to. Something about Shiroya wasn't right.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The convenient loss of memory, the sudden appearance in that room... She'd also changed completely when I'd mentioned using the Sekimeiya again and contradicted her own past self.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh... You're still here?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yeah. Did you find Sai?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: N-No.{w} Sorry to ask like this, but what time is it?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...{w}I'm sorry?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It should be {time=20:50} soon.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...{w}R-Really...? Okay.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: This is starting to get ridiculous. What is up with you two?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I don't understand... Maybe you were right, Shiroya. We'll wait...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Erina made her way to where she'd been sitting, but there was only so much I could ignore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell did you just do? "What time is it"? You might as well have said "I just used the Sekimeiya, how far back did I go?" right to my face.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She'd come from hallway B, so that was where I went. Shiroya and Erina followed me without saying anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...And the Sekimeiya's not here. You didn't even put it back?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're wrong... I didn't do this.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Why did you ask for the time, then?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: To know how much time was left.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Of course.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm telling the truth. I went to search for Sai, but I couldn't find him. I only meant to ask how much time I'd been gone.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I closed the glass.{w} Erina had been gone for about five minutes. If she had actually traveled, a version of her that was still to touch the Sekimeiya existed somewhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Was everyone just a liar? She could've traveled, but Sai could've also easily hidden it himself. I hadn't locked the cabinet, so I didn't know what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I felt disconcerted, frustrated, and even wary of Shiroya, who might've been hiding something from me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I noticed the brief instant in which Erina's expression showed surprise. She was still in hallway B, staring at her left.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you see something?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I walked up to her, but I found nothing that stood out in the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't see anything.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I was getting mad. I wanted to get out with Shiroya more than anything, so what was with her continued silence?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do we just ignore this, then? Do we think the police can understand even a shred of what happened here?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Or do we use these last minutes to find Sai and the Sekimeiya? If he took it, he must have something in mind, and as much as I want to get out, I'm not fond of letting him do as he pleases.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Y-Yes... Maybe we should search for him.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Search complete. You all did an amazing job this time.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Ah!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Sai's face peeked in from hallway B, the lobby side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did I hear that the Sekimeiya's gone? We should've counted every time it happened since the start. What's this, the twelfth?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And none of them were your doing, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Not a single one. Of course, none of you did it this time either, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: This sneaky Sekimeiya must keep teleporting away, making us doubt each other when, in reality, none of us would do something so dishonest as lying or taking it ourselves.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And you never chased us with a knife, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Did that happen? It's {time=20:51.} Let's go to the lobby.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm being serious. You did try to kill me, and I still don't even know why.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Atsuki, are you stupid? How would I get a knife? There's no place to hide one, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That Sai was not the same one I'd punched. I clenched my fist, ready to do it for the first time again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you sure you didn't imagine it? I'm not stupid enough to kill someone, and there's no knife I could've used.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I glanced at Shiroya's purse and gestured at her to open it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She unzipped it and showed me its contents.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Where is it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...I don't know.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: The knife wasn't there. She had traveled again, which might have gotten rid of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm sure the police will do a great job at figuring out what happened. Now, let's wait in the lobby.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I went to hallway A. Someone had hidden the Sekimeiya one last time, right before the exit would open. I had no idea what purpose that served, but there had to be one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked up to the storeroom. Every time the Sekimeiya was hidden, we were able to find it. The last few minutes we had were enough to do it one more time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You want to spend the remaining time doing this shit again? Go ahead.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I would. Once I felt the storeroom was empty, I moved on to the crystal room A5.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd hoped I wouldn't have to see Isla's face again, but there was no helping it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kept going from room to room, meeting Sai's sneer in between. Behind him were Shiroya and Erina, completely neutral and unhelpful.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I got to the security room and was assaulted by the stench of death again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The computer screens were suspended, so I pressed a key to light them up, trying not to step on all the blood. The time displayed was {time=20:55}, which matched Sai's.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Most of the drawers were filled with papers I'd never bothered to read. Something that caught my attention was that one was full of batteries, but they were too packed for the Sekimeiya to be in any of them. I looked inside the suitcase, but it was still empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, before I left, I kneeled beside Katei's body. Under the desk was the computer tower. To look behind it, I held my breath and crawled up to it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There it was. The Sekimeiya glowed white, contrasting the obscured space between the desk and the wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Making sure not to touch it with my skin, I dragged it out. It was scorching, so I had to hold it with the bottom of my shirt to leave the room with it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}You did it. Happy now?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I made my way past the three and put it in the cabinet. Without a second thought, I locked it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Given how hot it had been, Erina had some credibility. If she had just traveled from the future, the Sekimeiya shouldn't have been that hot, and she could no longer travel after our current point—the Sekimeiya would stay locked away until the police came. Knowing her actions could've altered reality, though, it wasn't for certain.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know what you hoped to accomplish, but there you go. Now we can wait. Is that a problem for you?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Not at all. Why would it be?{w} Oh, you still think I hid the Sekimeiya myself. Now you can see you're wrong. Let's go to the lobby, as I've been saying.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}All right.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The four of us left the Sekimeiya behind and entered the lobby. In less than ten minutes, the metal shutter was supposed to open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We approached where we'd been sitting and reclaimed our places. Everything had been set up for our departure.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I glanced at the three people next to me. Sai looked indifferent, while Erina appeared serious. At my right, I began to think Shiroya was a little tense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Hm? ...Is anything wrong?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I don't know. Are you looking forward to leaving?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Yes, I can't wait.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Her melancholic tone took me aback, leaving me without a reply.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Three people had died, and Akaro had vanished. Was he somehow still in the tower? It seemed that only four of us were minutes away from feeling the cold air rolling off the mountains.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya and I first entered the lobby when the night sky was above us, and in a few minutes, we would hopefully see it again. The countdown was leading toward the result of a battle only a few of us were aware of—what we'd been told about the alarm versus the recording we'd heard.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In just a few minutes, one would win. It would not take much time for us to become aware of our fate.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai was the only remaining person who hadn't heard the recording and fittingly looked the most carefree. Perhaps he'd soon understand that his future was much more grim than expected.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina had lost her daughter and a fair chunk of her sanity. Understanding her thoughts had, at one point, become an impossible task, and I wasn't sure what she was hoping would happen next.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: One thing was certain: during those twelve hours, we hadn't figured anything out. There were too many things left unexplained—things that had eluded me and would most likely continue to do so.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Miiya wouldn't come back to life despite the inexplicable mentions of her. People had died for incomprehensible reasons. We'd been granted access to a time travel device and gotten nothing out of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even just minutes previously, the Sekimeiya had been hidden, and I had no idea why. I could barely grasp most of the day's events and definitely couldn't understand some others at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The inevitable outcome was right around the corner. The Sekimeiya had been part of murder cases and the smoke attack. It would soon make its way into the world, potentially leading to drastic changes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why had an object capable of time travel been in Ashiya Tower?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Thinking about the time we'd stepped into the building... We'd done that looking to overcome loss. Maybe that part had gone well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before that day, Shiroya had barely spoken for a week. Next to me, not much of that taciturn person remained... but I felt I understood her less than before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the past, I had never questioned her. I'd thought we'd known each other perfectly. That very thought was what allowed me to trust her even then, despite the oddness that seemed to emanate from her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's the time?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{time=21:00.} Only these last five minutes are left.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No sound was coming through the shutter, but many people were surely on the other side of it. Police, Ashiya, and even townspeople. As soon as they saw Erina's bloody clothes, they would begin to understand what we had gone through.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'd probably be interrogated. We would become murder suspects, but we'd also see the streets of Yushibana again. After that, we'd be released, and Shiroya and I could go back home.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know what to expect in that regard. I'd never thought about it, but perhaps some people knew about the existence of the Sekimeiya, and once we showed our knowledge of it, we'd become a threat...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Or would the police not believe a word we said? It wasn't clear yet whether the cameras had been working. If someone's plan to steal the Sekimeiya was about to succeed, the outside world could end up never believing our story.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'd all been staring at the floor or our laps—a sign of our exhaustion and need to get out. I felt I heard a sound, so I abruptly looked up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was nothing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}What?{w} Where's Erina?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's a great question. Did she go somewhere?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The hallway doors were closed, and it seemed unlikely she could've left through one of them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, at our right was the mechanical room. She'd been the closest to it, and it was possible she'd silently made her way inside. I couldn't imagine why she would, and I glanced around the room to be sure she really wasn't with us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You two didn't hear anything, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...I didn't.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I looked into Shiroya's eyes, but she didn't do the same. Instead, she had the same nervous look from earlier.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, she stood up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Huh?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Don't forget what I said... I meant all of it.{w} Now stay here, and don't follow me.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Wh—
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Before I could finish, she took off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She ran to hallway B and disappeared through it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My heart jumped, but I couldn't move.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My suspicion had been confirmed in the easiest way. That wasn't the Shiroya I knew.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A flash came to me. Just earlier, I had looked at her purse.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The knife wasn't there...{w} That's fine. That doesn't mean anything.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But... what else should have been in her purse?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Her wallet, my keys, our identification, and the two tickets for today's event.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Right... I didn't realize it. At least two of those things were missing.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: My keys weren't there, and neither were our tickets... However, there were keys. Did I recognize them...?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I turned my head to face Sai. Like me, he looked dumbfounded and remained immobilized by Shiroya's words.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The lights suddenly went out. Sai's face disappeared from sight as everything became dark.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: S-Sai...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He was still there. We stood up, letting out heavy breaths.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck happened...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You're asking the wrong person.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}What time is it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: His watch gave off a faint blue light.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Only two minutes left...? Why did the lights go off?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Did you not notice that?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Notice what?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: A-Ah!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Erina's voice came from the right, sounding desperate and in pain.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey! What's going on? I-I think my finger is bleeding! Wh-Why are the lights off!?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Where were you!?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm serious! Did you not see a flashing light?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes! I saw it too. For an instant, I saw a flashing light! I don't know what it was!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Me too... After that, the lights went off.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What the fuck are you two talking about? I didn't see that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: A-And then my finger started hurting! It's seriously bleeding! What h-happened!?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No idea... but before the lights went off, Shiroya suddenly ran to hallway B.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Huh? Then... did she do this!?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: How would she!? And why the hell did you just leave!?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: My eyes had begun to adapt to the darkness, and thanks to a faint light coming from the reception desk, I could see the closest wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait... Atsuki.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Why's the shutter still there, then?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It could be about to open. We don't know exactly the time the alarm went off. Maybe it was at {time=9:06.}
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We stared at it. It could open at any second.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Lost in the darkness, we stood, hoping our rescue was seconds away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could very faintly see the metal surface of the shutter. It was still there, looking like the same imposing blockade it always had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No way...
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I'm pretty sure it should've opened already. It's been more than twelve hours.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I-I knew it.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What did you know?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Answer me!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Erina kept silent, but we could hear her breathing.{w} Letting our hearts hammer our chests, we kept facing the sealed entrance, our promised freedom slipping away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {time=21:08.} What the fuck? Why is it still closed!?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: There it was. We had a winner.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was the recording's prediction. The tower wasn't going to open then, and it wouldn't for a very long time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How could it have happened? Why would the outside abandon us?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is Shiroya's fault! She knew something would happen!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I found the open door to hallway B and went through it. It was completely dark, but a breeze lured me to the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The room was cold. Had Shiroya run to get the Sekimeiya? I carefully walked to the cabinet, moved aside the curtain, and tried to open the glass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It should've been locked, but it wasn't. The glass was partially open, and I could put my hand inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I felt the Sekimeiya's surface and confirmed it was still there. However, something had definitely been done to the cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki! Are you here? Why is it so cold?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I am! Shiroya! Where did you go!?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: There are no light switches anywhere, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Is it a power outage...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It couldn't be. The temperature function of the cabinet was still working.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The security room... The doors hadn't opened, but other functions might have come back, such as the internet connection.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I dashed to the hallway and slammed my body into the door of the security room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What...!?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I continued trying to push it open, but it wouldn't budge.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't tell me... Is the security room locked?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I-It is.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Can't we unlock it?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Katei had the key, but his body is inside.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It's {time=21:10}! There's no way the time is wrong...! Why is this still going?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai, who'd been ignorant of the recording since the start, hadn't foreseen such an outcome. I used the last amount of strength I had to pathetically walk back to the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The metal shutter was still there, proving something other than time would be needed to get rid of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My body crumpled down; I couldn't keep going.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A month? What kind of joke was that? I couldn't bear one more second.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya's words played back in my head. "Don't forget what I said... I meant all of it."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I laughed, alone. I didn't know where I was, what anything had become... none of it. Nothing we'd done had any meaning. We'd made it to the end of that impossibly long day for nothing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The words Shiroya had abandoned me with... Were they supposed to be reassuring?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to continue yelling her name, but my voice broke. She'd known what would happen and hadn't warned us. She'd kept waiting at our side, bolstering our hope, until she'd run away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why...!? She would never have done that... I couldn't let a single day change my view of her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I couldn't help but despair. I wanted to leave. I wanted to be hit by the icy air and feel released. I wanted to talk to more people, even if they were the police.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And it wouldn't happen. Could we survive an entire month? Of course not...! Shiroya hadn't been mentioned in the recording, so would I not see her for weeks?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Would the nightmare persist in the Sekimeiya's domain? It was too horrible of a thought to bear. People had died, and I still didn't know who, how, why...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The lights had gone out, so I followed their example. I closed my eyes, intensifying the darkness, before I felt once again how insignificant I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Chapter 1 Credits
As they feared, their time in Ashiya Tower wouldn't end yet.
The warning they'd received hadn't been enough to prepare them.
And their uncertain future threatened to be cruel.
Since the mysteries had begun to stack up, they knew they couldn't withstand them.
Many details that sheltered the truth had been left ungrasped.
And they were ignorant to one important fact...
Their lives had just been saved.
Nobody could imagine why the Sekimeiya had been exposed to them.
Nobody could imagine the beautiful labyrinth they were creating.
A transparent labyrinth that engulfed its own creators.
A labyrinth that didn't hide truth anywhere.
And whose walls could be broken.
Every riddle, no matter how small, was accompanied by an answer.
However, some of those answers weren't held by anyone.
Not by anyone inside the tower, that is.
...What about you?
Inevitably, every riddle will be unfolded.
Every detail will strengthen.
And meaning will arise.
When the time comes, I wish you will be prepared.
The peak was within reach, but it felt unattainable.
Was the reason the path taken?
To climb to the top, others were essential.
Only then will the puzzle be laid out and every spot contain its proper piece.
Inside the dark tower, there was only one thing that could be taken for granted...
The path to comprehension extended far past the one to freedom.
Lone Thread
Amidst the vast internet was a specific forum thread.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The date showed it had been written in the afternoon of November 24th, 2011. It contained two paragraphs.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I swear this is all the truth, I'm not messing around. I'm a bit scared, though, and I'm not sure what to do.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: I think I just woke up from a really strange dream. It felt hyperrealistic, and I'm still shaking...
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: I don't know if it means anything. Maybe it was a premonition, I'm not sure. However, I'd be careful on the 15th of next month.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: If I don't say this anonymously, I'll be laughed at, or even fired... On the 15th, Ashiya will hold a big event in the tower, and there'll be a terrorist attack.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: It will be called... the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: Soon, maybe they will announce it. I don't think I'm a prophet or anything, but I'm still trying to calm down. This time, it felt too real to let it pass.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: That's what I dreamed. It's so bizarre I still think it might've really happened. That's why I feel the need to post it, in case it actually means something.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: Do not go to that event if it happens. Some people even got trapped inside, but I don't know what happened to them.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: I think something might be wrong with me... I don't know why, but I'm not home. I can hardly believe it's still the 24th, and I don't know what I'm doing at my parents' house.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: Sorry to rant about this, but I need to let it out somewhere. I've been suffering from a few mental issues, but nothing has been as bad as this. I've been living alone for two years while my condition has gotten worse and worse. I feel I can't continue on my own, and letting people around me know it might be a horrible idea.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: Anyway, maybe some of you will have some advice. I know posting here isn't the most effective thing, but it's very hard for me to talk about this out loud. Thank you for reading.
entries.speaker: c4

entries.text: The thread gathered very few views and only a handful of replies. It had been posted on a nearly desolate subcategory dedicated to Yushibana events.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Two days later came the last reply before the thread was locked. The foolish warning wasn't enough to prevent the incident, foreseen three weeks prior.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When November came to an end, the thread had gathered 33 views. However, just one month later, it had grown to the thousands.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The identity behind the poster was never released, but some figured it out.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And the account wasn't used again, leaving many people wondering by themselves what had happened during the days leading to the 15th and on the fated, final one.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Crystallized
Maxi was startled as Atsuki and Shiroya looked at each other. The sound they'd just heard brought with it a semblance of normalcy that they'd craved.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Standing up from the sofa, Atsuki walked up to the front door of his house and did what he'd been waiting for all day.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Upon turning the handle and opening the door, he saw a figure he'd not seen in a long time. The same person he'd always known—he'd almost expected her to be uncomfortable or look out of sorts. Instead, he realized that he was the one who appeared that way.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Hey."{w=0.5} After a long few seconds, Miiya put on a smile and made her way in.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There, she saw Shiroya walking toward the door, nearly in disbelief at seeing her after so long.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Miiya...! I'm glad to see you. It's been a while.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Me too.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: She glanced at her surroundings, remembering the many times she'd been there in the past. On the floor, after recognizing Miiya, Maxi looked happy to see her too.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It really has been a while since we got together like this, yeah.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: ...Yeah.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: ...It feels like it's been way longer. It's so strange to see other people here.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Miiya bent down and scratched behind Maxi's ear, an action she'd picked up from Atsuki. Both he and Shiroya watched her wordlessly, unsure what they could say.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Well, what have you two been up to?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Um... Not much, honestly. I haven't really talked to anyone from school in a while.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: It's the same for me. No one's been around.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Miiya could easily recognize that they were both acting awkwardly, and the last thing she wanted after reaching out to Atsuki was for him to distance himself again.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shame there aren't any good movies to go see. We could catch up that way.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Ah, well, it's not like the theater here's that great anyway. I regret going every time.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Planning on moving to the big city so you can go to fancy theaters? I bet you want central heating too.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: ...I don't know. I'd rather not think about that, you know? It's not like living here is all bad or anything, but sometimes you just want... more.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Oh, us bumpkins aren't good enough? I see how it is. I feel you, though. The last time I watched a movie there was almost a year ago, and it was horrible. A better catalog would be great.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Wait, is that the one you recommended to us? The one you said not to look up or read the premise of? We never ended up going, but I still had it on my mind.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Oh, did I? Very possible. It was one of a kind. I wouldn't even mind watching it again with you two, but I'll be shocked if it hasn't been discontinued.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Hey, isn't it pretty cold in here? I'm pretty used to it outside, but I can never relax indoors if the temperature isn't just right.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Yeah, sorry. I've gotten into the habit of turning the heat on and then back off once it gets warm again.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Maybe we can win the lottery and spring for a house with a sauna. If more than one of us enters, it's a sure thing.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: I wish.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Oh, you do? I didn't figure you were the polygamous type.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: What!?
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: She didn't mean it like that.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Lighten up! Both of you are so stiff.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: S-Sorry. It's just been a while. I'm not used to being around people.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: I actually passed by the lottery office just now and thought about giving it a shot, but I didn't want to be late. I was also really eager to see Maxi and Umi, you know? I've been thinking of getting a few cats, and I see that Umi's been eyeing me from under that couch, so maybe she wants to come with me. God, she's so cute.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: I don't think so.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: I figured I'd just have to bribe my parents, but they've been more stubborn than usual. Apparently, both of them are a bit allergic, but they won't even let me just have them in my room. I've been trying to get a job, but I haven't had much luck yet.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Where have you been looking anyway?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Well...
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: They had many things to talk about, and Miiya's willingness to break the ice was much appreciated. Atsuki and Shiroya both viewed her as the missing link in their lives that had finally been restored.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hours went by thanks to all the things they wanted to let out. Their future decisions, what their past months had been like, and many more thoughts they'd been keeping to themselves.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: For Atsuki, talking about it was hard. He wanted to ignore some problems for a while instead of acknowledging them; deep down, however, he knew he couldn't do that forever. Miiya had given him an excuse to approach it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But as time went on, they realized they'd soon not have much to talk about or do together, and the mood began to sour. They weren't at school anymore, so talking about what their days had been like wasn't the same.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Oh, I found this on the way here.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Atsuki and Shiroya lifted their heads. Miiya was holding a gray flyer with wet stains from where the snow had fallen on it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It says November 29th, so it was put up today. I found it on a streetlight close to here and thought it sounded interesting.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Isn't that the Ashiya logo?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Oh, yeah. I know you two don't like them very much, but read what it says.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Intrigued, Shiroya took the paper from her and read it out loud.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The Sekimeiya? ...On the third Thursday of next month, we will hold the largest event we have ever had the pleasure to put together in Ashiya Tower.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Make sure not to miss it, as we will show the rarest gemstone to have been found in recent years. Like every Thursday, the special visit will start at {time=9.}
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: I thought that we could go before your birthdays.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: When they looked at each other, Atsuki and Shiroya knew they couldn't refuse. They'd never entered Ashiya Tower, and their families usually would've prevented them, but neither of them were personally against going once while their parents were overseas. Both of them also agreed that what they'd read sounded intriguing.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Look, it says that if we want to attend, we should hurry up and buy the tickets from this website.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Knowing what their answer would be, Miiya walked to the computer and input the URL. With Atsuki and Shiroya looking over her shoulders, the three pricey tickets were purchased.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was money neither Shiroya nor Atsuki had intended to spend, but to them, it was worthwhile. The thought of going somewhere together even made them smile.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: They bought the tickets using Atsuki's payment details, but they all paid for their own. After that, they printed them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There we go. I'm hoping they're not exaggerating. It said we'll go in groups of three, so we should be able to enter together.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Atsuki and Shiroya felt satisfied and appreciative of Miiya. She folded the papers and put them in a purse she'd long ago left in Atsuki's house, which brought back memories of all the times she'd worn it with them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki's heater, once turned on, was comfortable, so they spent the entire time in his house until it felt appropriate to leave.{w} Miiya's parents informed her they'd made dinner for her, and Shiroya took it as her cue as well. After saying their goodbyes, Atsuki saw both girls leaving on different paths.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It hadn't been the most fun day they could recall, but at least Atsuki felt at peace, as it had been exactly what he'd needed after spending many months by himself.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He went to sleep looking forward to the next day, when they'd agreed to meet again.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was the afternoon, and it had just started snowing. Phone in hand, Atsuki waited at the spot they'd settled on, close to the school they'd recently graduated from. He saw a flyer stuck on the bus stop, titled "The Sekimeiya", identical to the one Miiya had shown him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He saw Miiya approaching, and she sped up upon seeing him as well. Minutes later, Shiroya came from the same direction, and the three found themselves at a bus stop with a plastic roof, not having decided where to go next.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Unfazed by the snow, they walked toward a stone path, reminiscent of the days when they'd left school together.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A few younger students could be seen in groups near benches, and some of their faces were recognizable. Like everyone else around them, they sat on one of the benches, their coats protecting them from the icy surface that remained after wiping off the snow.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I kind of missed this routine.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: It's definitely something you get used to. I can't believe years start going by so quickly.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: On the plus side, we don't have to deal with anything involving physics anymore. What a drag of a class.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Please don't remind me. I can't believe how many times Miss Mayuko pulled someone out into the hallway. Why be a teacher if you're going to act like that?
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Yeah. You'd think you couldn't get away with that in such a small town. All of the parents should have been up in arms about it.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Isn't that normal? I almost expect small towns like this to have murder cults all the adults initiate the kids into.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Well, not mine. Unless they're part of a foreign chapter and making arrangements right now.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Shiroya's parents and mine would definitely be in it together.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Actually, they haven't tried to get you to move again, have they?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Oh.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: It's not constant, but sometimes, yeah. I feel guilty, but... a big part of me wants to be here. I don't like that my mom is being so pushy about it. At least she gets the message if I ignore the call or just outright tell her no, but after a couple of weeks, she'll try again.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: My parents both keep doing the same thing. Is it too strained for you?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: It really is... My birthday's coming up, and she hasn't even mentioned it. I bet the only thing she's going to do for it is ask me to leave again. Like it's a gift for me.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Sorry. I shouldn't have brought it up.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: It's fine. I just wish she supported me living the way I want to, you know? It's not like I ever got bad grades or anything when we were in school. I proved I could take care of things.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: I'm not so sure. You remember, what was it, five years ago? You couldn't even look at a map and tell me where you were on it.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: That was different! It had never come up before. You can't hold that against me.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: And what about that time we had to catalog local animals? You didn't even know where to start looking.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Come on, Atsuki...
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: No, no, I want to hear this. Go on.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: We were supposed to build a list of animals that lived around here. It was one of those big, year-long projects... Actually, you were here for that, weren't you?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Yeah, but we didn't really know each other back then.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Well, Shiroya had no clue what to do. We went out to the edge of town and looked for, well, anything. It was still fall then, and we actually stumbled into a bunch of lizards.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Ooh, I bet she made her usual shocked face when she sees anything that moves.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Of course.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: God. You're not one to talk, Miiya.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: The best part was that she, uh... panicked a bit and stepped on one of their tails. It popped right off, and she screamed.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: I didn't know their tails came off and grew back! It had never come up before!
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: How can you not know that?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: I just didn't! You don't even see lizards once the cold hits.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: I honestly thought you saw a bear or something.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: No way. I'd have left you for dead.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Ice cold. Although black bears aren't that aggressive... usually.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Yeah, I'd have been totally fine, and you would've regretted your betrayal. You've told me way too many things that I could use against you.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Ooh, like what? You can tell me.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: A-Anyway, turned out that we completely misunderstood and tried to catch one too. Really, all we had to do was tell what kind of animal it was. Not the species, the, uh, genus.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Yeah. I felt like an idiot.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: So you didn't catch a bear? Shame.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: I've known Shiroya long enough that it wouldn't surprise me. She's good with animals, but she needs a bit of time to warm up to them. I'm sure a bear would grow a liking to her fast.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Hmm.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: You think so? I'd probably just play dead and hope to survive.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Well, you're always very sweet with Umi, and she seems to really like you. Honestly, I was a bit jealous of you in the past. If I didn't know better, I'd think you'd end up becoming a vet.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Me...? I doubt it, yeah. I stopped considering that when I was twelve.{w} That's so much school just to get your foot in the door. It's not like I want to end up being some boring office worker or something, but I want to have time for myself too...
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Could just find a nice rich guy and become a gold digger instead.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Heh. Yeah, I doubt that too.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: So do I. You should've seen her as a kid, Miiya. She didn't want anything to do with boys.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Except you?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Well... I didn't want anything to do with them either most of the time. For a while, both of us didn't have a great relationship with our classmates, so... we just kind of hung out with each other. I don't really know how it happened, but our parents definitely contributed to it too.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: All the girls had their cliques, that's how. It's insane how they get in a town like this. One person says something bad about you and it spreads fast, even if it's not true. Most of them ended up maturing, fortunately, but it was really bad at the start. Atsuki was never like that, though.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: Well, I'd be an asshole if I was. You're right, though, things got a lot better after middle school, probably because everyone's too busy with doing well to pick fights.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: I'm not so sure about that. Look at all the old farts here who go on and on about how terrible Ashiya is.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: As far as I'm concerned, both groups suck.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: How moderate of you. A man after my own heart.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: They kept talking like that for quite some time, whiling away the day in the way that made them most comfortable. Existing with each other was enough for them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Eventually, their coats were no longer able to protect them from the icy air. The short winter day came to an end as the sky began to darken.{w} Colliding with her own misty breath, Miiya stood up and asked whether they'd like to walk around to warm themselves up.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: From Seeuta D'ella Park, they would usually head home. Instead, they headed in the opposite direction, toward the more rustic part of Yushibana, which bordered the surrounding mountain range.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: They weren't unfamiliar with it, but it was rare they'd end up there. It barely had shops, and most buildings were residences. However, the narrow brick streets adorned by the dim snow made it particularly cozy, quiet footsteps the only audible sound.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya took out her phone and looked at the time: {time=20:27.} Aimlessly walking, they noticed the falling snow was getting lighter. People were entering their homes for the night, and some tire tracks had recently been carved into the snow.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What's that?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Miiya had been living in Yushibana for many years, but she was well aware that the other two knew the town much better. She pointed at a bright window next to an opaque door, the view of its interior covered by a curtain.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I believe it's a jewelry shop. Maybe the owner lives here since there's a second level.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: And it's still open?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Every lit window on the path had been high up, so that one stood out. In recent years, a few amateur jewelers had been appearing throughout Yushibana, selling the gemstones found in the nearby mountains.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Timidly, Shiroya approached the door and tried to open it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Oh!{w=0.4} Hello, it's not usual I get a late visit. Are you searching for anything in particular?
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: While the old man stepped out from behind the reception desk, Shiroya turned around to meet Atsuki's gaze. He simply shrugged.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Noticing Miiya's look of interest, the owner addressed her, slowly bringing her inside.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Anything that you see can be put on a necklace, earrings, or even a ring. Are you three looking to buy matching necklaces? Kids usually ask for that.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: N-Not really, no.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: The owner didn't give up, looking at Shiroya for her own answer. On both sides of his shirt was the logo of the shop: Musashi Gemstones.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The three of them stepped farther into the shop and heard the door closing behind them, preserving the warmth. They saw that only a few ceiling lights were on and spotted a heater on the opposite side of the room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was a modest shop with wooden shelves showcasing different kinds of colored stones, each with a price tag next to it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Even at my age, I regularly go to the two mountains behind us. I've found all that you see here, without exception.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: The shop was separated by the shelves, and the three found themselves under the obligation to look through them. It was evident that many of the pieces were of lesser quality than the others and were being showcased with hopes they'd eventually be sold.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Being the most interested, Miiya started going through them, knowing she had enough money to buy one if it grabbed her attention. She kept in mind the ones she liked while she continued stepping farther into the shop.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya had also seemed captivated by a couple of them, but Atsuki had quickly decided to wait near the entrance, doubting he'd have an interest in anything.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Don't you want to look at them? See here, I have put together a few wristbands of different colors, and I believe I still have one I'm sure would suit you very well.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: When Atsuki looked at the first shelf, he had a quick change of heart. He saw two similar triangular stones in a shining dark blue—his favorite color.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Do you like these? They're tanzanite, one of the most beautiful gems.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: Behind the shelf, Atsuki could hear the two girls who had come back to his life. He truly hoped things would stay as they were.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Can these be put in a pendant?" Atsuki spoke in a quiet voice, with the idea to secretly buy matching pendants for them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Of course! Come here.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: The owner took both gems and crouched behind the reception desk. In no time, he fitted the two of them into pendants.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The price was affordable, so Atsuki paid it without saying a word.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The two girls hadn't heard him; Shiroya had stopped in the middle of the shop and was staring at a specific display. After her was Miiya, who'd seen almost everything on offer. She was close to a wooden door, which she believed must've led to a higher level where the old man lived.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Miiya frowned. Upon entering, she'd barely noticed an odd smell which had become a little unpleasant. She couldn't help but feel as if she'd {tip=smell}smelled it before{/tip}, but she couldn't determine what it was.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: While the owner was putting both pendants in a bag, the door opened, making him quickly let go of them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hello. I'm sorry for coming earlier than arranged.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: No, don't worry! I'm happy to see you.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: Atsuki saw the owner morphing his face into a big smile. Through the door came a man wearing an expensive-looking coat that covered most of his face. The owner took him to the reception table, where they began to talk in quiet voices.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: From the side, Atsuki heard the man speaking briefly. After a nod, the owner walked toward the opposite side of the room and came back after a minute, bringing a heavy-looking, small box.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "I'm not done, give me a moment. Oh, and you're aware of what I discussed with Lei, right? The price will be double the usual." Those were the sole words Atsuki was able to make out, which made him think that something of high value was being traded. Then, the owner walked back toward the opposite side.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the meantime, the other man peeked inside the box and closed it again.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Slightly curious, Atsuki glanced at the owner, walking toward Miiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But in an instant, he couldn't spot him anymore, as a dense, dark smoke had invaded his field of vision.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Behind him, he heard the sound of a door closing. Before he could put two and two together, he collapsed, incapable of movement.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The entire narrow shop had been inundated by the sudden smoke. Out of the four people, none of them were able to resist falling unconscious during the brief instants where they could be alarmed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Kid! Can you hear me!?
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Atsuki began to recognize a few words, and his eyes shot open. When he saw that he was still in the shop, he remembered having passed out.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Battling a headache, he stood up and saw two unfamiliar men.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What the hell happened here...!? Are you okay?
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Atsuki didn't respond and instead peeked past one of the shelves.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There were both blood and pieces of skin scattered across the farther walls. When he took one step forward, he saw a huge hole in the floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Wh-Where are the two girls that were here?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Nobody replied. Not because they didn't want to answer, but because they didn't know. However, going off the blood, they felt they couldn't have responded regardless.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Behind the two men, Atsuki spotted the owner, looking down at his feet. There was a streak of blood running across his face.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hey! Answer me...!
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Th-There was an explosion a few minutes ago. That's all we know.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Atsuki rushed toward the hole and looked in it, but it was pitch-black. He couldn't see a thing.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He could hardly believe his eyes. Shiroya and Miiya had been in the impact zone. Realistically, it was impossible they were alive, but Atsuki found himself rejecting the thought, refusing the gore spread around the shop.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...We've called the police. They should be coming soon.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: What the hell is down here? How did the floor break like this?
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: I came in and didn't see anyone because there was some smoke in the air. I thought the lights were off, so I flipped that switch. I instead turned off the lights, so I turned them back on. ...I think it caused a dust explosion.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: If there was gas in the air, turning on the light might've triggered one. They're powerful enough to take down walls, or this floor...
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Atsuki denied what he was hearing as he kept staring at the blood surrounding the hole. The entire far side of the shop had basically disappeared. He stood, stunned, recalling the powered-off heater that had been in that corner despite the warmth.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Very soon, the police appeared, followed by an ambulance. Atsuki explained what had happened, shaking every word out.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He had to be brought to the hospital where his parents used to work in case he'd suffered any damage from either the smoke or the explosion.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hours later, after asking continuously, he was told that below the store was a drainage channel where they'd found an unconscious person. However, only traces had been found of the other girl.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The description confirmed to Atsuki that Shiroya was alive, and whose remnants those had been.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Unresponsive, Atsuki lay back, internally falling apart.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya was brought to the hospital. She was in a coma from having fallen so far down, but a nearby shelf had prevented the explosion from hitting her directly.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The next day, the police released the details of the events. An individual had released smoke that had put four people to sleep. A short time later, a gas explosion had occurred. It had happened due to the shop's heater being of an older design—one which lacked a failsafe. The heater had burned through all the oxygen immediately surrounding it, which had extinguished its flame but allowed it to continue releasing gas.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Given the size of the explosion, that must've happened before the smoke had been released. Then, as everyone had fallen unconscious, nobody had been able to recognize the artificial smell of the gas and ventilate the area, causing it to build up.{w} At {time=21}, when the lights had been turned on, the small spark had ignited that gas.{w} The two people farthest from the center of the blast hadn't been critically harmed, but they'd been sent to the hospital. One girl had entered a coma after falling through the broken floor and hitting her head, and the last girl, who'd been the closest to the heater, had died instantly.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The individual hadn't been caught, but their motive was unclear, as nothing had been stolen. Furthermore, it seemed the explosion itself had been an accident.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki had gone to visit Shiroya, whose parents hadn't shown up. Looking at her resting face, he was unbelievably relieved that nothing had happened to her, but he couldn't process the fact that he'd never see Miiya again. Every time he remembered how happy she'd looked to be back with them, Atsuki's heart seemed to shatter once more.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Days later, Shiroya woke up without having suffered any lasting mental damage, and the two of them were able to go live together, trying to support each other after what had happened.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The day before the 15th, the purse where Miiya had put the three tickets was still in view. They couldn't sleep and decided to walk to Ashiya Tower very early.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: They looked at the night sky, knowing Miiya wasn't under it anymore. However, as they turned their eyes back to each other, both of them wanted to believe that loss could be overcome. They were still alive.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After a long wait, they approached the tower and were able to find shelter in it until the event began, the warmth inside a small comfort.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Grounded Strobe

I'd never entered Ashiya Tower before, but after waiting inside for so long, I'd begun to feel familiar with those walls. More and more people had continued entering through the main door, lengthening the queue behind us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: *yawn*
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I glanced at my right and saw Atsuki's tired face. We'd been in silence for a long time, and I knew there wasn't much I could do to change that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How tired are you?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: A bit... I'll be fine, though.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Mingled with the tiredness was misery. Instead of looking back at me, he continued to stare at the rightmost column. Slightly frustrated, I awkwardly averted my eyes too.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd known him for a very long time, and he looked like a completely different person. It seemed the distance between us would keep extending despite the reason why we'd come to that building.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The premise had been to prevent what had happened from disrupting our relationship, but I felt that achieving that was far out of my reach. In addition, I'd had to constantly shape my attitude around it, which I hated.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew how bad of an idea showing my discontent would've been, so I kept it to myself and continued mirroring his face.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everyone who's waiting in line, please get your tickets out.
entries.speaker: q

entries.text: The receptionist, who'd been sharing in the quietness, stood up and walked toward us with a barcode scanner.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were at the front of the line, so I handed her our two tickets. She hovered the machine over both barcodes until it released a quiet beep for each one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There you go.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: She gave them back to me with a smile, and I put them in my purse.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Oh.{w} I'm glad to see you're back. I hope you enjoy the event.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Wh-What?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: For the first time since we'd entered, she glanced at Atsuki's face before saying that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What did she mean...? I've never been here.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I shrugged since she'd already moved on to the man at our side, but I imagined she'd probably confused him for someone else.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was still more than an hour left until {time=9}, when the front door would open. I'd stopped being curious about what we'd be shown as a result of the overbearing mixture of tiredness and coldness. I'd been paying attention to the brief conversations I could hear to stave off boredom, and they all kept detailing how strange the whole event was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Standing up for so long was building up pain on the lower side of my back, so I had to force the thought of enduring it for over another hour out of my mind. I stretched my limbs and torso, trying to resist the urge to lie on the floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya...?
entries.speaker: q

entries.text: I'd managed to leave my mind empty, but I abruptly turned around when I heard a quiet voice coming from my left. A man was crouching next to me, and when he stood up, I saw his older face underneath white hair.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is this yours? I think you dropped it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He showed me a ticket that must've fallen from my purse when I'd stretched my muscles. I nodded and put it back inside, all while unnerved by his stiff motions.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Thank you.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: After turning around, he spent a few seconds staying still until he walked toward the door on the left. He gripped the knob and opened it before slowly disappearing through it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We weren't supposed to enter yet, so given how nobody apprehended him, he had to be an employee. Atsuki's mood didn't seem to have improved at all, which only caused my own form of anxiety to emerge.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had no way to get rid of it, so all I did was stand up uncomfortably with no perception of what time it was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After a long, lonesome wait, I began to feel more confident and calm. My posture didn't change, but reminding myself that everything would get much better had borne fruits.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It must've already been {time=9}, because we were told we could advance through the left door if we weren't part of the event. Nobody did, though—everyone present was gathered behind us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sorry for the wait, everyone. We'll now begin the group entrances.
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: A blonde woman wearing a dark suit came out of our door. I recalled seeing her face in the lobby not much earlier.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My name is Naomi. I'll be chaperoning today's guided visit.
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: As you likely already know, groups of three will move forward in turns. Each visit is estimated to take approximately fifteen minutes.
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: Addressing the multitude all at once, she glossed over the procedure and prohibitions. Once she was done, she looked over her glasses.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you three the first group?
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: I wasn't sure Atsuki had paid attention to her discourse, and the man at our side was visibly out of it. I opened my mouth so that we wouldn't waste more time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, we've been here for a while.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Perfect. Please follow me to the event room to be the first to see the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: Quietly, she turned around and walked through the door. All the chatter had faded away, so the three of us walked behind her, the sound of our footsteps filling up the space.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the other side was a long hallway with ornate decorations. There were a few open doors in both walls and a handrail linking all of them together.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The woman stepped up to a door in the middle of the left wall and opened it for us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is where we hold many of our events. Make your way inside.
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: I crossed gazes with the strange man, whose look and behavior felt out of place. He entered first and stared at the red curtain that was undoubtedly covering the gemstone we'd all come to see.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Aside from the display case, the room was empty and only contained a security camera with a flickering green light.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: More people than I'd imagined were intrigued about the day's event. Personally, I was a little curious, so I'd proposed coming despite what had happened. Atsuki had immediately agreed to prove that he was strong enough to get through. Whether to me or himself, though, I didn't know.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He was the last to enter, and Naomi closed the door. Then, she asked for our introductions before starting to build up anticipation. According to her, we were sharing space with something of incredible value which had been found in the surrounding mountains.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Part of the experience is the touch, so I will open the glass and let you experience it yourselves. However, I must insist that you be gentle and keep your hands inside the cabinet at all times.
entries.speaker: sa
