entries.text: She took out a keyring from her pocket and isolated one of the smaller keys, which she inserted in a keyhole next to the curtain.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I have a question.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Hm? What is it?
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: You keep mentioning how valuable the Sekimeiya is, but is there proof of that? The way you're explaining it, you don't even say what kind of gem it is, only that it's "rare".
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: But the value could've been arbitrarily created by Ashiya, as it's not being officially recognized as anything more than an unusual discovery.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Well, I will let you decide that for yourself. As you said, it's not categorized because nobody was able to properly appraise it. That's all you need to be assured of its value.
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: I apologize for being skeptical, but you must be aware that Ashiya aren't exactly recognized for their fairness.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Do you have a reason to say that?
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: Yes, that everyone in the lobby sounded as skeptical as I am.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Maybe seeing it for yourself will convince you.
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: That's what I'm hoping.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Atsuki and I listened to the conversation until Naomi crouched to grab the bottom of the curtain. The real value of the Sekimeiya wasn't what had piqued my curiosity, as I thought its appearance was what caused all the excitement.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But Naomi's motion was cut off. Before she raised the curtain all the way up, my vision was obstructed by dense smoke that forced me to shut my eyes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Instantly, I recognized I was rapidly losing control of my body, and I fell to the floor. Nobody responded to my yell, and Atsuki's desperate gasp was all I heard before silence reigned supreme.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Immobile on the floor, reality distanced itself from me. It was all too familiar of an experience, but before I could think about that any longer, I blacked out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Hey!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Arcology
The world vibrated. I saw Atsuki's hair next to my eyes, and his arm shook me while his entire figure was covered by a dark substance. When he saw I'd awakened, he backed off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you feel okay?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Uh, y— *cough*{w} *cough* *cough*{w} Wh-What happened? We're still here?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Mixing a nod with a shrug, he glanced at the drastically changed scenery. The smoke had tainted everything it touched, including ourselves, and the room had become very dark.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hh—{w} ...What the fuck is this...?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: All I could do with my strength was look sideways, where I saw Akaro trying to sit up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where did N-Naomi go?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I don't know. She wasn't here when I woke up.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Looks like she left through that door.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Akaro managed to stand up and looked through it. Even though none of us had touched it, it was slightly open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The left hallway was very dark too, and I could see the smoke had blocked the ceiling lights from illuminating it. Strangely, it didn't seem like anyone else was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In addition, none of us had discerned the origin of the smoke. As my mind started to get clearer, I began to process what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you hear the alarm before we fell unconscious?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What alarm?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: My look told him I hadn't either. Apparently, shortly after I'd been knocked out, a wordless alarm had played.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was fairly obvious: there'd been a terrorist attack. Fortunately, Atsuki and I were safe, although all of us were clearly unsettled by the solitude.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We didn't know how long we'd been asleep or what had happened during that blank period of time. However, something stood out in the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The three of us were staring at it, and I began to feel able to stand up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did someone do this to steal the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Akaro shrugged, wondering the same thing. While Atsuki was still on the floor, I approached the curtain.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I resumed Naomi's action and raised the curtain all the way up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, never mind. It's still here.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: It is?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I turned around and nodded. Akaro approached me and saw with his own eyes the egg-shaped object contained within the glass, on top of a smooth cushion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is this really it? I figured they were making a big deal out of nothing, but it's even more underwhelming than I thought.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It's glowing a little. Maybe that's why?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: ...I wonder where Naomi is. This seems pretty fishy.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What do you mean...?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: That there's nobody here. I know this seems like an attack, but you know what I said regarding Ashiya's reputation, right?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I find it hard to believe they'd set up so much advertisement just for this thing. I'm sure they had something in mind to use this event for. Maybe this was it.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...I don't follow.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It happened right before we could see the Sekimeiya, and an employee left. Nobody entered yet, and we weren't moved. I have an idea of what's going on.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I'm sure they wanted to use this opportunity to pull out some countermeasure against Xyn, but I don't know what it really entailed. We probably got caught in the middle of it.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Akaro filled in Atsuki, who'd never heard of Xyn.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I still have trouble understanding what you're getting at.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What does this situation scream to you?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: "Failed robbery attempt", right?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: They might've purposely acted out a failed attack since they're desperate to publicly say they won once against Xyn. I'm immediately noticing a bunch of odd details that point to that.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Didn't you say they always attack during the night? Why would they do it during the day?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: If anything, that points further at Xyn not being behind it, and a false flag is the possibility next in line. Let's see how much time has passed and why nobody else is here. If I'm wrong, the police or Ashiya should know.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I helped Atsuki stay up, and we brushed the remnants of smoke off ourselves. Both of us were extremely tired. The sudden turn of events felt almost surreal, but he still looked distant, almost divorced from reality.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It took a few seconds for us to walk normally, but the left hallway was as we'd seen through the door—completely desolate.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We opened the opposite door and glanced at the right hallway, where we'd come from. It was in the same state as its parallel neighbor, indicating that whatever had happened was large-scale.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is that a person?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Y-You're right. Hey! What the hell happened...!?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: He sped up toward them, while I stopped.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you okay? I'm sorry I made you come here.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: No... Don't worry. None of this is your fault.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...It wasn't my fault, so I didn't push it. I sighed, a bit irritated, and passed it off as loosening myself up, like I'd been getting used to doing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to the lobby door, we introduced ourselves to Erina and Sai, as well as Katei—the person I'd exchanged words with before. Sai, Erina, and her daughter had been the group behind us and fell unconscious while waiting in the hallway. Katei told us he worked in the tower as a security manager and that he was trying to piece together what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Naomi was gone?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He looked down, worried.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been suspecting her, but I can't believe I was right.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We have to find her. I'm almost certain she was behind the attack.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What do you mean, "we have to find her"? How can you even be sure she's still here?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Through the poor illumination, I was able to see many expressions lowering at once.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei revealed the effects of the alarm Atsuki had heard. Although the trigger was unknown, it had sealed every method of escape for twelve hours.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Despite Akaro's insistence, Katei kept repeating that he wasn't allowed to reveal anything else, but he claimed he was unsure about other details.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't get what you're saying. The Sekimeiya wasn't stolen: it's still in that cabinet, so you can't just ignore the activation of the alarm.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: If that's true, I'm as clueless as you are.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What does it look like?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's basically a big egg.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You're right. That's the Sekimeiya.{w} In case Naomi didn't warn you, the Sekimeiya must never be taken out of its cabinet. The temperature provided to it is essential to maintain it well. Did you keep it shut inside?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Yes.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Hm... I wonder if the alarm halted the plan, or if Xyn intends to take it out once the time expires.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: See what I told you two? He already believes Xyn are behind this. That could very well be Ashiya's intention.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Isla, whose mother hadn't stopped trying to bring her back to consciousness, opened her eyes and coughed a few times. After a few awkward seconds, Katei told her what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...?{w} Why can't we leave?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: The exit is blocked off, and so are all the windows above. It's to prevent thieves from escaping.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So a thief is here?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Well, we don't think anything was stolen, so it's very possible something went wrong.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You're not giving us much to work with. What could've gone wrong?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: As I said, the system behind the alarm is new and has hardly been tested. Plenty of things could have.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: And you don't think the timing was way too precise for that?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Let's go to the lobby. I'm curious about the blocked door.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Interrupting the conversation, Sai stood up and told us to follow him. His intrigue was certainly shared, so we went through the door at our side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Behind it was the untouched lobby. Even though four lights had turned off, the middle one shined strongly at our eyes, causing all of us to grimace as we stared at the imposing shutter that had appeared in front of the exit. The only trace of all the people who'd been there was the janitor's bucket.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Forget what I said.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It was clearly impossible to take that down, completely keeping us shut inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: According to Katei, the remaining door in the lobby area led to a little basement below us that stored the boiler, and there was no feasible way to leave the building before it automatically opened. He also told us that the alarm had disabled the computer on the reception desk.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were rightfully frustrated, as it seemed all of us had gotten innocently trapped, and we weren't even sure why. Thankfully, though, everyone was keeping calm.{w} I was quite tired, which might have watered down my reaction to everything. It was hard to believe what I was experiencing was real, but I would most likely fall asleep somewhere well before the deadline.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The hallway door was slightly open, so someone went through it after the smoke was released, or else this hall would be stained as well.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Look, the one to the other hallway's open too. Was it you, Katei?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Are all the windows this well blocked too?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: They should be.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Do we have to spend the entire time isolated? Can we not even talk to the outside to understand what happened? This is ridiculous.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Oh, w—
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We can't, actually.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I thought for a second we might've been able to, but I just realized the alarm's side effects made that impossible.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's insane. Why would this alarm even be created that way?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I recall telling you I'm not allowed to disclose that.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Is there footage from all the cameras that we could look at?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No. The alarm made that impossible as well.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I apologize. I personally looked at every room on this floor, and I'm confident in saying we're the only people here. Right now, our priority is finding Naomi, who I suspect is hiding upstairs.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Is there anything of importance you found while you investigated?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes. The farthest crystal room in hallway A is the only other one in which the smoke was released. That's how we refer to the exhibition rooms, by the way.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Huh? Smoke was released in another room? Why?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei shook his head, indicating that he couldn't answer. As we had nowhere else to go, we were compelled to move over to it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A sturdy, gray door caught our attention first, and thanks to the map next to it, we learned that the security room was behind it. We could also see the basic layout of the floor we were on, named the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As it says there, this is the security room, but we won't be able to access it. The door was locked by the alarm, and we have no means to open it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Forced to accept that, we kept walking toward the room Katei had indicated on the map, labeled A5.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The appearance of the narrow room perfectly replicated the hallways. Every curtain was stained black, and very little light let us see where we were.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, we were at least able to shine some light on the situation by revealing that the contents of all the cabinets had been removed, which Katei hadn't noticed. At first glance, we could tell it was a well-conceived plan.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Despite that, it was Sai who quickly proposed a different idea. The lack of gems in that room could've been a mere diversion, as it was too hard to believe something as important as the Sekimeiya hadn't been the target of a real robbery attempt.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the last and shorter hallway were the bathrooms, which nobody entered.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's in the staff room? Could we find a phone there?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No. Every staff member has a personal locker, but we could only open mine, and I don't keep any devices inside.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...There's a reason why I believe Naomi hid upstairs if she's part of this, like I suspect. Above us are five desolate floors full of offices. However, there's a seventh floor that we call the attic, or the Ashiya floor.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei explained the story behind its existence, and he left the most important detail for the end.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't have the key to access it—only Naomi does. She's the sole, trusted individual chosen to preserve its interior as well as possible, and she possesses the only key I know of.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So she can stay inside for as long as she pleases.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: That's right. If Atsuki is correct, and she was still in the event room when the alarm went off, she has to be hiding. Otherwise, she would've shown herself already. The attic makes the most sense for that.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I didn't find anyone else on this floor, so she's most certainly above. I doubt we'll be able to do anything if she's locked in the attic, but we have to do all we can to find her.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: A door was in the middle of the staircase. Katei was surprised to see it unlocked because it shouldn't have opened in the past few days. When we were about to walk up the stairs, Isla asked whether we could take the elevator instead.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Indifferently, Sai tried to open its door, but it didn't budge.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei told us what we needed to know about it. No key was necessary to access the other floors with it except for the attic, which required Naomi's special key.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, it's not going to work.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Right now, the elevator won't move if you call it. The alarm disabled it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...I see. Sorry, Isla, but there's nothing we can do about that.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Aww.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Isla was displeased, but she was doing a fairly good job of not making a scene for a child her age. The wooziness left by unconsciousness probably played some part in that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The second floor looked absolutely nothing like the first. Varying shades of blue and gray surrounded us, emanating a far calmer atmosphere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Our goal was to inspect the whole building. While we had Katei's guarantee that there was no one on the crystal floor, we knew nothing about the ones above it. However, assuming he was right about the attic, we wouldn't find Naomi anyway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We began with the bathrooms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After those, we inspected the offices, occupying the main body of the floor. There were three office rooms separated by translucent walls, all containing powered-off computers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next, the blocked windows made us stop. Just like below, exiting by force was out of the question.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Lastly, we saw the corridor leading to the third floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It looked exactly like the second, with swapped staircases.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We repeated the same process and concluded there was nothing to be found on it. Katei didn't have the login information for the computers, so our single way to measure the time was Sai's wristwatch. According to that, the time was {time=9:50.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With Katei at the front, we stepped onto the fourth floor. While the bathrooms were being checked, I felt someone's hand on my shoulder.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Acid Rain
It was Atsuki's. He was at the back of the group, maintaining his predictable reserved attitude.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Look at this. I found it in the staircase.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What was surprising was seeing a silver key on the palm of his hand. It looked fairly modern, and not like one that would belong to any door nearby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, hm.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Wait.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: When I turned around to face the others, he stopped me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd like to not tell them.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: At his signal, I walked down the stairs with him. Everyone else was either in the bathrooms or waiting next to them, so they didn't notice us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This doesn't look like an ordinary key, so it should open a special door.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh, the attic's?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I don't think so. Doesn't it remind you of the security room door?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Hm... I guess it does.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I could be imagining things, but I think there are a few details Katei mentioned that don't make any sense.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Really...?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: And if this really opens the security room, it could confirm that.{w} Wasn't Katei in front of us all this time, checking the floor as if he was looking for something?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Is that so? I didn't pay attention.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: It's possible he was trying to find this key, which he didn't tell us about. If it's related to the security room... it makes sense he would've kept it a secret since there are some inconsistencies there.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: While he walked around the floor, he filled me in on what he'd been suspecting. A few assertions Katei had made about the time of the attack contradicted each other.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was taken aback. Not by the idea that Katei was potentially lying, but because Atsuki had been thinking about all of it. During the previous days, he'd looked like a person whose life had been drained out of him. At that moment, he was completely serious, which made me consider that he thought the attack was related to what had happened two weeks earlier.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Realizing that he'd gone back to being someone I could have a conversation with, I decided to humor him and follow him downstairs. In truth, what he was saying made sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei specifically stated that the alarm shut the door to the security room. If he wanted to hide the existence of its key, it followed that we could open it despite whatever reason he had to prevent that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Given that he worked inside it and seemed to expect the key to be on the floor of the office rooms, maybe he'd been the one to drop it and wasn't completely sure where it fell.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: One of Atsuki's points was undeniable: Katei had been surprised to hear Naomi was gone, but he later claimed that he inspected the entire lowest floor. He claimed to leave both doors in the lobby open while he searched, but all the crystal rooms he'd supposedly looked into were closed. It was an indication that he wanted to direct us upward, where he knew he could find his key...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Also, I think he actually saw it, but he didn't say anything. He probably wanted to grab it when we moved on.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I see.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Hey...! Where are you two going?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: On the second floor, we turned around and saw Erina and Isla. They were alone and must have realized we'd left.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I found this key, and I'd like to know if it belongs to the security room.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Without hesitating, Atsuki told Erina what his intent was, at which she looked a little surprised. After hearing that, she took Isla's hand and came with us. Isla didn't object, as it seemed the crystal floor was where she preferred to be.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If Katei had a reason to keep us away from the security room, we had no idea what it was. Atsuki was right to point out that he'd lied more than once—we couldn't trust that those lies were for the sake of confidentiality. We had no obligation to tell him what we were doing instead of just entering the room before he could think of a way to keep us out of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were in front of the security room. The metallic door did resemble the key we'd found, and it was hard to believe they weren't a match.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki inserted it in the keyhole and turned.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh?{w} It enters all the way, but it's not unlocking it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The key was getting stuck in the middle of the turn, but as he'd said, it had to be the correct one. We stood behind him, confused.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That means the door is open, right?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Atsuki looked down and met Isla's eyes. After considering her conclusion, he twisted the doorknob and pushed the door open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're right... What the hell? It wasn't even locked.{w} This was the right key, though...
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: From the hallway, we saw many lit screens in front of us illuminating a dim space. It seemed like a bit of smoke had leaked through the gaps of the door.{w} Slowly, we made our way in, wondering whether Katei had purposely lied or simply been incorrect.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei said the alarm locked the door. You really think that was a lie to stop us from trying to open it...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: If that's it, he must have something to hide, probably on the computer.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: On top of the desk were three monitors. The one in the middle had its entire screen occupied by a messy program related to the security cameras, while both side monitors were only displaying the desktop.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We got closer to them. There was a single chair in front of the middle screen that Atsuki gripped the back of.{w} He was going to sit on it, but he stopped short.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We thought the lights had gone off until we saw only the screens had, which darkened the room considerably. The ones above, displaying the real time footage of the security cameras, were still working.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did the computer shut down?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The fans are still going. It probably entered sleep mode because it's been a while since anyone used it.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Hm.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He grabbed the mouse, and as soon as he moved it, the three screens powered back on, showing the same images as before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Should I try to look at anything? We might get in trouble... If Katei's plan was to keep us out of this room, he won't be able to do so anymore.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Maybe he wanted to find the key and lock the door before we realized it was open. You know, so we'd believe what he said about the alarm locking it.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Thanks to the taskbar, I noticed that a few programs were working in the background. Maybe something we couldn't see was hidden in one of them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey, isn't that weird?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...What is?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Behind the chair, Erina was looking up at the live screens. They were showing different parts of the floor we were on, although a few of them displayed only a static, black image. According to Katei, that was due to the smoke covering them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But after looking at them for a few seconds, we noticed the large inconsistency Erina had seen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, that one. It's showing hallway B.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Wait, you're right. How is that possible...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Hallway B was clearly visible through one of the monitors. Although a bit of smoke obstructed the view, it wasn't enough to block it completely. The angle was from a corner above the door to the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's basically where we fell unconscious. It's impossible the smoke didn't hit it as much as the other cameras. The difference is huge.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Something must be wrong about this, then... This has to be the live footage since the ceiling and walls are covered by smoke.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It followed that the difference had to be the camera itself. We turned around and stepped back into hallway A. The silence told us that nobody was close to us, but it was unlikely that would continue for very long. Erina closed the security room behind her, causing a loud noise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The covered cabinet still sat awkwardly in the event room, which we passed through to enter hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's that one.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: In the left corner, above the lobby door, was a security camera with a flickering green light.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All of us frowned. After all, it looked identical to the other ones, but with one very important distinction.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's almost no smoke on its lens... How's that even possible?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: The camera itself is obviously stained, so there's no way the lens wasn't hit directly by the smoke.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Did someone clean it off?{w} I doubt anyone paid attention to this camera when we were here before, so we can't know how long it's been like this.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: If someone wiped off some of the smoke, it could only have been Katei or Naomi. I'm pretty sure Naomi was really knocked unconscious, so only Katei is left.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: M-Maybe Sai could have, if he faked waking up after me. I don't know how, though.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Why are you sure there's no one else here?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: A hidden person could've done it too, yeah...
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We haven't seen anyone else, Isla. It's too high to reach it normally, and I think removing all the smoke stuck there would take some time.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Maybe this is what Katei was hiding from us. I don't think we would have realized this lens was clean without going into the security room. It's black like the smoke, and there's very little light here.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yeah, and we noticed as soon as we took one look inside. That might make more sense than him only wanting us to not use the computer. He could've just ordered us to not touch it.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Do you seriously think he's behind this?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I don't know, I just thought a few of his claims didn't make sense. Being a member of the security staff would let him pull some things off, though, so maybe.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: You two have to know about Xyn, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yeah, Akaro talked about them briefly.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I'm sure everyone who's aware of them has assumed they're involved in this. I wouldn't rule out this whole thing being some complicated plan, so keeping this camera working might be what they want.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: We walked to hallway C with a few things to question the others about. It didn't seem like they were trying to find us, as we would have immediately heard them calling.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When we arrived at the fourth floor, we still hadn't found anyone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did they keep going without us?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I guess so.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The bathrooms, where we'd last seen them, were open and empty. We circled through the floor and arrived on the fifth one for the first time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It didn't look different from the others, and we couldn't see anyone. We repeated the same route we had on the lower floors, reaching the last one we had access to.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The attic door should be here, so maybe they found a way to get in.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: We went to the opposite corridor, where we found the entrance to the next floor. Although it looked like a dead end at first, a gray door came into view when we got closer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, this must lead to the attic.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Upon turning the knob, Erina realized the door was locked, like we'd been told.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It can't be that they're inside. Maybe they followed us down and we missed each other.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: A little lost, we walked back and stood in front of the offices. We hadn't checked the last few since it had seemed unlikely the others would've still been looking through them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki and I checked the third partition and didn't find anyone. Then, we opened the two bathrooms, which were also vacant.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The same was repeated on the fifth floor with identical results.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When we were walking down to the fourth, we stumbled upon someone going up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, here you are! I couldn't find you.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Are you alone...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I am. Where did you go? I was using the bathroom below and saw that nobody was still outside when I left.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Huh? We found the key to the security room, so we went to the crystal floor. Katei and Sai didn't come with us, though.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...I-I'm confused.{w} Why did you not wait for us? Did you actually open the security room?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Yes, that's why we'd like to find Katei.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: ...I see. I looked through the remaining floors since I imagined you all kept going up, but they were empty. I got to the Ashiya floor's door, which I couldn't open. After that, I walked back down to the crystal floor, but I haven't found anyone until now.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It appeared we'd actually missed each other. Since we'd just looked through the floors above us, we kept descending.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, here you are! Where the hell did you go?{w} And where's Katei?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: As soon as we stepped onto the third floor, we reunited with Sai, who rapidly approached us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're alone too? ...We found the key to the security room and went to the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Where did you find it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Atsuki saw it in this staircase.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Huh, I see, and you went to check if it worked?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We nodded, awaiting his explanation.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I suddenly saw you were all gone and didn't know if you'd walked down or toward the offices, but I figured I hadn't noticed you'd gone down the stairs.{w} ...I didn't find anyone when I went all the way down. I was gonna search through the first floor until I heard a sound coming from the stairs that I followed up here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So we missed you on the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He shrugged.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I get what you're saying, though. You were able to open the security room.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Before we could explain the more important details, another person appeared from the office corridor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, here you are! I knew I'd probably missed you up here.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Where were you?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I should be the one asking that. I got out of the bathroom and saw that nobody was waiting outside. There was no one on the upper floors, so I went back down. I thought that maybe all of you went down to the crystal floor for some reason.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It didn't seem like anyone was there, so I figured that I missed all of you inside the offices somewhere.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hm... We probably passed each other when I was looking alone through the higher floors.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Well, why did you all leave...? Of course, nobody has seen Naomi, right?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'm curious about something. Why exactly is it that we can't enter the security room?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The security room? Didn't I mention it? The alarm locked it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: And there's no way to undo that lock?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's surprising, seeing as they found the key and unlocked it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wh-What?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Atsuki took the silver key out of his pocket and showed it to him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What the hell? Of course I knew this key could unlock it, but where did you find it?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: In this staircase.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: That's very strange. There aren't many keys like this one, and I left mine inside the security room without thinking about it. That's why I thought we'd have no way to enter again.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: But you said that you left after the alarm played, right? You would've had to unlock the door to get out if the alarm locked it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...No key is needed to unlock it from the inside, and after closing the door from the outside, it automatically locked itself again since I didn't disable many of the alarm's functions.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'm confused. Even though we found the key, we didn't use it to unlock the door. It was already unlocked.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...{w}Excuse me?{w} That's not how it was programmed to work.{w} Regardless, is that why you suddenly left? To see if you could open the security room?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: None of you are permitted to enter without my consent. Why was I not informed about the key?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'm sure it was because of all the stuff you've said. I would've done the same thing. It appears the door being locked is just another false claim of yours.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What?{w} What is wrong with what I've said?{w} And that must've been a malfunction in the alarm. I had no way to confirm the lock was set when I left since the inner knob undoes it by itself, and I didn't check behind me to see if it locked automatically. It should have, but it appears it didn't.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I suppose that's not too ridiculous.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Wait a second. We can enter the security room! Why the hell are we talking about this!? Now we have a way to communicate with the outside. I said the alarm shut it down because I thought it locked the way in. We'll be able to look at the recorded footage as well!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Oh, that's fantastic. Let's go, then.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Although, it wouldn't exactly have been the alarm to have cut off our access to it. It would've been your ineptitude for not bringing your key out with you.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I can't deny that. It was my mistake.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: And yet an identical key was found up here. We'll see if you can find yours inside the room.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei nodded slowly and began to walk back. When the conversation ceased and the rest of us followed in silence, I glanced over at Atsuki. His brief bout of investigation had been just that: brief. Emptiness was the only thing written on his face whenever he wasn't pursuing some thought.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nobody next to him had a clue how he was feeling, and he'd decided to at least pass himself off as stable. His initiative from before had been a tad surprising, but it was clear that his mind was someplace else entirely.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With how strong those emotions were supposed to be, adopting a made-up expression of sorrow was pathetically easy. Out of recent habit, the sight of his face made my own a mirror, and I let my shoulders drop.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were walking down the stairs that led to the second floor when Sai's voice brought us to a halt.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei, how many keys do you have?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He turned around, staring at Sai uncertainly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's not too hard of a question, is it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We understood the reason behind it. As soon as Katei began to walk down the stairs, conspicuous, metallic noises came from him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Earlier, you did have a few keys, but the sound you were making just now was significantly different. Like they'd doubled in number, even.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're out of your mind.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Perhaps, which is why I'm asking.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What exactly is the issue? I am entrusted with many keys so that my job goes smoothly.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Like I said, the issue is that it sounded like you have more now. Did you recently come across a few?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'm intrigued, then. Care to show them? Maybe I'm going insane.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'd rather not. These aren't keys visitors are supposed to have.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Did you miss the word "show"? I'm not going to take any.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Seeing that he was against the request, Sai took two steps forward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Although it was Katei who looked down on him, with a quick motion, Sai rapidly snaked his hand in and out of Katei's deep pocket, where the metallic sound had come from.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: With one finger, Sai was holding a keyring with four keys on it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I suppose these would make the noise. Why did you not want to show them to us?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Because I didn't feel like humoring your condescending attitude. Are you satisfied now?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hardly. What do they open? And what's this thing? ...Tape?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Stuck on the keyring was a dark, tiny piece of material. When he separated it from the keys, we identified it as duct tape, and it had smoke residue on it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, isn't that one...?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I grabbed the keys and looked at them on my palm.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes, the Sekimeiya cabinet's. This is the keyring Naomi had.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh, wouldn't that explain it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Naomi's keyring? That's a big leap you're making. This is my own, with the same keys Naomi has.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Are you sure?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes, I am aware of the keys I'm given. This was the original set, in fact. Naomi was given a replica of it since her job was recently expanded.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So, all these keys belong to you and you didn't find it just now.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You do understand there's a simple way to prove whether you're lying, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What are you talking about?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see. You don't get it.{w} You're claiming these are yours, am I right? You didn't just come across Naomi whatsoever.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...You're being very irritating. How do you intend to prove whatever accusation you're making?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It's not a definitive way, but earlier, you said that Naomi has the attic key and you don't.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Yes.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So, if one of these keys opens the attic, we can confirm you're lying, which I was already fairly certain of. How does that sound?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I think this one might fit in the keyhole we saw.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: This one? It's definitely the odd one out. I'm glad Naomi didn't keep it separated.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai turned around and started walking up the stairs. Even though going to the security room was a priority, nobody stopped him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If he was right, and Katei had recently obtained that keyring, he knew exactly where Naomi was and had been given those keys after constructing the illusion that the attic was only accessible for her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What are you even trying to prove? There are quite a few things I'm simply not allowed to speak about.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: As we were reaching the sixth floor, Katei's mumbles stopped Sai.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you implying that you didn't tell us you had the key for the attic so that we wouldn't try to access it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm implying that you're vastly overstepping.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That might sound intimidating if you hadn't lied so much already.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You are merely assuming that.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Of course, I can't prove that the security room didn't stay open because of an error, so yeah, I will assume that was something you said to temporarily cover your ass.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...You will end up regretting all this.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai ignored him and looked at his side, where the elevator was. He approached it and pressed the circular button, which Katei had assured us would do nothing earlier.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I might as well check if the elevator is still working due to another error since it seems your claims can be ignored.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...The elevator was disabled. That's much more unlikely to have gone wrong. If it was working for some reason, the button would light up when it arrived.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Do you remember the lights in the lobby? That was also caused by the alarm, so it appears the security room was the single exception.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai accepted that Katei was probably right in that instance and kept walking.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After making it around the floor, we stood in front of the sturdy-looking door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I picked the key that seemed to fit and inserted it into the keyhole. After a turn, the door was unlocked.{w} Sai wasted no time in opening it and looking within.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I will give you all a warning. Do not enter this place. This is a very special floor that must not ever be accessed by visitors.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Let me tell you what's actually happening now. Given how likely it is that Naomi's in this place and you were planning to enter it freely, we're going to ignore your warning.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Once again, even though Katei looked around at everyone, nobody stepped forward to side with him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi must be in this building, and if she hasn't shown herself yet, she must want to keep on hiding. You said you wanted to find her too, right? Regardless of whether the two of you are working together, she's probably here. We just confirmed the elevator's not working, so she's cornered.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I can't believe what I'm hearing. Go ahead and screw yourselves over, but don't be surprised by the consequences.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Without a second thought, Sai went past the door and began to climb up a dark staircase.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We followed behind him, forming a single-file line within the narrow space. Sai stopped at the top, in front of another closed door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After applying force to open it, we could make out the room in front of him. Atsuki and I were behind, so the three of us were first to see what was on the sofa.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Whoa, what's that doing there? ...Is it the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Y-Yes.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We'd only described its appearance to the people who hadn't seen it, but a bright egg was exactly what was resting on the sofa.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What? Was it brought here?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Do you really see the Sekimeiya in there? Why are you not going in?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Wait. The floor has recent footprints on it, and someone was here not long ago.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You don't say. If the Sekimeiya's there, someone had to have just brought it up.{w} Oh, that could be really bad...! It needs to be put in its cabinet immediately! Please, step aside.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...{w}Do you think these footprints make any sense?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He looked at the two of us.{w} I stared at the floor, trying to understand what he was getting at. A few seconds later, neither of us had responded.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's a little hard to see. Maybe I'm misinterpreting them.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Can you go in so we can see what you mean?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Are you talking about the faded ones?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yeah. They don't continue, and not only those.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Please, let me get through. The Sekimeiya has to be brought down...! I already told you how important that is.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I looked at the floor again. The fuzzy carpet had preserved the more recent footprints, so the movements of the person who'd been there were recorded. It didn't seem like there was a security camera anywhere, so the footprints were our only indication.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was a line of them going from our door to the sofa, and it looked like it had been traversed more than once. From the sofa, a single pair of footprints went to a door, and from there, they came back to where we were.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai took a large step forward, trying to cover up the least possible existing footprints. Atsuki and I did the same.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're right...! It's the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: As soon as he saw it, he rushed over but stopped abruptly at the sofa.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh...! It's pretty.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Stop! None of you must touch it. That could make things even worse.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It doesn't seem damaged to me. Is that not how it usually looks?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Erina, Isla, and Akaro joined us on the left side, beside the footprints Katei had run over.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you sure it would damage it? Naomi said we could touch it.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Under normal circumstances, yes. Have you not heard what I've been saying? The cabinet downstairs provides it with a cold temperature. If you were to touch it with your bare skin, it would heat it up even more, and that could be dangerous.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So was it not you who left it here?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wh-What!? Of course not!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, your footprints are pretty much identical to the ones you just stepped on, and you had the key to enter.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei frowned and looked at his feet. The footprints did look fairly recent, so it was easy to notice the resemblance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's ridiculous. Look at Akaro's. You can't tell me they're any different.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: And out of you two, who could've entered this place?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Neither of us, probably. To get the Sekimeiya here, I would've had to go to the crystal floor, up to the attic, and then back down. All without taking the elevator, and you all remember I appeared from below where you were. There's no way I would've had enough time.{w} Are you forgetting Naomi? She's the only person who could have left these footprints unless she gave her key to someone else. I can't believe she'd leave the Sekimeiya here. She knew full well about the cold it needs.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I really don't believe these are Naomi's. According to you, she could still be here, right? Where do these two doors go?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That one goes to the kitchen, and that's the hallway.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...{w}It's still visible: under the more recent footprints, there are other ones, much harder to notice and smaller in size. Like the rest, they go from the entrance to the sofa, where the Sekimeiya is.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Oh, you're right, that one's different.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I would assume they're from when the Sekimeiya was left on the sofa, but that can't be it. It should have still been on the crystal floor then.{w} What bugs me is they don't seem to continue. Once they get to the sofa, they don't go anywhere else. I don't believe they go back to the door either, but I might be missing the returning ones. Now that Katei walked over them, it's even harder to tell.{w} It's still somewhat possible to distinguish the size and direction they're facing. Without a doubt, they don't belong to the same person who left the other ones. That's Katei, if you were wondering.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What kind of movie are you making in your head?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You went to the sofa and probably placed the Sekimeiya there. Perhaps there was something else sitting on there that the previous person left behind. Then, you went through that hallway door, and you later came back to leave through the main door.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: However, this doesn't make sense either. Going off the number of footprints, it seems like you went from the door to the sofa twice, but only once from the sofa to the hallway. What the hell happened there? You didn't jump to the kitchen, did you?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: This is the most preposterous thing I have ever heard! We have to go back down right now.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I thought you wanted to find Naomi. Like I said, the older footprints don't seem to leave through the door, and the elevator doesn't work. That means she's probably still here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: This is a very small place. It shouldn't take more than half a minute to confirm it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...{w}By the way, what's this smell?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I was wondering that. It's a bit strong.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I don't know. These rooms are pretty much abandoned, so it must be something from here. It's not that bad.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hm...{w} I feel like I've smelled it before, but I don't know where.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Really?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I might be imagining it.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Sai tried to power on the TV, but it didn't seem functional. He opened the hallway door next, evidently unconcerned about stepping over the footprints any further.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, let's see if Naomi's here. Come on.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Every room was quickly checked. The entire attic was arranged like a modest apartment, but it was well-preserved, probably thanks to Naomi.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I finished at the higher level of the left bedroom. Aside from the bedrooms, there was only a bathroom, the kitchen, and an empty storage room with no light. Surprisingly, there were security cameras even in the bedrooms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And Naomi was nowhere to be found. To make sure she couldn't have left unseen, Katei and Akaro waited in the hallway and living room respectively. We could be certain the attic was empty by the time we arrived.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All of us reunited.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't get it either. What the hell is Naomi doing...?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You're right. It's bizarre, but only because of the footprints I pointed out.{w} You have Naomi's keyring, so you must know where she is. In addition, it seems like your own footprints did the same as hers at least one of the times they went from the entrance to the sofa.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I will repeat myself. Those were not mine.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Honestly, the question is there no matter who they belonged to. From the sofa, the only way to stop the footprints would be by jumping to the kitchen, which isn't carpeted.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Suddenly, he turned around and entered the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I peeked in and saw him walking toward the elevator.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He grabbed its handle and tried to open it. Just like on the crystal floor, it didn't budge.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I already checked if it was here.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Once some silent seconds had passed, he pressed the elevator button, sighing after nothing occurred.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This doesn't make any sense. Unless I misinterpreted it, the person who left the footprints should still be here. Maybe even two people.{w} Was it a trick in case we noticed them? What if the first person stayed on the sofa, and when Katei came, they exited through the main door, stepping over his footprints and taking advantage of the bigger shoe size?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Everyone went quiet. To Sai, it probably seemed like we found what he was saying to be a bit of a reach.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I know that still doesn't explain the set of Katei's footprints that didn't continue, but that could've been fabricated by him all at once if he wanted to make it seem like he walked to the sofa twice.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Nobody said anything in response. When he realized we were all staring at something, he turned around to find the spot but failed to notice anything important.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell are you all looking at?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...The button. It lit up for a second, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yeah!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: It did.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Again, he grabbed the handle and pulled it toward him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We heard and saw the elevator opening. Pressing the button had brought it to the attic, and its interior was empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, it's working! Now we can use it.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...Of course. They just left with the elevator. It has to be that.{w} Katei!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We heard a sigh coming from the living room and subsequently footsteps approaching.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, the elevator was here?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No, the elevator was not here. I just called it, and it arrived.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What? That's not possible.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: They all saw it. The elevator is working.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But it wasn't a few minutes ago. We just tested it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Could the alarm not have affected the attic's button?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...No, it did.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I believe you're lying again. After all, your footprints indicated that you escaped from here the same way the other ones did, and it could only have been with the elevator.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I will choose to stop playing along with you. However, if the elevator is really working, I can only think of one explanation that makes sense.{w} ...That it was just enabled, minutes or seconds ago, while we were all here.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Oh, I see. It just turned on magically. That tracks.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Have you forgotten about Naomi again? She still has to be somewhere. Not only that, you left the security room open, and she might've had enough information to know how to revert some effects of the alarm.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...{w}You're so stupid.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Of course, if the elevator was enabled just now, Naomi, who most likely left the initial footprints, couldn't have escaped this place.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: However, you just said "you left the security room open".
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Have you forgotten about the lie you told us earlier? You said that after closing the door of the security room, it would lock itself automatically.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So, did you just assume they didn't close the door after leaving? Did you see it open, maybe?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm pretty sure we did close it when we left.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I know it was closed when I went back up—that's why I'm saying all this. And of course, it didn't lock itself automatically, which is why he said that you'd left it open, completely ignoring the contradictory claim he made earlier to cover his previous lie up.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not sure why you sound so excited.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So, am I wrong?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're on a wrong streak. We already determined earlier that the alarm underwent an error and didn't lock the security room after I left, did we not?{w} Why would I assume that it worked after they closed it? I figured the error probably repeated, and the door wouldn't have locked itself even if they closed it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I don't know what your problem is, but cut it out. As I said, Naomi might've just reenabled the elevator.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: How do you pretend to explain the footprints, then?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Hell if I know. I barely get what you're talking about, and I'm inclined to believe it's another delusion of yours.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Now, for the love of God, let's go to the crystal floor. Naomi might be there, and the Sekimeiya needs to be put in the cabinet. We have to contact the outside as well.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: All right! We'll take the elevator!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Oh, not all of us will be able to at once. Only four people can use it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: As soon as she heard that, Isla rushed inside, dragging Erina by her shirt.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Me. I'm going. E-le-va-tor.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: You still have the attic key, right?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: We'll walk down, then. It's very important that this floor remains locked, even if Naomi has her own key. I don't want any of you coming in without my knowledge.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sure.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai and Akaro entered the elevator.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hurry up and leave now. You won't be able to make it back up without the key. As you see, it is required to enable the floor 7 button. We won't leave until you're gone.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai rolled his eyes and let go of the door. A few seconds later, Katei checked that the elevator had left. He spent a few seconds in thought before lightly pushing my and Atsuki's shoulders back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Since he had left the living room, Atsuki went there through the kitchen, confirming that the attic was empty, although it was clear that nobody had gone there just by looking at the floor's footprints.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei stared at the Sekimeiya for a few seconds. Then, he crouched to lift it up and held it in his hands using the long sleeves of his uniform.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's go.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We carefully went down the dark staircase. Outside, I took the keyring out of my purse and locked the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Through the silence, we descended. I caught a glimpse of Atsuki's face again. I'd been trying to avoid looking at it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Usually, I figured he would've taken Sai much more seriously, but he'd hardly appeared to care about what the guy said. His suspicion toward Katei wasn't the indicator I'd been waiting for.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How much longer would I have to play along for? Ever since she'd exited our lives, I'd kept telling myself that it would all eventually go back to how it was at the beginning. However, dealing with his attitude until then and with my parents in the background was way too frustrating.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were living in his house, which had been his immediate idea. If it weren't for that, I would've assumed his mental state wasn't going to get better any time soon and that he wanted to remain alone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Behind Atsuki was Katei, who my focus switched to. His face was hardly a more pleasant sight, as it looked slightly distressed and in pain—traces that disappeared as soon as his eyes met mine. I had no clue what had happened during the attack, but plenty of things about him were iffy at best.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As soon as we began to step down the last staircase, we saw a few people in hallway A, who immediately gestured at us to hurry toward them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Take a look at the security room.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Erina and Isla were next to its door, peering inside. Katei paid no mind to Sai and pushed open the door to the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With one hand, he raised the curtain, opened the glass, and put the Sekimeiya inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, give me the keys.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I took them from my purse and handed them to him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is a manual lock, right? Does it shut the cabinet without needing the key?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Erina, Isla, and Akaro were looking from the door, indicating with their eyes that they'd found something.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes. I was just going to lock it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Atsuki turned a dial on the left side of the cabinet and verified that it could only be unlocked with a key identical to the one Naomi had used.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do not take it out under any circumstances. It's very likely Naomi brought it to the attic, so we need to find her as soon as possible.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I bet you want to know what happened in the security room first.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What happened?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai jerked his head, telling us to see for ourselves.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Awkwardly, Katei made his way to the hallway and walked up to the security room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh—{w} Was it like this when you came?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes. The elevator had been reenabled, so I wanted to go to the security room. This is how we found it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Atsuki and I, who hadn't yet seen the problem, approached the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was very easy to tell what was wrong from the hallway. Every monitor was displaying a black screen, and the drone of the computer had ceased.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did the computer stop working?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: There's still the ceiling light, so I assume so.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The computer did not stop working. It must've been turned off. The monitors above it won't display anything while the computer's off.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He walked into the room while everyone entered after him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, after pressing the power button, there was no change.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell...?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Also, the door was closed, but not locked, just like you figured.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I see... I have no idea what was done, but the computer couldn't have stopped working by itself.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You didn't do it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well, you were on this floor before you reunited with us, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I was only here for a few seconds, unlike you all.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The computer was working when we left.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: We could've used it for several things, so someone disabled it deliberately. Who had the chance to do that?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You, Akaro, Sai, or Naomi.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Katei glanced at Sai when I mentioned him, as he was under the impression he'd been with us when we went down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, you didn't hear that, but I wasn't with them the whole time. I didn't enter this room, though.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What about Atsuki?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The four of us went together.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I see...
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: {tip=suspicion}...{/tip}
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So, from your point of view, we are the only people who could've entered this room after you left it with the computer running.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You might be ignoring something, though. Someone used this computer after we all met up again.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The elevator was reenabled when we were in the attic, which means that Naomi turned off the computer after doing so and is still hiding. It makes sense because she knows what we could do with it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Would she really have any idea how to power on the elevator?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Even if she didn't know in detail, it is fairly simple to work out. I imagine she was told about the alarm and its functions, after all.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I thought that made enough sense, except for one important detail.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But if Naomi didn't want us to use this computer, why did she not power it off earlier?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Probably because she was in the attic. But most importantly, because she thought this room was locked, even though it remained open because the alarm failed to lock it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...If it's true that the alarm should've locked it after leaving, sure.{w} But even if it did malfunction, the only reason why we didn't enter before was because you'd left your key inside, right?{w} Normally, she would've expected you to bring it out and be able to open the door whenever. It doesn't make sense to say she cared about us using the computer because we should've been able to get in here right away, while it was still working.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I'd forgotten about that key. You said you left yours in this room, so where is it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei opened a drawer and took all of its papers out as he spoke.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's possible she was keeping track of what we were doing from somewhere and knew that I hadn't unlocked the room yet. When she saw you'd opened it, you gave her an easy chance to power off the computer, even though I don't know how exactly she did it. I'm not sure why you're all having such a hard time believing me.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I-It's not here...
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Atsuki took the key he'd found out of his pocket.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This must be your key, then.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I guess so... But how the hell did it make it to the third floor?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei took it from Atsuki's hand and left it in the same drawer he'd searched through.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nobody answered him. Before, Atsuki had told me that he'd seen Katei staring at the floor on the higher levels of the building. If he'd known he needed to find the key somewhere, he must have deliberately withheld that, aware that the door had been left open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, as soon as we'd managed to enter, someone had immediately taken the opportunity to power off the computer. The intentions of that person coincided with Katei's if Atsuki's theory was right.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's clear is that whoever shut down the computer enabled the elevator before doing so...
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: And Katei's the one person who would definitely know how to do that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I agree that it seems strange Naomi would know how to accomplish that without having a lot of time to experiment.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So, it could be that powering off the computer enabled the elevator at the same time. It shouldn't have been the case, but I can't rule it out with the lack of testing this alarm had.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Go see whether the lobby's lights are working again. If they are, it's possible the alarm's secondary effects were reversed when the computer was turned off, as the way to disable them is very different from the main one, which blocks the exit.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Even though the computer doesn't work, the camera system functions independently. I don't know if it was shut down, so it's possible the cameras are still recording and that we simply can't look at the footage.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I want to try a few things here and see if I can get the computer running again, so you can leave me be if you want. I will recommend once again that we find Naomi.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: After a light shrug, Sai spoke.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sure. We still haven't looked through this entire floor. If we can't find Naomi here, we'll have to search the entire building in more depth.{w} Oh, there's something else I meant to ask you. Inside the elevator, there's a stop button that's supposed to enable communication with the outside. Would that help us?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No, it won't. The alarm's effects may not have worked perfectly, but one of them was to disable that connection. If you press the button, you'll get locked inside until {time=21}, so I'd advise you not to do it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hm, I see. I'm glad we didn't go for it, then.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai moved to hallway A, and the others followed him. I was about to leave as well, but Katei's look stopped me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once he and I were alone, he spoke in a quiet whisper.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How well do you know Atsuki? The two of you are friends, right?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Oh, yeah...
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: We hadn't spoken much, but we'd been together in the lobby and were the same age, so it made sense for him to assume that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you trust him?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I don't know if you're working with him. If you are, I'm warning you to stop whatever you're doing, but if you aren't, I will tell you directly: he is lying.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He's lying to you and everyone else. He was the one who brought the Sekimeiya to the attic.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: No, he wasn't. I've been with him the entire time.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Look, if you're actually unaware of whatever he's doing, make sure to keep an eye on him, and don't ever leave him alone. Make sure he can't ever take the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Internally, I laughed. Of course, suspecting Atsuki hadn't at all crossed my mind. Under normal circumstances, I might possibly have believed that he was messing around and something he'd done had been misinterpreted, but Katei had just outed himself as a liar.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Out of curiosity, why are you saying he brought the Sekimeiya to the attic?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: ...I can't tell you that, but you can take my word for it. I am certain that he did.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I tried not to snort and walked out to hallway A. I didn't know what was up with Katei, but everything about him was questionable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why had he told me that? If it was all a lie, what did he plan to accomplish by telling me about it without even specifying any details? Even if he really did believe it, why would he have approached the person most likely to be working with his suspect?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: From all I could tell, the guy was a moron, plain and simple. At least Sai thought about what he said, even if he came across as a loose cannon.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I saw the others had gone to the lobby, so I joined them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, the lights do work.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The four smaller lights were functioning again. However, that couldn't be taken as confirmation of anything since Katei had been the one to suggest checking them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Without saying anything else, Sai walked to the other hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Strangely, he went straight to the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Terraformed
Why did you come here?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: So Katei doesn't see me.
entries.speaker: sai
