entries.text: Nonchalantly, he put out his hand to Atsuki.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you want the keys?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Precisely.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: To unlock the cabinet.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What's the point? It could be dangerous for the Sekimeiya. Let's not cause problems we can avoid.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I want to touch it, though...
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: And there should be no problem with that. You said Naomi was gonna let you do it, but Katei made sure nobody would touch it.{w} You all understand he's been lying, don't you? And the Sekimeiya was brought to the attic, either by him or Naomi—the two people who should've known a higher temperature could be damaging.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's pretty suspicious, right? I bet he exaggerated the need for the temperature so we wouldn't get it out. However, he took it out himself earlier and brought it to the attic.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You don't think it was Naomi?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: The keyring that Atsuki has might be hers. Katei had to lie and say he had an identical one. That means it's pretty unlikely she was the one to move the Sekimeiya, so she probably can't access the attic at the moment.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: However, there's one thing I find incredibly strange, and I'm not sure why Katei hasn't tried to excuse it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: A few minutes ago, he made you lock the attic, claiming he didn't want anyone entering it without his knowledge. Now, he said he was going to manually lock this cabinet so that nobody could open it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But he didn't ask for the keyring and let Atsuki keep it. That's just plain contradictory, and not something he would ignore.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're actually right. He should've made sure to keep it for himself after locking the attic.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Which leads me to a single conclusion: Katei is, to put it politely, of low intelligence.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He might just be working with Naomi, who does have an identical set of keys. It's fair to assume he wanted the attic and this cabinet locked to give Naomi a way out. She can still unlock both of them, and by letting Atsuki keep the keys, he'll always be a possible suspect for Naomi's actions.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Otherwise, it doesn't make sense. He must know how hard it is to believe that the keyring Atsuki has isn't Naomi's and is taking advantage of that to make us think only Atsuki can use it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It sounds like he made up that the Sekimeiya had to be kept here for a reason, right? It was in the attic and nothing happened to it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Atsuki walked forward, unlocked the cabinet with the key, and scrolled open the glass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This compartment is definitely kept pretty cold.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: That hardly matters. Take it out. There's something I'm especially curious about.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Atsuki sighed and looked at the useless camera that wasn't recording him. With both hands, he grabbed the cushion and took it out. Then, he placed it on top of the cabinet, with the Sekimeiya resting in the middle.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He stepped back. Katei had made it clear he didn't want us to touch it, so Atsuki didn't lay a hand on it himself and simply allowed Sai to do so if he wished.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Of course, nothing's happening to it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: This is a bad idea, Sai.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Nobody was sure why he'd pushed back against Katei's orders so much, but Isla walked up to the cabinet and tried to reach the Sekimeiya with her arm.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You are here. I haven't been ab—
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What the hell...!? What are you doing!?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Seeing his expression, Isla dashed away before Katei ran to the cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I said many times how importa—
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Nobody cut him off, but that sentence never finished.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Whoa, what the fuck?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We'd all seen the same thing. Katei had run toward the Sekimeiya and made to grab it. ...Then, his entire figure vanished from the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At the same time, the Sekimeiya had turned gray, as if reacting to Katei's touch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While we exchanged speechless looks, we saw Akaro staring through the hallway A door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What the fuck did you just do?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We approached it and saw Katei in the hallway, close to the security room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki was in just as much disbelief as the rest of us. I thought I must've missed something, but Sai's question confirmed we'd all interpreted it the same way.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did this man just teleport?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Like ours, Katei's eyes lacked comprehension, and he only let out some words seconds after the minimal echo had faded away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I just...{w} traveled to the past.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...What?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Traveled to the past? Is that what we're supposed to believe...?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Nobody could accuse Katei of a trick, as we'd all seen him disappear.{w} He was breathing heavily, and he started to move his arms, checking that his body worked as usual.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I know how it sounds, but that's what it felt like. No... what the hell just happened?{w} It did feel like I went back a few seconds, to when I was walking from the security room to the event room.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He slowly returned to the event room and stared at the Sekimeiya, which had changed colors.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This thing is dangerous. Did it darken when I touched it? I know I felt it burning.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: While nobody answered, he approached it and put it inside the cabinet with its cushion, avoiding direct contact with it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What the hell?{w} It turned white again.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Did you know this would happen?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What? Of co—
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: This is why you insisted we couldn't get the Sekimeiya out of this cabinet, that we shouldn't touch it, and it's why you never touched it directly when you brought it down.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What are you talking about? I'm as confused as you are.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: As he spoke, he manually locked the cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That thing just made you teleport out of the room, and either you or Naomi brought it to the attic. You knew what it would do. That's why the fucking footprints were so weird, like someone had disappeared right in front of the Sekimeiya!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The conversation began to sound utterly surreal, but Sai was making sense. If the Sekimeiya had really teleported Katei, it recontextualized a few things.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What are you even accusing me of? I touched it and instantly found myself in the hallway. I have no clue how it happened. I can't even believe what I'm saying!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I couldn't help but agree with Sai. Katei had rushed to the Sekimeiya as soon as he'd seen it above the cabinet, and he'd touched it with his own skin in his panic despite his previous caution on the top floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I came here after hearing voices to inform you that I hadn't been able to power the computer back on.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: And, unbelievable as it seemed, it sounded like he was trying to change the subject.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I still have more things to try, though. I know I've repeated myself quite a few times, but it's clear now that the Sekimeiya must be kept here.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You said it made you travel to the past, but you're just going to ignore that?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I know I don't want to try it again... whatever might have really happened. I have very little information about the Sekimeiya, but this is no ordinary gem, as expected.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: It has to stay here until the shutter opens. There's no way it isn't dangerous, and the cold temperature must keep it stable in some way. I wasn't given any information on why it's essential, but Naomi might know more about it, so we come back to the same point: we must find her.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He walked toward us, and then to hallway A.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...If I manage to power the computer and cameras back on, that'll be the best way to find her.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then, he walked to the security room and left our field of vision.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck...? He did it again!{w} Does he think we're idiots? He walked away from a stone that made him teleport and didn't demand the keys!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're right, yeah. If he wanted to keep it locked in this cabinet, he would've made sure to ask for those back.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: He's definitely working with Naomi. Whatever it is, he isn't being truthful in the slightest.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Unlock it again.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Of course, after all that Katei had said, we could just take the Sekimeiya out of the cabinet again, and it was fairly stupid to think that we wouldn't. Without thinking about it, Atsuki undid Katei's lock.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He opened the glass and once again took out the cushion holding the Sekimeiya. The gemstone had gone back to glowing white, but Atsuki didn't place it anywhere. He looked at it curiously, with both of his hands occupied.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What, do we touch it?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Most of us looked skeptical or even embarrassed to try. Sai, who I'd imagined would be the first to attempt it, appeared hesitant.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were staring at the Sekimeiya, when in an instant, the opposite door had become our focus. From behind the shut door to hallway B came a sound we had to confirm we'd heard.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi... it has to be her.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: We all got closer to the door, and Akaro opened it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The hallway was empty, but it contained many doors none of us had entered yet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It came from pretty close to the door, but it looks like she hid already.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Was she listening and ran away when she realized she'd been heard?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We'd left the way to the lobby open, but if Naomi had been sneaking up on us, it was possible she'd closed herself behind one of the multitude of doors we could see. If that was the case, we finally had a chance to confront her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We hadn't yet inspected the whole crystal floor, and we still had to locate her. The Sekimeiya rolled slightly on top of the cushion, which Atsuki laid on the floor next to him. Meanwhile, the rest of us opened door after door and briefly looked through each room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All the crystal rooms were empty, and midway, we noticed that some of the cabinets could be opened to reveal spacious interiors. The staff room contained numerous lockers we couldn't open, and the small cleaning room had several cleaning products, a large cart, and some buckets. In the end, we hadn't found anyone in hallway B or in the bathrooms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But we knew we had heard a person, so we didn't stop there. While Atsuki continued looking through hallway B, we went down to the mechanical room, which was empty and somewhat foreboding.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei was kneeling under the desk in the security room. We quietly ignored him and searched through hallway A's rooms. Again, every crystal room was identical except for the one that had been hit by the smoke. ...Like the storeroom, though, it was empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We knew Naomi had been very close to us, but we'd failed to find her, and we had to prioritize the Sekimeiya before extending the search to the higher floors. Exasperated, we returned to see Atsuki waiting on the spot where we'd last seen him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the floor were the cushion and the Sekimeiya. When it was clear we hadn't found anyone, he looked at them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Remember the smell from the attic? It might've come from the Sekimeiya. I started noticing it here some time ago.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh, huh.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I'm going to touch it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I felt slight traces of tension for a second. Was it really possible he was about to travel through time? I didn't think I could really take that seriously, but seeing him about to try made me uncomfortable. It was almost laughable how all of us looked on in anticipation, trying to confirm whether we'd lost our minds or not.{w} His hand got closer and closer to the gem until no distance separated it from him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As he touched it, he was instantly no longer touching it. Atsuki was gone, and the Sekimeiya turned gray.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everybody else was occupied with the realization that the Sekimeiya's powers were real, but I ran forward, perceiving another sound from hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The door wasn't fully closed, so I opened it all the way. I'd heard a sound just as Atsuki had disappeared, and I knew someone was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The instant I peeked around it, I saw him. Hesitantly glancing from hallway C was Atsuki, whose eyes pierced mine until he removed himself from behind the corner. Slowly, he began to walk up to me as I wondered what to say.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, i-it worked...? You went to the past?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Um... Y-Yes. I suppose so.{w} I can't... I can't believe it, though.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Everyone else was petrified, suppressing their sheer shock, but I noticed that someone who should've been there was missing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is Sai not here?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Oh, y-you're right. I don't think he's been here for a bit.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: How is this possible...? I don't get it, but if you went to the past, why didn't you appear in this room? That's what happened to Katei.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Hm...{w} I don't think I traveled a few seconds through time, but actually minutes. About twenty, I'd say.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh, what? That long ago, we were still in the attic, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Atsuki nodded, clearly disconcerted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We could only look at the Sekimeiya, which was a different color than it should've been.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: L-Let me see.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He crouched again and placed his hand on it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's not doing anything, and it's cold. ...It must do nothing when it's this color.{w} It's just a thought, but maybe I traveled farther because it spent more time out of the cabinet. When Katei touched it, it had barely been out for any time at all.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He grabbed the cushion with both hands and walked to the cabinet. Mere seconds after he put it back in its place, the Sekimeiya started glowing again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This again.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We could only stare in confusion as he closed the glass. The keyring had been left in the keyhole, so he took it out before thinking about how to phrase what he wanted to say.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I still can't believe what just happened to me, but I think we should go along with what Katei said and leave this in the cabinet until we can leave.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I frowned a little while he locked the cabinet with the wheel. He held out his arm to hand me the keyring, which I put in my purse without question, even though it confused me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I mean, what else would we do?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Atsuki didn't answer, but I imagined the way he'd internally responded to that question. A few days ago, I'd heard the words "I wish I could go back in time" coming out of his mouth. I couldn't believe he was actually going to casually leave the Sekimeiya locked away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Honestly, that would have been ideal. I'd been expecting a much different reaction, and I couldn't discard it entirely. He could've easily been trying to fool the others by giving the keys to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No one spoke up, probably only thanks to the fact that Sai wasn't around. Akaro had indicated he wasn't in hallway A either, so we had no idea if he was even nearby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did you make the sound in hallway B earlier?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Oh, yeah, I did. That was when I realized I had really traveled through time. I moved to the second floor fast enough to stay out of sight.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: That's just insane. ...Were we actually searching for you? Where the hell is Naomi, then?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We stepped into the gloomy hallway A.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Actually, where is Sai? That's another good question.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I know he was with us when we searched this hallway.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Did he go somewhere...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Annoyed, Akaro rapidly glanced through the doors.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He's not here. Did you see what happened to him?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: He directed that question at Atsuki, who'd gone several minutes to the past and remained hidden.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...No. I was on the second floor, so all I know is that he didn't go up.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He's still here, then...
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Faint sounds had been coming from the security room, where Katei was. To confirm that he was alone, we walked up to the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We could see him leaning back on the chair in defeat due to all the screens still being black.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Oh, I haven't been able to fix anything. I apologize.{w} I am completely lost; I don't even know what the issue is. Everything is properly arranged and connected, so unless no electricity is reaching the outlets, I'm out of ideas.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He crouched and crawled under the desk, failing to realize that Sai wasn't with us. We approached him and silently stared while he kept repeating how confused he was from the floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And you still haven't found Naomi... You were inspecting this floor just now, right?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Yes. She wasn't here.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That's very strange. She might have been able to keep dodging us, but there's no way that'll work for too long. There's no place where she could hide forever.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He crawled out and let himself fall back onto the chair, looking exhausted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Behind him, all of us kept silent. We were all digesting the fact that time travel had occurred right in front of us, but it didn't seem like Katei found that particularly relevant, as he only looked concerned about his computer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I noticed that Atsuki was remaining by himself next to the door. I wouldn't have approached him, but I saw him staring curiously into the distance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Is there anything...{w} Oh, the elevator?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: As soon as I glanced at hallway C, I could see that the elevator's door was very slightly open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's not closed, yeah.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Akaro approached us with a frown, but Katei addressed it before he got far.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, it's been like that for a while. I noticed it when we walked down from the attic and figured the others purposely left it like that.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We didn't.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It must not have closed properly when you got off, then. I've seen it happen in the past.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hm, I see. I didn't notice it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Me neither.{w} ...Wait, I just remembered the hallway B camera. The one that had its lens completely clean.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Going by their looks, Akaro and Katei didn't know what I was talking about.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Excuse me...?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Right, the one above the door to the lobby.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yeah, its footage was being displayed up there.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Are you serious?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Both of them hurried out of the room while the rest of us awkwardly stayed put.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla, clinging to her mother's legs, had become a little more relaxed. She inquisitively looked around, time travel evidently not much of a weight on her mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: During the silence, I approached the computer. I was slightly interested in its mysterious shutdown, but I didn't examine it too thoroughly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It didn't take the others long to return.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You saw it, right?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: What the hell...? Was it cleaned?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: There's no way we would know.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: We looked at Katei, who'd put his hand in one of his deep pockets but took it back out empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I don't have it anymore, but do you remember when—
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Wait, where the hell is Sai?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...{w}After looking at each other, we let him know we'd recently lost track of Sai. Before Katei could get too alarmed, Akaro cut in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What were you gonna say? We've already searched for Sai, and the Sekimeiya's locked in the cabinet.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...{w}The duct tape, remember? Sai took out my keyring, and it had a piece of duct tape attached to it. That piece had smoke residue on it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We all remembered what he was talking about and began to understand why he'd brought it up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I know it was duct tape because one side was still sticky, which means that it was only hit on the front side. In other words, it was stuck somewhere when the smoke was released.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Where did it even come from?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...{w}When I walked down to the crystal floor, searching for you, I found it hidden behind a handrail and put it in my pocket to inquire about it. That's when it got stuck to the keyring.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: So it was placed on the lens of that camera, which prevented the smoke from hitting it. Afterward, it was removed...
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I'm confused about a few things. Why would someone do that? They had to already know the smoke attack would happen.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: And it was removed before we entered the security room.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Additionally, leaving it behind a handrail seemed strange. If they wanted to throw it away, flushing it down the toilet seemed ideal, as fingerprints could otherwise present a problem.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That logic led to the thought that Katei, who might have orchestrated the whole thing, had the opportunity to place the duct tape himself and keep it in his pocket, unaware that we'd find it. I opted not to speculate about that out loud and let everyone else come to the conclusions they wanted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the end, Katei sighed and sat on his chair again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell is Naomi doing...? We can't even use the computer to figure anything out.{w} Do you all think Sai ran away on his own? Now we need to find both of them.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We lost track of him when we were searching this hallway, which would've been a good opportunity to sneak away. I have no idea why he'd do that, though.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Once again, Katei pressed the computer's power button in frustration while looking at all the powered-off screens.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe now you can believe that he was the one up to something. I'm just trying to do my job.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Whether they believed him or not, nobody spoke up for a while.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even if two people had traveled through time, we all had our own reasons to keep still in the narrow room, prioritizing internal thoughts before going out to find the two missing people.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were still behind Katei's chair, awaiting any decision, when noise came from the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As we turned around, we saw Sai staring at us next to the unassertive Atsuki.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-Where were you!?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Me? I just took a detour to the bathroom.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Katei's smirk perfectly conveyed his reaction, but Sai ignored it. Instead, he slipped into the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, what are we doing here? You still can't fix your own computer?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What do you think?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I think that we just found out we can travel to the past and are instead trying to fix a computer. Wouldn't it be a better idea to go back in time and see who did this?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You really can't expect us to take you seriously.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Sai, what were you doing just now? You definitely weren't in the bathroom.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Did you check all of them?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You have to give up on him. Whatever he was doing will be exposed eventually.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Anyway, who has the keys now?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I have them.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I see. ...Is there a reason why we're here?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No. We should try to find Naomi again.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: That's what I'm saying.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Where Is The Mask
As Sai left the room, we all exchanged looks, wondering what his intentions really were. We began to disperse into hallway A behind him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki hadn't yet moved from the door, and his expression had gotten considerably murkier. I had no idea what it meant anymore, so I walked up to him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is it going better?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: ...Huh?{w} Sorry, I don't know. I just can't believe it. I really traveled through time.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Well, I can't believe it either.{w} ...Are you sure you don't want to do it again?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: What? Travel through time?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yeah.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: No, of course I do.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I'm trying to understand some things. I traveled a few minutes to the past, to the attic, which might make sense. I'm not sure if that's enough, though.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...Oh, I see.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: He didn't seem to even notice my reply. Since he'd gone quiet again, I walked away slowly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When Sai saw that, he approached me and spoke in a hushed tone so that his words reached only my ears.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You think Atsuki's hiding something, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: You definitely know him, but you realized something he said didn't make sense.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What the hell are you talking about?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Am I wrong? He traveled to the past with the Sekimeiya—that much I know.{w} Then, he simply reunited with you guys. Am I missing something?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: N-No? What are you getting at?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: If I'm not missing anything, I don't know. However, he is hiding something, and apparently even from you.{w} I'm sure he'll want to use the Sekimeiya again, so if he doesn't tell you that, assume that he's lying and try to stop him.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Trying his best to sound mysterious, Sai walked away. The two most suspicious people there had inquired about Atsuki, and once again, I could only laugh inwardly as I sighed outwardly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Try to stop him." They didn't need to tell me that, but I wouldn't do anything. In any case, given that I'd been told the same thing again, it was very possible Atsuki was actually trying to pull something off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If Naomi's really hiding, we'll never find her if we go in one group. Let's disperse ourselves through the building. There's no way we'll miss her if we do that.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What a good idea.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: In the blink of an eye, Atsuki and I were the only remaining people in hallway A.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla had dragged Erina into a crystal room, Akaro had disappeared off to hallway C, and Sai and Katei had gone up the stairs individually. Despite sharing a common objective, there was no coordination, and everyone had silently chosen their own path to take.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were left a little puzzled, as everyone had walked away from the Sekimeiya which only I could take out of the cabinet. Was it because Atsuki told us he didn't want to use it? I couldn't exactly ask anyone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Well, what do we do?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: You're asking me? I don't know. I'm just tired.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Me too. You've been awake for longer, though.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I know.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I suppose we could go to the attic. You have the key, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yeah, but we probably shouldn't go in alone, and splitting up to find Naomi won't work if half of us stay still.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I'm not sure it'd work anyway. If the exit closed as the alarm went off and she's hiding somewhere, she must be confident she won't be found. And if she's working with Katei, he's definitely confident we won't find her.{w} We've already been everywhere in this building, so I don't think it's essential that we keep looking for her. If she can be found, it'll happen eventually.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...What do you want, then?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I want to go to the attic. I need to lie down for a bit.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We'd been told not to enter without Katei's consent, but he was the one who let us keep the keys. I hesitated, but I had no reason to object, so I just shrugged and headed over to the elevator.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I noticed something had changed when I reached for the handle.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The door's not open anymore.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Oh, yeah, it was earlier. {tip=perspective}Sai used it{/tip}.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: That makes sense.{w} ...And it's still here.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: There was no resistance when I tried to open the door, meaning that Sai had gotten off on the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki nodded before stepping in. I took the keyring from my purse and inserted the attic key into the first keyhole. The light around the floor 7 button activated, and after pressing it, we began to ascend.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know what to think of Atsuki, but we were at least getting far away from the Sekimeiya, which felt as strange as everyone else having left. With dull eyes, he stared at the door until the trip ended. I just wished we'd gone to sleep the previous night.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I felt a little uncomfortable stepping onto the wooden floor, aware that there were about to be cameras pointed right at us. That sensation didn't seem to be shared by Atsuki, who directly approached the living room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It doesn't look like anyone else has been here.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Plenty of footprints were still visible, and I figured Atsuki knew they were the same ones we'd seen before leaving.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey, hasn't the smell from earlier faded away a lot?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh, I think you're right.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: ...I'm so exhausted... Even if we shouldn't be here, at least nobody will bother us, assuming Naomi really can't get in.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He walked down the hallway, sighing deeply. After choosing to open the right door, I heard him falling onto the bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I entered the room and recalled that there was only one bed. He was already lying face-down, all energy drained out of him. I stood by the door for a moment and then closed it after stepping in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could've gone to the neighboring room, but I decided to go to the upper level instead.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There, I shakily sat on one of the beds, finding my situation unnerving. My whole body was stiff, and my mind felt numb. After a while, I managed to lie down, and the mattress reminded my body how tired it was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't fight the tiredness. Under foreign bed sheets, recorded by a camera on that forbidden floor, I pushed my consciousness away until it dissipated.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I woke up, I realized I must not have slept for very long, as I didn't feel like I had dreamed at all. I was still uneasy, and I hadn't turned off the light.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While I didn't know the time, it was fairly likely that people were looking for us and couldn't get in the attic. I didn't care anymore; my back hurt, and I was just as tired as before. I slowly stood up and approached the light switch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But my hand stopped before touching it, and so did my whole body.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did I just do this?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I'd noticed something very important next to the bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was only one thing I did before falling asleep: look at my purse. I'd stared at it and then forced myself to look away, nervous that it was so out in the open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Because if I'd fallen asleep, someone could've looked inside. ...And that was something that couldn't happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I crouched very slowly and then looked at it from the same position as before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It moved. It wasn't like that when I fell asleep.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The difference was minimal, but I noticed it immediately, and it was no mistake.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No, did he...?{w} Or did I just poke it when I stood up?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I widened the opening with my fingers and looked inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everything's here.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Nothing had been taken, but that didn't settle it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The keys were inside. If someone had gone through my purse, it was very likely those keys were the target, but they were far from my concern.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki and I should've been alone in the attic, which had both of its entrances locked.{w} I suddenly wasn't sensing my tiredness anymore. I grabbed my purse and approached the hatch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was shut, so I slowly lifted it up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Are you awake?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Uh,{w=0.4} yes...{w=0.5} I only slept for a few minutes and couldn't do it again.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: How do you know it was only a few minutes?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Huh? That's just what it felt like. Did you just wake up?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I took a few seconds to reply while I climbed down the ladder. The light was turned on, and the sheets over him were in disarray.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, I don't know how long it's been.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I spent a very long time trying to sleep again, so I think at least two hours.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh, really...?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: *yawn*{w} Yeah, and I don't think it'll happen. Are you still tired?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: No, I'm fine now.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I see.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I felt as if part of my mind had cleared up. We'd seriously gotten trapped in the building, and Atsuki had traveled through time. ...Could that be true? Could that really have happened?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He sat on the bed and stretched his arms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was so absurd that I hadn't been able to react when I'd seen him teleport. It had all suddenly happened with no room for doubt, but what was going on? Only after waking up had I begun to comprehend how strange it was that he'd wanted to go to the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you hear anything outside the bedroom?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: No. We might really have the only key to this place.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Since I didn't want to ask, I approached the door. The chain wasn't set, so I turned the handle to see if he'd locked it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The door opened smoothly, indicating that anyone could've made their way in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you want to go back down? I was waiting for you to wake up. I'm not as tired anymore.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...{w}Yeah, sure.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Was I being toyed with? The more seconds passed, the more I felt that way.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki stood up and silently walked to the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nobody crossed this carpet. I can hardly see the footprints anymore.{w} ...You have the key with you, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Well, we should probably use the elevator again, so I don't think we'll need it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He tried to open the door, but he couldn't.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I suppose someone called it while we were sleeping.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I leaned on the wall while he pressed the button. I was acting disinterested naturally, but I couldn't get the sight of my purse out of my head.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The silent orange light indicated the elevator's arrival. Atsuki pulled the door open, and we walked in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The elevator began to descend toward the lowest floor—the destination that Atsuki had chosen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I guess we'll have to apologize for going up, but we were really tired. I wonder if they found Naomi...
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Atsuki was resembling Katei more and more to me, and I didn't know if I could trust him.{w} Behind him was the red stop button, which Katei claimed would confine us inside until the alarm's effects automatically reverted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I didn't dare touch it, allowing the doors to open. After Atsuki pushed open the outer one, hallway C came into sight, just as barren as we remembered it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's go to the security room. Maybe we can look at the time.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: The light was on, but no screens were. That meant that Sai's watch was still all we had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It hasn't been fixed... I can't hear anyone, but they should be somewhere on this floor.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Atsuki was ready to leave, but I couldn't help but feel iffy about the computer's shutdown. Katei was the only one who tried to fix it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Since we were alone, I crouched under the desk and stared at the mess of cables that Katei had been examining.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Uh...
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: After glancing back and forth, an oddity stood out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Can you even see properly down there?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes, and this cable isn't plugged in.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I don't know what it's for, but Katei said that everything was in place.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Can you tell where it should go?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The angle was uncomfortable on my neck, but I strained to look behind the computer tower and found a slot that could fit. Forced to use my left hand, I grabbed the cable and managed to plug it into the computer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know if that did anything, but it's plugged in now.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I clambered out as Atsuki pressed the power button.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A few seconds later, the system began to run.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...A-Are you serious?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The middle screen lit up, and a loading logo glowed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't get it. Did Katei do this and hope we wouldn't look at the cables?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I'd begun to gather hope, but it dissipated as soon as the computer turned off again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Huh? Is it still not working?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Confused, Atsuki powered it on one more time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The same thing happened: seconds after running, it automatically powered off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki looked under the desk in case he could spot the problem.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't see anything clearly wrong. Maybe the operating system got damaged.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I see... We need to tell the others about this—especially Katei.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Right.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We were about to leave when Atsuki remembered what I'd said.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, wait. We might still be able to look at the time.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He walked back toward the computer and powered it on. While it was running, he looked at the screen and pressed one of the suggested keys. Then, the screen changed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I just accessed the BIOS. If I knew more about computers, I might be able to pinpoint the issue, but look here.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: In the top right corner, "{time=13:16}" was displayed in black digits.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, {time=13} already. I guess I did sleep for over two hours.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Ye—
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...Did you hear that?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Hm? I didn't hear anything.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: He warily walked to the hallway A door and looked through it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I think I heard something in the lobby.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Seeing how cautious he was, I approached it myself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nobody was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Still fazed by the imposing shutter, Atsuki walked forward a little.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did I imagine it...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Both other doors were shut. Atsuki circled the room at a slow pace and stopped to smell the air. Then, he continued his circle with a frown.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's this open drawer. It wasn't like this before, was it?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I moved over to him. Behind the reception desk, one of the drawers wasn't fully closed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, no, I don't think so.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: We looked inside and confirmed that there was nothing in it. Then, Atsuki proceeded to open all the other drawers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's only papers in a few of them.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: That's strange. I honestly can't be sure it wasn't open before.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Something else we'll have to ask.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: While walking toward hallway B, Atsuki noticed I still hadn't moved.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: What's up?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Come back. You hear this faint buzz, right?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Yes. It's coming from below, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It's the boiler. I was thinking that it must be really annoying to work at this chair with this constant noise.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: But then I thought that it might not have been as noticeable before. You didn't go to the mechanical room, but the rest of us did. I'm not sure it was audible from up here.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: O-Oh.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He looked at the door he'd not yet gone through.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Actually, I remember beginning to hear the sound as we were going down the stairs.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: As soon as he opened it, the intensity of the sound strengthened. There was no light on the stairs, and they immediately made a sharp turn.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You think the boiler got louder, then?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh, that's not what I meant.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: After a few steps forward, I confirmed my assumption: the short door leading to the mechanical room was partially open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's this door. It was shut when we came, so the sound didn't reach us. I don't remember if we closed it when we left.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Ah, I see. So at most, it means that someone went down here, but I'm sure they searched for us and Naomi. It's fine.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He began descending the stairs. If he'd really heard a sound coming from the lobby, it was possible someone was under us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After widening the gap of the door, he stepped into the basement room, which was constantly beset by the buzzing noise. I stopped behind him, waiting for my eyes to adjust to the illumination the faint light bulb offered.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But even when that happened, the darkness still reigned. Atsuki started to walk slowly in order to comprehend where he was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I-I don't think there's anyone here.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I could discern a few pieces of furniture that Atsuki had moved aside and the walls closest to me. Strangely, I felt relieved to hear there was nobody with us, even though we wanted to find the others.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, no.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Hm?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Look.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I thought we were about to leave, but that wasn't the case. I approached the dark blob Atsuki was next to until it was revealed to be a pile of chairs. Behind it, on the floor, was an abnormal, weak glow.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya. The gemstone we'd come to see and which possessed a mysterious power. Immobile on the floor, it resembled the ceiling light.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai was right. Katei had the key, and he used it while we were in the attic.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...Yeah.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I'm not sure why he'd hide the Sekimeiya, though.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I don't think it makes any sense. He would've had better places to hide it, like his locker.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: You think so? We could force him to open it at any time, and it would be easily found after the exit opens.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Atsuki crouched next to the Sekimeiya and stared at it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Are you gonna use it?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: We don't know how long it's been here for, so it might not be a good idea.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: What do you mean?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Well, if the time you travel depends on how long it spends out of the cabinet, you could go really far back.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Oh... Hm, I see.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Once again, he went quiet. I had no idea what he was thinking, but I knew I didn't like it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai had warned me not to let Atsuki get his hands on the Sekimeiya, and I had no idea why. All I knew was that he was keeping some of his thoughts to himself, and I suspected he'd lied to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He was concocting something—that I was sure of. Not only because I knew him, he'd outright admitted it to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: For once, the silence wasn't entirely pure. The mechanical room's noise was pervasive. Minutes after staring at the gemstone, Atsuki's hand hovered over it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What are you doing?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: It's hot, the air around it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh, that's weird.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: When I touched it earlier, I felt a zap for an instant before I teleported. I have no idea how, but it heated up really fast. When I was holding the cushion from below, it went from cold to hot in a minute.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I didn't know how to answer, but the bizarre situation sunk in even further. What the hell was the Sekimeiya, and what was it doing with us?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you going to use it to change the past?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I don't know.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: That answer reinforced everything I'd been feeling. He couldn't not know. He knew exactly what his goal was, and I did too. So why was he acting so reserved?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But he didn't flesh out his answer, opting to resume his silence. Even though I couldn't see his face, his slow breathing told me all I needed to know.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I might've pushed the issue further if something hadn't hit me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When he teleported...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: After mentioning the time he'd touched the Sekimeiya, a glaring contradiction that I'd previously ignored reared its head.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You traveled to the attic, right?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He's lying.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There's no way he traveled to the attic. Did he not realize that it doesn't make sense?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: He said he traveled twenty minutes to the past. At that point, all of us were in the attic as well.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That's fine depending on where he appeared. It's not like he erased his past self, right? So if he appeared in one of the rooms after they'd been investigated, we wouldn't have seen him.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But there's a big problem.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Where in the attic did you appear?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Hm? In the kitchen, and I'm pretty sure that's because I went there before we left. It's something I was trying to figure out earlier.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Ah...
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: No, he's lying.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The only part of the attic where he could've appeared is the staircase at the entrance.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Every other place doesn't make sense. When we searched the whole floor, we made sure nobody could sneak past us. Katei waited in the corner of the hallway and Akaro in the living room.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: As Erina said, twenty minutes before the time he traveled, all of us were still in the attic and were about to leave. Atsuki, who had traveled, didn't deny that.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: According to him, he appeared in the kitchen and then we left. That's not right.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: For some reason, the elevator started functioning again, and Sai called it. Then he, Akaro, Erina, and Isla went to the crystal floor with it. However, Katei, Atsuki, and I left through the main door and locked it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Atsuki, after appearing in the kitchen, would not have been able to leave the attic.{w} He couldn't have left through the staircase before us, because there were no footprints that started from the kitchen.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When we left, we locked the main door, but most importantly, we learned that when the three of us arrived at the crystal floor, Katei saw the door of the elevator slightly open.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: How does he not understand that what he's saying is impossible? The elevator remained open on the crystal floor until a time after he'd already reunited with us. If he was in the attic, he couldn't have called it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It just doesn't work. When we were in the security room, the elevator was still open, and it had to be either Sai or Naomi who finally closed it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Could it be that it wasn't the group of four who left the door open? ...Is it possible Atsuki used the elevator immediately after them, and it was actually him who didn't close it properly?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I don't think he would've had enough time to call it back and go all the way down. ...And it's very unlikely the others wouldn't have seen him. It's even possible we would've heard the elevator going up and down from the offices.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So, how did he leave the attic?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It's not possible. He couldn't have. Both methods were unavailable.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The only way would've been with the key that I have. Even if he somehow got out, maybe by Naomi unlocking the door, he should've mentioned that it was unlocked when it wasn't supposed to be. He's definitely lying.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I became aware of the smell surrounding me, the one which almost seamlessly blended in. Its cold sensation had persisted in my nostrils since the first time we'd encountered it, so it hadn't immediately evident that it had strengthened again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...All right, I'll touch it. There's one thing I absolutely have to confirm.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: And what is that?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Whether or not the past can be changed.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...You think it can't?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I don't know; I wasn't able to change anything the last time. I have no idea how this will work.{w} I'll disappear from this room and appear somewhere else. If I try to change what I experienced, I don't know how the universe will react. Perhaps you won't notice any difference and I'll branch the world. Maybe this reality will instantly morph into the one I'm making.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Despite how ridiculous he sounded, all he was really saying was that he was about to leave me there. That maybe I'd stay in the world he'd disappeared from while he went on to find his better reality.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was annoying, and given everything else going on in my head, I simply shrugged. He would leave me behind with the Sekimeiya, which would be a great chance to fulfill Sai's request.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I was going to say that if the past can't be changed, I'll be above the stairs after I disappear, but there's no way that'll be the case. If I was there right now, I'd try to make a loud noise to change the past, so I have no clue what's about to happen.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He didn't talk about it further. Finally, the hand that'd been teasing contact for so long dropped to touch the shining gem. Instantly, Atsuki's outline disappeared.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Ten Interloping Eyes
Wh—!
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: And with it, the darkness disappeared as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I almost fell in place. Before I could crouch to grab the Sekimeiya, the door to the lobby was in front of me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was in hallway A. While the illumination was poor, it wasn't comparable to the mechanical room, mostly thanks to the light coming from the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had teleported; nothing else could've happened. I took one step forward and confirmed that my legs still worked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A voice came from over my shoulders. I turned around and saw Atsuki, who'd stiffened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: D-Did I just appear out of nowhere?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What...? No, that's what happened to me.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: ...Wait.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Were you just in the mechanical room?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Yes... I touched the Sekimeiya a second ago.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I showed up here as soon as you did that. Are we in the past...?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: ...{w}It teleported you as well? How come that didn't happen the other times?{w} And both of us appeared here...
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Hey! What the fuck...!? Where have you two been!?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai emerged from the event room. Behind him was Erina, who looked surprised to see us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Has anything happened?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What...!? You've been gone for over two hours! Answer the question!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Atsuki appeared wary, perhaps because Sai might have overheard what we'd been talking about.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We entered the event room. Isla was with them, and she looked a little sad, standing next to the cabinet with its empty interior exposed. The Sekimeiya was probably still in the mechanical room at that moment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We didn't get any sleep last night, so we were really tired and went to the attic. We woke up a few minutes ago.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What the fuck? You were sleeping? Why didn't you say anything!?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Because Katei wouldn't have let us.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...Excuse me?{w} Was Katei not with you?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What? No, he wasn't. We went alone.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Where is he, then? We haven't seen him either, not for a long time.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He wasn't with us.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: We thought the three of you were in the attic, which we couldn't enter.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It was just the two of us.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...{w}What the fuck, then!?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You don't have any idea where he went?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Well, we thought you three were locked up there, so we didn't search everywhere. We even thought Naomi could have been with you since she's still missing.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What about Akaro? Where is he?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: No idea, but I saw him not too long ago. He's been here the whole time.{w} Do you still have the key to the attic?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: ...I see. That's good.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Hold on. What happened to the Sekimeiya? Why is it not here?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We have no idea. We thought one of you came down to pick it up and brought it to the attic. The cabinet was locked, and none of us had the key to unlock it. If you two didn't take it out, Katei or Naomi must have another key.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's been gone from the cabinet for a while, but Akaro and I searched this floor and found it in a drawer in the lobby.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We put it back in here, and about twenty minutes ago, we realized it had been taken out again. Again, Katei or Naomi did that if it wasn't one of you.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}Oh, right, what time is it?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He showed us his wristwatch. Immediately, Atsuki turned to face me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew why. At that moment, we had just walked down the stairs to the mechanical room. We'd been down there for a while, and then we had appeared in hallway A during the time we'd been in the security room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki wanted to change the past, and he had the chance to do so. I doubted that he wanted to be seen by his past self, but making a loud noise would serve as a confirmation that the possibility existed. If nothing else, I'd be able to witness it too thanks to traveling with him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, it was at that moment that a sound reached our ears.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As we glanced at the hallway A door, the sound got louder. It didn't take much time for the door to open, revealing Akaro on the other side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everyone present was surprised at the same time.{w} While Akaro hadn't expected to see me and Atsuki, we hadn't expected to see who he was with either.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At his side was Katei, who had supposedly been missing for quite some time. He stared at us hesitantly, evidently anticipating our reaction.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...H-Hey! What the fuck have you been doing!?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Remaining silent, Katei turned to the cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You found them too...?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: They said they were sleeping alone in the attic. ...Katei, what are you waiting for? Where the fuck have you been?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I've been here.{w} *sigh*
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I'm sorry?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I've been here this whole time. I didn't go anywhere.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Wh-What? Do you know how long it's been since we saw you?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm being serious. Do you have any idea how long we've been looking around for you?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's been almost {tip=hours}three hours{/tip}, I know. I couldn't have gone anywhere. I just came across Akaro ten minutes ago.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I saw him in hallway C and asked him the same thing. He said he'd been here looking for us. We went to the sixth floor to find you since I'd seen you there earlier and I didn't know where Erina and Isla were.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I looked at Atsuki, who'd been quiet for a while. He was thinking about something, but was it along the lines of everyone showing up meaning that the past couldn't change? It still should've been as simple as going to the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where is the Sekimeiya? And did I hear that you two were sleeping in the attic...? Did I not tell you—
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Shut up. What the fuck did that even mean?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You said that it's almost been three hours since we saw you. How the fuck do you even know that?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What? I answered your question.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: "Almost three hours" is awfully precise, and it's correct. If you truly were here, and for some reason didn't see anyone for three hours, would your sense of time be good enough to know that?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you doing this again...? Trying to blame me for anything you can?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You're a fucking liar! You haven't been here for hours! Where the fuck were you, and why are you back? The computer doesn't work, and I'm the only one with a watch. How did you accurately say that you've been gone for three hours!?{w} Hey, did Naomi have a watch? Does anyone remember?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The three members of the first group shrugged. Atsuki and I knew there was still a way to use the computer to know the time, but I didn't even get the chance to consider if we should mention it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh...! Did you hear that!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Hear what?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Didn't a sound come from the lobby?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I didn't hear anything.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Nobody had. Probably not even Atsuki, who took no time to exit the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Our past selves still had to be in the mechanical room. If the past couldn't be changed, it meant that something would always prevent him from proceeding, but the arrival of Katei and Akaro hadn't conclusively proven it. Confused, the rest of us followed behind him and saw him opening the door to the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once he opened that door, he didn't take even a step forward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Instead, he froze in place, and as he stopped gripping the knob, he turned his head back to us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who...{w} is this?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We dashed to the door.{w} ...When we looked through it, we immediately realized that wasn't the only question to ask.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Ah! Isla, stay over there!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: A single body lay down on the floor over a vast pool of blood.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no meaning to be found. No smell of blood, no identity of the corpse, but a death that defied reason. Furthermore, the past had changed. Not because of the appearance of a body, but because of Erina's yell, which had spread throughout the crystal floor—a yell we hadn't heard while we'd been downstairs.{w} I immediately understood that someone had been killed. I'd gone over the concept of death many times in my mind, so I simply stared at that dreamlike scene before I was pushed aside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isn't he...!?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The shock had paralyzed everyone, and Katei was the first to snap out of it. He ran toward the body and turned it around, trying not to step on all the blood around it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, I recognize him too. Wasn't he there?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai pointed at the shutter, prompting me to remember that I also knew the man, who was dressed in a police uniform.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Y-Yes... That's where I s-saw him, while we were waiting. Fuck.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Atsuki's voice cracked. He wouldn't take his eyes off the body.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He's been here at the tower recently. I don't know his name, but he was investigating a possible terrorist attack.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Katei crouched and used two fingers to verify that there was no pulse.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He didn't say it out loud.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is a knife wound.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The uniform on his chest had been pierced a single time, but the knife in question wasn't there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A knife...? How did this person get in? Look at the blood. ...This happened minutes ago.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He entered the same way Katei left.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: You've been missing for the last three hours. Just as you reappear, this person shows up dead. This is no coincidence.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What the hell are you talking about? How would I have left!?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I don't know. You remember the Sekimeiya, right? As you said, it's not in the cabinet right now, and you're an excellent candidate to have taken it out.{w} It's possible this man entered the tower after it was locked down, and if you did so too, your disappearance, your knowledge of the time, and this knife you're talking about... would all make sense.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I cannot believe what I'm hearing! I've been here the entire time! And I couldn't have unlocked the cabinet!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Enraged, Katei pulled up the man's shirt and uncovered his waist.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes, look at this! This is why I thought it must've been a knife. It was his own!{w} He still has his baton, but his knife is gone. I personally saw that he had a knife right here a few days ago.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He continued examining his clothes and pockets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Oh! He has a walkie-talkie!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Everyone's eyes widened until we saw Katei pressing every button and showing us its blank display.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is it not working? Let me see.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Katei gave Akaro the device. After fiddling with it for a while, he noticed what was wrong.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...There's a battery missing, and the cover isn't properly attached. There's also a crack here on the bottom, look.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: These work with normal batteries?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Apparently, and this cover can be manually removed. Maybe they failed to break it by force and removed a battery instead.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Are there batteries like these anywhere?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No, I really don't think so...
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: He left the device on the floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So the killer did this to prevent us from talking to people outside once again.{w} I have to assume that you still have not found Naomi, so instead of blaming me, consider that it's very possible this person has been here since we got trapped, and we didn't find him just like we couldn't find Naomi.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Okay, then you killed him?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}Don't say stuff like that. I didn't do this.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Then who did? It seems like it could've been anyone, but your story is by far the most questionable one. Do we really have to keep listening to this Naomi boogeyman schtick?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Stop.{w} Akaro, is what you said earlier true? That you found Katei ten minutes before coming to the event room?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Uh... Yes, I don't know if it really was ten minutes, though.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What time is it right now?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It's unlikely Katei did this, then. Six minutes ago, this hadn't happened yet.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...{w}Is that so? You two were talking in hallway A. Did you look at the lobby? I recall the door was shut.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We did.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He's right.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: At {time=13:17}, we'd walked down to the mechanical room, which meant that the man had died while we'd been under him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...If you're not lying, then forget what I said. Everyone has an alibi, unless two or more people did it.{w} You two were together, Katei and Akaro were together, and me, Erina, and Isla were together.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We looked past the door, where Erina was crouching next to Isla, comforting her from a sight she hadn't seen. Despite that, she was burying her face in her arms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A dour mood had overtaken the entire group. I wasn't sure if it was because they had been exposed to death or because they feared the killer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki's demeanor had changed the least, probably because it didn't have far to go anyway. Regardless, I had to put on the same appearance, and it came naturally after the previous two weeks. The death of that man meant nothing to me, and I was only a little intrigued. I'd always known I'd react like that, and while I knew I couldn't show it, I didn't feel it was necessarily problematic as long as nobody found out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, it was actually Naomi...?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I have no idea how this man entered the tower. It's possible he was here from the beginning, or there could actually be a secret way in. It wouldn't surprise me given the track record this place has. However, he's a police officer, so whoever did this might've killed him just because of that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not sure how they took his knife or how we didn't hear a fight. In fact, I have no clue what happened.{w} None of us have blood on our clothes, which I suppose doesn't mean anything since it doesn't seem like much blood sprayed out, but I'll remind you all again that the Sekimeiya was hidden a while ago. All of us go back to having no alibi when everyone is able to go to the past.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you joking? Do you think one of us will go to the past and kill him?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Well, you said Naomi still has a set of keys identical to yours. Whether or not that's true, we know of someone who does for sure.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Multiple pairs of eyes faced me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I have it. We didn't hide the Sekimeiya, though.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: ...And if we had, we wouldn't have needed it to do this because we're the ones who saw the lobby empty just minutes ago.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: That's right, which forces me to point out the topic you were discussing in hallway A.{w} "I touched the Sekimeiya a second ago." Didn't those words come out of your mouth?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: They did. So you lied; you didn't see the lobby before I heard you since you appeared there from the future.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...You're right, but we did see it before touching the Sekimeiya. It doesn't invalidate what we said.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: You're admitting it, good. Is this travel yet to happen?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I think it just happened. I don't know if anything went differently this time, but we found the Sekimeiya in the mechanical room, so whoever took it hid it there.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Below us...? And you appeared in the hallway...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm confused. You found the Sekimeiya? ...And I don't get how you got to that conclusion, Sai. Atsuki appeared there from the future, so he's the only one who couldn't have been able to look at the lobby before you saw them, right?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: No, both of—
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He stopped himself when he realized he'd made a mistake. His pause was what made Atsuki and me notice it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh...! You know exactly what happened, don't you?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: You overheard our conversation, when we said we had traveled together.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Akaro thought only I appeared in the hallway, but you know both of us did. I touched the Sekimeiya, which made both of us travel at the same time.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: And you were about to say "no, both of them traveled". However, given the knowledge of the Sekimeiya you should have, that shouldn't be possible. After touching it, the Sekimeiya would power off, and it would take a while before anyone could activate it again.{w} Does that mean that you knew that was possible? You haven't explained much about what you did during the time we were in the attic.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...What are you talking about? I was gonna say that both of you traveled together because it's what you two said. I stopped myself when I realized that Akaro was right; it didn't make sense.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...No, I don't think so.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Sai shook his head, disregarding Atsuki's accusation. Then, he walked to the mechanical room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, you two traveled recently, right? Should we just ignore the fact that you avoided telling us the location of the Sekimeiya, if we're to believe you didn't hide it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He didn't wait for an answer before he began to descend the staircase. The door had been left slightly open by the two of us so that the darkness below was at least slightly alleviated.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki shared dubious looks with the others at Sai sidestepping the issue, but there was no choice except waiting for him to return.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You don't think he wanted to use the Sekimeiya, do you?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Atsuki walked to the door, worried about Sai's intentions, but he stopped himself short after a couple steps.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was right. They're lying.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What? We aren't.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Where is the Sekimeiya supposed to be, then?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It was behind the pile of chairs.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Incorrect. There was nothing down there.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you sure?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: You're all free to go see by yourselves.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I knew that couldn't be true. We'd most likely arrived at the lobby before we'd disappeared from the mechanical room, so the Sekimeiya had to still be there. If Sai was so blatantly lying, had he found a way to frame us?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Can you open that hip pack?
