entries.text: We began to put that plan into effect. If one of us was the real culprit, they could purposely leave something, or someone, undiscovered. That was why all of us looked everywhere there was to look—so that everyone could agree with the result in the end.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Since Isla had claimed she'd found the Sekimeiya in one of the wardrobes, it was possible something had gone unseen for a while. We didn't only look for people, but for anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every floor had a place where someone could wait to prevent anyone else from passing. Erina and Isla took that job to make the search valid.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Doing all of it took a while, but on floor 3, the search hadn't gone any differently from the others; we still had zero results.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were in front of the floor 2 offices, ready to move on to the last floor. We expected to be stopped on the way to the staircase, as Isla couldn't be allowed to walk down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And yet our expectations were betrayed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Look at the elevator...!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Next to the elevator, the metallic panel holding the button was properly attached.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, what the fuck...? Weren't all the buttons inside it when we sent it up?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I don't know. Maybe one had been taken out.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: It doesn't matter. Do not press it.{w} Someone is guaranteed to have been on the crystal floor, and their only way out is the storeroom. Just in case, we shouldn't bring the elevator here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Isla, give Akaro the Sekimeiya. It's too dangerous to go down.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: H-Huh...? No.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Sai was the first to walk down while Atsuki looked at both bathrooms. Meanwhile, Isla kept tightening her arms, reluctant to let go of the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla, this is important. You can't go down there.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...It's just to the event room.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Erina, it's fine. You can both come.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wh-What...? Not a chance.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Look, just get down here. Don't argue.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I looked through the door and understood what Sai meant. There was no blood. Not only that, I proceeded down, and there was no body anywhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh my God, this is ridiculous.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Was it all removed?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What, with a mop? Wouldn't stains be visible?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: The elevator button has been reattached here too.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I'll just go to the event room.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Wait...!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Erina dashed ahead of her and opened the door herself.{w} It didn't seem like there was anything inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Whatever, put it in. Nobody can leave this floor without being seen, at least.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Okay.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Wait, it's still here.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Huh... Really?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Atsuki had uncovered the cabinet, and the truth was plain to see: the Sekimeiya was still on its cushion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh...! There are two of them!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Isla rapidly unwrapped the sheet to prove that she hadn't lied.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hang on, it's not here. The thread I left.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It's not here...! The Sekimeiya!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Isla desperately looked all through the sheet, but the Sekimeiya wasn't there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I promise I didn't lie! I had it here!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Atsuki crouched and felt the cloth.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Y-You didn't lie...! It's burning.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yeah. It started to feel hot on the fourth floor.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: You felt it when the Sekimeiya was in the center...? I'll bet it was extremely hot, then. Also, the cabinet is still locked.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I-Is this what you're implying? That it was taken out of the cabinet since the thread is gone and then brought to the attic? Then, at some point, it teleported inside again?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'm not implying anything, but that's what could've happened.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: That doesn't make sense.{w} It really doesn't—the cabinet is locked. That would mean that whoever took the Sekimeiya out locked the cabinet while it was empty.{w} I have another idea. Let me take the Sekimeiya. Akaro and Katei, you watch the stairs.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Because the last time it wasn't working, remember? I can test if it is now without activating it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Okay.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Is that really okay? We came here to leave it where it's safe.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: We need to understand what's happening. It must be done.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: After all that time, I still had the keyring, so I took it out and unlocked the cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai grabbed the Sekimeiya with his sleeves, causing the curtain to fall, and put it in the middle of the sheet. He then closed the glass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was very cold, so let's see if that changes.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He wrapped it around with one layer of the cloth and waited a few seconds with his hand over it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It is getting hot—definitely.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: When Atsuki tried it, he agreed as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All right, I'm sure there's someone on this floor. Don't take your eyes off the stairs. I'm not sure we'll find them, though.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why do you say that?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The last time, the Sekimeiya disappeared from my hands when I walked to the event room, and this time, it disappeared from within the sheet when we were walking to the event room. Could it be related to that?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Back then, you said it was burning and you could hardly hold it. Is it possible it teleports when it gets too hot?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: And the next time we found it, it wasn't working. It could be that...
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It's working now, but we can test it. If the outer layer of the sheet felt hot for Isla, it's possible that it making the sheet hot made it heat up even more quickly.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai wrapped the Sekimeiya up completely once again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Like this, I can't easily tell if the Sekimeiya's still in here or not.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We waited a bit, but ultimately, to know if it had disappeared, the ball would have to be unwrapped.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You remember when it disappeared the last time, right? Immediately after that, our footprints vanished from the attic...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I suppose I can try leaving and entering this room, if that's what's doing it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He picked up the sheet and went in and out of the door a couple times.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It seems that if it disappears, it appears somewhere close by. It might be impossible to understand what it's doing, though, and we can at least keep it locked up if we have it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...There's no way I'm no longer holding it, right? It must still be in the center of the sheet. Let's just finish the search.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai dropped the ball on the floor of hallway A, where he could view the staircase as well. He grabbed one edge of the sheet and began to unroll it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I think it's still he—
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The sheet disappeared.{w} Between Sai's hands, not only had the sheet vanished, but also the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It did happen again...
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I was able to see that the Sekimeiya was there. It disappeared when Sai touched it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: But why is the sheet gone too...?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I couldn't touch it anymore because of how hot it was. That could be why it also disappeared—Isla was touching it when the Sekimeiya teleported the previous time.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: She couldn't have touched the Sekimeiya itself, though.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Wh—!{w} Oh my God, I almost had a heart attack!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The door! It fucking closed!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai stood up rapidly and opened the event room, but he didn't see anyone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It didn't make a sound. ...Was it the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Sai uncovered the cabinet's curtain, but that time, it was empty and still unlocked. I noticed that the hallway B door was slightly open—I thought that had changed too.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is going way beyond me. If there's someone on this floor, let's just fucking find them.{w} I have no idea if we were right. Maybe if the Sekimeiya overheats, it teleports away, but only this time it happened when it was touched.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai went straight to the storeroom and came back with the information we needed to know the most.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It hasn't been opened again.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That made everyone even tenser. The chance to find the culprit was closer than ever.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Fuck... Let's hurry. The Sekimeiya might've appeared on this floor.{w} I didn't think this through. If someone's actually here, there's a chance it'll allow them to escape.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Like before, while Erina and Isla stayed outside, all of us went to inspect every individual room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was first to enter room A1. Within one of the cabinets, I found the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hesitated a little, but I had no reason to keep it to myself anymore, and it was going to be found anyway. I made sure not to touch it directly and brought it to the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You found it? Thank God.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Was it inside a cabinet again?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: It's not locked anymore.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We faced Sai and saw he'd opened the security room. When most of us ran in, we were met with the many powered-off screens.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai pressed the computer's power button, and it started up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, right after that, it automatically shut down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell? Is some piece of hardware not being detected?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Hey! Come to the lobby...!
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Akaro's strained voice made us abandon the computer. Behind the door to the lobby, déjà vu was what awaited us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She's gone...! Again...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Now two bodies have disappeared, and both of them were definitely dead. If they're not on this floor, I'm just lost.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wait, no. I'm so stupid...
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What have you done?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I know it looks like she vanished, but I think there's more to it.{w} Naomi and the policeman are still here, but do you remember when I brought both bodies to the lobby? I don't think the policeman was here.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...Excuse me?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I think... I just placed them near the door and hardly paid attention. I think I didn't realize the policeman had disappeared. I remember this part of the floor being completely empty for the second I looked at it.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We could hardly be surprised anymore, and there was very little reason to doubt Akaro.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, the policeman disappeared and reappeared...? Let's make sure we can't find the other bodies before I go insane.{w} ...Oh wait, look at Naomi's head.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: From the wound she had, quite a bit of blood was pouring out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes, more blood is coming out than before.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: And it seems like it started just now, right? Otherwise, the pool on the floor would be much bigger.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You're right...
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Erina had kept Isla close to hallway C so that she wouldn't go near the lobby. Hammered by a thousand new questions, we confirmed there was nothing in the room below us. Afterward, I had something to say.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya isn't getting hotter yet. That's not normal, right?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Oh, is it not working again?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai felt my sleeve and confirmed that it wasn't hot at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's just like before. After teleporting, it doesn't work.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...Right.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We'll just leave it in the cabinet. We only have hallway B left.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Knowing that thinking about anything would be useless until every room was searched, we entered hallway B. There, the same procedure started.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We moved in coordination from room to room, looking at every cabinet along the way. Rapidly, the number of remaining places decreased as we approached the bathrooms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Finally, there were none left. In no location had there been a person or either of the bodies that had vanished. In addition, according to Sai, the storeroom door hadn't opened again. The answer, no matter what it was, must've hinged on the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...There's nothing else we can do. Even if there really is someone with us, they know how to not be found. It's very clear that whatever's been happening here is way over our heads.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Sai felt my sleeve again. Failing to notice any heat, he touched the Sekimeiya, and nothing happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't touch it again. Our priority at this point is just to make it out of here safely.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: There was really no rebuttal to that. Since we'd been unable to figure anything out, a sensation lingered: if we truly were up against a real culprit, we were no match for them. And supposing multiple people had died due to being threats to that person, our single goal was not to become a threat ourselves.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We had just performed a perfect search. There was no room for anyone to be hiding, and as a result, there was absolutely nothing more we could do to fight back. We had to resign ourselves to passing the time and nothing more.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to Erina and Isla was the elevator. We walked to it, following Sai.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The elevator was in the attic when we left, but I didn't count on the buttons getting reattached. I can think of one escape route.{w} We saw that the call button was there on the second floor. When we were inspecting the offices, perhaps they called the elevator. If it came from the attic, we wouldn't have heard it since we were on the same floor as the elevator.{w} Similarly, if they immediately took it to escape to another floor, we wouldn't have heard that either.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: N-No, that couldn't have happened.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: No? What do you mean?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Someone was always watching the stairs and elevator since we came to the crystal floor, right?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: So look. The elevator is open.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Wh-What?{w} You're... right.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The door wasn't properly closed; a tiny gap was keeping it open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's nothing. All the buttons are gone. Even the blood is.{w} But I see what you mean. The elevator had to be here with the door open since we arrived, so if the culprit took it on the second floor, they got off here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...This doesn't make any sense. How did the elevator get here? If it came before us, we would've heard it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yeah, I can only think of the way I said. When we were on the second floor, our mystery person called it, which was imperceptible for us. They brought it here, left with all the panels, and kept the door open. ...That's the only thing that makes any sense, but it still doesn't explain how the hell they managed to not be found.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I guess there's one way.{w} The Sekimeiya disappeared from the sheet Isla was carrying, right? And we found it inside the cabinet in the event room.{w} Even if the killer was here, they couldn't have escaped with the Sekimeiya because they would've left the cabinet glass open. I guess it's possible they found it somewhere else, and it teleported to the cabinet after they touched it. That's all I can think.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Our conclusion didn't change. There was absolutely nothing we could do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We placed the Sekimeiya in the cabinet and locked it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Afterward...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had the chance to go to the security room and saw Atsuki was already there. The time displayed on the BIOS was {time=15:45}, which was five minutes after locking up the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei was drawn in by the open door when the computer had already been shut down. He said he wanted to get to the bottom of the issue, so we left him behind, working in his room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Despite Erina saying that she and Isla would go back to the attic after we finished searching, they were still on the crystal floor. Two corpses had disappeared, and the search indicated that one of us was likely the culprit, so Erina had no problem accepting Isla's request to stay in room A1.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It finally began to feel like our goal was waiting for the exit to unlock. For many minutes, nothing happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai and Akaro were in the lobby, avoiding the sight of the blood flowing out of Naomi's head. Atsuki sat on the staircase in hallway C.{w} ...I roamed around the floor a couple of times, and none of those positions changed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There were five hours left until {time=21}, and I'd never been good at waiting around. It didn't seem like anyone had more business with the Sekimeiya or any interest in continuing to argue. While that was the ideal scenario, having to simply wait began to stress me out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Over the span of an hour, I was the only person wandering around. Nobody said anything to me as they waited patiently.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My body started to severely reject the repetitive colors of the walls, and going over all the gems had only been entertaining for so long. I walked to the staircase, where Atsuki was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Apparently, he was there to keep an eye on the storeroom so that nobody could enter the building. Before I could say anything, he asked me to briefly take over for him as he attempted to use the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Silently, we unlocked the cabinet, but it didn't seem like the Sekimeiya had started working.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm going to the attic.
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I didn't think anyone had left the crystal floor in a while, and even though staying with the rest was safer, we'd confirmed every floor was empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...But it didn't make any sense. Who had removed the bodies? Who had messed with the elevator buttons? Who had opened the storeroom door?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki sounded hesitant at first, but he dropped it quickly. The tiredness was kicking in, and I missed letting the time pass on a bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked at the elevator, which I still found unsettling, and opened the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was empty. There was nobody inside. No buttons, and no blood either...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked up instead. As I ascended the floors, the thought strengthened: what were we doing? Someone else was with us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The button had been attached on the third floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...And on the fourth, on the fifth, on the sixth... I arrived at the attic door and noticed that the key was no longer inserted into the keyhole.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I turned the doorknob and opened the door slowly. It was still unlocked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I fixed my eyes on the floor of the living room. Our footprints were faded, and it didn't seem like anyone had been there recently.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to the elevator was a metallic panel with its button, exactly where it was designed to be. It only made my head feel more numb. Had someone really reattached all of them when we hadn't been looking?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I approached both bedrooms. Even though I couldn't sense anyone around, I wasn't going to look.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened the left door and sat on the bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no way I could feel comfortable. The uneasiness immobilized me for a long time until I was able to lie down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had my purse next to me, and that time, I shut the light off. That finally allowed me to close my eyes and hope that the next time I opened them, I could walk out of the tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't realize I'd fallen asleep, but a noise caused me to wake up. Once I regained my senses, I sharpened them to try to distinguish what I'd heard, but nothing else reached me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The situation repeated. I felt like I'd blinked in and out of existence, but the sound that woke me the second time was louder.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to me, the door opened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then the light came on. I had my face under the sheet, facing the wall. With no strength to react, I waited.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Are you awake?"{w} It was Atsuki's voice.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't want to reply, so I kept quiet, figuring that if he had something important to say, he'd try to wake me up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Instead, the light turned back off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Soon, so did I.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The faintest sounds kept waking me up. They had started coming from above me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Someone had gone up the ladder.{w} I tried not to mind it and keep sleeping.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, I felt almost rested, as if I'd slept for hours. Minutes after failing to sleep again, I stretched my limbs and yawned deeply.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was very dark, but my purse was still on the bed. I grabbed it, slowly sat up, and then stood.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had no sense of space, but it wasn't unpleasant. It couldn't be too late in the day either—it was likely Atsuki or someone would come get me before the deadline, and Katei probably wouldn't be a fan of Ashiya entering the tower and finding someone sleeping in the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Pond
Out of nowhere, the light turned on. I found myself standing in the middle of the room, alone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Did you do that? Are you Atsuki?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I looked at the ceiling, figuring someone above me had flipped the switch, but there was no response.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Instead, a petrifying yell came from the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...oor! ...re you!?
entries.speaker: q

entries.text: I stared at the closed door before slowly approaching, wondering if I was losing it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I turned the handle gently and peered into the hallway. The voice was coming from in front of me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I just heard you! Please, open the door!
entries.speaker: q

entries.text: ...How is this possible? It's her again.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I wasn't taken aback anymore or even afraid. I just wanted out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Between the two bedrooms, I wondered if I was being consciously punished. That couldn't be.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But as much as I despised it, it was reality. Once again, the obvious laws of the world were being flagrantly defied.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...You're still here, right? What are you planning?
entries.speaker: q

entries.text: Was she actually talking to me? I had no idea.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While I wanted to know what was happening, I knew I wouldn't try to open the door. Instead, concealing my presence as much as possible, I stepped back to the living room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I know you're here! At least answer!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I couldn't tell anymore if she was still yelling. I looked down and saw recent footprints going from the hallway to the staircase.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I gripped the handle and tried to open the door.{w} It was locked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: From my purse, I took the keys out and got the door to open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the other side, I inserted the key into the keyhole again and rotated it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know whether to keep going forward. The sixth floor felt desolate, and I had no objective. Perhaps not trying to find out what was happening was smarter.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, someone had been above me in the bedroom, and they hadn't answered my question. That was what made me keep walking away from the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked down the next staircase as the echo of my own footsteps accompanied me. If people were still waiting in the lobby, I could stay there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hardly felt like I was alive as I descended the mirrored floors; the entire sequence of events felt like nothing more than a dream. I trudged through all of them until a gray door was in front of me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki was no longer sitting on the lowest step behind it. Instead, there was a trail of fresh blood.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The floor had a strange smell to it. It could've been the same one we'd smelled throughout the day, but I didn't think that was all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Cautiously, I walked to the lobby. The blood I'd seen shouldn't have been enough to cause someone to die, but there was an imposing, foreboding atmosphere permeating the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Nobody.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The two bodies had disappeared with almost all the blood, and only the shutter remained. Partially unable to believe it, I took timid steps toward the center of the lobby, where I saw that its emptiness was absolute.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I opened the hallway B door, the sensation was identical. Was it possible I was alone?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The urge to find someone increased. I didn't want to go back to the attic despite knowing it was inhabited. I tried to uncoil my tightly wound muscles and opened my mouth.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Hey! Is anyone there...!?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: I received no answer, but one of the open doors grabbed my attention. It was the staff room's.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It stood out, as it was very slightly open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I approached it, but once inside, I wasn't sure it'd been the right call.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood still and smelled the air. It was somehow fairly strong, but it wasn't a particular smell anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Something Atsuki had said came to mind. One of the keys I had could belong to Naomi's locker. We hadn't tried that yet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If he was right, the possibility that a phone could be found was nonzero. I looked at the keys on my palm and figured the smallest one could fit in the lockers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I inserted it into the first one and tried to turn it. However, the whole locker shook, refusing to open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, a metallic sound rang out right in front of me. Something had hit the locker from the inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked up and saw three slits in the door. Despite the darkness that should've existed behind them, I discerned a glow.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It could only have been one thing. Despite being filled with questions, my mind was blank. My hand was drawn to the shape that had begun to take form behind the dark lines, and through the narrow space, I made contact, hoping with all my might that I would be brought to the awaited time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, hallway A was my next sight.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {w=1.0}Then, I fell to the floor immediately after appearing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Disoriented and confused, I stood back up. I had no way to know how far I'd been sent.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It mustn't have been too long; the hallway looked just as desolate as before. I walked ahead and opened the security room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: An unexpected realization hit me instantly. Katei was dead—the stench of his blood had been secluded within the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It seemed he had managed to get the computer back to work, its buzzing adding to the surrealness. I approached cautiously, trying not to breathe.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I pressed a key, the three screens lit up, and on the middle one, I saw a message.{w} "{time=10:04}: Camera(s) disabled and associated footage erased".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...At {time=10:04}, the recordings were erased...?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The screen also showed the time: {time=18:21.} Directly below it was Katei's head—the epicenter of all the blood. It was beyond doubt that he had been killed as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I recalled the person above me, in the bedroom. Who was that, and what had happened while I was asleep?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I left the room behind. From far away, I noticed that the blood I'd seen on the staircase wasn't there yet. Slowly, I directed myself to one of the closed doors in the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Wait, that...?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: High up, something caught my attention. Through the smoke, a circular, intermittent green light could be seen on one of the cameras. I spun in place and saw that many of them had it. I remembered that the last time I'd seen that light was very early in the morning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The computer. It reenabled the cameras. This really must mean that they weren't recording until now, right...?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Hopeful, I entered one of the rooms. There was something else I had to see.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The cabinet was covered by its curtain. If the Sekimeiya was behind it, it was possible someone else was soon to be on the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It wasn't. The cabinet was completely empty. I let go of the curtain and stepped back, startled.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Just next to my feet, I'd noticed there was a bit of blood. That made four places I'd seen some.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd run away from the attic, but even if I wanted to go back, it was no guarantee anyone would be there at the moment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hallway B was still empty, but I understood my situation. Any room could've been hiding a new death.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Now the staff room is closed, unlike many others... Is someone going to enter it soon?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I moved to the center of the hallway, dwarfed by its overwhelming walls. There, I felt genuinely scared for my life. Had I avoided being a target by going to the attic?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Unable to decide on whether to go back up, I remained paralyzed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Who are you?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: E-Erina...! You scared me. Wh-What's with all that blood?{w} Wait, who am I? {tip=miiya}A-Are you...?{/tip}
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: Who... are you? I don't think I've seen you before. How did you get here?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I don't know what that means...! I'm Miiya, I've been here the whole time! Do you not remember?
entries.speaker: c2s

entries.text: M-Miiya...?{w} My head hurts a lot... I don't remember you.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What happened? Did you get hurt? Where are the others?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: I got hit in the head, yes. And I don't know. I-I haven't seen anyone in a long time.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: How did you get hit? You're covered in blood.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: I don't know... I was knocked out from behind.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What...? What happened to the bodies?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Naomi and the policeman. Did they disappear?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Naomi...? No, the first one's there.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: There? Why?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: I approached the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the floor, two curtains lay, one covering Naomi's body.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: See...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Why was she brought here?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: What? Hasn't she been here since she died?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No. We brought her to the lobby. Do you really not remember?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: What about the policeman?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Wh... What policeman?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: She was definitely not mentally stable. The hit she'd suffered had clearly been grave, and going off the blood, it was likely she only survived due to luck. However, something told me that wasn't it. The dried-up blood on her... Could she have been the body that had disappeared?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stared at her and forced that thought out of my mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked around the room, figuring there wasn't much to learn from Erina. However, someone had tried to kill her, so my worries had been warranted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I saw the camera, I realized that the green light wasn't there despite the lack of smoke. Then, my attention was grabbed by a temperature regulation wheel next to a cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why's that broken...?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Hm? Oh, yeah... I think that's how we found it.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I walked over to it, frowning. How could the wheel have broken? It had been undamaged earlier.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The temperature was set to 0 °C. I grabbed the bottom of the lid and tried to lift it up. It was locked, so I had to unlock it the way I'd seen it done the last time we'd all searched.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, what...? It's the Sekimeiya. ...And the cabinet is super cold.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: The Seki... But we already took it out...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I don't understand you.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: It needs to be put in the cabinet. It could get damaged.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Oh, y-yes.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: I reached into the cabinet and picked up the Sekimeiya up without directly touching it.{w} It was considerably cold. I didn't think that touching it would send me far through time, but as it could've made me stay trapped in the building for longer, I decided I wouldn't do it again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Why are you holding it like that?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Do you not remember that either?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...{w}Oh, right...! It can send you to the past.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...Yes.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: I left to hallway B, unsettled by Erina's attitude, a part of me wondering if she was trying to deceive me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Have you gone to the past?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What? Y-Yes. I guess you really don't remember.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...I left the Sekimeiya in the cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What did you do after?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What does that mean?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Did you change the past?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: To some degree. Why are you asking this?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Then, this is how...!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: When was the last time you saw the others?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...I don't remember.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...Oh, in the attic, I think. I haven't gone back.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Why not? What about Isla?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...I was with her until just now.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What? That's not what you said before.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: No...? I didn't say anything about her.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: You said you hadn't seen anyone in a while.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: O-Oh, I guess so. I didn't include her...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Why not? Where did you see her?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: She's still in the same room.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What room?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: We entered hallway A, and Erina brought me to the farthest crystal room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the center of the smoke-stained walls, one of the cabinets was open. Within it, Isla rested, with a pale and somewhat peaceful expression.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: W-Wait, she's...?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: I-I knew it. You weren't here all this time. It wasn't me.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Of course I've been here! What happened to her?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Can't you see it? She was... killed. Was it you? You could have done it if it's true that you were here...!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I don't know what you're talking about. Tell me directly. When did this happen?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: It was... many hours ago. It's been hours...!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...{w}That's not true. You're mistaken. It couldn't have been more than three hours ago.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: N-No... It's been more than that.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: That wasn't right. I let go of the breath I'd been holding and looked at Isla again. It didn't seem like there was any blood around her, but her immobile face and chest were confirmation enough of her death.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina had gone quiet too, and she was making no effort at hiding how much she was trying to focus. However, the thoughts whirling through her head were indecipherable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I waited, thinking she'd have something to say at any moment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was anyone else killed? I saw Katei's body in the security room.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...N-No. I don't think so.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: So, the rest were in the attic. I was utterly confused, but that seemed to be the conclusion. It was possible I was sleeping up there at that moment as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wha—!?{w=0.3} What are you doing!?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: I still feel like I've never seen you before. ...Did you lock the cabinet?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The cabinet...? No, I didn't.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: She had snatched the keys from my purse and was staring at them in her hand.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: These keys... Why do you have them?{w} Is this one for the cabi—
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: With a quick motion, I took them back, and she failed to react.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't get it! What do you—
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...iroya! Hey! Where are you!?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Atsuki...!{w} Did he see her?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I dashed out of the room, paying no mind to Erina's surprise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya! Can you hear me!?
entries.speaker: a4

entries.text: The voice was coming from hallway B. Did that mean she was down there as well?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I rapidly reached the staircase and went up half of the way. From behind the gray door, I saw Erina's feet as she wandered in confusion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: —re okay, ri—!? If yo— ...me, ple— ...thing!
entries.speaker: a4

entries.text: The sound stopped soon after Erina followed it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did that mean that she'd been found, or had Atsuki given up?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I'd noticed earlier, the trail of blood had disappeared from there too. That meant it was still to happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I began to slowly step down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wondered what I'd be told if I showed myself, but it was hard to care about that with how much I wanted to know what the fuck was happening.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina wasn't there anymore. As I approached hallway B, the voices came back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...earing them earlier, were you...?
entries.speaker: aki4

entries.text: Who the hell are you? Or even you... How can you two exist!?
entries.speaker: a4

entries.text: What? ...Does he really not know why she's here?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: They sounded close to the lobby, but I didn't peek in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...not understand? Did— ...pop into existen—
entries.speaker: a4

entries.text: They opened a door. It must've been closer to me, as I started to understand them more easily. Erina was still clearly groggy, but I could make things out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: About Erina, I think what happened isn't what you think.
entries.speaker: s4

entries.text: What's with that tone of voice? When did she even get to know Erina?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Erina even accused me of not being here previously, so why didn't she say that to her too?{w} She's the one who hasn't been here, and earlier, it sounded like she was locked in the attic. Did the person above me do that? And that still has yet to happen...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I'm not sure... I remember I was drawn to this room, and then I think I blacked out.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: That was close to what she'd told me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Are you the same Shiroya who disappeared from the event room with Sai?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I wish I could explain everything to you, but I still don't really know what happened.{w} But, yes. I'm really glad to see you again.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: While I didn't understand Atsuki's question, it was clear something had happened while I was asleep. It all sounded like she was alive and neither of them knew how that had come to occur.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What's with those clothes, then? Why is the cross not on them? Why did you ignore me when we saw each other in the event room and when I kept shouting your name?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...Well, I—
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Hey... I'm still confused, but I have a question.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...Huh?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The Sekimeiya... does it really make you travel through time?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...A girl? You saw Shiroya?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Um...{w} I guess it couldn't have been anyone else.{w} ...It must have been Shiroya.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Erina asked for the Sekimeiya, but it sounded like neither of them knew where it was. However, despite Erina's condition, we had brought it to the event room minutes earlier, so she wasn't satisfied when she was told it wasn't there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's not it at all... Remember that Sai and Akaro took the cabinet key. They probably have the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Their words continued to make no sense. I was the one who had the key.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...They entered the event room. As soon as the door closed, it acted as a barrier for the sound inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once I was certain the hallway was empty, I stepped in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I approached the door and placed my ear against it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't hear anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did they leave?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Finally, I heard a sound coming from the room. The opposite door had opened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...fuck— ...ing here?{w=0.4} ...succ— ...plan of—
entries.speaker: a4

entries.text: This door is too thick to make anything out... It sounds like he's close to the cabinet.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I recognized Sai's voice, but not what he said.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: For as long as I stayed there, I didn't comprehend anything.{w} I knew I could be found out easily, but I wasn't against that. In fact, I considered opening the door, but I would listen from a distance for as long as I could.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I silently entered the staff room. Then, I placed my ear against the left wall, which was directly next to the cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...as that?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Don't mind me, like you said.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It was still hard to hear Sai, but the thin wall made Atsuki's voice interpretable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's just a personal paper. ...nothing to do with you or the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Ve—
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So, did any of you see Miiya...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: There...! Is she gonna say it?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: You don't know her, right? I... I knew I wasn't going insane.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: H-How do you know that name?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: She's the person I was with earlier, before I saw you two... It just came back to me. I don't know where she went, though.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What's with— ...elirious?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's not it. ...not just some name she made up.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Do you kno—
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...We do, but Erina couldn't have seen her. She couldn't be here.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I couldn't process what I was hearing. Was I actually being punished? That insane possibility was only becoming more of a reality.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's not what she means... She's not anywhere right now.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh? ...dead?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Dead...?{w} Are they really talking about me?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: What the fuck is this...? Of course I'm not dead!
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Shut up.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...right? ...saving with— ...kimeiya not—
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai, shut the fuck up. If it was, I promise you that we would've done it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I was right there. I'd been right there the whole time...! What were they talking about!?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know whether I should have entered the room or not. I was a lot more hesitant, and it almost felt as if they knew that I was listening in on them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's probably been— ...minutes already, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...fifteen min—... arrived.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you sure I'll go far enough back?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...I'm going, then. ...you coming with me?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Is she about to touch the Sekimeiya...?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...She said earlier she wanted to save Isla. Did they figure out how to use the Sekimeiya? They've only been there a few minutes...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Was the past going to be changed? That could have already been happening.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was possible that the past had changed drastically while I'd been unconscious. Was I living in a world completely different from the one I'd gone to sleep in?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Wait... what?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Why didn't it work!? Did Sai disappear?{w} Was everything that he said a lie...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I couldn't tell what had happened. Had Sai left, or had he time traveled?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...you ever want me to save Isla? ...you involved in the first place!?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: You're wrong. We don't know how the Sekimeiya works, but this shouldn't have happened...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Had nothing happened...? I'd been completely frozen for minutes, trying to pick up everything I could.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Wait! Where did it go!?{w} It's not here!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It... teleported.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The Sekimeiya... teleported.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It was activated, but they didn't vanish—only the Sekimeiya teleported. That's happened before...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Atsuki, tell me... What do I need to do to travel through time?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Exactly what Sai and I told you. I don't know why it didn't work just now.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: They haven't experienced this before... Is that it?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That idea was the driving force that made me immediately turn around and dash to the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...!{w} It's closed...! I didn't close it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The Sekimeiya had seemingly vanished by itself. I'd just had an epiphany, but instead of trying to think everything through, I opened the door and ran to hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's still no blood here.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And this door...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Dismissing the elevator, I stepped up. There, I ran across the floor, releasing all my built-up energy. As soon as I reached the next staircase, I did the same.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So that nothing would fall out, I held my purse tightly and continued running, planning on reaching the highest place in the building.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't slow down, knowing that if I did, my exhaustion would catch up with me. I bolted up the fourth staircase and continued in a straight line.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Delayed Reflection
Whoa...!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Atsuki...!
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: I stopped abruptly and almost fell down. If Atsuki was there, did that mean that I'd been right?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What happened?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I had to pant hoarsely before I could speak again. Meanwhile, I thought of the question I wanted to ask, realizing he hadn't found my presence strange.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Th-This might sound strange, but... wh-what's the last place where you saw me?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: The last place...? That's what I was gonna say. I saw you weren't sleeping anymore, so I was walking down to see if I could find where you'd gone.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...{w}Then were you above me... in the bedroom?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Oh, yes. Sorry, was I noisy? I just climbed down the ladder and saw you weren't there anymore.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I couldn't believe it. It was him, the Atsuki I'd been with the whole day. However, on the crystal floor, there was another Atsuki—one who had said I couldn't be there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Anyway, what were you in such a rush for? And that question...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...No, I was just going back up. I didn't realize you were in the attic too.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Oh.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...Do you want to go up, then?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes, we can stay there.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Did you see anyone? They were all still waiting when I went to the attic.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I didn't.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: I see.{w} ...It should already be pretty late, but you still have the cabinet key, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yeah.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: We walked up, but my heart hadn't slowed down yet. What kind of mess were we in? No matter the answer, the right call was ignoring it and trying to make the time pass without complications.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And yet I couldn't get the words out of my head. According to the people on the crystal floor, I should've been dead.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Suddenly, a head appeared from around the office corridor. When we looked at each other, the three of us froze, everyone equally shocked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It was Atsuki. A body identical to him, with his face and clothes, who had been waiting by the door to the offices. He looked at himself, speechless, and without moving an inch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey, answer me! You really were here... Are you really me? What the fuck is going on!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: For him, it must've been a surreal shock, but I looked at the bizarre scene with just as much confusion. Were there three versions of Atsuki in the building at once?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Finally, the person in front of us spoke.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I didn't think you'd be here.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: Wh-What!? What does that mean!? You're me, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I am.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: What the fuck is happening, then!? I thought it was impossible that we'd see each other. Was that wrong?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: In a way, yes.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: What the fuck...? Tell me, then! What's going on!? How the fuck can you even exist!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: While I had no idea of how to interpret the scene, it was clear the Atsuki we'd bumped into had a higher understanding of what was happening. It didn't seem he found my existence strange either.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I'm sorry, I'm not sure how to answer that question.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: What...!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I know exactly how you feel, I promise. I will tell you one thing, though, since we've already met: you shouldn't worry about anything.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: I shouldn't worry? There's no way you're actually me, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I am. I promise, it will all be fine.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: Wh-What...? How can you tell? And how would that even be possible!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I know how it sounds, but I genuinely don't have time to explain, and I'm not sure I could.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: What does that even mean...!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Look, we're the same person. Just trust me, or yourself, on this. Sincerely, everything should turn out fine.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: Those words almost broke the person at my side. He'd been told by himself that there was nothing to fear.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You believe me, right? Like I said, I don't have much time.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: Emotional, Atsuki nodded.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But that c-can't be the case...! Shiroya... died again!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Again? What do you mean?
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: Do you not know that? She was killed here, and her body disappeared from the lobby!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The other Atsuki looked confused and deep in thought.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You should believe what I say. I still don't fully understand how that works, but you have to trust me.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: ...You can't explain it? Then there's no way you're actually telling the truth, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I am. While I can't be fully confident about what I'm saying, I'll just ask you to believe me.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: ...{w}Okay.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...Good. I suppose there's one thing you could do, then.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Wait here a second.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: He disappeared from where he'd come after giving me an intense gaze. I was right next to them, but I felt more distant than ever before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Was that a future version of you?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: I-I have no idea.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Then, is that true...? Will Shiroya be all right?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...I don't know. I thought I'd try to use the Sekimeiya a bit later and go a few hours to the past... Th-That wouldn't be enough, but if I managed to keep doing that... That's the only idea I had, but I didn't even know if the Sekimeiya would work again.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I see. ...Whoever that was, we have to put all our faith in him.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...Yeah.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He soon came back running. Between his hands was the Sekimeiya. It seemed like it might've teleported to the attic that time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Take this, but don't touch it.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: Atsuki handed himself the Sekimeiya and received it, hiding his hands under his sleeves.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You two should hurry back down. On the second floor, enter the second partition, leave the Sekimeiya {tip=floor}on the floor{/tip}, and wait there.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: On the second floor?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes. From there, if anyone passes by, you should hear them. If you hear the elevator four times, you can go back down and place the Sekimeiya in its cabinet. Make sure that it isn't activated again.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: However, it's possible that the first time, instead of hearing the elevator, you'll hear someone running up. If that happens, once you hear the elevator two times, you can go down and place the Sekimeiya in the cabinet.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: O-Okay, and... after that, you're saying everything will be fine, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes. Wait patiently with everyone on the crystal floor and make sure to get out safely. I'll pray with you for what will happen after that.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: All... All right.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Atsuki turned around and ran back, putting all his faith in himself. As he did, the second Atsuki pierced me with his eyes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Goodbye, Miiya.
entries.speaker: c2a2

entries.text: In front of me, I saw a look I knew I'd seen before that day. However, he quickly turned it away from me, glancing downward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Goodbye.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Almost in a curious manner, I responded with only one word. Then, I turned around and started sprinting.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki and I ran all the way down until we reached the second floor. Out of breath, he held the door to the offices open, and we entered the second one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He placed the Sekimeiya on the floor as instructed and stepped away from it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's no way this can work—whatever's about to happen...
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Why not?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...He didn't know she had died again. I had the idea that she could be saved by going to the past and hiding her since she wasn't found, but doesn't this mean that she'll end up here and be killed?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Well, whoever that Atsuki was, he knew more than we do, and when you told him we'd found her dead, he still said it would be fine.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: That's true...
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Her body disappeared from the lobby even though we still remember it. Maybe that's what indicates that the past will be changed so she doesn't die here either.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Would it work like this...?{w} It might. The proof that she's dead doesn't exist anymore.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He can't just be a future self of mine; that wouldn't make any sense. ...The way he came to exist might be how he'll try to save Shiroya, but I have no idea what it could be.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I heard a faint, deep sound.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...That's the elevator, right? This is the first time.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yeah. He said that he didn't have much time and was right in saying that the elevator would be used.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: So we have to hear it three more times until we can leave.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The second time came immediately.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Oh. It went through twice because it was called and then used.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Where should the elevator have been?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: It was in the attic the last time I checked, from the time I went there. If that was still the case, someone just went up.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: That must be it. It's just like he said, either the elevator would be used twice or someone would run up.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...So he knew someone would go to the attic, but not how.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: And at some point, it will happen again.{w} We're supposed to hear the elevator two more times. That means it'll end up in the attic again.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...If you're saying that wasn't a future version of you, how is it possible he knew all this?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...{w}I don't know.{w} It doesn't make any sense, does it? The flow of time wouldn't work like that. It's impossible.{w} ...Also, he told us to wait safely and get out of the tower. There's no way I'll be able to use the Sekimeiya once we're outside, and that still wouldn't make any sense. Nothing does.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He's right. But she's on the crystal floor, alongside a third Atsuki. It can't be that the world was changed so that she never died, because that Atsuki was surprised to see her too.{w} One of them was probably who went up to the attic, but what will come out of this? Will different versions of us remain? The other Atsuki didn't make it sound like that.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...I should have been dead. Why?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {tip=dead}{i}I should be dead. Atsuki was right.{/i}{/tip} I should be, but I'm not.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...It can't be they were talking about that, can it?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The answer had to revolve around the Sekimeiya's disappearance. Maybe, whenever that occurred, the changes made were applied to the world.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It had teleported to the attic, so if nothing else happened, the state of the world would stay as it was.{w} But there were so many things to iron out. Three Atsukis existed at once. She had appeared out of nowhere in front of one of them. Not all the disappeared corpses had reappeared alive.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was everything really going to resolve itself if we buried our heads in the sand until we could leave the building?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...And the Sekimeiya was in the attic. Did it teleport there, or did he unlock the cabinet with a key of his own?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I don't know, but I still have the keys. I should probably leave them somewhere before we get out.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...Did we lock the cabinet the last time?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh, you're right. I said I'd go to the attic and we never locked it.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: So he just brought it up.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...In fact, the Sekimeiya had moved twice before. Erina and I had found it in a cabinet in room B4, next to Naomi's moved body. In the future, it was in one of the lockers, and it wasn't Naomi's. We'd never seen which one was Katei's, so it might've been his.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was all tied together. When I'd found the Sekimeiya in the staff room, there had been blood on the crystal floor. When Atsuki had seen that I was no longer sleeping, no yells had come from the opposite bedroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But there was no way to make sense of it. Had the blood on the crystal floor disappeared at the same time as the Sekimeiya? Even if so, it was all far too volatile, and I didn't know what had happened while I was asleep.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A very important question came to mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the bedroom... did you turn on the light?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Oh, yes, sorry. I didn't know you were there.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I mean later, when you were already above.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Hm? No, I didn't. I'm confused by what you mean.{w} I came down, and it seemed like you weren't there because I couldn't hear you. I did turn on the light to confirm it, but you were already gone. Is that what you meant?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...{w}Yes, sorry. I thought someone might have turned it on after you came.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: I don't know. I didn't hear anything.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I see.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: What the hell, then?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I don't even know if turning off the light in the upper bedroom would've turned it off where I was anyway.{w} This doesn't make any sense...!
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I sat on one of the chairs. I couldn't be too frustrated—the outcome had already been guaranteed. We'd soon make it out, and she was probably going to magically revive.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, fuck...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I should leave the keys somewhere before we get out because they'll look at my purse...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And there was one more thing that couldn't be found.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It was fine. I'd just have to flush it down the toilet or something.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I realized the contents of my purse could be seen from where it was on the floor, so I slowly moved it aside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait...{w} ...Is it not here?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I stared at my purse, baffled. Then, I grabbed it and took the keys out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Yeah, I'll leave these somewhere. I'd rather not be asked about why I had them.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: I'm sure it'd be fine anyway.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: {tip=note}It wasn't there.{/tip} In my purse were the keyring, the tickets we'd bought for the event, our identification, and our keys.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was it really taken while I was asleep...?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There's no way.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Wait, no.{w} I bet I know what happened.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It disappeared. That's it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: At some point, it disappeared from my purse and from this world. That's what's been happening. As Atsuki said, in this world, there's no remaining proof that she's dead.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There was nothing else to care about. Knowing that, calmly waiting felt much more doable than before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I remained sitting on that chair, unable to hear anything beyond Atsuki's breathing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was many minutes later when we heard the elevator for the third time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There it is...!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Let's see if we hear it again immediately.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: We did. Just a minute later, the fourth came.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All right, let's go... Hopefully, nobody sees us.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I opened the door, and Atsuki crouched to grab the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How the fuck can it be this hot...!? It hurts to even get my fingers close to it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We heard an unexpected sound.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, what...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We both listened more intently, and I could tell that we were hearing footsteps coming from the staircase leading down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: W-Wait, it should be fine, right...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What the fuck...!? What are you doing here!?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai saw me through the glass. Next to him was Akaro, even though his running hadn't been heard from inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki! Come here! I fucking see the Sekimeiya!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What did you do...? You didn't stop on this floor, right?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Don't be stupid. He has the Sekimeiya. He probably used it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Do you mean that I just took the elevator?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Holy shit, man. Will this attitude stop?{w} Why were you waiting here? You knew we'd go up, right? Was your idea to make us chase you to then touch the Sekimeiya and wait here to sneak back down?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I didn't do any of that.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He probably understood it. Another version of Atsuki had just used the elevator. That was why Sai was accusing him of touching the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, while he probably thought it was the version he'd spoken with, he was unaware of the other one who'd been on the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What now, then? What were you planning to do with that Sekimeiya? As I thought, you're also in on this plan, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Me...?{w} I don't even know what you're talking about.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: Even though fainter, we perceived the same sound. The elevator had just been used.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was the elevator, and I bet I know who that is.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Who...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Atsuki looked a little uncertain. There had been no mention of a fifth elevator sound.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who? The girl who I bet was supposed to meet with you two right now, after you'd made it down from here with the Sekimeiya. It's unfortunate you were too incompetent to handle such a simple plan.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What?{w} I'm being serious. I have absolutely no idea what you're talking about. What girl?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I'm not sure what the idea behind this is, really. Were you actually able to open the storeroom door?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}Answer me. What girl?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: *sigh*
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What even was her name, Akaro?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Hm.{w} ...Shiroya, right?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: The sixth time came. The elevator passed through our floor as Atsuki's eyes widened. He understood it immediately: she was already present.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, fuck... She realized you hadn't come and went back up.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai sprinted toward the third floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait! Stop!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Akaro! Go down and wait in front of the storeroom! It could've been sent empty!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Akaro looked hesitant for a moment, but he followed Sai's order. In an instant, Atsuki and I were alone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell? What do we do?
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...{w}We should put the Sekimeiya in the cabinet and stay on the crystal floor. That's what we were told.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: All right.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: We ran behind Akaro.{w} I looked down and saw that there was still no blood on the floor or the staircase.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...!?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: On the floor, below the elevator panel, there was a folded piece of paper. Atsuki and Akaro were ahead of me, so they didn't see me grabbing it and putting it in my purse.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did it... not disappear after all?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Akaro was in the storeroom, but I just followed behind Atsuki, completely lost for words. How the hell had that made it there?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The event room was empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened the unlocked empty cabinet, and Atsuki left the Sekimeiya inside. That time, he didn't forget to lock it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We left the Sekimeiya in the cabinet.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...We promise we don't know what you were talking about. Why did Sai say that it was Shiroya who'd taken the elevator? That's the... girl who died.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: So you remember now?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Did I not...? Of course I do. She was in the elevator and then disappeared from the lobby.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: That's right, but she was here just minutes ago and said she was going to the attic. That's why Sai believes you're responsible.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: How many minutes ago?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I don't know, quite a few, and you were here too with the Erina who disappeared.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: The Erina who died...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes. She had her clothes caked with dried blood. You two took the elevator up just now.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: So the person who used the elevator the first time was her, and the second time it was Atsuki and Erina.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had met that version of Erina as well, and neither she nor Atsuki were the people we'd been with since that morning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That wasn't me. I'm being serious.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He's right. We've been in the attic all this time and haven't seen anyone.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: That's not easy to believe. You were hiding in the offices with the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It wasn't us who brought the Sekimeiya up. We found it in the attic. We also weren't hiding in the offices, we were searching them before coming back down.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I don't know.{w} I can't just assume you're lying after all that's happened.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...Where are the others?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Well, Katei should be in the security room, and I saw Erina and Isla hadn't left the crystal room they were in.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: While Atsuki opened the door to the security room, I looked at the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi's corpse had returned there, and along with the policeman, they were lying on the floor in solitude. The wound on Naomi's head had stopped bleeding, so the pool below it had reached its limit.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The status of the room had gone back to normal after changing continuously. Was that the version the outside world would see?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked to my right and saw Katei lying back on his chair in front of all the powered-off screens.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, it's you two. It's been a while.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: ...Yes, we just came back from the attic.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He wasn't dead below his desk, and it was clear he'd failed to fix the computer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...How's this going?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I stopped a while ago. I have no idea what the issue is, so I'll need other people to look into it.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: I see.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: When we opened the door in front, we saw the last two people. Isla was not lying face-up inside a dark cabinet, but instead ogling one of the uncovered glass displays.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Hello.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Erina stood up after seeing the two of us. There was no blood on her clothes, and she seemed pretty tired.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did something happen?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Oh, no. We weren't sure if you were still here.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We've been here the whole time.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: That's good. The time is getting closer.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: You said the Erina covered in blood was here too?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes. She and the girl—the two dead bodies that disappeared. For a second, I thought they'd been alive the whole time, but that couldn't be it.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Wait, is that it...? Could it be that they were genuinely brought back to life?{w} But, no... If another version of me existed, it must be something completely different.
entries.speaker: c2a
