entries.text: If that really wasn't you, then I'm really confused. According to him, that girl had been with us the entire day. Since this morning.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: There was absolutely fucking nobody in the attic or anywhere.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Really?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Sai came from the stairs and entered the storeroom, all while I considered how strange that assertion was. Had he simply failed to find the others?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Two different versions of Atsuki, the other Erina, and her too. They all should've been there. Something else still didn't make sense either.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The elevator had been used two more times after the fourth. We knew who had used it the first four times and that everyone who should've been on the crystal floor was present. So, who had taken the final two trips and gone above us?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The door hasn't been opened again. ...Where's the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: In the cabinet.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: In the cabinet? Akaro, don't you understand that their friend could be here? She could've taken it already!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Hey, I did what you said.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Offended, Sai hurried to the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro explained to us what happened. That wasn't me, and we don't want to take it out of here again.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What did he say?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That both of them were sleeping in the attic and found the Sekimeiya there. Then, they came down, searching through every floor until we saw them.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Is that what we're supposed to believe? That the people who have the key to the cabinet conveniently found it where they were, and that instead of hurrying to bring it back, they looked through the entire building with it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...That's what happened.{w} Did you really not find anyone? Aren't you the one who says that I took the elevator up?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes. I'm only one person, though, so I couldn't really search optimally.{w} But it is possible there was nobody to find if the three people who should've been there merely traveled with the Sekimeiya, which, again, you happened to have.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't exactly know what happened, so what is it that you're accusing me of?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...{w}I'm accusing you of trying to execute a plan that might involve getting the Sekimeiya out of the tower. Of lying openly, and of working with that girl you know who didn't get trapped with us.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I'm sorry, but I can't really take you seriously. I woke up a few minutes ago and have no idea what any of this is about. Since Akaro is backing you up, I guess it's true that the two missing bodies reappeared, but it seems they're gone again, right? Erina is with Isla two rooms over, and she looks totally okay.{w} Also, I already said that I don't want to take the Sekimeiya out of here again.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Sai approached Atsuki and touched his sleeves.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was working again, huh? Your shirt is burning.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But we didn't activate it, and we never will.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: However, if it's true that I was here and said things that didn't make sense...{w} You're right, I know that girl, Shiroya. She's an old friend of mine who... died two weeks ago. I don't have any idea why she was here today or how that's possible.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: You just said that the storeroom door hasn't opened again. And the elevator was used two times, right? If it's true that they were here... they must still be. And I can guarantee it because we had the Sekimeiya and didn't use it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: So we have to go find them. You were just one person looking around, so they could have dodged you. All of us together can find them. Then, we'll work out exactly what happened.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Let's go.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...Are you fucking serious?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Now I'm sure. You're spewing an immense amount of bullshit out of that idiotic mouth of yours.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't care how you did it, but you're right: they have to be here because the elevator was used again. I don't care if they traveled to the past or if they just avoided me.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I had a theory ready that entailed Shiroya waiting for the elevator sound on the second floor and activating the Sekimeiya so that you'd all travel. After all, what's most strange is that the Sekimeiya was on the second floor right after you took the elevator up.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: With all the waiting, you probably had a somewhat thought-out plan ready. However, that hardly matters. What matters is that you're not getting the chance to take the Sekimeiya out again.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Did you think we'd all just go looking now? You're not moving from here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: And how will you enforce that?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Don't you think Akaro easily could?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Neither of you are leaving this room. Give me the keys too.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I handed him the keyring, feigning a defeated face.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Whatever the fuck you had planned with that girl won't happen as long as we stay here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai moved to hallway A and went to the storeroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It seems she didn't take the sole chance she had to escape. I'm not letting the storeroom out of my sight again, so the police will definitely catch this person who's supposedly dead.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: At least one of them must be here, between Shiroya and Erina. However, it's probably both, and they're not going to show themselves.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The best thing is that there's no need to search for them. The Sekimeiya is shut in here, so they can't activate it to escape. The storeroom is out of the question too. They're basically trapped.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's currently {time=19:32.} There's no need to search for them, but don't worry—they'll be found as soon as the police enter the building. If you really do want that, you're not opposed, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...!{w} I still think we should find them because I want to understand what happened. If we find them, you'll believe all that I'm saying.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I see. Then we'll go ahead and believe it after {time=21}, when two versions of you are found.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...If that's what you want, I'm fine with that too. I-I suppose we can wait here. There's not that much time left.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Precisely.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I think that's for the best too.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It appeared it had been settled. After a few minutes, I was the first to sit on the floor, leaning on the dirty wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everyone in the room was silently on alert. Eventually, Sai's taunting attitude receded, and he started to look doubtful.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, {time=21} kept approaching at a steady pace, and nobody seemed against that. I wanted to get rid of the note in my purse, but I couldn't go to the bathroom to flush it away. When no one was looking at me, I stuffed it inside one of my shoes. The police would probably search us after we left, so my purse wasn't a good place to hide it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei left the security room and was told we were waiting together. For the last stretch of the day, he entered the dim room with us to maintain our protection of the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No matter what the truth was, our shared distrust was palpable. Anyone could've been lying the entire day. Perhaps, after the police entered, we'd eventually learn all about what the people we'd gotten trapped with had done.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't think anything good could come of it. After all, there was a killer in the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Miiya and Atsuki had been told by another Atsuki that as long as they stayed on the crystal floor, everything should turn out fine.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The mystery behind the people who had gone to the attic... Nobody could be certain what had happened to them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Were they still in the tower? Or had Sai failed to find them because they had vanished?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was possible that they were waiting near the event room. If that was the case, they would be found by the police.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A few of the people in the room had similar thoughts.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Should the less suspicious among them look for the others while everyone else waited in the event room? Given the amount of time left, it sounded risky and unnecessary.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But Miiya kept thinking about one thing.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "I want to search the building again."
"I want to stay in the event room."
Finding Self
As the time kept passing, Miiya's conflict grew.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The Atsuki they'd spoken with had said that if they stayed together on the crystal floor, everything would turn out to be fine.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, did that imply that if they were to scatter through the building, that guarantee would be voided?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Who had taken the last elevator trip? How did that Atsuki plan to accomplish what he'd said? ...Would anyone be found if they were to inspect every floor?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Can't you see already that we weren't lying?" Miiya spoke.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Someone must definitely be here; that's not a question. If you think we want to leave this room empty as we search, someone can just stay here.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Atsuki threw her a frown. They had managed to keep everyone together, so what was with that sudden input?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You didn't listen to me, did you? Neither of you will leave this room until the shutter opens. I'm sure there's a reason why you want us to look for whoever's here, and given what you just said, it might not be related to this room.
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: What would that be? There's no harm in searching as long as someone stays behind. It can be you, if you want.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Atsuki joined in, baiting the same reaction as before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Stop it. We're not leaving. It's very late already, so there's no reason to at all.
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Then I'm going alone.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: What? No, you—
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Miiya didn't give anyone a chance to object. She sprinted toward the hallway A door, and before Akaro had time to react, she ran to the stairs.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What the fuck!? Stop! What the fuck are you doing!?
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Sai's voice didn't reach Miiya, who had disappeared to the second floor. Everyone ran behind her, hesitant to go up, as her goal could've been to lure them away.{w} Meanwhile, Atsuki was lost and began to feel a despicable anxiety building up. Why was Miiya objecting to the only thing they had to do?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "What's happening...?" Erina peeked out of the crystal room after Sai had called the elevator.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Erina! Please, you and Isla stay in the event room! It's very important!
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Atsuki, you stop right here. I have no fucking idea what you're doing, but don't follow her!
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Knowing he was going to be physically stopped, Atsuki ignored Sai and dashed up the stairs. In his mind, he only wanted to stop Miiya and ensure that whatever she was doing didn't prove fatal.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What the fuck...!? You two, follow him! Someone has to take the elevator. I'm doing it since I have the key to the attic.
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: On the second floor, Akaro and Katei found Atsuki inside the partitions. Miiya had made it sound as if she'd wanted to search the whole building, so she could've been anywhere.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki, wait!
entries.speaker: aknn

entries.text: I won't wait...! We have to find her; it's dangerous to be alone. Sai passed us by, so this is going to go quickly.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: It didn't seem like Atsuki was lying. Both Akaro and Katei thought that he genuinely wanted to find Miiya as soon as possible.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If they were to fight over it, and Miiya and Atsuki had something planned, it was possible that fighting itself was what would allow it to succeed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The three of them moved one floor higher with the condition that Atsuki wouldn't be left alone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As long as the elevator wasn't used again, they were fairly certain that Miiya wouldn't be the only person found. They knew that it was very likely someone else was present on one of the floors.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki and Akaro entered the three partitions of the third floor, but they were empty.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The same occurred one floor above.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The fifth and the sixth were desolate as well. It should've been settled, then: there were at least five people in the attic.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Miiya, Sai, Shiroya, another Atsuki, and a mysterious fifth person.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: They approached the door to the attic, but someone came out of it first.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was Miiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When she saw the group, she stopped moving. As the three got closer, they saw there was blood on her forehead.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Wh-What happened...!? Are you okay?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Uh, I don't know.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: You don't know?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Yes. ...I think I might've lost my memory.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Nobody responded. Instead, they waited, wanting to hear that it had been a joke.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But that didn't happen. After a few silent seconds, Miiya lowered her eyebrows.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I'm serious. I must've hit my head on these stairs.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: She showed them what she was talking about. Just like they'd seen hours earlier on the crystal floor, the edge of one of the steps was covered in blood.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Did you trip while running up, then?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: I said that I don't know. It must be my blood, because it's fresh and I'm bleeding.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: W-Wait. Are you really saying that you lost your memory?
entries.speaker: aknn

entries.text: Yes. Do you think I'm joking?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Atsuki, what the hell is this?
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: What? I have no idea. ...What exactly do you not remember?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: I said that I don't remember anything.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Nothing at all?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: I think so.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: You're joking. You hit your head and lost your memories, like in a damn movie?
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: Yeah. Memory loss is a real thing, and why are you all so defensive? Shouldn't you be worried?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Everyone was very hesitant. Could she really have been telling the truth? The fresh blood on the stairs was unquestionable.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So you don't remember anything in general? What about the date or who we are?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Again, no. Where are we?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Answering that was too ridiculous. However, if she was lying, what was the purpose?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: They felt conflicted, but they had already noticed that Miiya seemed different. She had never looked at them like that, and her words felt colder than before.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "You're Miiya. Do you not know that either?" Atsuki spoke.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: No. It's pretty strange. I don't know anything about myself, but I know how to speak. I suppose this is how this kind of memory loss works.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: You really can't be telling the truth.
entries.speaker: aknn

entries.text: Why not? Would I lie about this? My head does hurt a lot.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: If you hit your head and you're not lying, it should be short-term memory loss, right? Everything should slowly come back to you soon.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: I don't know.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Where are we, though? Why is there a camera there?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: ...I doubt that's recording. Do you know what Ashiya Tower is? That's where we are.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Hm... Not really, no.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: It's a big building where we got trapped this morning. Do you not know any of that? There was an attack, and the exit closed.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Oh, really? So we can't leave?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Atsuki, do you actually believe she's telling the truth?
entries.speaker: aknn

entries.text: I am telling the truth. Is memory loss that rare? I don't think so, right?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: I wonder what Sai will have to say about this. He should be in the attic.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: Who's that?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: ...Someone else we got trapped with. Erina and Isla too, who are on the lowest floor. It's almost time for the exit to open, so you'll have to go straight to the hospital.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Nobody could believe that what they were hearing was real. The timing felt too coincidental, and they knew that Miiya had run to the attic for a reason, intentionally going against what everyone else wanted.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Do you think this might have anything to do with the Sekimeiya? A side effect, or something?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: The what?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: You really don't remember that either. What about the murders? You shouldn't be alone. Do you not remember Shiroya either?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: ...Murders? Did someone die?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Yes. A killer is with us.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Really? And it could be anyone?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: It's not so simple, but yes.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: I see.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: Sai didn't take the elevator again, so he should still be in the attic. Maybe he found someone.
entries.speaker: aknn

entries.text: It's very possible.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: Someone? Do you mean the killer?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: ...I don't know.
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: They stepped into the living room, but nothing could be heard.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Since the elevator was there, they didn't want to make noise.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The door to the hallway was open, so they peeked through it. Immediately, they saw something.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: One of the bedrooms was conspicuously open.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As soon as they looked inside, there were gasps.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai's body lay facing down on the floor. His back had been pierced, apparent by the narrow hole in his shirt, which was soaked in blood.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Oh my God, no...
entries.speaker: aknn

entries.text: The four people stared at the scene with wide eyes. ...Sai had been killed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Katei slowly crouched to grab the keyring, which had fallen from Sai's pocket. Having it on his person was what had allowed his death.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Then, they ran to the living room. His killer must've been there, hidden in one of the rooms. ...They couldn't let them escape.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You two wait here.
entries.speaker: aknn

entries.text: The young pair was left behind in the living room while Akaro and Katei looked through the rooms, their heartbeats hammering in their chests.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki's heart did the same as he slowly opened his mouth.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Are you telling the truth? Why did you want to go to the attic?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: He had noticed something.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When they'd all stepped into the living room, he had looked at the floor. There, he'd seen recent footprints going from the stairs to the hallway... and then back.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He only wanted an explanation he could accept, but his question hardly garnered a reaction.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Akaro and Katei confirmed that the elevator was present—and empty. Very carefully, they looked at the storeroom and then walked to the kitchen.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Lastly, only the two bedrooms remained. In the right one was Sai's lifeless body, but they couldn't find anyone else.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The last place was the mirrored, opposite bedroom. Aside from its lack of a corpse, it was identical.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Baffled, they walked back to the living room. There, they saw Atsuki's dead body.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Unlike Sai's, his body was facing the ceiling, but the same type of wound was present in his chest, blood rapidly flowing out of it. Neither of the men could believe what they were seeing.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: W-Was it her?
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: Miiya was nowhere to be found. Only after he had died did Atsuki's words begin to carry weight. In the end, they thought, he really hadn't been working with her.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Akaro and Katei couldn't move. A killer was near them, but where? Could it be that one of them had done it while they'd each looked at a different bedroom?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...No. Miiya was the killer; they couldn't think anything else. If another person had done it, she would've yelled. If she had run away, she probably would've been heard. Therefore, the only possible conclusion was that she had killed Atsuki and walked away.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Why? Such a question was irrelevant. If she had shown her true colors openly, everyone was in immense danger.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Akaro approached the elevator, but he couldn't open its door.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was brought down.
entries.speaker: aknn

entries.text: They knew they had to hurry, but it wasn't so simple. As they ran down the stairs, the fear continually caused them to stagger.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At any moment, their lives could be extinguished. They were trapped with a killer who had a weapon and had gone almost twelve hours without being caught. Would they be able to get through the last stretch?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: An attack could've been waiting around any corner, but the thought of Erina and Isla pushed them onward.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, as they sped down the stairs, they were oblivious to the nightmarish yells that resounded at the bottom of the tower.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Erina! Isla! Are you there!?
entries.speaker: aknn

entries.text: They ran to the open door. Through it, they saw exactly the image they had tried to forbid from entering their minds.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A mother and her daughter lay on the floor, their bodies no different from the two in the attic. Their torsos had been pierced, and blood was slowly spreading across the floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There's no way...
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: ...Katei, you have the keys, right?
entries.speaker: aknn

entries.text: Wh-What?
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: She must want everyone dead. We need to lock ourselves up somewhere, but get the Sekimeiya out! If we're attacked, we'll be able to escape by touching it.
entries.speaker: aknn

entries.text: Agreeing that it was the best course of action, Katei ran to the cabinet and unlocked it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Moments later, the hallway B door opened.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After a minute had gone by, a third body lay between Erina and Isla.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was Akaro's. It had been pierced multiple times in the stomach, and no trace of life dwelled in it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Next to the cabinet was the gray Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When the time came, the shutter opened and the police rushed into Ashiya Tower.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the lobby was the first indication of the bloodbath that had transpired. Dead eyes watched the officers from the floor, inviting them to a hell of corridors and blood.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Afterward, many more bodies were found.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the event room, Erina's, Isla's, and Akaro's.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In hallway C, Miiya's.{w} On the first staircase, Katei's.{w} Close to them, thrown on the floor, was a screwdriver covered in more than one person's blood.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the attic, Atsuki and Sai rested.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: All of them were dead. In addition, it was confirmed that all of them had died instantly. That meant that they couldn't have killed each other.{w} However, the police raided the whole building and didn't find anyone else.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Because before they had stepped into Ashiya Tower, not a speck of life had existed within it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The gray Sekimeiya was found next to the cabinet and placed inside it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the attic, hidden in a drawer in the kitchen, a playback device was found. Curiously, one of the officers pressed the play button, but nothing seemed to happen. After fiddling with it, he determined that it was broken.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the storeroom, the movable wall was discovered. When the police managed to open the door behind it, Sai's mark was removed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So, then, what had happened? Who had killed everyone? Every single person who had gotten trapped in the tower had been attacked by someone else.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: An investigation went on for a very long time, but nobody had access to the swathes of information that they were missing.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So when a conclusion was reached, it was impossible to feel that the truth had really been found.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The sudden, bloody spree was the final mystery of December 15th, 2011, which eluded the grasp of everyone who tried to solve it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Ending: Reward
Delayed Reflection
Permafrost
I didn't move from where I was. I only wanted to finally get out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, when Sai had revealed the time, uncertainty had begun to creep in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was {time=20.} The unbelievable day was coming to an end, but there was still something we were missing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The truth. We knew nothing about what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though many of the strange things that had occurred felt at least theoretically possible to understand, when I tried to think about them, I couldn't.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe the problem was that I couldn't be sure if I was right about anything, but technically, there was proof that untangling the day's events was possible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The existence of the Atsuki we'd talked to was inexplicable, but the fact that he'd known what would happen and told us of a certain outcome proved that the truth was attainable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Despite that, as the seconds ticked along, the answers I tried to reach changed more and more.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What would happen to me? ...I looked up to try to believe that nothing would, but I had no way to know.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At that moment, many people had to be on the other side of the shutter, and my parents were surely present among them. It was a given that we would be thoroughly questioned by the police and that an extensive investigation was to come.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And lastly, by an enigmatic version of Atsuki, we'd been assured that she would somehow come back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It didn't make any sense, but I had started to care less and less about that. She was alive, and it didn't seem like the fact that she had died twice mattered much. She would come back and maybe bring an explanation with her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd never wished her any harm, but after her death, I'd realized that her absence was simply better. I didn't want her back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Just as I'd been fond of Atsuki since years in the past, I'd never liked her constant presence. The me from two weeks earlier had shrugged off her disappearance, and the me stuck in the tower couldn't even care about her imminent return. It was all tiresome.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Coming to the exhibit had ironically worked to bring her back, and it might've been for the better. Even though Atsuki had offered for me to stay with him temporarily, I'd never been sure he would have recovered without going to live with his parents.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We had to accept we were leaving many questions behind, but there were plenty more in the outside world. Perhaps it wasn't a bad idea to consider finding a job somewhere else if I had the chance. I'd recently learned how much I despised acting differently than I felt, which was bound to persist if I didn't.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's the time?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Atsuki, you wouldn't by chance have been telling the truth, would you?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I was.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...{w}Akaro, do you remember Erina? Do you think she had all her buttons?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: O-Oh... I didn't notice.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Me neither; I didn't consider it. I think she might've had all of them, though.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}I didn't lie about anything.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: If that's true, maybe we really should do what you proposed and go search again.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You think so?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Isn't it too late for that? It's unlikely anything else will happen if we just stay here.
entries.speaker: m

entries.text: ...{w}I suppose.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: When I looked at the rest, I noticed that I wasn't the only person feeling nervous. All of them had their own worries and doubts about what was coming.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was it freedom that awaited? What would the world do when it found out about the Sekimeiya's powers? The answers were approaching.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Those last twenty minutes were holding the shutter in place. I was good at calming myself down, and that was all I could do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The only movement in the room came from Atsuki bouncing his leg. I closed my eyes, wanting to leave the smoke-stained walls behind as soon as possible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What was that?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It's coming from the lobby.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Five minutes later, we heard a rough sound. Upon stepping into hallway A, it became clear the lobby was the source.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, isn't that...?
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: We walked to the door and opened it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...!? It hasn't been twelve hours yet...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The shutter was withdrawing, the friction producing the sound we'd heard. Nothing mattered anymore: the faint light of the night had begun to cross the smooth glass of the exit door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-Wha...
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: N-Naomi...!
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: What's ha...ppening?
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: It's already time! Come on, Isla.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Wh—
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Perplexed, we stared at Naomi, who slowly raised herself off the floor. She seemed to be in pain, with a strong headache. As soon as she saw the blood below her, she understood it was hers and gasped.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh...? Y-You're okay?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: The shutter retracted all the way. Behind the door, one of multiple dark silhouettes placed its hand on the handle.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But before it opened, Naomi looked at all of us, her eyes driving stakes into our bodies.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She opened her mouth, and her words were mixed with the sound of our freedom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Y-You...! You're a murderer!{w} And you! ...You're behind this attack!
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: Chapter 2 Credits
The moonlight glanced off the floor of the lobby.
Eight pairs of eyes saw the outside world unveiled to them again as the door they'd entered through reopened.
At that instant, nothing else mattered.
The icy air they'd longed for was in reach. It was time for Ashiya Tower to be exposed.
After that long day, the final result—the world's truth—had been decided.
Many policemen rushed inside the vast lobby.
They saw a group of people next to a door, but there was a more pressing matter.
Lying on the floor was a man wearing their own uniform.
That juxtaposition of life and death signified the end of the Sekimeiya's play.
For one side, it was time to gather questions. For the other, it was time to let them go.
Everyone was taken outside, where they saw the stars had always been above them.
But it was soon understood that the events of that day held uncountable mysteries.
The entire building was raided, and nobody else was found.
The Sekimeiya, believed to be the target of the attack, hadn't been taken.
A secret door existed in the storeroom, which they were sure the deceased policeman had gone through.
However, it was locked.
To most of the eight witnesses, that was of no consequence.
They had no choice but to value their freedom, and they didn't hold the keys to enough questions.
Safely escaping a killer's reach had to be enough for them.
Monetary compensation was given to some due to Ashiya's reckless security measures.
Others were held accountable for potential crimes such as murder and theft.
None of those eight would ever have the chance to fully learn what had happened that day in the tower.
But they were aware of the Sekimeiya's powers.
However, only two people spoke of them.
Naturally, their statements were ridiculed and interpreted as a laughable, coordinated attempt at cover.
In the distant future, the Sekimeiya would return to the tower.
Against the unbelievable claims of the guilty parties, no visitor's touch would allow a travel through time.
From then onward, the Sekimeiya would stay in the special cabinet, symbolizing Xyn's failure.
There was a lingering question within two of the survivors.
One isolated from the simple curiosity of the outside world.
It entailed the veracity of some words they'd heard.
"Everything should turn out fine."
Almost four days had passed.
But it didn't feel that long. It felt, to them, as if that promise had been made mere hours ago.
Had it already turned out to be false?
It was impossible to know.
Had those words truly been said?
That, too, was impossible to know.
Then, they learned.
They understood that they had been aided.
Who had it been? A divine presence?
There was nobody to thank, so their gratefulness didn't reach anyone.
But they knew that entity existed and that it had made possible the bright future ahead.
Atsuki's phone rang.
On the screen, he saw a name he thought he'd never read again.
He picked up as quickly as possible, and he heard a voice he thought he'd never hear again.
"A-Atsuki...? What the hell... happened to me?"
Sunrise
A handful of police cars had gathered at the entrance of Ashiya Tower, ensuring complete isolation of the inside.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That had gone on for hours, and Yushibana's citizens had continually extended the crowd behind the authorities. Thirteen police officers stood in front of them like sentinels.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A thick layer of metal had been covering the door of the building all day, and it had been many hours since communication with the inside had suddenly cut off.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Next to the blocked entrance stood the people in charge of the operation. Suripo was told the time: in less than twenty minutes, the blockade would open. They had prepared for all possible outcomes.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Suripo had been there since the previous night, withstanding the constant noise of the curious and alarmed citizens and trying to converse with the stubborn Ashiya representative who had shown up in the morning. After breathing deeply, he approached one of the police cars.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Kano, have you seen Vaisude recently?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: The policeman under Suripo's orders frowned, realizing that he actually hadn't seen Vaisude in hours.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I haven't. Did something happen to him?
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: He was in his car earlier, but I haven't managed to get in touch with him since. I saw he wasn't waiting in the car, and he didn't pick up when I tried to call him.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Kano looked through his left window toward the car Vaisude had been in. It was next to the tower's entrance, and as he'd been told, nobody could be seen through its open windows.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I apologize, but I don't know what he went to do. I haven't spoken to him all day.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Suripo walked away slowly, a little concerned. Days prior, Vaisude had been insistent in saying that an attack would occur on the morning of the 15th. However, he'd also kept saying that it was a hunch and that he didn't have proof of it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Furthermore, after their talk, Vaisude had told Suripo that he wouldn't come to work again. He wasn't directly under Suripo's command, but he knew Suripo had been in charge of Ashiya and Xyn's confrontation and that he knew about its details more than his actual boss.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On the morning of the 15th, two more police teams had been sent to Ashiya Tower to take control of the situation after the attack. At that time, Suripo had seen Vaisude in the team he'd always been part of.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Suripo knew he might've had valuable information, having correctly foreseen the attack. However, in the past, he hadn't provided any, so Suripo hadn't prioritized going to question him. Later on, when he'd looked, he had been unable to find Vaisude.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After talking to his colleagues, they'd all claimed not to know his whereabouts either.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Suripo was indecisive. If Vaisude had known about Xyn's attack, why had he only warned them that it would occur? He hadn't accomplished anything, as it had already been a well-known possibility.{w} And even if he'd been involved with Xyn in some way, the same question had to be asked.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: His disappearance was suspicious. Had he gone off to act as a part of their plan, or had something happened to him? At no point had he told anyone about it, and nobody had seen him leaving.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Confident that those questions would be answered in the future, Suripo walked back to the shutter to continue waiting for {time=21:04}, when the entrance would open.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Near the back of the crowd, standing off by herself, was a lone blonde woman in a heavy coat. She repeatedly twisted a lock of her hair in one hand, murmuring quietly to herself as the people nearby continued their own louder musings.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The smell around here... I wonder what's causing it. You can barely tell it's there, but it's persistent... Is it related?
entries.speaker: q

entries.text: The conversation nearby turned to the topic of Xyn and their potential involvement. She went quiet, listening intently for any clues, but it was all information she'd heard within the past few minutes regurgitated once again. Her left foot tapped an unconscious rhythm on the ground.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She wasn't sure how she'd gotten involved in the events around the tower, but once she realized something unnatural was occurring, she couldn't ignore it. Curiosity drove her to appear outside, in spite of the persistent crowd of bored townspeople.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Suripo turned back, surveying the crowd once more. In the darkness, her blonde hair and slight fidgeting stood out. His caution getting the better of him, he decided to approach, as she wasn't a resident of the town he'd ever seen before.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Excuse me. Would you be able to answer a couple of questions for me?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Hello?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: H-Hmm? Do you... mean me, maybe...?
entries.speaker: q

entries.text: Yes. How long have you been here?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Oh, ah... Only a little while, maybe an hour. I was... curious about the tower. What's happening inside. Like everyone else here is, of course.
entries.speaker: q

entries.text: A thin film of sweat formed on her forehead. It wasn't the first time she'd been questioned by a police officer, but being singled out still made her nervous. Within her coat, she rubbed her arms.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And your name?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: It's {tip=larles}Larles{/tip}. Just Larles is fine. I know it sounds odd, but it's normal where I'm from, I promise.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Suripo couldn't place her accent. It had a particular sound to it that he'd never heard before, not even from any kind of shows or songs.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Would you happen to have any form of identification on you?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Trembling like a leaf in the chilly winter breeze, Larles withdrew an object from her interior coat pocket and tapped it a few times. She opened and presented it to Suripo, but her hand shook so thoroughly that he couldn't read it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Gently removing it from her grip, he took a closer look and flipped through it. A passport. Completely valid, as far as he could tell, with nothing remotely questionable about it. Her name matched what she claimed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Nodding slightly, Suripo handed it back to her. Instead of stowing it back in her pocket, Larles began to tap a consistent beat on it, trying to calm her nerves.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Did you just move here?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: I'm here on... business. Official business. I just, well, the tower was big news and it reminded me of one back where I'm from. That, and it seemed strange...
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Strange how?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Well, um, everyone's talking about it, right? How strange it is for people to be trapped inside... I-I'm only in town for a little while. I can leave if you think I'm suspicious...
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Suripo arched an eyebrow. She was certainly suspicious, but not in the way that a Xyn plant would be. She was too obvious, and clearly harmless in his eyes.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It's the most confusing thing I've ever seen... Why can't it be opened? I've been here a few times now, and nothing seemed out of place, but today there's a big event and no explaining it. Do the police know anything? Everyone around here is clueless like me...
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: I can't get into what we know and don't know in detail. I'm sure you understand.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Of course, yes. But don't you think there has to be some kind of supernatural component? Like maybe everyone inside time traveled and now they're in the past, at a time when nobody else is inside. Do we even know they're still in there? There's no way to see inside, right?
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Suripo blinked in disbelief. She claimed to be in Yushibana on some kind of business, but he didn't believe that. Her bringing up an outlandish topic like time travel most likely meant that she was with some kind of magazine or news company and trying to bait readers.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Where did you get this idea from?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Um, it was someone in the crowd who mentioned it, and I thought it made a lot of sense...
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Still wary, she gestured indiscriminately at the people around the building. They had formed small, isolated bubbles in places, continuing to increase in volume as the time approached.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I see. Have you noticed anyone around here doing anything questionable? Or what about them disappearing?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: It was Suripo's subtle way of discerning if she'd seen Vaisude recently. He was still concerned about his location.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: No, sir, sorry to say. If I had seen anything out of place, I would have told all of you immediately. Promise! I don't want to get in your way at all, only find out the truth.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: At that moment, Larles received a summons she could not ignore. She had known her time was short, but not that she wouldn't even be able to see the conclusion of the tower's mystery.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Actually, I just got a call. I have to be going. Sorry, but would you mind if I took my leave?
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Suripo sighed. She hadn't even pulled out a phone to check a call. He was no closer to an answer than he had been a few minutes ago, and he didn't expect such sudden excuses. Mentally, he made a note to check into her identity later, just in case his intuition was wrong, but she seemed unreliable at best.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Well, thank you for your time. If you notice anything later on, please feel free to let us know.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Suripo returned to his position. Larles fidgeted slightly, unsure that he had believed her. She didn't have any desire to confuse the locals and desperately wanted to see the shutter open. It was too unique for her to ignore.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But she was out of time. She couldn't afford to stay any longer. Sighing in resignation, she turned away from the building and began to walk. She had hoped that there was enough time to satisfy her curiosity, but it was inevitable.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Larles made a promise to herself. Whenever she got the opportunity, she would return and determine the truth of that day with her own eyes. She couldn't get into the tower normally, but with enough preparation, it could be done.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Resolving herself, she vanished into the night.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Remember what I said. One of the people inside is a terrorist who will try something to steal the Sekimeiya. Any of the people here could be their comrade, and you must prioritize keeping their plan from succeeding.
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: You can stop saying that. I'm well aware of what could be going on.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Lei wasn't a blood relative of Ashiya, but she'd been sent as their representative, speaking on their behalf, and had been giving the police any essential information.{w} From the get-go, she had stated that the process of stealing the Sekimeiya was underway despite Ashiya's public declarations, which were that Xyn's plan had immediately failed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was almost {time=21}, and the winter sky had long ago darkened, bringing a sheer cold to everyone who'd kept waiting to witness the resolution of a long day.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This smell again... What the hell is it?
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: Suripo wasn't sure either. Throughout the whole day, they'd sporadically noticed a strange smell next to the tower. However, they hadn't been able to identify its source, nor the smell itself.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: {time=21} came. The crowd was kept back by the group of policemen in front of the tower, but even the officials were partially curious how the shutter would withdraw.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Speculation hadn't stopped. The widespread belief was that everything had been part of Xyn's plan and Ashiya had no way of stopping it. However, nobody could agree on how Xyn would actually do it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Multiple groups of those with similar views formed the crowd outside the tower. On one side was the simply curious portion. On the other, the older citizens were eagerly awaiting Ashiya's defeat, voicing their harsh thoughts on the family.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It had become known that the exit was going to remain closed for twelve hours, and although the police had kept quiet, something had seemingly caused disorder among them less than an hour after the attack.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Additionally, the names of the trapped people had been released, but nobody had seen or heard of any of their relatives waiting outside for them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When the police stood up, everyone knew the time had come, and the flash of some cameras started to illuminate the dark exterior of the tower.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The last minutes were quiet. The police had been exchanging words, but they were too far from the crowd to be heard.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Will this be enough people to apprehend everyone? We don't want something funny occurring.
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: That's not a concern. Nobody will have a way to sneak anything out.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: There were only a few seconds left. Nobody knew the exact time the shutter had closed, but they had determined it had been right about {time=9:04.}
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Finally, letting out a loud and hoarse noise, the heavy shutter began to rise until it fully disappeared from view. At the same time, some people in the crowd began to point up, where the same thing was happening to the covered windows.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The door wasn't blocked anymore, and the bright lobby could be seen through it. Immediately, the policemen rushed in while Suripo's expectations remained unmet.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He'd been continuously told that someone would try to exit immediately with the Sekimeiya, and that they would need to be hastily detained. However, nobody could be seen inside.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Wh-What the fuck is this!?
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Before they could step into the tower, the team who'd rushed in was instantly taken aback, making brief eye contact with the confused multitude outside while covering their noses and grimacing.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...What's wrong!?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: There's something inside! It could be dangerous!
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Everyone who'd stayed next to the door understood immediately. After it had opened, it hadn't taken much time for the smell they'd been noticing to drastically intensify. That confirmed it had been coming from within the tower, something they had previously discounted.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Twelve hours earlier, unidentified smoke had been released on the first floor of the tower. Right away, the possibility of it being poisonous had been presented.{w} However, they'd abandoned it as soon as the safety of the trapped individuals had been confirmed less than an hour later. Nonetheless, they'd prepared equipment such as masks just to be careful.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When they rushed to grab their equipment, the crowd began to show concern for the eight people trapped, whose figures hadn't yet appeared.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I knew it! Didn't I tell you they were planning something!? You all better not let them get away with whatever they're trying to do!
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: Everyone had retreated from the entrance as soon as it had been perceived as dangerous. That could well have been an opening for someone inside to escape, but no such thing occurred.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: From a truck, the police took out protective suits alongside an optical gas imaging camera, as whatever had hit their noses had been invisible. The team ran back to the lobby and scanned the area with it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Look... There's definitely something inside.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Everyone who looked at the image saw what appeared to be very dense gas occupying the entire hall. It looked white in the image, and it seemed to completely lack a source.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The people in the back could see every movement, and they understood that the situation was being communicated through wireless devices.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The gas was unidentified, but they'd all inhaled some of it. However, even if it was toxic, the masks and suits would work as protection. Knowing that, the same team who'd tried to enter did so once again, hiding their faces behind the protective filters.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Look for the Sekimeiya in the cabinet! If it's empty, finding the Sekimeiya is the priority!
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: Lei had informed them of how the Sekimeiya looked and the necessity for cold temperature. Everyone who'd entered knew the Sekimeiya had to be immediately placed inside the cabinet, but after the precarious situation had been revealed, their focus was to secure everyone inside.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hey, look!
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Five people had entered. Before they could disperse through the building, one alerted the others and pointed at the floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There, they saw dried blood. Not a single soul was in the lobby awaiting their escape—there was only blood. A foreboding emotion ate at the edges of the men who'd gone in first.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: While everyone else waited impatiently, those five officers began to scatter, opening every room and trying to uncover every unseen spot. They knew the layout of the building and had been given a way to enter every place that could be locked.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: One man confirmed that the mechanical room was barren and rushed back up to enter hallway B, its walls nearly as dark.{w} There, an old friend of his frantically tried to find the people who should've been trapped inside. A great deal of blood was on the floor toward the end of the hallway, which only compounded the officers' uneasiness.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When he entered one of the crystal rooms on the right side, he saw the first person and stopped in place, turning around to confirm with the man behind him that what he was seeing was real.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the opposite hallway was a longer trail of blood. The security room was the first place to be opened, so they didn't have to wait long to have their fears confirmed.{w} Then, in a deeper room, they saw an even more wretched nightmare.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, when one of the bathrooms was opened, any comprehension they had instantly shattered.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: They walked up the first staircase and saw a person standing there.{w} It was a girl with blue hair who looked a little disoriented.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Everyone rushed to her and confirmed her safety. Instead of hammering her with questions, being under the impression that the gas could've been toxic, one of the men escorted her to the lobby, where she was hit by the air she'd been longing for.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The search continued, as more people were yet to be found. However, when the police reached the attic's door, there had been no new discovery.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: One of them had been given that key after pressuring Ashiya. Once the highest level of the tower was unlocked, they rushed inside.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Less than half a minute was needed to understand that three people were missing. However, even though they hadn't found anyone in the attic, they had spotted something else they'd been searching for.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The entrance had been closed again to prevent the gas from escaping, and every bystander had shifted farther back after being informed of the possible danger.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Suripo continued to wait for the arrival of his team, the only sound being the confused muttering of the crowd. At his side, Lei was visibly tense.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: One of their men appeared from hallway A with a girl who seemed to be in pain.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "...Are you okay?" Suripo asked.{w} The girl nodded faintly and looked away from him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What's your name?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Shiroya.
entries.speaker: snn

entries.text: I see. I'm really sorry you had to go through this.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: But the other policeman glared at Suripo, who didn't know what else was inside.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Then, he walked to a car with Shiroya, where the eight people trapped inside were planned to be held.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After five minutes of no development, a second policeman came back. Outside, he took his mask off, and the look in his eyes was enough to convey what he'd seen.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Four of them are... dead. Counting everyone, there should be {tip=three}three left{/tip}.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Wh-What...!?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: They were killed... But the others aren't anywhere inside. We haven't found the other three people who should be here.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Are you fucking serious? What about the Sekimeiya!?
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: Don't worry about that.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: He explained that, in the attic, they'd found an egg-shaped white object that matched the Sekimeiya's description. Then, it had been brought to the cabinet downstairs as instructed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Then...! Someone got into the cabinet. This plan definitely revolved around the Sekimeiya, but it failed. That has to be it.
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: Lei looked relieved despite having been told about four casualties. However, Suripo still hadn't understood his subordinate.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: H-How is it possible the other three haven't been found? Are you sure you searched everywhere?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Yes. Did you personally speak with all of them?
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: I did. They all told me their names. They have to be inside.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Two more policemen came from the hallways and reported the same result. However, one of them inquired about something different.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Is it possible they could have escaped? I saw a door in the storeroom I wasn't aware of.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: What the hell are you talking about?
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: The man told them about the movable wall and about the door with a missing handle. Instead of entering to witness it by themselves, they walked to the left side of the building and estimated where the storeroom might've been.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What the fuck is this...?
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: After just a minute of searching, a faint outline had been found resembling a door. Furthermore, although it was exceptionally well-hidden, they saw a keyhole that meshed perfectly with the surface of the wall.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There's no way this is a door! No such thing exists in the storeroom!
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: Suripo ignored her; there was obviously a door. However, it didn't explain anything.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Nobody could've escaped through here. Very soon after the attack occurred, people started watching from both sides. And not just the civilians gathered out here, but also the police.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Lei was astonished, as no such door should've existed. However, even though she couldn't trust that nobody could've escaped, she wasn't that concerned. After all, the well-being of the Sekimeiya had been confirmed. In the worst-case scenario, the Xyn members had fled.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And given what I saw, nobody could've opened it from the inside. The handle had been removed, and there was no lock to pick.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: No... There's no way this leads inside the tower. It's impossible I wouldn't know about it.
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: We can determine that easily.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: The keyhole looked old, and Suripo believed that opening it without the key would be doable. If it was rusty or had been frozen, it could've been impossible, but if it was in a decent state, it shouldn't have taken him very long.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He instructed his subordinate to run to his car, where he had a standard lock picking set. Once he received it, Suripo began to fiddle with the lock and quickly found that picking it was possible.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This door is locked. We'd have to do this even if we had a handle.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: The other two looked at him, trying to suppress their own shivering. It wasn't from the cold alone—they'd learned that people had died, but also that some were missing. If the door led to a hidden room, the rest could've been inside.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The major part of the crowd was occupied with looking at the entrance, so they didn't pay much attention to the people who'd gone to the left side of the building. After a few short minutes, the lock clicked, and the door swung in.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There's no fucking way... How did I not know about this!? And how could Xyn!?
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: The three of them saw the dark storeroom, with the wall that the other policeman had closed hiding the hallway door from view.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was truly the storeroom. The peculiar smell started to become prominent once again, so they rushed back out and walked to the main entrance, wondering if that door had truly been used as a method of escape. It seemed it hadn't been possible to open from the inside, but the handle could've been removed by the people who hadn't escaped or while the door had been open.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Outside the front door, they saw the final man who'd entered the building. All of them confirmed the same story: four people had died, and there was nobody else alive.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: One of the victims is Naomi Cabca, who worked in the tower. However, two bodies that look exactly like her are inside. None of the people who got trapped shared her last name, correct?
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Suripo kept growing more confused and shook his head. Four of the people he'd talked to in the morning had died, which he still had trouble accepting. What the hell had happened in the tower?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I took images of the inside. The gas is present practically around the entire building in different quantities, but I wasn't able to find a source for it.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: What...? How's that possible?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: I also took pictures of the bodies.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Suripo remembered the voice of the child he'd heard at the start of that long day after looking at her face. The pictures also encompassed all the blood found in the hallways and elevator.{w} Two of the bodies had the same face and clothing, which was incredibly odd, as nothing like that had been mentioned during the brief period of communication with those inside.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: These bodies must be taken out. We don't know what happened or what this gas is, but it's in the entire building. A proper investigation might not be able to occur for a while with these circumstances.{w} However, the security cameras have been recording since this all started. Save all the footage to a drive.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: The door had been closed again, but even then, they felt the smell was still present. They kept taking more steps back while the orders to analyze the gas were being sent.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Suripo saw that one of his men was holding something.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What's that?
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Oh, it's something I found on the first floor. Take a look at it.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Suripo reached out and grabbed a tiny piece of paper. He began to read the words written on it out loud.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hello... I'm sorry that I have to write this.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: I still can't believe what happened. I haven't been able to stop crying, but I've always tried to tell myself that these things just occur.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: I know how selfish it is that I'm writing this, but I won't be able to live with myself if I don't.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: I need to say it.{w} I've always wanted to, and I can't believe I never will.{w} I love you.
entries.speaker: sunn

entries.text: Everyone who heard Suripo was bewildered.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And then, when they understood that the events of that day contained innumerably more mysteries than they'd expected, as their only wish, they hoped that all the truth could be exposed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Self-Fulfillment
The sun had long ago set, letting the sheer cold prevail in the streets of Yushibana.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Near the outskirts, the moon and a few light posts provided the only illumination. It was late, and everyone around was preparing to end their day.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Not one of them saw the figure of a young girl appearing by the entrance of a house, below a stone roof.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She found herself leaning against the cold wall and quickly looked down.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Light snow was falling, but she was still able to discern some of the footprints she'd once left.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Next to the wheel marks, she knew that what she was seeing were the imprints of three different pairs of shoes. One trail was hers, and the other two belonged to two of her friends.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She traced them with her eyes and followed them to a door in the middle of the street. Next to it was a modest window with a curtain concealing the interior.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Light was coming from the other side, but it was very faint. Without wasting time, she dashed to the door and opened it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She had appeared from the future. Instants earlier, she had been inside Ashiya Tower, on December 15th.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was fifteen days before that time, so she knew what was soon to happen in the tiny store she'd hastily run to.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At one point, her friend Atsuki had told her that it was possible to change the past. She firmly believed that she could make it happen herself.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She pulled open the door, planning to diverge the world from the one she knew.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Her field of vision was filled by lingering smoke. Knowing not to breathe in, she glanced down as the door closed behind her.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There, she saw the first two people who'd fallen unconscious. They had already escaped danger.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She ran through the oppressive cloud and looked behind the stand of shelves.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On the floor was her own body. She recalled the time she'd seen the smoke appearing and been unable to resist the loss of consciousness.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She would be fine as well, so she stepped to the far side of the room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As she did so, she couldn't help but briefly breathe the polluted air. She was afraid it would knock her out, but instead, she noticed something.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was the smell from that day... And she knew what it was.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Behind the prominent stenches of the smoke and artificial gas, there was a third, hidden smell, present all around the shop. It was a possibility she'd already explored, so it didn't come as a surprise to her, but there was no time to think as she looked behind the last set of shelves.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She saw the last person. Her friend, Miiya, was unconscious on the floor, facing the ceiling. Just behind her was a powered-off heater, silently emitting the deadly gas that had once ended her life.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The range of the explosion would not be large, so saving her friend was doable, and she was confident she'd succeed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She kneeled and grabbed the shoulders of the unconscious girl. Then, she stepped back to drop her behind the shelves that would protect her.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At that point, she was saved, but she kept moving back, so that the soon-to-break floor wouldn't swallow her. Once she was absent from all danger, the girl stood up and looked at her past self.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She didn't know the exact time, but her job hadn't ended yet.{w} She stepped up to her own shoulders and grabbed them. After lifting herself, she began to back up.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Then, her heart suddenly skipped a beat.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She turned around. She didn't see the door opening because a wooden shelf was blocking her sight, but soon after she heard its sound, the lights turned off.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There was no time to react.{w} During the instants before the light came back on, the girl closed her eyes and attempted to cover her face with her arms.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The floor had shattered, and she found herself falling with the rubble, the deadly light shrinking within the familiar darkness.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hex Ladder
We'd been in front of the queue for a long time, looking at the dull, wooden door that would soon open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked behind me and noticed that a lot of people were waiting. The entrance kept opening, sending icy breezes toward my neck.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd never seen the interior of Ashiya Tower before, and I'd never believed I'd ever enter it. The lobby felt empty despite all the people that had come due to the vast and dreary amount of space.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I think it'll be time soon.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yeah, probably less than twenty minutes.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I'd had my mind empty all day, with no capacity to hold a conversation. Atsuki knew that and kept restlessly glancing around.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hated the way I'd become and silently apologized for putting him through even more pain. It was early in the morning, and we hadn't slept. Almost exhausted, I let my head drop and thoughtlessly stared at the floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: During the previous week, I could hardly even claim to have been alive. The death of our friend had shaken me in a way I'd never expected.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After lonesome months going over the most important decisions of my life, I'd considered Atsuki's call a breath of fresh air. What was the point in going to study abroad if it wasn't what I wanted the most? When I'd been at Atsuki's house, I'd felt embarrassed for not realizing before how straightforward the decision had always been.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But reality had hit me way harder just the next day. I'd finally decided on something, and it was rejected.{w} Why had Miiya died? It wasn't fair. The three of us were so happy that day, so why had it been Miiya's last?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Of course, anyone could die at any point. I'd heard those words many times, but I had never really understood them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What if I'd died instead? What if Atsuki had? Why was I so selfishly sad that my future wouldn't be as I'd believed during that day? At the very least, she had been unconscious...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My thoughts were a mess, so I'd put what little willpower I had into keeping them blank. Otherwise, I'd keep replaying the span of time in which I'd awakened next to Atsuki and heard everything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't easy to accept that the previous two weeks had actually happened, but I already considered them the two worst of my life. I'd known Atsuki for many years, and the person next to me was just a cast-off shell of his. I'd never seen him look so depressed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, despite the impact everything had on me, I'd also been able to think positively. That was why we were in Ashiya Tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We couldn't let Miiya's death take us down too. The three of us had spoken about missing the old days and about how hard the summer months had been. Even though it was just the two of us, Atsuki and I had wanted to come to Ashiya's event. We wanted to overcome everything together.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But that wasn't fair. She didn't deserve that either... The mere thought of imagining a cheerful future without Miiya was heartbreaking.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She typically hadn't shown much emotion, but I knew she'd had a good heart. I hated that after her death, I regretted not speaking to her enough... I hated how little I'd known about her despite how often the three of us had been together.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It couldn't have been fair that I regretted that only because she had died. And that, despite how broken I felt, the sadness her parents were experiencing didn't mean as much to me because I'd never talked to them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew how shallow and unreasonable some of my thoughts were, but that wasn't enough to put an end to them. Was I just selfish? ...I kept wondering if that was all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You three are the first group, correct?
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: A woman had been talking about what we would do, and she was addressing us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Yes." After a long wait, Atsuki answered with a plain and quiet voice.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...All right, then. Please follow me to the event room to be the first to see the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: sa

entries.text: Right. That day, Ashiya were showcasing a new discovery. I couldn't feel the intrigue I'd once faintly had, so after the two people at my side went through the door, I followed behind them with slow steps.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the opposite side was a long corridor, vast and completely lacking in comfort. I didn't see where the others had gone, but a few of the doors were open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you feeling better?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh... Yeah, I'm fine. Don't worry about it.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I walked toward one of the doors, but it didn't seem like anyone was behind it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Do you regret coming?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I turned around, saddened to hear that question.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...No, of course not.{w} I'm seriously glad we're here. I mean it.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I didn't regret having come at all. The part of me that could feel it was really glad Atsuki was still at my side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I know how you feel, okay? It's... the same for me. It doesn't help a lot to say it, but I don't want to see you sad.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I'm here because I want to be, Atsuki. I'm okay. This is where I need to be right now. Sorry, I must look terrible.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...You know this isn't something you need to apologize for. Nothing about this is your fault.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I'm... not so sure. I wish I didn't have to be a drag for you now.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: H-Hey, come on. If you want to leave, we still can. Don't feel like you have to push yourself for my sake.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It's all right. Thank you.{w} Let's continue, though. I was the one who wanted to come.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Okay.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The woman called us from one of the rooms, and we shut ourselves inside it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Behind a velvet curtain was the gemstone we would be shown. After we introduced ourselves, we were told the basics behind its discovery and rarity, leading up to the cabinet containing it being unlocked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But as the curtain rose, something else did. A dense and dark smoke filled my vision, and before I could realize that I should have held my breath, I fell to the floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki... Wha...
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: My heart went wild, but I couldn't move any other part of my body. My mind flashed to the last time smoke had put me to sleep, and remembering what the outcome had been, I desperately tried to resist the urge to close my eyes.
entries.speaker: i
