entries.text: That time, I didn't wake up in the hospital. I was in the same room as before. Immobile, I stared at the floor, my awareness gradually returning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are y—*cough* *cough*
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes... I think so. *cough*
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I was relieved to see that both of us were okay. Akaro, the other man, was safe too, but we quickly saw that Naomi was gone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was the beginning of a very long day. There had been an attack in the tower, and plenty of questions came with it. The first one was the origin of the smoke that had knocked us out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There took place the first real conversation I'd had with Atsuki in days. We were forced to discuss what we'd been caught up in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And that was what we'd most needed. We hadn't talked about anything because we didn't have the strength to say what we wanted. The situation we ended up in forced us to talk to each other again.{w} When I noticed that we were speaking normally, I was grateful that coming to the tower had given us what we'd been looking for.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, the future that should've been waiting for us was challenged by the same thing that had made it attainable: the events that unfolded in Ashiya Tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the hallway, we met Erina, Isla, Katei, and Sai. There, we learned that we would spend twelve hours in the building due to an alarm that had been recently installed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It should've gone off whenever the Sekimeiya was stolen, but when we looked in its cabinet, that was immediately thrown into question.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: From the security room, we contacted the outside, which clarified the outline of what had happened. After that, we were assaulted by question after question.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The computer turned off out of the blue, leaving us unable to look at the recorded footage. Then, we looked for Naomi, who should've been somewhere in the building.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We separated into two groups and looked through the upper floors. There, we learned about the predictions Isla's friend had made.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And that Naomi had come from the floors below, demanding to talk to Katei privately.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was when Atsuki and I noticed the first signs of the underlying factor of our imprisonment. The elevator was brought up, but we couldn't find who'd boarded it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The reason... was time travel. The Sekimeiya, which we had come to see, possessed the power to send people through time. As ridiculous as it sounded, we had no choice but to accept it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was it true that everything happened for a reason? Had we been given the ability to undo the past after wishing for it? If so, there were two different, bright futures on the horizon.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We could leave the tower after moving past Miiya's death... or we could go to the past and save her. Just when it seemed the wound was beginning to heal, we were captivated by a slim hope.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it looked like the world might have been mocking us instead. We drew the conclusion that changing the past was likely not doable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to our two possible futures, there was something darker. It first appeared when we saw Naomi's body on the floor, devoid of life and soaked in blood.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Trapped with us was a killer—a person who'd produced the same pain we'd felt before.{w} There had to be justice for Naomi, but we were unable to figure out the truth behind her death.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Something became clear very early on: when we could leave the building, everything would be much different from when we'd entered it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was one of the people who'd discovered Naomi's corpse responsible for her death? I despised that thought, but more than that, I despised whoever that person was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We heard a sound that indicated someone else was around us, but we couldn't find anyone. It seemed that during the time we'd looked for the culprit, the elevator had moved in a strange way. Whatever they were doing kept happening right under our noses.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And soon, we came across the bathrooms on the lowest floor. Inside the men's was Naomi's body.{w} Not the one we'd already found, but a different one. That confirmed what we'd all already imagined: in the tower with us, while the world couldn't see it, something beyond the bounds of possibility was taking place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We managed to enter the attic thanks to one of the keys Naomi had. Up there, the footprints on the carpet informed us that such impossibilities extended to every place in the building.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And lastly, inside Isla's purse, we found a greater harbinger of hopelessness than anything before it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Would we spend more than a month in that building? As impossible as it sounded, that word didn't mean much anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Attempting to solve the smaller questions, Atsuki and I walked all the way down from the attic. There, I traveled through time for the first time, but it wasn't me who touched the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We began to learn more and more about how the time travel functioned, but the biggest blockade stood resolutely in place: the past wasn't changing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Some time later, we traveled again. We appeared in the attic, but we had to stay put in one of the bedrooms. We were very tired, so we both lay in the beds.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Despite how disheartening it was, we were able to calmly talk about the Sekimeiya. I no longer believed that we had much hope of understanding it or using it to our advantage, but we could at least try.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And even that faint belief was thrown back in our faces. When we woke up, we found out that the Sekimeiya had taken Isla's life—that reality was truly as ruthless as we'd feared.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What had happened to her was shrouded in mystery, but the Sekimeiya had been the catalyst. At my side, I saw Erina's devastation and wondered if my own even came close.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After a long wait in the lobby, I found a hidden mechanism in the storeroom. Past a movable wall, there was a door without a handle that appeared to lead outside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But after what some of us had heard from the recorder, it wasn't possible to think that freedom was so close. Was it truly a single door away?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina suggested locking ourselves up in a room. That was the best and safest way to reach the time limit. We chose one of the bedrooms in the attic and decided to stay there for the remaining hours.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, we didn't even last two hours before a wave of questions forced the lock open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I did my best to keep my mood positive, but every time I looked around me, I hated seeing where I was. I'd spent days avoiding the sun, and it had become what I wanted to see the most. On top of that, due to how little I'd slept, my head was constantly cloudy, and my body felt physically drained.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We had already accepted that the Sekimeiya wouldn't bring anything beneficial. It wouldn't let us change the past, and touching it would make us stay locked in the tower for longer. So I told Atsuki that we shouldn't do it again—the most important thing was making it out safely.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But all over the lowest floor was proof that the torment had continued, and when we opened the door to the security room, we saw that Katei, who'd been heavily suspected, had been killed as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the opposite hallway was Erina's body, collapsed on the floor. Crushed from the sight, we walked to the center of the floor, wishing to be isolated so that we wouldn't become the next targets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What made us leave was who Atsuki saw. According to him, he'd seen another version of me in the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It didn't make sense. Who had he seen, and why? I didn't want to prolong our stay, but it seemed I had...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When we took the elevator all the way down from the attic, we were intercepted. On the third floor, a sudden knife threatened to cut our lives short. Were we about to die too? There was no way we'd let that happen, so we ran as fast as we could.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Through an exhausting chase, we heard the voice of our attacker. It was Sai, one of the people who'd been with us since that morning.{w} What had we done to be chased with a knife? His voice conveyed that attempting to ask that would be fatal.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, when the three of us ended up in the event room, his deadly gaze ceased.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The moment he left the knife on the floor, our heart rates finally began to slow down. He revealed that he had to do something that required the use of the Sekimeiya in the cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After we failed to find him in any of the rooms where he could've been, he managed to obtain the Sekimeiya and threatened to use it at any time. He made no effort at hiding that there was something he wanted to do upon activating it, so given what he'd done to us and that he had probably been behind some of the murders, we couldn't let him succeed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While he continued taunting us, the range of the Sekimeiya increased. Minutes later, when he was about to touch it, Atsuki and I ran toward him to be encompassed in his travel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai made contact with the Sekimeiya, but he didn't disappear. Only my surroundings did.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Karma
In front of me was Sai. Both of us had appeared in the right-hand bedroom of the attic.{w} When Sai's eyes met mine, he raised his eyebrows, hesitant to move.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The knife almost fell from my grip, but I still held it in my right hand. I had picked it up in the event room when Sai purposely left it behind, and it didn't disappear after traveling.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What was it that you wanted to do?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Nothing.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He had reiterated many times that he had to go to the past to do something, but he didn't expect me to appear with him. I was in front of the door while he stared at the knife in my hand. If I didn't move, I could make sure to prevent whatever he wanted to do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then it's fine if we stay here, right? You only needed to travel to the past, so that shouldn't be a problem.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Are you threatening me with that knife? You know these cameras are recording, don't you?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...We definitely only went some minutes into the past. We're going to spend them here until we get to the point we were at. Atsuki's not here, so he appeared somewhere else.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: You really are threatening me with a knife? How bizarre. I suppose we can stay here for a bit since that dumbass will probably search for us. I'm confused, though. Didn't really foresee this one.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What did you expect to happen?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: You can't really think I'll tell you anything while you have that pointed at me, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I looked at the knife. Was I really threatening him...? He had chased us with it, and while it was fair, the thought of threatening someone with their own death was sickening.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I'm confused. Why did we appear here? How is it possible that I appeared with the knife in the attic when I only had it in the event room?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I recall telling you and Atsuki that you were wrong about what you said. You mean that you've never been in this bedroom with the knife, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Maybe I was right and you were wrong, then.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wait, what time is it?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He looked at his wristwatch and sighed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's no current time.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He showed me the tiny display from afar. It was blank.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It stopped working? That's what Katei said happened earlier, right?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yes. It seems it wasn't the battery's problem, but the watch's. Even if it was working, it's unlikely it would display the real time anyway.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Take a few steps back.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Why?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Just do it.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He backed farther into the room without turning around. He could've run at me at any point, so I wanted to feel a little more secure.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked to the drawer stand and opened the highest one while making sure Sai couldn't dash to the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Inside was the key to the bedroom. When we'd been running from Sai, we'd considered that he grabbed it to prevent us from locking ourselves inside, but it was still there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He saw me taking it out and frowned. Then, he began to slowly approach me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Stop.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: You wouldn't be thinking about locking me in here, right? That would be very mean.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That wasn't my intention. By attempting to trap him from outside, I would've given him a chance to push the door open and overpower me. That was why I wanted to lock the door from the inside, so that he couldn't simply rush to it and leave at any moment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I inserted the key into the inner keyhole and turned it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...You locked both of us in? Very courageous.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I dropped the key in my purse and zipped it. If Sai had been thinking about forcing his way out, that would make him less likely to attempt it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I continued standing in front of the door, a little calmer than before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: For a while, Sai looked pensive and maybe even uncertain. Trying to decipher his thoughts had rarely proven useful.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you going to tell me why you wanted to go to the past?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Nope.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Then are you fine staying here?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...I suppose. This is all a little annoying.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What are you thinking about? You seem pretty preoccupied.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: You want me to be honest? I'm thinking about whether I should kill you.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That sent a chill through my body. He really had tried to kill Atsuki, and he was willing to kill me.{w} What we wanted was to leave the building safely, and by keeping Sai locked away, I'd intended to prevent more things from happening. ...I began to worry about my decision.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why do you look scared? You're the one with a knife.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I suppose that was a little misleading. I'm not trying to kill you. As I said, I'm debating whether I should.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You remember what I said, right? You will die—that's a guarantee. Because I pretty much know it for a fact, I'm wondering whether I should make it happen myself.{w} Since I have confirmation of your death, it's very likely that if I try to push you into a wall, I'll kill you. I have no reason to think I'll end up safe, though. That knife you have is pretty scary, and I wouldn't want to be recorded.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Y-You're still saying that I'm going to die? Why...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Because I've seen it. Are you really unaware that the blood in the lobby is yours?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's not...! That wasn't my blood.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Then we go back to what I already said. I know what I'm saying for certain, but the details of it are a mystery to me.{w} I do feel bad for you. You were in a coma for a while, right? If I remember correctly, the name that was put out was yours. It's unfortunate that you'll die here after surviving that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I raised the knife to protect myself. The likelihood that he was telling the truth kept growing as he talked. Did that really mean that I was close to dying? Would it just be him who would do it? ...Or was he making it up to scare me?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd seen Atsuki's face when he'd been told about that supposed fate of mine. The way he'd looked, and nothing more, was enough motivation to fight for my life.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm trying to sympathize with you, but it's not easy when you're pointing that knife at me.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Where did you even find this?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Haven't I told you already? If you want to keep asking questions, don't repeat them.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: His prediction that I would die had allowed him to assert control again, which was probably intentional. I tried to erase the worry from my face.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I didn't say anything else, he went back to thinking. With a few steps of separation, we both stood, silently on alert.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Minutes later, nothing else had happened, but I'd realized one thing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We had gone some minutes to the past. Given that we hadn't heard anything around us, it was very likely we'd arrived at a time after Atsuki and I left the attic due to being chased.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That meant that the entrance to the attic was locked, so if Atsuki hadn't also appeared inside, he had no way to reach us. I had no reason to think he would have appeared with the key.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked inside my purse and saw that the key to the attic was still inside. Just like the knife, it had appeared with me in the bedroom despite there being no possible location to be replicated that met those conditions...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey, Shiroya, how much time do you think we traveled? It's not like we went an hour back, right? Twenty or thirty minutes, I'd say.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He had taken a few steps closer without alerting me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I-I don't know.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Well, don't you think we've passed that threshold already? Shouldn't we get going?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He wants to leave. Does that mean that he can still do what he wanted? It's not possible we went much farther back, is it...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Not going to say anything?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I thought a bit more.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I shouldn't believe anything that he says just because he sounds convincing. He's sounded convincing before at times when I knew for a fact he was lying.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: He knows more about how the Sekimeiya works but is refusing to say anything, so he has a reason to keep that to himself.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: He definitely has something in mind, and maybe if he reveals it, whatever he's planning won't work. ...But I can make sure that it won't work as long as we stay here.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The problem is Atsuki. If he could enter the attic, I could tell him what's happening without unlocking the door.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If he didn't travel, around now is when he should start to search for us.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't decide. It was very possible that the force behind most of what had happened throughout the day was Sai. There wasn't a lot of time left until {time=21}, and if I could seclude him during that last stretch, we had the chance to leave safely.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi, Isla, Katei, and Erina have died. The people behind that had to be either Sai or Akaro.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And the recorder, which has contents that are practically impossible, could've been arranged with Sai, Akaro, and Isla. Not only that, but Sai had a knife, and he already proved to be a deadly threat to Atsuki and probably me. If we just stay here, he won't be able to harm him or use the Sekimeiya again.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Of course, the recording itself was fabricated using the Sekimeiya. Sai knows the most about it, so he's the perfect person to be responsible for it. ...Why would he create that? Why would Isla have it?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If he's been lying recently... Why would he say that I'll die or that the blood in the lobby is mine? That's impossible. That blood can't be mine, so why would he say it?{w} It matches with the recording because I wasn't mentioned once in it. Could it be that he's consistently trying follow a story that he's set up?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And either way, I can't die as long as we stay here and I protect myself. Does that mean that if I decide to leave, Sai's claims become the truth?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I can't decide. ...Because if Sai isn't the culprit, then it's Akaro, who could be anywhere, and then Atsuki would be up against him alone.{w} Both Akaro and Sai have acted suspicious in their own ways, and Sai sounded hostile toward him earlier. ...But that could easily be a trick since they escaped the bedroom together.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: On the other hand, if Akaro's the one we need to worry about, it's hard to imagine we'll be able to do anything to stop him even after leaving the bedroom.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...So keeping Sai shut in here is the safest move. The only real problem is that I can't tell Atsuki what's happening unless he gets into the attic.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Hello?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}I won't move.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: What? ...Why? That's not what you said earlier.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You tried to kill Atsuki and threatened me. There's no way I'll just let you go.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Hey, aren't you the one currently threatening me?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you sure you can do this? Will you kill me if I try to unlock the door and leave? Remember that you're being recorded.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You shouldn't try it.{w} Also, I don't think the cameras are recording.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I shouldn't? There's a time travel device downstairs, so I'm having trouble understanding why I shouldn't try to resist abandoning it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Is that what you want? The Sekimeiya for yourself?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: It would be pretty stupid to deny that. I'm sure you wouldn't turn it away either.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I didn't want to humor him anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He didn't say anything else, so the quiet returned.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is that it? Have we decided that we'll spend the rest of our time in here? It should only be a bit more than two hours unless we went really far back, which wouldn't make sense.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd spent a large amount of time standing up, so I sat on the bed. I took the strap of my purse from around my neck so that Sai wouldn't knock me down if he pulled on it and left it at my side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He paid no mind to it and kept looking at the floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I still felt severely conflicted and worried about Atsuki's situation. Although the more I thought, the more I felt I couldn't let Sai free, and it was highly unlikely I could successfully lock him in from outside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Time kept moving in the silent attic. We must have been alone, as the lack of sound was overwhelming.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Eventually, Sai stood up without opening his mouth. That was the first noise I'd heard in minutes, and I stared at him curiously.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He slowly stepped to the door with his empty hands raised.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What are you doing...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I saw him gripping the handle, and my heart sped up with uncertainty. However, when he tried to open the door, the lock prevented it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Oh, it's locked. Right.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: By the way, you never reattached the chain, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The chain? What are you talking about?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Nothing.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He shook his head and retreaded his steps.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I saw his nonchalant look while I was still frowning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you just try to leave?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Absolutely not.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}Is this how you and Akaro escaped the bedroom the last time? That was what Atsuki suspected.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: By trying to open a locked door?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: By opening it and then going back in time to unlock it. Did you wait until now to try it because it was unlikely it would've worked earlier?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: You're incorrect.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He approached the drawer stand and took the screwdriver out of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What's that for?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Don't worry, I don't want to use it as a weapon. Who reattached the handles?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...It was me and Atsuki, after everyone left.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: You didn't do it right, then. From here, I noticed it was a little loose, and I just turned it to see if I was right. You didn't attach it properly.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I looked at the handle and didn't see anything wrong with it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Holding the screwdriver, Sai stepped to the door again. I moved back a little, afraid of the sharply pointed tool.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He inserted it into one of the screws and removed it. Then, he unscrewed the one in the opposite corner while I stared, dumbfounded. I didn't know what he was doing, but messing with the handle wouldn't let him open the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: See? These two go in the bottom. You swapped them.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What are you talking about? They're the same.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He ignored me and unscrewed the last two, which dropped the handle to the floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No, they aren't. You don't understand much about screws, do you?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I stood up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Move away. I don't know what you're trying to do, but stop.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...I'm not trying to do anything, though. Do you not want me to attach it properly?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No. Step back.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He sighed and backed off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I guess I locked myself in even further.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He left the screwdriver in the drawer and looked at his feet, biting his lower lip.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I sat back on the bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Soon after, out of nowhere, he sat on the other side of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't sit here.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: What? That's just rude. I'm tired.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Stand up.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: *sigh* Fine.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But instead of standing up, with a very quick motion, he extended his arm toward me. Startled, I looked down and saw he'd unzipped my purse.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh—!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I stood up fast enough, tightly gripping my purse and the knife.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, damn it.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: My heart quickly calmed down as I stared at his childish expression.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck are you doing...!?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: It was just a joke. I couldn't have left anyway since you have that knife with you.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}You remember what you asked earlier, right? Yes, if you get close to me again, I will use the knife. Don't move again.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: All right. You can't even take a simple joke.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He let his body fall and lay on the bed, yawning while face-down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Stand up.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I don't think so. Sorry, I just wanted the bed for myself. You told me not to get close to you, so I won't. I'm tired—I said so earlier.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I didn't care anymore. I approached the desk and sat on it, resting my back on my purse and protecting it against the wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There you go. That's much better.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He repositioned his face on the pillow and closed his eyes.{w} ...A couple of minutes later, he hadn't moved at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd buried my face in my knees. What was happening outside the attic? A piercing pain had arisen in my chest, and there was no getting rid of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I began to heavily regret my decision when I considered the possibility that I wouldn't see Atsuki again. ...What if he had already been attacked?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I raised my eyes and saw Sai still lying down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's no way he won't hear me if I try to leave, right...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I jumped back a little when he moved. After a long yawn, he sat up and stretched his arms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He saw me staring at him but didn't react. Instead, he crouched to grab the handle from the floor, stood up, and turned around.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I heard a sound, but I didn't believe it. Regardless, the door opened, and Sai removed the key he'd inserted into the keyhole.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I didn't run to the door because I knew I was doomed. The handle was detached, so as soon as I stood up, Sai would close the door, locking me in behind him. Frozen, all I could do was ask what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You really didn't see that I took the key from your purse? You thought I'd only unzipped it? I have it right here.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I couldn't believe it, but he had the key in his left hand. While I processed what he'd said, his smile widened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: W-Wait... Is this why you removed the handle?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Of course. Otherwise, it's unlikely I could've repaid the favor and locked you in. I figured it was only fair. I can't believe you didn't realize I wanted the bed for myself just to be closer to the door than you. You're not very smart, are you?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai, what are you—
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Now, goodbye. I have things to do.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: From the hallway, I heard Sai locking the door. That didn't matter, because even if he left it unlocked, I had no way to leave.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Still trying to wrap my head around what had happened, I stood up slowly and approached the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't open it. It was exactly the same way all of us had previously locked ourselves in that very bedroom. Sai had left with the handle and the key, so I knew I had no way to get out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No... Now Atsuki's definitely in danger.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Sai...! Come back! Just for a second...!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: There was no response. The attic felt just as desolate as when Sai had been there.{w} I noticed that I still had the knife in my hand. I slid it through the gap of the door, trying to push open the latch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I frantically moved my arm up and down, but it simply got stuck in the middle.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai...!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I knew he wouldn't come back. Trying to calm my nerves, I sat on the bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm sure he used the elevator because he shouldn't be able to leave through the main door. That means the attic is still locked. Not even he should be able to enter again once he leaves.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Or maybe that's not right. ...When Atsuki and I locked ourselves in the attic, Sai was able to come in anyway.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Is there nothing I can do...? I can't take this door down.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I tried to go over ways to leave, but I couldn't think of anything. All at once, the overwhelming stress came back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My hand began to hurt, so I stopped pounding on the door. There was no way for me to reach anyone or for anyone to reach me. Inside a locked building, on a locked floor, I was trapped in that locked room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I realized I hadn't gone to the higher level of the bedroom. I climbed up the ladder, but I couldn't find anything. The only traces of life were the messy sheets from the time we'd been waiting there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Would I have to spend two hours there? I could only feel the piercing pain strengthening, threatening to eventually leave me breathless.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I have the only key to the attic Katei mentioned. ...There's no way the police won't have another one, right...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...At least I have the knife, so Sai won't be able to use it, and he said he didn't want to harm Atsuki anymore.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Why did we have to come here...? We should've just stayed home...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I hated it, but I couldn't avoid thinking about the worst possibilities. The thought of losing my two friends in as many weeks was unbearable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every time I managed to calm my thoughts, they returned, more and more terrifying. It was impossible for me to fall asleep, and the pain in my chest increased if I tried to lie down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I spent the time thinking miserably in front of the door, the persistent fear that I might've let the killer run free with Atsuki unprotected eating away at me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even after what I'd already experienced, the way I felt then was far beyond anything I'd ever known. If I could describe Miiya's death as an earthquake, I was experiencing one an order of magnitude higher.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It hadn't been easy to accept her death, and I, of course, still hadn't moved past it. But it was incomparable. Knowing for a fact that a friend had died was far less of a strain than fearing that a friend could be about to die.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Both were horrific, but only one of them involved fear, and Atsuki being in danger potentially due to my own failure only made it worse. I imagined that if any kind of hell existed, the way I felt while alone in that room must have come close.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...o that? ...uki?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I looked back abruptly the moment a voice reached my ears. More than ten minutes had passed when I perceived that sound coming from directly behind the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey! Are you there!?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Was that Sai...? Nobody else could've entered the attic.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Open the door! Who are you!?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: There was no response.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't imagine it, right?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I hadn't—there was another sound. The other bedroom opened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I just heard you! Please, open the door!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Once again, there was no response.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is Sai ignoring me? Either that, or someone traveled to the attic.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...You're still here, right? What are you planning?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I breathed hoarsely before letting out more exhausted yells.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I know you're here! At least answer!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He just walked away...!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Please! At least say something!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Rather than exert myself any further, I simply focused my hearing. It made no difference.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What are you doing!? Please, come back!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Nothing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What is he doing...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Hey...!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: All I could hear were my desperate breaths.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did he only now leave the attic, then?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I defeatedly fell on the bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Soon, my vision began to fade. I'd drained some of the scarce energy I had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Thankfully, the inside of my head had gone numb, so I could finally stop thinking. The lancing pain in my chest intensified, but I was able to withstand it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Minutes were passing by, but it didn't feel like it. I didn't close my eyes or try to relax. The only thing I could feel was despair.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Uh... What the fuck?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wh—
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A new voice. That time, it came from the room I was in, and I recognized it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I lifted my head without thinking and saw Sai standing in the middle of the bedroom. As soon as he saw me, he dashed toward the door, but I rapidly stood up as I grabbed the knife next to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: H-Hey, chill with that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He stepped back while I tried to understand what was happening.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did I really travel to this goddamn bedroom? That's just unfortunate.{w} What's with that look? You're still here? How long has it been? ...I guess I just trapped myself.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I cleared my throat, feeling unable to speak.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...D-Did you just travel from the future?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yeah, maybe. How long have you been here?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I looked at his wristwatch, but the display was still blank.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you have the key?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...The key? No.{w} Answer my question. How long has it been since I left?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I don't know, maybe half an hour! Show me what you have!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I approached him slowly, staying at a distance that prevented him from grabbing the knife. If he still had the key he'd snatched from my purse, I had to leave immediately.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't you get that it's impossible I still have the key? It's like you said a while ago.{w} I just appeared in the middle of this bedroom, looking at the door. Obviously, that coordinate is from the time you were in front of the door, pointing the knife at me. At that point, I didn't have the key yet.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Just show me your pockets.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Sure. I can do that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Start with your hip pack.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: My hip pack? Of course.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He unzipped it. Inside, I noticed a key that he hadn't had in the past.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey, it's not for this bedroom.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He handed it to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is for the bathrooms, right? Did you kill Katei?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I wouldn't do that to him. It would be like punching a kid for getting into the cookies, they don't know better. Anyway, let's continue.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I left the bathroom key on the drawer stand. Then, Sai placed a hand on the right pocket of his pants and highlighted the outline of a key. Following that, he took it out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was the key to the Sekimeiya cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He kept it and continued by putting his hand in his left pocket.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No. ...Stop.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Show me everything you have in the other pocket.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: What? I just showed what I had.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Do it.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He put his hand inside the right pocket and brought out another key.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, shit. Isn't this the key to this very bedroom?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Give it to me.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...Fucking Atsuki. How did he get me with this?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I left the key on the drawer stand and looked at Sai sternly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's the key to the other bedroom.{w} Take your hand out of the pocket.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Turn it inside out.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Hesitantly, he did so.{w} One last key remained inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck? What were these doing in my pocket?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: So he had the key because he touched the Sekimeiya with it, just like how I appeared here with the knife because I had it when I traveled. ...Atsuki and I were definitely wrong.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Give me the key.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Hm... You can't expect me to give you anything when you're pointing at me with that scary knife.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I'm not approaching you to give you anything.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Then just throw it!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I've had too many awkward moments trying to do that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai, throw me the key.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: All right, we'll do the following.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He turned around and began to quickly climb up the ladder.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What are you doing!? Come down!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I didn't even have time to consider following him. Seconds after he had disappeared from view, he jumped back down to where I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He extended both of his hands. They were empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is how I'm giving you the key. I left it up there so that you can obtain it without me getting close to that pointy knife.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What? No. Go get it.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Well, that's not happening.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What are you trying to do? Do you still have it and want me to go up so you can leave?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Oh, not at all. I'm not like that.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I can show you my pockets if you want.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He showed the contents of all his pockets, and except for a single key, they were identical to the time we'd all showed our possessions.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, I also have the attic key, but I guess that doesn't matter much to you.{w} Are you happy now? Do you think I might have it in my hair? It's pretty messy today. Maybe in one of my shoes?{w} Don't worry, I left it up top.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He kept clearing places where he might've hidden the key on himself until I was forced to accept that he didn't have it anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Anywhere else?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What is he doing...!? Could he have hidden it somewhere in this section of the bedroom and I didn't realize?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Wait in that corner.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: No problem.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He approached the empty corner of the room and leaned back with a carefree face. I glanced all around, thinking about whether he could've left the key anywhere before climbing up the ladder. I knew I hadn't seen anything, but I couldn't trust it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Indecisive, I looked through the few places I could think of where a key could've been hidden. The bed, the wardrobe, the drawers... I didn't find it anywhere, as it was impossible he had hidden it to begin with.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What are you even searching for? I just left it there, below the bed.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Then go get it!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I don't want to.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I walked up to him slowly, running out of breath.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Whoa, what's with that face? You wouldn't be thinking of killing me in front of those cameras when I'm just trying to give you a key, would you?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why don't you go up first and then I follow you?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I'm way too tired to climb this ladder again.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He wants me to go up so that he can leave me behind again. How, though...!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: You should believe me. If you hurry up, you might be fast enough to save him.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I came from the future, remember? I'm not exactly sure how far back I went, but it's possible Atsuki hasn't died yet.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}You're lying.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Me? I haven't lied all day.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No, you are...
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Am I? Are you sure...? I just found him dead, but I don't even know what happened to him. I guess it was Akaro.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No, it didn't matter that he could've been lying or that it was unlikely the past could be changed. Before I could keep thinking, I was hastily climbing the ladder.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I crouched next to the bed and looked under it. It was dark, so I had to wait for my vision to adjust.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Bye!
entries.speaker: sai4

entries.text: There's no way.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't react. I just kept looking at the floor, where there was nothing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I crawled back out and stood up, unable to raise my head. I glanced down through the hatch and saw the empty bedroom with the door closed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He was... lying. He had to have been.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't move. I didn't know what had happened, but all my energy was directed at denying what Sai had said.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once I got back down, I examined the door and saw that nothing about it had changed. There was still no way to open it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't knock on the door or yell. I just sat down, staring at my lap.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It kept happening. Every time I thought I couldn't feel more miserable, I did.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: During the minutes I sat paralyzed on the floor, I didn't perceive any sound. Once again, I was alone in the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And so I began to think that perhaps I didn't want to leave. If what waited for me outside was what I'd been told, it was better to stay inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Fortunately, that thought was what let me snap out of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No, I need to leave. Was Sai able to leave without the key? There's no way, right? He was just able to hide that he had it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stood up and tried to think rationally. There was nothing around that indicated what he'd done.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was nothing under the bed, so he was just lying about leaving the key there. He only wanted me to go up so he could lock me in again.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The key I'd left on the stand was still there. I knew it wasn't the right one, but I tried to use it anyway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The door didn't unlock.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I did all I could to dispel the fog in my mind and think about what had happened. I had to leave urgently, and if there was a way out, I needed to find it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went up to the second level and looked below the bed again. Without a doubt, there was nothing there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He closed the door when he left, so he definitely opened and left through it...!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Is it possible he opened it without the key? That shouldn't be it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The way he could've left the bedroom the very first time... by opening the door, going to the past, and unlocking it... That shouldn't have been possible either because there was no handle to open it from the inside even if it had been unlocked from the outside.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Is it possible that he approached the door, saw it open, traveled to the past, and opened it from the outside to let himself leave? Could he have known enough about the Sekimeiya to pull that off?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If so, I might have been able to do it myself. I climbed down and stared at the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't opening. ...Was that not possible?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It hadn't worked for Atsuki when he tried it. Maybe it really wouldn't ever occur.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to think more about it. How could I open the door?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: For even longer, I stood still, mustering all my remaining mental strength to figure out how to escape.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...How had Sai done it? Had he used the key? If so, how?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Wait.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Did I let him do this?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: This is it. There's no way it's not.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: As soon as I thought back on one thing, the way Sai had escaped appeared in my head.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When he appeared in the middle of the bedroom... Of course, he even said it.{w} That location belonged to the time I'd been blocking his path to the door.{w} That's how he escaped the first time. At that point, the key to the bedroom was already in his pocket, which is why he had it when he appeared from the future. Atsuki said it too, that he grabbed it when he was chasing us.{w} But, for some reason, there was another key in the drawer. At some point, the key got duplicated.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The time he snatched the key from my purse... it only felt like he unzipped it. That's all he did. He tricked me into thinking that he'd grabbed the key, when in reality he left with one he had from the beginning. ...Did he just make me think I was trapped?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I looked at the desk. That was where I'd left my purse a while ago.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And the only place in this bedroom I didn't search... was in my own purse, where he knew the other key still was.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I approached it and looked inside. Of course, the key was missing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...He just wanted me to go up so he could grab the key from my purse. It's still unzipped.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I set my eyes on the hatch and rapidly made my way up the ladder.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I'm right, the other key must be somewhere here in the second level. He just hid it better to trick me.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There weren't many places to look through. I frantically went through all of them in search of a very small key.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As soon as I started unzipping the leftmost mattress, a metal key fell to the floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I breathed deeply before picking it up and clambering down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I grabbed my purse, ran to the door, and inserted the key. It finally opened, and I saw the walls of the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I sped toward the living room while I stored the knife in my purse and took the attic key out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The most recent footprints there were definitely Sai's, which went to the staircase. I rapidly followed them down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...!{w} You're all right!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He's okay. Sai was just lying. Thank God.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I panted, suddenly realizing that I was out of breath.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Oh, she was actually inside. I'm glad we found you.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wh-What!? He locked me in here!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Me? That's funny. I locked you in, but the key's in the keyhole, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Was he acting like he wanted to find me? He locked me in the bedroom!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I'm sorry?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I've been here for almost two hours! He shut me in!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: So you chose to hole up in the attic and want to blame me for it... why, exactly?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I couldn't look at Sai anymore. No matter whether he was the person behind everything, I hated him and the unquestionable malice behind his actions. However, {time=21} was very close, and creating more conflicts would only be a problem.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you okay?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes... I just ran from the bedroom. I'm fine.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Let's pretend I locked you in a bedroom. I'm not sure why I'd even do that, but how did you leave?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...With the key.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: But I thought I trapped you there?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Yes, but not with the key! I know what you did!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I became a witch and learned magic, huh? We can go with that if you don't want to tell the truth.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...W-Wait! Erina!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I suddenly processed what I was seeing without tunnel vision and saw Erina next to them, her clothing coated in dried blood.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're alive?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Y-Yes...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I'm sorry if this sounds strange, but are you the same Shiroya who disappeared from the event room with Sai?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Hm? Yes, I've been here since then.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I... see.{w} We didn't check Erina's pulse, remember...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: O-Oh! Thank God, and sorry...
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: After thinking incorrectly for so long, I felt immensely relieved. Despite all that had happened, those of us who were still alive, including Erina, had to make it out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's with the blood, though?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I don't know. I got hit in the head, so my memories are a little fuzzy.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Oh. ...What time is it?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Hm... It's {time=19:40.}
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It's so late... What happened while I was here? And your watch is working again?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Huh? Yes, of course.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wait, what's with your clothes? You were wearing different ones.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Right. When we went to the past, we lost track of that Shiroya, but she still has to be around. I'm confused, though. Where did she come from?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wh-What...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I waited for a response, but nobody gave one. Had the version of me that Atsuki saw reappeared...?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Can you come with me for a second?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Y-Yeah.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Can't you just talk openly here?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Atsuki ignored him and brought me to the fifth floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You know Sai's lying, right? He really locked me in a bedroom and told me you died...! I was so worried.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: What...? Don't worry, I believe you, even though I still don't understand Sai very much. I wanted to tell you about what just happened.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Hm?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I think... the past can be changed somehow.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It can...? Did you try it?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I did, but I'm not sure what to make of the results.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Those few words made me drop everything I had assumed. After what we'd experienced, was it actually possible for us to undo what had already happened?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's possible what I changed only affected some people. I definitely went back in time and altered the events I'd experienced. Sai recognizes the change, but I'm not sure Erina does.{w} It felt like both realities met, leading into differing memories. That could be what happened to Akaro, when his version of events contradicted ours. Maybe someone made some change that didn't affect us, or maybe it didn't affect Akaro.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: That sounds way too complicated... I'm not sure I follow, but you mean...
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: If we go to the past, I'm pretty sure we could drastically change the way things played out. It's possible some people would still remember this reality, but the change should persist.{w} It's possible two realities just converged, but the real one comes from my change. It overlapped the last one despite some people potentially still remembering it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: So then... We just have to want to change the past? Is that the only requirement?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If we travel to the point Isla died, we can overwrite her death...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd long ago decided I wouldn't touch the Sekimeiya again, but the most fundamental reason was that we'd concluded it wasn't possible to alter the past.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I recalled my own selfishness and how much I despised it. If we were able to undo what had happened but chose not to, that was infinitely worse.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's keep going.{w} I last traveled from the staff room. Let's go there.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We walked all the way down. In the reality where we were, many people had died. Even if changing the past was doable, how much could we really deviate from it?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That didn't matter. As long as we could prevent the suffering I'd felt for at least one person, we had to do it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We slowly reached the crystal floor. On the way down, I noticed that the smell hanging around us all day was getting stronger.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's all this blood...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: It's mine. As you can see, I hurt my hand in the elevator. I don't even know why it stopped bleeding.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Does it hurt? That's kind of a lot.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Don't worry, it's fine...
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We entered the staff room, and I saw that a new locker was open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...!{w} It's gone.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Did you leave it in this locker? How?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I found the key in the cleaning room. I know how that sounds, but I guess no one needed a key to get it. I touched it with the locker open.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh... Could anyone have taken it, then?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: It would've been easy, but I'm not completely sure. The door doesn't look like it moved, so it also could've teleported.{w} While you were in the attic, we saw that happen. I definitely witnessed the Sekimeiya teleport to its cabinet.{w} But Sai could've easily grabbed it. Akaro as well. I saw him, and he should still be here somewhere. It was before I changed the past, but all I did was draw attention to hallway A. There's no way that was enough to overwrite Akaro's existence.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We went to the event room and saw the empty cabinet. Once more, we wanted to find the Sekimeiya that someone might have hidden.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Since that morning, a recurring question had been why anyone would hide the Sekimeiya when it could easily be found. I'd thought of many possible answers, but if the past could be changed, it had always been a flawed question.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Of course, if anyone was directing things toward a future they wanted, they wouldn't want anyone to deviate things on their own with the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Like always, whether it teleported or someone hid it, it has to be nearby and in a place we can access. We can find it.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Was that person Sai, who knew the most about the Sekimeiya? Had an unknown person really orchestrated everything behind the scenes? I couldn't believe how fast I'd changed my mind and how much I wanted to find the Sekimeiya. Was it possible we could leave the tower in a world where I hadn't spent those two hours in that bedroom?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was taking Atsuki's word, but if we found the Sekimeiya, determining whether the past could be changed should've been simple. However, we had concluded before that it wasn't possible because it had already been attempted. A ton of things implied that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wanted to erase the painful hours we'd all spent in the tower. But if that was possible, what if we could stay there for a whole month? There would be much more we could undo.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The exit was near. In two hours, we were bound to learn about the future we'd be stuck with.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, yeah, the Sekimeiya's gone. I was searching for it before we went up.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I'm sure you were.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: There's not much time left... Let's wait for the shutter to open.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What about the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Who knows? I couldn't find it, but why do you care?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Akaro might be responsible, and he could have taken it outside. If that happened, there's nothing we can do.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: However, if it's still inside, the police will find it immediately, right? It can be hidden from us, but not from them.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Erina, do you know where the Sekimeiya might be?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: What...? No, I don't.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Then none of us do. If it was deliberately hidden, I don't see the point in searching for it anymore.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You know where it is, right?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He must be the one who's been taking it all this time, and he's definitely had a reason. He doesn't want us to search for it so that he can keep it where he has it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: You're free to enlighten me. If I knew where it was, what would my endgame be? Hoping the police don't find it? There's no way that would happen.{w} Someone took it when we weren't around. That must mean they have the means to keep it out of ours and the police's sights. Otherwise, hiding it is pointless.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Of course, that's only assuming the past can't be changed. With how much Sai's proven to know about the Sekimeiya, there's no way he's not aware of whether it can do that or not.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: You say that, but it's been happening since this morning, and it was never hidden in a place the police wouldn't have inspected.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: You could have a plan, too. When the police enter, as soon as they find the Sekimeiya, they'll activate it. That'll make everyone around it disappear, leaving a free path for you to retrieve it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Are you even listening to yourself? You think I want to steal the Sekimeiya? Sure, I wouldn't say no to having it, but that's not gonna work out.{w} First of all, they'd simply appear in the past. If a bunch of people time travel, the panic would ruin any kind of plan like that. At least a few people have to know what the Sekimeiya is capable of too, right? Why would they send the police to grab it if they know what touching it would do?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I think I agree with him... That wouldn't work.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Hiding the Sekimeiya is pointless, that's a fact. Incidentally, there's no place the police would ignore. What that means is that if the Sekimeiya's here, there's no reason to search for it. What I find most likely is that it's already outside, though.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: All right. I agree, so let's just wait.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I frowned as I looked at him, but he avoided meeting my eyes and glanced back at Sai instead.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Perfect. We've had enough headaches, so let's go to the lobby.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Is this a bluff to waste time...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If we want to go to the past, we want the Sekimeiya to spend a while out of the cabinet, which we accomplish by doing what Sai wants for a while. Eventually, we can find it, just like we have every time we've extensively looked for it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Atsuki whispered to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did you lose the knife?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I shook my head and showed him my purse, still unzipped.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you get it from Sai after you two appeared somewhere?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: No... I still don't understand it either. Both of us appeared in the attic, and I already had it. I'd forgotten to mention it, but yeah, that doesn't make sense with how we thought the Sekimeiya worked.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Okay, let's sit around and wait. I'm exhausted and just want to get out, so I hope nothing else happens. Whatever Xyn or the culprit are up to is no concern of ours anymore...{w} I have no idea what happened to Akaro, but I don't care. If he's behind this whole mess, he'll face the consequences.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Exactly one hour and ten minutes. That's all we have to get through to reclaim our freedom.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: There was no reason to humor Sai anymore. I didn't believe for a second he wasn't lying. We sat on the left of the shutter without saying a word.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He had needed to leave the bedroom to finish up a part of his plan. He admitted that himself, so there was no way he simply wanted to get out of the tower while unaware of the Sekimeiya's whereabouts.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It can't be that he's not the same Sai, right...? No... Even though his watch is working, he definitely knows what happened in the bedroom.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We waited for a long time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was the ideal thing to do. If we were able to find the Sekimeiya, we would do it after it had gathered enough energy. If finding it wasn't possible, we were calmly going through the final stretch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If the recording was real, then we would either not find the Sekimeiya or changing the past would turn out to be impossible. However, I was convinced it was fake. No matter why it existed, it couldn't have been legitimate.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I spent some time going over all the possible outcomes. What if the Sekimeiya was in one of the temperature regulation cabinets, not gathering any heat?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If changing the past was possible, that was still fine. We could go a short time back, get it out of the cabinet, and progressively extend the distance traveled.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai continued to update us with the time. We'd spent 25 minutes sitting down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is it possible Sai's trying to trick us again?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What if he knows what we want to do? If he does, he could have set his wristwatch back a while to make it seem like we have more time. Did he anticipate things enough to have also edited the computer's time?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...The shutter could open at any moment.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stood up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Wait here. I'm going to the bathroom.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I'd been needing to go for a while, and I had to before walking through the whole building. According to Sai, there were forty minutes left, but we couldn't trust that. Once I came back, we had to find the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, all right.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Can't you wait?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: No. Don't worry, though, I won't go anywhere else.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I knew he'd insist on stopping me, so I went over to the hallway B door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I entered the left bathroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I jumped instantly, feeling my back burn.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The tank... was burning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew what that had to mean. I grabbed the top with both hands and lifted it up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya was on top of a pipe, touching the side I'd leaned on. It was well-balanced, positioned so that it didn't fall into the water.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How hot does it have to be for the heat to reach the other side...? And I still feel the burn.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But here it is... And it's working for sure.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The past could be changed. Were those words true?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If so, I knew I could go really far back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Should I tell them? ...Was it even Sai who left it here? He knew where I was going.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}Atsuki wanted to find the Sekimeiya and change the past. If I told him, I knew he would activate it. However, I wasn't sure I wanted that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: His desire was to erase the deaths we'd experienced, but that wouldn't occur if he changed the past. He would still remember them, and how would it even work? Would he be stuck in a world with another self of his?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If he went to the past and changed things, he would end up personally suffering for it and would remember everything. If I did that instead... he wouldn't.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We didn't know where Akaro was, but he or Sai had the best chance of being behind everything. If I went to tell the others that I'd found the Sekimeiya, it was very possible Sai would purposely always stay in range. He could then prevent the changes we wanted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And ultimately, it was a fact that they'd all said they talked to a self of mine I wasn't aware of. Would that end up being myself despite me being sure that it couldn't be the case?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If so, then I wouldn't be able to change the past. I was in the reality where that other self of mine appeared.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hovered my hand over the gem and felt the imposing heat around it, repelling me. I realized I couldn't breathe properly due to the strange smell from all day. It was at its greatest intensity yet, reaching oppressive levels.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With my left hand under my coat, I lifted the Sekimeiya out of the tank. Its heat was burning me through the cloth, but I resisted the intense pain.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is the last chance we have to save anyone. Maybe saving Miiya is impossible, but I'm holding the possibility to erase Erina's suffering, Isla's, Naomi's, or even Katei's. If that works, nothing should be undoable, and then I could tell Atsuki what I've done and work together with him to save Miiya.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I still knew he wanted to change the past, and maybe he didn't want to get rid of the memories he had. Who was I to decide that by myself and effectively erase the Atsuki I knew in that moment...?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I couldn't hesitate. If I chose not to activate the Sekimeiya, I might not have been able to live with myself. I couldn't accept acting only in my own self-interest.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I lowered my right hand slowly, toward the harmless-looking gem. I shut my eyes and gritted my teeth in pain, pushing through the burning aura until I made contact with the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At that point, Shiroya disappeared from the bathroom.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She also disappeared from the crystal floor and from Ashiya Tower. She went much farther through time than she had expected.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The oblivious people who remained in the lobby would soon realize that something had happened and would search for the missing Shiroya through all seven floors...
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Liquid Canvas
—Wha—{w=1} ...Ow.{w=0.8} Where... is this?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I felt my body lying on cold stone. I opened my eyes, but I couldn't see a thing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is this still the tower...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I tried to stand up, but my whole body hurt. When I moved, I realized I was wearing different clothes under my coat and that the air was much colder.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Ah...! What...!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I suddenly felt a throbbing pain in my head that stopped all my movements. It wasn't only my head—there wasn't a single part of my body that didn't hurt.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stayed still, hoping the unbearable headache would fade away. In the meantime, my vision began to adjust a little.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't see light anywhere, but I was still able to make out the space around me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is this underground...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That was all I could really tell, but when I looked up, I understood where I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The ceiling is broken, and there's a bit of light... That's where I fell from.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I was in some kind of channel, directly below the gem shop we'd gone to that day.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Bewildered, I tried to think. However, an immense headache was still numbing my mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did I appear here? From the tower?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't think that was it. I remembered traveling from the bathroom on the crystal floor, but something was amiss.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every time I'd gone through time, I'd instantly appeared somewhere. That time, I'd woken up on the ground, and my whole body hurt. ...Had there been something in between, then? It felt like there had to have been, but my mind was too foggy to know.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where am I? How far back did I go?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Under the thick, brown coat I usually wore, I identified the clothes I was in. They were the ones I'd woken up with in the hospital—the ones I'd worn the day Miiya died.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kept trying to push my mind for an answer, but I had no idea what had happened. When I finally collected myself somewhat, I noticed that I had my purse around my shoulder. I unzipped it and felt the interior with my hand.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The knife isn't here. Why did I not travel with it this time?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Wait, this...!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I retracted my hand, gripping a familiar object. After fiddling with it, a rectangular light appeared in front of me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was my phone. The time displayed was {time=21:10}, but I only wanted to look at the date. I navigated deeper into the settings menu to access the current date. Then, I stared at the screen, reading it over and over.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: November 30th.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait... that... doesn't make any sense.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: November 30th? Did I go fifteen days to the past?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That day, at that time, I was already in a coma. I'd fallen from that ceiling up there, and I woke up in a hospital room days later.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I looked around me, but I didn't see anyone else.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If that's where I am... has my old body already been taken to the hospital? But why does my whole body hurt? This has never happened before...
entries.speaker: nm
