entries.text: My mind felt really clouded. After touching the Sekimeiya, I'd woken up in that sewer. I hadn't instantly appeared there, so I didn't fully understand what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Could I have overwritten my past self since I touched the Sekimeiya while willing to change the past?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I tried to stand up, but a sudden, piercing headache made me collapse to the ground. My cheek hit cold stone again, and the faint light slowly vanished.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wanted to move, but none of my muscles responded. My entire body was sore, like I'd received countless punches. Even the scarce willpower to reopen my eyes left me, as if I'd exhausted all my energy in an instant.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My senses dulled—the world darkened—my coat tightly enveloped me—{w} And then it was gone.{w} The cold and pain disappeared too, leaving me floating in the middle of nowhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no sound. I was conscious, but I didn't know where I was or why I was there. My awareness became a single, thin stream devoid of thought.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The stressful events of the tower disappeared, and the tension I'd been holding in for the previous weeks vanished. A great sense of relief washed over me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No, I was on the ground in an underground tunnel. That fleeting notion sparked into my brain multiple times, but it was never enough to disrupt the silence.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The world was consumed by my growing existence until eventually I was the only thing in it. Perhaps it had always been like that. For longer than time itself, I drifted aimlessly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who was I? I was surprised to feel curious about that question. The nothingness had become the only thing I knew, so the tiniest vestige of uncertainty was enough to bring me into disarray.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A distant figure began to take shape in the darkness, and it grew until I became one with it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's... me.{w} ...And there's Atsuki.{w} Not from now, but when we were still children. Laughing. Playing. Having fun.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Hey, Shiroya! Check this out!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He handed me a small flower with dark purple petals, contrasting with the white world surrounding us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So pretty! I'm sure Danny would love it!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I gingerly placed the flower on the stuffed tiger's head, then held it up to my face.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wow! It looks so good on you, doesn't it?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Without missing a beat, the boy in front of me spoke up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm sure it would look nicer on you.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He took the flower off the toy and began fidgeting with my shirt.{w} When he was done, I couldn't help but smile.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Seamlessly, the world changed. We were riding on our bikes down the streets of Yushibana.{w} ...And then we were drinking hot chocolate after playing in the snow. One after another, fond memories played in my vision, and I once again became a child.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wasn't just experiencing memories, I also created new scenarios. We'd always wanted to hang out in the big cities, and that had become possible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The innocent pleasure dimmed softly as the world faded back to nothing. I couldn't object or resist, as if I was a baby on the verge of awareness.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After an eternity, my mind reawakened. Another figure appeared far in the distance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Miiya.{w} I liked her as a friend, but...{w} When did it get so complicated?{w} She was gone. But even when she was alive, things didn't feel completely right. Myriad moments of before her death flowed into my mind. We were smiling and laughing in all of them, but as I watched us from above, I just wondered if she'd ever actually considered me a friend. We had spent time together, but I wasn't sure what it had meant.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She joined our little world and warped it into something different. Not better, not worse, just different. And her departure made it very different once again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We had access to a time travel device. We had no idea how it worked, but could we use it to rescue her?{w} Did I... even want to rescue her?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Of course I did. Anything to bring us back to a sense of "normal". Anything to bring back the happier days.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Were the days with Miiya better than the days without her? Yes, but... why? Why was it all so messy?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My existence folded in on itself. A momentary jolt, a sense of disorientation, running around in the darkness.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was the Sekimeiya a blessing or a curse? An object that reworked the flow of time. An object that kept us confined in the past...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My senses dulled again. I kept drifting in the dark and gentle abyss. Or maybe I wasn't drifting at all. I realized I didn't know anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I felt a cold breeze as the darkness began to lift. Part of me wanted to stay there forever, wrapped in black.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The sensation of possessing a body gradually came back to me. My limbs existed again.{w} In an instant, I became acutely aware of a pain in my cheek. I was resting on a pebble.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked around me, the faint light illuminating the sewer. My eyes were wet, almost as if I'd been crying.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm... still underground. What just happened?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: My head throbbed relentlessly while I came to terms with the realization that I'd fallen unconscious. After so long, I tried to move my arm and received a faint response.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Right... I just traveled from the tower. It's November 30th... Again.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I exhaled deeply, pulling myself together. That dream, if it could be called that, was almost like the coma I'd been in once already, a haze of half-concepts. It was almost frightening how lost I'd gotten in it.{w} I remembered fragments of it, but the question of whether I wanted to save Miiya was still vividly present in my mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Of course I want Miiya to live. What kind of question is that? And what would Atsuki do without her?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I rested for a bit longer, trying to drive off those intrusive thoughts, until I was eventually able to sit up. I was still lost in the dark, so I pulled out my phone and looked at the time. It was {time=21:34.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's only been about thirty minutes...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I laboriously stood up and took some mindless steps. I couldn't feel anything around me except the hard concrete. I supposed it wasn't a sewer that I was in since it didn't really smell at all, but I had no idea what it was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait... What am I supposed to do now? Can I really change the past? What the hell is this? Did I appear two weeks into the past, but mere minutes too late to save Miiya? It can't be, right...? Why would I have gone so far back?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Completely perplexed, I walked forward, toward the darkness. It wasn't possible to reach the hole above me, so I had to hope I could walk out of there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After a few steps, I ran into a wall. The darkness should've been terrifying, but I wasn't scared. I needed to get out of there and hope I could find out where I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I flipped open my phone, but the light from the screen wasn't enough to illuminate the path ahead. After feeling the space, I knew there were two tunnels in front of me, one much larger than the other.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could only go through one, so I kept walking toward the one that seemed wide and dry.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I can change the past... can I prevent the attack in the tower from happening? I can at least prevent Atsuki and myself from going there, but would this really work?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What would happen to me? I've already thought of this, but if I change the past, would I remain in a world with another version of myself?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And if I can do that, should I? Instead of trying to travel back one more time and save Miiya in the first place?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}The darkness had become absolute. On that day, the Sekimeiya must've been somewhere. As Ashiya's announcement had already been made public, they were probably keeping it somewhere in the tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked for minutes, every individual step feeling surreal, and the bright image of the screen frozen in my mind. November 30th...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kept going, hugging the wall next to me. At one point, the path began to slant up, making every step tougher.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...How do I get out of here? Should there be a ladder somewhere?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: For an entire day, I'd grown used to hearing the echo of my own footsteps with no other sound. I wasn't in that tower anymore, but the sensation was identical.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I slowly increased my pace. I was so close to finally being outside again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The tunnel was a straight path, seemingly unending. After walking for a while, I started to feel a little desperate.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was I going toward an exit, or was I completely lost? I couldn't see anything that distinguished where I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was too dedicated to my path to turn around and go the other way. It almost felt like there would be a monster waiting behind me if I did. I could only keep moving, almost like I was in a dream of an ever-lengthening corridor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Finally, that sensation ended. I located a ladder and climbed out of the channel's end. Around me was a grassy field covered in snow, the sky firmly situated above me. It was real.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't fathom the image. In front of me, I saw Yushibana, entirely still. A chilly breeze forced me to shrug my coat higher and cover my neck.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been trapped for hours in a building I could see the faintest outline of on the horizon, but that wasn't all. Seeing Yushibana below me brought a relief I hadn't known was possible. Seeing that I'd been released, all my questions fell away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know why I was atop that hill or what had happened to me. All I knew in that moment was a soaring sense of liberty. I was actually free.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked inside my purse again and saw keys.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: These belong to my apartment. They're not Atsuki's.{w} ...The tickets aren't here either.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I pushed off the snow on the stone that formed the tunnel and sat on it. Every part of my body still hurt, especially my back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was breathing calmly, observing the silent town. From there, I could see the entirety of Yushibana. Close to me was the school I'd gone to and a familiar park next to it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no way to really be sure, but I assumed that the tunnel I'd gone through was part of some kind of drainage system. It sloped down the hill into the center of town, and I couldn't think of any other function for it than collecting water that would otherwise flood.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It didn't really matter. I was out. The drainage channel, or whatever it was, hadn't swept me away or drowned me. That long tunnel was a path to salvation. I didn't know the true state of the world I was looking down on, but all by myself, I was finally able to experience peace.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Forcing myself to move, I stood up and began to descend a thin path that started from the tunnel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I sensed my boots pressing on the snow until I was down the hill. Upon turning around, I saw the trail of footprints that I'd left. ...As bizarre as it was, I looked at them as proof that I was really there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My phone showed {time=21:48}, and I was behind my school, where I'd rarely ever been at such a time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Much farther in the distance, I could see the top of the only structure that rivaled Ashiya Tower's height.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The hospital... Is that where I am right now? Or am I being brought there?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't comprehend yet how the travel had worked, but I walked around the school and found myself in the park we'd been at that very day.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I started to hear faint voices around me and saw dark silhouettes next to one of the benches. Of course, I wasn't alone in the town.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Unaware of where I was headed, I followed the steps we'd taken at a time that felt like a distant past.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Tall, round lights illuminated the rustic part of Yushibana. That day, we'd just happened to end up at a modest shop, but the present me deliberately walked to it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What will happen if they see me? There's gotta be someone there. ...That's bound to change the past, right?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I remembered all the narrow streets. No light could be seen through almost any window, and most of the footprints still on the ground ended at various doors.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked from the final turn and stared at where the shop had been.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: In front of the door were two people talking to each other. One of them wore a suit, and the other wore casual clothes for the cold.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't recognize either of them.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Should I step forward? What would they ask me, and how would I answer anything?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I chose to stay still. If the past could be changed, that wasn't the way to do it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to them was the window that had once grabbed our attention. I couldn't hear anything they were saying, but they hadn't sensed me either.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Not long after, the man in a suit walked away. The other person saw him off and stayed where he'd been. That gave me the chance to look at his face.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh... It's the owner of the shop.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The other man was walking toward me, so I backed off toward another path to avoid being seen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I suddenly bumped into a car camouflaged by the dark. In the sky, the moon was hardly visible, not helping things. Fortunately, the snow on the ground told me where I was every step.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I seemed to be the only person there, so I kept going until I arrived at a road full of wheel marks.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The streets were wider, and a couple walked by me. After so long, there was life around me, and the strain on my shoulders slowly faded away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Should I just go home?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Atsuki was also brought to the hospital, and I was there for a week. I have the keys, so I really can just do that.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: For what purpose was I in the past, standing next to a lonesome streetlight? I knew I had to do something. I could change history... But sleep was the only thing on my mind. My body still felt battered and weakened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Getting to my bed was my priority. Everything else had become a background concern, as there was nothing I could do right then.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why am I so tired? I feel different from when I was in the tower. ...Is it because this is how I was at this time on November 30th?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: My apartment was close by, and I needed to rest. At that time of night, nobody should've been there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The cold was starting to get to me, so I tightened my coat around my shoulders as I walked. Taking my time, I observed my surroundings as I walked, all of them covered in the same white layer of snow.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What will I do...? I can only hope that I'll understand everything better tomorrow, but I should have enough time to think about it. If I'm right... my parents aren't even in Japan, I'm about to spend a week in the hospital, and then I'll go to live with Atsuki. I can just be at my apartment until the 15th comes again.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But then what? Should I try to make us not go to the tower? How would I attempt to prevent the attack from happening? Even if Atsuki and I don't go, there are people who will die.{w} And in both cases, I'm giving up on going to the past again to save Miiya. If the past can be changed, I can't just leave her to die.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But this is still really scary. At the time I change the past, I'll be stuck in a world with another self of mine, and I won't be the original.{w} The me that Atsuki saw in the event room... will it really be me? Will I decide that I don't want to change the past just so that I keep living in a world where I'm the only version of myself? I wouldn't do that, would I?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Arriving home, I saw a few people talking to each other. They had no idea I was from the future. Of course, nobody knew about the Sekimeiya's powers yet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...How is that actually possible? The Sekimeiya has already been announced as a discovery, so why will they let the public touch it with what it can do? Did Ashiya not know about that? I have no idea where it even came from.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: In the past, all those questions still had no answers. I turned toward a narrower street full of apartment blocks and looked far ahead.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stopped in the middle of it and went up a white, metallic staircase. On the way, I took my keys out and walked to a door below a "C" plate.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood in front of it and tried to sharpen my hearing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I can't hear anything...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A little nervous, I inserted the key into the keyhole and kept it there for a while. Finally, I decided to turn it, making little noise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Should I try to be silent? If I'm somehow in here, do I want to not be heard? What would I even do if I see myself? I can't go anywhere else.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I opened the door slowly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The faint light of the night illuminated the way in, and I took a hesitant step forward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naturally, I knew where the light switch was, so I reached out to it while I glanced around. When the ceiling lit up, I saw the same entrance I'd seen countless times before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to the door, I saw my reflection in the mirror. I looked a lot better than I'd imagined, probably because the body I was in hadn't made it to December yet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I closed the door and stood in the middle of the room, not much warmer. I still felt uneasy, so instead of taking off my shoes, I opened the door to the living room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was a large window with its blinds closed, and in the center of the room, a wooden table on top of a green carpet. Everything looked like it had when I'd left on the 30th.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I really was at home. There was an old TV on top of a low stand that I rarely used due to the poor signal, and colored cushions were scattered all over the floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to me was the door to the kitchen. In the sink were the few dishes I hadn't washed, and in a corner was the laundry I hadn't finished. That day, I'd been really looking forward to meeting Atsuki and Miiya, and although we hadn't ended up doing much, I'd been excited to go.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I walked back and opened the other door in the entryway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After lighting up the short hallway, I stepped to the first door. My bedroom was behind it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Farther back were the last three doors. One led to my parents' bedroom, the other to the bathroom, and the last was a guest room with a small bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been storing things in the guest room since it'd been unused for so long, cramming a bookcase full. Recently, my drive to read had dropped off, but I still kept my favorites front and center.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nothing was out of place. Everything I'd put in there hadn't moved even slightly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There really is nobody here.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was the same modest apartment I'd always lived in, but it seemed like I'd last been there a very long time in the past.{w} I'd left a trail of slick, snowy footprints, so I went to the entrance and dropped my boots beside the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I entered my bedroom and draped my wet coat on a chair. My headache had been weakening, but many of my muscles were still sore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't even tell if I was hungry, and my thirst was dwarfed by how tired I was. I left my purse next to the bed and fell on it with the clothes I'd been wearing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I closed my eyes on top of the large pillow and gradually wormed my way under the blankets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was exhausted, but I didn't fall asleep immediately. There were too many things I had to think about.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd just spent more than twelve hours sealed inside Ashiya Tower, so the sensation of my bed was far beyond welcome. However, it seemed I had suddenly arrived on the day where everything started.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the distance of the town must've been Atsuki, crying about the possibility of losing his two closest friends. Somewhere else, other people were surely thinking about the attack they'd orchestrate on December 15th.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I soon felt like I should've turned on the heater, but I couldn't get out of bed. My mind went through most of the events I'd been caught up in, and I still didn't reach a single conclusion. I had wanted to change the past, but comfortable as I was beneath two blankets, that was comparable to moving a mountain by hand.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh—
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A sound reached my covered ears and woke me up. I was frightened at first, but I quickly realized it had come from outside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And it didn't stop.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Fireworks?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Hearing fireworks in Yushibana was rare, but it was the start of the holiday season.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I removed my head from under the blankets and paid attention to the sound. While it wasn't close to where I was, brief sparks of light could be seen through the window.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew the air was still chilly, but I braced myself and pushed the blankets aside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I sat up and looked at my phone. It was {time=1:06.}{w} When I looked behind me, I saw the large screen of glass turning orange momentarily, reflecting the distant light.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...They really are fireworks. I never hear them here because the police always shut them down, but I bet someone sneaked some into town and wanted to celebrate the holidays.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I see...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't help but feel as if they were welcoming me, although I knew the truth was far from that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was in a coma, so I'd never truly heard or seen those fireworks. There was nothing I wanted more than to view them with Atsuki and Miiya, but that couldn't happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Would it be possible to change the past so that it could?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The past is really changing, though.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It had already been changed. That I was seeing those fireworks was the proof.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was allowed to live through what I'd missed out on—the two weeks where I hadn't lived.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I simply stared at the distant lights. My eyelids were drooping, but I didn't want to stop watching.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The fireworks didn't last much longer. After a few minutes, the stronger ones went off, and they all calmly ceased.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I dropped back onto the bed, still with no energy to turn on the heater or put on warmer clothes. That time, I fell asleep almost instantly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened my eyes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Fresh Start
I wasn't in the attic. I was in my own bedroom, facing the pillow I'd evidently rolled off of.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The whole room was lit, sunlight streaming through the window. With my face still under the blankets, I closed my eyes again, not yet wanting to face the cold.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The first day of December...{w} Miiya's not here anymore, I'm in the hospital, and Atsuki's probably at his house.{w} Or, I guess I'm actually in my bed.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I vividly remembered parts of a dream I'd just had. We'd all still been in the tower, and while the details escaped my grasp, it had entailed a messy conflict with the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Out of nowhere, I realized I'd been lying in bed for a while without doing anything.{w} ...It had happened so quickly. It felt like just minutes ago I'd been waiting with everyone in the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been distressed in the tower, so why was I acting like nothing had happened? Was it just because I'd traveled to the past? Because there were two blank weeks ahead of me, and there was no reason to go over things I'd worried about once already? That logic didn't make a lot of sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd gone to the past to change it, and I hadn't known how far I'd go. Since I was in the hospital at the time, as long as I went to Atsuki's house, I'd be changing the past. If he saw two versions of myself, he would have to believe anything I said.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I didn't rush out of bed, and I probably knew the real reason why. It was sheer burnout.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In a way, it was similar to how I'd felt before meeting up with Atsuki and Miiya, the period when I had absolutely no idea what to do with myself. I'd gone nowhere and done nothing for an amount of time I couldn't measure. I had lost track of days, existing solely in my apartment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It had been a major depressive episode at the very least, but getting back together with not only one friend, but two, was the remedy for that. That was what I'd thought, anyway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Miiya had died, and I'd entered a coma. If I'd been living in a haze before, it evolved into a thick fog at that point. I was a shell of a person for a while, thinking almost exclusively about dangerously dark things. I was grateful that Atsuki hadn't given up on me entirely for everything I'd put him through.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it was a distinctly different situation. Rather than falling deeper into dysfunction, I had obtained a goal after going so far into the past. An abstract one, but a goal nonetheless.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kept lying there until my remaining tiredness dissipated. I knew I had to do something, but I didn't know what.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I gathered the strength to sit up and looked at the window. Going off the strong light, I had slept for quite a few hours.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My purse was next to the bed, so I grabbed my phone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {time=12:43.}..{w} It's late.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: As the buildings in Yushibana weren't very tall, I was able to see a good deal of the snow-covered town from my room. It wasn't snowing, and the sky was pretty clear. From behind the window, I felt as if I was aware of the fate of the entire town, even though what I knew was only related to a modest fraction of all those buildings.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The icy air quickly got to me, so I went to the hallway, carefully walking on the wooden floor so that I wouldn't stagger.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I reached the heater, which I'd normally only turn on during the nights since my parents were the ones who paid for my expenses and I didn't want to risk upsetting them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This will be fine, right? Nobody's supposed to be living here, but I doubt it'll be noticed that gas and water were used.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I hesitated a little, but I needed to get rid of the oppressive cold. Seconds after I turned the heater on, it let out a buzzing sound from the pipes running behind the wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I guess even if someone does notice, it'll be at the end of this month or maybe after that. It should be okay.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had a water bottle on the table. I never liked drinking tap water, so I always spent a bit of my monthly money on bottled water. Filters just weren't enough.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't bother pouring it in a glass. The hours I'd spent in Ashiya Tower no longer applied to my body, but I was extremely thirsty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: To avoid grocery shopping too often, I usually had a cabinet packed with supplies. I would refill it at the beginning of every month, which was why it was almost empty. I looked inside and grabbed a bag of mixed nuts. As expected, they weren't very good, as they had sat in the cabinet all month, but I ate all of them almost instantly due to how hungry I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked to the living room, almost like it was routine. The blinds were keeping the space dim, but I rarely bothered raising them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After going to the bathroom, I stood in front of my wardrobe, wondering which clothes to change into. I'd lived alone for many months already, so I started the day as if it were a normal one.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is it worth trying to make it seem like nobody's been here?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't know how, but if the past can be changed, I'm planning on doing it. There shouldn't be a huge need to hide my stay.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Or is that right? Could it be that while I was in the hospital and at Atsuki's house, another version of me was already living here? There's no way, is there? That would mean that everything will happen as I remember it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If the past will only change if I consciously make it, it shouldn't matter whether I was already living here in the reality I know. After all, I didn't come home for the purpose of changing the past.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If it's like this, and I intend to say that up until I decide to change history, everything could play out exactly as it once did, it should be confirmation that I'll be able to safely stay here until the 15th.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There's nothing that makes it an impossibility, so it could be that I always lived here and that I'm not changing the past yet. My parents never called me to say that someone was living at my place, and I never learned about it otherwise before the 15th, so I can secretly stay here, right? No contradictions.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had no clue if it would work like that, but worrying about it felt pointless. I chose some casual clothes to put on and stepped back to the living room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}And now what?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Even though I had spent a long while living alone in that apartment, I'd always had plenty of things to think about, all of which I'd ended up pushing aside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wouldn't, by chance, remember a lottery winning combination, would I...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...The only reason why I hadn't thought that seriously was because I knew I didn't. Sai had mentioned using the Sekimeiya to win the lottery, but it wasn't actually that crazy of an idea.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't think it was greedy, either. In fact, what felt selfish was not taking the chance when it was provided.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I could change the past, I would go back in time again, because that would allow Miiya to be saved. That meant I simply had to remember a winning number before that point. That would create the possibility of a perfect future.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was I simply daydreaming in a hellish world? As long as the past could be changed, it didn't seem so. That future certainly felt attainable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where is the Sekimeiya right now? Ashiya should have it somewhere, but they must be protecting it from Xyn, so there's no way I could touch it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Wait, no. That might not be the case.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Katei and Suripo explained it to us. The Sekimeiya is merely bait for Xyn to get trapped in the tower. So it's definitely there right now.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: They also said that the mechanism to trigger the alarm is based on the cabinet being forced open. Also, Xyn never attacked before the 15th.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Doesn't that mean that I can change the past by going there during the night and forcing the cabinet open? It's probably not in the event room yet, but it must be somewhere unavailable to the public.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If I break it open, the alarm will lock me inside, and someone else will be locked in the security room. According to Katei, he hadn't been taking the night shifts recently, so it'll probably be someone else. Will they buy that I'm a Xyn member?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It sounded pretty dangerous. That could've been a way to travel to the past again, but if it didn't work, I would be caught by the police, ruining everything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why were there times where touching the Sekimeiya didn't do anything? What if it just won't work before the 15th, which is why nobody noticed its powers?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Even if the main entrance of the building is locked, assuming the storeroom door did lead to the outside, I could maybe enter through it.{w} ...There's no way I could take the entire cabinet out without triggering the alarm. Someone would be looking at the cameras, and I don't even know where the cabinet is.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...But to begin with, why did I go so far into the past? I still don't get that.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Sekimeiya was in the water tank, but it couldn't have been there for very long. According to Atsuki, he hid it in one of the lockers a while before that. ...Is it possible it gathered a lot of energy for another reason?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Even thinking about it in my living room, there were many things I didn't know about the Sekimeiya. If I could be sure such a plan could work, and I knew how to go days into the past, saving Miiya should've been fairly simple.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's no way that I'll let everything happen exactly as it did already just so that I have a guarantee that the Sekimeiya will work, right...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The unknown version of me that had been seen in the tower still haunted me, but that couldn't be it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No. If I were to do that, I would also prevent Atsuki and myself from going. That's completely out of the question.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...I wasn't even sure about my situation. My appearance in that dark tunnel was different from all the other times. Instead of teleporting instantly, I had awakened, so I still felt like there was something I was missing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We thought about this once, didn't we? That maybe traveling very far through time would make your memories foggy. Could that be why I feel this way? Is there something that I can't remember...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I wasn't sure. If there were some memories missing, I had no idea how to get them back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood up from the carpet and went to my room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My purse was still next to my bed. I picked it up and put on my coat. Then, I walked to the doorway, where I'd left the keys I'd appeared with.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wanted to go outside. If it really was the first day of December, and what I'd thought of applied, there should've been no issue with that. Nobody would be aware that I couldn't be walking in the streets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I put on my boots and opened the door. As expected, the air enclosed by all the mountains was overwhelmingly cold, but I really wanted to go out. On the snow were my footprints from the previous day, and some others ending at the nearby apartments.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was very rare for me to want to leave the house without knowing why. I usually only went outside with some purpose in mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was true that a lot of responsibility was weighing on me, but I didn't feel pressured. The freedom to make choices allowed me to remain relaxed to some degree.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked at my purse. My wallet was inside it, containing the same amount of money I'd counted before leaving to meet Atsuki and Miiya—not that much.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I closed the door and walked down the stairs. I lived close to the outskirts, and there usually weren't many people around. That wasn't too different that day, as only a handful of people were slowly walking on the sidewalk, wearing overcoats and exhaling misty breaths.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe I really should've thought about where to go before leaving.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I walked toward the center of Yushibana, every street looking identical due to the coating of snow. There were a few parked cars and a bunch of footprints on the ground, but the environment felt pretty desolate. Everyone was inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everything in the immediate vicinity was residential, so I kept thinking about where to go.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I guess I don't have to go anywhere. I could just come back when I get tired.{w} This is only for today, though. I seriously need to decide on what to do.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There were enough citizens in Yushibana that it wasn't very common to know people on the street. That was what allowed me to be unafraid of being recognized and questioned about being in the hospital.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Should I go to the tower? What would I even do?{w} And what else is there in town? The library? How long has it been since I went there? Too long, honestly...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I could try to eat something.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It had also been a while since I'd eaten anything outside. I always had to use my money well and cook at home.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I guess I can do whatever I want with the money that I have. It's been duplicated.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had my purse next to me when I woke up in the hospital, so the original money is there. ...And I'm thinking about winning the lottery.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I arrived at the busier section of Yushibana, where I immediately saw a lot more people. Looking all around, I saw that not many stores were open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This might not be a good idea. I've been to all these places at some point.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Is it possible that being recognized could be problematic? Would I be changing the past if I accidentally see someone who knows I should be in the hospital?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There's no way what happened wasn't on the news. Even people who don't know me could recognize me.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Nothing should happen. If someone sees it as a big issue, then the past has been changed, but that seems very unlikely. And there's no way anything would happen to me. ...Even if I'm found out, it won't make getting to the Sekimeiya any harder.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What would I do, though? I wouldn't want to let Atsuki know. I already traveled to the past alone, going against what the Atsuki in the tower said.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Was I being selfish again? ...Potentially hindering any attempt to save Miiya?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't personally seen the past change yet. Only Atsuki had said that it was possible, and even he hadn't known the full specifics behind it. The worst scenario simply seemed to be me having to use the Sekimeiya on the 15th, taking advantage of the attack.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I turned toward a narrower street. As expected, Ina Café was open. It was pretty rare for it to be closed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The barista there definitely knows me, and I need to understand better where I am. ...How will someone who knows me react if they see me on this day?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I walked to the entrance, finally making up my mind. Through the glass, I saw that the interior was empty and Darfee was wiping down one of the tables. It had been a long time since I'd been there, but there was a time in my life where I frequented the place, enjoying the calm atmosphere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the ground was a square carpet to clean the snow off my shoes. I used it before opening the door and hesitantly walking in, immediately feeling the warm temperature.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Darfee didn't turn around yet, so I looked at what was on the menu. Like in the past, there were light drinks and meals, as well as alcoholic beverages closer to the night.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Hello.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Hello.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: He suddenly turned around.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {tip=ha}Ha—{/tip}
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Shiroya...!
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Yeah. It's been a while.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Oh my God! Y-You're all right!
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...So you know what happened. I am, yes.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Of course! You were on the news!
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I managed a bitter smile in response to his relieved expression.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm so glad you were released so quickly! How are you?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Makes sense. I'm supposed to be in a coma.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'm okay. I was released yesterday. Fortunately, nothing major happened to me.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: That's really good to hear. If you came to relax and try to forget things, we don't have to talk about it.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...It's fine. You don't have to worry.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Are you sure? I can't imagine what it must be like to lose someone close to you at your age. I'm so sorry.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...{w}Thank you.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Do you have any idea what happened? A lot of details weren't published.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Unfortunately, no. It all happened suddenly, and we were just caught up in it.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He looked down, very clearly pitying me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you want coffee? I'm sorry, I don't have much else right now.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: N-No, I don't think I need any right now.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Are you sure? I can make you the Kalitsu Special.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...What is that?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: It's nothing. That's the special.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: He cracked a halfhearted smile, obviously trying to cheer me up. I tried to return the look, but I wasn't sure if my own smile was visible or not.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked behind the glass cover, where a few pastries remained.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I'm a bit hungry. I could go for this.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I pointed at one covered with dried chocolate.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Of course. Give me a second.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...He moved behind the bar, removed it with metallic tongs, and put it on a small plate, which he placed in front of me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Here. Don't worry about asking for anything else.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Thank you.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I bit into it—I was hungrier than I'd thought.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What will happen when he realizes that I'm still in the hospital? I haven't heard anything about Darfee in a while, so if everything were to happen as I remember, he shouldn't do anything. I really don't like having to lie to him, though.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I kept eating while he washed the few dishes left.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're done? Do you want another one?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I'm okay, but thank you.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: All right. I'm seriously happy to see you, though. I couldn't believe it when I saw your face on the news.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...Me too. Sorry for not coming around in a while.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Don't worry about that. Are your parents here?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Darfee had to be in his late thirties, but he was a good friend of my parents, who'd actually brought me there for the first time. I hadn't spoken to him that many times, but I figured he was familiar enough with me, as he'd known me since I was a kid.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They aren't.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: No? Will they come soon? They will, right?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...I don't know. As of now, they'll stay overseas.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He looked puzzled and disappointed. In fact, I did know that they wouldn't come. Even after waking from my coma, they would only talk to me through phone calls. ...Too busy with administrative work, of course.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's right. What will even happen now? Two identical copies of my phone exist. How will calls work?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I suppose it doesn't matter. If both phones react when they call me, I'll just have to not pick up. If only mine rings, the past would be changing.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Do come here any time you want. You're more than welcome.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...I will. I just wanted to leave my home today.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I completely understand. That's good for you to do.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Yeah...
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I think I will have coffee.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Absolutely. How do you want it?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...It's pretty late for coffee, actually. I'm not sure, anything that's not too strong, and without milk or sugar.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: As always. Give me a second.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: He grabbed a short, transparent glass and filled it halfway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you want it alongside anything?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: He pointed at some bottles higher up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Those have alcohol, right?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...Then no. I've never had any of that.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I understand, but maybe you should. Last thing I wanna do is make an alcoholic out of you, but it doesn't hurt in small quantities.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: It's okay. I'd prefer not to.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He nodded and filled it all the way up. I was kind of surprised he offered—I wasn't old enough to drink, and I could have gotten away with technically barely breaking the law, but I wasn't in the mood anyway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He left the glass next to the empty plate. As usual, it was overly hot.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stretched my hands behind my back and looked around me. I was the only person there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A newspaper...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A few seats away, there was an open newspaper that someone had probably started reading and left behind. I pinched it and pulled it toward me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It should say today's date.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I looked at the top right corner, and, as expected, there was the date.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It really is December 1st.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Is this new?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: The newspaper? Yes.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I brought it closer and looked at the pages for current news. It was Yushinews, so events from Yushibana were highlighted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Miiya and I must appear somewhere in here.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I flipped the pages toward the start, as I felt it should've been important enough to put it at the beginning. When I got to the initial two, I stopped myself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Here it is.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The category was "November", and there were many brief articles. The last one was titled "Gas Explosion Late at Night".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I read the tiny letters next to a black and white picture of the shop.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Miiya Moiromo, a twenty-year-old girl, is the only casualty of a local gas explosion that occurred in the evening of November 30th. Shiroya Mirana, another young girl nineteen years of age, was gravely injured and immediately sent to the hospital. Her condition is critical, although she wasn't directly hit by the explosion."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "The incident occurred when an unknown individual released smoke that caused four people inside to lose consciousness. The other two were too far from the range to receive any serious injuries. While everyone was unconscious, a heater depleted its surrounding oxygen after its flame went out, and when a visitor turned on the lights, an immediate explosion of short radius but intense force occurred.{w} It killed the first victim instantly and broke the floor of the shop. The second girl, Mirana, was protected by the furniture next to her but fell through the broken floor."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It happened just like I remember.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And it doesn't even say why the incident happened.{w} ...Right, on the 15th, when smoke knocked us out for the second time, I thought that both incidents must have been caused by the same people. That would be Xyn.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}Wait, it actually is this. I'm not wrong.{w} It was caused by Xyn. That's why no further details got published.{w} That's what Katei told us. Xyn had already tried to steal the Sekimeiya once, but they failed. They almost caught the person behind it, but since they ended up escaping, it wasn't published that they'd been from Xyn.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Oh, of course... In the attic, I knew I recognized that smell. I smelled it in that shop. ...That's what happened there. Xyn tried to steal the Sekimeiya before it was brought to Ashiya Tower.{w} The Sekimeiya was in the shop, and for some reason, Xyn didn't succeed.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That made sense as the outline of what had occurred, but it didn't mean anything to me aside from the fact that Miiya's life had been taken during an attempt to steal a gemstone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At that point, did Xyn know what the Sekimeiya would do, or did they attempt to steal just another simple gem that Ashiya had? The advertising had just started.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I huffed, deeply frustrated.{w} I began to drink the coffee, and as I scanned the pages, more concise articles came into view.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I read the title of one higher up on the page.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "Unknown Man Escapes from Prison Cell".{w} Intrigued by the premise, I read the body of the article.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "In the afternoon of November 24th, the camera of a prison cell recorded a prisoner escaping from it."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...? Is it talking about a prison here?{w} I don't think there's a proper one in Yushibana, so maybe it's just talking about holding cells in the police department.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "The identity of that person remains unknown. They were dressed as a prisoner, but no footage shows who they were or how they ended up in that cell. The corridor they were in was unprotected, as nobody should've been inside the cell. By the time the footage recording them was noticed, they'd already disappeared.{w} The cell itself was unlocked, supposedly due to being vacant. There was no security in that area, so it is possible the individual left the entire building. Their identity and the way they got to that cell are under investigation, but no method to reach it such as a hidden passage between cells was found to exist."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell?{w} I never heard about this. I guess I don't really watch or read the news.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Next to the paragraph was a picture. It showed a still black and white image of the footage, which displayed the bars protecting the cell. The door was open, and the man could be seen leaving it. However, due to the high angle, his face couldn't be seen, and the single detail to go off of was his short, dark-looking hair.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This person supposedly appeared in a cell, huh? I guess there are many unsolved mysteries I could solve by factoring in the Sekimeiya. Who's to say it hasn't been used in crimes before it made its way to Ashiya...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I downed the rest of my coffee. It wasn't supposed to be strong, and I didn't feel any reaction from it. At one point, coffee had stopped always having a positive effect on me, and sometimes it would do more harm than good, so I'd stopped drinking it frequently.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're done? Do you want anything else?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I'm fine.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I stood up from the stool and looked at my purse.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're not going to try to pay me, are you? Don't even think about it.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Oh... Are you sure?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Of course, and come back any time you feel like it. I'm serious when I say that I was really glad to see you, and I'm relieved to see that you're all right.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Okay. I really appreciate it.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I don't want to stick my nose in your business, but I think you should talk to your parents. I can do it if you prefer. I can't believe they haven't come.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...Don't worry, I have been talking to them. I think I prefer to be alone, though.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Is that so...? I see.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I smiled and walked to the entrance. Seeing the desolate street from such a warm place made for a very pleasant contrast.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Bye.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I'll see you. There are a lot of things I want to talk to you about, so come back when you want. As you can see, we're not even closed on Sundays, so it can be any day. I wish you the best to get through this.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I nodded and left the shop.{w} Did I look like a person burying a lot of pain? To be talking casually and smiling only one day after Miiya's death, I assumed that was the only explanation to Darfee.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I unconsciously picked a side and walked away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everything around me, existence itself, felt calm. I still wondered how that was possible. Only days previously, I'd questioned whether I would even speak again. Just what had happened to me?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't that I didn't feel that pain as my own anymore or that I simply expected Miiya's death to be overwritten. After all, even if I did erase it, my memories wouldn't go away. Had all the terrible events afterward outweighed it, made it insignificant? How did that make sense?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No matter the reason why I felt so tranquil, I liked it. Being able to feel any kind of comfort was a welcome change, even if the future was uncertain, and even if it all still revolved around the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went back to Ramon street. In the center of Yushibana, it was the largest one, ending at the town hall. No cars could go through it, and it was where you could usually see the most people.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was Sunday, so it made sense that most places were closed. I'd thought of going to the tower earlier, but that wasn't even possible, as it closed on Sundays.{w} While I thought about what to do next, my legs automatically turned me toward a branching street.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know whether to stop myself, so I continued. I hadn't really intended to go any direction in particular, but it was a path I'd taken before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As opposed to the wider street, that one was only lined by residences, and it led to a one-way road, just as I remembered it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After ignoring two branching paths, I turned toward Enric avenue. From both sidewalks grew tall, skinny trees covered by the snow, elegantly draping over the path. It was a pretty place to live in, situated on the opposite side of Yushibana from my apartment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't bring myself to walk any farther, and I only stared into the distance from the corner. I was looking at Atsuki's house.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Near it, I could discern some people outside of their own houses, but Atsuki's was still.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't think I should let myself be seen...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I hadn't had any reason to go there, but I knew that if Atsuki saw me, I'd end up explaining everything that had happened. While a part of me wanted to do that, it wasn't strong enough to force me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is there light...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The road had very few wheel marks, and no cars were allowed to park. I crossed it to get a little closer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah. He's in the living room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Through his window, it was possible to see the light on the opposite side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After waking up from my coma, he'd told me that he'd only left his house to go to the hospital, and that he'd otherwise spent all his time miserable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew how he was feeling on the other side of the glass, and if I simply showed myself, I could help him. So then, why did that not feel like the best idea?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I surreptitiously approached the door, wondering if it was simply because I would ideally overwrite time anyway. Since I planned to change the past, was there no need to make the reality I was in better?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It also meant that if everything were to somehow play out as I remembered, the Atsuki I'd been with had always known that I'd traveled to the past and hadn't mentioned it so that it could happen. How likely was that, honestly?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I got startled as soon as I peeked through the bars of his front gate. I hadn't seen Maxi sitting in front of the wooden door, where there was no snow.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He seemed afraid for an instant when he saw me, but then he ran to me, squeezing his head through the bars.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's just me. Do you know that I should be in the hospital? What are you doing here? It's very cold.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I looked up as I petted him. I knew Atsuki wouldn't look through the window since Maxi tended to bark whenever other dogs passed by anyway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I figured Umi was inside the house. Both of them had a hole in the door to enter and exit through.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If nothing changes, what will happen on the 15th? I still don't understand what was up with the recording.{w} Could it really be that the exit will be locked for a month? If so, the police should take care of these two, right...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I looked at Maxi's face as he happily stared back at me. If I remembered well, he was eight and had been born on May 26th.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What if Atsuki was wrong and the past can't be changed? I could change it by ringing the doorbell right now, but that's not something I want to do.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Doesn't me constantly not wanting to do things that change the past indicate that it can't change?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What if I leave a note saying that I'm fine?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That didn't sound like a good idea either. There was no way Atsuki would read it and assume that I'd traveled to the past. Although he would then tell me after I woke up, so it would guarantee a change.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When will I be able to tell whether things can change or not? There should be something I could do to confirm it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And I suppose that if it can't happen in the end, it's a given that the version of me they saw on the 15th will end up being me.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Could it be that I'll have failed to conclude whether I can change the past even by the 15th? If I haven't been able to touch the Sekimeiya by then, I'll go to the tower. It just doesn't make sense that I would let everything repeat...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I could prevent the recording from occurring so that Maxi and Umi aren't in danger. What if I decide to be the one who removed the handle in the storeroom and keep it so that I can leave at any time? Would that make any sense...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stepped away from the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't worry. I'll be back soon.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I kept walking back, but Maxi didn't take his eyes off me until I'd disappeared from his view.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: One of Atsuki's neighbors was looking at me too, and she waved at me from a distance. I knew I'd seen her before, so I awkwardly returned the gesture. She opened her mouth to say something brief, but I couldn't hear her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I waited to see if she'd repeat herself, but it didn't seem like she'd realized I hadn't heard her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I don't know enough about what happened these days to do something and actually be sure I've changed the past. At least not in a non-drastic way, like by speaking to Atsuki. I could go to my hospital room and draw something on my face that I didn't wake up with...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I walked all the way down the street until I was back at the wider Ramon.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I seriously need to know if I'm going to be able to change what happened, and pretty urgently too. If it's not possible, then every attempt I make at getting to the Sekimeiya before the 15th is automatically bound to fail.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The time Katei said that someone from Xyn had tried to steal the Sekimeiya... There's no way I'll be the person behind that, right? Would he have said so if he'd known about it? I guess if the past can't be changed and someone did attempt to steal the Sekimeiya on the 30th, I have a guarantee that I won't be caught because he didn't mention that.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A lot more people than I remembered were walking up and down the stone path. As usual, most of the snow had been removed so it didn't hinder anyone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tended not to like being in that busy street, but I wanted to appreciate people simply existing around me. Most of them were slightly hunched over to feel warmer, wearing scarves around their necks.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was still a little hesitant. At any point, someone could've asked me about the hospital. I could recognize a few people I'd seen before, and I wasn't sure if I was imagining the stares I felt.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are they actually looking at me? There's no way it's because I'm supposed to be at the hospital, right...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I looked back, but the feeling had disappeared. I thought to myself that I was probably just pointlessly worried about that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was directing myself back home. The cold would soon become hard to bear, and I was a little tired. Nonetheless, going outside had been as pleasant as I'd thought it would be.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On my way to the drier roadway, I'd passed plenty of people living their own lives. Evidently, the time had only stopped for me and Atsuki.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd left the center of Yushibana, so my surroundings felt a lot less lively. Due to the temperature, the sky was devoid of birds, and seeing other animals wasn't common. Walking on the snow became a lot harder, but I'd grown used to it more every year.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I saw something wrapped around a streetlight and approached it warily.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "The Sekimeiya".{w} It was a flyer marked by the touch of many snowflakes. I'd seen it before, but I didn't want to look at it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I walked away, my eyes locked on my feet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What if I draw something on the door of my apartment? I know that when I went home after waking up in the hospital, I didn't see anything. I think that was on the 8th, when I came home and just slept before calling Atsuki.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It's very possible that the past will only change if I intend my actions to cause a change. This means that everything I've done up until now could've always happened. If I put something on my door with the intent to change the past, that could prove it can happen.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I guess it wouldn't be absolute, though. I could only be sure if it's still there on the 8th. It wouldn't be an instant confirmation.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: One of the purposes of changing the past is to prevent Atsuki and myself from going to the tower. What if I send a warning to him saying not to go? If that ends up being all I'll be able to do, I shouldn't let Erina and Isla go either, but I don't know where they live.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I got my keys ready and put aside my musings until I got to the staircase of my apartment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went up and unlocked the door. As soon as I opened it, the inner temperature hit me, and I remembered I'd left the heater going.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Just in case, I shouldn't have it on very often.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After closing the door, I left my boots on the floor, my coat on a wooden hanger, and went to turn the heater off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sky Signals
I was beginning to feel a little dubious and nervous about Atsuki's assertion. Did the Sekimeiya really have the power to let someone alter the past?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I'll find out right now. I just need to decide that my next action will change history.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Wait... that would be very thoughtless.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd thought of calling Atsuki's phone for a second and then hanging up. As long as I did that, the past would change. He'd never told me about a call like that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I couldn't do it. It would tell him that I'd woken up, and then he'd find out otherwise. I hadn't thought it through.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is there anything else I could do to get the same result...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Oh, I can call my parents. When I talked to them on the phone, they definitely would have told me about receiving a call from my phone on December 1st.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: All right, so should I just consciously aim to change the past?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: This won't get me into trouble, right...? They'll simply call the hospital, and nobody will understand what happened.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I took the phone from my purse and looked at the screen. It was almost {time=15.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went to the contacts list, selected my mom, and pressed the call button.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The signal usually wasn't great, so I got closer to the window. Immediately after the first beep, I heard a voice.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya...! How are you!?{w} I'm so glad you called! We were so worried!
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: My mom's voice came through the speaker, her disturbance making her sound a little distorted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hello...! Are you there? What happened? You're okay, right?
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I didn't want to speak, so I pressed the red button and cut the call, surprised to feel a sharp heartache as I did so.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see. The past can be changed. Atsuki was right.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A call request appeared, "Mom" listed as the name.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't pick it up and simply waited it out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No other call came afterward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They must've called the hospital.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I let out a nervous breath and closed my phone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Why did I travel so many days back? That doesn't make sense. Were we wrong, and the time the Sekimeiya spent out of the cabinet wasn't what influenced the time traveled?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It's not possible that it spent enough time in the water tank to send me here. Either way, what's important is that I can replicate it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Before the 15th, if I'm not able to get the Sekimeiya, I can change the past and prevent Atsuki and myself from going to the tower. The 15th is the only time where I'm guaranteed to be able to touch the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There'll be the attack, and people will fall unconscious, probably except the attacker. If that period of time isn't enough, I'll have twelve hours to use it, during which people will get trapped again.{w} If it comes down to it, I might have to think of how to take advantage of what happened. When the smoke went off, there were many places that weren't hit...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Since the past can be changed... Even though the Sekimeiya must currently be in the tower to bait an attack from Xyn, it's possible that I'll be caught by the police if I try to go and touch it before the 15th. ...Just which option is better?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: At least if I get trapped by myself on a night before the 15th, the only person trapped with me will be the person in the security room. I only need to learn how to jump days into the past, which should be a lot more feasible if there aren't seven other people there.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...I really appeared just minutes too late to save Miiya. That's ridiculous.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And instead of appearing instantly, I felt like I woke up. ...When I touched the Sekimeiya in the water tank, the heat around it was clearly a lot stronger than every other time. So the heat it releases is related to the distance traveled, but the way it increases might be different from what we thought.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...I should probably try to eat something.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I went to the kitchen. I didn't like cooking and I wasn't great at it, but I'd lately gotten used to making my own food, as I didn't have many alternatives.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I'd been living at Atsuki's house, I'd only eaten by heating up prepared food that I couldn't afford. I opened the fridge, and as expected, there wasn't much to choose from. I was hungry due to walking around in the cold, so I wasn't picky.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A bit of meat remained in a plastic tray. I really only kept buying it because my parents used to.{w} I grabbed it and looked at my side. Thankfully, the frying pan was clean.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I usually avoided using oil because the sizzling always startled me, and as a result, I'd basically stopped caring about eating things that were plain. I ignored the full bottle and heated up the empty pan for a few seconds. Then, I carefully placed the last pieces of meat on it and took a step back as they cooked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After staring from a few steps back for a while, I used chopsticks to flip the chunks of meat around, forcefully ungluing them from the surface. I added salt and spice powder, garnished them the best I could, and cut it all up. The meal looked exactly like every other time I'd prepared it, and I brought it to the living room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I left the plate on the table and sat on a cushion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This doesn't even make sense. Where are the others?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I thought of something that should've come to mind much sooner.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki, Erina, Sai, and maybe Akaro. A bunch of people who must have been outside the tower too. Where are they?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I've been assuming I traveled alone, but that doesn't make any sense if we were at least right about one thing. If the range of the Sekimeiya was related to how far you went, there's no way the lobby wasn't included given that I traveled more than two weeks to the past.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Where are they? I had to have made someone else travel with me, and everyone should've appeared at the same time that I did... but I'm also not sure I was immediately aware right after touching the Sekimeiya and passed out for a little while, so who knows when that would be?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Was our understanding of the range incorrect too? If the range equaled the size of a crystal room when we traveled less than an hour... traveling fifteen days must have meant it extended far outside the tower.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I grabbed a slice of meat and brought it to my mouth.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's not good at all.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The taste was weird, but the spice did its job at obfuscating it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Ashiya and the police were right outside the tower. If they traveled to the past, I'm sure information about that would be widespread. There's no way a bunch of people traveling through time wouldn't create an uproar.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I appeared late on November 30th, where I'd been on that day. When we were in the tower, we thought about going ten minutes back but appearing where we'd been five minutes before traveling.{w} Did something like that happen again? Maybe I appeared at {time=21:10} where I'd been at {time=21:00}, so my old self wasn't there anymore. If I showed up exactly where I was at the time, I would've replaced my old self, and now I know that didn't happen.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We definitely know that the location you appear is based on a past one. If multiple people from Ashiya or the police were sent to the past, they might have all appeared in the same area, like their workplace.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Even if I tried to explain it like that, it didn't make a ton of sense. The range had to be immense, not just big enough to encompass the policemen right outside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I ate more, trying not to chew much. I wasn't sure if the meat was bland or just plain tasted bad, so I could avoid finding out by not biting into it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I bet we just were mistaken about the range as well. Or maybe it wasn't necessarily that. Maybe the range and the time the Sekimeiya spent out of the cabinet were related... that'd still make some sort of sense.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Because again, when I touched it, it couldn't have been there for too long. And the range couldn't have been that large either, so the question should only be why I went so many days into the past.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What if it's just random? We kinda let go of that thought because we didn't want it to be true, but it would make enough sense.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stopped eating. The aftertaste was getting worse, and the hunger had somewhat faded.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This could be really bad.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If I was the only person who traveled, then everything I've thought should still apply. On the other hand, if a bunch of other people went with me and there's no news about it, I have no idea what will happen.
entries.speaker: nm
