However, access to Ashiya Tower is strictly prohibited, as a potentially dangerous gas was found within it in high quantities.{w} While investigating the motive behind the attack is not the highest priority, aside from the gemstones found immediately after the authorities secured the situation, no other valuable items were found to be missing, indicating that theft may not have been the goal."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya couldn't see the walls of her apartment without feeling her heart shrinking. When she finally went back, she wondered what she was supposed to do.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She had spoken to her parents over the phone, and she'd been forced to speak about Atsuki's death and everything the police had asked her. Even though she'd been released without being considered guilty of anything, she hadn't been able to answer any questions about the attack on the 15th.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Lately, she'd had to talk a lot, but when she found herself at home, she didn't think she had the ability to produce a single sound.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The pillows were still scattered in her living room. The last time she'd been there, she'd managed to feel hopeful, but that felt so distant that it was hard to believe decades hadn't passed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya didn't know what the point of returning was. She had lost everything.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was the next day. She had slept and eaten, but it couldn't be said she'd done so for any particular reason.{w} The miserable way she felt... it was all too familiar to her, but the difference in potency was immense.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That day, she became aware of something she hadn't been told yet.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After turning on the television, she learned about the current situation in Yushibana.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It wasn't a secret that a large portion of the citizens was opposed to the presence Ashiya had built. Due to Ashiya Tower, Yushibana had undergone a drastic change throughout the recent years.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Perhaps the old activities of what had once been called the Ashiya family weren't as widely known, but what was a commonly shared fact was that when the tower had shifted into a personal exposition center, a new wave of people had taken over the town.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That was the fundamental dispute in Yushibana. The older citizens, aware of the way Ashiya had once been, were becoming outnumbered by the recent influx of people Ashiya had brought, who supported the now-corporation due to financial reasons and were ignorant of its roots.{w} After the 15th of December, the backlash Ashiya had received had been enormous. Through their poor security measures, they'd let two people be killed, and they hadn't publicly responded well to the ordeal, blinded by their battle against Xyn.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Unlike previously, the protests were so strong and visible that the supportive part of Yushibana joined in as well. Everything Ashiya had done to combat Xyn was being revealed, so the older citizens took the chance to expose all they knew about Ashiya's past, and rumors about the missing people and the unknown gas continued to circulate.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: All Ashiya kept saying was that they were still investigating what had happened—that they would find the missing people and expose those working as part of Xyn. Then, the tower would quickly open again.{w} However, everyone knew that nobody had entered that building since the 15th due to the unknown gas, so those statements were seen as a haphazard, lacking defense.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Where were the remaining people? Why had they not been in the tower?{w} One of them had died in a car accident, and another one had been unable to explain anything to the police. It didn't make sense; they should've been in the tower, late on the 15th. ...And what about the other three? They hadn't been found anywhere.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Soon, Ashiya went quiet. After days spent repeating themselves, it seemed they'd chosen to drop the subject entirely.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The news had been covered all over the nation and had even reached overseas. When it was noticed that Ashiya had stopped defending themselves from harsh criticism, it was assumed they'd concluded they were done for.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And that was correct. The next time an executive of Ashiya was seen, they were recorded exiting the tower, loading covered boxes onto a truck.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Later that day, from her apartment, Shiroya saw that scene being broadcast.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So, is it true that you're abandoning the tower? It's been speculated you're selling it. Is that correct? What do you have to say about all the employees you left without a job?
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: There was no reply from the Ashiya member.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The police haven't said anything else about the supposed gas that's inside. Is that not a concern anymore?
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: On the video, the snow was starting to melt in the background. The reporter tried to get the man to answer again, but she couldn't get him to speak.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya reached out to pet Maxi. In the corner, Umi's eyes seemed to be fixed on the screen, her dark fur camouflaged in the dim room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The screen morphed into static, the audio going with it. As the signal was very poor, it was frequently interrupted.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Staring at the television, Shiroya felt traces of motion sickness. Was it due to the rapidly flashing screen? It almost didn't seem that way.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Long ago, evolution had developed motion sickness. When one's sight blurred, as they could've been poisoned, they would react by vomiting to expel the poison. Shiroya was unsure if the static just made her feel that way or if her entire life had been poisoned.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Alone in her apartment, she didn't look away until the signal resolved.{w} When it did, someone else was speaking about the same topic, but very far from the tower.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...ya tower was bought. We don't have the details yet, but it appears the building is not theirs anymore. They just finished taking out anything of worth inside, so Ashiya's quietly leaving their old property behind.
entries.speaker: c5

entries.text: It became known that someone had offered to buy the tower from Ashiya, and they had accepted due to their awful position. In the blink of an eye, Ashiya, which had been seen as a source of power and wealth within Yushibana, had entirely vanished.{w} Who had been the buyer, however? It didn't seem that information was widely available.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Despite what many people felt in regards to Ashiya, a large portion of the citizens in Yushibana engaged in business with them, so the group falling to pieces brought hardship. Would the tower's new owner put the building to a similar use?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If not, it was very likely someone else from Yushibana would, as there were a variety of shops and attractions related to the gemstones in the surrounding mountains. As long as those shops could still sell gems, at least a few of them would avoid disaster.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But what would happen was soon revealed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The news finally came out: the building that had been Ashiya's for so many years would disappear.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That began to shine a bit of light on the situation. The demolition of the tower was something one part of Yushibana had always wished for. The structure that clearly didn't belong with the others—the one they'd all seen rapidly increasing in height throughout the years...
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Why had it been purchased just to be demolished? Had it been to follow that old, unattainable demand that Ashiya disappear? Did they hope the rumors still tied with that building would vanish so that something entirely new could be built? There was only speculation on those topics throughout Yushibana, and nothing more.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Weeks had passed, but any answers remained staunchly concealed. However, a date had already been appointed: on October 4th, the building would be destroyed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was a tall and wide structure, so demolishing it wasn't simple. As no buildings were directly next to it, though, there was little danger to any of the surroundings.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At some point, the unanswered questions had almost faded. Who had caused the incident on the 15th of December? Who had killed the two victims? Where were the remaining people? Given the blood that had been found, the worst had been assumed by all.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After so long, there was a reason why Shiroya and her cat had their heads out their window.{w} It was October 4th, and the sight they were beholding would no longer exist the following day.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the distance, the building stretching past the others was soon to fall. It could've been dangerous to get close to it, so many people were also watching from within their houses. Some of them were about to have a familiar view returned to them. Others, like Shiroya, could hardly imagine what a Yushibana without Ashiya Tower would be like.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At {time=12}, the demolition would begin. There'd been no correspondence from Ashiya in months. The facts behind the unknown gas and the deaths within the tower were still shrouded in darkness.{w} The interior of the building had been investigated a few times after the 15th, but nothing useful had been figured out. Ashiya had removed everything of value, so after it was verified by the new owner, the demolition seemed to pose no risk aside from the dust it would scatter across the hill behind the tower.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A minute before the appointed time, many pairs of eyes looked on from behind windows all over town.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: With a faint, deep sound, the building had abruptly fallen. In a second, a huge, brown cloud of dust was all that Shiroya could see on the other side of Yushibana.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It didn't seem like it had reached any of the nearest houses. Instead of waiting for it to dissipate, Shiroya shut the window and walked out of her bedroom.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Cleaning up the debris would be a long process, and while there was no news about what would happen afterward, the procedure would start a week from that day.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya returned in the afternoon. She'd gotten used to having the television on while she was at home. She'd never done that prior to everything that had happened to her, but it brought her some small form of solace to have any noise at all in her barren set of rooms.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She'd set the volume low because the sporadic static would be hard on her ears otherwise.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The bright screen projected light onto the ceiling. When the color drastically changed, Shiroya lifted her head.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She raised her entire body next. On the screen was a man speaking into a microphone.{w} She grabbed the remote and increased the volume, staring at the text beneath him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She had to read it a few times to comprehend it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "The last three people who were trapped in Ashiya Tower found dead".
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the corner of the screen was an image of the piled debris. Shiroya focused her hearing and began to process the deep voice of the reporter.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...en they started to be removed, the first body was found. It was that of Akaro Esata.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: A video began to play in the background. It showed people removing the debris and a pixelated red blob in the middle.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Another one was quickly found afterward, belonging to Sai Yomiya. Finally, when almost all the debris had been removed, Erina Majutsu's body was found.{w} The three bodies were heavily crushed, and it's believed some parts of them weren't found.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Shiroya listened in disbelief. She'd always known that when she'd touched the Sekimeiya, Atsuki, Erina, Sai, and Akaro had been in the lobby. Atsuki had died in a car accident, but the others had all disappeared. A long time ago, Shiroya had concluded that Atsuki must've traveled through time after her.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But this... What kind of sense did it make? The censoring prevented her from confirming the bodies' faces, but given their descriptions, it didn't seem like that would've been possible regardless.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As of now, what happened is unknown. While the bodies were severely smashed, they were not fully decomposed. It has been determined that they died the day of the demolition.{w} However, the possibility of the demolition itself causing their deaths has been thoroughly refuted. It was properly verified that nobody was in the building before the impact, and that's not the only reason.{w} The three bodies were below all the rubble. If the building had really fallen on them, their condition would be even worse. Strangely, some of the body parts that were recovered are practically intact, despite the state of most others.{w} There was no dust discovered on the bodies—neither inside their clothes nor in their mouths. For this reason, the situation is being handled very carefully, as the truth behind it might be appalling.{w} It has been considered that the bodies were disposed of within the rubble following the demolition since they couldn't have been directly hit by it. However, given how deep they were and the absence of blood around them, that was immediately discarded as well.{w} Even though the abundance of the unidentified old gas has disappeared, around the three bodies was where the last remaining traces were found.{w} This is an extremely delicate case that has carried unsolved questions with it all year. Now that everyone who was trapped in the building has been found, the authorities will do all they can to figure out what happened on that day.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Chapter 3 Credits (Forsaken Relay)
Shiroya turned off the television.
After months of dwelling on the incident, the reporter's words released her.
It was over.
The remaining hope she'd been carrying was gone.
She wouldn't see the people she'd been with that day again, and she wouldn't learn what had happened to them.
Over time, she'd come to accept that the time when the three had reunited had been but a second farewell.
Shiroya stepped out of her apartment one more time to visit the snowless world.
The sky above her didn't feel the same as it once had, but it was still there.
She had somewhere to go.
Earlier that day, she'd tried to walk there and stopped halfway.
Surrounded by green, she inhaled a familiar aroma.
She wanted to know if an offer she'd received long ago was still valid.
Finally hoping for something, she wished it wasn't too late.
And as she saw the last person who remained from her old life, she learned that she hadn't waited too long.
It wouldn't make her happy.
And it would probably not make her less lonely.
But the fact that she wanted it regardless was enough to know that she had to do it.
The next day, she had a reason to get up and fondly remembered the last time she'd awoken in high spirits.
The three gruesome bodies beneath the rubble...
That mystery was nowhere close to being solved.
There had been no new information from Ashiya.
They had vanished completely, and with them the route to any remaining answers.
The plain terrain where the tower had once been...
After years of the building's increasing height, nothing else would rise there.
It didn't take long for that place to become a thing of the past.
And for that inexplicable day to be merely a memory.
Once years had gone by, Shiroya's surroundings were different.
She wasn't far from Yushibana, but she didn't live there anymore.
Every time she looked at both animals still at her side, she remembered the person who'd always been with her.
He was someone she'd never forget and someone who didn't exist anymore.
Holding a packed, green folder, she laughed along with someone who'd never stepped into her hometown.
She explained the events of one particular December 15th as if they had happened long, long ago.
Leaving out crucial details, she maintained a natural voice as she thought back on that egg-shaped stone.
Was she the last person who remembered its powers?
...She really was the same person who'd once stepped into that tower, and the only survivor of that day.
Ending: Forsaken Relay
Axis Ropeway
Tethered
I would... change the past. I had a way to save Miiya, Atsuki, Isla, Katei, Naomi, Erina...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had traveled from the 15th to change the past alone, and even though I hadn't been aware of what would happen, I had considered the outcome with my other self.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Looking at the small town had finally brought me to lean toward an option. I'd decided to do my best to change the past, as the possible consequences didn't outweigh what good could be achieved.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But the tower I could see far in the distance... I still couldn't go there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The day I'd enter that building again would likely be the last day of my normal life, and even though I'd decided, the thought could still freeze me in place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wanted the days I had to persist, but that couldn't happen. My life in Yushibana was likely soon to end, and I could choose the length of the last stretch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I saved Miiya, I wouldn't show myself to her, Atsuki, and the other me, even though I didn't know yet what I would do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So the issue to solve was the possibility of a knowledgeable enemy who could change the past on their own and steal the Sekimeiya before the 15th.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't do much to combat that aside from rushing in, which I found far too risky. So I settled on another course of action and accepted that I would take it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Thursday was two days away.{w} Every Thursday morning, an event would be held in the tower. That was the day I chose to step into the building for the second time and find the Sekimeiya that was surely confined inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to breathe properly. If I wasn't beaten to it, I only had one more day that I'd chosen to give myself, hopelessly refusing to let them end so soon.{w} And the very next one, I'd go to the tower in the morning and think about the best way to act. Then, I'd put that into effect that very night.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What would the event be? I knew Atsuki had read the upcoming ones and said that only one seemed interesting in late January.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There, people will probably ask about the Sekimeiya. It might even be held in the event room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We had bought entrance tickets for the 15th many days prior, but when we'd waited in the lobby, I'd heard people trying to buy them at the reception desk. They'd all been sold out, but if you could buy the tickets directly there, it was probably common to do so on the day of less important events.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And if there are none left, I'll just pay for a normal visit. Joining whatever special event will happen isn't essential.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had to stop staring ahead. The strong wind kept whipping snow into my face, and prickling pains chipped at the corners of my eyes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Scanning the ground, I took the path that circled Yushibana.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The way wasn't perfectly even, and traversing the dense snow was difficult. I had to take the next path leading down, but I couldn't easily see it in the distance due to its identical color.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My stomach was demanding food, and the cold was becoming too prominent to bear. Protecting my head with my hood, I advanced steadily, knowing where I was headed for once.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was close to home. Even though I was going slow, I knew there wasn't much distance between both trails down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been glancing up here and there, but it was hard to recognize the narrow entrance to Yushibana I was going toward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At last, I saw the absence of brown at my right.{w} As I thought, it extended all the way down, leading to a dirt road close to my home.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped down the steep path, careful not to trip. Slowly, I descended until there was concrete below the snow and composed myself. The wind was noticeably weaker closer to the ground, so I raised my head again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The narrow path soon became a sidewalk where a couple of cars were parked. Like I'd seen from above, nobody seemed to be on the outskirts.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was less than two minutes away from home. My apartment was one block farther, but I had to walk a bit.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is someone behind me again?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I could see the metallic staircase far ahead, but I debated whether to stop.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No, yesterday that didn't work. They'll just run away.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Should I pass by my apartment? What if they want to know where I live?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I started to feel a little nervous. Had I actually felt someone behind me once more, or was it paranoia...? I just needed to go home.{w} I looked by my feet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could circle this block, and if new footsteps are here when I'm back, I'll know I'm not making anything up.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't change my pace, but I avoided even looking at my apartment. I'd just made a very important decision, but I felt indecisive again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even if I confirm that I'm right, what would I do? ...Ignore it?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd have to go home anyway.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Up ahead, the only way to see my back would be from directly behind me. If I suddenly turn around at the end and someone is watching me, I should see them as well.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I bit my lip and kept walking. I couldn't make any motions that indicated I thought someone was behind me or they'd be able to escape again. If someone was there, I just needed to know who it was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I managed to feel a bit of sweat forming on my palms despite the overwhelming cold. Depending on who it was, I might have had to act sooner than I expected.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had passed my apartment. If someone was really looking at me, would the curtain of snow conceal them? If they turned fast enough, identifying them would likely be impossible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I was close to the end of the street, where it curved into another one. If someone was watching me from behind at that moment, they had to be in eyeshot.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I instinctively turned around before I'd planned.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A sudden sound had broken the silence far behind me. And as I'd feared, the falling snow was blurring the image.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Frowning, I sprinted back the way I'd come, toward a blue smudge way ahead.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is that...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It immediately became visible. It was a police officer.{w} ...But that wasn't all, so I didn't stop.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before getting there, I understood what had happened. Next to the officer was a police car, and they'd just closed the back door after making someone else get in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh...! ...What's wrong?
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I panted breathlessly, my hands on my knees. A sudden dizziness invaded me, almost causing me to fall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you okay...?
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I nodded and slowly looked up. Instead of responding, I stared at the window of the car. The glass was tinted, so I couldn't see the interior of the vehicle.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: S-Sorry, did you just arrest someone?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Hm? Yes. What's the matter?
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...{w}I... was feeling like someone was following me just now. Could it have been this person?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: The man frowned and took out a tiny scrapbook.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's your name?
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Mine...?{w} ...It's Shiroya Mirana.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He looked at me and silently wrote on the paper.{w} Then, he suddenly smiled, completely shifting his expression.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see. You can stop worrying, then. If you think you were being followed, there's nothing to be afraid of.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Wh-What...? Can you let me see their face?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He looked at the black window.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No. I'm not allowed to do that.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...What about their name or the reason for arresting them?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: You can stop worrying—believe me. Right now, I'm not allowed to tell you any of that, but just wait for when it's made public.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I tried to produce some way of coercing him into telling me more, but I couldn't come up with anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I have to hurry. Don't hesitate to contact us if you feel you're being followed again, but I don't think you'll be having any more problems.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...Okay.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: The man nodded with a sympathetic smile and opened the door to the driver side, quickly shutting it again. Then, the car began to move and soon disappeared toward the direction I'd just run from.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked by my feet. The tire marks came from far away, and next to them was a group of footprints.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: These are mine. I looked at the ground earlier specifically for this.{w} ...And these were definitely not here before.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: They're the policeman's, though.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I kept looking down, trying to find a third pair of footprints.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There had to be a third pair right there, but I suddenly remembered the strange smile the officer had. Something felt odd about him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, these.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After taking a few steps forward, I noticed the trail of footprints coming from the same direction as the tire tracks.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It must be these since they end where the car was.{w} They also resemble the ones I saw yesterday.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I kept following them in reverse, hoping they would lead somewhere. However, I immediately realized that wouldn't work.{w} The more I walked, the more the footprints faded due to the falling snow. Soon, I could hardly even make out their shape.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I was right.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stopped myself, stress and relief pulling me from both sides.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The person who was following me was arrested... Maybe I was right that they were someone else who traveled from the 15th. Depending on what happened, just that alone could've led to their arrest.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What mattered was that someone who potentially wanted to steal the Sekimeiya was out of the picture. Being able to feel a little calmer in that regard was immensely beneficial.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...And he said that their identity would be made public. When's that gonna be, though? Assuming everything up until the 15th repeats itself, it won't be before that day, right? Otherwise, someone who went to the tower would've known a future self of theirs had been arrested.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't know what to think, but it seemed someone had really identified me and been following me. Added to their arrest, assuming that they'd traveled from the future seemed the most likely scenario.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I turned around. My apartment was right there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could barely keep myself standing anymore. I approached the staircase while I grabbed the keys and staggered my way to the front door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I lightly shook off the snow on me and turned the key clockwise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...How long had the heater been on? The change in temperature was more drastic than it had ever been.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hurriedly closed the door and left my coat and boots behind. I wanted to drop to the floor, but I managed to make it to the kitchen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew I still had the instant noodles I'd bought, so I grabbed the bowl I'd used last time, then washed and filled a pot.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once the water began to boil, I dropped the noodles in and watched them slowly spread out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It would take three minutes to cook. Meanwhile, I sipped water and tried to compose myself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't been able to eat in the tower, and I'd kept going for hours and hours there, but the cold outside in wintertime Yushibana was a real problem for me. I kept underestimating the importance of a reasonable surrounding temperature.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Someone following me had only thrown me further into disarray. I couldn't put into words why I'd felt again that they'd been watching me, but it was possible their goal had really been to learn where I lived. I was far beyond the point of assuming they only wanted to confirm who I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I removed most of the water from the pot and dropped the noodles in the bowl, garnishing it as I had before. The meal looked pretty ordinary, but I eagerly brought it to the living room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I ate some. They were hot and a bit stiff, but I kept going.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I eventually slowed down. Curiously, I took out the phone from my purse and looked at the time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {time=16} already... I was outside for so many hours.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The person who was just arrested... Could they have been from Xyn?{w} If so, that's a new occurrence, because we were told that no members had been caught yet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Were they someone I'd been with in the tower? ...It was frustrating that I hadn't been able to see their face.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I figured there was no point in getting hung up on it, so I kept eating as I thought back on what was most important.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It'll be Thursday in just two days... I'm giving myself tomorrow to enjoy, but I'm not sure that's what I want anymore. I'll probably just be nervous all day.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: On Thursday morning... finding the Sekimeiya and checking the door in the storeroom shouldn't take too long. After that, there are more important matters.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'll change the past drastically for the first time by going to Atsuki's house and taking the tickets we bought.{w} Later, I can go to Isla's house and either attempt to talk with whoever her friend really is or try to prevent them from going on the 15th in the same way.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That could be really important, because if I get caught by the police or I'm not able to find the Sekimeiya, at least I'll guarantee that the four of us don't go to the event.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'm not too sure what would happen then. It's pretty likely the two initial groups to get trapped would merely consist of different people, but I can't do anything about that.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd entirely cleaned out the bowl, so I brought it to the kitchen and picked up a pair of cereal bars.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, I had a thought I hadn't fully considered before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Could this be a bad idea...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Assuming I'm not able to find the Sekimeiya in the tower, should I really try to prevent any of us from going there? That might screw it all up.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Right now, the 15th is the failsafe in case I can't find the Sekimeiya beforehand. If I let everything repeat, I'll be able to touch it again on that day.{w} Hell, I could see where the recorder even came from, or even stay there for a month, depending on whether it's real or not.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But if Atsuki, Isla, Erina, and I don't go to the event, it will all be considerably different.{w} What if something causes the attack to fail?{w} What if Katei and Ashiya are able to unlock the exit this time?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That would get rid of the only guaranteed time where getting the Sekimeiya again will be possible.{w} So, if I don't find it anywhere on Thursday, maybe waiting until the 15th is the best call.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I discarded that idea at the start of all this for a reason. If I let the incident happen like it once did, where really is the proof that the past can change? It would mean that the version of myself Atsuki saw really was just me in the future.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But that's not the case anymore. This is what I hadn't considered yet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If I don't change anything else until the 15th and everything actually repeats, I won't have to enter the tower again.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Now I know something very important. At close to {time=16}, a very long travel took place, and it reached through the walls of the tower...{w} Could I place myself in that range, or would I be arrested?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Even though everyone close to the building will know that someone with my name is inside, would they recognize my face? All I'd have to do would be spot Vaisude and get very close to him at {time=16.}
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That would make me travel to the 24th of November. This would be the best possible outcome.{w} I'd make it far enough to be the first person to find the Sekimeiya in the mountains, stop all of this at the source, and save everyone.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Exploring what to do those days seemed like a foolish dream, but I thought about it for a bit. I'd been living in my apartment on the 24th, so if I actually wanted to go that far back, I'd have to seriously plan it out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It sounded great in concept, but I couldn't help but think it was an impossible avenue.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How would I get close to Vaisude without getting arrested? I could call him again to more accurately determine the time he'd traveled, but it was unlikely it would be that precise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I still had no idea why we'd found two Naomis, but I hated the idea of letting that repeat even if I'd be letting it happen again so that I could stop it later. In addition, even though it seemed like a given, I couldn't assume that large travel would still happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't think Vaisude had lied, but I'd somewhat changed history when I'd called my mom, and I didn't know what extra changes that implied. Furthermore, I had no idea if someone else would change the past differently; the butterfly effect could've easily prevented the {time=16} travel from happening.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If that was the case, would the Vaisude I'd spoken to exist in the world I was in? While I couldn't answer that, I was inclined to think that he would, and that his travel would merely not repeat due to the change.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened my eyes after a while. I saw the familiar ceiling I'd been staring at before, but the illumination had slightly changed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Turning to the window, I noticed the sun was setting.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had been going to sleep very early, so I was pretty tired. However, there was something I had to do that I didn't want to leave for the next day.{w} I'd been yawning and stretching on the floor, but I felt I had a bit of time before going to bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Since doing it on Thursday might have been a bad idea, I stood up and went to the entrance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The sky had gotten a lot darker, and the icy air almost changed my mind.{w} I quickly put my coat and boots back on, checked that everything was in my purse, and stepped out after turning off the lights.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Snow was still falling, but it was much lighter, like in the morning. I wondered whether to turn back to grab an umbrella, but I didn't intend to be out for too long, and it didn't seem like the snow was picking up at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went down the stairs and began to walk. ...I looked at the ground, where neither the tire tracks nor the footprints were visible anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was remarkable how different the periphery was compared to the center of the town. After some minutes, I'd only seen a handful of people quietly wandering with an umbrella, but the many lit windows all around gave away the presence of life.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I reached the lonely crosswalk leading to Ramon and saw the wide street ahead, illuminated by many faint streetlights. Home to many stores, it looked like an entrance to a different town, its wet stone occupied with passersby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's late, but I think it should be open...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I continued up the path, waiting for my destination to come into sight. While I'd never entered it, I recalled seeing it open at that hour.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It should be that.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Ahead and still in Ramon was what looked like a blue storefront with white letters above it. It read "Ishimaru".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood in front of its door. The interior was lit, and a woman was sitting behind a transparent wall. Nonetheless, I felt a bit reluctant to step in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was something about the situation that felt too surreal. I couldn't feel bad about myself, though, because what I was doing was a necessary step.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I pulled the door open and entered the small space, protected from the cold once more. The woman smiled warmly at me as I approached.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Good afternoon. You'd like to try your luck?
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...Yeah.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Perfect. Have you come here before? I don't think you have.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...No, I have. I came a while ago, but I'd forgotten to check if I'd won anything until now.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Ah, I see. What would you like, then?
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I thought about how to phrase the few questions I had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The number I had was for December 1st, I believe. I wonder, by the way, how long would it be valid for?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Oh, it's still valid, don't worry. They last a whole year.{w} Anyway, December 1st? Let me see.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I hadn't been sure what day to say, but I hadn't wanted to ask for the previous day's. If I went back to November, I'd change the past in a considerable way. Then, the butterfly effect could affect what I was doing.{w} I knew each digit of a winning lottery number was manually drawn every time, so if I changed the past and made it back to the same day, it was entirely possible the latest winning number would differ. A mere millisecond of difference could result in a different draw. I'd chosen December 1st because it was the next day after Miiya's death, and I didn't know how far back I'd end up being able to go.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After looking at a computer screen for a few seconds, the woman voiced a number.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: December 1st... I'm assuming you bought a standard Lotus-6 combination, correct?
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...Yes.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: On December 1st, the number drawn was 30-05-12-31-15-26, and the bonus number was 24.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...Ah, I don't think that was it. It would've been great to win on the first attempt.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Do you have the ticket? You might've won one of the secondary prizes if any of the last numbers coincide.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...I didn't bring it, no. I'm sure none match, though.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I see. That's unfortunate.{w} Do you want to try again?
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Maybe. I have a couple questions, though. I've always been curious about this.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Would I be able to ask for a specific number that I want?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yes, that's possible. We tend to sell packs of five different combinations, but you can also choose the numbers you want if it's what you prefer.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: All right.{w} How much would I have won if all the digits matched?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Let me see...{w} The main prize money of December 1st was ¥917,999,011.{w} It's even higher now. Nobody's won the jackpot in a while.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Oh, wow. I'm not sure what I'd do with so much money.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Some people say it's unlucky to win that much. It has ruined people's lives.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Yeah, I would be very overwhelmed.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I don't remember: how much does buying a number cost?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: It's just ¥200.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I see. ...Is it possible to buy a number that will be played the same day you buy it?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yes, but only before {time=17.} You don't have to worry about this today since the next Lotus-6 will be held on the 5th, this Thursday.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Ah, I understand. I think I'll come back, then. I'd like to think about the number I want.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: That's perfectly fine. I hope you're right on the mark.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Me too.{w} I'm sorry for having so many questions, but if I won, would my identity have to be revealed?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Oh, no, Japanese law doesn't enforce that.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: ...And how long would I have to wait to receive the money?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: No more than two weeks. You'd be able to choose whether to receive the full amount at once or monthly. You wouldn't have to worry about taxes, either.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Thank you! I was always curious about this.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I'm glad I could help. I'll see you next time.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I bowed and walked out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I began to walk down the street, repeating the numbers mentally. While writing them down was a good idea, I had to ensure I could memorize them, because it was likely any written note would disappear if I traveled far to the past again, just like the knife had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll probably just get in big trouble. Within two weeks, I'd receive the money in my bank account, so I'd probably have to take out the money before the other me notices what happened...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: For that, I'd have to duplicate my bank card or try to take it out of the other me's purse.{w} What would I do if I saw that so much money was added and immediately taken from my account? If it was investigated, security cameras would probably see me in the bank.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Maybe not taking everything would be a good idea. If I leave a part for the other me, would she keep quiet...? I'm not sure what I would do myself in that situation, honestly.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I could hardly take those thoughts seriously. ...Had I really assumed that I'd try to go live far away all by myself?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She also said that she'd never seen me there before. I suppose that means that there currently is no me who bought that number after going to the past. Of course, that will only happen when history is greatly altered, so it isn't the case yet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I still felt a little unsure. Would the number stay the same if I changed the past even a little bit...?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On December 1st, I will already have changed the past. However, I guess that if I travel to days before the 30th, I'll be able to obtain the Sekimeiya myself and redo this in a way so that the past only changes when I buy the number. I guess the past wouldn't even have to change in that instance. Buying the ticket wouldn't contradict any previous experiences.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A bit of snow was still falling, but it was hard to see it without looking at the streetlights. Yawning as I went, I walked back over my own steps until I arrived at my apartment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped in, leaving my coat and boots behind as usual. I thought of trying to eat something else, but I was too tired to bother, and nothing I had was appetizing anyway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I changed into the same nightwear and turned off the light in the entrance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took a piece of paper and a pen out of a drawer. Just in case, I wrote down the winning combination.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After that, I straightened up my blankets and buried myself underneath them, leaving my phone by the side of my bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Mom hasn't tried to call me again. I wonder what happened with that.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Once again, I found myself comfortably lying on my soft mattress while another version of myself was suffering in the hospital.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I moreso felt bad for the me I was, who only had two last opportunities to appreciate the touch of that old bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What was it?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I felt my head hurt a bit, but I tried to recall the winning combination before looking at the bedside table.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I felt like I'd only slept for the blink of an eye, as I vividly remembered the thoughts I'd had in the evening. I looked up, still covering my eyes with the bed sheets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Saving Reverie
...I shuffled the blankets aside. I'd gotten too used to the feeling of waking up to a warm room. It was almost more pleasant than being covered in softness.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't want to spend a long time in bed, so I pushed myself to get up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I raised the blinds, filling the bedroom with light. Behind the glass was the still image of a white Yushibana with the sun already up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The snow had ceased during the night, and a bit of fog was all that remained, especially prominent in the distant mountains. It was a beautiful and peaceful thing to see, but I felt some deep strain as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My phone showed {time=9:57.} I had no plans for the day, but it was a very special one. Like usual, I stepped to the bathroom and rubbed my eyes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I still had two cereal bars left. I tossed the wrappers in the trash and started to eat them as I tiredly stretched my arms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been nervously pacing as I ate them and stopped myself as soon as I realized it.{w} I didn't have anything to do, and repeatedly going over the same thoughts was only stressful. I'd decided to spend my final free day in as relaxing of a manner as I could manage, but I couldn't let myself keep worrying about losing precious time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went back to my bedroom and looked at the wardrobe to pick something to change into.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stared at what I had. I'd been selecting random clothes for the past few days, but I found myself thinking a little harder about it.{w} I had a blue hoodie that I really liked in mind, but I couldn't find it, so I ended up grabbing a long-sleeved orange shirt instead.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My laundry basket was nearly full. The previous day's clothes were there, and it had been a while since I'd washed them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Doing the laundry most certainly didn't matter anymore, but I dragged the basket to the kitchen nonetheless. The washing machine was there, next to another basket which was close to full.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tended to prioritize washing what I left in my bedroom, but I still had the blue hoodie in mind, so I rifled through both piles.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wasn't able to find it with a cursory inspection, but I didn't want to empty both baskets just for that, so I began to fill the washer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The machine wasn't too spacious, so I could only pick out part of the basket. Once I'd filled it with the top half, I pushed the round door shut and poured in a bit of laundry detergent.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had a number of clothes at home that I'd accumulated throughout the years, but since they were all on the cheap side, I didn't trust using hot water. When I pressed the big blue button, "30:00" appeared in red digits on the screen and began to count down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I grabbed the lighter bucket and brought it back to my bedroom, where it was more convenient.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I ended up sitting on the carpet. I was trying to calm my nerves, but as soon as I made any attempt to stop thinking, it became incredibly difficult.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wanted to go out again, somewhere. Staying still, the mess of emotions inside me was uncontrollable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Does it even matter, though? I can go to Ina, but it's not fair to say goodbye to someone without them knowing it, and I'd just be so sad without being able to say why...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, the past would change, and that'd be overwritten anyway.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...I really tried to keep my mood pleasant. It was possible I wouldn't find the Sekimeiya the next day, and even after traveling, I could go to Ina Café before the 30th to reach a time that wouldn't be deleted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The time had been passing far too fast, so I rested my head on a pillow, knowing that would slow it down. I stayed there for a few minutes and listened to the washer work. Even if doing the laundry didn't matter, my clothes could get moldy if they stayed inside for too long...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I heard it running from the living room. When the intensity increased, I knew the spin-dry had begun and that only a few minutes were left. I went to check.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could see the meshed clothes rapidly spinning behind the glass, and the countdown approaching the last three minutes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I watched the seconds tick until four zeros filled the screen. Then, I grabbed the plastic handle and opened the door. I placed a blue bucket below it and dropped the compact, wet mess of clothes in it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I dragged it to the wardrobe as well. I didn't have a dryer, so since the outside was freezing, I had to use a foldable washing line with the help of the heater.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I made room on the floor and opened it up, proceeding to grab the pieces and hang them individually.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They weren't too wet, so I kept crouching and using as few of my scarce clothespins as possible.{w} I took out a pretty blue and white shirt. I figured that I was still pretty tired since I thought I'd left it out of the washer due to the bad memories it brought, but I still hung it properly and kept going.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was done fairly quickly and looked at the neatly-hung laundry that would likely never be used. I turned around, looking down at my feet until I got to the front door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been going outside without a defined reason, and I felt obligated to do it again. Spending the entire day inside would have been too difficult.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I got ready to leave and recalled I'd left my purse in my bedroom, so I went to grab it along with my phone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was about to reach for the front door, but I walked to the kitchen instead, remembering the garbage bag where I'd thrown the cereal bar wrappers. It was almost full, so I made a knot with the bands and returned.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I pushed away a bit of snow that had accumulated on the ground, just like most of the neighboring apartments had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The cold was still biting, but I'd come to expect it by that point. Stepping with satisfying crunches, I went down the stairs. The sky had cleared completely, and the street seemed especially bright. I walked the opposite way as usual, toward the garbage bins.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They were at the very end of the street, past the curve that could be seen in the distance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I threw the bag in the bin for combustibles and started to walk toward the center of Yushibana.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As opposed to the previous day, my first view of Ramon was the crowded street it had always been. After crossing the road, I walked near the left buildings until I was on the thinner path.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Of course, Ina was open. I saw the large screen of glass and Darfee behind the counter, seemingly texting with his phone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Oh, hey! I'm glad to see you've taken a liking to this place again.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...Yeah.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I stepped up to the bar. Like the previous day, there was no one inside at that time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How are you?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I'm okay.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I must have looked a little worse than before. I figured he thought it was just due to Miiya's death, but there was much more affecting me than solely that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Do you want one of these?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: He pointed at the pastries I'd been eating across the past couple of days.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Yeah, I'm hungry.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He grabbed a small plate from below the counter and placed it in front of me with the pastry. I bit into it, a little bit tired of eating the same thing repeatedly, but glad that I at least had the option.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Going to sit at the same place again?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I turned to the table he was pointing to.{w} As I spun, something caught my eye.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was a TV close to the entrance. It was muted, but I could see a reporter speaking into a microphone.{w} I recalled the words of the police officer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I will, yeah.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I grabbed the plate and stepped back, but I sat on the opposite chair from last time so that I could see the screen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Would it be announced today...? That seems unlikely.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But as soon as I sat on the chair, I read the white text at the bottom of the screen, which had just changed from a different headline.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Stopping Power
"Xyn member caught for the first time yesterday in Yushibana".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had to read it two more times. That didn't make sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Can you turn the volume up, please?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Darfee looked at the TV, and when he read what it said, he did as I asked despite his own surprise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before he did, the image changed. That time, I immediately recognized what I saw, but once again, it didn't make any sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell...? ...Wasn't that in the newspaper?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The voice of the reporter began to reach us, and when it did, the image had transitioned once again.{w} For a second, it had been a short video recorded from a security camera. It showed a prison cell and a person in prison clothing hard to recognize due to the high angle.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...ested yesterday in a lonely street of Yushibana. He is believed to be a member of the criminal group Xyn, but his identity is unknown.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I tried to give meaning to those words, but I couldn't. The brief footage had been almost identical to the picture from the newspaper, and they were saying that the man's identity was unknown, just like in that article.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: An interrogation is taking place, and the police are actively attempting to identify the suspect. This is likely to be the first member of the group to be caught, so the situation is being properly taken care of.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: After those words, the reporter bowed, and an ad began to play.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked at Darfee, who appeared confused as well. Before he could say anything, I stood up and approached a table next to the counter.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd seen a pile of newspapers there before, and it hadn't moved. Immediately, I saw that the one I'd read was still there, facing down. I opened it and rushed to the first two pages.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's here—what was just shown looked exactly like this picture.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Darfee was looking at me with a serious face, and I brought the newspaper to him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sorry, I might be going insane, but I could've sworn I'd seen that before. Wasn't it exactly like this?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: U-Uh...
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: He looked at the article I was pointing to and narrowed his eyebrows further.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Y-You're right... It's the same cell, but this says it's from November 24th.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Didn't the person also look the same?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Did he...? I couldn't get a good look at him, but I can't in this picture either.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: He began to read the text.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I never learned about this... On November 24th, a prisoner escaped from a cell.{w} But Xyn isn't mentioned here even though they also said the identity of the person wasn't known.{w} ...How's that possible? They don't know the identity of someone they arrested?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I looked back at the TV, but it was still only ads.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yeah, it's strange. My mind immediately went to this article, but there's probably no correlation. Every cell must be recorded from this angle, so to me it seemed like they were the same.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Ah, it could be that.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I sat on the chair again. Of course, it was no coincidence.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The person who'd been arrested had been following me, meaning that it was very likely they had come from the future. Then, the person from the article had appeared in the cell on the 24th, a day I knew for a fact people had arrived at from the 15th.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell was going on, then? Could they have been the same person? A few days earlier, they'd appeared in that cell. The previous day, they'd been arrested.{w} What kind of coincidence was that? Had he been sent to the same cell? Had the police not realized that he was the person who'd escaped on the 24th? And why was his identity unknown if they thought he was a Xyn member?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was baffled, but an important piece of the puzzle came back to me. Once again, it was what Katei told us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Xyn had attempted to steal the Sekimeiya once before the 15th. They failed, and while the police had the chance to catch a Xyn member, they escaped.{w} I couldn't remember the exact way it was phrased, but that had happened once before the 15th...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What is the connection between the article and this arrest...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't help but feel that something was incredibly backward. The resemblance between both events was undeniable. Even Darfee immediately noticed it, unaware of the extra links I knew regarding the person and the Sekimeiya's travel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They caught a Xyn member for the first time.{w} ...But they'll escape before the 15th. Katei and the article prove that.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It couldn't be so straightforward because the article discussed an event from November 24th. While both events couldn't be the very same, they couldn't be separate either.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I ate what remained of the pastry, trying to clear the cloudy confusion that had arisen in my mind. Behind both of those events was the Sekimeiya—that by itself already gave away that something unnatural was at work.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's something crucial that I can't ignore.{w} In both cases, someone ended up in a prison cell. I don't know if the same person was caught both times, but it's very likely they came from the future. So, anything regarding them could differ from the reality I know.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Xyn member who traveled from the 15th could've already changed this. If he got arrested after traveling in this reality, there would be a second Xyn member caught after the first time—the person from the future who was following me.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}Trying to work it all out, I'd locked up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wasn't there something else Katei said? ...That Ashiya or the police chose not to reveal that they'd almost caught a Xyn member before they'd escaped.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Doesn't this fit all too well with the article? If both events are connected, the fact that the person in the cell was a Xyn member must match as well. However, in the article, that wasn't revealed. ...Could that be the original event that Katei told us about?{w} That person escaped and managed to get to the tower. After that, they traveled to the past and got caught again when they were following me. Somehow, the police still didn't know their identity, but this time it was revealed that they were a Xyn member.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's right. This must be a change made by a person who traveled from the 15th. After all, someone from Xyn was just revealed to have been caught, which never happened in our reality.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...But what I just came up with doesn't make sense either.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It doesn't make sense if the person from the 24th really teleported to the cell. Which must have happened, given what I know happened to Vaisude...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If whoever that person was traveled to the cell from the 15th, they couldn't have been the same person to be caught yesterday, because the second arrest must be a new event.{w} Could it be that history was changed, but I still remember the one that both I and that man came from because I also traveled from it?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I noticed a mistake I'd made.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the 24th, it's very likely a Xyn member appeared in a cell from the future. Now that I think of it, though, it can't be that he was actually caught and then escaped while Ashiya decided not to reveal he was from Xyn.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That doesn't match because Katei said they were caught after trying to steal the Sekimeiya before the 15th. It hadn't even been found on the 24th.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What the hell, then?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had very little information, so I looked at the screen when I heard the news had come back. Unfortunately, they began to talk about a different topic, and Darfee quickly turned down the volume and looked at me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nonetheless, it was probably a good thing. A member from Xyn who'd traveled from the 15th had been caught, and since that had been revealed, there was no reason to think he would escape. It was an event that hadn't occurred when we'd originally stepped into the tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Piecing all the details together with what I knew seemed almost impossible, as no possibility made total sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm... I did wonder before why he appeared in a jail cell on the 24th.{w} From the 15th, it's very likely he'd appear somewhere he'd been before in the past.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And now this could fit. If the arrest from yesterday always occurred, the position on the 24th could be based on today.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But then questions like how he was in the tower on the 15th or why he was following me start to crop up.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I slowed down, sensing a headache. No matter what the truth was, it was messy.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What was the link between both events? Which one was new, and which one had always happened? Regardless of the arrangement I tried, something always seemed to get in the way.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And when I'd calmed down internally, one option seemed more plausible than the others.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I believed that the 30th of November was the day somebody attempted to steal the Sekimeiya. That was probably correct since nobody was caught and no connection to Xyn was made. Katei would've been talking about this.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: On the 15th, a Xyn member traveled to the 24th and appeared in an unlocked cell. Due to that, he was able to escape.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After following me, he was caught yesterday. That changed the past because no Xyn member had been caught yet on the 15th.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What's iffy about this? That their identity was unknown, that the cell could've been the same one...?{w} The fact that they appeared in a cell on the 24th might also be a contradiction—they wouldn't have been there before traveling. I feel like there are more problems, but I don't know how to identify them.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...But if this is what happened, Xyn must be in disarray. Someone from their group was arrested when they're all still free. Could this make them rethink their attack? That could be bad.{w} Maybe Ashiya won't care about using the Sekimeiya as bait now that a Xyn member's been caught, but the event should still happen...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Oh, one thing definitely is strange, though.{w} On the 24th, the police weren't able to identify the person who appeared in the cell. But he was arrested in the street yesterday, and that policeman almost seemed like he knew that it was a good arrest to make.{w} That doesn't make any sense. That man was in the tower on the 15th, so if the police were fine with arresting him yesterday, it follows they would've also arrested him immediately on the morning of the 15th.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Could it be that didn't happen because he entered the tower through the storeroom? And, if what happened on the 24th somehow made the police arrest him yesterday, wouldn't they have said that he'd been the one who had appeared in the cell on the 24th?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Whatever the case, it seemed like an enigma that I probably had to put aside. It was at least good that the person following me had been caught. It could only have been beneficial to my plan.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you thinking about the news?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Darfee addressed me after I'd been in thought for a few minutes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A bit. It just threw me off.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I see. Well, it's good that someone from that group finally got caught.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Yeah, I agree.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: The past had certainly changed in front of me. I wasn't in the same reality I knew, so letting everything repeat to remain as the only me was not an option anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was still the major worry that the Sekimeiya could be stolen at any moment. Even if someone from the future had been removed from the equation, that didn't completely rule out the possibility.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As a matter of fact, the Sekimeiya could have already been stolen. How did the police know that the person they'd caught was with Xyn? Was it because he'd already taken it? The thought of that sent a chill down my spine.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Do you know about the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Huh? ...What do you mean?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Ashiya's event.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Hm? Yeah, of course.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Well, nobody stole the Sekimeiya, right...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: The Sekimeiya...? N-No. ...As far as I know, at least.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: All right, I just wanted to make sure since I haven't been paying attention to the news.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He looked a little concerned, so I turned to the window. Did he think it was bad I had my thoughts elsewhere after a friend of mine had died? I doubted it, but that was the impression his look gave me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stared out the window. I could only see the narrow street, as opposed to the moving Ramon. ...Just what had happened to the world I knew?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At that point, it was best to focus on what still mattered.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With no snow falling, there'd been hardly any movement outside. A few people had come to buy the remaining bread, but time seemed to have stilled for a while.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood up from the chair and informed Darfee that I'd be heading out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: All right, Shiroya. Have a good day. It'll be ¥150.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I took out three coins from my wallet and handed them to him. He mirrored my smile but not the underlying sadness behind it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Goodbye.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I'll see you.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...I walked out of the door and stepped onto the snow again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I made some distance from Ina, brooding all the while. I had a hard time accepting that it might have been my last visit.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been slowly walking down Ramon when I stopped myself to stare at a street branching off on the other side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd taken that path many times to get to Atsuki's house, so I soon realized I was nervously biting my lip again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't have anywhere to go in more ways than one. A huge change in history had occurred—I'd never go back to the world I knew.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That meant that making sure Atsuki and I couldn't go to the event had become an even higher priority. It no longer had a downside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I'd decided the previous day that I'd do it on Thursday, but that was potentially a bad idea. I didn't know when Atsuki would leave his house, and waiting in front of it all day wasn't something I wanted to do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After all, if it got too late, I'd have to ring the bell and face him.{w} ...I didn't think I could do that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I only had one job: setting up a future that was perfect for everyone but me, then walking away from it. I couldn't fight that anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I crossed the street and walked through the narrower one, arriving at a part of Yushibana I'd always found pretty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At other times of the year, you could see the green leaves beneath the snow of the tall trees. The road was still white, but it was almost immaculate. I slowly crossed to the opposite sidewalk.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki's house was there. Before I got too close, a sharp pain in my chest stopped me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Would I really never enter it again?{w} Could I really have been mere minutes away from going in and out of that door for the last time?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had a hard time believing it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I ran up to the gate before that hesitation could take hold of me completely.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I looked through the bars. Maxi wasn't in front of the door anymore, but his small paws had left imprints in the snow around it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He is here.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There was light behind a curtain. With no guarantee that Atsuki wouldn't see me, I stepped behind a tree.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I really didn't want to be seen. If I talked to Atsuki, I was afraid that I would lose any resolve I had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I can't just stay here all day, waiting for him to leave. I don't even know if he will.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There was a last resort available. Since I knew where he kept an extra house key, just behind the gate, I could try to enter the house and silently grab Miiya's purse, which had been left in the living room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Not now, though. If it wasn't a coincidence that he was in the hospital when I woke up, he should leave at some point.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Would he leave if I called him from my phone and quickly hung up?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}I decided against that again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Should I just wait here...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I crossed back to the other side of the road and surveyed the door from afar. I looked around; it appeared I was the only person there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Most of the trees there were too thin to cover me, so there was nowhere I could safely watch from.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I glanced at a corner far ahead. I'd be able to see the window from there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Slightly hesitant, I walked to it and peered at his house. As I'd thought, I'd be able to see him leaving while still being out of sight.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was something a bit worrying that I also noticed, however. It was the trail of footprints I'd left.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Will he notice the trail going behind the tree?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It seemed unlikely that he'd think it was suspicious, but he could find me by following them with his eyes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll just have to be careful.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...But no matter what I thought, I was uncomfortable. I couldn't take my eyes off his house, and I didn't particularly enjoy the thought of spending my last real day in Yushibana spying on Atsuki.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I need to do it, though.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I hid myself and leaned against the dark, cold wall.{w} Suddenly, I recognized what I was looking at.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd seen that very street the previous day, when I'd been following Isla.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's right... There's no reason not to do the same with Isla since I might know where she lives as well.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Leaving Enric behind, I walked until a crossing street turned to the right. There was the entrance to the dead end I'd been at.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stared at the short house where the small footprints had ended the previous day. I couldn't see any light coming from inside, and nobody was around me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Faded footprints were scattered all over the ground, and some ended at that front door. I placed myself behind the same black car as before to avoid being right in the middle of the path.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wondered what to do. Changing the past no longer felt like an obstacle, so I was free to decide on anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla should be at school, but I don't know about Erina, and I don't know if anyone else lives here. ...How the hell can I take their tickets for the event when I don't even know where they're keeping them?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}I considered two important facts: in the attic, Erina had implied they'd bought the tickets pretty early. That meant they were likely to already have them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Secondly, before locking ourselves in the bedroom, everyone's possessions had been looked at. While tickets for the event had been found on almost everyone who'd been a visitor, none had been in Erina's purse.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They were probably inside Isla's, then. Could they already be there...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The pressure of being in a crucial moment was getting to me. I stepped out and slowly approached the door.
entries.speaker: i
