entries.text: If Erina and Isla didn't go to the tower, different people would in their place. It was overwhelmingly likely that as long as Ashiya had the Sekimeiya, people would get trapped in that building. However, Isla's fate could be averted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...And I could change the past. When I was in front of the door, I stared at the tiny white bell at its side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina and Isla don't know me. I can just press it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But what about Isla's friend? What was the truth behind that...? Is someone else really living here with them?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: My arm reached out and touched the cold doorbell almost unconsciously, like it was another organism.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But really, what should I say...? I suppose that'll vary depending on who opens the door.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd seen no light inside, so maybe nobody would. I firmly rang the doorbell.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Is there actually nobody here?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A day earlier, the small footprints had ended at the door, and it was close to the same time of the day that it had been.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I suspected I knew what the reason was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla! Are you here...!?{w} It's me, Shiroya!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: There was no reply.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is she out again?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd wondered about it already, but my intention was to take the tickets from Erina and Isla. If I did that, Isla couldn't travel to the past... so her "friend" might no longer have existed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I'd seen her from the café during school hours. That had to be an Isla who'd traveled from the future.{w} Why had she been out of her house? I figured she wouldn't have wanted to show herself anywhere, which was why she wasn't opening the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla, are you here?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I knocked on the door lightly, but it didn't seem like I'd be answered.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The mystery behind Isla's friend was nowhere near solved. If their real identity was an Isla who'd come from the future, why hadn't she prevented herself from going to the event? My intention was to do just that, so my unease grew. Plenty of things about Isla had been questionable when looking back at it, but the voice recorder and her friend's existence were the biggest ones.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been standing there for a while, and nothing had changed. Part of me wanted to give up, but the idea of her friend purposely not opening the door was one I didn't like at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Suddenly, the door opened wide and I saw the dark interior.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was nobody there. I'd simply tried to open the door and succeeded.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It was unlocked?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd grabbed the handle to make some noise, and I'd accidentally pushed forward.{w} I didn't move. I kept staring inside until I was sure it was vacant. Then, I lightly pushed the door a bit more and took a careful step in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I scanned the area and immediately noticed a wide assortment of items on the ground. Toys, dolls, coloring books, and markers. In the corner was a pile of laundry, and the walls had a few faded scribbles on them, as if someone had tried to wash them away. There were also pictures of a child at various stages of growth, and her mother was occasionally in the shot with her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened the entryway closet in search of the purse and was faced with a few women's and girls' jackets. Scattered in the closet were clothes you wouldn't typically see when visiting someone's house.{w} An apron with the name of a local restaurant, a uniform for a factory worker, and a cap branded with the logo of a convenience store.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't have to search for long. Right inside was the purse Isla had been wearing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Without hesitation, I looked inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The most important issue was resolved immediately—the recorder wasn't there. I saw a pack of tissues and small sunglasses, but no tickets either.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, this is strange. When we found the recorder, I looked at this purse, and the tickets weren't there either. ...Were they in Isla's pockets?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I felt a sudden chill and looked at my sides. Nobody was there, but that in itself was very strange...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why... is this purse here? Yesterday, the reason why I recognized Isla was precisely because she was wearing the purse outside. If she's outside right now, why is her purse here?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There was some kind of creeping, unknown dread at my back, but I immediately rationalized it away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The person I saw yesterday was likely Isla's "friend". She was wearing her purse, and she isn't here right now.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: This purse belongs to the original Isla who's at school. If that's it, this makes a lot of sense.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But why was the door unlocked? Was it a normal thing for them? ...And why would the other Isla be going anywhere during the day?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The chance to take their tickets was there. Instead of focusing on specifics, I just had to take that simple action.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And when I let go of the purse, I noticed I'd missed a lower pocket.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I unzipped it and narrowed my eyes. All I saw were two folded pieces of paper that I easily recognized.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I grabbed them with two fingers and unfolded them, confirming they were the event tickets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't give it another thought before dashing out and closing the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I froze up, realizing how suspicious I looked. I instinctively crumpled the tickets in my fist, but nobody was around to see me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I breathed deeply and began to walk away, calm and nonchalant. I had prevented it; I wasn't in my world anymore, but Isla wouldn't die.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What would happen with Isla? If two versions of her really existed, then it seemed they'd both permanently persist in a single reality. However, I'd already decided once that was the better option, so I'd just put her in the same situation as me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I soon made it back to Enric avenue. From the same corner, I saw light behind Atsuki's window.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stared at it for a bit, but I gave up after a short while. I just wanted to go home and wait for tomorrow to come.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd always liked walking through that street, but I turned around and moved to Ramon as I stepped through the thin, parallel path.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Tomorrow, I'll definitely have to take our tickets, no matter how. It might not be as much of a priority as I thought, though.{w} If I find the Sekimeiya in the tower and enter it during the night, I'll either travel through time or be caught by the police. If I travel through time, taking our tickets won't matter since I'll change the past. ...And if I get caught by the police, there's no way Atsuki won't learn about it. I'm not sure what would happen to my other self, but I doubt she and Atsuki would just go to the tower on the 15th.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I would still do it, just in case. For the time being, I simply kept going over the lottery numbers in my head, slowly approaching my apartment. When I was getting close, I saw the footprints I'd left earlier, but again, it seemed that the previous day's weren't there. ...However much my steps left impressions, it was clear that they were all bound to eventually fade.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Of course, it was warm inside my apartment again. I shrugged off my coat almost immediately.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked at my phone. It was {time=14:04.}{w} There was nothing else I wanted to do for the day, so I went to the kitchen after a long pause.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As much as I disliked the idea of eating noodles again, I had nothing else. I didn't want to go buy food again because I'd just feel like I was doing something else in Yushibana for the last time. Like the day before, I washed the only pot I had and boiled a bit of water before dropping a stiff block of noodles in it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I waited for them to be cooked, sparingly moving them with two new chopsticks. When four minutes had passed, I poured most of the liquid out and let the noodles fall into a bowl.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew exactly what their taste would be before I began to eat. It was really getting old, but I powered through.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The bowl was empty, and I could hardly tell I'd just eaten. I tried to lie on the floor, but it was a bit uncomfortable for my stomach. Instead, I grabbed the bowl and brought it back to the kitchen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I placed it in the sink and opened the cabinet with the food I'd bought. After inspecting it briefly, I indifferently closed the wooden door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was about to drop the packaging of the noodles into the trash, but I remembered I'd thrown out the bag earlier. I took the roll out of a drawer and placed a new, empty bag in the corner. I thought back on the tickets and looked inside my purse. I'd left both of them there, so I threw them in the garbage as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went back to sit on one of the scattered cushions. As much as I felt incredibly overwhelmed, I was out of things to think about. Eventually, I dropped on the floor and emptily let time pass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was surreal to think the walls around me, which I'd seen for so many years, could soon disappear forever. There was so much uncertainty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No matter what awaited... my future was going to be miserable. Every scenario led to roughly the same thing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...How was it going to be anything better than terrible? I would either get caught by the police or have to keep on living with sketchy money I wasn't even sure I knew how to obtain.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd have no proper identity and no idea how to get a new one or do anything else... There's no way this will work, and the other version of me will live her life completely clueless, maybe until she finds out she was arrested somewhere.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Even if none of those options occur... if I can't go back in time again, but I also don't get caught... What the hell happens then? I'd just have to explain everything to Atsuki and myself. ...What would my thoughts have been if another version of myself appeared like that during the impact of Miiya's death?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There really wasn't a good possible way it could all end. Even though I'd chosen the sole path that could save Miiya, achieving it was actually no guarantee.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At this time tomorrow, I'll already have been in the tower, and I'll be thinking about the best way to act. If I can't pull things off in the night, what the hell will I say to the police? They'll immediately realize another me is in the hospital.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I wonder what would happen if I revealed what the Sekimeiya can do. They'd have to believe me due to my existence.{w} And then what? Would they let me go with no real identity of my own? Would the Sekimeiya be kept a secret? If so, there's no chance I'd be able to live anything akin to a normal life.{w} Honestly, maybe getting caught by the police would be better... Or, if I'm able to save Miiya, I could reveal myself, and they'd decide what to do.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}I realized I'd just thought that and pitied myself. I'd been feeling sporadic senses of liberty the past few days after being shut away for so long, so the fact that I'd seen an outcome deprived of any freedom as acceptable was just disheartening.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was undoubtedly absurd that I'd held off from going to the tower for so long. My hesitation could have doomed me at any point. I was just selfish. I wanted those tranquil days to continue despite knowing they couldn't—being in my living room was proof enough of that...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It appeared to just be misfortune that what I wanted was the single thing that definitely couldn't happen. Ironically, there was no going back. The important decision had already been made, and I was only stalling out the clock.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My mind hadn't changed, and if I went back to the time I'd decided, the result wouldn't differ. It had been clear from the beginning that there was no win-win situation.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't possible to go back to my old world, not even with the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I traveled days through time, I wouldn't be able to let everything play out as it once had anymore. There were people who'd traveled from the 15th and changed history... In the blink of an eye, the world I'd always lived in had distanced from me so much that it was no longer reachable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, with no room for doubt, attempting to save Miiya was what I had to do. I needed to figure out a way to travel days through time once more and save her. If I took the Sekimeiya before November 27th, that'd be the best I could do. ...And then, after that would come a new decision, almost as important as the last.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After lying on the floor for so long, my nervousness gradually dissipated. There was no way I'd be able to calm myself the next day, but the beige walls of my living room were oddly relaxing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe I really was spending my last hours there, as unbelievable as it felt. I was in a situation I didn't think anyone else had ever been in, and I was the one who had chosen to go through it alone. But I was at a point where I really had to believe in my decisions, and I was confident in thinking that giving myself that last day had been the right thing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't keep the myriad of thoughts from circling through my mind, but they eventually faded into the background. Time advanced, the light slowly abandoning the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}What the hell was I thinking?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd had to keep so many things in mind that I couldn't really be surprised I'd made such a large oversight.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took Isla's and Erina's tickets to prevent them from going to the tower on the 15th. It sounded like a good idea because they could've sold out quickly...{w} I completely ignored that they could simply print them out again. ...I don't think they'd have to buy new ones.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I sighed, exasperated. I'd never had a printer, so I hadn't thought it through. I knew Atsuki and I hadn't checked our tickets until the 14th, but we would've been able to print new ones if they hadn't been there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How the hell do I do this, then? Unless Erina and Isla don't notice that their tickets are gone until they're in the tower, they can just go anyway.{w} At least in the case of Atsuki and myself, it was seeing our tickets that made us decide to go through with attending the event, so we might actually not go if I do take them.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I really didn't want to think very hard about it, but I wasn't too worried. If I got caught by the police, Atsuki and I probably wouldn't go to the event, but if I wasn't able to find the Sekimeiya, I'd have to think of something else. Maybe a note wasn't a horrible idea, or I could break his printer. There had to be at least one way to stop Atsuki and me from going.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And Erina and Isla... If I'm not able to travel, I could just try to talk to them again, but I'm not sure what I'd say. I wonder if they'd accuse me of stealing their tickets if I suddenly show up warning them not to go.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd think about that tomorrow, after getting inside the tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't moved in too long, and I'd begun to feel tired. The sun was setting, so my body was requesting that I sleep at the same time it had gotten accustomed to.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It seemed laughable to think I'd be able to fall asleep. I could try to quell the onslaught of my thoughts, but there was no getting rid of them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once again, the same sharp pain hit me when I thought that it could have been my last night in that apartment. If I managed to go back in time the next day, it really was possible I'd never rest in my bed again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I already thought of this, but I shouldn't take it lightly. How exactly am I going to get in the tower tomorrow night if I'm getting tired at this time?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd enter the tower with a plan in mind. It could entail staying there for the entire duration or rushing out of the building with the Sekimeiya. While I wasn't sure yet, I didn't want to blow it due to a lack of sleep, and simply drinking coffee to stay awake had backfired numerous times.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I thought of placing the clothes I'd washed into the wardrobe, but I just couldn't bring myself to do it. There was nothing I could do but keep lying down, awaiting the time where I'd force myself into bed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But a while later, that time hadn't come. While I was tired, I couldn't manage to stand up, as that would mean finally abandoning the life I had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...If I stayed on the floor, it would mean the last night in my bed had already happened, and for some reason, I preferred that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sleep Paralysis
I managed to stand up, but only to turn off the light.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The room had become fully dark. I couldn't tell how much time had passed since I had looked away from the small, red light on the TV.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, I knew it had been a while. My head rested on a cushion, and the feel of the carpet was comforting. Even though I had no blanket, the heater allowed me to remain in the middle of the floor, contacting the table with my back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I hadn't fallen asleep. I had only sensed time passing, my vivid trains of thought infinitely spiraling into chaotic repetition.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That became mentally exhausting. I just wanted to fall asleep, but it didn't seem like it would ever happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The absolute silence had persisted for what felt like hours. At one point, I realized that I'd fallen asleep just for my awareness to instantly return.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That might've happened a few more times. However, I still felt as if I'd been awake the whole time, desperately trying to lose consciousness.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was the sun going to rise at any point? I had to go to the tower in the morning so that I had enough time until the next night.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I thought of setting an alarm, but I couldn't briefly sleep and be drowsy on such an important day.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been thinking about grabbing my phone for a while until I finally extended my arm and felt around the surface of the table. I dragged my phone toward me and shut my eyes tightly as I flipped it open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Soft, blue light soaked through my eyelids, prompting me to raise them. Then, I stared at the upper corner and waited for my blurry vision to fade.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's so late...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Next to the numbers, I saw the words "No service".
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Huh?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't think I'd seen them before, but I closed my phone to combat an abrupt headache.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After that, I dropped my head back on the pillow, starting to seriously worry.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no way I'd be in time for the event that would start in four hours. ...At least that wasn't too important.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it didn't feel like I'd ever fall asleep. When I had, I'd immediately reawakened, and once I'd seen the light of my phone, I couldn't get it out of my mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The entrance fee on the 15th had been pretty expensive... I believed I had enough money in my wallet, but if not, I still had the option of buying a normal visit.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I rolled onto my back. Being there was getting unbearable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Most of my stress had faded a long while ago, but that still hadn't been enough to fall asleep. The impression that I was wasting any of my time was intrusive.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I finally sat up and noticed that I really wasn't tired. After a short time, my constricting headache started to fade.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I grabbed my phone again. It was {time=5:30.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the 15th, we'd gone to the tower during the night because we hadn't been able to fall asleep. ...It was still very early, though.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I go before sleeping, I could come back later and rest until the afternoon. If I'll have to spend a long time in the tower the next night, that'll help me not be exhausted.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was doubtful I'd be able to sleep after coming back, when I'd finally be aware of the crucial details I needed.{w} But since it was likely Atsuki wouldn't be at home late in the day, I didn't think it was a terrible idea.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no way I'd be able to lie back down again after sitting up, let alone sleep. I'd been on that carpet for so many hours.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was still a bit dizzy, but I managed to carefully stand in the darkness and step out of the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: More than three hours remained until {time=9}, when the tower's halls would open to the public. On the 15th, though, Atsuki and I had been in the lobby since much earlier.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know if it was a bad idea, but I grabbed my coat and stepped into the pair of boots on the floor. I gripped the door and slowly pushed it open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The air was frigid as usual, but I couldn't feel any wind. A multitude of stars filled the dark sky, unmatched by the row of streetlights across the closest walkway. Not a soul could be seen, and the imposing atmosphere made me reconsider going out so early.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped forward, the snow stiff beneath my feet. I couldn't make out that layer of white anywhere but directly underneath the lights.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had my purse with me, so I closed the door and descended the stairs, purposely avoiding the frozen handrail.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked in the direction of the tower. However, for once, I couldn't see it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no chance I'd get lost, so I started to walk toward its location. As the tower was on the outskirts, the streetlights soon ceased, making me hug walls to know where I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't very far, and despite the eerie scenery, I was glad I'd left my apartment. I had to be in the tower in the morning, and I knew its entrance opened far before {time=9.} A receptionist had been there when we'd arrived, so I could try to buy tickets for the event and think about questions I wanted to ask.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kept walking, hoping I was getting closer. I could hardly see anything a few steps ahead, and as all lights had disappeared, I had to confirm the sensation of movement by looking at the ground.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I started to see more of the round light bulbs in the distance. I knew what it meant. That was the plaza in front of Ashiya Tower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I got closer and closer until I started to perceive the lights' quiet buzz. Then, I followed the path with my eyes, ending where the tower stood.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There it was. The immense building in the form of a huge shadow that covered the many stars behind it. I slowly got closer to it, interspersing the hum of the lights with sharp steps.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, before I expected to, I hit a wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It was the wall of the tower, which I suddenly hit with my foot. Startled, I felt it with my hand, expecting a cold stone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I touched something else entirely. My fingers felt a smooth, glassy surface, and as I stared at it with confusion, my vision adjusted just enough to understand where I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It was the door. No thick shutter was there either, as I could recognize the floor of the lobby a step beyond the glass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wondered to myself why I'd been surprised and immediately concluded that it was because there was no light. I'd suddenly hit the glass with no warning since the lights behind it weren't turned on.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Instead of putting my hand back in my pocket, I grabbed my phone. The screen displayed {time=5:48.} Then, I hesitantly gripped the handle of the door and tried to open it.{w} Like it seemed, it was locked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped back carefully, trying to get a feel for my surroundings.{w} ...And all I determined was that I was completely alone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the 15th, that door had been highlighted by the warm light behind it, and we'd entered it at {time=6.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That time was very close, but I began to wonder whether that had been a special occasion. Maybe they'd anticipated people would come very early and that was why the tower had been open at {time=6.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Over three hours were left until {time=9.} When would the entrance open? I had no way to know how long I'd have to wait.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I leaned on the icy metal of a nearby streetlight, the cold penetrating to my back. The light made my misty breath visible, emphasizing the harsh cold even further. Without a doubt, I wouldn't be able to stay there for long.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't take my eyes off the entrance, but I could hardly see it from where I'd moved to. As I waited outside, I knew people were behind the wall. At the very least, I knew someone was in the security room, waiting for a sudden attack that could come at any moment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood, covering my neck as much as I could. The ring of lights let me see slightly ahead in every direction, but past them, there was only darkness.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I figured something had to happen soon, but even if I wanted to, I didn't feel capable of turning back. If I moved again, I wouldn't be able to withstand the temperature, and physical fatigue was beginning to set back in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I felt like I'd been there for some time, I slowly took my hand out of my fuzzy coat, and with my thumb, I flipped open my phone to look at the time again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {time=6:03.}..{w} It had only been a few minutes, and the words "No service" were still there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd also looked at my phone on the 15th, before we'd been asked to leave them behind with the guards. By {time=6:03}, we'd already been allowed to step in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How much longer do I have to be here...? Is the tower not going to open until {time=9}?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I was still staring at the building. Any moment, the light behind the glass could turn on. Maybe someone would come and unlock it from the outside. ...There was no way it would remain closed for three more hours.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Without needing to look at my phone, I knew the time was passing glacially. The few minutes I'd been there had already felt much longer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Somehow, they had also passed very quickly. Had I really been there for more than twenty minutes? I felt as if even my mind had frozen through, a complete opposite from the spiraling mess it'd been at home.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wanted to close my eyes and slowly sit on the ground. Everything around me was dark enough that it wouldn't have made much difference, and it almost felt like my body was gradually sliding down the streetlight anyway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hoped I was retaining enough of my scarce strength to be able to walk into the building when the time came. I still believed that the lights would suddenly turn on, but I hadn't sensed a thing since I'd stopped moving.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I looked at the time again, it was {time=6:28.} Once more, it seemed as if the last half hour had happened in an instant, while the next one would last an eternity.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why was nothing happening? Even though it was so early, why was I alone? On the 15th, the group of people waiting for the event had begun hours before it started. Had that never been the case before?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even so, when would the door open? It was horrible not knowing how long I'd have to be there for.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The woman who was at the reception desk should come at any time. She was here so early, and so were the guards.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Oh, Katei too. ...He said he'd been taking the daily shifts recently.{w} Uh... did he say when he started? ...It should also be well before {time=9.}
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't do anything but keep waiting. I desperately needed that door to open, and I had only managed to stay out in the cold for so long because I believed it would.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to move my right hand, but I couldn't feel the soft touch of my pocket anymore. ...Was something really going to happen?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was hard to breathe properly, and the sporadic, soft wind began to feel painful. The harsh electric sound, which I'd thought to be minor upon arriving, was practically blaring.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had been there for an hour, and not a thing had changed. I blanched at the thought of waiting for two more hours, but the longer it went on, the sooner I thought it had to end.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The night had stretched out for so long that my eyes were beginning to close on their own. I just wanted to lie in my bed...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The last stretch would not be any easier on me. Soon, Ina would open, but there was no way I could walk there. The temperature inside the tower was regulated, and that was where I needed to be.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The same wait continued until {time=7} came. The time I'd spent could've been summarized in a blink, as each second had been identical.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When would something happen...!? I wanted to sleep and know where the Sekimeiya was. I just needed to step into the tower, but why was it not open already? I had hit the point of real, pressing fear.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't think straight. That small plaza was the only illuminated place I could see, and I had to be as close to the entrance as I could.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I looked up, but I couldn't see anything past the dark, monolithic slab of the building.{w} I hadn't moved in so long that turning my head was painful. I had to do it slowly, but I managed to see the stars.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Wait...{w} Am I crazy...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was the same starry sky. Just like everything below it, nothing had changed above.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...? This doesn't make any sense.{w} Where's...{w} the sun?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stared up with wide eyes. The dark sky looked just as it had when I'd left my apartment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, speechless, I looked back at my phone.{w} {time=7:04.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't understand... It's like the world has stopped moving.{w} No service... Why? Why does my phone have no service!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd witnessed the sun rising from behind the mountains countless times. But at that moment, no hint of light peeked out from over them. It was {time=7} already, so why was Yushibana still covered in darkness?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd felt that time might not have been passing since I'd leaned on that streetlight. Astonished, I forced myself to step forward and spun.{w} Nothing at all had changed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no meaning I could think of. After all, no matter how certain I felt, it was impossible that everything had just stopped. Inevitably, the sun would rise, obliterating the night.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But with each second that seemingly passed, the more I doubted any had. I'd spent what seemed like eons convinced the lights in the lobby would turn on at any moment, and they still hadn't.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What was I waiting for? The tower should've opened already. Without a doubt, the sun should've begun to rise already.{w} ...Waiting had become my only protest, but time staunchly refused to advance to the next day.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was nothing else I could do. I wanted to fall back into my bed and feel the warmth of my apartment, but my legs wouldn't be able to carry me far from that undefined plaza.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Two days before then, I'd also felt like the world had something wrong with it, but everything had solved itself in the end. Was the same thing happening again? How long had I waited then for normalcy to return?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no way I was in the wrong, like I'd thought the other day. Nobody was there; everything felt still, and it had even since I'd arrived. I was alone among nothingness. The light above me was a star, and everything for light years around was the void.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hugged my body even tighter. I'd been convinced the cold would end at some point, but it continued without end, eroding me. Would {time=9} be no different? I could no longer tell myself it was impossible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My eyes remained locked to the sky. I was terrified, desperately wishing that I was back in my room, but simultaneously overcome with curiosity. Both of those conflicting feelings locked me in place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It didn't make any sense. Where was the light, the people, or the real world? Traveling through time with the Sekimeiya, as insane as it had been, was at least clearly traveling through time. I had no idea what I was experiencing in front of the tower. It had no name, no concept.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had to go back home. Even though I felt almost unable to walk, I was only a few minutes away, and every second I waited slightly reduced the energy I had to go back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even so, I was hypnotized by that unchanging sky. Was there an explanation behind the state of the world, or was it another question without an answer?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Time was certainly advancing, but I couldn't make out even a hint of a white outline. The sun was nowhere to be seen—not the faintest trace of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If the world had frozen, would it ever unfreeze? If so, then the next question was whether I'd get to see that happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't believe my legs were still supporting my weight. There was nowhere to sit except the slick ground itself. Wanting to confirm how much time had passed, I painfully lowered my neck to look at my phone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {time=7:30.}..{w} "{tip=phone}No service{/tip}".{w} That time, I slowly moved my finger up to the call button.{w} It was freezing, but it still registered my touch. The moment I pressed it, I called my mother's number.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}A quiet, robotic voice came out of the speaker.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We couldn't connect to the line.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Immediately, a beep played, indicating that the call had been cut.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I entered something like a state of shock, unable to move the phone away from my ear. Something was very wrong—I could no longer believe anything else. The place I was at that moment was not the real world.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd gone back to looking at the sky. Where could I be if not in the real world? Was I in a dream after I'd finally fallen asleep on that soft carpet?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Usually, verifying that would've been very simple. However, as I could hardly feel my skin anymore, even after pinching my hand, I wasn't able to conclude it was reality.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No, it was reality. The minimal sensation had been enough to confirm that. When we'd been in the tower, I'd felt almost the same way regarding how dreamlike everything was. Was there, then, an explanation behind an unmoving world?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who could possibly interpret anything about that explanation if it existed in the first place? Hadn't I been the only person to notice it two days earlier? After all, it felt as if I was the root cause. The world wasn't permitting me to enter the next day even though it already should have started.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If that was it, was there anything I could do? There were precisely zero ideas that came to mind about what was happening to me or how I could resolve it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And there was no fleeing either. If abandoning the idea of going to the tower would advance everything to the next day, there was no solution.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I could still somewhat feel my hand. What was clear was that staying still was getting me nowhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Still gripping my phone, I took it out again. According to it, time had definitely been passing, as it showed {time=7:35.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Making sure I could still move my legs, I stepped closer to the building. Immediately, the bricks that formed the front wall became visible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The lobby looked as it had earlier, the tower just as unchanging as its surroundings. I stepped to the left, trying to make out the reception desk. Even though it was very dark, I was sure nobody was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had little to no force left in the motion, but I grabbed the handle again and tried to push.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It didn't budge at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya was close to me, somewhere behind that door. If the world had frozen in place, wasn't it the perfect opportunity to obtain it?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't sense a single living thing anywhere, so there was no need to devise a plan. I just had to find the Sekimeiya and hope that after using it, things would fix themselves.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So I continued stepping away from the door until no light remained in front of me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked forward, following the rough wall with my arm. It continued for a short while, but I soon lost it. When that happened, I turned to the right, and something cold hit my shins.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was grass, covered with snow that I shook off before it could stick to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, I put out my right hand and walked ahead, tracing the wall with my bare fingers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd gone around to the left side of the building, having considered the possibility of another way in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Going to the storeroom wasn't the only way to determine if that door really connected to the outside. ...It was completely dark, and the surface of the building was like a block of ice. However, if there was a door somewhere in it, I believed I could find it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Would I be able to open it if I did? It didn't sound likely, but there was a chance I could enter, and I no longer feared the possibility of someone seeing me through the cameras. Staying outside was far more intimidating.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I really was exhausted, and the tall grass made the path harder to get through. However, as it was fully dark, I had to be very attentive.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With my forefinger, I slowly traced a line through the wall, attempting to discern the thinnest gap that could've outlined a door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The cold surface was uneven and bumpy, so I rapidly lost all hope. If there was a door somewhere, I wouldn't find it so easily even if I could roughly tell where the storeroom was. As I walked, the fear of passing out began to grow inside me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Out of nowhere, the wall ended, and I found myself at the back of the tower. In front of me, I could no longer see the stars, as an invisibly dark mountain extended just ahead.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I turned around and felt the wall again with my left hand. Eyes closed, I started to retrace my steps, feeling an awful mix of negative emotions.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I suddenly stopped when I remembered something from the day we'd been inside that immense building.{w} If that door had really led to the wall I was at, there was a way I could find it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to forcefully press my hand against the wall. Naturally, nothing happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If a door was there, it must've been made or covered with the same bricks as everywhere else. However, when we'd been in the storeroom, we had shaken the door from the inside, and it had made a rattling sound.{w} ...If the other side was the wall, then shaking it from the outside would produce the same sound.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With no light bulbs around, all sound had disappeared, and during the winter, it was rare to hear insects at night. But the silence felt far too unnatural to be justified.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took one step forward and softly hit the wall with a fist. All it produced was an instant, dry noise, and no part of the wall moved in the slightest.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I recalled the width of the door and that I was definitely close to the storeroom. After the next step, I repeated the same tired motion, and the result was identical.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, I stepped again and hit the wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was that it...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The sound had been different. To confirm it, I hit the same spot, trying to apply a bit more strength I wasn't sure I had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The sound I heard was different.{w} Speechless, I extended my arm to the wall and pushed. When I did, I felt it move.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...? Did I open it?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Bridge

After so long, that was what made my heart speed up. I felt the edges and confirmed the outline of a door.{w} Akaro had been right after all. That door in the storeroom was the only thing blocking our way out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I'd gotten it to open easily just by pushing it. However, it had opened inwardly, which was why we hadn't been able to do it in the storeroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped toward the door. I couldn't see a thing, but when I felt the inner walls, I immediately identified them: I was back in the storeroom on the tower's crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I couldn't move. The fear of someone being in the security room resurfaced. If I walked forward and got caught, that was the end of everything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The door was covered by bricks, and its gaps were incredibly thin. When I felt it from the inside, I noticed something very important.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh... There's no handle. It was already gone that morning.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: More importantly, that meant that if I closed the door, I wouldn't be able to open it from the inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked deeper into the narrow entrance, leaving it open. There hadn't been much wind outside, so I didn't think it would close on its own.{w} Immediately, I hit another wall. It was what concealed the area I was in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was in its regular position, separating both sides of the storeroom. I put my hand on it and felt it around the right edge, where the opening mechanism was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: From that side, the little aperture was noticeable to the touch. When I dragged the wall open, however, I couldn't see any difference, as there was no light beyond it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took another cautious step and felt a soft texture. I really was in the storeroom. What I was making contact with was the damaged couch we'd seen next to the wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't see anything, but I knew the door to hallway A was in front of me. ...Was it open or closed? While I couldn't know that, what I did know was that the lights were off on the other side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no camera in the storeroom, but as soon as I opened the next door, I would be recorded. ...The question was whether the security room was vacant or not.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I didn't know what to do. Of course, there had to be someone in the security room, but there simultaneously couldn't be—the world had frozen.{w} What would happen if I was seen? I couldn't claim to have randomly found the hidden door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But the chance I had was perfect. The tower seemed lifeless, so I could find the Sekimeiya and leave. ...If it was true that nobody was there, I could even set off the alarm and let the Sekimeiya store time for twelve hours, as there wouldn't be anyone in the security room to complete the deactivation process.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Ultimately, I reached my arm toward the door. The day would evidently never begin, so between attempting to walk back home and trying to obtain the Sekimeiya, the decision had already been made.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I felt a metallic knob and turned it. Once more, after opening a door, the darkness persisted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't see hallway A, but I knew I was there. I was immediately certain that I wasn't in a dream due to my senses.{w} It was the smell. The same strange smell that had characterized the building on that long day tinged the air again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I knew it wasn't the scent of the building itself. On the evening of the 15th, I'd identified the real source.{w} The Sekimeiya. When we'd been close to it, the smell had strengthened, and when we'd been farther from it, it had always been weaker.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I'd thought, the Sekimeiya had to be there, somewhere in the building. ...And going off the intensity, it was close.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't taken another step into the hallway, but I'd been there for some seconds and nothing had occurred. Then, I realized that my impression had been incorrect. After opening the door, there had been a subtle change I'd taken a bit to notice.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A tiny green light could be seen high up, slowly flickering. It belonged to a security camera.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We'd never learned the true meaning behind those lights. Did they indicate that I was being recorded or something else? Was my figure being displayed in the security room?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everything was cold and still. The only remaining movement was from that inanimate light.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The security room had to be soulless, but I couldn't believe it. Even though that belief was close to proven, I couldn't accept it. Slowly, I began to take silent steps toward the metallic door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: An occurrence from the 15th was repeating. In just the short time I'd been there, the smell had blended in, becoming harder and harder to notice despite its prior strength.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The first time we noticed this smell, wasn't Katei confused about it too? ...But if it came from the Sekimeiya, he should've smelled it during the previous two weeks...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I hit the wall at my side, failing to walk in a straight line. Carefully, I continued to move until I felt a doorknob.{w} It was the security room's, so I gently gripped it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had to see it with my own eyes. Was nobody on the other side? It couldn't be. Ashiya had been anticipating Xyn's attack, so why would nobody be stationed at the cameras?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I knew the room would be empty because I hadn't been seen. When I slowly opened the door, nothing but darkness waited for me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was nobody inside. I knew there were many monitors in front of me, but none of them were on.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was unbelievable. Why had all life vanished from the world? Why had all the surrounding lights gone dark when electricity still flowed?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked into the room as I recognized a red light near the floor, doubting whether the button it belonged to still functioned.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I reached out and felt around in front of me. When I touched the chair, I moved it aside and crouched next to the light.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I pressed the button softly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A whirring sound came from my side. Following it, one of the screens turned on.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The computer had powered on, and a single monitor displayed a loading bar. At last, I could see the dim walls around me, the blue light projecting onto them. Without a doubt, I was the only person there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Soon, the bar filled and was replaced by an authentication screen. I remembered that Katei had entered a long ID and password, so there was no chance I could access it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd confirmed I was alone, as ridiculous as it seemed. I was about to walk out when the messiness of the room caught my attention.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The objects on the desk were scattered around, and almost all the drawers were partially open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What had happened? On the 15th, when we'd stepped inside for the first time, the room had looked considerably different.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Had someone tried to find something? ...I began to feel uneasy.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh... {w}This is...!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Glancing at the many open drawers, I saw something next to a pile of files.{w} I pulled the heavy compartment open and tried to reach the bottom with a finger.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...A brown key, large and rusty. After putting it in front of the light, I confirmed it was the one I suspected.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's the key we found on the floor of hallway A... We later thought it could've been for the storeroom door.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And... it was in the security room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There'd been a few reasons to think that the person who dropped the key was one of the culprits behind the attack.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And at that moment, when it was essential for the cameras to be monitored, nobody was in the security room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was there a reason after all? ...Could the frozen world have merely been an illusion?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There were many things that made me uneasy, so I walked to the door. My breathing had begun to accelerate.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The key was still in my hand. It was potentially an essential part of the culprit's plan, so I took it with me, accepting that the past could change. If there was no copy of it, it wouldn't be found in hallway A anymore, and the entire attack could fail depending on its importance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I felt around the lobby door until I found its knob.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could see a red light by the reception desk, but it wasn't enough to illuminate the lobby, even with the streetlights shining faintly from beyond the glass.{w} I questioned it again. Why was the entire floor dark when I'd been able to turn on the computer?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: From the inside, the exterior door wasn't fully transparent, but it was enough to see that the sun hadn't risen yet. It seemed entirely futile to think about that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But if there really was a reason behind it, the mirrored stillness of the tower had the same cause. I could attempt to grasp it from that angle.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Disoriented, I walked across the smooth floor with my arm out. Where was the Sekimeiya? If Ashiya's intent was to make Xyn break open the cabinet, it couldn't be well-hidden.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was a room below me. There'd been nothing in the storeroom, so the mechanical room was a rational place to store the cabinet.{w} But more importantly, I knew that the light breakers were there. There were no switches on the walls, so if the breakers were on, I would have no idea why the tower was still dark.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I followed the surface of the desk around. There, I searched across the wall until I'd taken hold of a door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A tenebrous staircase led down from the other side of that door. I descended it, carefully placing each of my steps.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It wasn't as narrow as I recalled. The cabinet would have fit if brought down. After I made the sharp turn below, I felt the following door, which I accidentally opened with my knee.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The bulb was no longer emitting any light, but the difference was minimal. I knew the space was filled with furniture, so I gingerly stepped to the wall with the circuit breakers.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hit the plastic panel with my arm. Naturally, I couldn't see the state of the switches, so I hoped what I had at hand would be enough.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took out my phone and placed its screen in front of the panel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The breakers were right behind it, so the faint light was enough to let me see the direction they were pointing to. I slowly panned the phone across the plastic surface, taking a look at all of them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They were all pointing up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...So, like with the sun, there was no reason behind the lack of light within the tower. It didn't make any sense, but I put my phone away and reached my arm back up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When my phone had hit the plastic, I'd heard a metallic sound. As the ceiling was very low, I had no problem reaching the top of the panel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Uh...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Two cold objects were there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I grabbed them with two fingers and opened my palm. Even though I couldn't see anything, I could identify their shape.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took my phone back out and directed its light at what I was holding.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {tip=keys}Two more keys{/tip}.{w} Once they were illuminated, I recognized them as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait... This is the attic's.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But that wasn't all, because the other one was unmistakably the Sekimeiya cabinet's.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I... just have to find the cabinet, then...! I can just unlock it. I don't have to break it open.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Why the hell had those keys been there? Both of them were supposed to have few or no replicas and be carefully protected.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nothing made any sense. How many mysteries layered around the Sekimeiya? ...I began to question what to do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I have to hurry and find the cabinet, but then what? Should I try to trigger the alarm or just silently unlock it and take the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd been recorded by cameras, so even though I had the cabinet key, shutting down the tower sounded like a fine idea. However, anyone who knew about the secret door could enter at any point.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If the rusty key is really for that door, I could try to lock it from the inside...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I tried to move, but the obstacles in the room didn't make it easy. Could the cabinet have been there? While it seemed like a good place, neither the lobby nor the mechanical room had cameras.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There were chairs and tables on the floor, so I had to move some aside to get to every part of the room. Even though it was impossible for anyone to be there, I kept trying to be silent and failing as I scattered things that I couldn't see.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After a while, I knew the cabinet wasn't there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had no idea if I needed to hurry or not, so I went up the staircase without wasting any more time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped back into the lobby. ...Where would the Sekimeiya have been? There were a couple of places I knew to prioritize over the others.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked to hallway B, hitting the hard column with my shoulder.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The green lights on the cameras were still there, but my legs moved automatically, recalling the steps needed to reach the place called the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was it set up as it had been the 15th? Finding out would be simple, and if the cabinet wasn't there, my last idea was the room in front of it, B4, where the cabinets with temperature regulation were.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After I'd taken a few steps, I turned around.{w} Through the door, I was peering back into the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: My heart sped up all by itself while I scrambled to understand why my line of sight was completely black.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could see nothing but darkness, and that didn't make any sense...{w} Because from there, I should've been able to see the lights of the reception desk.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What... happened?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I closed and opened my eyes a few times, wondering if I was the problem.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There it was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Stunned, I stared at it. I hadn't moved at all, so I didn't understand. I really wanted to doubt my eyes, but the light had suddenly come back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And even though I could see it beyond the door, my heart hadn't slowed down. It was the same sensation as when I'd turned around while being tailed in the snow.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was only silence.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I backed away slowly without taking my eyes off the light.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And eventually, the wall covered it as I kept approaching the door at my right.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I found the doorknob and opened the way to the bridge between the hallways.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was... cold.{w} As soon as I took a step in, I perceived a decrease in temperature.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What is this...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't believe I was able to feel any colder. However, after opening that door, the change had been instant.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I approached the place where the cabinet had been, the temperature continued to decrease.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It is here.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: In the middle of the wall, I felt the cold touch of a curtain. I raised it as fast as I could, forcing my hand into a claw grip.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And when it was out of the way, I didn't have to wonder what was behind it. There was a faint glow, making the crimson texture beneath it visible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't believe it. The Sekimeiya was there, but what had happened in that place? With my free hand, I reached in to verify if the cabinet was open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I'd thought, the glass wasn't properly closed. That was why the entire room felt chilly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had to decide what to do, but I couldn't think straight. ...I had the Sekimeiya at hand—I didn't even need the key that I'd found.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I felt the glass with my hand. The gap wasn't big enough to get it through, so I tried to scroll it farther down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...I couldn't move it. It seemed to be stuck in place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why is it not opening...? It can't be locked.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I kept applying force and noticed that it was moving a little. Before I could reach the Sekimeiya, though, I let go of the glass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's that...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stared at the cushion around the Sekimeiya. My first impression had been mistaken, as it wasn't just crimson.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is that... white?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It appeared to be stained by a substance, but I couldn't tell what it was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Frowning, I kept trying to push open the glass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Is it cracked?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The surface felt rough, as if it had been damaged.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A loud noise invaded my ears right as I got the glass unstuck.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is that the alarm...!? Why!?{w} Did I just break it!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd never heard that sound, but it had to be the same one that played when we were trapped.{w} I started to lose control of my nerves. What was happening? I'd triggered it after doing something to the cabinet, and I couldn't see what.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood still, praying for the sound to disappear. I was being locked in, but nobody was in the security room, and I'd left the storeroom door open.{w} As I stood, I perceived a fainter and rougher sound coming from the lobby. It was the shutter, closing automatically.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The silence came back, but I still couldn't get it together.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Of course, the past had changed—the alarm had been activated before the 15th. ...But why?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I looked at the Sekimeiya, still faintly glowing. I should've had enough time to escape with it, and I didn't know if the world would return to normal on its own.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I put my hand through the opening and immediately stopped.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It didn't make any sense, but I was too exhausted to react. The inside of the cabinet, which I expected to be the coldest part of the room, was hot. In fact, as I got closer to the Sekimeiya, I felt a hot aura reminiscent of the one in the water tank.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait...!{w} Does this mean that I can travel really far back again?{w} Why, though...!? The cabinet shouldn't allow it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I raised my hand and felt the freezing air that the cabinet was releasing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I touched the white stain on the cushion and knew I hadn't been mistaken; something was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was considerably hot, and it felt as if something had dried on the cloth. As I moved my hand around it, I noticed it was in abundance, whatever it was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What was it...? I couldn't tell, but there were also tiny pieces with a rocky texture scattered across the cushion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My fingers felt something different and tried to grab it. It was larger than the strange substance above it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell is this...?{w} A card?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Its texture and form resembled one, but it was pretty small. I took it out of the cabinet and felt its hot touch, painfully confused.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was stained like the cushion, but I couldn't tell what it was. ...I grabbed my phone and shined its faint light on the object.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Just like I'd thought, it was a very tiny card. On it, a single word was written.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {tip=card}XYN{/tip}.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A chill ran down my spine. They had been there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But why...? They shouldn't have attacked until the 15th. Was it as I'd feared? Had one of the members traveled from the 15th, changing history with an early attack?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stared at the Sekimeiya... Most importantly, why was it still there if Xyn had already attacked?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had so many questions and no faith that any would be answered. I began to move my hand toward the glow inside the cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The searing air around it was all I could be sure of. It was ridiculously hot, completely overpowering the cabinet's icy interior. My frozen hand penetrated the barrier of hot air—the temperature was all I needed to know the Sekimeiya's energy was comparable to when it had been in the water tank.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Would touching it bring back life to the world? From the 15th, I'd gone fifteen days back. It didn't matter that I'd have nowhere to stay; I would have time to work all those matters out. I just had to go back in time and root out the problem by obtaining the Sekimeiya before anyone else did.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My hand, cold as it was, began to burn painfully. I was so close to the Sekimeiya and to leaving behind yet another reality.{w} I shut my eyes, mustering up the will to move my hand farther. I expected that by the next time I opened them, my surroundings would have morphed entirely.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: River
The light... had come back. But I was in the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where is this...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I turned around slowly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A-Atsuki...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: H—{w} You...!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We both looked shocked to see each other. At that time, I saw the shutter and the powered-off lights. Those were the effects of the alarm.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A-Are you Shiroya...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What? Y-Yes. Where are we? I just appeared here.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I couldn't believe it was him. I'd thought seeing him again wasn't possible. However, the look he gave me seemed full of suspicion. His eyes were piercing mine, and he appeared wary.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I felt my body and noticed my heart skip a beat. I was wearing different clothes, ones I'd washed the day before.{w} As soon as the world had unfrozen, so had I. I could move my hand without it cramping, as if the time I'd spent outside had been erased. ...And when I did, I realized I wasn't tired anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: W-Wait, that...
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I followed his eyes toward the hallway B door. When I gave it a closer look, I saw the crucial detail I'd missed.{w} Its edges were dark. I'd seen it before, so I didn't have to wonder what it meant.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It's the smoke, right?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Y-Yes, but doesn't it look different?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I'm not sure where we are. I just appeared here too.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: As he said that, he approached the door. Unlike mine, his clothes were the ones he'd worn on the 15th, but they were clean.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A sound that came from hallway B made Atsuki stop.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A door had closed. He went still, trying to stay silent, and I did the same.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A few seconds later, he kept going and grabbed the knob. When he opened the door, I couldn't believe what I saw.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, fuck. Don't breathe.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Wh-What...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: No light filled the hallway; only a dark fog did. Without a doubt, it was the same smoke that had knocked us out, although its density seemed much lower.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Right next to us were three people on the floor: Erina, Isla, and Sai, who had all just lost consciousness.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A-Are we on the morning of the 15th?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: After staring at the scene with perplexity, Atsuki's face slowly turned to me, and he spoke in a quiet voice.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Are you really Shiroya? The real one?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What does that mean...!? Who else would I be?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...What do you remember? Please, tell me everything.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What!? I-I don't know what you mean! We got trapped here, and a bunch of things happened!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: What happened? How did you end up here?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: H-Huh? A lot of things! Do you remember everything? Late into the day, we were in the lobby, and I went to the bathroom. There, I activated the Sekimeiya and appeared on the 30th of November, below that gem shop.{w} Then... a few days later, I entered the tower and touched the Sekimeiya. That's how I just appeared here.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: That was why... the image my brain was receiving didn't make any sense. How could it be real? How could that have been the start of December 15th?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: W-Wait, that's all...? What about appearing after you'd gone to the bathroom? Do you remember that?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What? N-No...? I found the Sekimeiya in the toilet's water tank and went a long way into the past.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...{w}Are you really... the real Shiroya? I don't really understand what you're telling me.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I didn't either. Had he just appeared there at the same time as me? Didn't that mean that he'd been encompassed by the range of my travel?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait a second. That sound from before was a door, right? It sounded like it came from the right wall.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I think so.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: It had to be that one, then.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He pointed at one of the doors, and I understood why he'd said that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's where Naomi died and where I traveled for the first time. If the smoke was just released, someone might have just been there because it's where the temperature regulation cabinets are.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...{w}I didn't know what to say, but he was the Atsuki I'd been with that day. How was I talking to him? Hadn't his existence been overwritten...?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I think we just heard the culprit. I have no idea why we're here, but only a few people should be conscious at this time.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He gestured at me to follow him and not breathe. Before I could react, he was dashing toward that door, so I did the same, covering my face with an arm.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While I still trailed behind, he looked at me and seemed to frown. However, he ended up going through the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The crystal room was empty, and every cabinet had its curtain neatly in place. If the sound had come from there, someone had just left.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki closed the door carefully so that his voice wouldn't be heard.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you see the door to the lobby?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...What about it?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: We just left it open.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh. Does that matter?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: You remember, right? When we met everyone else, Sai pointed out that it was open, and Katei said he did that. I'm pretty sure it looked exactly the way we just left it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I see what you mean, but please answer one thing for me. Why are we here? Did something happen after I traveled to the past?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He looked down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are you telling me the truth? Do you not know what happened after?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I don't...! I just told you. I appeared on the 30th of November.{w} I stayed at my apartment while my past self was in the hospital, and a few days later, I entered the tower.{w} I have no idea what happened there, though. The Sekimeiya was already in the cabinet, and I touched it since nobody was in the security room. After that, I appeared in the lobby with you. Now we're here.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: As soon as he took what I was saying as sincere, his way of looking at me changed entirely. I finally felt like the person in front of me was the Atsuki I'd wanted to be back with.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, you said you traveled to the 30th? Did you try to save Miiya?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I couldn't... I appeared too late for that, but I did change the past—
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I had to cut that sentence short. The past had changed, hadn't it? If that was the case, how could the same incident have been starting again? How was it possible we'd left the lobby door open exactly like we'd seen it in that morning, and how could Atsuki have possessed the memories of that long day? How the hell was I back there...!?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm trying to understand what you've said...
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Don't worry, even I don't understand anything of what I lived through. I'm not lying, though.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...Then I'm not sure it would help if I told you what happened after you left.{w} Another version of you was there, but it wasn't you, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: N-No. I have no idea who that was.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Well, we weren't able to leave when the time came. I'm not sure what happened, why, or how, but the lights went off, and we couldn't get out.{w} ...You remember the recording, right?{w} It was real.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Wait, what...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yes, it did happen. It wasn't a trick.{w} It still doesn't make any sense, though. I can't wrap my head around what happened.{w} You said that you touched the Sekimeiya in the event room days before the 15th, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Y-Yes.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I see. What the fuck, then...? I don't get anything.{w} I thought I got caught up in your travel and both of us appeared in front of the hallway B door, the location where we were on the morning of the 15th.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: But that makes no sense...! And look at my clothes, I wasn't wearing these on the 15th!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Only my purse and coat matched what I'd worn on that day.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're right, actually. Were you wearing them when you touched the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I shook my head and followed Atsuki's line of sight as soon as I saw he'd noticed something. We approached one of the cabinets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...That's where the Sekimeiya was, right?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yes, and look at the wheel.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It said 0 °C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's set to be cold... Oh, and it's not damaged yet. Wasn't this the one with a crack?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yes... it was.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I stared while Atsuki peeked behind the cabinet to unlock it. He raised it alongside the curtain, and I stepped beside him to look inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What?{w} I...{w=0.4} don't get it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The Sekimeiya. It was there, emitting a bright white in the middle of the empty cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Someone left it in here.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yes, which is what I don't get. When we woke up, it was in the event room, still in its cabinet.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: You're... right.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Seemingly overwhelmed, Atsuki covered his hand with his sleeve and brought the Sekimeiya out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's set to 0 °C, but the cabinet isn't cold at all.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It could've been set just now, so it didn't have enough time to cool off.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: God, the Sekimeiya is burning, though...!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: As soon as I heard that, I extended my arm, startling Atsuki. I shook my head—I didn't want to make contact. I only wanted to feel the air around it.
entries.speaker: i
