entries.text: Sorry, when I touched it in the bathroom, its surroundings were incredibly hot. ...I can feel the heat, but it's nothing like then.{w} Do you know more about how the Sekimeiya works?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I know nothing, and even less with what you've told me.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It's working, so if we're really at the start of the incident, wouldn't touching it put us outside?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: M-Maybe. That's what I was thinking. It should be hot enough for that.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The real state of the world was unknown. I had no idea where we were or what was beyond the walls of the tower. However, if touching the Sekimeiya would send us far enough to escape it, it would guarantee the real Atsuki would still exist even if I couldn't comprehend his return.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's touch it.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Atsuki nodded and moved closer while I stared at the Sekimeiya, wishing I was moments away from never seeing it again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When his hand touched it, the Sekimeiya disappeared.{w} That was all I'd wanted. However, nothing else did.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Huh?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We were in the same crystal room. We hadn't even moved. Speechless, I stared at his hands and the floor in search of the stone that had vanished.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Th-This is what happened before. It teleported, and we didn't travel.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: That had escaped my mind a long time ago. ...The Sekimeiya's teleportation.{w} What caused it...!? Would it sometimes reject a travel? If so, why had it happened then...!?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, n-no... I-It can't be that.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: That time, it was Atsuki who followed my petrified eyes. As soon as he took a glance at the cabinet, he almost fell from the shock.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What the fuck...? It didn't fall, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I shook my head.{w} The lid that Atsuki had just opened... The instant the Sekimeiya disappeared, it had closed without producing a sound. And that wasn't all. Over it, the velvet curtain covered it perfectly, making the cabinet look like every other one in the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did we actually travel through time? ...Are we at a point before I opened it?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: A distinct sound entered our ears, and we turned to the door. ...Someone was running through the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Could he have been right? As we ran to the door, I wondered. ...Were the walls of the hallway bright and elegant or dark and dirty? At the same time, we gripped the knob and burst through the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Immediately, we were forced to cover our faces. It didn't make any sense, but the smoke was still there. The sound of footsteps at least couldn't have been a mistake, so after our initial surprise, we looked both ways.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...We couldn't see anyone, but the sound hadn't faded away. It seemed they'd run to hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki tugged my sleeve, telling me to follow. It was likely the culprit was there—the one who'd just left the Sekimeiya behind. But I hesitated a bit, frowning as I kept staring at the lobby side. Were my eyes playing tricks on me?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Covering our faces, we chased behind the sound. Very little smoke remained, so it was easy to avoid breathing it until we got to the clean hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The footsteps were quickly dissipating in the distance. We looked at each other to verify that we'd both heard them going up the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We bolted to them and were met with the gray door, fully open. Early on the 15th, Katei had acted surprised to see it unlocked, but where was he at that moment if not running up the floors?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We stepped onto the second floor. It was a scene I'd thought I wouldn't see again, causing my face to unconsciously screw up in disgust.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't believe I was circling those floors once more, but as I did, my mind went back to the door to the lobby. After leaving the crystal room, it had looked more open than before.{w} That was strange, because as Atsuki said, the way we'd left it was just like how it was that morning, before Sai opened it all the way.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, the most important detail was higher up, above the three sleeping bodies. I hadn't been able to give it a good look, but the camera's lens had seemed to reflect the light of the crystal room.{w} Then, I'd looked at the other lenses and thought that they more clearly had smoke on them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As we sprinted as fast as we could, I was amazed by the energy I had. Before touching the Sekimeiya, I'd had difficulty even staying steady.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had no idea who we were following, but Naomi and Katei were the likely choices. Why were they running up? It had all happened at once after we'd touched the disappearing Sekimeiya. What the hell was that about?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki once told me he'd seen it teleport to its cabinet. That seemed to resolve the doubt from earlier—it had just teleported to the event room, which was why it was there when we woke up.{w} The important question was what else the disappearance implied. The cabinet's reversion to its previous state revealed a secondary effect.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After a while, the mesh of footsteps began to sound distorted. We were on the third floor, and I tried to sharpen my hearing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What exactly was I hearing? The footsteps ahead, mine, and Atsuki's.{w} Why did it sound as if there were more?{w} The echo could've been messing with me, but it seemed as if another pair of footsteps was running just behind us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We hadn't let out a single word since leaving the crystal floor. When we stepped on the sixth, a sound dominated the air.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As we'd feared, only one door could've closed, found on the other side of the floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We didn't slow down until the attic's entrance was in front of us. Panting, Atsuki grabbed the doorknob, but he couldn't get it to open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Damn it...!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It was locked. As we stared in defeat, I realized nobody was trying to catch up to us, so I took the time to sort out my thoughts.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I suddenly remembered something and looked at my waist. My purse was still there, so I unzipped it and looked inside. Immediately, I took something out and showed it to Atsuki.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...!? Why do you have it!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I... don't know... I found it when I entered the tower, in the mechanical room. I found the rusty key in a drawer in the security room as well, but... how is it possible I still have them when my clothes completely changed?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: It didn't make any sense, but I could open the attic. I inserted the key into the keyhole without wasting any more time.{w} When it unlocked, I slowly pushed the door open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The dim staircase extended beyond us. Instead of rushing up, we stepped forward silently, as the person we'd been chasing couldn't know that we had a key, and the elevator had been disabled by the alarm.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At the front, I began to ascend the stairs, the light of the living room slowly creeping in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The next door was open. As I reached the top, I extended my neck past it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, I saw who was there.{w} Naomi.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Her back was facing me, as she was staring at an open black suitcase on the sofa.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I turned around to let Atsuki know.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was confused. It was considerably dark, but I couldn't even make out his figure.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Are you here?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I whispered in the quietest voice I could muster, but I received no response.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Puzzled, I slowly went down the steps, careful not to hit him. However, by the time I reached the door, I hadn't sensed him yet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sunken Vessel
What...? Did he leave!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I gripped the doorknob and pushed on the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}It didn't make any sense. It was ridiculous to think that it could. However, the door was locked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't even try to think it over. With the key in my hand, I unlocked the door and opened it all the way.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The vast corridor was vacant.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A-Atsuki...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: My whisper didn't reach anyone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did he leave...? There's no way. He couldn't have locked the door.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't hear anything above the stairs, but Naomi was there. I knew Atsuki hadn't stepped ahead of me, though.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What had just happened...? I hadn't heard anything, but someone locked the door. ...With my guard up, I walked to the corridor with the offices.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It didn't feel like anyone was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't have missed the sound of the door locking. I would've also heard Atsuki's movements, and he wouldn't have suddenly left me...!
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was unbelievable. That was an Atsuki who couldn't exist anymore, but he'd been there!
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kept circling the floor, carefully scanning it.{w} He couldn't have faded out of existence just like that—the door proved something else had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi was in the attic. I'd seen a black suitcase in front of her, which had to be the one we found the first time we entered that place...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went down the stairs, wanting to believe Atsuki was still somewhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Could it have been due to the Sekimeiya, which had disappeared from our sight? If he had somehow traveled through time, I wanted to believe he was nearby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was the morning of the 15th. ...Why? How had I ended up back on that day?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Those events should've been erased completely, so why were they repeating?{w} ...Maybe it didn't matter if I really had returned to my world. I would soon learn if everything I'd experienced would happen again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It really wouldn't make any sense if it did. The smoke had just been released. It appeared Naomi hadn't suffered from the effects of the smoke and escaped to the attic with a suitcase.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Could that long day actually happen again? Not only was I there, but so was an Atsuki who'd experienced it too. ...How many times had we searched the whole building? It was impossible I could avoid being spotted by all those searches.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The events that followed would soon diverge from what I knew. The past would be changed, which was something that should have already happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Who had returned the world to that state? What had the Sekimeiya really been doing to us? As I proceeded down the floors, I simply wished to reunite with the Atsuki I'd been separated from twice.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Wait!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I quickly rifled through my pockets, but they were empty. Then, I stared at my purse in disbelief.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Why isn't my phone here?{w} Why...? I had it when I touched the Sekimeiya, and the keys that I found in the mechanical room are still here with the one for my apartment. Why the hell is only my phone gone!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was laughable, as if we were being toyed with. My phone, which I needed the most, was the sole item in my purse that hadn't appeared with me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But of course, there was another major difference: my clothes. Aside from my coat, they weren't the ones I'd been wearing when I touched the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, that's not right. Not all the keys are here.{w} I have the attic's and the rusty key, but not the cabinet's. Why? Why didn't that one travel with me!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was the only one missing, but why? What the hell was different about it!?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I returned to the crystal floor, searching for the Atsuki I'd just been talking to. Both of us had been disconcerted to be back there, and I couldn't stomach the thought of reliving the same twelve hours.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was the Sekimeiya a sentient being deciding our fate? It almost seemed malicious, but I had to use it to finally break free. I knew plenty of days could be traveled at a time, so we just had to touch it. But when we'd tried that, our travel had failed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What was the reason, then? Why were we forced to stay? Part of me wanted to know the answers to such heavy questions, and part of me wanted to have never even known they existed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped down. The walls ahead looked different than they had minutes prior, as the smoke had rapidly dried up on them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, the suitcase isn't here...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I hadn't noticed that when we'd run up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was the beginning of the incident. There were probably next to no people who were conscious, but it was possible someone had faked being knocked out. As I silently walked to hallway B, I couldn't help but wonder what I'd witness.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They're already up.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I hid myself as well as I could, staring at the dark end of the hallway. I could see Erina and Sai checking up on Isla, who was still unconscious.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The three of us should definitely be in the event room, then.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But there was no trace of the Atsuki I'd just been with, and I had no idea what could've happened to him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The camera...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was very hard to see from so far away, but it wasn't reflecting anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did I imagine the lens being clean?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And strangely, behind the three of them, the door to the lobby looked just like it had right before we'd run up. Had it actually moved since Atsuki and I had gone through it? I hadn't the faintest idea. Questioning reality and myself had become roughly equivalent concepts.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...If Atsuki's still here, both of us will try to stay away from the group, so we should find each other quickly.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Was he there, though? ...Or had he disappeared entirely? I couldn't tell which option the locked attic door pointed to.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was nothing I could do. I had no idea if the Sekimeiya had teleported to its cabinet, and I couldn't leave through the storeroom. Still unable to believe the sight of those dark walls, I stared from a distance, waiting for the imminent, unending day to begin.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I heard a door opening and saw three people slowly emerging from the event room. They were Atsuki, Akaro, and myself, stained by the dry substance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Speechless, I saw my old self slowly walking to the others, facing the dark floor. Once they all saw each other, they began to speak.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Their voices were too quiet to understand, but I knew what they were saying. I really was at the start of that day.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But wait.{w} Where's Katei...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There was no tall figure in a uniform next to them. ...When we'd left the event room for the first time, he'd already been there with the other group.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I verified that I wasn't mistaken. Katei was nowhere to be seen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then... this isn't the start of the day we know. Everything is bound to differ.{w} ...Could Katei have seen me here, which made him hesitant to show himself?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Just what had happened to the world...!? Where exactly was I, and how had I ended up there!? Failing to know such fundamentals made my head spin.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, everything will be different. It's gotta be because I'm here, and the first time I wasn't. None of what happened is guaranteed to repeat.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Atsuki I'd just been with couldn't exist anymore, but he couldn't have disappeared because of something I'd done! After all, I would've vanished with him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I really wanted to find him again and get out. I'd tried to internalize that I'd never talk to him again, but I'd evidently failed, as I could feel relief while the people near the entrance met each other for the first time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: For some reason, I had seen him again, and he had to still be somewhere. It was possible to break free with him, something that seemed impossible for the longest time. We were not in our original world, so even though we'd be stuck with different versions of ourselves, that really didn't matter.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't tell what they were talking about, but they would soon search the whole building. That meant I would eventually be discovered.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked at my clothes. What the hell would I say if I was found? They'd immediately notice I wasn't the same person—I had less smoke on me, and my clothes were different.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd had a fairly absurd thought.{w} "I can enter the attic, so what if I put on the clothes from up there and make up an excuse like being too cold or that my clothes were itchy due to the smoke?"
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Of course, that brought my mind to the self of mine Atsuki had once seen. According to him, she had been wearing clothes from the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...This wouldn't make any sense.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'm not in that reality anymore. The person Atsuki saw can't be me. ...It's impossible.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had no idea how the universe worked. Was it remotely possible for me to go back to that world? It shouldn't have been, but if I could, I wanted to finish that circle.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once, I'd willingly abandoned that reality, but I had slowly learned that it was a mistake. What I still had there was not something I could leave behind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Didn't it work like this a few times on the 15th...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If I go to the attic and put on clothes from the wardrobe, what would the reason be? To hope I'll end up in that reality again, where a version of me with those clothes existed? ...Doesn't that not make sense? Like Atsuki and I talked about, it's an event with no origin, a paradox.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But the reason I just thought about changing my clothes was to conceal myself as part of this reality, not just to complete a loop where it already happened. Would I have thought of this even if I didn't know about the version of me Atsuki saw?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Naomi was just in the attic. On the 15th, we found two dead versions of her, but that doesn't have to repeat. My original world should be long gone...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But right now, I'm not there, and I can get the clothes that me was wearing. ...If they lead me back to that reality, it would explain why we still found them in the attic when we ran up. They had never been taken out.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The elevator was supposedly disabled, so I started going up on foot.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The attic door was still unlocked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was me who unlocked it. On the 15th, we couldn't get it to open when we came across it because Naomi had shut herself inside.{w} ...Since it hasn't been locked again, she must not have left yet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I slowly ascended the steps, unsure what to think of Naomi.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was she behind the attack? ...Someone would soon try to kill her, but what was their motive?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could see the light of the living room through the slightly open door. When I went still, the attic felt completely soulless.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I finally took a glance at the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I couldn't see anyone, so I had to step a little closer. When I did, it made no difference.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi wasn't there anymore. Just a few minutes ago, she had been standing on the carpet, looking at the suitcase, which had remained open on the soft cushion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Were my eyes deceiving me? ...Perplexed, I stepped onto the carpet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I recalled the first time I'd set foot inside. Back then, an identical suitcase had been on that couch, but it was empty. That wasn't the case at the moment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was not only one Sekimeiya in it, but a second. One of them was gray, and the other shined faintly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I was staring at them, the disabled one became white.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why...? Why are there two?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I hovered my hand over the one on the right. It was hard to notice, but I definitely felt a warm aura. I could touch it and travel right there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't fathom the sight. Why was there another Sekimeiya next to it?{w} I knew from what Atsuki told me that two had existed at one point...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...And it appeared they had since the very start. How had a second one come to exist? I only knew that just before I'd entered the room, one of them had been activated.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi must've touched it, and she appeared somewhere else.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I looked down at the carpeted floor. Naomi's footprints ended exactly where I was. However, I couldn't help but feel something was wrong.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isn't this... the opposite of what we saw?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When we all entered the attic, her footprints began at the suitcase.{w} Now, they end at it, and I already mixed mine with hers.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I forced myself to drop it. No matter why, two Sekimeiya were in front of me. I nervously stared at them, knowing Naomi could be anywhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: One of them was supposed to be on the crystal floor, and duplicating it had never sounded possible. However, it was very evident its powers went far beyond the mere time travel we'd once learned about.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Would they let me travel, or would that be denied again? I faltered, desperately trying to make up my mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why had Atsuki suddenly disappeared...!? He had to still exist...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wasn't in our reality, but was it really possible to return to it...? If I traveled to the past right then, even outside of the tower, that Atsuki would likely not be there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The world is being constantly changed, and not only by me. To be back together outside, we'd need to travel to the past at the same time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It made me want to tear my hair out. Was there really a reason why I was at the beginning of the incident? ...Would I be sent back to my reality if I merely followed some sort of destiny?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: These two Sekimeiya... This could be good.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The existence of an extra one isn't known, and Naomi just traveled somewhere thinking she left the attic locked. I can hide one of them, and the group won't be aware of the one I have even if they enter the attic.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After that, I just have to find Atsuki and bring him to the Sekimeiya that'll a lot of energy. That's how we'll be able to leave.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Who knew about that second Sekimeiya? Was it only Naomi? On the 15th, she had appeared from the lower floors, asking to talk to Katei privately. Maybe that was where she ended up after she vanished from the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could be sure the previously gray one worked, so I grabbed it, avoiding direct contact. I knew very well about the lack of good hiding spots, so I considered where to leave it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had personally found the hidden area in the storeroom, and it was possible Katei knew about it. Because of that, somewhere in the attic immediately seemed like the best option.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I entered the rightmost bedroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Keeping my hands off the gem, I opened the wardrobe. Once I looked inside, I remembered the two pieces of clothing Atsuki had pointed at.{w} They were a white shirt and a dark gray pair of pants, larger than what I usually wore. There was nothing else to put on.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked around me, wondering where to leave the Sekimeiya. Since I had to find Atsuki, I couldn't stay with it, but there weren't many places in the attic that could conceal things for long. The best I could think to do was crouch next to the bed and let the Sekimeiya roll up to the wall underneath it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The door to the attic was still unlocked, so I had to hurry. I took off my coat and grabbed both pieces of clothing, sensing a bizarre surrealness as I put them on. Would that mere action guarantee my return to that world? There was nothing else I could do to aim for that.{w} ...Had the me that Atsuki had seen really been me after all?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tied my coat and old clothing around my waist together and exited the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The other Sekimeiya still sat on the sofa. What would happen to it? Would anyone find it before the rest entered the attic?{w} We had only been able to come in thanks to the keys on Naomi's dead body. Someone in the tower had to be plotting her death right then, so I needed to find her and see if I could prevent that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I locked the door with my key. Then, going down the floors, I thought about something Atsuki had said after we'd met again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He claimed the recording was real.{w} What the hell did that even mean? Did they really spend an entire month here? There's no way.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What had happened after my travel? The eyes he'd looked at me with had first been filled with suspicion, but why...? Who could I have been if not the "real Shiroya"?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's going to be quite a few hours until the time he saw me with these clothes in hallway B. Will I be there by that time somehow?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I knew my goals were slightly contradictory. After all, that reality wasn't where the Atsuki I was searching for was. However, if I really got there, I could show myself to the others as soon as I traveled to the past from the bathroom. Then, I would suddenly be the original me again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went down the multiple staircases, feeling the odd touch of my new clothes. When I got to the last one, I noticed voices coming from hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They quickly faded, and I realized the group was moving to hallway B. I silently looked past the gray door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei's still not with them.{w} There's no way they talked to the outside.{w} Why is Katei not showing himself? He still has to be here, doesn't he...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I could hear doors opening, the sound of them searching through hallway B. I knew they'd soon go up the floors, so if I wasn't careful, I could easily be found. The storeroom and the attic were the only somewhat unreachable places.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where could Atsuki be!? Is it possible he went to the past and was teleported outside the tower?{w} ...Even if that happened, would he not have entered it again? I suppose not if the incident had already started.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When I was sure hallway C was empty, I stepped down and silently walked to A.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Eventually, as I'd expected, the group came closer again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: To avoid being seen, I hid myself in one of the crystal rooms which had just been investigated, A5. It was the one that had been hit by the smoke, and I could see the gems were still missing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ..ake— ...evator?
entries.speaker: il4

entries.text: I recognized all their voices, and the conversation they were having was fairly familiar to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...em to be worki—
entries.speaker: sai4

entries.text: After noticing the elevator wasn't functioning, they loudly went up the stairs. As Katei wasn't with them, their pace was much quicker, and they didn't consider the unlocked door to floor 2 odd.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...And they didn't find the suitcase in hallway C.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: On that day, we'd been beset with questions from the word go. Who discarded that suitcase? ...What caused the computer's shutdown?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After some time had passed, I exited the room. Was Atsuki there as well, hiding like I was?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Still puzzled by Katei's absence, I went to check the live camera feed. I assumed the monitors were working.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The door wasn't opening.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's locked...? Why?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: As soon as I asked myself that, I knew the answer: the alarm had locked it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...And Katei hasn't unlocked it yet. I guess this proves he wasn't in the security room during the attack.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Or... could it be he's currently still inside?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Only the shutter was in the lobby. At that time, no blood had been spilled yet, and the shining floor remained spotless.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Aside from the darker tone, the case was identical in hallway B. I looked up at the closest camera and confirmed every part of it had been covered by the smoke.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At first glance, nobody else was on the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Atsuki?{w} Are you here...?{w} Atsuki!
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I felt like my voice was audible across the entire crystal floor, but nobody was drawn to it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Naomi had to be somewhere too, but I wasn't sure she'd show herself to me. As I didn't want to be in the middle of the hallway, I walked toward a place I had to check.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I entered the storeroom and rapidly closed the door behind me. The fake wall was keeping the larger corridor hidden, so I carefully felt it for the opening mechanism.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After finding it, I slid it to the back and opened it with ease.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I shut myself in. I couldn't believe that secret passage hadn't had any relevance during the day. It served some kind of purpose, and it was likely someone else still in the tower knew about it. I couldn't feel completely safe there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After shutting myself in, the complete darkness returned.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped up to the final door, aware of where it led.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't see anything, so I'd blindly felt its surface with one hand. ...Something else was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is the handle...! It hasn't been taken off!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I gripped the freezing metal and turned it downward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Immediately, the door smoothly moved toward me, allowing bright light to illuminate the gloomy walls.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before the gap widened, I hastily closed it again. I'd seen white grass at my feet and the surrounding mountains above. The door... was not locked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Has the handle not been removed yet...? ...Or did it never happen this time?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Puzzled, I tried to understand why stepping out of the building was possible.{w} ...On the 15th, the handle had been taken off. When I'd entered the tower during the night, it had already been gone. So how could it possibly have been attached right then?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was a line of reasoning that made a bit of sense.{w} In the morning of that day, we had found a rusty key on the floor of hallway A. ...It was a key I had in my purse at that very moment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After feeling its rough surface, I took it out and inserted it into the keyhole. Upon turning it, I successfully locked the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It really was for this door, then...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And we had found it very early on. It was likely that the handle had been gone since the start.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why would it have been removed so early? Of course, to prevent us from leaving.{w} ...But how would anyone have done that? After all, the alarm was supposed to be a secret. We didn't even learn what really triggered it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Whoever took it off knew about the alarm in addition to the secret door's existence. Normally, I would assume that the door was always taken into consideration for whatever the attack entailed...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But the fact that it was open just now contradicts that, especially because when I entered the tower through it, the handle was already gone.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I see. ...The handle was removed days before the 15th, but this didn't repeat this time, so the door is unlocked. Someone who traveled far to the past must have removed the handle, aware of the alarm and secret door thanks to their future knowledge.{w} But... did they see the handle removed before they traveled and then remove it in the past, making it a loop with no start...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: In any case, this isn't that same world. In this one, the handle wasn't taken off days in advance by anyone. I'm not sure what the cause of these differences is, but there is another major one that must be related.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Katei's absence. I don't think he's in the building right now.{w} In the past, I found the key for this door in his security room. On the 15th, we found it in hallway A, where I bet he dropped it. ...I wonder why he didn't go back for it.{w} Was Katei responsible for all this? That doesn't make a ton of sense, but he had this key. He was ready to leave through this door because he knew the alarm would go off and block every other method of escape. If someone hadn't removed the handle in the past, we might never have even seen him.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So what happened here?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Did he leave right after the smoke was released? I wonder what this plan was really about, then, because Naomi ran up with the Sekimeiya. ...Well, with two of them.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I still had no clue what the attack actually was. I didn't know who was innocent and who wasn't. However, that wasn't the most important thing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What should I do now?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Everyone can leave. Katei's not here, so they must not know what happened or how long they'll have to be here for.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Was Katei behind all the deaths? Did he kill Naomi? ...If he did, they should all be safe. But I don't know what Naomi's intentions are, and Katei also ended up dying in our world.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But it wasn't so simple. If everyone left just like that, I wouldn't return to that world. The only way that could happen was by still being in the tower in the afternoon.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What if Atsuki wasn't with me anymore? If everyone left, I'd finally cement a world with an extra version of myself.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How would it happen? How would I ever return to that world? Just as I didn't know that, I had no clue how I'd ended up where I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was possible the world would morph as the hours went on. People would learn about time travel and eventually go back in time. Upon altering the past, the world's status would shift.{w} It was a mystery how the changes were applied, but I didn't think it was impossible that I could get to where I wanted merely by letting the hours pass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I knew where two Sekimeiya were, and while it was possible I could leave with them, it was incredibly risky—I had no way to know whether traveling to the past was still a good idea.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I turned around and walked toward the wall.{w} ...I thought I'd heard a sound coming from the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I held my breath, staying as close to the wall as possible. The storeroom was uncomfortably cold, so I didn't directly touch the tile.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Had I been mistaken, or had someone crossed the hallway? After focusing my hearing, I hadn't heard anything else.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...If it was the group, I figured they would be talking and have audible footsteps. Unless I'd imagined it, it was either one or two people.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Could it have been Atsuki? I began to debate what to do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He knows about this place. If it's him, he should come here eventually.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd been rigidly on alert for a couple of minutes. If someone was close to me, I wasn't perceiving them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...That was until an abrupt yell came. A faint but shrill yell that instantly pierced my chest.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Seconds later, a door was shut.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It had paralyzed me on the spot. Staring at the darkness, I kept replaying the brusque, feminine yell that had immediately lapsed into silence.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had to rush out of the storeroom. That yell was full of nothing but despair, and someone was still there.{w} I wanted to deny I'd even heard it, but I forced myself to move.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened the wall and very slowly stepped forward. Then, I placed my hand on the hallway doorknob. It was dangerous, but I desperately wanted to see that I'd been wrong.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The hallway seemed completely empty. I distinctly felt the sensation that nobody else was there, but I knew that couldn't be the case.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The door that had closed... All of them were, but my legs began to walk toward one in particular.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I realized how fast my heart had gotten when I gripped the door, and once I opened it, that only intensified.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't been wrong, but the sight I saw wasn't what I expected.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There were two bodies lying on the floor. The room was dim, but I instantly identified them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There couldn't be a more terrifying sight. While my hands trembled and I began to step back, a fate that had been once stated replayed like a record.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...On the floor was my own body, facing me with blank eyes. It had been my own anguished yell that I'd heard.{w} Next to it was Naomi, her head dripping blood beneath one of my arms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Without making noise, I closed the door. Someone was still present—someone who had killed me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't let myself be seen. A sudden dizziness invaded me as I glanced back and forth between both sides of the corridor. Trying not to lurch, I reached the storeroom again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Behind the wall, I let out a long breath, that merciless image still burned into my retinas.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I... had been killed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How had that happened...? Even though the body I'd seen wasn't mine, my own could barely support itself either.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who... had done it? If Katei wasn't in the tower, very few options remained. ...I'd even been wrong about Naomi's safety, as she'd fallen victim next to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had to think straight—it was crucial not to lose myself. The person who had killed Naomi the first time must've targeted me as well... but why...!? And who had it been...!?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no sound I could pick up. The closing door had been the last time I'd perceived someone's presence.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had to calm myself down. The world I was in wouldn't remain.{w} It would be entirely modified until it warped into the day I'd lived through. That would erase my death.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That... had to happen. I didn't know how, or why, but it had to.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki... The new one. Where is he?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: My heart wouldn't slow down. Atsuki was going to see my body soon. ...Just thinking about that made it hard to breathe.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Miiya had just died. I couldn't let him see me dead too, or he might have given up entirely instead of fighting. I didn't want to imagine the brief thoughts going through my own head before dying either, but I couldn't stop imagining them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Two Sekimeiya were in the attic. Trying to undo what had happened was possible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everyone was above me, and as the elevator didn't work, I couldn't rush up. I hadn't wanted to travel through time, but Atsuki couldn't see that I'd died, no matter if it could be reversed later.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was the killer close to me? If I was found, I would become a target. They would have no issue killing me twice. Even though I hadn't heard anything again, they could've been quietly staying somewhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was someone who wanted to kill me since this morning. I have to figure out who it was so that I can be careful later or in case I travel to the past again.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Why had I separated myself from the others? In the morning, I had been careful not to remain alone or with people I didn't trust.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was unbearably terrified, so I froze behind the wall. Paralyzed by fear, I was unable to leave that place.{w} I had to go to the event room and move the bodies to where I was so that they wouldn't be found. If the killer noticed me, however, everything would be over.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So I stayed there, hopelessly regretting all that had happened. The temperature in that part of the building wasn't regulated at all, so the cold seeped into me, but even that had stopped being perceived by my body. ...Nothing was until footsteps finally broke the silence again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It had been a few minutes. Suddenly, faint voices came from the hallway. I immediately knew the group had returned.{w} I couldn't even hesitate. Without wasting time, someone ran past, toward the event room. Then, a voice came from there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...s not here!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: It was Sai. It appeared the storeroom door, being lower quality than the rest, let sound pass easily. But Sai's words weren't the ones I'd expected.{w} Upon hearing that, everyone else ran to the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...ou serious? The three of them must've taken it!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: ...What? Have they not seen the bodies?{w} "The three of them". Naomi, myself, and someone else went down at some point. This third person must be the killer...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...hy! We need to find them!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: ...That voice was Isla's. Puzzled, I still managed to comprehend what had happened. The bodies had been removed, but the Sekimeiya had been taken. They didn't seem to have noticed any blood on the floor, so it had been quickly cleaned as well.{w} However, something didn't make sense.{w} "The three of them must've taken it!" Erina said that. If only those three were possible suspects, the whole group saw the Sekimeiya in the cabinet before going up.{w} ...How was that possible? I had just seen two in the attic...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya! ...Are you here!?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Shiroya...!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: ...e has to be here.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Hey! Shiroya...!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Atsuki's voice increased in volume; he was getting closer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who have I heard? ...Atsuki, Erina, Isla, Sai. ...Is only Akaro left?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: As soon as I thought that, a fifth voice came from the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Here you are! You need to come up!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: That's Akaro...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What happened!?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Just come with me! You'll see!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I could tell he was near the staircase. When everyone heard that, they followed his sudden order and ran up, demanding an explanation. In the blink of an eye, empty silence returned to the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Was he the one who'd killed me? Unless someone had traveled from the future, I saw no other conclusion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew next to nothing about Akaro. He had been shrouded in uncertainty the entire day. At some point, he even disappeared for hours, and Atsuki only saw him once after that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Had he always been Naomi's killer? ...Why had he never killed me, though? What had led to my own death?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Reality had to change. No matter how, the other world had to be brought back. ...Was that truly possible? Would it occur out of nowhere?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I continued to wait in that secret corridor. If the bodies had been moved but not brought to my hiding spot, it was very likely the culprit wasn't aware of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I began to worry. If Akaro was the killer, why get everyone to rush upstairs? It had always been so hard to figure out the culprit's intentions, but I at least knew it was odd that he'd been above the group when he was supposed to be on the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once a few silent minutes had passed, a sudden sound met my ears.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What was that...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was a single metallic sound, one which I couldn't identify.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I heard nothing for a few brief moments, but then there was a follow-up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, did the elevator just open? Then what was that first sound?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I focused my hearing as much as I could. I couldn't be sure, but both sounds had come from where the elevator was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I let more time pass, but nothing else came.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was sure I hadn't been mistaken. Someone had just been there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had to stay where I was. Something was happening, but the person I'd heard had made very little noise on purpose. I couldn't let myself be noticed by them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was another long while where nothing was heard from the storeroom, but once again, the silence was eventually broken when sound came from the staircase.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Here too! What the fuck!?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: They have to be somewhere.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Shiroya! Where are you...!?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I told you! I don't know what the fuck they're doing, but they're hiding from us!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Shiroya isn't doing anything! It has to be Naomi!{w} Shiroya! If you're here, please come out!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: What was I hearing? It was clear something had happened, but I couldn't discern what.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's no way we won't find them if we split up. Atsuki, if you don't want to believe it, I invite you to find her.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I don't care if you're lying or not! She wouldn't do this!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Listen to me! Not only is she hiding with Naomi, but you're incredibly suspicious! They're obviously doing this shit for a reason, but we won't find them if we don't split up.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: He's right. They must have the Sekimeiya, so this has to be part of their plan.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: What plan!? She has no plan!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Then where is she? If she's not involved, why would Naomi do that?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: ...I don't know!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I could tell it was Atsuki who began to open the hallway doors. After loudly opening the storeroom's, he rapidly moved on.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya! Holy shit, please!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: It sounded like everyone was dispersing. Some of them went back up while others joined Atsuki. ...They were searching for two dead people.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The noise moved to the other hallway and eventually quieted. I couldn't understand what they were saying anymore, but I didn't think anything had been found.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everyone was scattered around, and as people went up the stairs, the silence returned again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Where could the bodies have been hidden? Is it possible the security room was opened?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Naomi had possessed the key to the attic, so her killer could've obtained it. But how would both bodies have been brought up when the elevator didn't work?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could notice a couple people still wandering nearby. Katei wasn't there, so their knowledge of the attic was limited.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once some time had passed, most of them ended up back on the crystal floor. In hallway C, they were discussing what could've happened after not finding anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...es, they have to be on the Ashiya floor. That's why this was done.{w} The elevator wasn't working earlier, so they prevented us from using it as soon as it was up and running again.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: ...roya is not doing this...! She must have been locked in there.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: ...ound it!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Akaro shouted from a distance, shutting down the conversation. When he spoke again, he had run down the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Look! It was on the fourth floor!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Huh. Where?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: In one of the drawers! I looked through all of them. That's where they hid it.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: That's weird. They must be on the Ashiya floor, right? Why would they hide the Sekimeiya outside of it?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Hell if I know, but you were right. Their plan was to take the Sekimeiya. Now that we found it, we have to hold on to it until this situation is resolved.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: So what are you saying we should do?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: If we stay in a room, whatever they're trying won't work. They won't be able to get the Sekimeiya again, and none of us will leave it alone. Don't think you're in the clear, either.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I'm telling you that Shiroya isn't part of this...! I have no idea what Naomi wanted, but she brought her to the attic! There's no way I'm staying anywhere without finding her!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I think we should do what Akaro says, Atsuki. If you're right, there's nothing we can do. No matter what their intent is, they're screwed if we stay with the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I'm not going to just sit around! We need to find her!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: ...{w}Was Akaro the killer? When he proposed staying somewhere, an idea came to mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nobody had been found, so the Atsuki I'd briefly reunited with was likely nowhere. I knew he didn't have the key to the attic, so if he was elsewhere, they would've seen him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki, you need to listen to us. If what you're saying is true, we're out of options. However, the Sekimeiya has already been taken once, and they're the only people who could've done this. Even if someone else got trapped, the reality is the same. Whatever plan they have won't work now, so cooperate with us.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I mean, you're free not to. You can keep searching around, but it's evident they're hidden someplace we can't access. Until we can leave, we have to stay somewhere. Splitting ourselves up might just be what they need.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: You're all insane! We don't know how long that'll take! Naomi's the one who did this, so we have to find Shiroya right now!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Akaro had found the Sekimeiya. Was it the one he hid? If he hadn't lied about its whereabouts, it wasn't either of the two I'd seen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They were sure someone else had to be in the building, and that definitely had something to do with the metallic sound I'd heard after everyone went upstairs. Something had happened while they'd been together, so from their point of view, someone else was there and took the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it wasn't me or Naomi. Could it have been Katei, or was he long gone? ...There was one last explanation.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The time travel nobody was yet aware of. If someone had traveled to the past, it would've created the illusion of another person. On top of that, Akaro was holding the very thing that allowed that time travel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We shouldn't leave it in the event room again. We have to hide it from them, just in case.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Akaro's voice distanced as he spoke, and everyone followed him to hallway B. From the other side, I could still hear Atsuki's muddled refusal.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...On my end, I had made up my mind. I slowly opened both doors in front of me and stepped out of the storeroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro and Sai were insistent about staying in a crystal room. Their actions in the other world had been vastly different, especially Sai's.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It didn't seem like the bodies could've been in the attic, so it was possible Atsuki would find them if he searched hard enough. He was against staying in a room with everyone before finding me. That was one of the reasons I abandoned my hiding spot.{w} I couldn't leave him alone, even if I wished the world would change. If he couldn't find me, he would suffer alone for hours. ...Even so, as I saw the hallway, I kept trembling. I really wanted to talk to him as if nothing had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nobody heard the sound of my steps. Who had killed me and Naomi? That question also brought me to leave the storeroom.{w} If it wasn't anyone in hallway B, I wouldn't be safe staying by myself. If it was one of them, I would be safe as long as we were all together, and it was possible I could determine who was responsible.{w} As long as nothing tricky happened, we would remain in one place. If I made sure that continued, it was a good way to let the time advance until the afternoon. It would almost guarantee that the interior of the tower remained calm.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was also curious to know what had been happening. When I turned to hallway C, I instantly understood what the sound I'd heard really was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh... The panel was taken off...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The elevator button wasn't there. Only wires coming out of the wall remained where the metallic panel had been.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sh-Shiroya!
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I suddenly turned to face Atsuki and ran to him, my heart rate increasing as I approached.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-Where were you!? I've searched everywhere!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: When the others saw me, they dashed over. In the meantime, I thought of what to say, hating the need to lie.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck are those clothes?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: N-Naomi gave them to me. ...I told her I was cold and that my old clothes were a bit itchy.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: What the fuck? Where is she!?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I-I don't know... We went to the highest floor, but she suddenly disappeared. I think she locked herself in there.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Are you serious? What did she want?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Huh...? What do you mean?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I'd been looking at the floor, stuttering as I made everything up. ...When I finally looked at the rest, I noticed what greatly stood out from them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Akaro's eyes. They couldn't believe what they were seeing, and his body was solid as a rock. I needed nothing else to know who my killer was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In his hands was a glowing Sekimeiya. However, I immediately saw something I assumed nobody had realized.{w} His sleeve was between it and his skin. He was purposely avoiding contact with it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What did Naomi have to tell you, I mean.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I... don't know. She didn't tell me anything. Can you explain what happened there? Why is the elevator button gone?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...Slow down. What do you mean she didn't tell you anything? She asked to talk to you and Akaro privately. Did she never follow up on that?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: N-No. ...I told her I was cold, and she gave me this.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I see. That's also what Akaro said. That you two suddenly disappeared.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Y-Yes, sorry.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: That's when we heard the elevator, then. Did Naomi activate it?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...You heard it?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yes, it passed through the fourth floor twice. We thought it couldn't have been the elevator since it wasn't working, but it had to be.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I see. I don't know why, but it worked when Naomi called it.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...It did? After that, we all came here and saw that the Sekimeiya had been stolen. Did neither of you do that?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wait, wh-what? No. We never went there.{w} In the attic, she gave me these, and when we left, she suddenly ran back and locked herself inside.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I really hated lying like that. Naomi had been killed, and I was setting her up as the culprit. Meanwhile, Akaro's body hadn't moved in the slightest.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It seemed they had accepted my claims. They were absurd, especially the clothing part since I was colder than before, but Naomi was already suspicious to them, so they seemed to believe what I was saying.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Really, though, what happened to the button...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...When we saw that the Sekimeiya was gone, Akaro told us to run upstairs. He'd been searching for you two, and we missed him when he was in the offices.{w} On the fourth floor, the panel had been ripped off. We went up and saw that they were gone on the fifth and sixth as well. Sai tried to open the doors, but the elevator wasn't there.{w} By the time we ran all the way down, it had happened on the first three floors too, and the elevator wasn't there either.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yeah. We heard it moving two more times when we were going down. If you're telling the truth, I guess that was Naomi.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I am... I don't know what she did after she locked herself up, but I've been looking for you until now...
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: In any case, it doesn't matter. We found the Sekimeiya, and we'll stay with it in a room until we can leave so that it isn't stolen again.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Only one door was open in hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Was that where you were going?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Finally, Akaro spoke. From the storeroom, I'd noticed his voice sounded rougher and sharper than I remembered, but that seemed to have disappeared.{w} When I looked at him, he turned around and walked to that room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I thought we should leave the Sekimeiya here. ...Naomi can open the other cabinet, and just like it, I noticed these can get cold too.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: That was why the room had caught my attention. It was room B4, where we'd found the first Naomi and where the Sekimeiya had been hidden.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's bigger too, so I think it's a good idea.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Once again, without looking at us, Akaro walked into the room and raised the lid of a cabinet, undoing the back lock. After placing the Sekimeiya inside, he rotated the two temperature wheels.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I set it to 5 °C. Let's just leave it in here.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Everyone entered while I narrowed my eyes. Katei wasn't there, so he hadn't repeatedly warned them not to get the Sekimeiya out of the cabinet. Despite that, Akaro had gone out of his way to keep it in a cold space.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He had knowledge of the Sekimeiya—the way he held it was the giveaway. He had to be the one who had stolen it, not just the killer. Atsuki and I had seen the temperature set to 0 °C more than once, and Akaro specifically set it to 5 °C, so there was no way he didn't know about that requirement.{w} ...The temperature of the Sekimeiya's display cabinet wasn't visible, so I wondered what it was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nobody was questioning Akaro's bizarre actions. Perhaps it was normal only I was seeing them as such. Similarly, as nobody was questioning what I'd said, I made my way in and sat on the floor, leaning against a cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki sat to my left. Most strain had disappeared from his face, but I could only feel like I was lying to him. The person he'd entered the building with had been killed, something I could hardly believe.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How had everything taken that turn...? I didn't want to be there. I wanted to be back home or in the lobby, about to leave with Atsuki. I was foolish to hope anything would get better by simply waiting.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The door closed. Sai sat in front of it, blocking the exit. He was insistent about not leaving, and as he looked at me from the opposite end of the room, I could still sense his suspicion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Lastly, when I least expected it, Akaro approached us. ...I glanced at him, but his eyes didn't meet mine.{w} Then, he sat to my right, between me and the cabinet containing the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: For long seconds, I nervously waited for him to say something while he stared at his lap. In the end, when he raised his head, all he did was exhale a long-held breath before staring back down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Simulation Therapy
A while later, the single sound within the room had been that of Isla's steps. She continually walked from cabinet to cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh...! Look at this one!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Erina followed her daughter around the room and mimicked her sounds of amazement.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wow, the swirls on it are so pretty!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Gleefully, they circled the room until they'd observed all the gems.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The last time, all of us had looked at the gems, so the situation clearly differed.{w} Atsuki hadn't so much as shifted one of his legs since we'd come in. I'd wanted to talk to him, but I hadn't expected he would act that way. Before entering the tower, he and I had spoken very little. That gradually changed during the day, but the Atsuki next to me looked just like he had at his house.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Oh, let me see that, Isla.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Everyone looked at her purse, where I was staring. I'd just realized there was something very important to check.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: These? They're sunglasses!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Sunglasses in the winter? Isn't that a little strange?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Nope! They block the sun reflecting off the snow. Here, try them on.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: She came closer and handed them to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm... They're too small for me, but I'm sure they fit you perfectly.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: She put them on with a big grin.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's okay! You can try again when I'm bigger.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...The recorder isn't there. I don't get it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: From farther away, Erina smiled at us. I couldn't help but feel that I'd never seen her look that way in the other world.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla took off her glasses and ran across the room. I had no idea what to think of her, the recording, or her friend. I knew she had died once, though. If we stayed put, that was much less likely to repeat.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: For a while, Isla's quiet footsteps punctuated the silence as she moved to each cabinet. She'd already looked through all of them, but staying still seemed to be difficult for her. Erina simply followed her daughter's movements with her eyes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I noticed that the silence had gone on for longer than usual, I glanced back up. It took me a bit to spot Isla in front of the cabinet with the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She was staring at it with a piercing gaze, her figure completely rigid. Out of nowhere, her right hand began to reach for the lid, moving almost imperceptibly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But before she made contact with it, Akaro noticed what I was looking at.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hey, Isla, what are you doing? The Sekimeiya shouldn't be taken out of there.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...Why not?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: I already explained. I put it somewhere cold, like it was in the event room. Naomi told us not to take it out of the cabinet, so it's better to keep it shut.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I won't take it away. I just want to look at it again.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: You have plenty of other gems to look at. I know you came to the tower for the Sekimeiya, but it's a lot more boring than all the other stones in this room.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Hmph.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Disappointed, Isla turned around. She continued going from cabinet to cabinet, and every once in a while, she'd glare at Akaro from a distance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once she had circled around the room, she was once again in front of the cabinet with the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it was glowing, right? Ash, um... Ashiya said that it was the rarest discovery of the century! What if it has super... um, supernatural powers?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Don't be silly. You don't know much about Ashiya, do you?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I do! I hear about them all the time!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Heh, yeah, but I'll give you some advice. Don't trust anything Ashiya say. You wouldn't like to know how they obtained some of the gemstones you were looking at.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Hmm?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Unprompted, Isla sat next to Akaro, demanding a detailed explanation.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...They've never been known for their decent practices. That's the best way I can put it. I guess kids nowadays aren't very in touch with their history.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Upon seeing that Isla had sat with us, Erina came over too.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You mean they're not good people?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Ah, I've told her about this before. It's why I had reservations about bringing her here.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Huh? I don't remember that.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Well, at least in the past they weren't. Right now, it's a bit harder to say, but God only knows what the reason behind today's event was.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What did you mean before? How have they gotten all these gems?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Do you know anything about gemstones? There are many types. Geodes, for example, look like normal rocks on the outside but are fractal-like on the inside. Ashiya push themselves to have an event every week and change the displayed gemstones often, so in the past they've displayed fake geodes.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: People love looking for extraterrestrial gems—materials that came from space. I bet you that if any of the ones here are supposedly one of those, they were found in one of the mountains you see every day.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I can't give you proof of this, but some of them are lab-created too. Ashiya can't trick everyone, but it clearly works favorably for them. For a while, they displayed a Verdelite Tourmaline labeled as a Chrome Tourmaline, which is much rarer. They're easily distinguished if you have a magnet, but they look very similar if you only have your eyes.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Oh...! You know a lot about this!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Not as much as you would imagine. It's hard not to hear about these things, really. Of course, I'm not surprised the Sekimeiya doesn't seem to be anything special.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Even if it's not, we would have to pay a fortune if we broke it. Akaro's right, it's better to leave it be.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Exactly.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I didn't want Isla to object, so I attempted to change the topic, and the appearance of her house was the first thing that came to my mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She must be a handful. I bet she leaves a mess at home.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: She's got her moments, but we manage. She's all I've got, after all.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Akaro's expression softened. I knew he had to be hiding a lot, but it was hard to think even his appearance was insincere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see. That must be difficult. Say, Isla, how's school going? Shouldn't you be there right now?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Yes, but Mom let me skip classes! I like having a day off because not everyone there is nice.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Some kids are mean to you?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Well, Amelie never lets me play with them, and everyone does what she says.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Ah, is that so? Well, I'll come talk with Amelie once we're out. I had to deal with people like her when I was your age too.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Really? My teacher already tried, but Amelie didn't change at all.
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Don't worry. If she continues, we'll have another talk.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Isla grinned at the thought of a big, scary man like Akaro intimidating her school enemy. Meanwhile, Erina watched over them from above with melancholic eyes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Mom, Mister Akaro is a nice man. Can he be my new daddy?
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...You want him to be your dad? What do you think he'll say when he sees your bedroom?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Huh? I'll clean it! I promise!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: You always say that. It stays clean for three days, and then you forget about your promise.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Not this time! You'll never remind me again!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: Sweetie, you know how much work being in charge of you is, right? Do you really want to put that on him?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I-I'm not that bad!
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: ...It sounded like it was Akaro's time to chime in, but he kept quiet, looking somewhere else.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: His lack of input abruptly ended that topic, so Isla stood up. Instead of returning to the cabinet with the Sekimeiya, she continued romping around the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It took a while, but eventually, she calmed down and sat a bit away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Time passed, and everyone kept to themselves. Sai still leaned against the door, looking nowhere but the floor. It probably hadn't been long enough for the others to get to know his personality and why the way he was acting was unusual.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I realized I no longer had the pendant I'd worn on the 15th. It didn't seem like anyone had noticed, but I would have no excuse if someone did.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...So Naomi hasn't shown up.{w} Did she not say anything when she locked herself inside the top floor?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Finally, Akaro spoke again. His voice was quiet, and the steely look in his eyes from before we'd entered the room was completely gone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No, she didn't... I don't know what got into her, but I assume she wanted to do whatever she did to the elevator.{w} I guess while we're here, there's nothing she can do anymore.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I understand.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Out of curiosity, are you the girl who fell into a coma two weeks ago? I think I saw your name on the news.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Uh, y-yes. ...That was me.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Although he was speaking quietly, Atsuki heard that too and looked at Akaro curiously.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Damn, that must've been a scare. It's good to see you're all right now.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Yeah...
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: There was an explosion close to here, right? Didn't someone die, and {tip=gan}a person{/tip} was sent to the hospital?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Y-Yes... A friend of ours died. Two people were hospitalized.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...Oh.{w} I'm very sorry.{w} I can't imagine what that would be like at your age. I thought earlier that something about you two looked off. I'm really sorry for bringing it up.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It's all right. Don't worry about it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Atsuki said what I'd been about to.{w} Then, Akaro gave us a look of pity. I could only wonder why he'd said any of that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I did lose someone very close to me a long time ago too. I don't imagine this is something you want to hear from a person you don't know, but all I wish now is that I hadn't thought that much about it.{w} At the time, I thought I'd be disrespecting the dead if I tried to get over it, but that nearly ate me alive.{w} I guess you're already doing much better than me if you're here. Thinking too hard about these things when they just happened can be pure torture.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: The worst part is trying to convince yourself that there's some meaning in it. Sometimes, bad things just happen because they happen, and that's all there is to it. I wanted to believe there was a greater plan, but...
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Anyway, the important thing is that you're both still alive. Finding any meaning in that is up to you. Just living and moving past it is enough.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...I agree. That's why we came here.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Atsuki spoke where I couldn't. Akaro being supportive was something I hadn't expected in the slightest, especially given that I was sure he'd killed me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I know people can't choose a way to react, and I shouldn't be giving any advice. ...It's much easier said than done, but if you can, don't regret anything that you did.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...Are you okay?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Atsuki looked at me with sorrowful eyes. When I nodded, he went back to staring at his lap.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...And you? I'm sorry, we shouldn't have come.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Don't be. I'm still glad we're here, and don't worry about me. I'm fine.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: All right.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I smiled, but he didn't look up again.
entries.speaker: i
