entries.text: Isla had finished her most recent survey of the cabinets and was sitting in the middle of the room. I looked at the ceiling, where the camera was, and noticed that no green light flickered below the lens.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I saw Sai looking at his wristwatch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How long have we been trapped for?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Uh... almost two hours. It's {time=11.}
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Two hours...? How much longer do we have to be here? This is getting ridiculous.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It's really strange. I wonder if they're having issues opening the shutter.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: In any case, it has to unlock at any moment.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...If only we had waited like that the first time. Nobody knew about the Sekimeiya's powers. That was likely why the time had been passing so smoothly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Of course, nobody but Akaro. The way he had held it hadn't been a coincidence. ...I didn't know why, but aware of its powers, his intention was to keep us shut in a room while the Sekimeiya was with us.{w} Did he know about the twelve hour limit? ...Or was the reason tied to the other Sekimeiya that I'd seen? I still potentially had one hidden in the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He was the killer who'd hidden his victims' bodies. He had conjured the illusion that Naomi was still alive thanks to the Sekimeiya.{w} ...Next to me, he hadn't opened his mouth again. He knew that I was lying and must've seen me as a threat, but his brief conversation with us had left me dazed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everyone was quiet. For a long time, all we heard was Isla fidgeting with her sunglasses and sporadic sighs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to keep excess thoughts to a minimum. I couldn't understand the strange world I'd suddenly been sent to, so to stave off exhaustion, my mind had remained empty for a while.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It's {time=13.}
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai read the time out loud every half hour. Rather than comforting us, it made things drag on. I'd gotten pretty tired again just by sitting down for so long.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After a while, Sai spoke again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: *sigh*{w}{w=0.7} ...I'm going to the bathroom.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Everyone watched him stand up, but the silence remained as he left the room. We'd been sitting for a long time, so it wasn't reasonable to stop him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai had been practically parked in front of the door, but the atmosphere hadn't changed with him gone. The concern began when a few minutes passed without him returning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd immediately considered the possibility that he had an ulterior motive, but everyone else took longer to reach that conclusion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Where exactly did Sai go?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Do you think he was lying? It's been a long time since he left.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Don't think about him. If he doesn't want to come back, it's not our problem.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Could Akaro and Sai have been working together? What the hell were they doing, then...?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What if something happened to him?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Don't be ridiculous. Do you think Naomi attacked him? We would've heard that.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I don't trust him. I think he might be trying to make us search for him so that we leave the room.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...Really? I don't think that makes much sense.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Forget about him. No matter why he left, staying here is the right call.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It eventually became clear Sai wasn't coming back. He'd left with our only method to measure the time, but it felt like almost half an hour had passed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Seriously, what the fuck is happening? It's been hours.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Nobody responded.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Still next to me, Atsuki and Akaro patiently waited. On the floor lay a tired Isla, while Erina's face showed the most worry.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Simultaneously, Atsuki and I looked at the ceiling.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did you hear something?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I think so.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...What are you talking about?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It sounded like someone just walked above us. And did you not hear sounds coming from the crystal floor a few minutes ago?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What? I didn't hear that.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Erina hadn't noticed anything either.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everyone was on alert, but the sound had been very brief, immediately engulfed by the silence again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, just a few minutes later, it repeated.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Th-There! Did you hear it?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: We all nodded that time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Someone's on the second floor.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Didn't it sound like more than one person?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...More than one?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: My mind jumped to the other Atsuki. ...Was he still there?{w} We listened with rapt attention, but there was nothing else to hear.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It took less time to repeat than before, and when it did, we were sure more than one person was outside our room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's Sai and Naomi. ...What the fuck are they doing?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Erina grimaced at his language but opted not to reprimand him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It has to be them. There's no way we missed anyone.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Don't think about leaving. Whatever they're doing won't matter as long as we're here.{w} It's not our business either. They're the ones who could be committing a crime.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We didn't move, but during the following minutes, the same faint sound of footsteps was heard two more times.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Whoever they were, they'd been moving through the building. At one point, it seemed as if a sound came from the crystal floor itself, but I didn't mention that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Who was there? Akaro had reiterated that Naomi and Sai were trying to lure us out, but my curiosity went beyond that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Unmistakably, more than one person was moving around. However, Naomi couldn't have been included. I knew she was dead.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then who was the other person? With everything seemingly unchanging, my need to know had only grown larger. Could it have been Atsuki? I didn't think so. Had Katei been there the whole time? I didn't think so either.{w} ...Was it someone who'd traveled through time?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Whoever it was, they hadn't been heard in a while.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What time is it now? Are we going to be here all day?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It was getting unbearable even for me, who knew when the supposed end was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina walked a few steps. I thought she only wanted to stretch her body again, but that wasn't it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I have to go to the bathroom.{w} Do you need to go too, Isla?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: il

entries.text: She shook her head.{w} At the same time, the rest of us looked on with skepticism after what had happened with Sai.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Don't worry, it shouldn't matter if only one of us leaves. I doubt I'll come across Sai or Naomi, but I'll be right back.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...But she wasn't.{w} After a little while, we realized the same thing had occurred.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And since she'd left, the sporadic sounds had returned. Someone had walked above us and on the crystal floor, but all of those noises were faint.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Eventually, even Isla began to look concerned, quietly staring at the empty door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When Sai didn't come back, it was natural to assume it was his choice. The case wasn't the same with Erina.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Someone was there—someone who shouldn't have been there. Had they prevented both people from coming back to us...?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't take it anymore. Once again, the sounds had momentarily stopped, but I had to know who else was in the building. As I was convinced Akaro had been my killer, I didn't fear leaving the room anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll go too.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: H-Huh?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I'll come back, though. Sorry, we've been here for too long.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Before he could object, I walked to the door. I didn't exactly want to leave Atsuki behind, but I had no choice.{w} I hadn't missed Akaro's sudden frown, but he kept his mouth shut as I passed by Isla.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked both ways. Nothing about the hallway appeared immediately odd, but the darkness was imposing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The lobby door was open. Drawn to it, I tried not to make a sound.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Both bodies were there, near the hallway A door. Like before, my own looked at the ceiling with empty eyes, while drops of blood had stained the floor beneath Naomi's head.{w} In addition, all the ceiling lights were on, even the ones that the alarm had disabled and weren't working in the morning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew Sai had once tried to kill us, but those bodies couldn't have been his doing alone. Recalling the faint sounds I'd heard from inside the room, I slowly stepped to the other door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The bodies had been moved to the lobby, and there was no way the other Atsuki would've done that. Unable to look at them up close, I hurried out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No way.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Someone was far ahead, next to the staircase.{w} A pool of blood extended around a third fallen body, lying in the illuminated zone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina. What's happening...!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: My heart dropped like a stone. I looked away from her body, but I had to fight back tears.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Had the killer been outside all along?{w} It was too overwhelming—I couldn't bear it anymore. But the next thing I heard was footsteps from hallway B, causing my heart to drop even further.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I ran as fast as I could, but I was too late. All I saw was Atsuki's figure disappearing into the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I clenched my fists, desperately thinking about what to do. He had already seen both bodies, but there'd been no audible reaction.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Suddenly, someone else came out of the crystal room. Before I hid myself behind the wall, I was able to see Akaro.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What now...!? Do I have to hide again?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Everything had gone down the drain so fast. I felt unable to move, as if my racing heart was using all my energy.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Hey! Where the fuck are all of you!?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I looked at the hallway again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As soon as I did, I saw Akaro coming out of the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, he began to get closer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He might notice me if I try to leave.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...What?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Did he enter... the staff room?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd heard Akaro's short steps and then a door closing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...But before I could think about it, I realized Atsuki was in hallway A, slowly approaching Erina.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had nowhere to hide. As a last-ditch effort, I darted to the bathrooms, which I could see were empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I slowly closed the door of the women's and locked it with the inner latch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I can stay here. Katei was the one who had the key.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Soon after I heard Atsuki's steps reach Erina's body, they ran up the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What is he doing? Does he want to find whoever else is in the building?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: From Atsuki's point of view, only Sai or an extra person could've killed the three of them. My body wore different clothes, but there was no way he'd care about that while unaware of what the Sekimeiya could do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hated thinking about it. He'd found me dead, and I couldn't even imagine what I would've felt in his place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once his steps had disappeared, I continued to pay attention so that I could hear what was happening in hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But nothing did. Since Akaro had shut himself in a room, I'd heard no new movement.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is he still there? ...What about Isla?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Could the door have been preventing the sound from reaching me?{w} No. I'd heard Atsuki going up the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...And why did he only call for us once? He immediately went quiet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't know where Akaro was, but the time when Atsuki had seen the me in different clothing was slowly approaching. I just had to wait a bit more to see whether my hopes had been in vain.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How's this possible? Where did everyone go?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd been in the bathroom for several minutes, but the impossible silence hadn't ceased. We'd heard sounds from the crystal room. Someone had to be there. ...Why was everything so quiet, then?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Should I go to the storeroom?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I unlocked the door. I had the chance to go back there, so I slowly opened the way out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is there really nobody here?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The silence persisted once I stepped out. I'd wanted to run straight to the storeroom, but I noticed that all the doors in hallway B were closed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What about Isla? She can't see Erina's body.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Wait.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I approached room B4 as soon as a thought came to mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After a deep breath, I twisted the doorknob.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Undertow
She's not here.{w} Oh... I was right.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The cabinet where the Sekimeiya had been was open. I stepped up to it and glanced inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya was still there, and its color was white. After staring at it for a while, I reached inside and took it out, protected by my long sleeves.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's cold.{w} ...They must've traveled, though. That's why the sounds stopped.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...But where were they? I was clueless.{w} Why had the Sekimeiya been touched, and why had it allowed someone to travel? The temperature in the cabinet was frigid.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked to the hallway and then to the staff room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Holding the Sekimeiya with one hand, I opened the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He's not here. I'm pretty sure this is where he went.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I... should bring the Sekimeiya to the storeroom.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Without thinking twice, I ran to hallway A.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked both ways to confirm that nobody was there and gripped the doorknob.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: My jaw dropped, and I stared at the lobby. Its door had been left open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Were my eyes betraying me? As I got closer, I knew that I hadn't imagined it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where's Naomi...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Only my own corpse remained on the floor. Although the red pool of Naomi's blood was still next to it, the body it belonged to wasn't there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The sensation that had once faded came back, reminding me of where I was. Inexplicable mysteries were bound to occur on December 15th.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I turned around; trying to think it through was useless. Even though I didn't know what I was waiting for, it was clear anything could happen, so going back to my own world wasn't far-fetched.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I entered the hidden part of the storeroom and dropped the Sekimeiya on the floor. Glowing in the darkness, its temperature was noticeably higher than after I'd taken it out of the cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I least expected it, a crucial piece of the puzzle fell into place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, of course...! How did I not realize this earlier?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I left the storeroom. If what had been in the lobby was a pool, near the staircase, Erina's body lay on a sea of blood.{w} ...That Erina, below the broken elevator... We had never spoken to her. That was because she had died.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did it make any sense? My idea was muddled, but I was sure it was on the right track.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had to make sure of something. ...I had to make sure Akaro and Isla weren't anywhere.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Even though an immense amount of things didn't add up, I thought I'd found one of the keys. As I bolted up the stairs, details reinforced that thought.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's gotta be later than {time=15.} That fits perfectly.{w} And... the drop of blood that Atsuki and I saw in the lobby... It was exactly where Naomi's body left it before vanishing.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When I reached the offices, I stopped myself abruptly. There was something on the floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Another Sekimeiya...?{w} Could this be the one I hid?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I hovered my hand over it. An aura of heat surrounded it, so it was functional as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I picked it up, I felt that it was even hotter than I'd thought. Thanks to the thick clothes from the attic, I was able to bring it with me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did Atsuki see it? This had to be here for a while.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Running up the floors, I saw that every elevator panel had been taken off. Had Akaro been responsible for that? I had no clue anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Eventually, I reached the attic's door. Every floor had been vacant, but the attic couldn't be.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was open, so I could see the narrow staircase ahead.{w} Why? Why wasn't the door locked anymore? Furthermore, the key was inserted in the outer keyhole.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Many footprints were pressed into the carpet. It didn't make any sense, but I didn't care. I also saw that the suitcase was no longer on the sofa.{w} As soon as I stepped into the living room, I heard a noise coming from one of the bedrooms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd hidden the Sekimeiya there hours earlier. When I got closer, I could make out the sound better, and I locked up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki was crying. I could see his torso on top of the bed, twitching rhythmically.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He had seen the dead bodies—my own death.{w} I was still alive, though.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I recalled what Sai had told us a long time in the past. According to him, the drop of blood in the lobby was mine.{w} He'd been wrong, hadn't he? It was Naomi's.{w} In that case, why had he said that? And why had he been both right and wrong about my fate?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped back, careful not to make a sound. Perhaps I was a monster for that, but it was the only thing I could do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki had learned that the me of his world had died. I wanted to go back to mine, so I couldn't show myself and disappear on him again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Aside from Atsuki and me, the whole tower was empty. How could that be, though? Where were Akaro and Isla?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The answer to that question was one I already knew.{w} They were in my world. They were the proof that going back was possible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At the point I was, an Akaro had appeared in the attic. His memories had differed from ours, and there had been a major distinction between us—he didn't know Katei.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It had taken me a while to process it, but everything he said had started to make sense. The events he described were the ones I'd just lived through.{w} He'd sympathized with us, and he'd been surprised to hear we'd found Naomi's body but not that she'd died. After all, he had killed her in the world I was in, hadn't he?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai? I have no idea. He left the room earlier and didn't come back. What are you all even doing here?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I mean... what I said. Why are you all here?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: We tried to stay put in one place together. Do you not remember that?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: No, I do. That doesn't answer my question, though.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: How does it not answer your question? You and Sai escaped, and now you came back.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What!? That's not true! I didn't escape.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: And Isla... What the hell happened to her?{w} At the same time that Akaro appeared, Erina swore she heard Isla just outside the bedroom.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, the last person, Sai... Where was he?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sai who chased us with a knife... Who was he?{w} ...The one who left the crystal room a while ago is the one who had the chance to see my body in the lobby. Is that where he made a mistake?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I went back to the storeroom and moved behind the wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After dropping the Sekimeiya, I shifted my focus to the one I'd left there earlier.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How did they reach that world? There can only be one answer: with the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The cabinet was open, so they touched the Sekimeiya. Even Sai could've touched the other one after leaving the room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's what brought them there. It has to be.{w} How did I even get here in the first place? It was by touching the Sekimeiya. ...And why did Atsuki disappear from this world? I'd bet it happened when Naomi touched the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So then, why would it send me to another world as opposed to making me travel through time?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't know that. It didn't make any sense. However, I could be confident it would work. It had already been proven.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After all, Atsuki had seen me on the crystal floor wearing the clothes I was wearing that very second. If I touched the Sekimeiya, I was guaranteed to go back.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't waste any more time. The darkness highlighted two glows, but my hand only approached one. It was the one I believed Akaro and Isla used.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Before I realized it, the glow disappeared in an instant of brief heat.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did it power off...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I extended my hand more and understood that wasn't the case. ...It hadn't just powered off. The Sekimeiya wasn't there anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to find the other one, but I couldn't. The darkness had become absolute yet again, and as I smelled the air, I felt I noticed a difference.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did it work? I didn't teleport.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I touched the walls around me. I was still in the storeroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stood up and took off to the door at the end of the corridor. When I hit it, I frantically felt its surface with my hand.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's not here! The handle's gone!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had... made it back. I really had.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I dropped to the floor, exhausted and overwhelmed. There were so many things that I didn't understand, but I'd been right about the most important one. I closed my eyes, letting out short breaths until they slowed down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Transformative Interference
What do I want to do now...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I wasn't safe in the storeroom anymore. The handle was gone, so everyone should have known about the hidden section. It appeared I had two options to choose from.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How did the world function? Even though I'd changed the past, I'd gone back to a reality that I'd long thought erased. Just that fact made me doubt it was possible to alter history.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, I had to think it was possible. I could do it right that moment. If I showed myself, I would change the events I'd experienced. And that was what I had to choose.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Whether to change the past or not. ...Did both options make sense?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I let everything repeat, the current version of myself will travel from the bathroom. That will let me take her place once again. ...I'd have to let Katei die for that.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And still, to do it, I couldn't merely stay put. I had to purposely let Atsuki see me to seal the start and end of the loop.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Will that be how it'll work in the end?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If I divert the events from the ones I remember, two versions of me will persist. It might also erase the Atsuki I met this morning, or myself, depending on what the consequences will be...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Like I'd wanted, I had eventually returned to my target world by just waiting. The proper circumstances had aligned to fulfill what had to happen. If I just waited a while longer, I would arrive at the truth of Atsuki seeing me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know the exact time, so I got as close to the hallway as possible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I can't really hear anything.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Hm...{w} I'm pretty sure someone should be here, no matter what time it is.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We didn't look at the storeroom again when we left the attic, did we...? I might really be able to stay here undiscovered.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Had I always been there all along? I had a lot of trouble visualizing exactly what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Trying to perceive any sound, I continued pressing my ear against the wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Once again, that led into minutes of silence, and as they kept passing, my concern only strengthened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was I really in the same place? Maybe the handleless door hadn't been the proof I thought.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is probably the time we were locked in the attic, but we know things happened down here while we were above. ...What's with the complete silence, then?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Akaro who appeared in the bedroom... He has to be the one I was with just now. If that's correct, Isla was actually in the attic as well when Erina heard her.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So then, what happened to them? Why did we never find Isla, and why did Akaro disappear?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We had left Akaro in the lower level of the bedroom. A while later, he disappeared. Furthermore, the chain hadn't been removed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was a simple explanation—disappearing with the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When the ominous silence had gone on for a while, I decided to open the door in front of the wall.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Hallway A.{w} Immediately, I noticed something that differed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The elevator button is in place.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Is it correct that if I don't intend to change the past, it won't? If so, that'll be very convenient.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I mean, I have proof that I'll still be here hours later, so I can do whatever I want as long as I don't purposely change the past.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I went up the staircase. ...Could Isla have been in the attic?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had to see it with my own eyes. I had to confirm I was back there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I reached the attic's door. Next to every elevator on the way up, the metallic panels had been properly attached.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked at the floor of the living room. Even though it had changed considerably, there were still recent footprints, and the empty suitcase was back on the sofa.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait a second.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stared by my feet after stepping in and remembered something Atsuki had once said.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A-Are these Isla's? They can't be, right? And I think they're a bit too big.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I couldn't make any sound. Slowly, I stepped to the hallway and saw all that I needed to see.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's no handle here either...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That could've only meant one thing. As I stood there, we were all behind that door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, is Isla here?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Like we'd once done, I took off my boots to reach the other bedroom while making the least amount of noise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So was the kitchen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And the storeroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...She's not here.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}I put on my boots and closed the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then what the hell happened to her? Did she—
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Hold on.{w} That's it. ...That's what happened!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The identity of Isla's friend...{w} I had finally figured it out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Isla had died, so how could she have been alive within a month? Atsuki had already stated that the recording was no trap.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There were many things I had learned. Vaisude revealed that there was a large travel at around {time=16.} That was how he had appeared on the 24th of November, and it happened to fit with the approximate date Isla's friend had appeared.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And that's not all. This also explains another mystery: Akaro's disappearance.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There's someone else who appeared on the 24th of November. The person who escaped from a prison cell, who I really have to assume was Akaro.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: At {time=16}, there was a very large travel, and everyone who got caught up in it appeared on the 24th of November. Three people who traveled were Vaisude, Isla, and Akaro.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Akaro who appeared in the cell wasn't the same Akaro we originally met in the morning. In a way, that explains some of the questions I had.{w} Didn't Atsuki say that he'd seen Akaro once again? That was the version of him who escaped the bedroom with Sai.{w} Why did he appear in prison, and what did he do later? I don't know, but at this point I have no doubt Akaro was the Xyn member trapped with us.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And that's how both Islas met. ...Earlier, when we were in the bedroom, Erina's and Isla's behavior seemed different. That's because in that world, her "friend" never appeared.{w} This is the solution to Atsuki's problem. After going to the past, she didn't recreate what she had lived through. For her, that was happening for the first time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When I thought about it, all the things we'd heard about her friend made sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "She said that if we stayed calm in one place, nobody would be hurt."{w} That's exactly what we did. We stayed in a crystal room, and Isla never saw any of the dead bodies.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "She said that even though she didn't know how it would end or how long we'd stay here for, she'd wait for me at home."{w} I see. The reason she didn't know how it would end was because she traveled to the past in the middle of the day, and she didn't know how long we'd stay because Katei hadn't been there to explain the alarm.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It makes sense. Isla was told that seven people would get trapped and that it'd be three men and four women. That's just because the other Isla wasn't counting Katei.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There was one last thing Isla had told us. Her friend assured her that she would get to touch the Sekimeiya.{w} The Isla I'd just been with had touched it. In the crystal room, she asked about it, but Akaro told her not to. When he left Isla alone, I'm sure she took advantage of it. That was why the cabinet was open and why both of them appeared in the world I was in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's only one thing I find strange... If she appeared in this world in that room, she would've noticed that a curtain had appeared on the floor with Naomi's corpse under it. ...Did she see it?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Hm... the Sekimeiya was inside the cabinet, so she had to climb inside to touch it. If she changed worlds inside the cabinet, she would have shut herself in there, because it's locked in this world. I wonder what exactly happened.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And when did the recording come into play in all of this...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A sound came from the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did they open the door...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Someone was there, but I could only hear footsteps.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I made sure not to move, but I couldn't discern who it was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It has to be us. ...We just left the bedroom.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: They're still there.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The sound wasn't reaching well where I was. There had been brief periods of silence, but I could tell the hallway was not empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Soon, the dry footsteps faded away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did they leave? That wasn't only one person.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I should go back to the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't like the idea of staying in the attic, but I could've been seen if I went all the way down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No matter who that was, I can probably make it down before them.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I tried to open the elevator, but it didn't budge. Then, as soon as I pressed the button, I felt a spark in my mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Whoa, what the hell...?{w} Did this happen again?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Dumbfounded, I stared at the button until it lit up orange.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Inside the elevator, I pressed the lowest button.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While I descended the building, I reeled from confusion. ...What had just happened?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I opened the door on the crystal floor and made a quick dash to the storeroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I paid my utmost attention behind the door. What was about to happen was very important.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There it is!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Someone appeared from the staircase.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It's more than one person. It has to be the same people who just left the attic.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That meant it had to be us. It had to be us... Atsuki and me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Was that me? I just heard a voice.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I wasn't sure, but they didn't speak again. Instead, they got closer to where I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And as the sound of their footsteps increased, they quickly decreased. Then, they opened a door. ...I had to think it was the event room's.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell...? It has to be us, but it doesn't make sense.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Something else had to happen, so I waited for it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I waited... for something that didn't happen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nobody else came from the staircase side. In fact, ever since the footsteps had crossed the hallway, I hadn't heard anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In just a few minutes, I began to doubt what had been confirmed. I doubted I really was back in that world.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I glanced at hallway A. Nobody was there, but I believed it was easy to confirm where I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Cautiously, I walked to the lobby door. I opened it slowly, creating the tiniest gap.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I'd thought, something was wrong.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was completely empty. My own body had disappeared even though a single drop of blood remained near the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why... Why is nobody here?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I went to the event room, where the door had been left open. ...The display cabinet was empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's no chance I'm not back, is there?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had to be, and a way to be sure was in hallway B. But something else grabbed my attention as soon as I stepped in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A door was open. It belonged to the farthest crystal room, B6.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I approached it slowly and soon saw what was behind it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya was just inside the room. Its color was white, and nobody was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could only frown as I walked up to it. That was the place we had traveled from after leaving the attic. Many things indicated I was in that world.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But not all. There was something that wasn't right, and it was baffling.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So there are two Sekimeiya here as well...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That had to be right, and no matter what was happening, keeping one was a good idea. Still rattled, I picked it up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The headache was coming back, so I left quickly and directed myself to the room I'd wanted to inspect.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: B4, where I'd been for hours. When I opened the door, I found what I expected on the other side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Naomi was on the floor, under a curtain. There were bloodstains near her and on the wall, too.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Just what the hell is happening?{w} The Sekimeiya I have right now is the one we touched in that crystal room, right...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I just took it, so that's why we didn't find it later. ...Instead, we found it in a drawer.{w} That must not have been the same one. ...Is that it?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The structure of those events didn't make sense. There was a major contradiction.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I approached one of the cabinets. Its side wheel was damaged.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's the same cabinet we saw that day.{w} ...Actually, I should keep the Sekimeiya here. I was thinking of bringing it to the storeroom, but that could be risky depending on what happened.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After all, why had I traveled back to that world? Due to an idea I'd had, I didn't want to stay near the Sekimeiya. For the same reason, I had to turn the wheel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro set it to 5 °C, but that must not have been enough, because the Sekimeiya still worked when Isla touched it. ...We found it set to 0 °C, so that might be better.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I still couldn't easily believe what I was thinking. ...Had everything really happened as I thought?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew I had to be wrong about something, so what made the most sense... was that I was mistaken about what time it was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...After all, I had used the elevator.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the attic, I'd been so distracted that I hardly considered the elevator would be audible. In fact, while I'd thought about it, I'd been blinded by the assumption that if I didn't mean to change the past, everything would repeat, and I was at no risk of being seen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If everything did happen the same way, it was guaranteed that I wouldn't be found. Therefore, using the elevator to go to the crystal floor was safe. That had been my unconscious thought process.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it had generated a logical issue in my mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who had caused the noises I'd heard in the attic? I'd assumed that was the time we'd left the bedroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But what had happened after that?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki and I went down to the crystal floor and then to the event room. That's what I heard from the storeroom just now.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, we found the Sekimeiya in room B6. We touched it and traveled through time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We appeared back in the bedroom, and then we went to the lobby before our original versions arrived on the crystal floor. We determined that we'd gone five minutes to the past.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: However, that didn't make any sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The elevator was another key detail to those events.{w} After leaving the attic's bedroom for the first time, we had heard the elevator twice on the office floors.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, when we traveled five minutes to the past, I pressed the button in the attic. That's why we thought it was us who called it from the attic and took it down.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And just now, when I called the elevator, I thought "Did this happen again? Did I once again call the elevator without realizing that I was going to produce the sound I'd already heard?"
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That was wrong, though. It couldn't have happened "again" because both elevator trips were the very same.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After Atsuki and I touched the Sekimeiya and appeared in the bedroom, I called the elevator, producing the sound we heard before traveling. Now, right after the old versions of us went down, I called the elevator, producing the sound we heard.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Which one was right, and which one was wrong? Only one was the truth.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was the reason why I was skeptical about my surroundings. I was in that world, but there had to be something I was mistaken about.{w} If it was the time of day, everything made sense. If the sounds I'd heard in the attic hadn't belonged to our past selves, there was no contradiction.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But was that it...? It didn't seem likely. From the storeroom, I was pretty sure I'd heard my own voice. That would've been when we'd checked the elevator to confirm that it arrived on the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I just caused the sound we heard that day, then what the hell happened after we appeared in the bedroom?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Just a few minutes prior, I'd confirmed nobody was in the lobby. ...But the versions of us who had touched the Sekimeiya in B6 were supposed to be there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who had caused the elevator noises? No matter which one was correct, the other interpretation was completely wrong.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been trying to combat my headache to understand what had happened. Even though both versions of things made perfect sense separately, it was impossible to reconcile them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...In the storeroom, I touched the Sekimeiya and the world around me changed. Could something like that have happened when we touched it in room B6?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That seemed like it could make sense, but there was another problem. Atsuki had seen me after that point. That implied he was still in the same world.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd been caught up sorting everything out in my head when I heard someone just outside the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Who's that?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The sound only intensified, and soon, the door opened. When I saw who was there, I rushed over.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina...! A-Are you—
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Before I could finish, she fell to the floor.{w} Her clothes were soaked in blood, and her expression was vacant. I moved to shake her shoulder, but she didn't respond.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What happened...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Disconcerted, I closed the door. I didn't want to be heard, and I wasn't sure who else was there. However, I calmed myself down when I recalled what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Right... Okay. She's not dead.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That was the room where we'd found her, and she had fallen in the same position. I placed a finger on her neck and felt the pulse we'd missed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She said she got hit in the head, but who did it...? All this blood can't be hers.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Who could've hit Erina? ...Akaro, Sai, and Katei. However, no one else but Katei had lost that much blood.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The blood is fresh. ...Katei's already dead, then.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I was once again lost. Everything was repeating, which meant that I hadn't been mistaken. What I'd heard in the attic was really us leaving the bedroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I doubted what to do. Sai and Akaro could've been very close by.{w} In the other world, Akaro had killed me, and in the one I was in, Sai would soon chase us with a knife. No matter what, I couldn't let myself be seen, so going to the storeroom was dangerous.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Katei and Erina left the attic together. They might've been attacked at the same time by Akaro or Sai.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So, what about us? Where were our past selves?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: According to my memories, we should have been in the lobby when I'd peeked into it, so I couldn't blindly trust what I remembered in that regard.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Maybe I should go to the storeroom anyway. If everything will play out the same, I can be sure I won't be seen.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Wait, no.{w} I don't have to.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I thought a little ahead. When we'd found Erina, we failed to realize that she was alive. Due to the shock, we'd barely stepped into the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could leave, but given what I knew, I didn't have to. If I stayed next to the door when it opened, our past selves wouldn't see me. It was better not to move.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I waited next to the door. From there, the whole floor seemed silent.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina had completely passed out. She hadn't moved an inch, and as the seconds passed, I kept wondering where Atsuki and the other me were.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't get it. Was I not properly remembering what had happened...?{w} I looked up at the camera. Was I being recorded in two different places simultaneously?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...?{w} The green light still isn't there. That's odd...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Sekimeiya was in my hands. I'd gotten distracted, so I hadn't left it in the cabinet. However, I'd also noticed something else that was strange, which had made me very reluctant to follow through with that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't have to wait long before I heard a door opening. It sounded like someone had come from the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Again, it's more than one person. ...Are they gonna go to the bathrooms?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: They did.{w} Then, another door was opened. ...I knew it was the staff room's.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It really is us. What the hell, then?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...et the Se—{w} ...has to be—
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: It is. That was Atsuki.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I remember what we did... After checking that Naomi's locker was still open, we found the Sekimeiya in a drawer in room B6. We brought it to the event room, and then we found Katei and Erina.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: As predicted, the steps eventually moved to the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I'm not mistaken, they'll come here soon.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: My tension grew, but I had to be fine as long as I didn't make noise. Meanwhile, I kept wondering what to do with the Sekimeiya that I had. ...I could be sure there had always been two of them, as we had just locked one in its cabinet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was no remaining doubt in my mind that I was right, so I waited. After finding Katei, it hadn't taken us very long to come across Erina.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And that was reflected by the sound behind the door. Mere minutes after it faded, the lobby door opened again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I knew full well the desolate atmosphere we'd experienced as we'd looked in every room. After that repeated, they opened the door next to me, and I was forced to relive the shock of seeing Erina's bloodied body through their sharp gasps.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki took two steps forward, and I heard my past self crumple down. Hidden behind the door, I held my breath.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's it... I can't look at her. Let's go...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Slowly, Atsuki turned around. I couldn't see it, but I felt the despair that came from him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Give me a second.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Before they left, Atsuki detached the curtain from the cabinet closest to him and covered Erina with it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I exhaled. I may have been in the same world I'd come from originally, but there were loads of things I didn't understand.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So now what?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Sekimeiya entailed a dilemma. I wanted to leave it behind, but that potentially created its own problem.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh...! This is what happened!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When I thought ahead, the answer to a persistent question was finally answered.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I... I just trapped myself.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd been going one step at a time, so I hadn't realized a direct result of what I'd done.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After finding Erina, we went to the event room, and Atsuki sat next to the hallway A door.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I finally understood... The reason why he'd seen me, and why that would repeat.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm trapped. As soon as I leave this room, Atsuki will hear and see me. ...That's what woke him up.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...And I had to leave. If I stayed there for much longer, a search would eventually find me. That wasn't all—I knew Erina would soon regain consciousness herself, and I had a reason to think Sai would search the room I was in fairly soon. ...I had to leave, and as soon as I did, I would force our past selves out of the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had a Sekimeiya with me, so teleporting out was an option. But it was one I couldn't risk, because I refused to leave the world I was in again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the event room, I had fallen asleep very quickly. I'd been dead tired that day.{w} I felt a similar exhaustion at that moment. I'd been in the tower for many hours already, but they'd fortunately been much less dense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After I leave, Atsuki will call for me, and I won't appear.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Unbelievable as it seemed, that aligned with what I wanted, so it made sense for it to occur. I could watch what had happened from a distance, and there was something I was curious about.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There was yet another reason—it would've caused a problem that I was finally sure existed.{w} I couldn't interact with my old self. It was the same thing we'd considered with Isla. If my past self met the future me and tried to keep everything exactly the same, she'd have to replicate precisely what she'd seen me do. Every word, every movement. No human was capable of that.{w} It was crucial not to be seen by both her and Atsuki.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A certain time was approaching. There was something I'd been avoiding thinking about.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On that mountain, I made a decision...{w} To change the past and save everyone. Miiya, Isla, Erina, Katei, Naomi...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: While that reality seemed distant, it was as close as ever. The time I'd found the Sekimeiya in the water tank would soon come. At that point, the Sekimeiya had shot me quite far through time, even though I didn't know why.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...When I go to the bathroom, I just have to stop my old self. ...That should let the Sekimeiya store even more energy, so if I touch it later, I'll go to November again. To a time before Miiya died.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That was all I had to do. If I changed the past in just the right way, accomplishing what I'd decided was well within reach.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And yet... I didn't know what to do.{w} Hadn't I also decided that going to the past was a mistake?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If I didn't interfere, my past self would travel, and I would become myself again. I could just leave with Atsuki...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But is that even the case...? Would that really be possible?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Atsuki from this morning said that the recording was real. We won't simply leave at {time=21.}
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And that wasn't all. He was suspicious of me and asked if I was the real Shiroya.{w} ...Why? What happened after I went back in time?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Up until then, my safety had been guaranteed because Atsuki had seen me late into the day. Beyond that point, I couldn't be confident about anything. On top of that, it was a fact that I'd never been mentioned in the recording.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I also recalled that I'd been seen again later, wearing the clothes from the attic. That had only been briefly mentioned, so I didn't know what it was about.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked down. When the Sekimeiya had begun to get too hot, I'd left it on the floor.{w} It was a bit difficult to decide what to do with it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My intention was to leave it in that cold cabinet, but I think something's odd about that.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Once I leave, our past selves will go to the attic. While they're returning, the elevator will be intercepted and Sai will chase them.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: They'll all end up in the event room, where Sai's attitude will flip. Something we didn't figure out was how he managed to not be found in hallway B when Atsuki searched through every room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If I left the Sekimeiya in that cabinet, that would've given him a way out. He could've disappeared by touching it. That was why I'd thought that he might've been about to investigate the room and find out that a Sekimeiya was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At that point, another Sekimeiya was in the event room. If there are only two, the only way Sai could've disappeared from one of these rooms is with the Sekimeiya that I have now.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I would keep it cold, so he'd have to take it out, wait for Atsuki to investigate the other rooms, and touch it as soon as this one was about to be searched in order to get away.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But it's not so straightforward, because according to Atsuki, he looked in every cabinet. If that's what happened, he should've seen the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Is it possible it teleported after Sai used it...? I'm not sure about that anymore.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}That was what seemed odd. Up until that point, everything I'd done that had matched with what I'd already lived through contained a purpose. The clothes, showing myself, the elevator... I hadn't repeated anything without a reason.{w} So then, what was going on? Would I leave the Sekimeiya there to give Sai a way to escape? ...Simply to avoid changing the past?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was weird. Because I had realized it, I had no reason to leave the Sekimeiya in that cabinet. Even though I wanted to hide it far from me, it didn't have to be in hallway B.{w} I didn't want to leave the Sekimeiya there. Aside from the fact that it would be consistent with my experiences, it would only bring negative consequences.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But didn't that mean Sai would still manage to hide anyway? After all, I wouldn't {i}not{/i} be doing it to change the past; disregarding my own interests purely to be consistent with what I'd already experienced wasn't how everything had worked so far.{w} That was what I was curious about and what I wanted to observe from a distance. How was Sai going to escape detection?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Helix
The more I thought about it, the more I believed that leaving the Sekimeiya in the cabinet wasn't the call.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I was sure, I looked at the door. It hadn't been properly closed, so I widened the gap without making a noise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It was as I'd thought. I could see Atsuki sleeping next to the hallway A door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took one step forward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Immediately, Atsuki's eyes opened. Raising his head, he stared right at me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I turned and walked down the hallway to reach the storeroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It really had been me. At that time, I had denied it completely, but the person Atsuki saw was the same me, in a sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: From inside the storeroom, I heard Atsuki slowly walking. He circled the floor until he was back at the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next, they would go to the security room to check the time before going to the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Something had just caught my eye.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The green light was on the hallway's camera...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Shiroya! Are you there!?
entries.speaker: a4

entries.text: It was ridiculous. ...I was, in fact, but I didn't want to be seen. Such a nonsensical prediction had turned out true.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Our old selves walked to the stairs to reach the attic. As soon as they were gone, I left as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd left the Sekimeiya on the crystal room floor, as I hadn't wanted to be seen with it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh. Don't tell me it's already gonna be gone.{w} ...Is this how Sai managed to disappear?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That made a lot of sense, so I sped up. Could he have grabbed it so fast?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: No. ...It's still here.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was behind the door, where I'd left it. Carefully, I picked it up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where should I put it...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Thinking about it, I walked to hallway C, where a sudden sound startled me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh—
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I retreated immediately.{w} ...In hallway A, I'd just seen Sai. He hadn't seen me in return, but something was very odd.{w} He'd been exiting the storeroom with a knife in his hand and was visibly shocked after looking at the stairs, where there was nothing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Slowly, I kept stepping back until I reached the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The sound of his footsteps came from hallway B. Then, he started to open doors.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did he notice me?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: With his free hand, he'd been touching his mouth. He was the Sai who had chased us, and he was about to intercept the elevator with us inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He's the one who said I would die. ...It's the Sai who locked me in the attic.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When he started getting closer, I approached hallway A.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That way, I avoided being seen as I returned to hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai appeared from the lobby and started to open doors in hallway A as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the hell is he doing...? It seems like he's being silent on purpose.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I knew he'd soon go up the floors, so I circled back to hallway B.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My heart rate was increasing. I couldn't feel safe anymore. ...Why had Sai said that I would die, and why had he chased us with a knife?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: His intentions were unfathomably enigmatic. However, I didn't think he'd declared my death because he'd already killed me. At one point, he'd stated that he'd be the one to kill me if he had to.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And the knife he was holding... Where had he gotten it from? There was something to consider.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd seen him exiting the storeroom, but he was searching through hallway A. ...So, he'd been in the storeroom before inspecting its hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Could he have come from the outside door? It can't be, can it? But it would explain the knife and how he was in the storeroom right after I left it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I heard something behind me and quickly hid myself in the cleaning room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who was that?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Someone had been in hallway B. When I considered it, I concluded it had to be Erina.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I froze, wondering if she could've seen me. I still had the Sekimeiya, but I really didn't want to activate it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It seemed I hadn't been seen. I couldn't hear her, but she wasn't coming.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't know what was happening, so I had to stay there. For a while, nothing happened at all.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That changed when someone started to get closer. The steps came from hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Are they coming over here? That's someone else, right?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The sound got louder until it was coming from right behind the door.{w} However, the steps kept going.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This way of walking... It's got to be Sai.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Was he circling the floor again? He'd come from hallway C and disappeared toward the lobby side.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}It didn't sound like he'd looked into all the rooms again, so I didn't understand.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When the silence returned, it stayed for even longer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did he go upstairs already?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What about Erina? That must've been her, but where is she now...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I thought about what would happen next in detail.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Our past selves are in the attic, and they'll try to come back here soon. ...I guess I get how the chase started.{w} I think Sai was searching for someone while holding that knife. I don't know why, but it's very possible he wanted to find Atsuki.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The elevator's on this floor, and Sai went up to search for Atsuki. When we called the elevator from the attic, he was on the third floor and heard it.{w} He probably figured it was empty, especially if he knew it was on the crystal floor. From his perspective, someone called it from the attic and was about to go back down.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's how he intercepted us. Seconds after he heard it, he called it from the third floor, knowing someone would be inside. ...If he was looking for someone in particular, that might be why he wasn't right outside when we opened the door.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...How did the chase go down, though? We locked ourselves in the attic, but somehow he had another key to open it.{w} We thought we couldn't try to lock ourselves in a bedroom because he took the key, but it was still in the drawer when he and I teleported in there later.{w} But that's not all. I found out Sai had the keys to both bedrooms in his pocket, and he even frowned when he saw one was in the drawer. That must be why he didn't take it to trap us... Did he think it wouldn't be there because he'd already taken it?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After trying to escape, we'll all end up in the event room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I should be able to stay here and leave when that happens.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I tried to loosen up. The cleaning cart was gone, so there was room on the floor to nervously walk in circles.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...They should be here soon. The chase didn't go on for that long.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had to attentively listen for our arrival, but my heartbeat wouldn't let me focus.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was late into the day. {time=21} was close to two hours away, and I'd touched the Sekimeiya in the bathroom a while before that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The most important time was approaching, and I had no idea what to do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I perceived the faint, running steps I'd known would come. We were going to the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shortly after they faded, the same sound repeated, and it quickly approached me.{w} It was Sai. He had appeared from hallway B, running into Atsuki.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: To avoid being heard, he slowed down momentarily until he bumped against Atsuki.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They'll... be in the event room for a while. I should be able to leave now.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't stay there, or else Atsuki would see me. Nervously, I turned the doorknob and slowly opened the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The event room was open, and I could faintly hear our voices. I carefully slipped to hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll be fine here.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...It won't take much for Sai to run out. Is it a good idea to try to see where he went?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "If I don't intend to change the past, it won't change." As long as that notion was correct, I could peek out from where I was, knowing I wouldn't be seen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...He didn't have enough time to go to hallway C, did he...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't think so, and even if he had, his reappearance still wouldn't make sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya was getting too hot, urging me to drop it, but I resisted. So close to it, it was undeniable that it had been the emitter of the strange smell.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While I awaited Sai's next move, I looked around me, wondering where Erina and Akaro were.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Prepared to react, I stood in place. I couldn't hear us from there, but I knew I'd notice Sai's escape.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Then it happened. He dashed out of the event room, his swift steps reaching me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As fast as I could, I looked at the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Huh?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Confused, I hid myself before Atsuki saw me. Then, I glanced at the Sekimeiya.{w} ...I still had it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't get it. Why was he not found?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Sai had sprinted straight ahead, shutting himself inside room B4, where I'd just been.{w} Could there have been a third Sekimeiya? If not, his disappearance couldn't be explained.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Ah, no.{w} I think I know what he did.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: At once, I understood what had happened. Sai had merely been playing with us. He hadn't lied about that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}It was absurd, but given his grin, I was sure it was the right answer. Something we'd told him had allowed him to pull it off.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where did you even get that knife!? Did you kill Katei and Erina?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...No. I haven't killed anyone.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Listen, here's a good question for you. I've seen Katei's and Erina's corpses. If I killed them, how come there's no blood on my clothes?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: We told him Erina died, but he knew the truth.{w} Before, when he was looking through the floor, he came across Erina. After that, she woke up and left the room. When I was in the cleaning room, Sai walked through the hallway again. Maybe he was drawn to the sound and saw Erina was gone.{w} In short, he knew she hadn't died and that she wasn't in that room anymore.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That was how he'd thought of a way to outsmart us, just like he said. He ran to that crystal room and covered himself with the curtain to make Atsuki think Erina was still beneath it. ...That was his trick.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I waited for Atsuki to enter the cleaning room and slowly stepped away.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We didn't have time to search this hallway, so I won't be found here.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I returned to the secret section of the cold storeroom. It was around the time Sai and I had traveled to the attic, so I'd soon have no understanding of what would happen below.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After a few seconds, I looked down at the glowing gem. The strong heat around the Sekimeiya seemed to have lessened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did it cool down a little?{w} It's still pretty hot, so it's not like I put it in the cold cabinets. That's weird.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It didn't matter. I knew I had to think. I had to come to a final conclusion...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But it was impossible. The time was rapidly approaching, and it didn't seem like I'd make a decision I wouldn't regret forever.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While the minutes kept passing, it didn't feel like they were to me. I was firmly trapped, with very little time left.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't heard our past selves in some time, so it was likely we'd already traveled.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Someone was walking in hallway A. Since I didn't know who it was, that meant my past self wasn't there anymore.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Who was it? It could've been Atsuki, Erina, or Akaro. Even though Sai had escaped from the attic, I didn't think it could've been him yet unless he traveled to the past.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Soon, identical-sounding steps passed by. They headed up the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They just left the floor. ...I wonder if it was Atsuki.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I wanted to leave, and that was a good time. I hadn't been able to get rid of the Sekimeiya, and I had the opportunity to leave it in the cold.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't see or hear anyone, so I stepped to the event room and slowly looked through the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was empty. Most importantly, the Sekimeiya wasn't on the floor, which meant someone had been there after our travel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It was probably Atsuki.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I moved to hallway B and walked to the crystal room in front.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Next to Naomi's body, the red curtain lay by itself. Without wasting time, I did what I'd planned earlier and left the Sekimeiya sealed away in the very first cabinet where we'd found it. When I closed it, a sound indicated it had locked automatically.{w} The wheel appeared damaged, but it still worked, so I was able to set the temperature to 0 °C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Hm, it might not be a good idea to go back.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Atsuki told me that he searched for me. If he comes from the stairs while I'm in the storeroom, I won't be able to leave before I'm found. ...If I'm here, I can avoid being seen by circling the hallways, like I did earlier with Sai.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I realized something. Up until then, there'd been reasons to avoid being seen. At the point I had reached, however, it wouldn't mean that much.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My past self is in the attic, so as long as she can't see me, it shouldn't matter. ...I can be a bit calmer about that, then.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Technically, I was guaranteed to be seen again—it was what I'd been told.{w} Not knowing what would happen was a little nerve-wracking, but Sai had been one person to see me. There was a bit of time left until that could happen, as he'd been in the attic for a while.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Where the hell are Erina and Akaro?{w} It's been so long since anyone saw Akaro. The one who came to the bedroom wasn't the same one who left with Sai. ...I know he's here, though.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I waited, expecting to hear someone at any point. Until then, the floor seemed deserted.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was minutes later when I turned to the lobby. I felt like I'd heard someone there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is there anyone there? I expected them to come from the stairs.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Seconds passed, and I hadn't heard anything else.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I could've been mistaken, so I slowly stepped to the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...No one.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Had I imagined it...? I entered, drawn once again by the blood ahead. Without a doubt, it was where the bigger pool had been earlier.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...!{w} I didn't imagine it this time. There's someone in hallway A.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I retreated slowly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait. There's someone in hallway B as well...!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I doubted what to do as I approached the mechanical room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I see. This is why I'll be seen. I can't enter either hallway, so as soon as someone comes here, they'll find me. It'll probably happen even if I go down.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}My only move was to wait. When I thought about it, I realized that being found wasn't so bad.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As long as Atsuki was one of the people I'd heard, I could stop worrying about my well-being. If I was with him until my past self left the attic, I knew Sai and Akaro wouldn't be a threat because Atsuki hadn't said that something had happened to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But what would I tell him...? No matter how much I wanted to talk to him, what could I possibly say...?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Atsuki from this morning... where is he?{w} Will I ever find him again? ...He was a future version of the Atsuki here, but how will everything lead into what happened? How will he end up at the beginning of this day?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After my past self traveled to November, could I stay with Atsuki? Even though it was possible the exit wouldn't open, could I just stay with him? According to him, a Shiroya who wasn't the "real Shiroya" would appear. ...Was it possible for me to change reality in a way so that wouldn't occur...?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...The end was very uncertain, even more than the first time I'd gone through it. I didn't know what would happen, what I would do, or what I could do.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}It didn't seem like anything was happening. I'd been expecting either door to open, but a few still minutes had already passed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I know I didn't imagine it. There was someone in both hallways. I guess it's just a matter of time since I know for a fact I'll be seen.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Hm...{w} could it be that I have already been seen? What if I didn't know about it, but it already happened?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It didn't seem likely that I'd just be ignored, but I had no way to know. No matter what, there was nothing else I could do but stay in place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...roya!{w=0.7} Hey!{w=0.5} Wher— ...you!?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Wh—{w} Atsuki?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Shiroya! Can you hear me!?
entries.speaker: a4

entries.text: What's happening...?
entries.speaker: nm
