entries.text: Like a sharp needle, Atsuki's voice pierced into my chest. The pain in those words wasn't one I'd heard before.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You're okay, right!? If you can hear me, please come out! Say something!
entries.speaker: a4

entries.text: In the sudden manner they'd started, the shouts faded with a wail. Then, in their place came a shrill cry.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki was sobbing like a broken person.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With a trembling hand, I grabbed the knob.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I pulled the door open, I saw Atsuki on the floor. He wasn't just crying—he was shaking. He was a wreck.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: H-Hey...
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...My hoarse voice didn't reach him.{w} Gently, and trying not to stagger, I took a step forward.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When he saw me, he gathered himself enough to stop shaking and warily stood up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Are you actually Shiroya?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...{w}I didn't know what to say. When his eyes pierced into mine, any words I could have prepared flew out of my mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-Where were you? What's with those clothes?{w} Are you the same person who disappeared with Sai?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The same person...? I'm not. Not in the sense he means.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It felt like my voice was stuck in my throat, and my thoughts were all over the place. ...Had that exact conversation always happened while I'd been in the attic?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I-I'm sorry... I'm very confused too. ...I-I guess so, though.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: You guess so?{w} What do you mean? You remember everything, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Right now...
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I stopped myself. From hallway C, a figure approached.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Yes?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...It was Erina. The look in her eyes and her way of walking had cut me off.{w} When Atsuki turned around, he hardly reacted, so I was unsure if he already knew what had happened to her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'm glad to see you two are safe. I was a bit worried...{w} Wh-What's with those clothes? You weren't wearing them earlier, were you...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Who the hell are you? Or even you... How can you two exist!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: It was the Erina we'd assumed was dead. Her clothes were stained with blood, and she appeared to be groggy.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where were you? How did you just appear out of nowhere!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: In response to that, Erina slowly knitted her brow.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What do you not understand? Did you just pop into existence at some point?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: No... Why do you think that?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Have you looked at that room? Your body is there.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What...? That one? It... can't be.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I knew you were lying. I-I can't be here, of course not...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...Shiroya, what the hell is happening? Answer my other questions. How can you exist when it shouldn't be possible? Did the same thing happen to Erina?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: To Erina? She should be dead, right?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I stepped to the door. Of course, Erina's body was no longer there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: About Erina, I think what happened isn't what you think.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: That's probably right. I can't think of anything anymore.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...Under those stained clothes, there's no wound, right?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: There never was one. The body you think disappeared is her.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Do you mean that she never died?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I nodded. When we found Erina, the shock of Katei's death was still affecting us. We hadn't checked to confirm her death because we hadn't even doubted it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A-Are you serious...?{w} Were you playing dead, then? Or just unconscious? It doesn't look like you feel very well.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I'm not sure... I remember I was drawn to this room, and then I think I blacked out.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Drawn? By a noise?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: N-No... Something stronger, but I'm not sure what, exactly. I don't know whose blood this is, but since I woke up, I've felt... groggy and numb.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I... see.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I had no idea what that was about. I'd been in the room when she had appeared, but I hadn't sensed anything like that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Shiroya, do you remember finding her body as well? And you realized what really happened? ...You still haven't explained what you're doing here. Are you the same Shiroya who disappeared from the event room with Sai?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I wish I could explain everything to you, but I still don't really know what happened.{w} But, yes. I'm really glad to see you again.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I smiled and felt a wave of relief. It didn't matter that I didn't know why I was there again—those words had been the most sincere of my life.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What's with those clothes, then? Why is the cross not on them? Why did you ignore me when we saw each other in the event room and when I kept shouting your name?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...Well, I—
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Hey... I'm still confused, but I have a question.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...Huh?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The Sekimeiya... does it really make you travel through time?{w} How does it work?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: If I understand it... touching it with your skin activates it, right? And you can go far into the past if it's out of the cabinet for a while.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: That's... what I've been working under, yes.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He looked at me in case I had an objection. Even after everything that had happened, that still should've been correct, so I nodded uncertainly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was thinking. Why don't I just go back in time to save Isla?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Atsuki and I looked at each other, and I wondered about her proposition. What would happen if Erina changed the past? What would happen to the world and to us?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know why I didn't think of it earlier. Someone killed her a few hours ago, so I just have to go to that time and prevent it.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Saving Isla was something I could do. It should've been possible, given what I knew.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I couldn't find the Sekimeiya. I kept looking at Isla's face for a very long time, and she told me that she could be saved. Then, I saw a girl, and after that I heard you shouting.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...A girl? You saw Shiroya?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Um...{w} I guess it couldn't have been anyone else.{w} ...It must have been Shiroya.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Oh, she did? I wonder if she's talking about the time before she fell unconscious, when I was in the crystal room with her.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I also saw what happened to Katei... It looked horrible. Did someone do that?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...It couldn't have been an accident.{w} But anyway, the Sekimeiya's not in the event room.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Are you sure...?{w} Do you know where it could be? I really need to find it.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: No. I suspect Sai or Akaro must've taken it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I knew where one was, but I couldn't bring myself to say it. Once again, the decision of whether to change the past had to be made, and I couldn't do it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Are you lying?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What? No, I'm not.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...{w}Is he not? Who has the Sekimeiya Sai and I traveled with?{w} ...If he does, I understand why he'd lie. Right now, he believes the past can't be changed.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Actually, that's right. He changed his mind on that before I got out of the attic. He said he'd changed the past.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I frowned. ...What exactly was going to happen?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The way you two reacted. You don't want me to save Isla, do you?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: That's not it at all... Remember that Sai and Akaro took the cabinet key. They probably have the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: It seemed Erina was seeing through us. Discontent, she walked to the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I-I knew it! You were lying...
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: You didn't want me to look at the cabinet!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The Sekimeiya's here... Did Atsuki leave it in the cabinet? I don't think he would have.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I looked at him. As I'd thought, he was visibly confused—the Sekimeiya shouldn't have been there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Erina opened the glass and rolled the Sekimeiya into her purse, not wanting to touch it for the time being. Following that, she immediately let the curtain fall back down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After a long silence, the hallway A door opened. When we looked over, someone was stepping into the room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Uh...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: It was Sai. He had already escaped from the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's up?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...What the fuck are you even doing here? Did you succeed with that plan of yours?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh, not quite, unfortunately. I thought Erina was dead. What's she doing with the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You thought that too? No. I'm going to go to the past to save Isla.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Huh. I doubt that. The past can't be changed.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's nonsense! I'm going to the past, so I'll prevent Isla from dying. You've used the Sekimeiya before, right? How long do I need to wait to go enough hours back?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Um... It should be about fifteen minutes, but I still find it unlikely you'll change anything.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai... where the fuck did you go? Were you in the attic?{w} Do you know where Shiroya went? I saw her disappear with you.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Isn't she next to you? What's with those clothes, anyway? Aren't they from there?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...They are.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I see, they're definitely an improvement for you.{w} And just ignore me, Atsuki. I was busy sorting something out.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: "Sorting something out". I couldn't help but react, as I knew he had just locked my past self in the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, right, I'd forgotten about this too.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I found this just now. I tried to read it, but my head hurt a lot. Do you know what it is?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Out of nowhere, Erina took out a piece of paper from her purse and handed it to Atsuki. I saw some black letters on it, but I didn't recognize what it was.{w} Immediately, he stashed it in his pocket.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: H-Hey... What was that?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Don't mind me, like you said.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: You look pretty nervous. I saw something written there.{w} You were pretty in control of things when you pulled off that trick with the key earlier, so why is this getting you all worked up? Do you wanna hide it that badly?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...{w}It's just a personal paper. It has nothing to do with you or the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Very intriguing, then.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...A personal paper? I didn't think I'd seen it before.{w} When I glanced at him, he immediately looked away, leaving me a little surprised.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, did any of you see Miiya...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Wh...
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Who?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You don't know her, right? I... I knew I wasn't going insane.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: H-How do you know that name?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: She's the person I was with earlier, before I saw you two... It just came back to me. I don't know where she went, though.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: What...? What just happened?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's not possible. How could she have seen Miiya!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What's with that reaction? Don't you see she's just delirious?{w} She didn't die, but I have a pretty good idea of what happened to her. Say, did you hallucinate someone?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's not it. That's not just some name she made up.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Do you know this person, then?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...We do, but Erina couldn't have seen her. She couldn't be here.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Are you sure? She could've entered through the storeroom. She could've even traveled from the future since the Sekimeiya's bound to be exposed to the outside world.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's not what she means... She's not anywhere right now.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Oh? Is she dead?{w} ...Wait, Miiya, you said...?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That was the biggest blow I'd been dealt in a long time. I'd grown to think I partially understood what had happened, but a few words were enough to shatter everything.{w} What did it mean? Could it have been another prediction from the world? Had my own decision been handed to me, confirming that I would save Miiya?{w} There was no way—that didn't make sense. If I'd changed the past, many more things would've differed as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...No. She's with us. She has red hair, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...Did you actually see her? What did she say?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: She told me her name, but she didn't look lost or anything. She knew me, too...{w} She just suddenly ran away, and I haven't seen her again. I definitely thought I hadn't seen her before, but I honestly wasn't sure.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...{w}There was no way to make sense of what she was saying. It seemed the structure of the world had been warped beyond comprehension.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know how to interpret this. Did you all agree to make up this story for when I appeared?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Shut up.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Well, I'm trying to figure things out myself and I thought I was close to understanding quite a bit, but now there's a bunch of shit I don't get, and it doesn't feel great.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: You did mean she died, right? Is saving her with the Sekimeiya not an option?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai, shut the fuck up. If it was, I promise you that we would've done it.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Hm...
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Was Atsuki right? I didn't know anymore—I'd never known. Saving Miiya alongside everyone else was supposed to be possible, because traveling days to the past could soon occur. How did that tie into what Erina said, though? There was no longer anything that made sense.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's probably been close to fifteen minutes already, right?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: I'd say so. Yes, it's been almost fifteen minutes since I arrived.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Are you sure I'll go far enough back?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: She died at around {time=14}, right? It should be enough, yes.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Okay. I'm going, then. Are all of you coming with me?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Don't worry, we're far enough from you.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I understand. Well... goodbye for now.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Sai had kept lying to Erina, claiming fifteen minutes was long enough to go hours back. However, I couldn't be entirely sure that was impossible.{w} As she got her hand closer to her purse, the three of us stepped back. Given what we knew about the range, we were outside of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But I was concerned. Were we highly mistaken about how the range worked? I didn't stop retreating until Erina's hand contacted the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And when it did, something I hadn't even imagined occurred.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai was the only person to disappear.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Wait... what?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I was speechless. Erina had touched the Sekimeiya, and we'd been farther away than Sai. It didn't make any sense why he was the only one to vanish.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why didn't it work!? Did Sai disappear?{w} Was everything that he said a lie...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: It was almost laughable. We'd always been so far from the truth.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Admit it... Did you ever want me to save Isla? Were you... Were you involved in the first place!?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: You're wrong. We don't know how the Sekimeiya works, but this shouldn't have happened...
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: No matter what I thought, it didn't make sense. I couldn't even come up with a baseless explanation.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Wait! Where did it go!?{w} It's not here!
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Erina's wide eyes were fixed on her purse. ...It was empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, what...?{w} The Sekimeiya disappeared?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It... teleported.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Perplexed, Atsuki walked to the cabinet. When he raised the curtain, we saw the Sekimeiya sitting comfortably behind the glass.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did it... teleport to the cabinet? This has to be what Atsuki talked about.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Atsuki, tell me... What do I need to do to travel through time?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Exactly what Sai and I told you. I don't know why it didn't work just now.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: No... That's not it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Sekimeiya didn't teleport. ...That's wrong.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I thought back on what had just happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Erina opened the glass and rolled the Sekimeiya into her purse, not wanting to touch it for the time being. Following that, she immediately let the curtain fall back down."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "Perplexed, Atsuki walked to the cabinet. When he raised the curtain, we saw the Sekimeiya sitting comfortably behind the glass."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She didn't close the glass before lowering the curtain, but it's closed right now anyway. ...The Sekimeiya didn't teleport.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I looked at the floor, and my heart skipped a beat. There was no drop of blood.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, the reason why only Sai disappeared...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Can I... not save Isla? Why did it not work...?{w} Oh, of course.{w} What was I even thinking? Traveling to the past isn't possible.{w} You lied about it since the beginning, right? That's why it didn't work: it can't happen. I actually fell for it.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Just wait here. I'll be back in a second.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Before we could react, Atsuki went to hallway B. I left Erina behind and saw him entering the staff room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, was I right? ...But I don't get it. The Sekimeiya shouldn't have been in the cabinet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: He promptly came back out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Did it disappear?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I see. So it is as I thought.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Wh-What did you want to do?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Oh, I'm just wondering about Sai's whereabouts because an extra version of him has existed somewhere in the past.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Did we never see him in so many hours?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: ...I'm not sure, but he has to be somewhere.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: There you are. What were you doing?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Sai appeared from the lobby.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Wh...? What the fuck?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: On his face, there was only shock. I saw it very well, as his eyes were boring a hole through me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Huh?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...!{w} Wh-Who the fuck are you? How are you here?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Before I recovered from hearing that, someone came from the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Whoa! What's this girl doing here!?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: It was Akaro, and I understood. It was the time when Atsuki had seen him again; it wasn't happening for the first time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki! Now you have to answer! Who is she?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...Are you actually acting as if you don't recognize me?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Of course we don't!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Well... No.{w} Of course we do.{w} Aren't you... dead?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Dead? ...When did I die? Did it happen again?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: M-Me...? Why would I be dead?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: And you too, Erina! I thought you'd died!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Wh...? Isn't that what you said earlier?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Earlier? What the hell are you talking about?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...There was no question. That Sai wasn't the same person we'd just been with.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sai, what time is it?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Uh...{w} it's {time=18:43.}
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why? Did you time travel?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: N-No. I didn't.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: He's right, though. Are you a future version of Erina or something?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What...?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Well, you're not dead after all, but we felt your pulse... In any case, I figured you would've come from the future. What even happened to you?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Um... I can't remember much. I think someone hit my head, and I fell unconscious. I don't know what happened before that.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Yeah, that's about what we knew too. Sorry that we can't be of more use.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I don't get it either, but I'm glad you're safe. This means you're not guaranteed to end up dead, but you... What even is your name? How did you get here?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I've been here since the start.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: That's not true.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: ...What? How could that possibly not be true?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Hold on, though... Your name... I think I might actually remember that.{w} Shi... roya, was it? My memories are a little foggy.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: I nodded, puzzled.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I thought so. Like I said... I thought you'd died.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: As you can see, I'm alive.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Do you have a twin, by any chance?
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What? No.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: But, then... It doesn't make any sense. I'm still really confused...
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: What the fuck do you mean you're "confused"!? She just showed up like that! Did you enter through the storeroom?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I've been with you since {time=9}, Sai.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: That's a load of crap. Regardless, you'll definitely die. I'm sorry to tell you like that, but you're not making it easy for us. Atsuki, I know you know her.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I'm going to die? That's not true. It has to be another false fate, spawned the same way as the other.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}I do, and she's telling the truth.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Are you just fucking with me? What's the point of lying so blatantly?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He's... He's telling the truth. Shiroya's been with us the entire time.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: The entire time? Not even you have been here since {time=9}!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: E-Excuse me?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Well, you get what I mean. You don't remember when you got attacked or where you came from very well, right?{w} Of course, Erina and Isla have been here the whole time, but not you.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The Sekimeiya had disappeared as soon as Erina touched it. In the storeroom, the same thing had happened to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked around, wondering where I was.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The camera...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Above the door to the lobby, a camera focused its lens on us. Unlike all the others, no smoke was on its smooth surface.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And the green light isn't there.{w} It's... that world. The one from this morning.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Did you notice something?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Then, that Atsuki... Is he here? When Naomi touched the Sekimeiya, I'm sure he stayed behind.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}I... need to go somewhere.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Wh-What...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I'm sorry, I need to go to the attic.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Before he could say anything, I took off for hallway C.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Please, don't follow me.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: There was a reason I had to do that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Atsuki from that morning... It was very possible he was somewhere, and I really wanted to find him again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The attic had been where we'd parted, but I had to go alone. He was a future version of the Atsuki I'd just been with.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd concluded that two versions of the same person could never interact with each other because it was a real paradox devoid of origin. ...And paradoxes were impossibilities. If Atsuki came with me, it would guarantee I'd never find his future self. In the world we were in, it was very possible the door to the attic had been open, how we'd left it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Going by myself, I could find him. He was the future version of the Atsuki I'd just been with.{w} I'd just told him I was going there, so if his future self was in that world, I knew he would be waiting.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And it would let me verify my conclusion—that there was no past self of mine locked in a bedroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I confirmed I wasn't being followed, I exhaled in relief. I tried to open the elevator, but it wasn't there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I should use it. If he's on another floor, he'll at least hear me.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I pressed the button and waited for the elevator.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once it had come, I stepped inside. The "7" button wasn't available, but I still had the key to the attic.{w} After getting it out of my purse, I enabled the button and pressed it to start ascending.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: On the way, my anticipation compounded, my heartbeat meshed with the slight friction of the ropes above.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Upon arriving, I slowly opened the door, revealing an empty hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stepped out and walked to the turn. As soon as I looked ahead, it was settled: my past self wasn't there, and both bedrooms were open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...But where was Atsuki? It didn't seem like anyone was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I headed to the living room and looked at the floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: These footprints... They're very recent.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, a sound came from the stairs. Fixing my eyes on the door, I noticed it was approaching.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And finally, it opened.{w} The person behind it... Were they the one I wanted to see?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There you are... You did come.{w} I'd forgotten you had the key to the attic.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Are you... the Atsuki from this morning?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yeah. I'm glad I wasn't wrong.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Y-You knew I would be here, right? You remembered what happened.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: He nodded.{w} That was it. I'd finally found him. We just had to stay together from that point on.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What had happened after I'd traveled didn't matter anymore. As long as I stayed with Atsuki, we would be together at {time=21}, which he had lived through once already.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was so relieved, and he looked the same. However, there was something else on his face. ...I felt it was exhaustion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Have you been here all this time? When you disappeared this morning, I tried to find you, but I was in another world, right?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I... think so. I learned a lot of things. It's been longer than you think since I saw you.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What do you mean? You said the recording was real, right? What happened at {time=21}? And why did both of us appear at the start of today?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...Why did we travel to this morning?{w} I know the answer now.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I remember what you told me. You said you traveled to the 30th of November, and that a few days later, you touched the Sekimeiya in the tower. Is that right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Y-Yes. That's when I appeared with you in the lobby.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: No, that's wrong. I know what happened to you.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: For a moment, I was lost. What did that mean? ...What had happened to me?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You didn't go to November... You went to the future.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...Wh-What? No I didn't. I went two weeks to the past.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I don't know why you think that, but I believe you went to the future.{w} You said that you entered the tower in early December. I believe that was the 5th of January instead.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The 5th of January? That doesn't make any sense.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: It didn't... make any sense. ...Did it?{w} The days I'd spent in my apartment. That had been in December, hadn't it?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Like I said, the recording was real. On the 5th of January, we were in the tower. That's why I appeared with you in the lobby when you touched the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: N-No. No. How would I have gone to the future? There's no way.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: With the Sekimeiya. There were two of them.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I... know. I saw that too. What do you mean, though?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I've thought about everything that happened. There always were two Sekimeiya, but only one of them made us go to the past. The other one made us go to the future instead.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The one in the water tank sent you to the future, but that wasn't the first time. ...It wasn't the first time you'd traveled forward in time. There were others.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I was at a loss for words. That couldn't be the truth; it didn't make sense.{w} But... if it had happened before...{w} Earlier, when our past selves had traveled to the attic... I'd pressed the elevator button two times, and only one of them could've caused the sound we'd heard. If we'd appeared in the future instead, that solved it.{w} We'd immediately thought we'd traveled just a few minutes to the past because the handle in the bedroom had been reattached and our footprints were still visible in the living room, but that would've been the case a few minutes into the future too. Was that really possible, though? Wouldn't we have noticed a ton of contradictions?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This will have no impact whatsoever, so answer as you see fit. Where did Shiroya travel?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So you read a story where Shiroya had traveled to the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In reality, she did travel to the future, and just like you, she never realized it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, everything around her pointed at the truth that she failed to notice. She felt free after so long, which prevented her from realizing that she was still trapped.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That was due to her narrow field of view. Just like her, depending on the way things were looked at, you would've been told an entirely different story.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But there's no shame in that. Both of them are just as valid.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Every mystery has been accompanied by the key to unlock it. Shiroya went to the future. That's why the days of the week didn't match December, when the 15th was a Thursday.{w} That's why it wasn't snowing when she stepped out of the drainage channel. That's why, as soon as she got home, she heard fireworks celebrating the new year.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But one time, Darfee told her she could drink alcohol. Given her birthday, that meant she was already twenty years old and legally allowed to drink.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There have been countless keys, but some of them have been much smaller than you might think. However, know they're there and hunt for them. The time where your success will be measured will come, and now it is very close.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So you read a story where Shiroya had traveled to the future.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That was the truth. Everything around her pointed to it, yet she failed to notice it. She felt free after so long, which prevented her from realizing that she was still trapped.

That's why, as soon as she got home, she heard fireworks celebrating the new year.

{cps=80}Everything she'd experienced...{w=0.4} How could it have happened in January?{nw}
{cps=80}It seemed impossible at first,{w=0.3} but she soon realized it wasn't.{w=0.7} Even if that was the case, {w=0.2}though,{w=0.2} there were many questions to answer.{nw}
{cps=80}...So...{w=0.4} what now?{w=0.7} What will happen at {time=21}?{nw}
{cps=80}It'll be fine.{w=0.4} We'll be able to leave.{nw}
{cps=80}Finally,{w=0.3} Shiroya breathed a sigh of relief,{w=0.4} but it was cut short by words she didn't expect.{nw}
{cps=80}This isn't over yet,{w=0.2} though.{w=0.5} We have to do one more thing.{nw}
{cps=80}Shiroya peered at him,{w=0.4} wondering just what he meant.{nw}
{cps=80}...{w=0.1}W{w=0.1}e{w=0.8} are going to save Miiya.{nw}
That wasn't the end for them.
But only the final step was left.
How could that goal be achieved?
Shiroya wondered that as she awaited Atsuki's next words.
Miiya, who had been seen in the tower... How would she be saved?
Shiroya had thought about it for countless hours.
But a way to save Miiya had always meant her own death.
She'd never believed it had been possible... to truly decide between the two worlds.
Would Atsuki come with her?
If they abandoned their world together, maybe it would be bearable.
But she soon learned that he wouldn't.
And that, though it had seemed impossible, there had always been a path toward a desirable outcome.

Failure
In the attic, Atsuki sobbed on top of a bed. He'd seen Shiroya's dead body. She had been killed, next to Naomi.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki couldn't believe the world had suddenly taken such a turn. Shiroya couldn't have possibly died mere days after Miiya. He had been hopeful the previous night—it was absurd for him to think that he was in reality.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But his tears conveyed what he already knew. He would never speak to Shiroya again.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He had run up the floors after seeing the body. The attic should've been locked, but that hadn't been the case. After failing to find who he'd been searching for, Atsuki had collapsed onto the bed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Meanwhile, the tower... was almost empty. Only one other person was in the building with Atsuki.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That person was Sai.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Puzzled, he stepped into hallway B. ...What had just happened?{w} Out of nowhere, the Sekimeiya had disappeared.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He wondered if he'd traveled through time. Even though he hadn't touched the Sekimeiya, something peculiar had occurred.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When he looked around him, his confusion intensified. Naomi wasn't in the bathroom.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Then, he saw the bloody corpse next to the stairs. Erina had died. Going off of the blood, it seemed she'd hit her head on the stairs and tumbled down.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai saw something else. There was no longer a green light on the security cameras. Did that mean they weren't recording?{w} Without a doubt, he wasn't where he'd been a minute ago.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai had recently learned valuable information regarding the Sekimeiya; he was confident he knew more than everyone else. However, he had no clue what had just happened.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He took his time looking through the crystal floor. Someone might've been there, and perhaps the Sekimeiya as well.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He stared into a crystal room. It was where they'd found Naomi's first corpse, but she had also vanished from there, and the velvet curtain, which had been laid on top of her, was attached to its original cabinet.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Deep in thought, Sai walked to room A5, where Isla had died. Lifting up the cabinet's lid, he verified her body was gone as well.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When he looked at the lobby, he was met with Shiroya's immobile body. Next to her was a puddle of blood, and her eyes showed that no life remained within them.{w} Shiroya had been killed... By who, though? ...Sai didn't find anything important among her belongings.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Again, he wondered. Where was he...? The corpses he knew of had vanished, while Shiroya and Erina, who should've been in the attic, had been killed.{w} What did the silence mean? Where was Atsuki and everyone else...? His wristwatch wouldn't help him figure any of that out, so he headed to the security room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But the door was locked.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Had Katei locked it? That seemed strange.{w} Sai wanted to know the time. The bodies vanishing indicated that he was in the past, but the truth couldn't have been so simple.{w} The future, perhaps? Had the earlier crimes been covered up? ...Sai wasn't sure what to think.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Then, he looked at the elevator, frowning in consternation. The button was gone...{w} Nonetheless, when he tried to open the door, it budged.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Inside it was blood and a pile of metallic panels.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was a long time later when Sai stepped into the attic. He hadn't found anyone else, and only the last floor remained. He immediately noticed that the suitcase was gone from the sofa.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But Atsuki's sobs began to reach his ears. His cries came in broken bursts, muffled by the pillow.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...What are you doing?
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Sai noticed that one of the bed sheets was gone. When Atsuki heard him, his head immediately turned and he saw him approaching through his bleary vision.{w} Then, Atsuki's fist flew. If Sai hadn't reacted fast enough, the blow would've broken his jaw.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Wh-What the fuck!?
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Sai felt his tongue. It was bleeding.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Before he could process it, Atsuki struck again. When Sai saw Atsuki's fist had barely missed its full impact, he realized it could've easily just killed him.{w} ...After all, from Atsuki's perspective, Sai had to be the murderer.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Everyone had stayed in a crystal room, and Sai had been the first to leave. Only Naomi should've been outside, but she had been one of the victims.{w} Then, Erina had left, and she had been killed as well. Lastly, after Shiroya's departure, she'd instantly been met with the same fate.{w} It was only Sai who could've done that; the one still alive, who had willingly not returned.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, Atsuki wasn't aware of where he was. He wasn't aware of what the Sekimeiya truly were, as he had never witnessed their powers.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Atsuki's third strike came, it was immediately returned. In Sai's hand was a knife that slashed Atsuki's shirt.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That confirmed it to him: Sai was the killer. He had just tried to make Atsuki his fourth victim.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He felt a chill up his spine. He couldn't die there, not after Shiroya's death, but he wasn't a match against Sai's knife.{w} Before he could swing again, Atsuki ran out of the room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You're not gonna fucking run away!
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Sai wouldn't let him go—not after he'd tried to kill him out of nowhere. On top of that, he was aware of a few things.{w} Nobody else was in the tower. Murders had occurred. The cameras didn't seem to be working. He had a knife.{w} ...He had been handed the perfect circumstances to finally know what killing a person was like.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When he'd cut his shirt, Sai had discerned fear within Atsuki's eyes. He had run away, but there weren't many places where he could hide.{w} Sai had enjoyed Atsuki's presence in the tower, and he was poised to enjoy it even more. Thanks to the knife he had, he could hunt him down.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And at the same time, he felt enraged. Atsuki had almost killed him; he'd almost suffered a sudden, clueless, and pathetic death.{w} His confusion toward the world was gone. In the blink of an eye, Sai's thoughts had shifted drastically.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He grabbed the key to the bedroom. Strangely, it wasn't where he'd left it, but in its original drawer.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Then, he grabbed the one in the other bedroom and removed its chain with a screwdriver. With that, Atsuki had very few places to hide.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The key to the attic had been in the door, and Sai had grabbed it. That meant Atsuki couldn't lock himself inside. The two remaining options Sai could think of were the security room and a bathroom, which could both be bypassed with Katei's keys.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He began to search for him, aware that Atsuki could attack first.{w} In the living room, he saw footprints running out, yet he cautiously looked through the whole floor to confirm Atsuki wasn't still there.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Coming out of the partitions, Sai stared at both bathrooms. He noticed only one of them was closed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I see, so you're here.
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Atsuki, open the door.
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Atsuki!{w} I bet you want to know what happened to Shiroya. Open, you stupid moron!
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: ...Oh, I see.{w} You're not answering...{w} because you're already dead.
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Sai grinned. In the storeroom on the crystal floor, he had found both Sekimeiya.{w} He'd had a reason to hide one while leaving the other there, but what mattered was that he had access to both.{w} That bathroom was where Atsuki had hidden. If Sai went to the past, he could wait for him inside. Hence, on the other side of the door, Atsuki must've already been dead, and a future version of Sai must've been waiting for his past self to leave.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Briskly, Sai ran all the way down. He didn't know which of the two Sekimeiya to activate, but it didn't matter.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Behind the storeroom's wall, Sai hurried to the glowing gemstone, knowing it had been there a long time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki had been in the bathroom on floor 6 since Sai had gone down. He had no idea how much time had passed, but the silence hadn't wavered once.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: How long had it been...? Perhaps two hours.{w} No matter the time, for Atsuki, it had felt like a still instant; Atsuki's mind had been consumed by the persistent image of Shiroya's corpse.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Why had Sai not come back? Had he killed everyone else...?{w} Atsuki was incapable of shedding more tears. He'd been in the tower almost the entire day, and he didn't know if the exit would ever unlock.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He wanted to leave the bathroom. Putting a firm end to Sai—that desire spurred him onward.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What if the police couldn't prove what he'd done? Exploring that thought for a second almost broke Atsuki.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He had to find Sai before the police... but he was wielding a knife, and Atsuki didn't know where he was.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Finally, Atsuki was able to reach the doorknob. He didn't think he had decided, but he couldn't stay there anymore.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai hadn't been waiting for him outside. The floor was as desolate as it had sounded.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki had heard him going down the stairs hours before. The red around his eyes had mostly faded, and they were otherwise empty. Slowly, he descended to the fifth floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But the Sai he was searching for wasn't there. He wasn't anywhere in that building.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When he arrived at the lowest floor, he was drawn to the open storeroom beyond Erina's lifeless body. There, he learned of its secret.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The movable wall was open, showing the way to the hidden corridor. Behind it, a strange light came from the floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki didn't react, but he crouched beside it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When he placed his finger on it, he retracted it immediately. He'd been burned, and before he could be surprised, the lights went out. Both the faint glow and the room's; the movable wall had closed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Astonished, Atsuki looked back. The wall was in place, and where there'd been a soft glow before, there was nothing.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He stood up and walked into the darkness. Immediately, he encountered a door that he couldn't open: its handle was missing.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He stepped back to the wall that had closed. It didn't seem to have a handle either, and he couldn't get it to open.{w} For an instant, Atsuki thought he'd been trapped, but he soon felt the area that allowed him to open the hidden wall.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the hallway, Atsuki stared at the stairs in fright.{w} What was happening to him? Erina had just been there, hadn't she? Yet she no longer was, and the sea of blood there had been reduced to a single droplet.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When he looked at the other side, the sensation persisted. The event room had been open before he'd entered the storeroom, but it wasn't anymore.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Nobody was in it, but the same glow lay on the floor near the cabinet. That was when Atsuki understood what it had been: the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As he crouched next to it, he shivered slightly at both the temperature of the room and how odd everything was. Could the Sekimeiya really have disappeared when he'd touched it? And why had he been burned? He still felt it on his finger.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Carefully, he reached out to it with his left hand.{w} Again, as soon as he contacted it, the gemstone disappeared and he felt a painful burn.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki was lost. Was he delusional? ...He couldn't convince himself that was impossible, but he'd seen it clearly: the gemstone had vanished.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He looked around, almost beginning to cry again in desperation. Hopefully, Shiroya's corpse had also been a hallucination, but he couldn't bring himself to verify it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He staggered to hallway B. Perhaps Akaro and Isla were still in that room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: They weren't. The room was empty.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The lobby door wasn't closed, but Atsuki quickly looked away. Instead, he went to hallway C, wondering if Erina had truly disappeared.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...She had. She really wasn't there.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki had failed to notice another change earlier: the elevator button. ...It was attached where it should have been on the wall.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He pressed it softly, causing the burn on his fingertip to prickle painfully.{w} Long seconds later, the button's outline flashed orange.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hesitantly, Atsuki tried to open the door.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At {time=21:04}, the shutter opened.{w} A group of policemen had been in front of it, awaiting that time. As soon as the glass came into view, they saw the figure of a young girl lying next to a puddle of blood.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, they couldn't rush in. An unknown gas was quickly detected inside the building.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When they were prepared, the team raided Ashiya Tower.{w} The girl in the lobby was young and had blue hair. She didn't have an open wound, so the blood next to her was strange.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On the other side of the door was another body. Along with a much larger pool of blood, an older woman was found. She had hit her head on a step, dying instantly.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What exactly had happened during the twelve hours when the tower had been sealed off? The officers were speechless as they stared at the corpses.{w} However, that was nothing compared to what awaited in hallway B.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Dimly lit, its entire floor was red. It took a moment for the first officer to realize that it was blood, not lighting.{w} Then, when he saw its source, the wind was knocked out of him.{w} He froze, knowing that would be the most gruesome image he'd ever see—the sad remains of what had once been a human being.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the middle of the hallway, by the door of a crystal room in the right wall, was the origin of the blood.{w} It wasn't a body. It was only half of one.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The other half was beyond the door, as it had split it in two.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The officer stared at it while his heart hammered. It looked like a young man.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: They raised the curtain to the Sekimeiya cabinet. As Ashiya had feared, it was empty.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Lei had let them know about the Sekimeiya's appearance and about the necessity for cold. They knew the Sekimeiya were two identical egg-shaped stones.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It didn't take long for them to be found. One was in the storeroom, behind a secret wall. The other had been hidden inside a crystal room in hallway B. As instructed, an officer brought them to their cabinet, but he felt something strange. Through his protective suit, he noticed one of the stones was hot. The other, however, was not.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Even when the police climbed to the highest floor, no one else had been found.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The team exited and reported their findings. Three people had been found dead, zero alive.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It didn't make sense; at least five were missing. Thanks to the entrance tickets, they knew the names of the people who hadn't been found outside.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: While the citizens learned the tragic events that had transpired, the bodies were identified.{w} The girl in the lobby was Shiroya Mirana.{w} The woman beside the stairs was Erina Majutsu.{w} And the body split in two was Sai Yomiya's.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There was a secret corridor in the storeroom that Ashiya didn't know about. When the police learned it led outside, a single conclusion was drawn: the missing people had left through it minutes after the attack. Since then, all sides of the tower had been observed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So... what had happened inside? Who had killed those three people?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The building was raided a second time. If someone was still there, they had to be found immediately. Every possible spot was inspected.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On the crystal floor, a member of the team entered the elevator. Blood and metallic panels were on the floor, but his attention went higher.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was the only remaining place in the tower. With the tools he'd been given, he unlocked the hatch on the ceiling to look into the narrow elevator shaft.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When he pulled his head up through it, he saw a face before his eyes.{w} It was that of a young, unconscious boy. Blood issued from his mouth in a thin stream.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The officer placed his hand under the boy's nose; he was still breathing. He gently shook his shoulder, but there was no response.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He was unsure how to safely remove the boy from where he was or how he'd even gotten there in the first place. The full extent of his injuries was also an unknown factor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He called for help, and a team of men slowly and gingerly extricated the boy shortly afterward.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki Hakutoki. That was the name of the person who'd been found above the elevator.{w} Hours after his rescue, he regained consciousness. At first, he sounded devastated due to the death of his close friend. However, as he continued to be questioned, his answers only grew stranger.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He didn't know how he'd ended up in the elevator shaft, and the events he described didn't make sense. According to him, the missing people had been in the building for hours, which the police rejected immediately, as there was no way they would have been able to escape through the secret door.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He didn't have a valid explanation for any of the deaths. No clues at the crime scenes pointed to their truth, and no video footage had been recorded. Quickly, the possibility that Atsuki was lying was presented—only he could've committed those murders.{w} He must've been lying: none of what he'd said could be the truth. However, nobody could be completely sure. Sai's death... It hadn't been natural.{w} How would Atsuki have killed him? How would anyone have killed him like that? And how would Atsuki have ended up unconscious above the elevator?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And, admittedly, there was a point of truth to Atsuki's words: the blood in the lobby.{w} Next to Shiroya's body, there'd been a puddle of blood, which was confirmed not to match with any of the bodies present.{w} Could it really have been... Naomi's? The corpse Atsuki swore had disappeared...?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The backlash Ashiya received was immense. They had allowed a tragedy to unfold on their own property.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After the attack, the tower didn't open again. Containing countless mysteries and an unknown gas, it was closed indefinitely.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And eventually, Ashiya's voice faded. There was nothing they could do anymore.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Many weeks had passed since December 15th. Lonely, Atsuki looked at the sky through the glass of a window.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He could not yet believe what his life had become, and imagining the worst years ahead of him, he could only cry.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The sky he saw... He wasn't happy he could still see it. He wanted it to disappear.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And it did.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Through the glass of a window, the cloudy sky could be seen.{w} However, no one was there to see it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Around the country, some people had the opportunity to witness the disappearance of countless citizens.{w} Speechless, they walked to where everyone had been... In the blink of an eye, the streets had become desolate, and even some cars had disappeared.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The news was heard across the world: every being within an immense radius had vanished—almost a third of Japan was gone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was humanity's most shocking event ever recorded. In a mere instant, millions of people disappeared without a trace. What had occurred was far beyond anyone's understanding.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You might know what was in the center of that radius.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A little town on the foot of a mountain range, called Yushibana.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Then, everyone traveled through time. That must be what you're thinking.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, not one of the people who disappeared reappeared anywhere. The instant they vanished, their existence was {tip=disappearance}erased forever{/tip}.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: First Cause Dilemma
Airun was covered by a vast cape of snow. During the winter, Calliant were the only flowers that had survived the climate, and they encompassed its entire spectrum of flora.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A member of a large range, the mountain extended behind Yushibana, its perpetual snowy top reaching higher than the others.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Years had passed since it had last been visited. It had long ago been said that only its neighbors were holders of innumerable gemstones.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On its base, different species of Calliant peeked through the snow. After so long, however, they were accompanied by something else.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Human footprints. Marked on the ground, they wandered about.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Far from them, a man walked on the snow. His name was Gan, and in the distance, he could see the mountains he'd often traveled through.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was the first time he'd brought his equipment to Airun. He'd always been curious to know whether the common belief about it being devoid of value was true.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And, after hours, he had verified it. He hadn't found any caves, and the surface had been harder to traverse than Airun's neighbors.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Disappointed, he walked back before the sun set. He'd been out all day, and he was exhausted.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He was walking down a narrow path when something caught his eye.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He'd already crossed the treeline, so tall trees were surrounding him. He stopped himself when he noticed an opening between two of them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Intrigued, he walked over to it, and as he got closer, he realized what it was.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: An entrance to a vast field of grass, enclosed by the trees that hid it from view.{w} However, what truly stood out was farther ahead.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There was a wooden cabin. In the corner of the field, it lay covered in white.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Speechless, he was drawn to it.{w} The grass was tall, and it had almost been concealed by the snow. Slowly making his way inward, Gan didn't take his eyes off the cabin.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He'd never heard about it, and it looked abandoned. Many questions came to him, but they all suddenly vanished.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He looked at the ground. On top of the snow, he'd almost missed something that easily blended in.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Was it... an egg? He crouched by its side and felt its surface. Strangely, no snow was on it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When he touched it, his face was one of amazement. It was incredibly smooth, but it was heavier than it looked. He'd never seen anything like it in his life.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What was it, and why was it there? Gan didn't care and was eager to bring it home.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It looked like a gemstone, but it hadn't been underground. Content to have found something, he kept walking toward the cabin.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The door was open, so he took a look inside.{w} A few spiders had set up shop there. Most of them had died out during the winter, but their webs still decorated the room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Gan didn't dare look down into the storeroom. The last thing he wanted was for some large spider still living down there to be disturbed by him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As he'd expected, it didn't seem like anyone had been there in a long time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The 27th of November was a Sunday. That was why Gan had chosen it to go to Airun.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Late into the day, he arrived at home. With one hand, he unlocked his front door.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He stepped into his shop, Musashi Gemstones.{w} He left his discovery on a stand and hurried to turn on the heater. Then, he grabbed the phone and dialed a number he had memorized.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Lei! I'm sorry to call you so late. Is this a good time?
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: What do you want?
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: I just found something that will interest you. You have to see it.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: Is it about a gemstone?
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: Y-Yes, but it's not a normal one. I found it on Airun, and it's unlike any I've seen.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: ...Is that so?{w} If you're not exaggerating, you might be in luck.
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: I'm not. I'm certain this would fit perfectly in the tower.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: Is it all right if I come tomorrow? I want to speak to you about something.
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: Yes, that's perfectly fine.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: I'll be there in the afternoon, then.
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: Thank you! I'll be waiting.{w} Good night.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: The call cut off.{w} Gan pumped his fist in relief. It had been a while since he'd struck a deal with Ashiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He sat on his chair. He was tired, and he had to think about what he'd say the next day.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A while later, he raised his head. He had noticed something.{w} A smell he hadn't perceived before was in his shop.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He couldn't discern what it was, but he slowly walked over to the gem he'd brought.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Was it the source? He got close to it, but he suddenly retreated.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Then, carefully, he placed his hand on it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...{w}It was hot. Very hot.{w} Why? It had been cold before. Why had its temperature changed?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Concerned, he grabbed it.{w} He examined it closely, but there was no explanation for the temperature change. What could've caused that? And most importantly, would it ward Ashiya off from buying it?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He stepped out of his shop. Outside, it had remained cold.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And soon after he did, the gem cooled down. In the blink of an eye, the warmth around it had faded.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Was it the surrounding temperature? No matter what, it hadn't seemed normal.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In awe, Gan stepped back in, letting the heat make contact with the gem.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Immediately, he noticed the change. The smooth surface began to heat up exponentially.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What did he have in his hands, exactly? How was such a rapid change in temperature occurring?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And would Ashiya be against taking such a thing? Gan began to worry.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He remembered that a long time ago, Ashiya had sold him storage cabinets, and one of them had been equipped with temperature regulation. Biting his lip, he went to his storage room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: One of the dusty cabinets had a wheel on its side. He dragged it close to an outlet and plugged it in.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The temperature in Yushibana was around 0 °C. Matching it, he rotated the wheel and brought the gemstone there.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After leaving it inside, he waited for the temperature to stabilize.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And when it had, he touched the gemstone one more time.{w} All warmth was long gone, and the smell had also faded.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was bizarre, but Gan's mind went again to Ashiya. What would they say about something so peculiar...?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Tired, he went to his bedroom. He knew he would fall asleep instantly.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He was still in his mountain equipment—jacket, hat, and gloves—so he hurried to take them off.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The next day, Lei came to visit Gan, who had been preparing what to say.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After a warm welcome, she was brought to the Sekimeiya—that was the name Gan had chosen for the gemstone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As soon as Lei saw it, she let him know Ashiya were interested in buying it. It had taken a lot less convincing than Gan had expected.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Lei let him know the reason. Ashiya had been searching for a unique gemstone, and the one he'd found would serve that purpose well.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Gan and Lei had long ago agreed on a standard starting sum per gemstone, which Gan couldn't pass on. However, he hadn't yet mentioned what he'd found out about the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Yesterday, I noticed the heater's temperature might've damaged it. That's why I've got it cold right now.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: Oh, it's cold in there?
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: ...Yes. I advise you to do the same. The lower temperature seemed to immediately alleviate the problem. It's currently set to 0 °C.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: That's fine. We can do that.
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: Good. Just in case, I would suggest you not touch it while it's not refrigerated. It's delicate, so I wouldn't risk it.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: Lei silently nodded.{w} Gan took a deep breath. If Ashiya did what he had instructed, there would be no problem.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: We'll deal with the paperwork, then. You know the usual.{w} We'll be here this Wednesday. Is {time=21} a good time? Sorry if it's too late, we're pretty overloaded.
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: Yes, any time is fine. I'm still open at that hour, so I'll have everything prepared.
entries.speaker: gan

entries.text: Perfect.
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: Both of them bowed, and Lei calmly exited his shop.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Gan woke up, he didn't open the shop. He'd been thinking that something else could've been on that mountain.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The gemstone he'd found... Why had it been there? Snow had fallen days prior, so why had none been on it?{w} Had someone dropped it there? Someone who knew about that place?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Ashiya paid well, so Gan hadn't stopped thinking about going back to that grassy field... Was it possible he had missed something?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When he spotted the familiar opening between the trees, Gan deviated from the narrow path.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Once more, he saw the short cabin. It was two days later, so his footprints had almost fully disappeared.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He scanned the terrain, slowly stepping forward. He noticed something and hurried over to it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A section of white stood out, but it wasn't snow. He approached and slowly reached down.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was another gemstone, identical to the one he'd found.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Gan searched through the entire field, but he found nothing else.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At home, he called Lei and told her about his latest discovery. When she heard it looked the same, she sounded interested.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, there was an issue: Ashiya had already revealed the Sekimeiya's existence. On that day, the primary announcements had been made.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You know what? This might be great.{w} You remember what I told you, don't you?{w} We're keeping the details of the Sekimeiya a secret, and this could be something perfect to reveal on the day of the event. We'll buy both of them.
entries.speaker: lei

entries.text: There were many things Lei hadn't told Gan, but that was the truth. If Xyn didn't make their move before the 15th, Ashiya could justify part of the build-up on the existence of two identical, paired gemstones.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That is why, until that day, most people who uttered the words "the Sekimeiya" weren't aware they were referring to two gemstones at once.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Corrosion Fatigue
In a small town encircled by mountains, a house stood out from the others. It was surrounded by an empty field, and it was often referred to as a mansion.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Nobody truly knew the family who lived in it, but the numerous nasty rumors about them were known by all.{w} For a long time, they were believed to be secretly authoritarian. However, crimes had recently started to be linked back to them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When the afternoon came, a swarm of students exited the single school in town. It was starting to get cold, so most of them walked home.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the mansion's living room, a thirteen-year-old boy named Kyuuka sat on a large sofa. It was his favorite spot, the most comfortable place in his own world. Idly, just passing the time, he watched whatever was on television by himself.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Most days, he would come home from school and do that. In the past, he had sometimes played with friends, but he had distanced himself from them as time went on.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Solitude was his preference. The lesson he had taught himself from years of exposure to others was that they weren't worth his time, and so once in a while, he wouldn't go to school for the simple reason that it was too much of a bother.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: His parents were upstairs. He had, over time, picked up on what their "business" entailed, but the details were neither accessible nor relevant to him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Kyuuka heard the door open. When he glanced over, he saw his older brother stepping in with a girl he'd never seen before.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Who's that?
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: She's a friend of mine. I'm just going to show her the house.
entries.speaker: nn

entries.text: Without saying a word, she was brought upstairs. Kyuuka saw it as none of his concern at all. In his eyes, she was either somebody related to his parents' business or just another source of entertainment for his brother.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When night had come, he hadn't seen anyone else.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After making his own food, Kyuuka walked to his bedroom. He couldn't easily fall asleep with things being so noisy, so he covered himself with the sheets.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The next evening, watching television as usual, he saw a familiar face. A girl had disappeared in the town where he lived.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Kyuuka wasn't remotely surprised. They didn't operate in shadows; there was no need to do so.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...She was the daughter of someone with strong ties to the town's leadership. That made sense. His brother was just carrying out something that was both productive and fun for him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hours later, his older brother came down from upstairs. He looked cheerful and left after silently waving to Kyuuka.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He'd learned the girl's name: Anora. It made no difference. Regardless of her name, she was locked in the same room as always.{w} Soon, he heard plaintive cries coming from above.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Kyuuka responded by turning up the volume.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Eventually, his brother came back with some bags he hadn't left with.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A day had passed with no minute full of silence. In the living room, Kyuuka tried to ignore the muffled noise. Whenever those situations occurred, he went to school just to get away from it for a while, but he had to come home eventually.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He didn't like it. He knew that girl was suffering, and he didn't want that.{w} However, he wouldn't talk his brother out of it, and he didn't want to annoy him. Furthermore, the room upstairs was always locked, and he couldn't bring himself to let anybody know.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She hadn't done anything to deserve it, presumably. Few of the people his brother brought home gave him that impression. He didn't think of himself as a bad person, and would have helped her if he could, but that was a mere notion. It wasn't realistic enough for him to act on.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That was why he'd always stayed aside, quietly sitting on that sofa.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But his mind suddenly changed when he saw something he hadn't seen in a long time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was a key.{w} When his brother had gone up loaded with what he'd bought, he'd left his keys in the keyhole.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Kyuuka silently stood up and walked over. He looked back, confirming his brother wasn't coming.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Then, he detached one of the keys from the ring and stored it in his pocket.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Beyond the wooden ceiling, she continued to yell. On some level, such barbarism disgusted Kyuuka. He was getting tired of it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sighing, he lay on his side to muffle the sound entering at least one of his ears. He'd endured louder, and for longer.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Part of him really did wish to take action for once, whether it was from the presence of the key or not. It had been ages since he'd had a conversation with his brother, but at some point, a part of him had come to revile his sibling.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He asked himself a question. Was it worth doing something?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Answering that was difficult for Kyuuka. He didn't like people. They were rude, selfish, and just too much effort to deal with. If any of them had cared about him, he might have thought differently.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On the other hand, he knew that he'd barely tried to speak to anyone in a long time, and his brother wasn't exactly deserving of anyone's attention, let alone approval.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: His parents and his brother—his whole family—was composed of deplorable individuals. He saw himself as different. It wasn't his choice to hurt people, and he would have actively stopped it if he could.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So, given the fact that he could, it only made sense to do so. When he thought about it like that, he came to a decision.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The next day, Kyuuka stayed home. As soon as his parents left the house, he went up the stairs.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The phone was there. Quietly, he dialed the police's number.{w} When they picked up, he anonymously revealed Anora's whereabouts, claiming to have heard yells coming from the house. Then, before his brother could hear him, he slipped back to his sofa.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There was no way out for his brother. He hadn't asked about the missing key, so thanks to that, he knew Anora would be found.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Many years earlier, Kyuuka's parents had added a secret to their house. An entrance, or exit, nobody would notice. Kyuuka had seen it being used a handful of times.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The rumors about the mansion were known by the whole town. The first time that someone had disappeared, the police had quickly shown up.{w} Yet, thanks to that well-hidden exit, Kyuuka's brother had avoided being caught.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Kyuuka knew that when the police appeared, his brother would try to escape with the girl. However, with the key that he had taken, that would be impossible.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hey, Kyuuka. What was that?
entries.speaker: nn
