The first mystery regarding its whereabouts already pointed at the truth that more than one Sekimeiya existed.{w} ...After all, when Sai left the storeroom, he made me touch it, and nothing happened.{w} It was definitely the third Sekimeiya—the one that had disappeared from the event room the first time. The Past Sekimeiya was in room B4 since we'd regained consciousness, so we never actually found the one that disappeared first.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Who hid the third Sekimeiya in the storeroom? That happened before Shiroya, Akaro, and I walked down from the sixth floor.{w} I don't believe it was Katei because he's likely the one who hid the two working Sekimeiya. If he wanted to also hide the third, which was originally in the event room, he would have done so while we were asleep.{w} I don't believe the other Naomi would have wanted to leave it there either.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There's one last likely candidate: Sai.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After Katei said that Naomi didn't want to return, the others investigated the crystal floor while Shiroya and I waited next to the elevator on the fourth floor. We were told exactly what happened.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Sai guarded hallway A from the stairs while Katei guarded hallway B and the lobby.{w} As the hallway B rooms were inspected, Sai could've gone to the event room to take the gemstone and hide it in the storeroom.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, he let the others discover that it had disappeared and asked Akaro to go find us.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When they came and told me what had happened, I thought you two had to get down here. Since we're dealing with this situation, I found it appropriate to join up and make sure nothing slipped away.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Why would he have done that?{w} ...At that point, we hadn't learned about the Sekimeiya's powers yet.{w} During the morning, Sai's attitude was different from how it was later. He often talked with me about what he thought and was visibly enjoying what was happening around him. When did that change, exactly?{w} I believe it was when we found out about time travel. He became a lot more reserved and hard to read. If he hid the Sekimeiya so early, his motive likely aligned to his original attitude.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The event room and hallway A weren't being recorded. He chose the storeroom, another place without cameras. Later on, he acted as if he'd found it there, so I don't think his intention was to keep it.{w} Did he do it for fun, or did he have a better reason? In any case, it's likely he already knew that he would point the finger at Katei, who he immediately accused.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So, going back a little, when we found the Past Sekimeiya in room B4, we thought it was the one that disappeared from the event room. After putting it in the cabinet, we split up and searched both hallways for the person who'd made a sound. During that time, the Past Sekimeiya was hidden somewhere else while the third Sekimeiya was in the storeroom.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It must've been Sai again. The only choices were the people in hallway B.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I was told Shiroya and Akaro looked through the rooms while Sai watched the hallway like I did. We had to make sure the person we were searching for was found, so the search took a while. During the time Shiroya and Akaro were inside the crystal rooms, Sai had the chance to pick up the key in room B4, take the Sekimeiya from the event room, and then hide it somewhere in hallway B.{w} After that, he slipped the cabinet key into Shiroya's purse as soon as possible.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: By acting like he'd found the Sekimeiya in the storeroom, he removed any potential blame from himself.{w} I didn't really think about it, but he said we couldn't trust Katei's search and never ended up looking at all the other rooms Katei went through.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And still, I'm sure there's another reason Sai did that.{w} I don't know why, but everyone thought only one Sekimeiya existed. By finding the one that didn't work, he made sure we wouldn't search for the one he had hidden.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I see... That must be the answer to that question.{w} "Why is the Sekimeiya being hidden when it can easily be found?"{w} I wonder who knew the truth. I wonder who knew that three Sekimeiya existed.{w} The people who did kept hiding them because leaving the third one in the event room cabinet meant no one would look for others. The quality of their hiding spots hardly mattered—we just found one Sekimeiya and thought that was it. Maybe they were often poorly hidden precisely so that we'd find one and stop the search before coming across another.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Akaro knew it from the beginning, and Sai learned it shortly after. They knew two real Sekimeiya existed alongside Xyn's fake. For twelve hours, they had a plan in mind: to keep one of the real Sekimeiya hidden.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If that was achieved, Ashiya would find two Sekimeiya, and they wouldn't search for the second real one. That was how they intended to pull it off and why they didn't want anyone else to know the truth. The Sekimeiya were hidden countless times, but the intent was rarely to keep them from being found.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: We still hadn't found the Naomi who'd made the sound, which meant that she had successfully escaped upstairs. That's why we searched through the higher floors.{w} Shiroya and I stayed on the fifth, and although we didn't hear anything, something strange happened with the elevator.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Sai heard it three times. Based on that, it started from the crystal floor, which was not where we'd last left it...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't believe Sai lied. Something happened during that time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's because in the event room, we heard another sound. It was the bathroom's door closing.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, inside it, we found Naomi's second body.{w} However, I later traveled forty minutes to the past and appeared on the crystal floor before we'd all come back down.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I kept a close eye on the bathroom, but nothing happened until Naomi entered it...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: First of all, why was Naomi not found? We inspected every floor but the attic. As I now understand the attic's footprints, I don't believe that Naomi went back there. Especially because she didn't have the key to unlock it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Somehow, the search failed to find her.{w} A different person stayed on each floor, so it's possible one wasn't investigated—the floor the person who used the elevator was supposed to guard.{w} ...Erina and Isla were on the second floor. Sai was on the third floor. Akaro was on the fourth floor. Shiroya and I were on the fifth floor. Katei was on the sixth floor.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The strongest candidate to consider is Akaro.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We told him we'd left the elevator on the fifth floor, but for some reason, it was originally below Sai. If he called it from the fourth, Sai would've heard it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, he used it to go to the crystal floor... Why, though?{w} I can't help but remember that it was him who proposed this arrangement. He wanted us to stay separated between different floors, leaving the crystal floor vacant.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Later, he would've gone back to the fourth floor, and finally, he would've sent it to the fifth, where it was supposed to be. Shiroya and I wouldn't have noticed that.{w} It definitely ended up there: Sai confirmed it when he called it from the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't get it, though. Why would Akaro do that? He knew his trips up and down could be heard, didn't he?{w} And Erina and Isla didn't hear the elevator even once. I suppose it's possible Akaro stopped on floor 2 and then used the elevator to the crystal floor if he knew that wouldn't be heard, but if that happened, surely he would've done the same on floor 3 so that Sai wouldn't hear him either...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Akaro had seen that one of the real Sekimeiya had been hidden in a cabinet with a damaged temperature wheel. It had changed colors, so he knew it wasn't the one Xyn had created.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Naomi A was going up the floors ahead of them, but she stopped on the fourth when she realized that was where Akaro would remain. She wanted to collect herself enough to talk to him; her shock at what Katei had done hadn't faded at all. ...However, before she did, he was gone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Akaro had a bad feeling. Something very strange was happening with the Sekimeiya, so he needed to see the cleaning cart for himself. When he did, he saw that the one he'd hidden was actually gone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Who had taken it? Not only the one in the cart, but also one of the two Akaro had left in the event room before lying on the floor. Silently, Akaro continued watching Katei, but it could've been Naomi as well.{w} Katei was acting like only one Sekimeiya existed, and Akaro didn't know the reason. It was rational to conclude that one of them being in a cold cabinet indicated the other was as well.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: During the previous search, he had looked through that room. He knew there was another cabinet that had been set to 0 °C.{w} The other real Sekimeiya was there, and it was all he needed. He only had to keep one hidden, but there weren't many places he could think of.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He took the Future Sekimeiya out of the cabinet. When he did, it turned gray immediately, but nothing happened to him. Did it really have time travel powers? He had a hard time believing that, but it had just changed colors before him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In a rush, he chose to hide it in the men's bathroom. Inside the water tank seemed like a good idea.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When I was staring at the bathroom door, Naomi appeared from the other side of hallway C. She likely came from above.{w} She was the Naomi who'd appeared in the attic, but her actions differed from the Naomi who'd been killed. Why? Why didn't she ask to talk to Katei? What was she doing, exactly, moving around through the building?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "Akaro's description of Naomi's face fell short of her actual expression. She was visibly terrified, breathing heavily, moving oddly, and stopping in place every few seconds."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I saw her face, there was no doubt in me that she'd seen her own dead body. She was avoiding being found, perhaps because she knew what her killer had done to her.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What was she doing, then? When she made the sound and when she walked to that bathroom...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'm not sure, but... she was killed right there. Naomi said a few words before her body was pulled in.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When Naomi entered the bathroom... someone else was there.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, when I approached it, my footsteps were audible: her killer slammed the door shut and locked it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: However, they couldn't have left before the point we all unlocked the door. They absolutely had to have disappeared from the bathroom.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: How? When I inspected it by myself a bit later, no Sekimeiya was there. I don't believe it was taken out before that point either.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When that Naomi was killed, the third Sekimeiya was still in the event room. It's very likely the other two were hidden somewhere on the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Did someone travel through time, bringing along Naomi's killer? If that's what happened, unless the Sekimeiya was on the second floor, I would've traveled too.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I think the answer is different. I believe the Sekimeiya was inside the bathroom even though I didn't find it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After killing Naomi, her killer activated it. I had already run away, so I didn't travel.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: They traveled to the future. After all, I'm pretty sure the Past Sekimeiya was in one of hallway B's crystal rooms, which is where Shiroya and I later traveled from.{w} Maybe I should've pieced together the reason why no Sekimeiya was found in the bathroom...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A while later, right after I couldn't find anything inside, I heard a sound coming from hallway A. It was Sai.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: He had traveled from the future, and in his hip pack was a disabled Sekimeiya that he didn't know about.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: He appeared with it—if that was the Future Sekimeiya, the one in the bathroom would've disappeared! It would have instantly teleported. I should've made that connection.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So, the person who traveled to the future... who was it? Who killed Naomi?{w} Knowing all of that, the answer has to be Akaro...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When I approached the bathroom, the door was slammed. I knew the whole floor was about to be inspected, so I ran up the stairs.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, eventually, the others walked up—they'd found the attic key.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: As soon as I could, I went back down. I tried to find Akaro, who had suddenly disappeared from the group. ...But I couldn't.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stopped myself when I saw the bathroom's door. It looked identical to how we'd seen it with the group when we found Akaro behind it, and I realized it had been me who'd left it like that. I concluded that no one else would touch the door.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And it never happened. I watched from a distance for minutes, and when the group came from the attic, Akaro was already there. I can only think he teleported inside.{w} Why didn't he leave, though?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's gotta be due to the mental state we found him in. He looked out of it and unresponsive, likely because he had just killed a second Naomi who couldn't have existed.{w} After locking the door, he touched the Sekimeiya in the bathroom and went some amount of minutes into the future. Seeing as he appeared in the bathroom, it makes me think it was him who hid the Sekimeiya there in the past. That's why he knew where it was and why he rapidly activated it in an attempt to escape.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But that doesn't explain the whole set of events. After we found Naomi's second body, we suddenly lost track of Akaro. We even looked all over the floor, but he wasn't anywhere, and Erina said he hadn't gone up.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The only explanation for all of this is that he traveled to the past. Later, he even admitted to having touched the Sekimeiya.{w} That makes a lot of sense. If Sai hid it in the crystal room that Shiroya and I later traveled from, we would've gone much more than forty minutes into the past.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That makes me think that Akaro saw through Sai. Maybe he was aware that more than one Sekimeiya existed.{w} If that was the case, from his point of view, only Sai could've hidden the Past Sekimeiya. He knew the one we found in the storeroom wasn't the same one, so it wouldn't have been too hard to find out where it was. I remember that Shiroya found it quickly because she noticed a slight bump in one of the gem cabinets.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: He traveled to the past, which is why we didn't find him. I'm not sure what led him to do it, but that reset the Sekimeiya's timer, allowing Shiroya and I to only travel forty minutes back when we found it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Later, Akaro said that upon touching the Sekimeiya, he teleported. However, he assured us he hadn't traveled through time.{w} He said he'd seen us searching through the floor, but he was probably referring to the search from minutes prior.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Specifically, when we went up the floors and the three elevator trips happened. It's also the time where he I think he stored the Future Sekimeiya in the bathroom, so seeing his past self might have drawn him there.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't know why he killed Naomi, but this has to be the truth. ...Was murdering her the cause of the state we found him in?{w} When we saw him, the first thing he did was ask Sai for the time, and when he heard it, he said that he hadn't traveled through time—that he'd only teleported.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Wouldn't this explain it?{w} He went minutes to the past. I could probably calculate the exact amount, but that seems unnecessary.{w} There, he killed Naomi and immediately went to the future when he heard me approaching the bathroom.{w} If both travels were similar in length, upon being told the current time, he would've thought that he hadn't traveled through time at all, especially because he appeared in the bathroom when he went to the future. He barely moved, so there was no way he'd earlier gone to the past...{w} But there seemed to be more to it than that. Akaro's voice seemed deeper in denial.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: In the bathroom, when the door opened, what Akaro last expected was to see Naomi lying on the floor again.{w} He had been incredibly worried that she'd seen him missing in the event room. If that had happened, she was a massive threat.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, out of nowhere, she had appeared dead in a room. Akaro, much to his own disgust, was relieved by that.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Yet, for some reason, it hadn't ended there. Once he had progressed to different worries, Naomi had appeared dead a second time.{w} Akaro had no idea what was happening inside the tower. He only wanted his plan to succeed in order to have a future ahead of him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Why was the bathroom suddenly empty? Where had her body gone? ...Could he really have gone to the past? The last time, the Sekimeiya had merely changed colors when he'd touched it, but that time, he appeared in hallway C.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The third time he saw Naomi's face, her eyes were staring into his. It couldn't be real; he doubted the stability of his own mind.{w} When her mouth opened, the words Akaro had been dreading entered his ears. She knew he had left the event room, and she knew that he'd been concealing it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Akaro lost himself in desperation. Naomi should've been dead—he couldn't comprehend how she'd come back. After a single, abrupt motion, she was on the floor, unresponsive.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Immediately after that, Akaro heard footsteps approaching from the hallway. He was barely able to make them out over the violent drumming in his ears. As fast as he could, he slammed the door and frantically looked around him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When I realized one of the keys the first Naomi had was the attic's, we went there for the first time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Sai pointed out that Naomi's footprints didn't make sense, and we found an empty suitcase on the sofa. ...It was the same one we saw in hallway C—it had come from another world alongside Naomi.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's likely where she was keeping the Sekimeiya. To change worlds, both had to be powered on, so they didn't travel with Naomi. That's why the suitcase was empty, and it's why it wasn't in the attic in this world.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And now that I think about it, someone reacted differently to both suitcases.{w} Katei.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Before we entered the attic, when Katei went to grab the bathroom key, he brought the suitcase in hallway C to the security room. But he never did that for the one in the attic.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Why...? That makes me think it's because Naomi brought it up there. That one wasn't a threat to him because he didn't know anything about it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We didn't find anything else of importance in the attic, so we went down to find Akaro. He was in a crystal floor bathroom and told us to leave him there for a while.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We ended up going back to the top... and in one of the bedrooms, I noticed the voice recorder in Isla's purse.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Now I know a lot more about the audio that we heard, but why was it there? Why did it travel to the past?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Can I figure that out? How did the recorder from the future end up on December 15th?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Thinking about it, it's very unlikely the device traveled to December 15th.{w} Isla said it was impossible someone dropped it in her purse, which means it was there when she entered the tower.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If that's the case, why did she have it before December 15th?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I think... I know the answer.{w} It has to be due to her "friend".
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Now I know that her friend was a version of her from another world. She met with our Isla quite a while before December 15th. She knew about the attack, so she traveled to the past at some point.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Apparently, when Sai and Akaro escaped from the attic, they met with "Isla". Even Erina heard her from the bedroom. She was dead at that point, so she probably wasn't the same Isla we'd been with.{w} Despite that, we never found her after we left the bedroom, so one explanation is that she traveled to the past at around that time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: She went many days into the past, and the location where she appeared had to be identical to where she'd be in the proportional future. That means days after December 15th.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So, what happened to the device after it recorded the audio? Isla saw Sai hiding it, and she ended up with it.{w} If the replicated location was from a time where she still had it in the future, she would've appeared with it in the past.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Isla's "friend" had the recorder days before the event; that's how it got to the past. ...Why was it inside our Isla's purse, then?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I can't know that, but it's likely the recorder appeared inside her friend's purse. Then, both Islas tried to hide the existence of the "friend" from Erina.{w} Two identical purses were in the past. There was probably a mix-up at some point, like the original Isla mistakenly taking the wrong purse on the day of the event for some reason.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't think I need to know exactly how it came to happen, but it had to be Isla's friend who caused the recording to exist in the past.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After we listened to it, Shiroya and I left the attic alone. Going down the floors, we came across Akaro, who kept walking up. Then, on the crystal floor, we saw that the Sekimeiya we left in the event room was no longer there.{w} Someone took the third Sekimeiya out of the cabinet. ...Who would've wanted to do that?{w} At first glance, Akaro seemed to be the only candidate. However, I know someone else was there.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Shiroya and I found the Past Sekimeiya in a hallway B crystal room, unaware that it wasn't the same one that had just disappeared. That's most likely where Sai chose to hide it a while earlier.{w} What stands out to me is that he chose a room with functional cameras after previously leaving it in the storeroom. I wonder if he was forced to or if he had a reason, because it happened when we were searching both hallways...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It had been there since the previous time the Sekimeiya had disappeared, so it's worth noting that it wasn't found when we looked for Akaro, especially since he would've left the glass open after traveling.{w} ...Recalling how that search went, though, I'm pretty sure I get why that happened.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We activated it and went forty minutes to the past. Thanks to that travel, we learned about the existence of the range.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After appearing in the security room, I witnessed what happened to the second Naomi. Then, I heard someone in hallway A: Sai.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: He was supposed to be in the attic. It's indisputable that he traveled through time. Due to his wristwatch, I'm sure he came from the future.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Much later, he admitted to remembering the time I'd seen him, so it was definitely the same Sai who told the people in the attic not to follow us.{w} The way he traveled to the past confused me for a while. That's because he was surprised to see me; he didn't know I'd also traveled. If he traveled after Shiroya and I returned to the attic, he would've had to fake his surprise upon seeing me.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: You perfectly remember when we went up to the attic to get the lithium battery, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Of course.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: How did you do that?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I said you're incompetent, but at least you're doing your best, unlike the others.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: That's my answer. I suppose it just appeared impressive from your point of view.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: How did he travel before Shiroya and I returned? The others said he was there the whole time.{w} ...Is that really the case, though?{w} Shiroya told me what she heard when she was listening to them.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Yes. He was leading the conversation, telling everyone not to follow us down. Akaro was there too, and he confirmed that he saw us. Sai told them all to wait for us because we'd be responsible for anything that happened after leaving of our own volition...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...I see. So he wanted the others not to come down.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: He kept saying it. He never left, and the elevator was still there with the door open. The conversation started winding down, and when they talked about going to the bathroom, I left right away so nobody would see me.{w} I stayed in the living room for a couple minutes with the doors closed, but I think that they all took that time to go to the bathroom, so I started going down again to find you. I looked through every floor until I saw you right as I was about to start with this one.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That was all Sai needed to trick the others.{w} Everyone went to the bathroom, so when it was his turn, he could've gone to the crystal floor. He had hidden the Past Sekimeiya, so he traveled after us when it had already gathered a lot of energy.{w} There was something curious about Sai's behavior. He kept insisting that he hadn't traveled to the past, and he was in a rush. He tried to run away from me twice.{w} That's probably because he had to be ready to go back to the attic. As soon as his past self "went to the bathroom", he returned as if nothing had happened, which made the others say that he never left the attic.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't know about the actual specifics. Shiroya said it was possible she missed him when she was inspecting the office rooms, but when we returned to the attic, we didn't see Sai's footprints in the living room...{w} That's strange, since I don't think he could've taken the elevator back up. The key was in the attic's door, and he wouldn't have appeared with it, so he couldn't have activated the floor 7 button. Furthermore, it should have been disabled in the attic anyway.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'm not sure if this is exactly what happened, but maybe when Shiroya was in the attic, Sai, claiming to go to the bathroom, sent the elevator to the crystal floor and called it. Then, he went to the bathroom.{w} Afterward, he took the elevator down. If Shiroya was still in the attic, she wouldn't have heard it. Sai traveled to the past, and that's where I met up with him.{w} Entering the elevator on the crystal floor and waiting for his past self to call it was one route back to the attic.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't know if his plan went this far or if I'm missing something else...{w} Maybe he did all of this just so he wouldn't be analyzed for what he wanted to do. He set it up so that Shiroya and I would be much easier to suspect.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But again, what about the cameras? They would've recorded him going down.{w} Later, he voiced his thoughts regarding that—he didn't think the recorded footage would ever see the light of the day. As far as he and the rest of us knew, the killer had willingly recorded themselves committing crimes.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What was it he wanted to do? He'd hidden a functional Sekimeiya, so I bet he wanted to know whether he'd really travel through time with it.{w} He took the third Sekimeiya away from the cabinet even though it was him who found it for us...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And the Future Sekimeiya... He appeared with it in his hip pack. I think he was genuinely surprised about that.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, when he ran away from me, he hid the Past Sekimeiya somewhere else. He knew I'd traveled through time, meaning that I was aware of its whereabouts.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There is one detail I'm still struggling to understand.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The screen on his wristwatch was blank. The fundamental answer behind that has to be the replicated location upon traveling to the past.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But, even if the watch looped through time infinitely and didn't just crumble into dust, why did the date go up to the year 9,999? There's no chance the battery would've lasted that long, and it was swapping it for a new one that let the watch work again.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The answer to that is clear: it's because a new battery was added before the location to be replicated took place in the future. Thanks to that, if the watch looped infinitely, the addition of the new battery would let each instance add up more time without the battery ever running out.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: However, this brings about another issue. Why didn't the watch work in the past?{w} After all, it worked again when we added the new battery. This means that minutes later, during the future location, the watch should've been working. It seems to be an impossibility that it wasn't working in the past, given both locations are supposed to be the same.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Is there an answer to this? One that makes sense?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If Sai traveled a second time before the future location, the battery would've instantly run out. However, I have no reason to believe that occurred. I think the answer could be something else.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If Sai swapped back the batteries before the future location, it would explain the broken watch in the past. However, I have no reason to believe that occurred. I think the answer could be something else.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Now that I think more about it, it could be due to the lithium battery itself.{w} It was in the attic, a place that's been abandoned for many years. It was, I have to assume, a battery that the Ashiya family had when they lived there.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Lithium batteries discharge something like 2%% of their capacity every month. When we put it in the watch, it was probably almost entirely discharged.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The small energy it had was enough to let the loop cap the timer at 9,999, but it also ran out before the future location.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We eventually learned that, in the lobby, Sai asked Katei for another lithium battery. At that point, I don't actually think he should've traveled through time again. That happened because the battery we'd obtained from the attic had already run out.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}But does this really make sense, or am I missing something crucial? I just remembered...{w} Sai must have synced his watch to the computer after we saw the "9,999" date since it was working when Shiroya and I returned to the attic. The time would always have been set to that specific point before reaching the end of the loop, so it couldn't have kept counting up...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Would the date have been able to reach "9,999" anyway? In the end, I'm not really sure I understand how that happened.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...After Shiroya and I reunited outside the security room, we went back to the attic, where we were told we'd been downstairs for fifty minutes. ...There, Sai's watch displayed the current time, but that was because he had seen it in the security room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We explained everything. Most importantly, the Sekimeiya had disappeared from the event room. That's why we went to the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When we got there, Sai was already gone.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We were fast enough to see him in front of the cleaning room, where he'd hidden a Sekimeiya.{w} I thought something then...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "Shiroya was looking around while I questioned Sai's ambiguous action. If he'd concealed the Sekimeiya in that room, I wasn't sure why he left upon realizing that we'd seen him. He had the opportunity to give up, but instead, he left for hallway C."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He likely wanted to travel through time, probably because he knew we were about to search the floor. But even though we'd seen him, he still had another Sekimeiya hidden somewhere else. In fact, at that point, he should've known where all three of them were, and he went toward hallway A...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And out of nowhere, I teleported. Shiroya saw the Sekimeiya's glow within the cleaning cart and made both of us appear in the attic.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: At the time, we thought we'd gone to the past. That's not what happened, though.{w} We recognized our locations—we'd been there half an hour before we'd traveled. That means we went half an hour to the future.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The staircase door is open, so this is past the time we unlocked the attic. There are a bunch of footprints next to the door, but I don't see ours. This must mean that you and I haven't gone down yet.{w} These are probably the ones that we left after going back up, when we found Akaro in the bathroom. We're not before that point since there are too many.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That was a big misinterpretation.{w} We were told what caused those footprints. It was the search that occurred after Isla went missing; the ones Shiroya and I had left were long buried.{w} They were all slightly faded too. There was no chance we'd just traveled a few seconds back, which led me to be pretty certain of the time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: How is that possible, though?{w} We heard a sound coming from the bedroom where we'd been. Who the hell was that? Nobody should've been there, right?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We hid ourselves, thinking we were escaping the sight of our past selves. ...It appears that didn't actually occur.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And in the second level of the opposite bedroom, both of us fell asleep.{w} When we woke up, we had no idea how long we'd been there for. That's why, when we were told the time, we thought we'd slept for quite a while. In reality, the main reason a lot of time had passed was because we'd gone to the future.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't believe it. We'd really misunderstood so many things.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When we woke up, we had no idea what transpired on the crystal floor. Tired and still uneasy about our nonexistent past selves, we went to the living room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Did we leave it like this?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: "We were used to looking at the footprints in front of the door, but that was no longer possible. The door was closed, and the movement of it had erased every single footprint nearby, creating an empty arc."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We must have. This means that the group already left, though.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: "Even though the motion of the door wiped out the nearby marks, there were many around the entire room. They were much fainter than the last time I'd seen them, but I was still able to recognize that new ones existed."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The new footprints weren't from the time we walked to the crystal floor. ...Who did they belong to?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...That was simple to solve—the remaining few gaps in that puzzle were all part of the same piece.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When we came down, we saw that the cleaning cart had disappeared. What was strange was that the Sekimeiya was in one of the buckets which had been below it.{w} But that wasn't the Future Sekimeiya; it wasn't working.{w} Why was the third Sekimeiya there? Had it also been in the cart when we'd traveled? Shiroya said something else was there, but would the third Sekimeiya not have disappeared with the cart? ...And she said it was a dark object.{w} I'm not sure, but I think I can guess what happened to the Future Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When Shiroya used it, the Future Sekimeiya remained in the cleaning room, but we only found the third Sekimeiya, which we decided to leave in Naomi's locker before going to the lobby.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There, Sai explained what happened while we were absent.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: He pointed out the fact that he was the first person to enter the cleaning room after our disappearance. Since we had followed him there, he knew it was possible we'd traveled.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "Sai, showing the strongest reaction, approached the room while letting out a conspicuous grunt.{w} He opened the door and stayed still for some time. Then, he entered the small space. Before the others had time to wonder what he was doing, he exited and told them that it was empty."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The powered-off Sekimeiya was there, and he put it in his hip pack. That's why he had appeared with it in the past...{w} In the cleaning room, the others were distracted by the missing cart, and Sai pointed out the third Sekimeiya in the bucket.{w} I'm still having trouble understanding the cause behind some of these details, though. He was only able to obtain the Future Sekimeiya like that because he had appeared with it and had hidden it in the cleaning room... This seems to be an event with no origin, so perhaps it's an indication that something else happened on top of it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "It was Sai who first questioned its status, as it somewhat contradicted a few things they'd concluded earlier. It was white, instead of the gray color they thought it'd become after teleporting two people and a whole cleaning cart."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Akaro saw us enter and never leave the cleaning room—they knew we traveled through time. However, there was another disappearance.{w} Katei's.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The remaining people searched through every room on the crystal floor, but they didn't find us.{w} When they were about to go up, Isla walked to room A5. That's when she fell into a cabinet and disappeared.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...I wonder what happened.{w} The cabinet she looked into is one that can be seen from the stairs, where she and Erina were waiting.{w} During the period Sai and Akaro investigated the rooms, I'm sure Sai quickly disposed of the Future Sekimeiya. That makes me think Isla saw him do that through the door's gap...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What happened to her, though? I don't really have any good idea.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The situation around her death was inscrutable, so I thought further ahead for the time being.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When the others saw Isla disappeared, they were unable to find a Sekimeiya in room A5's cabinet.{w} I'd bet it was powered off, and there was very little light. Since Sai knew the Sekimeiya was there, it wouldn't surprise me if he grabbed it immediately before the others saw it. I'm not sure about that, though.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Everyone thought Isla had to be somewhere in the building. That made them search through every floor, but nobody was found.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Isla wasn't found. Katei wasn't found. Shiroya and I weren't found.{w} Of course, we weren't found because we were in the process of traveling to the future. What about Katei, though?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't think Katei could've been found either.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Before we traveled to the future, we saw Sai in front of the cleaning room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "I wasn't sure what Sai planned to do, but we'd seen him standing in front of the door. Shiroya and I entered while Katei continued toward hallway C in pursuit of him."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When we traveled to the future, Katei was actually very close to us. We went half an hour forward, so I'm sure the range picked him up.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Half an hour earlier, he, Shiroya, and I were in the attic, so that's where we appeared in the future. Katei was in the rightmost bedroom.{w} He suddenly teleported there and left the room, disoriented. He's the one we heard approaching the door when we were in the hallway and who left the newer footprints in the living room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After failing to find anyone, Erina, Akaro, and Sai gave up and moved back to the lobby.{w} There was only silence for a long time until they heard a sound from hallway A.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was Katei. He had walked down after appearing in the bedroom, and Shiroya and I were about to fall asleep.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Where did you go...? We searched for you.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: "Sai shot the first question, and an immediate answer came that left the three of them unsatisfied."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I don't know. I think I experienced what Atsuki said... That teleportation. I've been searching for you.
entries.speaker: k

entries.text: Then, they looked into the cabinet where Isla had disappeared.{w} She was there, already dead. The Sekimeiya, meanwhile, was nowhere to be found.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After they waited in the lobby again, Shiroya and I appeared. We told them they hadn't found us because we'd been sleeping in the attic.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Understand that what you've told us is that you two spent all this time asleep in the attic. Despite this, you weren't found.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...You didn't find Katei either, so you obviously didn't do a great job. And you were in a rush, so you kept yelling Isla's name while quickly looking. I bet you didn't look at the upper levels of the bedrooms, which is where we were, and since we were asleep, we didn't hear you.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: This only made sense from our point of view, but Sai never denied it.{w} Why? There's no way he really didn't look at the upper levels, is there?{w} Perhaps that was the first indication he had that traveling to the future was possible, and he consciously chose not to let us know. Since he should've been in hallway C when Katei disappeared, I wonder if he turned around and realized what had happened to him too.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: In any case, when we went to see Isla with our own eyes, there was a major distinction: the Sekimeiya was there, emitting a faint glow.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What the hell happened? That Sekimeiya was working, and we had hidden the third one in Naomi's locker. ...How did that one appear back in the cabinet?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't get it. I don't know what happened to Isla.{w} Is there a whole other factor that I'm missing about this? Did something else occur that I don't know about?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Isla disappeared from the cabinet, but how? Did she go to the future? ...The Future Sekimeiya should've been powered off since we had just used it.{w} Even if that happened, did she reappear in that same cabinet, where she'd gone to look?{w} Why, though? She wasn't there in the past, was she? And why did she die?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Right, she yelled before falling in. What the hell does that mean? Did she go to the past?{w} Before, Sai had kept walking toward hallway A—perhaps he put the Future Sekimeiya where he had the past one, for whatever reason. Since the future one should've been powered off, Isla would've actually traveled back in time and not changed worlds. I can't know if the search took long enough for it to power back on, though.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But... that still doesn't make sense, does it? If she saw herself, what happened to her other body? Why the hell was it even there? And if both Sekimeiya were active, she should've changed worlds... Also, I know Sai could only put one in his hip pack, so the other would've been seen.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Most importantly, the Sekimeiya reappeared in that cabinet later. ...Did someone do this?{w} Or was it all an accident that didn't involve a murder?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It's possible someone killed her, but who? Who would've had a motive to do that? Who could've done that?{w} There was a whole search, and the Future Sekimeiya had just been used. It's possible a killer with an elaborate plan carried this out, but that's completely out of place.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...I don't believe she was killed. Her cause of death was one of the strangest details.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It's tough, isn't it?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What happened to Isla? Under the right circumstances, touching the Sekimeiya ended her life.{w} It wasn't an instant result, however. The complexity of what occurred might be a bit more involved than what you're imagining, as no world switches factored in.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The cabinet, both Sekimeiya, everyone's actions... Everything contributed to allow Isla's tragic demise.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This riddle will be left all to you, but know something:{w} when Isla looked into the cabinet for the first time, she saw the body of a young girl. It was her own, but that was far from her interpretation.{w} Inside the cabinet, she saw the image of her friend. Her mind and body both teetered on the edge, and she screamed as she toppled into that sarcophagus of a cabinet.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But if she wasn't killed, I don't know what could've happened... There are too many aspects that I don't get.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was frustrating. I'd had the information to solve everything so far, but I was lost when it came to Isla's death.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wish I could know what happened to her. She died right there, and she never revived. The Isla in the future wasn't the same person...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I looked at the voice recorder. The minutes had been ticking along, so I felt slightly rushed.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hated having to move on, but her death seemed to be surrounded by too many questions for me to solve.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Afterward, we simply stayed in the lobby.{w} It didn't look like any of us had the strength to stand again, but that changed when Katei and Sai left out of the blue.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Both of them said they went to the bathroom, but it's clear that's not what happened.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When I thought about it, I realized I could draw a solid conclusion.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya that appeared next to Isla's dead body was working...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I think it was the Past Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's because I put it in the Sekimeiya cabinet, and when we locked ourselves in the attic, it was still there.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We were told that when Sai and Akaro escaped, Akaro forced Sai to tell him where he'd stashed one of the Sekimeiya. At that point, he touched it and appeared in January, meaning that the one in the event room was the Past Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And there is something strange about this. If I'm right, Sai hid the Future Sekimeiya immediately after Isla's disappearance. This means that when Akaro touched it, it had already gathered energy for a ridiculously long time. A lot more than what I believe he needed to travel 21 days.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After Katei and Sai left the lobby, Shiroya and I came across an empty cabinet in room B4 that was set to 0 °C. That's what reset the stored time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'm not sure what happened exactly. Maybe Katei found the Sekimeiya and put it somewhere cold, but Sai saw that and removed it. The cabinet would've taken a bit to cool off, but a few minutes had passed...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After that, Shiroya discovered the storeroom's movable wall and the door with no handle.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: At the time, I was certain that secret place had been used by the culprit to escape the multiple searches we did.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't think it was ever used by anyone who didn't want to be seen, though.{w} I saw a single set of fingerprints, identical to the ones I saw this morning. ...Since this morning, no one had opened that door from the hallway.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Katei had the rusty key, and it fits the keyhole of that door. He definitely knew of its existence.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And immediately after that, Erina proposed that we confine ourselves. That's what led us to wait in the attic's bedroom, leaving the Past Sekimeiya behind in the event room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That marked the halfway point of our imprisonment. From there, though, everything only got crazier.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Despite our efforts, Sai and Akaro managed to escape. I wouldn't be surprised if they left the way I imagined it, with a thought-up loop.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I attempted to replicate that idea, but it didn't work. At the time, I thought of a number of reasons that could've prevented my success, but now I can think of even more.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: First off, at some point, Akaro traveled days into the future. It's possible that even the Isla from another world traveled days into the past. If I'd walked to the crystal floor, maybe I would've been involved in one of those travels.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Secondly, my idea was to leave, travel to the past, unlock the door, and reenter the bedroom immediately after my departure. That meant that my future location would've been in the bedroom, so I wouldn't have been able to appear outside it in the past.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Lastly, my plan entailed using the Sekimeiya we had hidden in Naomi's locker. It was the third Sekimeiya, so I highly doubt it would've ever worked.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After both of them left, an Akaro with different memories showed up. Even another Isla was there.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What happened outside the bedroom? I only have Akaro's version.{w} He touched the Sekimeiya Sai had hidden, and went to the fu—
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Wait, what the fuck? This doesn't make any sense.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...More than twenty minutes had passed, so it was safe to step back into the kitchen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How did I not think this through? There's no way we went to January 5th.{w} For that, we should've been in the tower 21 days before the 15th.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Akaro's clothes changed. I can't rule out that he was in the tower in the past. Our clothing didn't change, though. I certainly wasn't here in the past, so if I traveled 21 days to the future, I should've appeared far outside the tower.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What the hell...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That broke my entire train of thought. It was a major contradiction regarding what I'd concluded.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What happened at the end of the day?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: 21 days before the 15th... That was November 24th.{w} I was not in the tower at that time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I wonder what would happen if now I travel back in time to that day and go to the tower. ...I don't think that would explain it either.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Needless to say, that won't happen. It would mean that Sai and Erina would have to be there as well...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What the hell is this? How is it possible that we traveled to January 5th?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Is there another way? Could anything explain this...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I thought about our last minutes in the tower, right before {time=21.}{w} What exactly had caused the travel?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: One of the Sekimeiya was kept cold in the event room, which means that it was likely the Past Sekimeiya. The Future Sekimeiya must have been somewhere else, and it made us travel through time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But the replicated locations don't make any sense...!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had to think about everything that had happened during the last segment of the day.{w} When I did, a possibility came to mind.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We were definitely on December 15th. The call with Suripo should confirm that. Then, given Isla's words and the evaporated water, I'm certain that we arrived on January 5th.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: By simply thinking about what happened during the last stretch, an obvious problem immediately comes up: we shouldn't have been able to travel 21 days through time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A bit after {time=20:30}, we found the powered-off Sekimeiya in the water tank, and we left it in the cold cabinet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Then, we found Shiroya in a hallway A crystal room. I don't know who she really was, but she convinced me to wait in the lobby for the shutter to open.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Something I felt iffy about occurred then. Erina left, saying she was going to search for Sai. Later, when she came back, it sounded like she'd traveled through time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The Sekimeiya wasn't in the cabinet. I couldn't stand it anymore. I felt like everyone was lying to me.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I searched hallway A by myself and found a Sekimeiya in the security room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What's strange is that the Sekimeiya was scalding; it didn't make sense for Erina to have recently used it.{w} That makes me think it wasn't the same Sekimeiya that had just disappeared from the cabinet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After I found the Sekimeiya in the water tank, something about Sai also seemed off.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...{w}We still haven't searched the whole floor. I'll go leave the Sekimeiya in the event room, and we won't move it again.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...There's nothing else to find, is there? Do you seriously believe Shiroya will be here? We've already found the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: "I stared at Sai's eyes, a little disconcerted. His voice sounded noticeably more nervous and tense than it had recently."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Is there something else to find here?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm? What would that be?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: He knew there was something left to be found—the Sekimeiya in the security room. He didn't care that we found one, but he was worried we would find the second one...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What's most important is that after I found it in the security room, I put it in the cabinet. But mere minutes later, we supposedly traveled to January 5th.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: This seems impossible. One Sekimeiya had just been taken out of the cabinet while the other one had just been left inside. There was no time to build up the necessary energy to travel 21 days through time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If the Future Sekimeiya was put in a hot place during those minutes, it could've gathered enough energy. However, that wouldn't explain the replicated location: I wasn't in the tower on November 24th.{w} So there is necessarily an answer that explains both mysteries at once.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Could it really be what I'm imagining...?{w} Before the exit unlocked, the Future Sekimeiya was activated. I believe the location where that happened is a very important detail.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It was in the mechanical room. That's where the Future Sekimeiya was at {time=21.}{w} And it was Erina who activated it. She was in the mechanical room when the lights went off.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: She still wanted to go to the past; she never stopped saying that. It was her last chance to do so.{w} Before then, she used the Sekimeiya we left in the cabinet. However, when she came back to the lobby and asked us the time, she had gone to the future instead. Based on what happened later, that had to be the Future Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Even so late into the day, Sai was still trying to keep the Sekimeiya hidden. He knew one was in the security room, and when Erina traveled to the future, it was his chance to take care of the other.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Erina came back, asking for the time. That's when we went to the event room and saw the empty cabinet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "I noticed the brief instant in which Erina's expression showed surprise. She was still in hallway B, staring at her left."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you see something?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh?
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: "I walked up to her, but I found nothing that stood out in the hallway."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...What she saw was Sai going through the mechanical room. That's where he left the Future Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Or do we use these last minutes to find Sai and the Sekimeiya? If he took it, he must have something in mind, and as much as I want to get out, I'm not fond of letting him do as he pleases.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Y-Yes... Maybe we should search for him.
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: Search complete. You all did an amazing job this time.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: But that's not all. Before, Erina noticed the mechanical room had been opened. That makes me think Sai was down there and came out when we went to the event room.{w} He knew I'd purposely left the cabinet unlocked. If he later hid the Sekimeiya in the mechanical room, he was probably scoping it out ahead of time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After that, Sai didn't waver as I looked through hallway A. He knew I would find one Sekimeiya, but not the one he'd just hidden.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Once I put the Past Sekimeiya in the cabinet, all of us, including Shiroya, went back to the lobby and kept waiting where we'd been before.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Erina didn't speak once. She knew the Sekimeiya Sai had hidden was still under us, and she was waiting for it to gather energy.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Before the exit unlocked, she disappeared from beside us—she went down to activate the Sekimeiya one final time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And she did. The ceiling of the mechanical room is very low, so the range encompassed us too, the people sitting right above it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Why did we go to January 5th, though? If that was the case, the range should've picked up everyone who'd been waiting outside the tower.{w} ...Somehow, Shiroya knew the travel would occur, and she ran away from us to avoid being involved...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But why? Why 21 days into the future?{w} On the surface, it seems like Erina activating the Sekimeiya would never result in that. However... I think I can tell what the answer is by simply running through what would've happened after she touched it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Sai frequently told us the current time. When Erina made us travel to the future, the Sekimeiya had gathered power for about fifteen minutes. At that point, we already knew that would result in roughly twenty minutes traveled.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So, we traveled twenty minutes to the future.{w} What would the locations have been?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Twenty minutes before the travel, Sai was in the mechanical room while Erina and I were in the lobby, sitting in the same spot.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What occurred relied on Sai's location upon appearing.{w} By that point, I had also learned that fifteen minutes stored resulted in five minutes of the Sekimeiya's recovery phase. After Erina touched the Sekimeiya, it spent five minutes off and then gathered energy for fifteen more minutes until we appeared.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When we appeared, Sai was in the mechanical room, where he would hide the Sekimeiya. So the instant we appeared, he activated it again.{w} ...I'm not sure how that happened fluidly, but I can think of a couple things that make a lot of sense.{w} Immediately, we went twenty more minutes to the future, and when we appeared, the Sekimeiya had gathered energy for another fifteen minutes.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That time, the locations were from the time Erina had touched the Sekimeiya. In other words, she was in the mechanical room while Sai and I were in the lobby.{w} So, we went twenty more minutes to the future.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It's incredibly unlikely that the time matched up exactly and perfectly replicated the instant in which we had appeared twenty minutes before. However, it's possible that location was what we defaulted to, as it was the closest location in which we "existed". That's all I can really assume there.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Again, when we appeared, it was Erina who instantly reactivated the Sekimeiya. This created a never-ending chain of twenty minutes jumping forward.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Only two locations alternated: the one in which Sai was in the mechanical room, and the one in which Erina was. Meanwhile, I was in the lobby regardless.{w} This explains why I didn't see the sudden, instant flashing they talked about.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: For some reason, on January 5th, the tower was empty. Katei told us once that the lights turn off every night and are manually turned on in the morning. So, if nobody was in the tower in the morning, the lights would've remained off.{w} However, before all the lights turned off permanently, every twenty minutes, Sai and Erina alternated between being in the lobby and in the mechanical room. Although it lasted an instant each time, due to the darkness in the mechanical room and the light in the lobby, they perceived a "flashing light".
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: On January 5th, the chain stopped. I don't know why, but we broke free of it, effectively traveling 21 days into the future.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And the final location was from when Erina was in the mechanical room, which is why it didn't feel like we changed places. And... since she would've appeared and activated the Sekimeiya instantly in the previous location, that must mean it overlapped with part of her body upon arriving. That's why she started bleeding at the end of the chain. The tip of her finger was missing.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Did all that really happen? And none of us realized it...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It explained things, but I still had a few doubts. Why had the tower been empty on January 5th? Why had the chain not gone on infinitely?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So Akaro actually was in the tower on November 24th. ...His hair was longer and a different color.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: He traveled to the future while we were in the attic, but there's something I'm confused about.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If I'm right, and the version of Isla who was there ended up being the "friend", she likely traveled before we left the bedroom. We weren't there for too long of a time, though, and we'd left the Past Sekimeiya in the cabinet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Akaro traveled to the future after he and Sai escaped, but since Isla was still there, she went to the past afterward.{w} Would there have been enough time to store the needed energy to go so far back?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: The reason she was able to go many days back was...
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Actually, yes. It was due to a bed sheet that the world C group had obtained in world A. When it was brought to world B, they wrapped it around the Past Sekimeiya and world switched back to world C. However, the sheet remained around the Sekimeiya in world B.{w} When it powered back on, the sheet was still very hot. That's why it took a short time to reach the needed amount of energy.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That's wrong. It was due to a bed sheet that the world C group had obtained in world A. When it was brought to world B, they wrapped it around the Past Sekimeiya and world switched back to world C. However, the sheet remained around the Sekimeiya in world B.{w} When it powered back on, the sheet was still very hot. That's why it took a short time to reach the needed amount of energy.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Akaro and Sai escaped from the bedroom, Sai was forced to reveal the location of the Future Sekimeiya and was immediately knocked out.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Isla A was there and heard it as well. Worried, she tried to get a response from the unconscious Sai, which only one person heard from the bedroom. Giving up, she went down in an attempt to prevent Akaro from damaging the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She found it powered off in one of the hallway B crystal rooms; Akaro was already gone. She knew the event room cabinet was equipped with temperature regulation, so she carried it there.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But after that, on the floor of hallway A, she found a sheet covering yet another Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Confused, she felt its surface, instantly vanishing from that place with the sheet. Immediately, she found herself on November 24th.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Someone else disappeared as well: Akaro A.{w} The bedroom where everyone stayed was directly above the event room, so the range reached him. From a locked bedroom, he appeared in an unlocked prison cell. That was when a policeman outside the building suddenly appeared 21 days in the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai woke up. He was near the elevator, so Isla's travel had missed him and the people in the upper level of the bedroom.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Disoriented, he walked to the event room and found out the others had left both Sekimeiya behind for him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He still had to complete his plan: to get out of the bedroom, he had to travel to the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Once he was done, Sai had both Sekimeiya for himself. Eager to resolve the doubts he had, he brought them both to a room—B6.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Unfortunately for him, he was only able to resolve his two major concerns before the world around him changed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When we left the bedroom... we quickly found out the third Sekimeiya had disappeared from Naomi's locker.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Who the hell did that? There's no way it teleported out.{w} ...Did anyone else have the key after all?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Yes, it was Akaro A.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was Akaro A.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You might remember he world switched while he was in the staff room, and he had Naomi A's keys.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: While he waited in room B4, he wondered if he had access to that locker, and when he went to confirm it, he saw someone had hidden a Sekimeiya there.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Mystified, he took it out with no comprehension that he was no longer in his own world.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...I wonder who it was. Maybe Sai, somehow.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After that, Shiroya and I found a Sekimeiya on the floor of a hallway B room, B6.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When we touched it, I'm pretty sure we went to the future...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We appeared where we'd been ten minutes before, so we went ten minutes to the future.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: We thought we'd gone to the very recent past because the footprints we'd just left looked recent. Since we went shortly into the future, that didn't change.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And then, we concluded we'd gone five minutes to the past because we thought that we'd taken the elevator and caused the trip we heard before traveling. Instead, someone else used it from the attic after we left the bedroom...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: On the crystal floor, we went to the lobby because our past selves hadn't gone there. Who did we hear if not ourselves? There was someone moving through the hallways.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: "We heard an indistinct sound coming from hallway A, made by a door."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's us. We just entered the event room.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: "We waited, and seconds later, the same sound came from hallway B. Unmistakably, a closing door had created it."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There aren't many people I can think of. Sai, Erina, Katei, and maybe the other Shiroya...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But given the movements, I might know who it was...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And that Shiroya... How the hell did she get there...!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Was she the Shiroya from this morning? Did she appear in the attic with Naomi and spend the whole day in the tower?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It can't be. We would've seen her, and what the hell was the deal with her clothes!? Or anything that she said!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: She was the same Shiroya I'd been with. She remembered what we'd done. ...That's all I get.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When we returned to room B6, the Sekimeiya we used wasn't there. Since we'd gone to the future, someone had time to take it away.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Instead, we found one in a cabinet drawer. It was considerably hot, so it was there for a long time.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But we decided not to activate it and brought it to its cabinet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If they had touched it, though, what would've happened? It has been a while since you asked for that.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki would've gone many hours back in time. The lights would not yet have turned on, and he would've found himself in the lobby.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You remember, right? He spent a long time in the staff room. Eventually, after the light was turned on in the morning, he was killed by Ido, who had the suitcase ready to prepare the attack.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Before his eyesight failed, Atsuki saw four people he recognized.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Two men, a woman, and a girl."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: One was Shiroya. She was naturally encompassed by the range when Atsuki touched the Sekimeiya.{w} However, she didn't appear in the lobby with him. Strangely, she appeared in a bathroom on the crystal floor, and when she left, she was seen from the security room and addressed through the microphone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki recognized Ido and Suripo as well: he had seen both of them during the long wait before the event.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The last person was Erina. She had been alive in room B4 next to Atsuki and Shiroya and appeared in the mechanical room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, she had been unconscious. Therefore, despite appearing in the past, she took a while to awaken.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Two impossibilities prevented this from happening. One was the butterfly effect.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Precisely. Atsuki died.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There should've been a world switch, but this is tied to the butterfly effect. After all, the Future Sekimeiya was between another Shiroya's hands, and that version of Shiroya couldn't have existed if they had gone to the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya could have existed, but not Atsuki. That is because he died.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Perhaps that problem helped you figure out the Sekimeiya's mechanics. Because Atsuki died, he could never have appeared in the lobby—he wouldn't have been there in the future.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, there's something to recognize: he had a wound on his right hand, and in the darkness, he saw that he had a key shaped like the one for Naomi's locker. ...It was Ido's instead, though; his appearing location was where he would've ended up traveling to the future in a chain of travels.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...That was when we found Katei dead in the security room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When Katei walked out of the bedroom, Erina followed close behind.{w} She didn't believe Atsuki and Shiroya had killed Isla. ...Sai and Akaro had been with her the entire time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, Katei had been missing during that time, and he hadn't explained himself.{w} She didn't trust him at all; he'd been lying all day. ...He had faked going to the bathroom to take advantage of Isla's death.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On the lowest floor, when Erina uttered his name, he turned around slowly.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A single question was asked. "Where were you when we couldn't find you?"
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Katei realized the meaning behind that. Erina suspected him of causing Isla's death.{w} He sighed quietly and then spoke.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I don't know exactly. When I was walking behind Sai, I suddenly appeared in the attic.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: ...What?
entries.speaker: akinn

entries.text: It's the truth. It likely happened when Shiroya and Atsuki touched the Sekimeiya, remember?
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: Why didn't you say this before!? And that doesn't tell me anything! Why didn't we find you!?
entries.speaker: akinn

entries.text: Katei stared into Erina's eyes. Her voice had never sounded so harsh.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I said I experienced the teleportation, and I am telling you the truth. I was beyond confused when I appeared there.{w} When I came down, the three of you were in the lobby.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: Although Erina wavered, she quickly dismissed Katei's claim as nonsense.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You're not even making sense! You were hiding in the storeroom, weren't you?
entries.speaker: akinn

entries.text: What? No! There are cameras in hallway C. What I'm saying will be proven.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: ...I don't believe it. The cameras aren't recording.
entries.speaker: akinn

entries.text: Yes they are! Don't you see the light!?
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: Katei saw nothing but hostility in Erina's face. Enough to appear as a threat.{w} Did she really think he had killed Isla? He didn't know anything about what had happened to her, but there was a way he could prove his innocence.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...You still haven't explained anything. Why didn't you say this earlier, and why didn't we find you?
entries.speaker: akinn

entries.text: Erina had no idea what to believe. No one else could've harmed Isla, but who would have? Why would anyone have done that to her daughter? Part of her wanted to abandon everything and just stop thinking altogether, placidly waiting the month it would take her daughter to return.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...I'm not lying. Maybe I can prove myself.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: Katei started walking to the security room, gesturing at Erina to come with him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It has been a long time since I've checked. Perhaps the security system is working again, just like what happened to the computer.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: In silence, Katei kneeled under the desk while Erina watched expectantly.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Again, there doesn't seem to be anything wrong with this.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: As he stood up, he nonchalantly took a rusty key out of his pocket and left it in a drawer.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This time, I won't forget to keep it somewhere safer.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: ...Katei sat on his chair and started up the three screens. As Erina stepped forward, he pressed the "archived footage" button.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: O-Oh! I-It's working!
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: A list of cameras appeared on the screen. Erina read them without so much as a twitch.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Look! I'll show you that I was telling the truth!
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: When Katei selected one, a video of hallway C came up, mainly focusing on the bathrooms. Frustrated, Katei used the time bar to skip ahead.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Here! I'm about to disappear!
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: Coming from hallway B, Sai stepped into C. Katei followed behind, and out of nowhere, his body vanished.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: See! That's when I appeared in the attic!
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: After he selected another camera and fast-forwarded further, Katei appeared from the second floor and entered hallway A.
entries.speaker: c
