entries.text: As I walked to the bathroom, I noticed she was going to the storeroom. I stopped myself once she was inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I approached it, intrigued as to what they were talking about.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They'll go to the attic pretty soon. I can listen in without being seen.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I saw that they were all next to the secret door. I hid inside the crystal room at its left.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I approached the wall and put my ear against it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...ut Atsuki had just finished looking through the whole floor.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Exactly.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I can hear them well enough.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What I think is that this door leads outside. The storeroom now stretches farther out than the crystal rooms, and it's a hidden locked door that would explain the policeman's appearance and Naomi's vanishing.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: W-Wait, really...? If a policeman entered, why did nobody else?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: They kept talking about the door. I knew it led outside, but it hadn't opened since that morning.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Finally, the other Atsuki returned.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck is this...?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: There he is. Do you know how to pick a lock?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: What? N-No?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: He was told about the discovery. Sai had noticed the storeroom was open while he was going up the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did you really not know about this?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I promise I didn't. I also don't think this door leads outside. There's no way I wouldn't have ever noticed it.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: And it makes sense that you didn't know about it if it doesn't lead outside?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: ...I'm just speechless. This room is practically unused, but I can't believe this existed.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: ...{w}Now a few things make sense, at least. As you said, nobody was found, so Naomi must've been here at some point.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Yes, yes. I'd like to advise you all on something.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I've made sure that if this door is opened again, I'll be able to tell.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: ...Huh?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...What? How?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I'm not telling you that. One of you could potentially manage to open this, so I'd rather not give you any indication of what I've done.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: What is this about...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...I think that's fair. It wouldn't be wise to demand that you tell us.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Just trust me. I will know if the door opens. However, it's possible it won't and that the plan already finished after the Sekimeiya was brought outside.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Let's go to the attic.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: ...To the attic? Why?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Do you think I'll believe you were walking around for hours and we didn't see you? You either went through this door or were in the attic.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: He wasn't with us. We know that much.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: You've said that before. I know.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: How do you intend to know whether I was there? I won't allow anyone in lightly.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: No? Then how come they spent three hours sleeping there?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: ...I haven't forgotten about that.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: In the off chance Naomi's still in the tower, she's up there, being covered by the three of you. I want to go see it by myself, and I'm sure Akaro and Erina aren't content with your words alone.
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: They left the storeroom and the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The rest happened as I'd already experienced it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stayed in that room until my past self went up. I'd chosen to hide in one of the second floor bathrooms, an unlikely place to be revisited.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I went to hallway B. I knew Sai would be the first one to return and that he'd look through the hallway A rooms.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It happened even sooner than I recalled. Evidently discontent with my search, he walked from room to room.{w} He didn't care about the third Sekimeiya; he'd been the one to leave it there. When he came to hallway B, I was already in a room in hallway A.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I just had to wait.{w} Sai would find the Future Sekimeiya and bring it to the event room. Then, the others would find the Past Sekimeiya and walk to the event room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Future Sekimeiya would be activated in the event room—it was the one that had been gray, and I was far enough from its range. That would leave me alone in the tower with my past self.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Picture Frame
I'm sure everything has taken shape in your mind, but I wonder what shape that is.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You remember this world, don't you? In it, many things weren't what they seemed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Its real shape is the last key you will need to reach the peak.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Two people waited in the lobby. {time=9:00} was approaching.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At that point, you may have realized something was wrong. Shiroya wasn't there; Miiya was occupying her place.{w} However, her name was spoken before the doors opened.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya...?
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: "I'd managed to leave my mind empty, but I abruptly turned around when I heard a quiet voice coming from my left. A man was crouching next to me, and when he stood up, I saw his older face underneath white hair."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Katei said Shiroya's name...
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Is this yours? I think you dropped it.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: "He showed me a ticket that must've fallen from my purse when I'd stretched my muscles. I nodded and put it back inside, all while unnerved by his stiff motions."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Everyone brought an identification card to verify their own tickets. Of course, the tickets had everyone's names on them. Katei read Shiroya's name and called for her.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Miiya was there with her own purse, which contained three tickets. When she stretched, one fell out, meaning that her purse hadn't been closed. In world B, when Shiroya opened her purse, she unzipped it—the tickets couldn't have fallen from her purse, as it was closed since long before {time=9.}
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hopefully, it was enjoyable to catch any of these details. However, although Shiroya's absence could be reasoned out, it wouldn't be surprising if your gut told you something was wrong before that. For everyone who'd gotten trapped in the tower, Shiroya was a girl who had died weeks ago.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When the group went up the floors, Atsuki found the key for the security room. Everyone splitting up created the chances for individuals to accomplish what they needed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The next time they reunited, Sai noticed the sound of keys coming from Katei's pocket. ...They were louder than they'd been before.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Katei was confronted, he showed them a set of keys belonging to Naomi. However, that's when he himself noticed something.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There were two identical keyrings in his pocket. That had made the metallic noise even easier to perceive.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At that point, Katei had traveled to the past one time. Upon appearing, he hadn't realized that the keyring Naomi had left behind suddenly appeared in his pocket.{w} Then, when he came across it, he put it inside. In that way, he came into possession of two copies.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Sai made him reveal it, he didn't know a second one remained in his pocket. That fact was what shaped Katei's actions.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In this world, he insisted the attic should be kept locked, and he made sure the Sekimeiya cabinet would always be. That way, he could unlock them with his secret set, setting up Atsuki and Miiya, who had the other one, as the only possible culprits.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai thought of a way to know whether that set was Naomi's: if one of the keys opened the attic, Katei's lie would be exposed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Before they got there, he decided to test if something else Katei had said was invalid too. On the sixth floor, he attempted to call the elevator, which should've been disabled.{w} They waited, but it never came.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, at that point, the elevator was already working again.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The first time Katei traveled to the past, he walked to the crystal floor. He saw an Atsuki from another world, which later made him question what everyone was saying.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Most importantly, he saw people leaving the security room, which had strangely been unlocked. That was his opportunity to shut the computer down. Since he was alone and hadn't told everyone about the cameras' green lights, in this world, he was able to power off the entire security system too as opposed to just one camera.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Later, when Sai called the elevator, Katei had already enabled it because he had found the attic key. However, it didn't come.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Katei suddenly froze up; would they notice their mistake?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...The elevator was disabled. That's much more unlikely to have gone wrong. If it was working for some reason, the button would light up when it arrived.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: The orange light never appeared—the elevator was already there, and you might recall that was the case in world B as well.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And not only that. Atsuki from world B was spying on the group, and when they entered the attic, he was on the sixth floor. He heard the elevator, but only once—when Isla, Erina, Sai, and Akaro took it down. Since it was called from the attic and Atsuki B only heard it once, it was originally on the sixth floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Either way, nobody saw through his ruse, and thanks to that, Katei was able to set up a stronger illusion later on.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When everyone entered the attic, they saw the strange footprints on the floor. They led to the sofa, where the Future Sekimeiya was.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Most people believed the Sekimeiya should've been on the crystal floor. If that was the case, someone had to have brought it up very recently, but it didn't seem possible for them to have left the attic.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That made Sai call the elevator, and it actually did arrive.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That was the feint Katei aimed for—that the elevator had just been enabled. That someone had been in the security room after they'd all stepped into the attic.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Following that, when everyone saw that the computer had lost power, what he said was reinforced; it must have happened after they had tried to call the elevator on the sixth floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At the same time, the Sekimeiya had disappeared from the cabinet. From their perspective, it had been brought to the attic.{w} However, Sai knew the truth. Just like in worlds A and B, he had quickly hidden the fake Sekimeiya when everyone had split up, so the one they'd retrieved from the attic was different.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That was when everyone else learned about time travel. Right before their eyes, Katei went to the future.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki reeled. He had to learn more about the Sekimeiya. He stayed close to it, and when the crystal floor had been inspected, he touched it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He went minutes to the future, but he wasn't alone. Sai had specifically gone to find the fake Sekimeiya he'd hidden, wondering whether it was still there, as well as whether it shared the same powers he'd witnessed. As he was returning to the event room from hallway B, he traveled with Atsuki.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki appeared in the attic, which was locked. The elevator had been left open on the crystal floor, so he couldn't leave through it either.{w} However, Sai appeared on the crystal floor since his group had left the attic earlier. He realized the elevator was open and allowed Atsuki to leave.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When they met, they thought they'd gone minutes to the past, although neither of them spoke about it. Atsuki recalled Sai had gone missing, so finding him in the past wasn't strange.{w} His misinterpretation arose due to Sai's watch, which had ended up minutes behind. When they returned to the others, they saw that everyone was in the security room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "As we turned around, we saw Sai staring at us next to the unassertive Atsuki."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Wh-Where were you!?
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: Me? I just took a detour to the bathroom.
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Sai wasn't exactly aware of how blatant his lie was. According to his watch, he should've been missing for very little time, but it had been much longer than he thought since he'd vanished. He didn't reveal what had happened to him, and because of that, he was the only person aware of the Sekimeiya's range.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Hours later, Suripo's dead body suddenly appeared. There's one last thing to settle.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Naomi still hadn't been found, and it seemed like nobody else could've committed the crime without having traveled through time. That belief led to a whole search with no result.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Something very important was found, though: the storeroom's secret corridor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Upon its discovery, you likely noticed that someone's actions differed from world B's.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world C, Sai did something to know whether the door was opened from that point on. That did not happen in world B.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The reason was the piece of duct tape they'd all seen. It had reminded Sai of his favorite novel, which made him think of setting up a check on that door.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After that, everyone ended up in the attic, where they hoped they could calmly spend the rest of their isolation in the bedrooms.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Of course, that wouldn't happen. It was Sai who soon tried to go back down unnoticed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What if Atsuki and Miiya hadn't alerted everyone to his departure?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Shiroya and Atsuki stayed in the attic. Sai had gone to the crystal floor, but they didn't follow him down."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Shiroya let out a sigh."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "They had no strength left, so they kept resting, trying to ignore what was happening around them."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Indeed, your choice made Miiya become Shiroya.{w} The world changed drastically. The butterfly effect amplifies even a single unwitting change.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In that world, Miiya couldn't have been saved. However, you wanted to know what would've happened if Sai was let loose. That caused Miiya to be replaced by Shiroya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That was one of numerous changes, alongside...
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Six pairs of eyes saw the identical scene."{w} Exactly, it was Katei's absence. The storeroom's door hadn't been locked, so he'd been able to leave before everyone awakened. In that world, nobody had told the group about keeping the Sekimeiya cold.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Six pairs of eyes saw the identical scene."{w} It was Katei's absence. The storeroom's door hadn't been locked, so he'd been able to leave before everyone awakened. In that world, nobody had told the group about keeping the Sekimeiya cold.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai roamed free for a long time, and on the crystal floor, he had access to both Sekimeiya. With his watch, he was able to figure out the basic mechanics behind traveling to the past and future.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That's how he came up with a plan to remain with the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What did he do? When he came back up, he showed everyone what the Sekimeiya were capable of. Right now, you understand them a lot more than at that time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...However, you might still have trouble figuring out what Sai did. He had to pull out something fairly clever to trick everyone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If you ever want to go back and attempt to see through his scenario, I hope you're able to beat him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In reality, Atsuki and Miiya brought everyone to the crystal floor in an attempt to find Sai. Before he was seen, the Past Sekimeiya was found in room B6.{w} Sai was in the event room, and he suddenly heard people approaching. Hoping it would let him escape, he touched the Future Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki and Miiya brought everyone to the crystal floor in an attempt to find him. Before he was seen, the Past Sekimeiya was found in room B6.{w} Sai was in the event room, and he suddenly heard people approaching. Hoping it would let him escape, he touched the Future Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Y—! You scared the fuck out of me!{w} Holy shit! What the fuck are you doing!? You almost hit me with the door!
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: He thought he was safe as soon as he touched it, but the door still burst open.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Don't you think that's a better question for you? What are you doing!?
entries.speaker: aknn

entries.text: I'm doing absolutely nothing.
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: "We turned to Katei, who hadn't interrupted us. He was perplexed, staring at his empty hands."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What's up with you?
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: ...Where's the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: What? I have no—
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: I-It disappeared. I legitimately felt it disappear.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: Excuse me?
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: Both had disappeared, as a world switch had been triggered. Oblivious, they found themselves in world A.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Sai spun and looked at the cabinet covered by the curtain. Then, he looked all around the room with a slight frown."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "I was also moderately puzzled. Katei couldn't have been lying. He didn't have the Sekimeiya, it wasn't on the floor, and he couldn't have hidden it anywhere without us seeing it."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Out of nowhere, the cabinet was covered by its curtain. However, that was nothing compared to what awaited in hallway C.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The panel to call the elevator was gone.{w} ...All of them were. They had been ripped off on every floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Wait, we didn't lock it, did we?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: You're right... I forgot to tell you to lock it because I was annoyed that Sai left.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: Whoa, then someone's definitely in here. Is it time to have a talk with Naomi? I wonder if she knows we can enter.
entries.speaker: sainn

entries.text: In the living room, their footprints had disappeared.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And Katei was the lucky person who found the Future Sekimeiya in the open refrigerator. ...Opening it had been the last thing Sai A would ever do.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki wanted to look at the BIOS's time, but the security room was locked. In addition, Sai realized the mark he'd left in the storeroom was gone. ...He was convinced someone had opened it, so he marked it again.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Of course, that was far from the truth, but it made them believe that someone else had entered the tower.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The next time they attempted to enter the attic, it was locked again.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "We all stared at the door in shock. It was locked."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Someone else is certainly in this building. I left the attic just now.
entries.speaker: knn

entries.text: The truth behind that was the secret keyring Katei still had. Long before he'd traveled to the future, he'd left it in the security room so that he couldn't be found with it. He'd been able to retrieve it when he'd appeared there.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He'd left the key inserted in the door because he knew what had happened with the elevator: it was in the attic despite the panel having vanished.{w} Inside, he'd found that world's attic key. He could keep everyone from entering the highest floor by locking the door in.{w} He left it by bringing the elevator to the sixth floor; he could keep it there as a hidden way up. Since he had his set of keys, he could always access the attic through the elevator he'd prepared.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But... it was found when Atsuki attempted to open it.{w} Inside, there were the bodies of Naomi C and Shiroya A.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The shock was natural. Naomi hadn't been seen for hours, and Shiroya had supposedly died weeks ago. It was undeniable that her existence was related to Atsuki and Miiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But nobody knew what had happened to the two women, and all they could do was bring them to the lobby.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: With the elevator, the group was able to reach the attic again, where they found the single key in its inner keyhole.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Over thirty minutes later, a new dead body was found near the hallway C stairs.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was Erina A's.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Erina C, who they'd been with, was in room A1 with Isla. Meanwhile, the world A group was waiting in room B4. After Sai, Erina had been the second person to leave.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Don't lie! It can only be you. You killed them."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Everyone saw Erina's body atop a pool of blood. Someone had just killed her, and Atsuki had heard her words before dying. ...She had confronted who she'd thought was the killer.{w} However, it quickly became clear that nobody could've easily committed the crime. Everyone stated what they'd been doing.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki said that after being the first to leave the attic, he'd spent a few minutes on the second floor. He said that at one point, he heard the elevator once.{w} Miiya said that she'd left second and remained on the third floor until Atsuki ran up from below, letting her know what had happened.{w} Sai and Katei claimed to have been above them, and their versions of events seemed to confirm each other.{w} Akaro claimed to have left the attic last when Erina and Isla had still been sitting on the sofa, and that afterward, he'd stayed on the sixth floor alone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The elevator was on the crystal floor. Since the panels hadn't been reattached, the "1" button must've been pressed from the attic.{w} It seemed like nobody could've performed a murder simply. The only way to get to the crystal floor after Atsuki's departure would've been by riding in the elevator with Erina and Isla. However, if that had happened, they couldn't have ended up above Atsuki when he'd gone to find everyone; nobody had seen them walking up, and the elevator hadn't been heard again.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There were three main options in everyone's minds, and one was correct.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki hadn't been lying; everything he said was the truth.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: People they didn't know about were present in the building—the world A group. However, none of them had left room B4.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The answer had to be the Sekimeiya. Someone would travel through time and kill Erina.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: For them, that seemed like a fickle solution; there was no way to prove it. If that was the case, unless the culprit had already escaped, they had to search for them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, for you, that solution might seem odd.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You know what happened in that world. The Past Sekimeiya was in room B4 with the world A group.{w} It was in the cabinet where Akaro had put it, and it wasn't activated until he and Isla world switched to world B.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After that, what happened to it? Shiroya B found it and was able to world switch to world B. Later on, Sai B found it was well and world switched back to world B.{w} Lastly, Atsuki A found it and also world switched to world B.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That was it. The Past Sekimeiya from world A wasn't activated ever again.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So then, who killed Erina? How did her killer show up before her and push her off the stairs?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Her killer couldn't have world switched before her. After all, they would've had to appear from world C, where Atsuki was experimenting with the Sekimeiya in the attic.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The Past Sekimeiya couldn't have been used to carry out her murder. The key to solving it was the Future Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was the one that Katei had found in the kitchen refrigerator. He hid it somewhere in the attic, which he locked, intending to keep it away from the others.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Before the world C group arrived in world A, only one person had touched the Future Sekimeiya: Sai A. However, he immediately died where he arrived. In other words, nobody from world A could've killed Erina.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Before her death, the world C group had been on the crystal floor; anyone who traveled to the future could've appeared there, bypassing Atsuki's view.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But that wouldn't have been all. After appearing there, they would've had to make it above him, and such a thing didn't seem simple. No Sekimeiya could've been activated on the crystal floor, and the elevator never went back up.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: People were leaving, and Isla said she wanted to come down too since she still hadn't seen all the gems. I noticed she was trying to cheer herself up a little despite the... two bodies we found, so even though I didn't want to leave, I went with her just so that it took her mind off it.
entries.speaker: akinn

entries.text: "People were leaving". Erina and Isla were on the sofa then, and from their point of view, not everyone had left the attic.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There's only one person who could've done it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "I walked to the bedrooms and opened the left one. I needed to throw myself onto the bed and be alone for some time."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "I stood in the middle of the floor 3 corridor. I didn't want to see the others, so I'd been thinking to myself."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "As anyone could've been anywhere, all I wanted was to wait. I could perceive faint footsteps above me, signaling someone was on the fourth floor. I approached a potted plant and sat next to it. I calmly felt the seconds pass, appreciating the sensation."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A-Are you alone...!? Where are the others?
entries.speaker: ann

entries.text: "He was pretty agitated, so I kept my composure and waited for him to tell me what had occurred. Everything about him gave away that he'd seen something frightful."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Erina's body lay facing down over a vast pool of blood, traces of which started in the middle of the staircase. I didn't have to walk farther down to know she was dead."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I-I think someone was on the floor above me at some point. Were you alone when you found her?
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: "I kept walking down while I silently wondered why he'd been alone. On the floor of hallway C, I pressed two fingers to Erina's body and waited for any perceptible movement."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It's not possible for us to take the elevator, so let's walk up. We should come across someone.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: "My heavy breathing was interrupting my words, and I didn't let my gaze stray from Erina. Being so close to her, I noticed that blood was coming out of the part of her head that hit the edge of a step."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "With what we'd talked about, could Erina's killer be identified? I didn't think so, but there was a chance I was failing to consider something."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "She was there, casually leaning against the line of cabinets. I could hardly believe what I was seeing, but there was no wariness in her eyes and not even a trace of blood near her."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Most people weren't aware that traveling to the future was possible. When Miiya noticed the peculiar smell again and touched the Sekimeiya, she immediately thought she'd traveled to the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She appeared where she'd been in the past; it was what had happened before. That made her think she'd gone back in time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She was alone above the hallway C stairs when she suddenly heard Erina's voice.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Don't lie! It can only be you. You killed them."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Erina had seen the bodies in the lobby. Shiroya had died, but she'd just been in the crystal room. Sai hadn't come back.{w} ...Naomi was dead, and earlier in the day, what had happened with the elevator buttons convinced Erina that the killer was someone they'd been unable to find.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Miiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The way Miiya looked at her only made her more convinced. When she dismissed the accusation with quiet, cold words, Erina ran up the stairs in sheer agitation.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She was quickly knocked back. In midair, she let out a yell that cut off upon impact.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Miiya wasn't sure what to do. She stared at Erina, processing the fact that she wasn't moving. Then, slowly, she took a few steps backward.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shock rushed through her when she heard footsteps approaching. Atsuki was about to see her.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: To hide from him, she rushed into one of the bathrooms on the second floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The first thing Atsuki did was run down the stairs and check Erina's pulse, which allowed Miiya to escape toward the third floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There, she heard someone above her. She'd looked at the security cameras and seen no green lights, which perhaps meant that she hadn't been recorded.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Nonetheless, she was completely certain that she'd changed the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, after Atsuki came running from below, she soon realized that she couldn't easily explain what had happened.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It's not possible for us to take the elevator, so let's walk up. We should come across someone.
entries.speaker: mnn

entries.text: She attempted to hide her future knowledge. At that point in time, the elevator hadn't been opened yet; nobody knew it was usable despite the broken panels.{w} And despite the fact that they should have been together recently, Atsuki had told her he'd been alone. ...Did that mean that she'd overwritten her past self?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "I saw that the attic key was inserted into the door. We all entered to find the missing person."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "I stared at the floor's footprints—the proof that the past had changed. I had no idea how, but it was undeniable that it greatly had."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Should I bring her to the lobby?

entries.text: My plan had been to use the Past Sekimeiya one more time after my past self's disappearance.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could live through November 30th a third time; I could save Miiya, as the news I'd read was the only obstacle in that pursuit.{w} In the world I was in, Shiroya didn't exist, but I had never seen her blood, no definitive proof of her death. Her absence was no real barrier.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After that, I had to return with Shiroya to our world. The way to accomplish it was by being in the center of the building at close to {time=19:30.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That was how I had to do it. If I attempted to change worlds before that point by using the two Sekimeiya, it was very likely I would appear someplace else. After all, that was how the group from the world I was in had vanished earlier, and I was completely confident they hadn't appeared in our world.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It should've been doable—I'd never really considered otherwise. ...What made my arm stop was the connection I'd just made.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Just before {time=19:30}, Sai had gone to the storeroom to check whether his mark had disappeared. At that time, the door hadn't opened yet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I left the attic; I didn't feel comfortable thinking there. If anyone came up with the elevator, I wouldn't hear them, so I chose to go to the sixth floor, where I would hear both the elevator and any approaching footsteps.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Of course, my plan implied a future version of myself was in the tower. A version of myself who had been there since the morning.{w} I'd known that, which was why I'd followed the group's movements—so that I could give myself a route to hide throughout the day, aware of where to be at all times.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Could that really be the case, though?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When I thought about it after having witnessed the whole series of events, my heartbeat grew erratic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is it...?{w} Just before the group left this world, the whole building was searched, when I replaced the other Atsuki without anyone noticing. Naturally, my future self wasn't found—that would've been a paradox, as I would've seen myself before knowing where I would be.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: So, why was that me not found? How will I avoid being found?{w} At the time, every single place was inspected except for the hidden area in the storeroom. However, I couldn't have been there, as my own past self already was.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I'd had the thought in the back of my mind: if a similar problem arose, the storeroom's secret could aid me. ...That was no longer the case.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My future self merely has to be here at {time=19:30.} ...It's not exact, but I'll say the search happened at {time=14.}{w} My past self was in the storeroom from {time=9} to {time=14.} Immediately after I left it, the fake wall was found by this world's group.{w} I thought that in the worst-case scenario, I could enter through the storeroom after the attack. ...But that's not possible. As soon as it was found, Sai marked it, and I know that mark will still be there at {time=19:30}, right before we returned to our world.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Knowing all that, it wasn't possible that a future self of mine would enter the tower after the {time=14} search.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: More importantly, it's very unlikely this would be possible either way. I shouldn't assume that I could enter through the storeroom without being seen. Technically, I could enter after {time=19:30} and travel to the past in order to be at the center of the building at the right time, but I don't know whether I'll be seen outside, and if I am, I'll be unable to travel back.{w} I shouldn't go back to the 30th with a plan that could fail, so I have to entirely rule out the storeroom.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That meant that for a future self of mine to be present at {time=19:30}, he would've had to be in the tower since a time before my past self had begun to wait in the storeroom.{w} Since I was aware of that, how could I avoid being found by the search at {time=14}?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's one way—by traveling to the future.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When could I have used the Future Sekimeiya to not be present at {time=14}?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: After the smoke was released, it was brought to the attic in a suitcase. The next time it moved was when Katei brought it to the crystal floor with the other Atsuki and Miiya.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I remember how he looked when he had it in his hands. He was in pain because the Sekimeiya hadn't been activated since it had been taken out of the cabinet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If my future self had used it before he brought it down, it would've reset and spent a while powered off. There's no way Katei would've had to hold it carefully like he did.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If I'd touched it at that point, I would've had to be in the storeroom during the night to appear in the tower in the future. Maybe that's possible, but there's too much uncertainty; there's clear room for failure.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I could explain Katei's face in a different way: I could leave the Sekimeiya in a hot place as I touch it. However, both Sekimeiya were in the attic. I would have to find out which was which, keep the past one in the refrigerator due to its large range, and travel to the future.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...I'd once put some thought into the type of web I was entangled in. I'd considered that in order to work around what you'd observed, having observed too much could be a fatal flaw.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At the time, I'd also come up with another concept in the form of thought-up loops, which were fundamentally similar to the way the Past Sekimeiya worked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's uncertain whether traveling to the future before Katei brought the Sekimeiya down will work out smoothly. However, I have a way to know if it will.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: A cue.{w} If I had a loop in my head, I could know whether it could be completed. If I thought about everything that I would do after touching the Past Sekimeiya, I could observe whether a cue I intended to leave would exist.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So, could I do this? If it works, I'll draw a mark with a pen beneath a drawer on this floor...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I went to the offices and walked up to the drawer I'd selected.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It's not here. There's no mark.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There'd been clear uncertainty behind the loop I'd thought of, but thanks to the lack of the cue, the uncertainty could be erased—that loop wouldn't work.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's impossible, then. I might be failing to realize the reason why it couldn't be executed. I don't know if it's just a tiny detail.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What about entering through the storeroom after {time=19:30} and then traveling to the past? Could that be possible?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If it is, I'll go back in time to a point after {time=14} and leave a mark beneath that drawer. If I need to, I'll travel back twice in order to make it to a point prior to now.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There was nothing there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That makes sense. That means I couldn't enter the building through the storeroom without being seen from outside.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I was growing nervous. Miiya was alive—success must've awaited me.{w} ...But could I be sure of that?{w} It was a guarantee that Miiya was alive, but what about Shiroya? The circumstances around her were what left room for doubt.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When the Future Sekimeiya was brought down from the attic, Katei used it. Then, the other Atsuki and Sai traveled minutes forward as well. There's no way I could travel before then.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But... the situation is the same later. I saw what happened to the Sekimeiya.{w} Sai, Akaro, and Katei moved them back and forth, but I remember it clearly—no place where the Future Sekimeiya was hidden was accessed by a future self of mine. My line of sight unconsciously blocked myself.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There's no way a future self of mine was on the crystal floor and wasn't seen by me or anyone who was there. The Future Sekimeiya wasn't activated, and neither was the past one.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Katei did go a long time to the future, but even if I were to enter his travel's range, I wouldn't go past {time=14.}
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: And when the Future Sekimeiya was hidden in the mechanical room, the other Atsuki and Miiya used it to go to the future.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Suripo's killer brought it to a room in hallway B. When I was enacting the search, I felt the air around it, which was burning. There's no way I had touched it before then.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...So is it not possible? Was there really no time where I could've gone to the future!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I thought of using the Past Sekimeiya instead. Its only use would've been to travel seconds back to a room that had just been inspected. However, I'd also felt the air around it during the search, and it had been even hotter... That path was blocked too.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}I felt lost. How the hell could I accomplish anything?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Traveling to the future before the attack won't be doable, and after the 30th, Ashiya already had the Sekimeiya. The days up to the 15th are useless.{w} It was the owner of that gem shop who found the Sekimeiya. On the 30th, it's very likely they were in that box I saw...{w} But they were taken by the man who released the smoke, and he ran away with them.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I know the smoke was released thanks to the news report I saw, so I can't obtain the Sekimeiya and save Miiya together. Not to mention that to appear in the tower on the 15th, I would also have to be there on the 15th of November.{w} I'm sure that after the man ran away with the box, he was caught. That's what Katei told us about, and it's the reason why the Sekimeiya returned to Ashiya. There's nothing I can do there.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Just in case, I need to try it.{w} A loop where I go to November 15th and remain inside the tower. Then, on November 30th, I take that box with the Sekimeiya.{w} As fast as possible, I make sure Miiya won't die and run away. Then, I travel to the future and appear after the search that happened at {time=14.}{w} I'll tell the police about the Sekimeiya's location before I travel so that they can find them and return them to Ashiya.{w} If this can work, a mark will be under that drawer.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: {tip=ohnoitdidntwork}It wasn't there{/tip}. It appeared that couldn't work either.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I kept thinking about the events that had occurred throughout the day in case I could find the smallest opening, but it really seemed like there was no place for a future self of mine to exist.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Does this mean that I can't be here at {time=19:30}? But that's the single guaranteed way I have to go back!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I could change worlds in the morning instead, after Shiroya and Naomi did. That's a lot less likely to bring me to the world I want, though...!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...Maybe there was no way to skip the {time=14} search, but what about another way around it?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Atsuki from this world looked at the rooms in hallway A. Then, I took his place and looked through the rest of the crystal floor.{w} Finally, Miiya and I completed all the other floors.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What if... my future self was in one of the hallway A rooms? Technically, that's how I was able to not be found that time. I told the Atsuki from this world to stay put, and he did so because it was his own request.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Could I do the same? Could I ask him to ignore having seen me?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I wondered that, well aware of the answer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I recalled the time he'd seen me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "I saw my own body stepping in. As he approached one of the cabinets, I knew there was only one thing I could do."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is very imp—
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Wha—
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: "He turned around with a startled gasp. His reaction was even more drastic when he saw me."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh-What!? Who are you!?{w=0.7} Are you... me?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: "I nodded, although it wasn't the entire truth."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is very important. Stay here until the search is finished.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: That reaction gave me the answer. That was the first time he'd seen another self of his.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Could my future self have told him to react that way? ...Word by word?{w} I didn't think that was how it worked; his reaction seemed completely genuine. Likely, the only way for me to make such a thing work would've been by considering it before seeing his reaction.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nonetheless, I verified whether it would work. If a mark was below the next desk, it would.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once again, there was nothing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I thought back to the look in Miiya's eyes. It had changed at one point.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What if she saw me? What if my future self was in the partitions on that floor?{w} Could he have told her to not reveal him?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That felt a little strange. If that had happened, why would her look have changed in that way? I knew the answer couldn't be that I would instruct her to do so.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Not only that, but if I stayed in that partition, the reason would've been due to knowing how Miiya's demeanor changed. In short, the result would've caused the effect.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Well, is that so? I did notice a while ago that there's something special about the offices on the fourth floor...{w} I'm pretty sure that nobody ever looked at them—neither in the morning nor later in the day. Miiya was the only person to inspect them. I spent the day following everyone to know where to be in a future loop.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Could my future self really have been there all the time? Could that work?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I tested it right away. If it could, a mark would be below a drawer...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There's nothing! What the fuck!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Once again, it seemed my idea was deemed an impossibility by the universe. For one reason or another, it wasn't something that could occur.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You've gotta be joking. I'm certain Miiya and Shiroya can both be alive in this world, but can I not return to mine? Do I have to hope changing worlds at another time will work?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...It had to be at {time=19:30.} I was fairly certain about that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If my future self had been in the attic when Shiroya and Naomi disappeared this morning, he would've appeared along with them. Even if not in the same world, I would reunite with Shiroya.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't think that's possible, though. I would've had to be there before Naomi unlocked the attic. When I looked through the cameras, I saw that our past selves were right behind her.{w} Even then, because the range didn't reach me, I'm not sure it would've reached the kitchen. There's no way I could've been in the living room, and I didn't see my footprints anywhere.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...That's not even everything. I need to be certain the travel will work because there's no way I'll have another chance. If I intend to change worlds when Shiroya and Naomi did, even if it works, I'll end up in a different world from this one. This means that I'll be unable to leave a physical indication for me to see now...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I don't think it would work, but what matters is that there's room for failure. I can't afford that.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had been lost in thought for a while when something alerted me. Someone was walking up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I quickly hid in the second partition and saw a single person walking past the glass. Fortunately, they hadn't seen me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Miiya? Why is she alone?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: All by herself, she went to the attic. She'd been yawning, so perhaps she wanted to rest on the beds.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya are in the refrigerator. She shouldn't see them.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I couldn't get distracted. I had to find a solution to my problem.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I attempted to come up with something else. There had to be something that would help me...!
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What if I let the Past Sekimeiya gather energy right now and I bring it somewhere so that its range reaches behind the tower?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I activate it and go a few minutes to the past, knowing that in the future, my future self will be right outside the tower, waiting to be encompassed. If I do that and think that I'll be in the tower in the future, will I appear inside it?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Or would I run into the same issue as trying to appear with an item that I can't obtain? I need to test it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I failed to see any cue.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Really? ...Is it just because I couldn't enter the tower by my own means, or is there another reason...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There's gotta be something else. I could get into the tower through the storeroom and affect Sai's mark. That should allow the travel to put me inside the tower, which would bypass the mark. So, his mark would only be affected in a hypothetical world. It should work...!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Something else... There had to be something else.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What if the Atsuki that Miiya has been with is my future self?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It sounded interesting. Before that morning, I could've replaced the Atsuki of that world by making him stay outside the tower. Then, I could've hidden in plain sight by acting as the Atsuki who'd gotten trapped.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Of course, it was an impossibility: I would've observed my own movements all along, giving them no origin. However, if I had thought about that concept early enough, I felt it would've been viable.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: My thoughts went back to the search at {time=14.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had thought about everything: my past self couldn't have been in the rooms I'd investigated. He couldn't have been in the rooms the other Atsuki had investigated. He couldn't have been in the places Miiya had investigated.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And he couldn't have been traveling forward in time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Where the hell had he been, then? The answer I was looking for had to be somewhere as well.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't forgotten about Miiya's change of attitude. She had come out of the fourth floor's partitions with an entirely different demeanor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Why? I knew my future self couldn't have been there.{w} So, then, what could she have seen?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was clear the way I was handling my thoughts wasn't proper; I had to widen their scope.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the end, only two things mattered: saving Miiya and returning to my world. The way I was thinking about it, those two aspects seemed to be incompatible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: How else could Miiya be saved, though? How the hell could the news I saw be bypassed?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There's no other way. I have to go back to the past again, to the 30th.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: This is what I determined. I can salvage this world's history. Since I'm from another world, I can save this one.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It has to be me—someone who hasn't observed the truth of this world yet. That's the only way.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It is the only way, isn't it?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...I suppose it's not. Only one part of that is correct.{w} It doesn't have to be me, but the only reason I can do it is that I'm not from this world. Only someone who isn't from this world can divert this world's history from their own. That's a better way to put it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's... right. I'm not the only person who can do this. It can be anyone from another world.{w} And... at {time=19}, the Shiroya from my world will appear here and go to the attic.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: She can do this too. ...Would that make a difference, though? Would that solve any problems?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I can tell her what I've learned. I can tell her everything. ...If she went to the past and saved this world, would she be able to be here at {time=19:30}?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: She couldn't have been in one of the rooms the Atsuki from this world investigated. The way he looked said more than enough. ...That means there's only one other possibility, but it doesn't make sense either.{w} It doesn't make sense.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When I looked under the next drawer, it was clear that the universe disagreed with me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I almost burst out laughing at what I saw. Not only from the absurdity of it existing, but also from how cartoonish it was. Maybe Shiroya had doodled something so goofy-looking just to elicit that reaction.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Stunned, part of me refused what I was seeing. It flew in the face of what I knew. If that was the truth, what was the meaning behind that search? Why had nobody been found?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did it really make more sense than the other ideas I'd envisioned? ...Perhaps it didn't matter. Success had been assured to me—I was extremely puzzled, but I felt relieved more than anything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oh, that's right. The rusty key...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That finally made sense. Before I'd entered the tower, the fact that I'd seen it in the outer keyhole had been almost ridiculous.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I felt a familiar sensation. In a few brief moments, swathes of problems still lingering in my mind slotted into place.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At {time=19:30}, that's who activated one of the Sekimeiya. That's why we returned to our world.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stood up slowly, my vision momentarily blurry. After some seconds, I began to approach the attic.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't see Miiya, but her footprints were visible.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was careful not to make a sound. The bedroom doors were closed, but it was very likely she was behind one of them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I shut myself in the kitchen. The recorder was still there, counting up the seconds. It had been an hour and a half since I'd started a new recording.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It must be about {time=17:30.}{w} I'll take the Sekimeiya out at {time=18:30.}
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It's strange... I know we'll change worlds at {time=19:30}, so I'll take both Sekimeiya out so that can happen...
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Doesn't that contradict what the universe just repeatedly denied? Won't I allow something to happen because I experienced the result first?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Maybe there's something I'm missing. Maybe I don't really understand why it will happen.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...I suppose it doesn't really matter, though. All I know is that it'll repeat.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I had to wait through the last stretch. I thought of going back to the sixth floor, but I chose to remain near the timer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}The news that I heard matched our world's. It was identical to how it would've been without my input.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's why I imagined everything had happened the same way. Then, I realized that didn't have to be the case. The news was the only thing I'd observed in this world.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: One girl had been severely injured, and the other hadn't been found. It matched up with what I'd personally experienced, although it wasn't the end. Seeing as it was the only barrier in this world, I could've gone back in time, saved Miiya, and prevented Shiroya from being found.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's what I thought as soon as I put together that I could alter this world's history. The news could remain consistent because it didn't lead to a single interpretation.{w} I also thought that everything finally made sense—that it was the reason why Miiya had been in the tower and why Shiroya had been absent. It fit with the plan I came up with, so I thought I finally understood this world.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...It didn't make as much sense as I thought. After all, I saw Miiya in the tower—I saw the result of a loop before I came up with it. The news hadn't actually been the only piece of this world I'd observed.{w} And maybe it makes real sense. ...I believe I know why I saw Miiya before I understood how she'd be saved.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I didn't step out of the kitchen. Miiya was close by, but I hadn't heard anything. If she hadn't silently left, she was sleeping in a bedroom.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Sixty more minutes had been added to the timer. It was finally {time=18:30.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At the same time that I took both Sekimeiya out of the refrigerator, I began a new recording.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is it. When the timer hits sixty minutes, it'll be {time=19:30.}
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I should keep waiting on the sixth floor. I don't know if Shiroya will use the elevator, but if she does, that's where she'll come out.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I was about to leave when I heard someone behind the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...!{w} Who's here?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Their steps approached one of the bedrooms and stepped inside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Is that all? Are they going to stay inside? I'm pretty sure whoever that was arrived with the elevator.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stood still, awaiting any other movement. ...But it seemed they would remain there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait a second. I might have overlooked something important.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Even though I never saw Miiya in our world, Erina apparently did. She was definitely there at one point and left that note behind, right?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: But she didn't stay there, or we would've seen her.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: That's odd. If Erina saw Miiya, it should've been at around this time. Slightly before it, actually.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Isn't she here right now, though...?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There was a chance she was about to appear in our world. If that would happen, it was evident I didn't understand the details behind it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Perhaps {time=19:30} wasn't the only time where returning would be possible. It could occur earlier too, at a time I wasn't aware of.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If that time was still yet to happen, I had to get away from the Sekimeiya, or else I could disappear before Shiroya's arrival.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hid the Sekimeiya on a high cabinet shelf, as keeping them in a drawer would've severely messed with the temperature.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, I stepped onto the sixth floor, and like before, I entered the offices.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Unless I've made a big mistake, she should be here in thirty minutes.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: If one of the Sekimeiya is activated before then for some reason, that'll cause the world change that could still happen. Since I know we'll return at {time=19:30}, though, I have a pretty strong guarantee that the Past Sekimeiya won't be the one activated.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I was so close. It had been more than two weeks since I'd seen her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had plenty of things to say, but I wanted to know her story too. Why would she run up to the attic? Why were her clothes different? What had she done in January?
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Just thinking about it made the time go by swiftly. The end was truly near.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood up and walked out. I was sure she was about to appear.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't have the voice recorder with me, but it had been close to half an hour. I stood still, trying to perceive the faintest sound.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: And it came. Finally, I heard what I'd been desperately wishing for.{w} Footsteps were approaching.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It wasn't who I'd been expecting. Miiya and the Atsuki she'd been with were there, staring deep into my eyes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What the fuck...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What the fuck? Why are they here!? Miiya should be in the attic!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Hey, answer me! You really were here... Are you really me? What the fuck is going on!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I didn't think you'd be here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Wh-What!? What does that mean!? You're me, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I am.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What the fuck is happening, then!? I thought it was impossible that we'd see each other. Was that wrong?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: In a way, yes.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What the fuck...? Tell me, then! What's going on!? How the fuck can you even exist!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I'm sorry, I'm not sure how to answer that question.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What...!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I know exactly how you feel, I promise. I will tell you one thing, though, since we've already met: you shouldn't worry about anything.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It must be too early. When we appeared in this world, Shiroya spent a short while on the crystal floor. It must not be time yet.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I shouldn't worry? There's no way you're actually me, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...I am. I promise, it will all be fine.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Wh-What...? How can you tell? And how would that even be possible!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I know how it sounds, but I genuinely don't have time to explain, and I'm not sure I could.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What does that even mean...!?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Look, we're the same person. Just trust me, or yourself, on this. Sincerely, everything should turn out fine.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: When he heard that, I saw my own body crumple down, and my heart ached. I didn't want to imagine how I felt.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You believe me, right? Like I said, I don't have much time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But that c-can't be the case...! Shiroya... died again!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Again? What do you mean?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Do you not know that? She was killed here, and her body disappeared from the lobby!
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: What...? What does that mean?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It can't be. She won't be in the tower.{w} This is the same as before! Someone is telling me that Shiroya's fate within the tower is death. Why have so many people said that!?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: It's not true! I've never seen her dead! That must be a mistake.{w} She'll be fine. It's impossible that she will die in the tower. We'll make sure of that.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: You should believe what I say. I still don't fully understand how that works, but you have to trust me.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...You can't explain it? Then there's no way you're actually telling the truth, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: I am. While I can't be fully confident about what I'm saying, I'll just ask you to believe me.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}Okay.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: ...Good. I suppose there's one thing you could do, then.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Wait here a second.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I turned around and went to the attic, where Miiya should've been.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya are still here. Neither of them were activated.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What the hell, then? I don't get what happened...!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: There was no time to wonder. After I grabbed the Future Sekimeiya, I dashed back out.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Take this, but don't touch it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I handed him the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You two should hurry back down. On the second floor, enter the second partition, leave the Sekimeiya on the floor, and wait there.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: On the second floor?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes. From there, if anyone passes by, you should hear them. If you hear the elevator four times, you can go back down and place the Sekimeiya in its cabinet. Make sure that it isn't activated again.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: However, it's possible that the first time, instead of hearing the elevator, you'll hear someone running up. If that happens, once you hear the elevator two times, you can go down and place the Sekimeiya in the cabinet.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I wasn't completely sure if Shiroya would walk up or take the elevator. However, a while after that, they would hear Erina and my past self taking it. That would be their cue to go down.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: O-Okay, and... after that, you're saying everything will be fine, right?
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: Yes. Wait patiently with everyone on the crystal floor and make sure to get out safely. I'll pray with you for what will happen after that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: All... All right.
entries.speaker: c2a

entries.text: The other Atsuki didn't waste time. As soon as he said that, he ran back toward the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Goodbye, Miiya.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It took all I had in me to say that and nothing more. It was a second goodbye. I would never see her again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Goodbye.
entries.speaker: m2

entries.text: Oblivious to the gravity of her farewell, she turned around and left my sight.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once I could no longer hear their running, I found myself standing alone. ...I couldn't bring myself to move.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If nothing happened very soon, I would've been wrong about everything.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I heard the elevator, all the tension within me was released. She was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She'd called the elevator from the crystal floor. I waited, and seconds later, I heard it again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait, what? Why did I hear it again? Doesn't that mean that it's going to the attic?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Oh, that's right! She had the key!
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I bolted off as fast as I could.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She was in the hallway. When she saw me, it was apparent we'd both been looking for each other.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There you are... You did come.{w} I'd forgotten you had the key to the attic.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you... the Atsuki from this morning?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah. I'm glad I wasn't wrong.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Y-You knew I would be here, right? You remembered what happened.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I nodded slowly. I was right about everything. ...We had reunited in a world other than our own.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Have you been here all this time? When you disappeared this morning, I tried to find you, but I was in another world, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I see. So she really is the same person who was here this morning.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I... think so. I learned a lot of things. It's been longer than you think since I saw you.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What do you mean? You said the recording was real, right? What happened at {time=21}? And why did both of us appear at the start of today?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Why did we travel to this morning?{w} I know the answer now.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I remember what you told me. You said you traveled to the 30th of November, and that a few days later, you touched the Sekimeiya in the tower. Is that right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Y-Yes. That's when I appeared with you in the lobby.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No, that's wrong. I know what happened to you.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She frowned. It seemed she hadn't entertained the possibility.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You didn't go to November... You went to the future.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Wh-What? No I didn't. I went two weeks to the past.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I don't know why you think that, but I believe you went to the future.{w} You said that you entered the tower in early December. I believe that was the 5th of January instead.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The 5th of January? That doesn't make any sense.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Like I said, the recording was real. On the 5th of January, we were in the tower. That's why I appeared with you in the lobby when you touched the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: N-No. No. How would I have gone to the future? There's no way.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: With the Sekimeiya. There were two of them.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I... know. I saw that too. What do you mean, though?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I've thought about everything that happened. There always were two Sekimeiya, but only one of them made us go to the past. The other one made us go to the future instead.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The one in the water tank sent you to the future, but that wasn't the first time. ...It wasn't the first time you'd traveled forward in time. There were others.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She looked astonished. For a while, she didn't respond.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A-Are you serious...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I am. I've been able to understand the Sekimeiya.{w} The Future Sekimeiya made us appear where we were in the past; I believe that could be part of your confusion. The Past Sekimeiya made us appear where we would be in the future.{w} ...And, if both ranges overlapped, the world around us would change instead.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: O{w=0.2}-Oh!{w=0.3} ...That makes sense. That's how I came back.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She stared off into the hallway, working with the information I'd given her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When she opened her mouth again, she asked what she most wanted an answer to.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: So... what now? What will happen at {time=21}?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It'll be fine. We'll be able to leave.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She breathed a sigh of relief. Everything could finally end.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This isn't over yet, though. We have to do one more thing.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...We{w=0.6} are going to save Miiya.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Wh-What? Really...?{w} Can the past really be changed after all!?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's not it. The past is set in stone.{w} But in a different world, the past is no different from the future for us.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Huh...?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We can save her in this world. If you travel, you can save her.{w} ...It has to be you, though.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What do you mean?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I walked to the kitchen. The recorder's timer showed 44:24.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That is the Past Sekimeiya. If you activate it when the timer reaches 63:14, you'll appear on November 30th. If you're there, Miiya will not die.{w} I can't come with you, though. If you activate it, anyone in the center of the building will go back to our world. If I travel to the past too, I won't be able to be there.{w} But, if it's you who does this, you will be. When December 15th comes, you'll be able to enter through the storeroom, and if you stay in the third partition on the fourth floor, you'll make it back to this point.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She looked overwhelmed. There was very little time left, so I was trying to explain everything rapidly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: W-Wait, so, I'll be able to prevent her death? And then, at this time, both of us will go back to our world?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: When I nodded, her eyes briefly widened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The seconds were passing quickly, so I had to make sure I could say everything I needed to.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You will appear on November 30th where you will be on December 30th. If you think about where you'll be, that's where you'll appear.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...What?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: On December 30th, you have to be in that gem shop so that you appear there in November.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: In the gem shop? I don't think that will be possible. ...It was still closed.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I-In that case, right outside it.{w} It was snowing on November 30th, wasn't it?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I bit my lip. I didn't know what would happen if she were to appear right on top of falling snow, given what had happened to me with the elevator's railing.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You'll have to be below a stone roof, where the snow won't hit you and there'll be none on the ground. Then, you'll be able to prevent Miiya from being hit by the explosion.{w} That's not all, though. There's something else very important. Your body can't be found.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: M-Mine?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I nodded, although I still didn't fully understand that. ...Why was her body the one that had to go missing? If the news had to be merely followed, why couldn't Miiya's be the one that wouldn't be found despite her well-being? ...The only reason it had to be Shiroya's was because I knew Miiya was in the tower. I still felt like there was something else to all of that.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Then, early on the 15th, you'll be able to enter the tower through the storeroom. You still have the rusty key, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Yes.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She showed it to me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You'll be able to stay in the third partition on the fourth floor. I know that'll work, because after {time=14}, you'll go to the sixth floor and leave some kind of indication for me under one of the drawers. The fifth desk from the left, in the first partition.{w} After that, you'll only need to leave momentarily at {time=15:30.} If you're in the floor 2 and 3 staircase, you'll avoid being inside the range of a travel. The range might actually reach the crystal floor, but if you're in a corner of the building a floor above, you'll avoid it. Just not in the crystal floor staircase since that's where I was at the time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: O-Okay...
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm sorry. There's not much time left.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: 50:06. I had to leave soon to escape the range, and I wasn't sure if I'd explained myself well at all. {tip=rush}Something about the rush I was in felt paradoxical{/tip}, but I had no time to try to think about it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let me check that nobody's in the bedrooms anymore. I don't know what happened to them, but someone might still be here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I looked at the four separate bedrooms, which were all vacant. Meanwhile, I felt my fingers beginning to tremble. Shiroya was there again, and it seemed as if the future finally had a distinct shape.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's it, then. Everything is ready.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It will work. I'm sure.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Y-Yeah.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Can I ask, though? ...Why are your clothes like this?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: O-Oh. I put them on hoping I would come back to the point you saw me.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Really? ...That's interesting.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: In fact, it seemed to go against most conclusions I'd made. There was no time to care, however.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait. You have the attic key. You should give it to me.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: You need it?
entries.speaker: s
