entries.text: No, but you will on January 26th. If I don't take it now, you won't be able to have it.{w} Because, at {time=21} today, the police will find you, and they'll take this key from you if you have it. I need to keep it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: And they won't take it if you have it?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...No.{w} I'd tell you why, but there's not enough time right now.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Five minutes were left until she would travel to the past. For me, I was five minutes away from returning to our world with her.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I grabbed the Past Sekimeiya and left it on the highest cabinet shelf, where it wasn't easy to see.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: If you activate it when it's there, in the instance that the people from this world come back up, it's possible they won't find it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I see.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...{w}I should go. I'm sure your future self is currently on the fourth floor. She's been there for hours.{w} You understand everything I said, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...I think so. When that screen says 63:14, I just have to touch the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You'll appear on the 30th, next to that gem shop.{w} I have to go now, but I guess I'm about to see you again. I'm sorry that there wasn't more time to explain.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: A-All right. I'll see you.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: But before I knew it, my body had jumped forward in a sudden impulse and was tightly embracing Shiroya. I couldn't stand the thought of anything going wrong from that point on.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Right next to my ear, I felt her surprised breath, and after the initial shock, her hands slowly tightened up behind me. I couldn't believe what was happening, but I took advantage of it and rested my head on her shoulder.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I wished the moment could go on forever, but the clock was ticking. When I let go of her, I couldn't bring myself to say anything else or even look directly at her again.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It was hard to turn around, but I had to. With my body still shaking, I trudged to the stairs, aware it was the last time my footprints would be left on that floor.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: 63 minutes. Shiroya tightly gripped the device that had once been found in Isla's purse while her heart raced from Atsuki's sudden hug.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Her other hand was reaching high above her, close to the Sekimeiya as she withstood the immense heat around it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She hadn't traveled to the past, but she was about to. She stared firmly at the numbers on the screen and gradually moved her hand deeper into the heat.{w} After fourteen more seconds had gone by, she felt the hard touch.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Light snow was falling on a dim street in Yushibana. Despite the few lit windows, not one of them saw the figure of a young girl appearing by the entrance of a house, below a stone roof.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She found herself leaning on the cold wall and rapidly looked down. There, she was able to see some of the footprints she'd once left.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She traced them up to an opaque door on the opposite side of the street. Wasting no time, she dashed over and opened it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Remnants of the smoke were in the air. It had already been released, but it wasn't too late.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On the floor, she saw the first two people to fall unconscious—those who had already escaped danger.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Behind the shelves were two girls. One was being protected by the wooden structures, whereas the other was an open target.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She crouched and grabbed the shoulders of the girl in red, shuffling backward to drop her behind the shield of shelves.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Once that danger was removed, she stood up and looked at her own body on the floor. She didn't know the exact time, but her work wasn't finished yet.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She picked herself up by her shoulders and began to retreat.{w} However, a slight sound caused her to spin around, and her heart skipped a beat.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She didn't see the door opening because a wooden shelf was blocking it. However, soon after she heard its squeaky sound, the lights turned off.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There was practically no time to react. During the instants before the light came back, the girl closed her eyes and attempted to cover her face with her arms.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The floor had been devastated, and she found herself falling with the rubble, the deadly light shrinking as she was consumed by familiar darkness.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She saw something shining above and heard very faint shouts. Her entire body was wracked with pain, but she was able to stand up.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When she looked around her, she saw there was light there too: an egg-shaped gemstone had rolled away, and it gave off a soft glow.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She heard a moan laced with pain. Her other self was conscious. She had been holding her as they'd fallen; that time, neither one of them had lapsed into a lengthy unconsciousness.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Her friend had told her something very important: her own body couldn't be found. She didn't understand why, but a realization immediately came to her.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As she took a slow step back, she saw her own self awakening. It was difficult to make out, but she saw that the other her was staring at the distant gemstone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That was when she understood... that the universe would do the rest—that she didn't have to enact something that was already meant to happen.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She stepped back. She knew the way out of there.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Meanwhile, the other girl approached the stone. The act of her touching it would be the {tip=force}driving force{/tip} behind a forthcoming attack in her town.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The girl found herself looking out upon a nostalgic view, but the snow was still piling up to form the scenery she'd once seen. Once more, she began walking to her empty apartment.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But when she realized that it would soon be December 1st, her destination changed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She had once felt a false sense of freedom walking down that path, but the kind she felt the second time was genuine; she knew where the path went.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It led to a place she hadn't thought existed, and one that she was eager to reach.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I arrived on the fourth floor and looked at the wall to my right. ...She had to be on the other side of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Nobody had been found, but... she was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened the door to the last partition.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: It's been a while.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Yeah.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: She rose from the chair she'd been sitting in, but she looked worn out. Although I had just left the attic, for her, that had happened fifteen days in the past.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: D-Did everything work out?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Before she could answer, we heard a noise.{w} It sounded like the elevator had opened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...ody's here! I... didn't pre—
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: Has it been enough time already?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: ...op the bleedi—
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I looked at Shiroya. We were back. It had really worked.{w} That was happening on the third floor, near the staircase. Our past selves had returned too, although they were unaware of it. Their voices hardly reached us, but I could understand them since I knew what they were saying.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...A-Ats—{w} ...not bleedi—
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: That's right. My past self was waiting outside the offices after traveling to the past. Right now, Shiroya's in the attic, and Sai's on the crystal floor.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What were you gonna say?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Um, everything did go well, but...{w} I saw Miiya earlier. She came in here once, and I'm pretty sure she saw me.{w} She didn't say anything, though. I almost froze from the shock, but before I could react, she had already left.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: R-Really?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: She nodded, still puzzled.{w} So, it really had been like that. It had happened as I'd imagined it.{w} I didn't get it. I'd known that she wouldn't be found thanks to the drawing under the drawer. Before seeing it, I hadn't come up with a reason to explain why Miiya hadn't found her, but at that point, I had realized that one wasn't needed. If she simply stayed there, she wouldn't be found. ...I still couldn't understand what had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What about the you from the other world? Is she okay?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. She wasn't found at the site of the explosion, but she wasn't harmed.{w} ...Why couldn't she be found?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...To match the news report that I saw. I did travel to November too, before you did, but I failed to accomplish anything.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I know. I saw you at the motel. I thought about staying there in case someone found me in my apartment.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You were there?{w} By the way, what keeps happening to your clothes? They're the ones you entered the tower with again, but you didn't have them when you went to the past.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, yeah. They're the ones from that world.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I see.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Ah. That time, right before {time=21}, I did think that something about her looked strange. It was so late into the day that I didn't realize it was the complete lack of smoke on her clothes. ...And her pendant is gone too—the thing that tied her with Miiya disappeared when she went to the future.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: She took a digital watch out of her purse.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You bought a watch? That's smart.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It's {time=19:37.}
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Shiroya pointed out very faint footsteps coming from the other side of the wall. Although I hadn't noticed them, I knew she was right.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's us. Myself, Sai, and Erina. We're going to the attic.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: They went around the floor and disappeared up the next staircase.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Now what, then? I don't know what happened at the end.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Let's go down first. I need to do something very important.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Okay.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I had very little strength within me, and Shiroya looked dizzy when she moved. We took our time walking down, knowing full well that there was nobody left beneath us.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Let's go to the security room.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Katei's dead body was there, filling the room with a stench I'd forgotten about. The monitors were working, which meant that someone had been there fifty minutes previously. Although it was slightly strange, I could barely bring myself to care.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Actually... I bet I know why. Only Sai could have used the computer, and not too long ago, he traveled to the past from the event room with Shiroya.{w} That would've disabled his watch, but the next time we saw him, it was working. Every time that happened, he came here to sync it with the computer's time. There was a drawer with a bunch of batteries.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What's that?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: A USB drive I brought to the tower in the other world. I have enough to put Katei and Akaro in jail with the footage on this.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Once the computer detected it, I saved two copies of the file. The normal folder with the saved footage was nowhere to be found, so I left them elsewhere. If necessary, I would reveal the location to the police. Then, I left the drive behind one of the drawers so that it could also be found.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: By the way, you left the rusty key outside the storeroom, right? Was that so that it wouldn't open from the inside?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's what I thought. Not completely sure how much sense it makes yet, but there's nothing I can do to fight it.{w} I have the rusty key right here too, by the way, but there's a slight problem. I'll need it on January 5th, and since you gave up yours, you'll also need this one on December 30th.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh, I guess so.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I looked under the desk. A Sekimeiya was there.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This is the Past Sekimeiya. My past self traveled with it very recently in the staff room, and Sai brought it here. It doesn't have a lot of power right now.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I left the rusty key on the floor of hallway A and closed the door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We need to duplicate it. Otherwise, we won't be able to have it on those days.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...{w}She didn't seem to know why that was the case.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'll go a very short distance back in time one last time. Since I left the key outside this room, my past self will be able to grab it and have it in the future. But since that will let me appear with it, I won't have to really grab it, which will duplicate it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Will that actually work?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes.{w} As soon as I leave, open the door.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...All right.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I stepped back and touched the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The light went out, but I knew where I was before I looked around me.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The mechanical room.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I confirmed that the rusty key was in my pocket.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When I went to hallway A, I saw it on the floor too.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I didn't have to wait very long until the security room opened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There we go, now we have two. Take this one.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: The movements of the rusty key were interesting. Shiroya had found it on January 5th, in our world. Then, she had traveled to December 15th and had still been holding it. Later, she had traveled to November 30th and had still been holding it. However, she'd used it to lock the storeroom from outside in the other world, which meant it couldn't be recovered.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: When we had talked, she had told me about its location, so I'd been able to find it in the other world's security room as well. That was the key we had just duplicated.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, it was the one she ended up with, and it was the one she would have on January 26th. As a result, when she had appeared on the 15th, she hadn't been holding the same key she'd found. The fact that she'd had to leave it outside the storeroom had made it transform.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What she'd appeared with had been a mesh of both. To obtain that key, both had been needed, and in a single instant, it had changed from the key of our world to the key of the other world.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The powered-off Sekimeiya was on the floor, so I put it back where I'd found it; there was no reason to do otherwise.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: We need to go to the mechanical room. The others will come back soon.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It's {time=19:45.} I'll travel to the past soon.{w} ...Sorry, to the future.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah. They must be coming down already.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: So, you stayed at Eagle Motel too?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yes. I was there until today. I didn't realize the owner wasn't a native.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: We heard people above us. The group was beginning their wait near the shutter.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Will it be fine if we stay here?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Hm... Not quite.{w} Once you leave for the bathroom, they'll search everywhere for you.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Wait, are they going to see us? They can't, right?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No. If my past self saw me, that'd be a paradox.{w} But there's no simple way out of this. The Future Sekimeiya will be powered off and Sai will stay next to it when it repowers, and the Past Sekimeiya will send us too far to hide us since it'll build up energy until your past self leaves. I doubt touching it twice would work due to the powered-off time.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: It was a very similar dilemma to the one I'd faced when searching the drawers for a marking. However, the answer was much clearer.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Ah, I need to be found, then. If they find me, the search will stop before they realize you're here.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I nodded in the darkness.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That's what you said, right? That I was still here even after I'd traveled from the bathroom.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: But what about at {time=21}? The shutter won't move, will it?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No, it will.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: What? Didn't you say that the recording was real?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yes, but before the exit opened, we went to the future. We appeared on January 5th, where the recording occurred.{w} So, if you're out of that range, you'll stay here and be able to leave.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Oh... that's what happened.{w} Where will the range be?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Here. Just before {time=21:05}, Erina is going to activate it. The Future Sekimeiya has yet to be brought here.{w} It won't be a normal travel, though. When she touches it, she'll trigger a chain reaction that will bring us to January 5th. We'll go twenty minutes to the future repeatedly. Akaro will appear a bit later because he traveled directly from today to January 5th after escaping from the bedroom with Sai.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: W-Wait, a chain reaction...? Do we just have to avoid being here when that happens?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...{w}Not being here twenty minutes before it's activated would also avoid it.{w} It won't be so simple, though...{w} Only you will be able to do that.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Hm? ...Wh-Why?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: The people above us will search for you soon. They'll find you, and then the shutter will open. You can leave this place.{w} I can't do that, though. There's something very important that still has to happen.{w} On January 5th, I'll have to be in the tower in order to appear on November 24th with the Sekimeiya. If I stay here, I'll travel to the future one more time. That's when I'll finally be able to leave.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Can't you just enter through the storeroom on the 5th?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: No... there are a few reasons why I can't.{w} The 5th is 21 days away. It's possible that getting out today will prevent me from being in the tower in the future.{w} I don't know what the police will do. If they find any evidence that incriminates me, being here on the 5th might not be possible. I'm sure my parents will keep trying to make me leave with them too. ...Staying here is the only way to guarantee it, and it's what I thought I'd do before I touched the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Technically, I knew I'd be in Yushibana on January 26th, but my parents had spent the previous two weeks telling me to go live with them. I feared they would give me no option after what had happened in the tower and force me to leave town until after January 5th.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: There are more reasons too. If both of us leave, the attic key will be taken from us, and we need it on the 26th. Leaving it somewhere until the 5th is risky, so I can just bring it there myself.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...You're right. When I traveled to the 15th, I had the attic key, but the cabinet key was the only one that wasn't in my purse. I still don't get that.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: The cabinet key? If the police found you with it, they would take it, so the only way to get it to the 26th would be by doing the same thing as with the attic's.{w} Did you ever need to unlock the cabinet?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...No. I don't think so.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I see. That's why, then. There's no reason to bring it to the 26th, so you didn't appear with it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Wait, so can't I do the same? We can both travel to the 5th.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: That's not true. On November 30th, you appeared outside the gem shop, right?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: ...Yes.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: So, on December 30th, you'll be out of the tower. That's why you can't stay here.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: I... see.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: It'll be fine. I'll just take a little longer.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Yeah.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: You can stay at my house too. At least you'll be with Maxi and Umi.{w} You were on January 5th once already, right? Was the tower not open?
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: N-No. I don't know why, but it seems it won't open again after today.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: ...Yeah, that's what I thought.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: There was a mountain of things I wanted to tell her, but we went silent for a while. Both of us were even more tired than we appeared, and we had to speak very quietly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Everything we'd gone through since we'd stepped into the tower was like an endless expanse of tangled web. I could hardly even recall what things had been like before I knew what the Sekimeiya were capable of.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But we had taken that day to its conclusion. Without any doubt, we were going to make it end.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: People had died in horrible ways. I didn't expect that the outside world would ever learn the full truth of what had happened within the tower, but at the very least, Shiroya and I knew. We had built a better reality out there through our own actions.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Surprisingly, I wasn't sad that the world where we had saved Miiya wasn't our own. Ours wasn't perfect, and I had no idea what awaited us in the future... but all I wanted was to step outside with Shiroya.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They'll leave soon. There's only forty minutes left.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Yeah. They'll go to the attic and come back down.{w} By the way, can I borrow your watch? It'll be useful to have it.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Take it.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Thanks.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Our wait was short. When the time came, we heard the group walking to the hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I guess I'll go.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: All right. I'll see you soon.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Are you going to stay here? You won't be seen?
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'm sure I'll be fine.
entries.speaker: a

entries.text: Okay.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: I'll see you.
entries.speaker: s

entries.text: Her shadowy figure slowly faded up the stairs.{w} I recalled the time we'd found her drowsy in room A1 and the words she'd told me in hallway C... They were words I'd hated before, but they had grown to bring me happiness.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The next time I heard sounds above me, she was already with them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stayed behind the piled furniture in the corner of the room. Like I'd expected, a single person came down soon after.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't see who they were, but it had to be Sai. He seemed to be looking around in the dark.{w} I feared he would find me until his movements slowed down. He kneeled under a table and stopped.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I bet he's looking for a good place to hide the Sekimeiya. Did he find one under that table?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I was doing my best to conceal my breathing, but he remained there for a long time. Finally, he seemed to decide he was done and walked up the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hardly had time to exhale before he was back. There was a glaring difference—the area between his hands was glowing.{w} Once more, he kneeled under the table and ran back up the stairs as soon as he was finished.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The Sekimeiya wasn't simply on the floor. From what I could see, he had tucked it just under the surface of the table—there seemed to be a tiny space where he'd left it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...{w}Now, my past self will find the Past Sekimeiya in the security room, and we'll all wait out the last few minutes in the lobby.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stared at the glowing numbers on the watch until {time=21:01} came. At that point, someone began to carefully descend the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: While I couldn't see their face, I knew it was Erina. She stood still until something caught her eye.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Perhaps Sai thought he had found a good hiding spot, but he hadn't factored in the mechanical room's darkness. The faint illumination gave it away after Erina looked around a little.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She approached it and crouched. Her figure covered the light, and suddenly, it was gone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wh—
entries.speaker: aki

entries.text: However, Erina was still there. Her outline had disappeared because the light had moved.{w} The faint ceiling light had turned off, and the Sekimeiya's glow couldn't be seen.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I hadn't felt anything myself, but I knew. I was on January 5th of 2012. Since I'd been in the mechanical room during both recurring locations, I had traveled seamlessly, and as my vision was more adjusted to the darkness, I could make out that a few pieces of furniture had moved slightly.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Oblivious, Erina crawled out. To her, the Sekimeiya had simply disappeared. Then, she walked to the stairs, likely thinking she had traveled to the past.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...It's still there; the Sekimeiya's on the floor. It rolled up to the wall.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Hey! What's going on!?
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: That time, when the door to the lobby opened, light didn't fill the stairs—the whole building was devoid of it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: The watch still showed {time=21:03}, but that was far from the real time. I could hear the others shouting above me. The shutter wasn't opening.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I can't get out yet. I'll need to have both Sekimeiya after the watch shows {time=22:30.}
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I was forcing Shiroya to wait, but I had to stay there for a little while longer.{w} When {time=21:50} came, I approached the stairs.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: At that time, my past self had traveled to the past. The others were soon to notice my absence.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I grabbed the Future Sekimeiya and stepped up the stairs. I could no longer see the walls of the lobby, but unfortunately, I knew I'd have to see them once more in the future.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't shake off the anticipation of stepping out. Even though I'd already left once before, it didn't feel like it.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked to the crystal room the past me had traveled from, B5. After feeling the floor, I realized that the powered-off Past Sekimeiya was there.{w} For the time being, I went to the crystal room at my right and put both inside a temperature regulation cabinet, setting it to where I believed 0 °C was. It seemed the curtains were all still raised.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I could've gone to the attic, but the last thing I wanted was to have to explain myself to anyone. ...My sole desire was for the final few minutes to elapse.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I walked to the lobby. I could feel the shutter with my hands.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I'd waited patiently all day, but I couldn't take it anymore. I needed time to move faster. The goal was right there, and I was the only person who knew.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...Minutes after I had started staring at Shiroya's watch, I heard voices in the far hallway.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...tsuki! Where the fuck—
entries.speaker: q4

entries.text: I kept looking down. It was already past {time=22.}
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Wait... are they actually searching for me?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Sai's yells got closer and closer. It seemed he was looking in every room.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: This piece of shit! The Sekimeiya's not in the cabinet!
entries.speaker: sai4

entries.text: Fuck. There's no way he'll find them, right?
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Look! I found the Sekimeiya!
entries.speaker: sai4

entries.text: What?{w} No. That's the third one.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: He had found it in another room in hallway B. He had plenty of energy to spare, as I heard him running to the event room and leaving it there. Fortunately, that caused him not to find the real ones.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki! I know you're here!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I didn't move. The darkness was all I needed to stay hidden.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He went to the mechanical room. Maybe he noticed the Sekimeiya he'd hidden was no longer there, but he didn't say anything. Afterward, he walked back with the others.{w} Akaro was there. Hopefully, the recording of him had been obtained by the police.{w} Erina and Isla were the last two. Their stories had been tragic in different ways. They were together again, but it was possible that Erina would never understand that the Isla she'd entered the tower with was gone.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What is going to happen with them? The police must've found her corpse, but now they'll see that she's still alive. ...I suppose the case is similar with Naomi.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I felt their voices fading. They were going back up.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Now that I think about it, it was when I traveled to {time=21:00} that my hand injury disappeared. Even though I only went 45 minutes to the past, it took me many days to reach the proportional future.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Right now, I have Shiroya's watch and the rusty key. When I was briefly at {time=21:00}, I might not have realized that. However, after Shiroya made me travel to the 15th, there's no way I had them.{w} I suppose that makes sense since that location was based on a point much farther into the future. That's still a little strange, though, because Shiroya did have the rusty key.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: I stopped myself there. I really didn't care anymore. No matter how many details had flown far over my head, I didn't care about any of them.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I stood there for what seemed like hours, but eventually, {time=22:30} came.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I tried to force myself to breathe properly. It wasn't over yet.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In the staff room, there was a keyring that I needed and I could obtain. I already had it in my pocket, though.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...I forgot that I need to go to the attic. I thought I'd never see that place again.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: When I'd thought up the loop to appear on November 24th, I'd imagined appearing with the Sekimeiya in a suitcase. The one in the security room was locked away, so I had to get the one on the attic's sofa.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I left the watch behind so that it wouldn't cast any light and gradually ascended. Every floor was dark, and my steps echoed more loudly than I liked.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Once I reached the highest door, I saw that the living room was empty.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was leaving my footprints behind, but it didn't matter. Once I'd taken the suitcase, I dashed back, leaving that place for good.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I took both Sekimeiya from the cold of the cabinet with my bare hands. The instant I activated them, I traveled the smallest fraction of time. Enough for it to have no real effect.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With the suitcase in hand, I descended to the lobby and sat on the floor. Then, I put the Sekimeiya inside it and placed both of my hands on them.{w} I suddenly realized a key had fallen from my pocket before I'd even taken it out willingly...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...That had been my plan before I'd gone to the 24th. I'd wanted to appear with the Sekimeiya, but for that, they had to be powered off in the future. It was very hard to calculate the exact second I needed to have them, so the position I was in was a good way to cover a longer stretch of time.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Every time a Sekimeiya powered on, my hands would immediately power it off, resulting in no effect whatsoever. Furthermore, they emitted no light, so nobody could see me in the dark.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: However, I had calculated enough... I only had to be there for ten more minutes.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: They were the last ten minutes I'd spend trapped in that place. The suitcase was on my lap, and both of my hands were planted firmly on the Sekimeiya's surfaces, too far apart to overlap their minuscule ranges.{w} ...It was the end. I knew I was in the position where I'd appeared on the 24th.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I couldn't check the time anymore; the watch was hidden behind the reception desk. Instead, I counted the seconds inside my head.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...She's there right now. I'm sure.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Time had passed. It hadn't frozen—it hadn't forbidden me from taking the final step.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I closed the suitcase and stood up, grabbing the fallen key. Before anything else, I went to retrieve Shiroya's watch.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I opened the hallway A door. Each step I took toward the storeroom was more surreal than the last. I took out the rusty key and suddenly understood why I wouldn't have it on the 26th.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was there; I could feel the dusty couch, and the wall wasn't blocking my way.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: With bated breath, I approached the final door—the one that could only be opened from the outside.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: ...And it was open.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki, you son of a bitch! Open the fucking door!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I know you just left! I heard you talking with Shiroya! You better come back right now!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Atsuki! Piece of shit!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: I'll convince everyone this was all your doing if you don't open this fucking door!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: At least tell the police we're here! I'm fucking hungry, man!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: ...I don't think he's coming.
entries.speaker: ak

entries.text: Can you just shut up?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Atsuki! You think I won't tell them that you left with the Sekimeiya!? This is your last chance to come back!
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: "Atsuki!"{w=1.1}{nw}
entries.speaker: saicenter

entries.text: While in a tip, saving and search jumps are disabled.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: An orb is used when an inline tip is not viable.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This could be to explain the setting, the chapter name, and so on.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world B, Katei assures the group that the event room, hallway A, and hallway B are the only places where the smoke was released. Despite the confidence behind his words, he misses room A5.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This doesn't happen in world C, as in that one, he had time to look through the crystal floor. In world B, though, after hearing a sound in room B4, Katei was forced to stay with Erina's group.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The reason why he doesn't mention room A5 is something that happened when Xyn was crafting their plan.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Finally, both subordinates understood how serious their boss was and broke into a sweat. As they took off and draped their heavy attire on the back of their chairs, they began to process each step of what they would be performing."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Katei was listening to Xyn putting together their plan, Ido eventually took off and leaned against his coat. That prevented Katei from clearly listening to the final part of their plan: the gemstones to be used as a fake out.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Even though the first six floors of the tower were searched through, nobody was found. Not because there was nobody to find, though—Naomi A was in the building.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In addition, she didn't have the attic key, so even though the last floor wasn't inspected, nobody was there. Why wasn't she found?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: During the search, Sai heard the elevator three times. That was Akaro's doing, but there's still an unexplained mystery: the starting position of the elevator.{w} It should've been on floor 5. Akaro knew that, so that's where he sent it in the end. However, before he called it, it was below the third floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Naomi A was responsible for that. She was aware another self of hers had been murdered, and she wanted to easily escape if she had to. She called it when everyone was on the crystal floor, and soon after that, she accidentally made a noise while trying to understand what the others were doing in the event room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That caused a search on the crystal floor, which Naomi A escaped by using the elevator so that she wouldn't be seen on the stairs. The elevator isn't very fast, so she took it to the second floor, where she waited to see if she'd be followed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Not long after that, the group went up to inspect the whole building, and they all stayed on different floors. Unable to access the attic, Naomi was cornered.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She went up a floor every time someone else did. When she saw Akaro staying on the fourth, she stopped. She had seen him gone from the event room when she'd awakened, and she didn't think he had killed her other self. Most importantly, Naomi realized that if she kept going up, she could end up stuck on Katei's floor, and she suspected him of her own murder.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Ready to be found by Akaro, Naomi stayed in the partitions of the fourth floor. However, he never came.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Sai travels to the past, he appears with the Future Sekimeiya in his hip pack. While unaware of this, he hides the fake Sekimeiya from the event room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Later, once he slips away from Atsuki, he proceeds to hide the Future and Past Sekimeiya. Even later, he obtains the Future Sekimeiya from the cleaning room and puts it in his hip pack.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That is the reason why he had appeared with it before, but if you follow his movements, you will notice that something is odd: Sai got the Future Sekimeiya from the cleaning room because he had appeared with it earlier and had hidden it there. However, he had appeared with it because he would have it in the future, which would only be possible because he had appeared with it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...Where exactly does this start? When does the Future Sekimeiya enter this cycle?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There are a handful of similar riddles left to be uncovered, and the answer is often different for each individual case.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Sai left the attic after Atsuki and Shiroya, he had a plan in mind. He traveled to the past from room B3 and appeared with the Future Sekimeiya on his person. However, due to what his plan entailed, he would've had the Future Sekimeiya in the future if it hadn't appeared in his hip pack.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Every time Sai travels to the past, the date of his watch changes to "9999-12-31", and its screen turns blank. This behavior will be one of the toughest questions Atsuki will face.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It seems to contradict the Sekimeiya's mechanics: infinite loops are needed to max out the watch's clock, yet the physical state of the watch doesn't deteriorate. This also happens with other devices such as the voice recorder and the digital clock in Eagle Motel.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What's the reason behind it? Unfortunately, Atsuki didn't come close to the right answer, as it's related to something he never considered.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What Shiroya saw next to the Future Sekimeiya were smoke grenades. Not only the one Akaro had left there initially, but all of them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: To conceal evidence, Akaro later brought the handful of grenades to the cleaning cart, and the moment that Shiroya made it disappear, they disappeared as well.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You might be wondering what happened in world C, where the cart never disappeared but no grenades were found.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In that world, Akaro also had the chance to put all the grenades in the cart. Then, they were never found, the same way Ido's set of keys wasn't found.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the lower bedroom, Sai had an idea about how he could escape the locked room they had set up. He only needed Katei to be distracted for an instant—he didn't want him to leave.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai told him that Atsuki had been threatening them. At first, Katei didn't believe a word of it.{w} However, Akaro quickly realized that Sai might've needed his assistance: Sai was claiming that Akaro had been threatened as well, and he could easily deny it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Akaro confirmed it, Katei's look changed.{w} He didn't believe it. He'd seen Akaro's first reaction; they were lying. Most importantly, Akaro was claiming that Atsuki had been behind the attack, and Katei knew who Akaro was.{w} ...Why? Did both of them suspect that Katei was behind Isla's death? Perhaps they wanted to see whether he could accept another version of events—if he denied it without considering it, he might've given himself away.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Katei yelled Atsuki's name as he climbed up, unaware that the door of the bedroom was opening while his shouts concealed the sound.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Where did Sai's knife come from?{w} Originally, it belonged to Suripo.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After his death in world C, Akaro heard a sound coming from hallway A: it was Katei, who had appeared in the security room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Akaro entered the hallway and prevented him from seeing the scene in the lobby. However, he hadn't had enough time to get rid of the knife, which he had under his shirt.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Later, when the group world switched to world A, Akaro finally had the chance to leave it behind after removing his fingerprints. It was there where Sai found it, after Shiroya pulled him to that world. Soon afterward, Sai returned to world B by world switching alone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The knife eventually ended up in Shiroya B's hands, but it vanished from existence when she traveled to December 30th with it in her purse.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki is able to find the right bedroom's key in the drawer, so had Sai failed to grab it? Had Sai ignored the fact that they could've locked themselves inside that room?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai thought he was still chasing Atsuki A, who had punched him in the face. The moment Atsuki A had run away, Sai had taken both bedroom keys to prevent him from staying inside one.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When the chase shifted to world B, Sai was unaware the world around him had changed. He entered the attic with the attic key from world A, and he didn't take the bedroom keys because he thought he had already taken them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Later, when he and Shiroya traveled to the attic's bedroom, Sai appeared with both bedroom keys, and they were still the ones from world A.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: By the way, you never reattached the chain, right?
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: The chain? What are you talking about?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Nothing.
entries.speaker: sai

entries.text: Sai had detached the bedroom chains in world A to prevent Atsuki from hiding in one, so that was further confirmation that the world around him had changed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Sai delivers a fatal blow to Shiroya, he stares at her fallen corpse. Something doesn't seem to make sense from his point of view.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He had already stated it as fact before—Shiroya would die. He had seen her corpse in world A, so he was certain that death was her inevitable fate.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The reason behind Sai's sudden confusion lies behind Shiroya's cause of death. When he saw her corpse in the lobby, he didn't see any physical wound. However, he'd just sliced the knife across her chest.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That causes Sai's momentary puzzlement, but he is able to instantly shrug it off and move on to his second victim.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai couldn't explain his recent experiences, but he was sure that something had happened to the world. The Atsuki who had punched him wasn't the same one he was speaking with, and the green lights on the cameras indicated that the state of the world was changing.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He recognized that the Atsuki in front of him was the same person he'd been with since that morning, and by hearing what he said, Sai began to slightly comprehend what had happened.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The first time the world had changed had been when both Sekimeiya had disappeared in room B6. Curious, Sai asked if that was where Atsuki and Shiroya had found the Sekimeiya, and upon having that confirmed, he learned something important.{w} Both Sekimeiya had been left behind there, and Atsuki and Shiroya had activated the one outside the drawer. That told Sai not only that they had gone to the future, but that when they had returned, someone had taken it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, they thought that the Sekimeiya had teleported to the drawer, when in truth, that one had also been there all along. Sai knew that the Sekimeiya in the event room was the past one and that he needed to use it in order to put together a plan he quickly came up with to take advantage of Atsuki's and Shiroya's story.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai is referring to the forum thread that Vaisude had posted in November. Back then, Sai had replied to it in a frivolous way, but it didn't take long for the Sekimeiya event to be announced. By the time that happened, the thread had already been locked.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Something was going to happen on December 15th—Sai knew that, and as proven by worlds A and C, he would've gone to the event even if he hadn't read that forum thread.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, in world B, the possibility of time travel was in his mind since the start. The moment that Atsuki traveled to the past, two things were confirmed to Sai.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: One: at one point during the day, a very large travel would occur. He had to be careful if he didn't want to be sent to November 24th, and he knew that traveling so far to the past would be possible.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Two: the forum poster was somewhere around them. During the twelve hours in the tower, Sai kept wondering who "7md_ag" could be.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At {time=10:04}, Katei had disabled the camera in room B4. He'd hidden both Sekimeiya there, so alongside removing the incriminating footage, he'd surreptitiously shut that camera down so that he could retrieve them later.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Atsuki and Shiroya found Katei's corpse, a message was on the computer: {time=10:04}: Camera(s) disabled and associated footage erased.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It had been there since Erina had attempted to display the footage from room B4. In other words, the message was only addressing that particular camera—none of the others had been disabled, as shown by the presence of the green lights.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki double-clicked on the camera selected on the list: "RECAM_12_01". It was the one Erina had attempted to display, so he was met with the same error.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Miiya noticed something when she world switched to world B. The camera in room B4 didn't have a green light, while all the others did.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When worlds C and B meet, neither of their perspectives makes sense to the other. If you recall everything that happened in world C, you will understand the meaning behind all of Sai's and Akaro's words.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Before them, the two bodies that had vanished reappeared: Shiroya and a bloody Erina. In addition, they thought Shiroya had died weeks in the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Given the blood on Erina's clothes, what Sai and Akaro instantly assumed was that she was the body that had disappeared from next to the crystal floor stairs.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Well, you're not dead after all, but we felt your pulse..."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And according to Erina, she didn't remember what had happened before she'd been attacked. Even though she was talking about a different attack, that led to Sai's strange statement: "Not even you have been here since {time=9}!"
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Of course, Erina and Isla have been here the whole time, but not you." She was not thought to be the same Erina who'd been with them since the morning, as the way she'd come into existence was still a mystery to them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Atsuki dashes out of the elevator, his eyes are closed due to the intense pain. That prevents him from seeing the trail of his own blood going from the storeroom toward the stairs.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Later, that helps him mistakenly believe that he altered history, as he never saw a result of his actions after deciding to try to change the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki finds the event room to be cold—the glass of the cabinet isn't properly shut.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It had been open since Erina had taken the Future Sekimeiya out before world switching to world C. After the group's departure, the Sekimeiya fell to the floor, and the glass was not closed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Two people entered the event room before Atsuki's return: Sai and Atsuki A.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Both of them noticed the cold, but neither of them closed the cabinet. Atsuki A touched the Future Sekimeiya and world switched to world C. Sai, who had locked Shiroya inside a bedroom a second time, arrived after Atsuki's vanishing and took the Sekimeiya from the floor, hiding it in the women's bathroom.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The smell released by the Sekimeiya as it gathered energy was often perceived in Ashiya Tower. It became the building's scent, and everyone grew used to it subconsciously.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, numerous times, the intensity of the smell seemed to increase. Why did this occur?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If the group spent hours in the attic, upon walking down to the crystal floor, if one of the Sekimeiya had been gathering energy there, the smell would seem more prominent.{w} But that's not all. Noticing the smell often indicated something else.{w} A world switch.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Atsuki and Erina were in world C, both real Sekimeiya were in the attic, so after returning to world B, Atsuki sensed that the smell was strangely strong.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Atsuki travels to the past, he notices that blood has stopped coming out of his injury. Additionally, he feels very tired.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The relation between those results is direct: the body he appeared in had lost a lot of blood.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, he never actually bled all that blood, so why did he appear in a body that had lost it?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Not only that, but the injury was still there, so why was no more blood coming out of it?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Before the time he will reach the replicated location in the future, Atsuki will rush to the crystal floor stairs and reopen his wound. To keep blood from flowing, he will bandage his hand with toilet paper.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That might help you answer the second question, but what about the first? When was all that blood lost? There's still a bit of time for you to find that answer.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai claims to have heard Atsuki's door slam, but that is not the truth. When Atsuki made that noise, Sai was in the process of traveling to the future; Erina's world switch brought him back to the attic's bedroom, where Shiroya had been trapped.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Why did he say that he had heard it, then?{w} He thought that Atsuki was testing him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He thought that the intent behind that question was to figure out whether he had traveled to the future and whether such a thing was possible. To prevent Atsuki from learning the truth, he claimed to have heard a sound he could only have heard if he'd traveled to the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Erina's mood seems to have changed since Atsuki left...
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When she made Atsuki and Shiroya world switch, to them, it seemed as if the Sekimeiya teleported to its cabinet—a Sekimeiya was there in world C.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was the fake Sekimeiya that the people of that world had left there before Miiya went to sleep in the attic. However, you might've noticed something strange.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Later in that world, when Atsuki and Miiya went down after waiting on the second floor, the cabinet in the event room was empty. ...Who took the fake Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Very few people would've had the chance, and it was Erina B who did. When her group arrived in world C, Atsuki went to the staff room to check if the Sekimeiya had disappeared from Ido's locker. He was followed by Shiroya, which gave Erina the perfect opportunity to silently take the fake Sekimeiya from the unlocked cabinet and put it in her purse.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She still wanted to travel to the past, so she calmly waited with the others while she thought that the Sekimeiya she had was gathering energy.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When she and Atsuki stopped on the third floor and returned to world B, Atsuki took the elevator down, and a future self of his appeared from the partitions, claiming to have traveled to the past and stopped the wound's bleeding.{w} "Wait... What? There's no way." Erina couldn't help but react that way, as she had the Sekimeiya in her purse.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The moment Atsuki left her alone next to the elevator, she reached inside her purse and attempted to travel through time. The Sekimeiya was there, but of course, nothing happened. That disappointment caused Erina's unresponsiveness when Atsuki returned with Sai.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This also erased the fake Sekimeiya in world C and led to the existence of two in world B. Erina soon got rid of hers, but the one that Akaro A had hidden was still in the building, and it was the one that the police found at {time=21.}
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Miiya feels as if she recognizes the smell in the gem shop, yet she isn't able to determine what it is... What exactly was in the air?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The answer is that two different smells were blending together—the smell of gas and the Sekimeiya's scent.{w} Miiya partly recognized the gas in the air, but due to the Sekimeiya's alien smell, she wasn't able to realize what it was.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On December 15th, Miiya and Shiroya were exposed to the Sekimeiya's smell once again, and they almost felt as if they'd smelled it once before.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Eden is a perfect world that was given to Adam and Eve. In this world, everyone who was trapped in the tower survived, and Shiroya, who was thought to have died, reappeared on her birthday.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It's a world that was given to Atsuki and Miiya, and just like Eden, it might look perfect at first glance; it's exactly what Atsuki and Shiroya wanted in world B.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...But that is far from the case. Eden is a world doomed to fail.{w} Not only that, but it is a single step away from disaster. It only requires the forbidden fruit.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The way Akaro initially portrays himself is quite different in worlds B and C. In world B, he hurries Naomi to unlock the cabinet.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "We know, and don't need this introduction, so let's move along. You've been praising this find of yours in every advertisement. Let's see how your claims hold up."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world C, however, he does the opposite. He stops Naomi to buy time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The reason is the same in both cases: the smoke bombs were timed to go off very soon. In world B, he didn't want them to go off before the cabinet unlocked, while in world C, he didn't want them to go off after the cabinet opened so that there was no staining on the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What causes the time difference between both worlds is the talk Atsuki and Shiroya have in hallway B before entering the event room. As such a thing doesn't occur in world C, Akaro is forced to take action, and after proving himself knowledgeable about Ashiya, he maintains that image, telling the group about Xyn as soon as they regain consciousness.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Katei questions out loud if Atsuki could've been the one to power off the computer. Once the conversation ends, he will talk to Miiya privately and tell her that Atsuki is lying to her. A bit later, even Sai will say something similar.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In both cases, the answer relies on Atsuki B, who was also in the building. You might recall that he thought Katei must have seen him when he crossed through floor 2 holding the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Aware of the Sekimeiya's powers, Katei could understand that his sighting of Atsuki was related to it. That's why he attempts to push the narrative that Atsuki was behind the computer's shutdown, certain that he was the one to take the fake Sekimeiya from the event room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Miiya doesn't notice that the Atsuki she's talking to is a different person than moments prior in the security room. Atsuki C had traveled to the future with Sai, and before his return, Atsuki B had occupied his place.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Some time after Sai and Atsuki C had appeared in the future, Sai had noticed that the elevator was open. Once he shut its door, it immediately ascended, as Atsuki had called it while trapped inside the attic.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai and Atsuki met, but neither of them said that they had traveled through time. When Atsuki saw the time on Sai's watch, the idea that he had traveled to the past was reinforced: before traveling, Sai had disappeared to check if the Sekimeiya he'd hidden in the storeroom had powers as well, so it made sense to find him separated from the group in the past. For Sai, it meant that he had traveled alongside Atsuki when he'd been going back to the event room; he learned that more than one person could travel at once.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When they returned to the security room, both of them believed that they had been gone for mere minutes, and they were not aware that an Atsuki had been with the group since their departure. That's why numerous things that Atsuki C says conflict with what Atsuki B did.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki B estimated that Atsuki C had traveled twenty minutes through time, but that wasn't that accurate. When Atsuki C gave his version, he said he traveled "a few minutes" to the past, aware that it couldn't have been as many as twenty because the attic had been locked.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Oh, yeah, it was earlier. Sai used it." Unaware that they'd talked about the elevator in the security room, Atsuki C affirms that Sai closed it—it's no speculation.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Later on, Miiya and Atsuki C will be in the mechanical room, and a similar situation will arise with neither of them noticing; Atsuki C doesn't know the theory that Atsuki B brought up regarding the Sekimeiya's power storage and will hear it for the first time from Miiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "We don't know how long it's been here for, so it might not be a good idea."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "What do you mean?"
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Well, if the time you travel depends on how long it spends out of the cabinet, you could go really far back."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Oh... Hm, I see."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai raises a good point: how is Katei able to know that he was missing for three hours?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Even though Sai accuses him of having left the building, the truth is that he had traveled to the future with Suripo. That doesn't answer the question, though. How is he able to tell how long he's been absent for?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The past location that was replicated was from the time Suripo was in the lobby. At that time, Katei was in the security room, so that's where he appeared.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What he immediately saw was the BIOS screen that Atsuki and Miiya had left behind, which displayed the current time and revealed to him that he had traveled to the future.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The reason why Akaro takes the walkie-talkie is not to try to repair it. What he wants is to justify the fingerprints that the police would have found on its surface.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Something similar happened in world B, although it was Katei who thought of it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Before Naomi A's body was found, he brought the suitcase from hallway C to the security room; he realized that he hadn't touched it when they'd found it, so he wanted everyone to see him touching it and leaving fingerprints.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Why does Isla call Miiya "Tanya"? Wasn't that Shiroya's nickname?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On November 30th, Atsuki bought both girls matching pendants. Even though they weren't real tanzanite, they were a convincing fake.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Miiya and Shiroya were wearing the pendant in their respective worlds, so Isla came up with the nickname "Tanya" for both of them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In room A1, Atsuki C met with Atsuki B, who took over the search and temporarily acted like Atsuki C. Minutes after that, Atsuki C timidly approached the storeroom and found everyone beside the secret door. There, he learned that he had completed the whole search without finding anything.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That was all the information he had, so every time he was accused of having ignored something on purpose, he couldn't directly reference the search, as he wasn't sure about how it had unfolded. That's why he asks Miiya if she knows where the Sekimeiya could be, just in case she is aware of a potential hole in a search he didn't witness.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: How many dichotomies were altered in this scenario?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai claimed that the Sekimeiya's main two powers, traveling to the past and future, were but a fraction of their capabilities.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Miiya stopped existing and Shiroya took her place.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Neither Ashiya nor Xyn ended up in possession of the real Sekimeiya. In this case, it was Sai who was able to keep both of them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There was one more dichotomy that was altered, and knowing it will help you figure out Sai's tricks.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: To achieve what he wanted, he altered the dichotomy between real and fake Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world A, before Akaro knocked out Naomi, she told him that the Sekimeiya must always remain in a cold place and that they could break if they remained outside their cabinet. He'd already heard that from Ido, but Naomi's tone of voice made it sound much more important.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That scared Akaro. Would both real Sekimeiya break if he kept them in the cleaning cart? Unaware that they were no longer there, Akaro concluded that he had to move them; he didn't know how long the shutter would stay there for, but he knew Ashiya Tower very well. Other cabinets with temperature functions existed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Thanks to the security room key that he had found and Naomi's keyring, Akaro went to the attic. There, he found both real Sekimeiya and traveled through time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As soon as he understood what happened, he created a plan and executed it. At the end of the plan, he put the Future Sekimeiya in the refrigerator, moved the suitcase, rejoined the group holding the Past Sekimeiya, and managed to keep it in a cold cabinet in B4 where everyone stayed for a long time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, both times, Akaro made a mistake. He wasn't aware of how cold the temperature had to be, as above 0 ºC, the Sekimeiya would always gather energy.{w} Unlike Atsuki, he didn't tamper with the temperature setting, and in room B4, he set the cabinet to 5 ºC. During the time the Sekimeiya spent under those conditions, both of them gathered energy at a slow rate.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Eventually, Sai left room B4 and started exploring the tower. At that point, the elevator was on floor 6, so he was able to see the hidden bodies and reach the attic.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Up there, he found the Future Sekimeiya in the refrigerator. The instant he touched it, he was split in half by the door of room B4.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Before his body appeared in the future, however, the door of the refrigerator was left open, which made Atsuki C notice that it was strangely cold in the attic. It was Katei C who found the Future Sekimeiya in the refrigerator, and he quickly hid it in a bedroom, where Miiya would soon activate it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The entire day, Miiya's thoughts carried mystery and ambiguity, rarely being organized or complete.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "How much longer would I have to play along for? Ever since she'd exited our lives, I'd kept telling myself that it would all eventually go back to how it was at the beginning."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Regardless, I had to put on the same appearance, and it came naturally after the previous two weeks."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Unlike Shiroya, she didn't fall into a coma, so she had been living with Atsuki for two weeks.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "She really was here, but..."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There was often something important to infer from her thoughts, especially after she murdered Erina.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She had killed a person. She'd wondered many times what that would be like, and she finally knew. Until {time=21}, her mind kept going back to that moment, ever-present in her thoughts, trying to make sense of what had really happened at the time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "She was there, casually leaning against the line of cabinets. I could hardly believe what I was seeing, but there was no wariness in her eyes and not even a trace of blood near her."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Miiya world switched to world B, she saw that the cameras' green lights had returned.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "...The computer. It reenabled the cameras. This really must mean that they weren't recording until now, right...?"
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Hopeful, I entered one of the rooms."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Could that mean that her murder hadn't been recorded? Just as she was trying to rationalize that, Erina appeared in hallway B.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Her clothes were caked in dried blood, and the wariness in her voice was back. In response, Miiya started to ask a question that she never finished.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "A-Are you...?"{w}—"the Erina that I already killed?"
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A lot more happened until {time=21.} Miiya saw another Atsuki and was told that Shiroya would come back to life. Although her mind was pulled from many different sides, in the event room, shortly before the shutter opened, she couldn't help but think about her own grim future.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "I didn't think anything good could come of it. After all, there was a killer in the room."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Despite that, as the seconds ticked along, the answers I tried to reach changed more and more.{w} What would happen to me? ...I looked up to try to believe that nothing would, but I had no way to know."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She looked up at the single camera in the room. The green light on it was no longer visible, but she had no way to know what that meant for her. As the final seconds passed by, Miiya continued to wonder if anyone would ever see the time she had pushed Erina off the stairs on the second floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Why does Atsuki B request that they leave the Sekimeiya on the ground on the second floor?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It's the Future Sekimeiya, and very soon, Shiroya B will travel all the way to November 30th. Since she is in the attic, what Atsuki wants is to prevent the range of the Future Sekimeiya from reaching Shiroya and causing a world switch.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He recalls the events that he lived through: he knows that a group of people is next to the elevator on the crystal floor. That's why the ground on the second floor is the best place to keep the Future Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Miiya agrees that she should be dead. From her point of view, she should have died.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On November 30th, she fell unconscious where a deadly explosion took place. However, when she woke up, her body had moved.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She had no idea what had happened—she'd begun to wonder if she was mistaken about the exact place she had fallen unconscious. Despite that... she should've died. To her, it didn't make sense that she was alive.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Something disappeared from Miiya's purse. The proof that Shiroya had died was no longer there.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was a note that Atsuki C had written days before December 15th, which Miiya had been careful not to reveal that she had in her purse.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So, when did it vanish? Despite Miiya's speculation, it wasn't a change in history that got rid of it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Miiya and Erina were together in room A5 in world B, Erina grabbed Miiya's set of keys from her purse with a quick motion. After that, Miiya dashed out of the room when she heard Atsuki calling Shiroya's name.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That caused the note to fall to the floor, and Erina picked it up. Minutes later, in the event room, she gave it to Atsuki B, which is how he obtained it originally, as it wasn't the same note that he'd already left behind a handrail.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If you follow the movements of the note, though, you might notice that something is off.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It only entered the tower in world C in Miiya's purse. Late into the day, when she went to world B, she dropped it and Erina picked it up.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Erina gave it to Atsuki B before the future location of one of his travels, which let him have it in the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He first saw it in the staff room and immediately tossed it behind one of the hallway B handrails, where the police of that world found it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There's one last key to understanding this puzzle. Before Miiya dropped the note for Erina to obtain it, she had traveled back in time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "I looked up and saw three slits in the door. Despite the darkness that should've existed behind them, I discerned a glow."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "It could only have been one thing. Despite being filled with questions, my mind was blank. My hand was drawn to the shape that had begun to take form behind the dark lines, and through the narrow space, I made contact, hoping with all my might that I would be brought to the awaited time."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "However, hallway A was my next sight."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: {w=1.0}"Then, I fell to the floor immediately after appearing."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: She appeared in hallway A, dropped the note next to Erina in room A5, and then the replicated location took place. In world C, she and Atsuki ran to the crystal floor after Akaro. Since they were ahead, they didn't notice her pick up the note. Afterwards, she ran to catch up with Atsuki, which is why she had appeared in hallway A in world B and immediately fallen to the floor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So there's a large inconsistency. If she dropped the note before the replicated location, why did she have it when she appeared in hallway A? She must've had it, or else she couldn't have dropped it in room A5.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Do you remember something Atsuki B thought regarding the note?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "I put my hand in my pocket, but the note wasn't there. It had disappeared at some point."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Right. The next time I traveled to the past, I didn't appear with it.{w} But... why? I should have.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: Oh, it's like I thought earlier. I had the note when I traveled to the past. From the staff room, I appeared in hallway B and then slammed the storeroom door to create a new noise. After that, I waited in the bathroom on the second floor.{w} There, I put my hand in my pocket because I wanted to flush the note away. However, it wasn't there.{w} That's why I didn't appear with it. I wanted to flush it away, so if I had, I wouldn't have held the note in the future, and I never could've appeared with it.
entries.speaker: nm

entries.text: What he thinks happened makes sense, and it would've happened if not for something he didn't realize. By the time he traveled from the staff room, he had already dropped the note Erina had given him in the event room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Sai was the least of my concerns. I barely put any thought into punching him, but before I did, I saw a conspicuous smile all over his face. It only faded momentarily, returning right after the blow."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Atsuki had an altercation with Sai C near the elevator after Shiroya left them behind. At that time, the note fell from his pocket.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And someone found it just minutes later. None other than Miiya herself.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "We ran behind Akaro. I looked down and saw that there was still no blood on the floor or the staircase."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What...!?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "On the floor, below the elevator panel, there was a folded piece of paper. Atsuki and Akaro were ahead of me, so they didn't see me grabbing it and putting it in my purse."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did it... not disappear after all?
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "Akaro was in the storeroom, but I just followed behind Atsuki, completely lost for words. How the hell had that made it there?"
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Right before she ran through hallway A to satisfy her previous travel, she reobtained the note.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And at {time=21}, the police didn't find it in her shoe, where she had stored it as a last-ditch effort. So, even though only one note entered the tower in the morning, a copy of it reached the end of worlds B and C.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In the hour before the tower unlocked, the scent of death enveloped Ashiya Tower. Everyone reached the last stretch of their imprisonment just to fall victim to a sudden, gruesome massacre.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...But what really took place inside the giant building? What was the cause behind the last second turn of events? Here are the facts you already know about:
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: 1. When the police entered the tower, nobody was alive inside it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: 2. All the deaths were instant, and two people couldn't have killed each other simultaneously.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: 3. No one committed suicide. Every single person who was trapped in the morning was attacked by another person.
entries.speaker: c
