entries.text: Those points alone raise a serious question: who killed the last person? Everyone who died was instantly killed by someone, so what happened to the last victim to fall dead?{w} Let's look at more facts surrounding the case:
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: 4. The police found and unlocked the hidden door in the storeroom. By doing so, they removed Sai's mark. In other words, that door hadn't been opened since Sai had marked it more than six hours earlier.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: 5. The police found one of the Sekimeiya gray and on the floor in the event room.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: 6. Everyone who died was killed by someone from their own world, and no killer world switched to another world. They all died in their own world, C, where they were found dead.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: 7. Everyone who died was pierced by the same screwdriver. When the last person died, their killer threw it away, and the police found it next to the crystal floor stairs.{w} If you're curious, when the police analyzed it, they found two different sets of fingerprints on its handle.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: One set of prints matched with Miiya's records. Do you know who else had wielded that screwdriver?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A handful of fingerprints belonging to Naomi C overlapped those from Miiya. Does that make sense, though? Wasn't Naomi lying on the floor in the lobby?{w} What really happened when the police raided the building?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "In the lobby was the first indication of the bloodbath that had transpired. Dead eyes watched the officers from the floor, inviting them to a hell of corridors and blood."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: They were Suripo's eyes—Naomi wasn't there.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She wasn't anywhere. As you know, the moment the first police officer took a step into the building, no speck of life dwelled anywhere.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But that's hardly a problem, is it? The gray Sekimeiya that the police found indicates that someone activated it shortly before the shutters rose. It was the Future Sekimeiya, which had previously failed to let Katei escape from his pursuer. Whoever activated it would not have been present when the police entered the building.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Let me refresh your memory of something you were once told.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Fortunately, everyone was able to leave safely. That included Naomi, who was woken up by the loud noise of the shutter."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "However, a single decision nearly sent everything spiraling into destruction."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Instead of the shutter, yells of pain that would've woken Naomi up before that time were almost let out. Disastrous yells that would've shattered everything that had been needed to get there."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "They were yells that, in reality, nobody ever heard. At {time=21:04}, the police entered the building.{w} Even though everyone was alive, Suripo was dead on the floor. The officers could hardly believe their eyes while the survivors emerged."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So, let's put together a plausible set of events.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world C, Naomi wasn't actually dead. The loud motion of the shutter woke her up at {time=21:04}, but in this imaginary world, Erina's and Isla's yells did so ahead of time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In a groggy state, she saw the killer finishing off Katei in hallway C, and the only thing she could do was dash at them and use their own weapon to seek instant vengeance.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Naomi roamed around the tower and witnessed the five other corpses, the scent of blood mingling with the smell of the Sekimeiya to create an odor unlike anything she'd ever smelled before. When she entered the event room, the Future Sekimeiya, which Katei had activated, had already powered back on. She ran to it to put it inside its cabinet, but she traveled to the future the moment she contacted the gemstone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When the police entered the building, no one was alive inside until Naomi reappeared. Everyone had been killed by someone else. The killer hadn't escaped through the storeroom or to another world. Everyone who had died was killed by someone from their own world. Every single person who had gotten trapped in the morning was attacked by another person—even Naomi, who was attacked and severely injured in world A by Akaro.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This seems to answer most questions, but of course, what about all the other murders? What happened before Naomi's reawakening?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The truth is something that wouldn't be theorized even once by the police or anyone who dared tackle the case. In their world, that is.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: You know about the time where everyone waited in the event room, calmly spending the last few minutes of the day-long countdown. No one present had any idea of what it had taken for that young, red-haired girl to be sitting there against a wall, staring indifferently at the walls and approaching her long-awaited release.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At that time, the thought of killing anyone was nowhere in her mind, and that didn't change when an impulse drew her out of the room. It was all she could do to obstruct the predictions that a mysterious Atsuki had made, but she had no intention to go any further than that. She had already abandoned the thoughts of death.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After all, she had already killed once. In world A, she had killed Erina, and repeating that act was not something she had even considered. While waiting in the event room, most of Miiya's thoughts were directed to her own well-being. The sight of the camera and not knowing whether her action had been recorded unnerved her.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So that begs the question that everyone would ask themselves. What drove someone to kill that many times mere minutes before their release? Completely ignorant to what she was doing, the moment Miiya rushed out of the event room, she created a world with only one survivor.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In this world, the shutter seems to unlock a few minutes before {time=21}, but that's merely a misunderstanding with Sai's wristwatch.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Earlier in the day, Sai traveled to the future alongside Atsuki. However, both of them thought they had traveled to the past, so Sai never believed that the time on his watch was incorrect.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: It was several minutes ahead of the real time, but the computer had stopped working, and when they world switched to A, the security room was locked. The first time he thought that it might've been wrong was when he heard the shutter opening.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Suripo speaks with Larles, a seemingly idiosyncratic individual who was ushered away in the commotion. Though, not by a phone call, like she claimed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Observers witnessing her were quick to spot something like a second set of arms rummaging in her coat, but most brushed it off as cosplay. There were no records regarding her existence anywhere on Earth.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: From the Doctor Who spin-off "Cwej: The Series". As per Kickstarter reward: Cameo Scene.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The initial reports say that three people are missing, but the real number is four: Atsuki, Erina, Sai, and Akaro. The reason behind this misunderstanding is Naomi A's body.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The police believed that at least eight people had been trapped, so when they found four dead bodies and Shiroya, they thought that only three people were unaccounted for.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Two of the dead bodies belonged to Naomi, so with a little more investigation, those numbers would be doubted.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki tells Shiroya to appear below a stone roof, but he doesn't have enough time to fully explain why.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If Shiroya had appeared wide in the open, her body would've collided with the falling snow, but that's not all. The roof would've been needed even if no snow had been falling at the moment she appeared.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That's due to the snow on the ground. If there had been any, Shiroya's future location would've been slightly sunk into it, in her own footprints. Those would not yet have existed in the past, so Shiroya's feet would've collided with an even layer of snow, and she would have lost the bottom portions of her feet, bleeding profusely.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The third chapter is called "Peripheral". The main story of this chapter happens outside of Ashiya Tower—it's the periphery of the story. Not only that, but its main goal resembles that of a computer peripheral.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: An external part of the computer essential for the entire machine to work. If Shiroya hadn't been there to relay the group from Chapter 1 to Chapter 5, the entire structure would've collapsed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Lastly, it references "peripheral vision", as this view is essential to solve the mysteries of this part of the story.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya's narrow field of view prevented her from noticing the truth around her, but if she had widened it ever so slightly, she would've taken notice of everything she was missing. Similarly, if your approach for this chapter had been different, your perception of it would've changed drastically.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai and Shiroya appear in the right bedroom of the attic, but the reason for that seems to be that they appeared inside it. After all, that's what lets them stay there until the time of the future location.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There are other instances where you might ask yourself similar questions. This seems like a paradox that appeared out of thin air.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, be certain that they all share something that makes them decipherable. There is no effect without a distinct cause.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Happy New Year!
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In this imaginary world... the real story converged with your request. Shiroya never returned to the tower on January 5th, leading to many changes.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: She wasn't there to save the lives of everyone who had activated a chain of future travels at the end of December 15th. Because she didn't go to the tower on January 5th, her future self didn't exist on December 15th; Shiroya wasn't there at the end of the day to prevent Atsuki from unplugging the cabinet. As a result, he ended up traveling to the future, and the two fake Sekimeiya the police put in the cabinet at {time=21} never ended up breaking.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On January 1st, when Atsuki found Shiroya, he ran behind her without thinking, causing the final accident that would forever change her life.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At the scene, a police officer approached her to ask for her name. As he'd thought, she was one of the people who should've been in the tower on December 15th, so she was taken into a car.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The rest of the missing people, however, were not found, which eventually put an end to Ashiya's desperate claims.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Months passed. In this world, the storeroom's secret was never found—Katei had escaped in the morning, and the door was always unlocked. That's why Shiroya never attempted to reenter the tower once she was freed. Despite all of those changes, however, the chain of future travels still took place. You might be able to figure out why.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And on October 4th, the tower was demolished, destroying the Future Sekimeiya. When the missing people appeared, their bodies collided with the fallen debris, killing them instantly. Days later, when the debris was being cleaned, the gruesome fate of the three missing people was finally known to all. Erina was discovered last, as she had appeared where the mechanical room had once been.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On December 15th, Isla A world switched to world B. There, she went many days into the past. When she touched the Sekimeiya, she was holding the purse she'd had in world A. Then, on November 24th, which purse did she appear with?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Interestingly, she appeared with the purse from world B.{w} It had the voice recorder inside, and there were no tickets for the event.{w} It's strange, though, isn't it? Why did she not appear with the purse from world A, which she'd been holding?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: While the two Islas tried to keep her identity hidden, the purses were swapped. Before going to the tower, Erina realized the tickets they'd bought weren't in the purse's pocket, so they printed them again. That's how the purse with the recorder was brought to the tower.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Meanwhile, Isla A was left home with the original purse from world B. Inside were the tickets that Erina B had originally printed, but before January 5th, Shiroya took them.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That's why, when Isla A reentered the tower, she was holding the empty purse from world B. It's why, when she arrived in the past, the purse she had was world B's, and the recorder was inside.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In other words, although two purses existed, they were the very same, as the Sekimeiya had joined them together.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Shiroya's phone says "No service", and she's unable to connect to her mother when she attempts to call her. The reason is the existence of a duplicate phone of hers.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In this world, when December 15th came to an end, Shiroya was the only person found in Ashiya Tower; she was the version of Shiroya that had saved Miiya in world C.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Soon after being taken in by the police, she was released and went to temporarily live in Atsuki's house to take care of his pets. She reobtained the phone she had left outside the tower on the morning of the 15th, so when Shiroya's mother called her number, both her original and copied phone received the call.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Depending on implementation, some phone services allow the use of the same phone number on multiple devices when notified beforehand. Shiroya's service provider noticed that two devices were receiving calls from the same source and terminated her phone's connection to prevent fraudulent use of the line, whether through her own fault or a third party's.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Of course, they wouldn't terminate her service without notifying her by mail, but mail takes a few days to arrive.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...{w}Don't worry, he'll come back soon.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...He didn't react. Maxi had been staring at me in silence for hours. It must have been strange for him to see me in Atsuki's house for so long.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Much like him, all I could do was stare at the clock. January 1st was slowly coming to an end.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After ignoring me, Maxi approached the front door.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You'll get to see him again in just four days. Even if you went to look for him, you wouldn't find him anywhere right now.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Because he was traveling to the future... It was insane to think about it so casually, but I was certain that Atsuki was nowhere in the world at that moment.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Seventeen days had passed since December 15th. Before that, I'd been in Eagle Motel for fifteen days. That had been after spending five days in January, immediately after those initial twelve hours...
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I was confident I was finally at the exit of the sprawling labyrinth, and during the past few days, I'd had a lot of time to ruminate on many of the things that had happened.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: That time I entered the tower from the storeroom, after spending hours in front of the tower and under the unchanging sky... That'll happen in four days.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Most of my thoughts had been directed to the brief interlude where I'd been in January by myself. Atsuki had told me that I'd gone to the future instead of the past, but that was all the information I had from him.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I touched the Sekimeiya in the bathroom and appeared under the gem shop. I first thought that I'd gone to November because I accessed the date settings on my phone and read November 30th. The time was {time=21:10.}
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I realized something important a while ago. My phone was from November 30th. Not only that, but I was wearing the clothes from that day, and my whole body was wracked with pain because it had just fallen from the shop. However, I appeared on December 30th.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And not on December 31st—on December 30th. Even though I heard fireworks welcoming the new year when I went home, I don't think I appeared in the past just a few hours earlier. After reading {time=21:10} and November 30th on my phone, I fell unconscious, and when I woke up, I felt as if I'd been there for an eternity. But according to the time, it had been less than half an hour.{w} There's no way. I was there for over a day. The body I'd appeared in had just fallen through the shop's floor, and I was unconscious until the next day, when I went home. I dreamed about many parts of my life for so long...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: November 30th and December 30th are both fifteen days apart from December 15th. On December 30th, the body I appeared in was the one from November 30th, which is why my phone displayed that date. That's how Atsuki said the Sekimeiya worked.{w} In the bathroom, I touched the Sekimeiya at about {time=20:30.} Since the body I appeared in was from November 30th at {time=21:00}, what that must mean is that the real time on December 30th was {time=20:00.} The time on my phone was always about one hour ahead.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I remember when I first woke up underground. As opposed to every other time, instead of instantly appearing there, I woke up, as if something had been in between my travel and my awakening.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I don't think I fully understand yet how the Sekimeiya functioned, but I might know why this happened. In this case, the body that was replicated was from after I'd fallen through the gem shop's floor. That means that it was already in a coma. When my future consciousness was placed within it, my body woke up.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I've had time to notice a few things I didn't realize at the time. When I walked out of that tunnel, no snow was falling—it was not November 30th. The moon phase that I saw didn't match with that day either.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I was really tired, so I don't know if that contributed to everything that I missed, but my first destination was the gem shop where I thought I'd just been. I saw the owner there, who might've been handling the repairs of his store or something, but I only recognized him when I saw his face...{w} because he was no longer wearing the shirt from that day, which had the shop's logo on both sides.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So I just went home, where everything looked like it had on November 30th. That's because after waking up from the coma, I was only there for one day before going to live with Atsuki.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I thought I had two weeks to change the past, and being free in those icy streets had made for an immense contrast.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I fell asleep in no time, but I was woken up by the sound of fireworks. Although my phone displayed {time=1}, midnight had just hit, and the fireworks were marking the start of the new year. ...I saw them again last night, once more by myself.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It was 2012. My past self wasn't in a coma, and Atsuki wasn't secluded in his house. However, those beliefs let me feel temporarily at peace.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The next day was today. I didn't even think that the cereal bars I'd brought to Atsuki's house should've still been in the kitchen. I just ate some mixed nuts and went outside, where I ended up at Ina Café after wandering through the white streets.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Hello.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: He suddenly turned around.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Ha—
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Shiroya...!
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Yeah. It's been a while.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Oh my God! Y-You're all right!
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...So you know what happened. I am, yes.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Of course! You were in the news!
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: "I managed a bitter smile in response to his relieved expression."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: He wasn't talking about the incident on November 30th... He was talking about the attack that had taken place in Ashiya Tower; the news about it reached everywhere.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I'm so glad you were released so quickly! How are you?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I'm okay. I was released yesterday. Fortunately, nothing major happened to me.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: At {time=21}, a team of policemen raided the building, and they only found me. I was thoroughly interrogated, but they released me pretty quickly.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That's really good to hear. If you came to relax and try to forget about it, we don't have to talk about it.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...It's fine. You don't have to worry.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Are you sure? I can't imagine what it must be like to lose someone close to you at your age. I'm so sorry.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Darfee knew that Atsuki hadn't been found when the tower unlocked. I've read many of the articles that reported the news, and due to all the deaths and the impossibility that the missing people escaped, the worst was assumed by almost everyone.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...{w}Thank you.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Do you have any idea what happened? A lot of details weren't published.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Unfortunately, no. It all happened suddenly, and we were just caught up in it.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: "He looked down, very clearly pitying me."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: As I was drinking my coffee, I saw a newspaper close to me.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It was the latest Yushinews edition. Naturally, the first thing I did was look at the date.{w} It said 12-01...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...{w}The Japanese date format is year-month-day, but I approached the newspaper intending to read the day's date. It didn't come to mind that Yushinews is a monthly newspaper.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I saw 12-01: 2012-January, as it was that month's edition. Instead, I interpreted it as December 1st.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And when I flipped back the pages, I ended up at the "November" section. In chronological order, every edition begins with the previous month's most important news. That's where I read about the gas explosion and the escape from a prison cell.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Before leaving, Darfee told me that it was Sunday. It was the truth, and it was an immense contradiction with what I believed...{w} That even made me think later that Miiya had died on a Saturday, which wasn't the case. After waking up in the hospital, I spent the days secluded from the world, and the case wasn't too different before November 30th. The days of the week meant nothing to me at the time.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: On the way back, I ended up next to this house. Silently, I walked to the gate and looked up, where I saw light behind a window.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...I looked up at the ceiling light. I'd been living at Atsuki's house since I'd been released by the police so that I could take care of his pets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: You saw me outside this morning, right?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Maxi didn't react to my question, but I knew he hadn't been in the living room for most of the day. I recalled the moment I'd seen him by the gate, long ago.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "I got startled as soon as I peeked through the bars of his front gate. I hadn't seen Maxi sitting in front of the wooden door, where there was no snow."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "He seemed afraid for an instant when he saw me, but then he ran to me, squeezing his head through the bars."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: Did seeing me scare you? You knew I was here, so it must've looked like I teleported out.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Curious to see me outside, he approached the gate but couldn't stop me from leaving. I found him waiting by the door, which is all he's done since I started living here. I think he's just waiting for Atsuki to come back.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: After that, I walked to my apartment. I noticed that people were looking at me, and I don't think that was just my imagination. One of the reasons I've stayed here is because most people recognize me as the only survivor of the 15th.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...When I got home, I decided to change the past by calling my mom.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Shiroya...! How are you!?{w} I'm so glad you called! We were so worried!
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Hello...! Are you there? What happened? You're okay, right?
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I didn't want to speak, so I cut the line, my mom's voice leaving me still. Immediately, my phone received a call from her, which I waited out.{w} After that, it took a while until I received another one, but that was the last time she called me.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I knew what had happened. Earlier that day, I had finally talked to my mom, calming her down.{w} When the police had released me, the phone I'd left outside the tower on the 15th had been returned to me. In the future, when my mother had called me, both existing phones had received the call, and I'd picked it up from Atsuki's house.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: After going over all that I'd experienced, I cooked a slice of meat. It was disgusting. I can't believe I didn't realize it tasted awful due to being in the fridge for more than a month.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And when the sun began to set, my phone showed {time=18.} Strangely, I was exhausted, so I didn't wait long before going to bed.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I woke up tomorrow, on January 2nd.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That's when I found that thread from November 24th, long since locked.{w} I was so close to discovering the truth there. I wanted to find the first ever mention of the word "Sekimeiya" to learn where it had been before Ashiya's announcement, so I sorted the results by oldest first. That made me miss all the articles reporting on what had happened on the 15th.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...But thanks to an attached picture, I was still able to reach Vaisude's apartment.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: On the way, I saw that there was no light behind the windows in Ashiya Tower. It made sense to me because Katei had said that nobody had been recently working on the office floors, but that was a mistake, since they were lit up on the 15th.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It had been more than a month since Vaisude had traveled to the past. He would go live with his parents, where he had appeared on the 24th of November...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And I, the only person to have been found in the tower, visited him. He thought it was due to his forum thread, and he was surprised when I left without saying a word.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Outside, I constantly felt eyes on me. What did Yushibana know about me? Slowly, I walked to its outskirts.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Next to my school, everything was silent. No classes were happening on a Monday, as it was during the winter holidays.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...And that's where I felt a presence behind me—where I saw footprints running away.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Who was it? That's something I'm not sure of yet. Who would've followed me in January? It could've been anyone who knew I was the only survivor of the attack.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But thankfully, nothing happened to me. I went home and tried to loosen up by cooking the food I'd bought.{w} Later that day, I received a call from an unknown number. Remembering the words Vaisude and I exchanged is pretty interesting.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...Hello?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: O-Oh, you picked up. Good.{w} Hey there.{w} Are you Shiroya...?
entries.speaker: v

entries.text: Huh? Yes. ...Who are you?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: You were at my place earlier, remember? My name's Vaisude.{w} I just need to ask this first. You were in Ashiya Tower during the terrorist attack on December 15th, right?
entries.speaker: v

entries.text: ...{w}December 15th? What are you talking about?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Wh-What? You know all about it, right? That's why you came to my place.
entries.speaker: v

entries.text: ...{w}I do, yeah. I was there.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I see. I knew I wasn't wrong.
entries.speaker: v

entries.text: Both of us referred to the 15th like it had already happened, and I thought it was because we had traveled to the past from that day, not because I was in the future...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There's a reason why I'm calling you. ...I don't know how this will sound, though.
entries.speaker: v

entries.text: ...What is it?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...Do you know... what I experienced? You read my thread from November, didn't you? That's how you found my apartment.
entries.speaker: v

entries.text: What did you experience?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Exactly what I wrote about...! From the 15th of December, I suddenly appeared on the 24th of November!
entries.speaker: v

entries.text: ...I see. You're right. I also traveled back in time.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Wh— R-Really...!? So that is what happened! How, though!?{w} A lot more people had to have come with me, right?{w} Then what will happen in two weeks? Do you think it will repeat?
entries.speaker: v

entries.text: It's very possible, but I'm not sure everything will be identical.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Yeah, that wouldn't make sense. I have no idea how it'll come to occur, but it'll happen again. People will travel to the past. I can't believe it.
entries.speaker: v

entries.text: ...I'm as confused as you are.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: "Then what will happen in two weeks? Do you think it will repeat?" I'm pretty sure I know why he said that.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: On the 15th, the dead bodies were found by the police, and in Isla's purse, the voice recorder we played was found too.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Its contents were summarized publicly, and I've read speculation regarding what it all means. Most people ignored the recording because it stated that the shutter wouldn't unlock when it clearly did.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But Vaisude must have known not to dismiss it—something else was hidden behind that audio. So, on January 2nd, something was still set to happen within two weeks. Perhaps the incident would repeat and someone would go to the past again to leave the recorder on December 15th.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...The conversation between the two of us kept going and going, but neither of us realized how different the other's perspective was.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I woke up pretty early on January 3rd. My phone showed {time=7:45}, but no light was making it through the gaps in the blinds.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I felt the need to go out again, and when I opened the front door, I saw the sun rising from behind the mountains. ...It was an hour earlier than I thought, and light snow was starting to fall.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That was the reason behind that foggy and soulless Yushibana. It culminated when I saw Ina Café closed, but when it was really {time=7:30}, the shutter rose.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So what have you been doing these last couple of days?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...{w}Not much. I went to Atsuki's house yesterday, and I was there for a while.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Atsuki's house? You think being there helps you?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: ...I think so, yeah.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I see.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: I could finally rest inside, and I did so for longer than I'd expected. I was only drawn out hours later when I saw someone I recognized in the distance.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It was Isla's friend, the Isla from the world I later ended up in. She had traveled from December 15th to November 24th, and for her, it had been a very long time since nobody had come back from the tower.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I followed her footprints up to her house, but I wasn't yet certain I wanted to change the past. When I felt a presence watching behind me again, I distanced myself from that place.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: And I ended up high on that mountain, where I finally made the decision to change the past and do all I could to save everyone.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: On the way back, I felt like the same person was following me, and that time, the police were ready to intercept them.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...{w}Hm, thinking about it, I might actually be able to find out who it was.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: S-Sorry, did you just arrest someone?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Hm? Yes. What's the matter?
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: I... was feeling like someone was following me just now. Could it have been this person?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: "The man frowned and took out a tiny scrapbook.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: What's your name?
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: Mine...?{w} ...It's Shiroya Mirana.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: "He looked at me and silently wrote on the paper.{w} Then, he suddenly smiled, completely shifting his expression."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I see. You can stop worrying, then. If you think you were being followed, there's nothing to be afraid of.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: At the time, I thought his smile was a bit strange, but he also recognized me as the only survivor. He had just caught the person believed to be behind the attack, so he told me that I could stop worrying.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There's a reason why the police released me without further complications. Right now, there's one person believed to have orchestrated the attack—Akaro, even though the police haven't released his name.{w} That's because a recording was found on the computer in the tower, one which showed Akaro's and Katei's movements during the time the smoke was released. Before {time=21}, Atsuki saved that recording on the computer. He brought it from the world where Miiya was saved.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: So, if the police believed they had caught a Xyn member, what's most likely is that it was Akaro.{w} I guess that's not all, though.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Atsuki also told me that after Sai and Akaro escaped from the bedroom in the attic, Akaro traveled to the future and appeared on January 5th. He couldn't have been following me on January 3rd.{w} Rather, what it means is that it was the other Akaro. The one who killed me in another world and then arrived in ours with Isla.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I traveled fifteen days to the future and appeared in the location where I'd been fifteen days in the past. The rule should be the opposite when you travel to the past. Vaisude appeared in his parents' house on November 24th, and by that amount of time in the future, he moved out to go live with them.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That's gotta be why that Akaro appeared in a cell on November 24th. He would be caught by the police on January 3rd and put in a prison cell. In November, the cell was vacant and unlocked, so he was able to walk right out of it. That's why the image looked the same as in the article when I saw the cell on TV.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When the evening of the 3rd came, I stepped out of my apartment again. The place I went to had been constantly in my mind, as it was essential to construct the future I wanted.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I came a while ago, but I'd forgotten to check if I'd won anything until now.{w} The number I had was for December 1st, I believe. I wonder, by the way, how long would it be valid for?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Oh, it's still valid, don't worry. They last a whole year.{w} Anyway, December 1st? Let me see.
entries.speaker: ns

entries.text: 30-05-12-31-15-26. Bonus 24. I still remember it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: There was a small piece of paper on the table containing those numbers. I had bought it in the other world before going to Eagle Motel. However, the winning number had been different.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: But that didn't matter. Even though it had been bought in another world, it was immensely valuable in the one I was in.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: January 4th was the final day I'd set for myself. It didn't matter anymore, but I did the laundry to pass the time.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I noticed that my favorite blue hoodie was missing. It was among the clothing I'd brought to Atsuki's house on December 9th.{w} Similarly, a shirt that brought bad memories and which I thought I'd left out of the washer was in the bucket. There were two versions of it, as it was the shirt I'd worn on November 30th, and I left it there both on December 8th and on January 1st.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...I didn't want to spend the whole day at home, so I went to Ina again.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That's where I learned that a Xyn member had been arrested for the first time. The latest edition of Yushinews was still there, and it would stay there for the rest of the month.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The news said that the identity of the person they caught was unknown. I wonder if Akaro wasn't his real name...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Are you thinking about the news?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: "Darfee addressed me after I'd been in thought for a few minutes."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: A bit. It just threw me off.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: I see. Well, it's good that someone from that group finally got caught.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Yeah, I agree.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: ...Do you know about the Sekimeiya?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Huh? ...What do you mean?
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Ashiya's event.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: Hm? Yeah, of course.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: Well, nobody stole the Sekimeiya, right...?
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: The Sekimeiya...? N-No. ...As far as I know, at least.
entries.speaker: d

entries.text: All right, I just wanted to make sure since I haven't been paying attention to the news.
entries.speaker: c3s

entries.text: From my perspective, what it all meant was that the past had changed, so I could go to Atsuki's house and prevent him from going to the tower in case something happened to me.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I had to wait for him to leave, which would never happen. As I waited, I realized that I could go back to Isla's house in the meantime.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When I rang the bell, nobody opened the door, and after knocking for some time, I noticed the door wasn't locked.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I'm just speculating, but when Isla traveled from December 15th to November 24th, it's likely she didn't appear with the keys to her house. Since Erina never came back from the tower, Isla would've had to keep the door unlocked when she left so that she could get back in.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Inside the house, I immediately found her purse. I took two tickets for the event on the 15th, which is pretty strange...{w} because if that was the purse of the Isla who'd traveled from the 15th, I'm not sure why the tickets would've been inside it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...The recording was real. On January 5th, everyone who's currently traveling to the future will make it happen.{w} But what about Isla? She'll be there too, and she's not currently traveling through time. ...The Isla from this world died in the cabinet, and the other Isla should currently be alone in her house.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: How will that Isla end up inside the tower on January 5th—the exact day that everyone will awaken? I can only think of one thing.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: After taking both tickets from her purse, I walked back home. Even though I didn't see anyone, Isla might have been careful about her situation. Maybe she noticed the strange footprints that went in and out of her house.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If she did, and retraced them to my apartment, she had the chance to follow my footprints all the way to the tower. I entered through the storeroom and left the door open, so that's one way she could've been there on the 5th.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: ...That Isla traveled from December 15th to November 24th. She went 21 days to the past.{w} 21 days after December 15th is January 5th. So her location upon appearing on November 24th may have been from January 5th.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: If that's correct, it might be how the voice recorder went to the past, although I don't really know any details. What's strange is that if Isla appeared with the recorder on November 24th, the Isla from this world shouldn't have had it in her purse on the 15th.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: An answer that explains two questions at once is that the purses were switched at some point before the 15th. That could be why the recorder ended up in the tower and why the tickets were still inside Isla's purse on January 4th.{w} If that's what happened, before going to the tower on December 15th, Isla or Erina must have realized that the tickets were no longer in the lower pocket of the purse and had to print them again.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Back home, I felt the time rapidly passing. I had no idea what would happen the next day, when I would finally visit the tower.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: My thoughts were racing, I couldn't get to sleep, and suddenly it was deep in the night. Eventually, it was clear I was just going to stay awake, so I had the thought of leaving anyway because the tower was supposed to open early. I never turned off the heater before leaving, and I never made the connection that it hadn't been turned on when it was December 8th. I'll have to go turn it off on the 5th so I don't waste power.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Anyway, when I arrived, the tower was locked, and nobody seemed to be there.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I really thought that the world had stopped moving. For a moment, I believed I would die there.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: The tower wouldn't open. It hadn't opened once since December 15th. The time discrepancy with my phone's clock was what made me think that the day wasn't starting.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Something that added to the illusion was my phone saying "No service". I'm still not sure what the cause of that was, but the cold definitely didn't let me think properly. The ground in front of the tower was buried in snow, too. Ashiya hadn't been maintaining the plaza like they tended to do.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I knew the secret of the building, though. I knew that a door probably existed in its left wall, and after feeling around carefully, I found it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I opened it just by pushing it lightly, which meant that it wasn't locked. I even saw that the handle inside was already taken off.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I bet the door was actually locked on the 15th due to how easily it opened in January. When the police interrogated me, they inquired about that secret area since they had found it open from the inside. They told me that they picked the lock and confirmed the door was really another exit.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Of course, since they didn't have the rusty key, they didn't lock the door again. That's why it was still unlocked on January 5th and not even properly closed. I got it to open just by putting my hand on it.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I entered the tower, which was as dark and cold as the outside world, its temperature no longer regulated for visitors. When I set foot in hallway A, I saw the green lights on the cameras. They were still recording.{w} But it's okay—I don't think it mattered. I was in the hallways, security room, lobby, mechanical room, and event room—all places that should've still been covered with smoke or that didn't have cameras in the first place.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: In the security room, I found Katei's rusty key. His body had already been taken away by the police, and I thought the room was all messy, as if someone had tried to find something.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: Then, above the breakers, I found the attic and Sekimeiya cabinet keys... And not only that.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: "I tried to move, but the obstacles in the room didn't make it easy. Could the cabinet have been there? While it seemed like a good place, neither the lobby nor the mechanical room had cameras."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: "There were chairs and tables on the floor, so I had to move some aside to get to every part of the room. Even though it was impossible for anyone to be there, I kept trying to be silent and failing as I scattered things that I couldn't see."
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: According to Atsuki, the Sekimeiya that sent us to the future was there. While searching for the cabinet, I moved it accidentally, which stopped the chain of travels and made everyone arrive on that day.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: As I was walking to the event room, I saw the reception desk lights flickering in the lobby. I turned around because I felt a presence behind me, and I don't think that was just paranoia.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: It had to be Atsuki. He had to be there too since both of us traveled back to the 15th when I touched the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I moved to the event room and felt that it was much colder than the rest of the building. The cabinet wasn't closed...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: When the police entered the building on the 15th, only the Sekimeiya that sent us to the past was in the cabinet. Ashiya said that the Sekimeiya weren't stolen, which means that the police found another one and put it in the cabinet. Of course, it wasn't the one in the mechanical room...
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: I remember the rush they were in when they found me. What must have happened is that they didn't close the cabinet, so on January 5th, that Sekimeiya had been gathering energy at an incredibly slow rate. That's why I was able to activate it inside the cabinet.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: But I'm not exactly sure how everything came to happen. There was something else in the cabinet, and I activated the alarm out of nowhere... What matters is that Atsuki and I returned to December 15th.
entries.speaker: n

entries.text: That was all the time I'd lived in January. The second coming of January 5th was the light at the end of a long tunnel.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I looked at the clock and saw that I was close to entering the second day of the year. After a long yawn, I stood up from the couch. I'd been sleeping in the guest room, just like before the 15th.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I had been there all day, and my body felt weak. As soon as I stood, I noticed a weight in one of my pockets.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: I reached my hand inside and took out a rusty key. There was one final use left for it, scheduled to happen in just three days. I gripped it tightly, ready to finally exit the labyrinth that we'd long ago been entrapped by.
entries.speaker: i

entries.text: In January, above the breakers, Shiroya finds the attic and Sekimeiya cabinet keys. Why were they there on January 5th, though?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Wait, no. You're definitely lying."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "Me? I don't ever lie."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "You don't have any key on you. That proves you hid them, because you should have the cabinet key."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...They were the keys that Sai had hidden after locking Shiroya in the attic's bedroom.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: At the end of December 15th, as soon as the shutter unlocked, the police were struck by a very strong smell. There, they saw an unidentifiable gas in the air as its source. It was the lingering range of the Sekimeiya.{w} When they raided the building with protective masks, a sole Sekimeiya was in the cabinet: the Past Sekimeiya. They knew another one had to be found, so they searched until one of the two fake Sekimeiya that existed was spotted in the attic.{w} They put it in the cabinet, but they were in a rush. That's why the glass wasn't properly closed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As the days passed, the cold temperature led to the effect Xyn had designed: the fake Sekimeiya left behind a card with their name. However, their method also damaged the cabinet's interior.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...And when Shiroya tried to open the glass all the way, it had been stuck. As soon as she applied a bit of force, one of the triggers for the alarm went off. However, there was no one for it to alert. Nobody had expected it to go off ever again.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Isla A traveled from December 15th to November 24th, she appeared with a burn mark on her finger. The Sekimeiya was immensely hot, so the burn would not have faded by the time the future position took place.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So then, why does Shiroya not appear with a burn mark when she travels from January 5th to December 15th? The number of days traveled is the same.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There's a key difference that prevented a burn from appearing on Shiroya's finger, and it becomes apparent when you track her movements.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After appearing on December 15th, Shiroya will spend many hours in world A until she arrives in world C and once again travels to the past. She will travel to November 30th to save Miiya in that world.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: For her to reach January 26th, almost two months will pass. That amount of time is what causes her to appear with no burn mark.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Despite Sai's initial reaction to the attack being different in the three worlds, there's something he always did at the start: hide the fake Sekimeiya.{w} Doing that opposed Katei's and Akaro's intentions, as Sai was not yet aware that three different Sekimeiya existed. Although his motives were slightly different in each world, the main goal was always the same.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world B, Sai took the fake Sekimeiya from the cabinet and hid it in the storeroom, where no cameras recorded him. In world C, when the group was inspecting the office floors, everyone was suddenly separated. That gave Sai the perfect chance to do the same thing.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In this world, A, Naomi C appeared before everyone. Unlike in the other worlds, she wanted to talk to Shiroya in addition to Akaro, as she had seen her world B self on the crystal floor separated from the group and wearing clothes from the attic—two versions of her existed at the same time, and Naomi, who had experienced time travel once, realized that Shiroya might have made contact with the Sekimeiya during the attack.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The three of them didn't return, so eventually, everyone walked to the crystal floor. Sai hurried to the event room, and as he yelled about the Sekimeiya's disappearance, he put it in his hip pack. Soon after, he hid it in room A5, where Atsuki C would find it hours later.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Akaro A says that one person was hospitalized, and he's referring to Atsuki. ...What about Gan, though?{w} The truth is that Gan was only sent to the hospital in world B.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Akaro A world switched to world B and then traveled to November 24th, he decided to walk away from Xyn's plan. He deeply regretted what he'd done in the tower, and he wished for history not to turn out the same way.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He knew he was in the past—he possessed valuable information. One of the things he did was remove the storeroom's handle. However, the first action he took to alter history came days prior.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: On November 30th, he had accidentally killed a young girl. It was the perfect chance to prevent that.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He knew that an explosion had occurred while everyone had been unconscious in the gem shop, so all he had to do was make sure that wouldn't repeat: he called Gan and told him to turn the heater off late on November 30th in order to prevent a disaster.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Akaro was confident he had saved the girl—Gan had told him that he would turn off the gas. However, Akaro was unaware that Gan did no such thing. He didn't put any real stock in such a bizarre phone call.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Afterward, the Sekimeiya were found, and mere days later, it was November 30th. The way events unfolded in world B slightly differed from world A.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Gan went to get the second Sekimeiya, he stopped himself in the middle of the shop. The moment he smelled the gas, the strange call came back to him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He glanced at the heater and approached it curiously just as dense smoke invaded the whole shop. He fell unconscious closer to the source of the explosion, so due to Akaro A's actions, Gan had to be sent to the hospital alongside Atsuki.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The Past Sekimeiya, which Atsuki touches, has been in the storeroom for numerous hours, so why is it that he doesn't have a burn mark on his finger when he world switches?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That's because of the temperature in the storeroom's secret corridor—the coldest place in the tower.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Atsuki touches the Sekimeiya, it has very little energy: the one with the massive range is in room A4, and it will remain undiscovered until June of 2012.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Along with Atsuki, almost a third of Japan disappears from the face of the Earth. Not only that, but they never appear anywhere.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In this world, when the police entered the tower at {time=21}, they found a real Sekimeiya and a fake. As instructed, they made sure both were kept cold.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki was the only person they were able to find, and since that day, the tower spent many weeks abandoned. Each second that passed, the real Sekimeiya that hadn't been found kept gaining energy.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The day that it was activated, its surface could've melted iron. The method through which that happened is a question of its own, but the effect became humanity's biggest mystery.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The range had been increasing every day, and it ended up taking away a third of Japan's population. The other real Sekimeiya was still refrigerated, so no world switch occurred. Given that the people who vanished didn't reappear anywhere, which Sekimeiya was activated? Did everyone go to the past or to the future?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If they had gone millennia to the past, they would never have been able to exist in the future location, so they wouldn't have appeared anywhere. If they had gone millennia to the future, they wouldn't have existed in the proportional past, so they wouldn't have appeared anywhere.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Calliants are the flowers that compose the flora of Airun's base. That is what this chapter is.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The base of the mountain, which lets it build all the way to the peak. In addition, this chapter is more grounded than the others.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Even though it's based on a real flower that can be found on snowy mountains, "calliant" is a made-up word.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Isla A traveled from December 15th to November 24th, she appeared with a burn mark on her finger. ...Why, though?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This is one of the clearest indications of an elusive rule of the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When someone traveled to the past, they were unable to keep feeling the pain of the burn they had noticed for an instant. The difference in Isla's case is the amount of time she traveled to the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When she touched it, the Past Sekimeiya was immensely hot, so normally, a painful burn would've remained on her skin. The amount of days that it took her to reach January 5th from November 24th would not have gotten rid of it. That's why she appeared with it in the first place.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In other words, the body she appeared in was that of one loop of her travel.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When she reached January 5th, the burn she'd appeared with had healed considerably, but it was still visible. If that body of hers had been the one to appear on November 24th, an instant chain of infinite loops would've made it impossible for her burn to ever appear.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Of course, that also means that she would've died instantly; she would've aged more than a month per loop and been unable to appear in November.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Instead, she appeared in a body that had undergone a single loop. This behavior can be observed in a number of travels, and it's the answer behind one of the toughest questions Atsuki will face.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Why does Atsuki's injury disappear when he travels forty minutes to the past? That's not what happened the last time he traveled back in time after getting injured.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The first reason is the amount of time it will take him to reach the future location. Even though it's minutes away, many weeks will pass until he returns to January 5th. That amount of time, enough for the injury to heal, is what makes him appear without it.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, there's another reason why his injury disappears, and it's unrelated to the amount of time that it will take him to return to January 5th. It's the same reason he doesn't appear with a burn mark when he travels all the way to November 24th, but that will be touched on a little later.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Certain events in this story have a specific characteristic to them: their origin seems unclear.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The handle of the storeroom's door has been taken off by Akaro A, but the means by which that happened are not straightforward.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Akaro world switched to world B, and in the attic, he was told about the existence of the secret door. Afterward, he traveled to the past and removed the handle from that door. It could be said that he was told about the existence of the door because he had removed its handle.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This is not the only instance where this seeming lack of causality takes place, so where exactly is it coming from?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world A, Akaro knew Xyn had been outsmarted. An alarm had trapped them in the tower, and the real Sekimeiya had vanished when he had woken up. Not only that, but he thought he had killed two people in order to bring his plan to success.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He hated the way the world had turned out, but altering the reality he'd experienced wasn't possible. However, eventually, he world switched to world B.{w} Someone else originally from world A came with him: Isla.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world A, Isla never expected that an attack would take place in the tower. She followed the adults and hoped that everything would be resolved quickly. ...A lot of time passed, though, and at one point, her mother had been missing for a while after going to the bathroom.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Isla couldn't bring herself to voice her worry, as that would've meant admitting that something could've happened to her mother. However, she regretted the way she'd acted; she wished she could've told Erina to stay with her.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Akaro and Isla world switched to world B. As soon as they appeared in that world, they shaped it in a way they couldn't change their own.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki and Shiroya B were able to save Miiya in world C, but didn't that only happen because she had already been saved?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This behavior of the world switch defined the relationship between the three worlds, instantly shaping three drastically different sets of events.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And when a two-way world switch happened, someone was pulled backward in the order of switches. In those instances, both worlds balanced each other out accordingly. By working like this, the world switches led into the progression between the three worlds.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In world A, only Atsuki made it to {time=21}, and he was accused of the murders that had taken place. Not a lot of time passed before a large portion of Japan suddenly disappeared forever.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: World B was a step up, but being between worlds A and C, it was filled with many bittersweet resolutions. Despite a few deaths, some people got out safely. Isla returned, but it wasn't the Isla who had died. Akaro was arrested, but it was the Akaro who most regretted what he'd done. Atsuki and Shiroya left happily, but they would never see Miiya again.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: World C existed thanks to world B. Everyone who was trapped got out alive. The people of that world faced numerous hardships, but they were all resolved. Naomi seemed to die, but she returned. Shiroya seemed to die, but she returned. Erina seemed to die, but she returned.{w} ...Then, why is it a world so close to world A?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A step was taken when world C was created, but what direction did it take? A bit more examination is needed to reach that answer.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In any case, the labyrinth spawned by the world switches always operated under the inherent progression that it had created. Some people from world A ended up in world B. Some people from world B ended up in world C, but their world A selves pulled them back to world B. Some people from world C visited worlds A and B, but they were able to safely return to world C.{w} Thanks to the recording obtained in world C, Akaro A was arrested in world B. Atsuki A was the only person from his world to momentarily reach world C, but he dropped all the way back to world A when his elevator ride to the top vanished out of nowhere, the exact moment Shiroya B traveled to November to make world C the world it was...
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The labyrinth never stopped spinning, and somewhere, it hid the peak that everyone wanted to reach. There's only one place where it would not have moved.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: I hope you had enough time to think about this mystery.{w} As you might have guessed, the Past Sekimeiya was involved.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai traveled to the past and appeared in the locked elevator. Before asking "why", though, it's necessary to ask "how". Without the Sekimeiya, in the future location of Sai's travel, he wouldn't have been able to enter the elevator. Hence, traveling to the past and appearing inside it seems impossible.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As long as the past and future states align and the events in between are possible, many elaborate setups can be created.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Consider this chart depicting one of Sai's possible journeys. Atsuki and Shiroya have trapped themselves in the elevator.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai thinks about his next course of action and decides to use the Past Sekimeiya. After allowing it to warm up, he touches it.{w} But how is his past position determined?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The answer is that he continues to live virtually, as if he did not time travel. Movements during this time can be natural or driven with clear intent. Let's say he virtually moves until he reaches room B4.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When he arrives in the past, he will be in room B4. Right now, this new timeline is imaginary. It will become real once the past state matches the future state.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Next, he takes out the Past Sekimeiya and allows it to warm up. He touches it and lives virtually until he reaches the floor 4 partitions.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: What's important is that the new timeline does not prevent the first travel from occurring.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This means that the Past Sekimeiya must be in the same location and charge state as it was when the first travel happened.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This travel creates another imaginary timeline, and Sai now exists before the elevator is stopped.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Taking this opportunity, he enters it and traps himself between floors.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Isn't this a contradiction, though? In the real timeline, Atsuki and Shiroya are in the elevator, but here, Sai is alone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Try thinking about what the original Sai sees and hears from his perspective. As long as the circumstances that allowed the first travel to happen are preserved, this is valid.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In any case, this is the power of virtual timelines. The absurdities will soon collapse into a single truth.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Notice that the future position of the third timeline no longer matches the second. Sai can no longer go to the 4th floor partitions since he's stuck in the elevator.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The result is that the future position in the second timeline is updated to match the third. The past position in the third timeline is updated accordingly.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In this latest iteration of the third timeline, Sai appears midair inside the elevator and crashes down. He repeats the process of trapping himself between floors.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The validity of the third timeline is preserved, so let's see what happens if we look farther into the future.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The future position of the first timeline is updated to be in the elevator, which updates the past position in the second timeline.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, this raises an issue.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Sai can no longer perform the second travel since now he appears in the stopped elevator.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This destroys the third timeline, but preserves its effect.{w} The future position in the first timeline is inside the elevator after it closed.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: After killing Atsuki and Shiroya, Sai's past and future positions finally match. The virtual timeline stabilizes and becomes reality.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Perhaps you don't like the idea that Atsuki and Shiroya aren't in the elevator in the third timeline.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That's fine. This merely demonstrates the concept.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Another method might involve Sai falling down the elevator shaft in a virtual timeline and entering the elevator from the top.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As long as the goal is achievable within the travel and the user has the will to reach it, the Past Sekimeiya will turn it into reality.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The key is to set the future state to be within the elevator. The exact method is not important as long as there is at least one valid option in the sea of possibilities.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The concept of virtual timelines and iterative updates can be found elsewhere in the story. I wonder what solutions you'll come up with.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki obtains an equation for the Sekimeiya's travel times using hypothetical worlds. We'll call these "virtual worlds".
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Through countless iterations, he uses his virtual selves to produce a result that's observed in the real world.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: While this concept works for him, Atsuki isn't aware of how lucky he is to formulate the plan the way he does.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Let's take a look at a simple travel using the Past Sekimeiya. In this example, we'll pay close attention to the age of the user throughout the sequence. The node {b}t{/b} represents the moment at which the Sekimeiya is activated.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The Sekimeiya sends the user twenty minutes back in time. In order to determine the user's state in the past, a virtual copy of the user is created that continues to live as if they had not time traveled. After twenty minutes, their final state is used in the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Both past and future locations are equidistant from the travel point, which means that in this virtual world, the user will arrive in the past being twenty minutes older than at the moment the Sekimeiya was activated.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And when the user makes it to the future copy point of the second virtual world, they will be sixty minutes older than at the moment of the travel.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: In this second world, the user is able to update their future state.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The state {b}t+20{/b} does not account for the user's behavior in the past, but {b}t+60{/b} does. This update stage is essential for convergence.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The next step is a third virtual world.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Since the previous stage's final position is copied, the user will age by another forty minutes and will be 100 minutes older at the end of the travel.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This stage exists to confirm the loop is stable. The user must have identical positions and possessions at {b}t+60{/b} and {b}t+100{/b}. The ages of the body and possessions will be slightly older, but everything else is identical.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: If the most recent virtual world was stable, the next step will apply the final result to the real world.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When the user appears in the past, they are sixty minutes older than the moment they touched the Sekimeiya, and in the copy point of the future, they will be 100 minutes older. When a user reaches the future state in reality, they have experienced five times the travel time.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: This is how infinite aging is avoided. The update stage is required to account for the user's actions in the past, and the final stable loop is frozen and applied to reality. Of course, every stage starts with the memories from the {b}t{/b} point.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: A clear example of this kind of sequence is Isla's burn. Touching the Sekimeiya left a burn scar on her finger that this system didn't have enough time to erase. Naturally, however, she didn't age infinitely.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Atsuki is able to successfully execute his plan, but he's not fully aware of how the Past Sekimeiya works. His understanding is that Sai's watch displayed the year 9,999 through infinite virtual loops.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: However, that's incorrect. If the loops operated like that, Sai would have instantly died in the process, and the watch would've disintegrated.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So let's consider a different way Atsuki could have formulated his plan.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "If I touch the Sekimeiya when fifteen minutes have passed, I'll go twenty minutes to the past and appear in the hallway holding a notepad. Depending on what it says, I'll do one of three things."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "1: If it has a formula written down, forty minutes later, I'll be holding it, so that's how I will have appeared with it."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "2: If I don't appear with a notepad, by using the Future Sekimeiya in the kitchen, I'll start working toward finding the formula. Before forty minutes pass, I'll obtain a notepad from the bedrooms, and in the top left corner of the first page, I'll write a "1" along with the progress I made in those forty minutes. In the future location, I'll be holding the notepad."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "3: If I find a notepad that doesn't contain the formula, it will have my current progress along with a number in the top left corner of the first page, which will indicate the amount of iterations that have occurred so far.{w} Using the information in the notepad, I'll start working to find the formula. Before the forty minutes pass, I'll write down the updated progress in a notepad from the bedrooms, increase the number I saw in the top left corner by one, and make sure that I'm holding it in the future location."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The concept is almost the same as the one he actually uses, but there's a very important distinction. In this example, Atsuki doesn't get any information before he travels. Instead, he appears with a notepad after traveling to the past.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: According to what Atsuki believes at this point in time, this sequence should've worked too since it's almost identical to what he believes happened to Sai's watch. However, if he had attempted it, it would not have worked.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The reason is simple. In the virtual worlds, the location of arrival would not have changed after the update stage. The same mechanism that prevents infinite aging would've prevented the infinite information gathering system. In the real world, Atsuki could only have appeared with a notepad containing sixty minutes' worth of information.{w} Not only that, but the plan contains a glaring contradiction. Points {b}t+60{/b} and {b}t+100{/b} are necessarily identical in every way except age, so appearing with a notepad that contains different information from the one that will be held in the future copy point is conceptually flawed. Even though it's what Atsuki believes happened to Sai's watch, it's fundamentally faulty, as it breaks the rule that past and future points must be identical.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: ...So why did his original plan work? Where's the loophole that allows him to manifest this infinitely iterated information without aging infinitely?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Let's refresh our memory on the method through which Atsuki obtains the Sekimeiya's formula.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "If I touch the Sekimeiya when fifteen minutes have passed, I'll go twenty minutes to the past.{w} But before I touch it, I'll open the door to the hallway and find a notepad from the bedrooms on the floor. Depending on what it says, I'll do one of three things."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "1: If it has a formula written down, I'll go twenty minutes to the past, obtain the notepad, write the formula down, and leave it in the hallway."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "2: If I don't find a notepad, I'll go twenty minutes to the past, and using the Future Sekimeiya in the kitchen, I'll start to work toward finding the formula. Before twenty minutes pass, I'll obtain a notepad from the bedrooms, and in the top left corner of the first page, I'll write a "1" along with the progress I made in those twenty minutes. Then, I'll leave it in the hallway."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: "3: If I find a notepad that doesn't contain the formula, it will have my current progress along with a number in the top left corner of the first page, which will indicate the amount of iterations that have occurred so far.{w} I'll go back to the past, and using the information I read in the notepad, I'll start working to find the formula. Before the twenty minutes pass, I'll write down the updated progress in a notepad from the bedrooms, increase the number I saw in the top left corner by one, and then leave the notepad in the hallway."
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: As you might've noticed, the reason behind his success lies in observing the information left by the virtual worlds before touching the Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The Atsukis in the virtual worlds leave the notepad in the hallway so that the Atsuki before the {b}t{/b} point can see it. In other words, stage 2 feeds information to stage 1.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That causes {b}t{/b}'s starting memories to continuously update, and the calculations made at the {b}t+60{/b} point are no longer locked to a state of a single round of calculations.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When the sequence converges and the final result is applied to the real world, Atsuki appears in the past having aged only sixty minutes but having spent infinite time computing. This is thanks to the virtual worlds continuously updating the starting point through real Atsuki's memories.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: When Isla A traveled from December 15th to November 24th, she appeared with a burn mark on her finger. The Sekimeiya was immensely hot, so the burn would not have faded by the time the future location took place.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: So then, why does Atsuki not appear with a burn mark on November 24th? The Sekimeiya was about as hot, and he will spend even fewer days to reach the future position since he will travel forward in time from December 15th to January 5th.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The answer lies in what will happen to Atsuki the night he will arrive at the motel. He will travel to the future in order to duplicate his money, but due to a miscalculation, he will replicate his body from November 24th.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That body didn't have a burn, so he never appeared with one.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The biggest reason why this loop doesn't work for Atsuki is that the box Atase took only contained the Past Sekimeiya.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: While he's rushing his actions, Atsuki can't help but feel like that doesn't make sense.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: He recalls that he returned to his world at {time=19:30}, which is approaching. That's why he rushes Shiroya to activate the Sekimeiya at that time and make the people in the center of the tower change worlds.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: But of course, that's slightly paradoxical. Why did the travel happen at {time=19:30} in the first place? His hurry to take this action only existed because the world switch had been lived through once, so why did it not just happen at a later point?
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: There's something Atsuki is mistaken about. Shiroya traveling to November 30th isn't what makes everyone world switch back to world B. It is Atsuki A who causes that when he travels from world B to world C, pulling them back to their world. That's why he has no control over the time at which the world switch takes place.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: Nonetheless, when Shiroya travels to November, she does cause a world switch. Both immense ranges still overlapped in the middle of the tower, and only one person found themselves there: Atsuki A, cluelessly taking the elevator up. Before his ride ends, Shiroya's touch makes him go back to world A, where no elevator is supporting him, and he falls onto the one below him.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: That burning touch of the Sekimeiya was the catalyst behind the events that unfolded on December 15th. Shiroya traveled to the future and suddenly found herself in her apartment. It was December 19th, and the first thing she did was call Atsuki's phone.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: During the twelve hours of December 15th, Atsuki B vaguely wondered something. He knew he had to make sure that Shiroya's body wouldn't be found in world C so that Miiya could be saved, but that would only work out because her body had already not been found. Atsuki wasn't sure how that detail had originated.{w} Regardless, he instructed Shiroya to keep her world C self hidden from the world. Yet, in the end, she didn't end up causing that: it was Shiroya C herself who was attracted to the Sekimeiya's glow and vanished from the world for weeks.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: The importance behind that action was even larger than Atsuki had thought. Due to Shiroya's disappearance, Akaro believed that he had killed a young girl, which developed into the attack of December 15th.
entries.speaker: c

entries.text: And although it was world C's own flow that made that happen, it was thanks to world B's influence that it occurred. Shiroya C avoided falling into a coma because her world B self shielded her while both of them fell through the floor of the gem shop.
entries.speaker: c
